faqs.question: What does the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge actually approve?
faqs.answer: More than a Dubai parent would expect. The published position is that the Ras Al Khaimah authority, like Sharjah's, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, and that the Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate. That is a wider remit than inspection alone. What it does not control is the awarding body: Cambridge, Pearson and the International Baccalaureate set their own syllabus codes, paper structures, timetables and criteria regardless of local approval. Knowing which body decides which thing tells you exactly who to ask when you need an answer.

faqs.question: If the regulator approves school fees, why are tutoring prices not regulated?
faqs.answer: Because they sit in completely different regulatory worlds, and both being called fees causes real confusion. Your school's tuition fee went through an approval process at emirate level and is published. A private tutor's hourly rate goes through no approval step, has no published tariff and no authority to appeal to. Treat any claim that a tutoring price is approved or set by an authority as false. The practical consequence is that the approved school fee is the firmer anchor for a budget conversation, and a tutoring quote is a market price in a market where local supply is thin.

faqs.question: How do I confirm which exam board my child's Ras Al Khaimah school uses?
faqs.answer: One email to the subject department, asked per subject rather than per child, because mixed entries across boards are normal and nobody announces them. Ask four things: which awarding body sets this subject's papers, which syllabus code, which tier where the subject is tiered and when that decision is final, and which administrative zone the centre sits in. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones, states it is essential to use the correct timetable version, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover an IGCSE child and a Diploma child in the same house?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and for good reasons rather than commercial ones. The two qualifications are marked against different things, the Diploma carries internally assessed components with school-set deadlines that IGCSE does not, and the calendars run on different clocks. A single hour divided between two children delivers a third of a session to each. What families generally want, once it is offered, is two separate arrangements scheduled back to back on the same evening, each matched to its own qualification and level and priced per subject.

faqs.question: How do the IGCSE series and the Diploma deadlines collide in one family year?
faqs.answer: Mostly in the spring, and the collision is worse than families expect. The Cambridge June series is the sitting a Ras Al Khaimah candidate takes, with November as the resit route; its papers fall across May and June, and its final entry deadline lands in the spring term, several months earlier. That spring window is also when the heaviest internal Diploma deadlines and the mock season sit, so one child is being entered for external papers while the other is closing components. Pearson runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 International GCSE timetable running to 19 November 2026 and those results reaching students in the following January. Ask the coordinator for the school's internal calendar, then overlay the official timetable for your centre's Cambridge zone on top of it rather than working from any date quoted on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Why is specialist tuition harder to find in Ras Al Khaimah than in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic rather than quality. The emirate's private-school set is smaller and concentrated in a few areas, so there are fewer departments, fewer option blocks per subject and a much smaller resident population of teachers who have taken a specific course to examination. The subjects that go short are consistent: Higher Level sciences, Group 2 languages beyond the common ones, Psychology, Computer Science and Arabic as a first language. The useful response is not to lower the specification but to stop using distance as the filter, because a tight radius is a smaller and worse-matched pool.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education still apply at a school with an international curriculum here?
faqs.answer: Yes. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. The published conditions are specific: separate classes must be organised for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited.

faqs.question: What does IB and IGCSE tuition cost around Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Published market figures, researched October 2026 and attributed: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end, which is generally group or university-student tutoring. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for qualified online work. A 2026 Dubai cost survey gives AED 200 to 450 and above for IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. In-home visits run AED 180 to 350, and AED 200 to 500 for independents once travel is inside the rate.

faqs.question: Is there an inspection report I can read for a private school in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Start with the Department of Knowledge, since it regulates private education in the emirate and approves the school's programmes and assessment methods, and ask the school directly for whatever judgement or report it holds. Read at subject level rather than at headline level, because a school rated well overall can contain a department identified as needing improvement, and the detail that matters is in the body of a report. Check the date too: a department can be rebuilt in two years, so a judgement describes the school as it was on the inspection dates.

faqs.question: Does "near me" matter at all if the tuition happens over video?
faqs.answer: Three local things still matter and one does not. The tutor's address does not. What does matter is the drive from your part of the emirate, because it decides the earliest hour a session can realistically start — later from Al Marjan Island or Digdaga than from Al Nakheel. The examination centre matters, because that is where your child physically sits the papers. And the school's own internal deadlines matter, because the plan is built backwards from them. Those three are worth establishing in the first term; the tutor's postcode never was.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give my child past papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: Marking your child's work against the published criteria is exactly what a tutor should be doing. Supplying a downloadable library of papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides is a different matter, because those documents belong to the awarding bodies. The correct route is to reference the official pages, link them, and work from material the school has legitimately issued. A provider advertising an archive of board material as a feature is telling you something about their judgement, and for unreleased material the exposure is more serious than copyright.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a weekday session can realistically start here?
faqs.answer: It depends on the drive rather than on the hour. From Al Nakheel or Khuzam, where the main school cluster sits, a late-afternoon start is workable. From Al Hamra Village, Al Marjan Island, Al Qusaidat or the inland villages the return journey eats the early evening, and a session booked optimistically for 16:30 in September becomes a 18:30 session by October. Our practice is to set the slot at the hour a household can actually keep every week, because a slot that gets missed produces no marked work and therefore no evidence of anything.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge and Pearson dates are genuinely fixed, and which can change?
faqs.answer: Pearson's published windows are the firmest thing you can plan against in the near term — the November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results on 22 January 2026 — and even those start life as provisional timetables that can be revised. Cambridge publishes key dates per series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, which is why a date that is correct for one centre can be wrong for another. Two things are worth knowing as fixed facts rather than dates: a UAE candidate sits the June and November series, and the February/March series belongs to India. Everything else, including the figures quoted here as worked examples, should be checked against the live official timetable and your statement of entry.

faqs.question: Do you offer home tuition in Ras Al Khaimah, or only lessons over video?
faqs.answer: Only over live video, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The in-home market genuinely exists and is priced on this page so you can weigh it fairly, usually on a two-hour minimum with travel inside the rate. The one thing a visit buys that a screen cannot is an adult in the room, which matters where supervision rather than teaching is the real need, and we will recommend it at the free diagnostic when that is the honest answer.

faqs.question: What if you cannot cover the subject my child needs?
faqs.answer: You get told, with the reason, rather than left on a list — and then three things are worth doing. Ask the school in writing what internal support exists for the course, because a department with four Higher Level students has options a parent cannot see. Ask the coordinator whether another family is in the same position, since two households needing the same scarce subject is the easiest problem in this market to solve. Then widen the search, judging candidates on which level they have taught to examination rather than on how near they live.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Confirm the entry, then get a diagnosis
ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingBody: Two short steps put a Ras Al Khaimah family ahead of almost everyone searching for this. First, email the subject department and ask, per subject, which awarding body, which syllabus code, which tier and when the tier is final, plus which administrative zone the centre sits in. Second, send us that answer with the year group, a photograph of recent marked work and the two evening windows your household can genuinely hold given the drive. You will get a named tutor and a slot, or a straight statement that the subject is not matchable right now and why. The first lesson is free and produces a written diagnosis, and nothing is taken before it happens.

intro.heading: Two routes, and the comparison nobody makes honestly
paragraphs: A family in Al Dhait with a child finishing Year 9 or Year 11 is facing a fork, and the advice available is usually partisan. Diploma schools explain why breadth matters. A Level schools explain why depth matters. Neither explains what either route demands of a particular student on a Tuesday evening in Grade 12, which is the information a parent needs.

The structural difference is simple to state. The Diploma carries six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with an internally assessed component in every subject. The IGCSE-then-A-Level route carries a larger number of subjects to 16 and then narrows sharply to three or four, with assessment concentrated in external papers and coursework varying by subject. One route spreads load across a wide front for two years; the other front-loads breadth at 16 and then concentrates.

That difference matters most for two kinds of student. A student who is strong across the board and manages deadlines well is well served by the Diploma, which rewards exactly that. A student who is excellent in three subjects and genuinely weak in one or two is often better served by narrowing, because the Diploma gives them no way to escape the weak subject and A Levels do. Neither of those is a statement about ability.

Al Dhait adds one local consideration. The emirate's private-school set is compact, so the choice may be a choice between two specific schools rather than between two abstract systems, and the quality of the particular department matters more than the system does. A strong teacher in a route that fits less well usually beats a weak teacher in the ideal route, and that is worth saying out loud because system comparisons rarely do.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is what parents search, and the honest answer is that either route is fully supportable from Al Dhait over a screen, which is not true of the local in-home pool for several subjects in either system.

Every rate on this page is attributed and dated October 2026. Equivalency statements come from a sourced report and are limited to what it actually says: for the British track there are published figures, and for the IB there is no published points threshold here, so none appears. No IB exam or results date appears either, because none has been verified from the board, whose own site returns an error to automated checking. Cambridge and Pearson dates, where they are needed, come from the boards' own exam-administration pages with the month they were read.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, assessed through tasks across the year. Its advantage going into the Diploma is habit: the student already writes to descriptors and already manages self-directed tasks, which is most of what the Diploma asks for beyond content.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the three core components, with internal assessment in every subject on school-set deadlines. programmes.name: A Levels and AS Levels
programmes.description: Three or four subjects carried in depth, assessed largely through external papers with coursework varying by subject. It rewards depth and allows a student to leave a weak subject behind at 16, at the cost of narrowing early and of a thinner spread if a plan changes.

sections.heading: The Diploma against IGCSE and A Levels
paragraphs: Set the two routes beside each other on the dimensions that affect a student's week, rather than on the dimensions schools market. Both are well-established, both are recognised, and both produce strong outcomes for students they suit. The useful question is which one suits this student.

The Diploma asks a student to carry six subjects for two years, three of them at Higher Level, while producing an internally assessed component in each, a 4,000-word Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and a CAS record. Nothing is dropped. A weak subject is carried to the end, and the breadth that is the programme's great strength is also the reason a student with one genuinely poor subject finds it punishing.

The A Level route asks a student to carry a wider set of subjects to 16, which produces a certificated grade spread, and then to narrow to three or four. Depth increases, the number of simultaneous deadlines falls, and a weak subject can be left behind. The cost is early specialisation: a student who narrows to sciences at 16 and discovers an interest in economics at 17 has fewer options than a Diploma student in the same position.

The table compares them on load, assessment, escape routes and what each rewards. It is a comparison rather than a recommendation, and the right answer differs between two children in the same house. It is also worth saying that neither route is the harder one in any general sense: they are hard in different places, and a student who finds one of them punishing would often have found the other comfortable.

sections.heading: What each route demands of a student
paragraphs: System comparisons are usually written about schools. The more useful version is written about students, because the same programme produces very different experiences depending on a small number of personal traits that are observable by Year 10.

The Diploma rewards three things in particular. Consistency across subjects, because six grades all count and there is no best-three calculation to hide behind. Deadline management, because the internal components run on school-set dates that nobody chases individually. And tolerance for carrying unfinished work, because a Diploma student always has four things partly done. A student who finishes one task before starting another will find the autumn of the final year genuinely difficult, regardless of ability.

The A Level route rewards depth tolerance and independent revision. Fewer subjects means more content per subject and more reliance on a student's own study outside lessons, with less scaffolding than a Diploma timetable provides. It also rewards decisiveness, because the subject choice at 16 is consequential and is made with less information than anybody would like.

The practical test for a family in Al Dhait is to look at the last two terms rather than at the last two report grades. Did the student hold several deadlines at once, or did things get finished at the last minute one at a time? Did they revise without being told, or only when a test was imminent? Those two answers predict route fit better than any subject mark does.

sections.heading: Recognition and equivalency compared
paragraphs: This is the section where most pages overreach, so the limits are set out first. The Ministry's published equivalency requirements for the British track are sourced and can be stated. For the IB, the source used for this project does not publish a points threshold, so none appears here and none should be taken from any tutoring page, including this one.

On the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One competitor page ranking for these queries states that six IGCSE subjects are required; the published rule is five.

For the American track, the same source gives English proficiency as a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No EmSAT requirement is mentioned in that source and no IB points figure is stated, which is precisely why this page declines to publish one.

Two further honesty points. Equivalency is a process performed by the Ministry of Education and the emirate's attestation channel, not by any tutoring provider, and tuition is not a requirement for it. And recognition at a particular university is a separate question from equivalency: a course specifies its own entry requirements, which should be read on the institution's own page rather than inferred from a national rule.

sections.heading: Two children on two routes: what each needs weekly
paragraphs: A number of households in this emirate end up running both systems at once, either because two children chose differently or because one school offered one route and another school the other. The weekly pattern that results is lopsided in a way worth planning for.

A Diploma student in the final year needs attention in bursts: a coursework cluster in the autumn that consumes everything for six weeks, then a long stretch of paper technique in the spring. An A Level student needs steadier attention across both years, with less clustering and more reliance on independent revision between sessions. Those two shapes fit together reasonably well, because the Diploma student's heavy period is the A Level student's steady one.

What collides is the quiet room and the parent. In Al Dhait, villa housing makes two simultaneous sessions physically possible, which many households in the emirate cannot manage. What remains finite is adult attention for chasing deadlines, and the Diploma student will absorb almost all of it in the autumn unless the A Level student's slot is explicitly protected.

The table sets the two weekly patterns side by side. The point is to decide the shape once, in September, rather than negotiating it every Sunday for a year. Two mechanisms make the arrangement hold. Every block gets an end date at the moment it is agreed, so nothing becomes the permanent default by accident. And the quieter child's session is reduced rather than cancelled in the heaviest weeks, because a child who learns twice that their work is the thing that gets dropped will usually stop bringing it up at all.

sections.heading: What each route costs to support
paragraphs: Tutoring cost differs between the routes in a way that is rarely mentioned, and it is not simply a function of how many subjects are taken. It depends on how many distinct things need external support and for how long.

On the Diploma, the support requests cluster around the three Higher Levels and the core components. A household supporting one Higher Level subject weekly across both years, plus a block of Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge work in the final autumn, is buying two distinct products. Using Bestimate's published monthly estimates, a weekly one-hour session sits at AED 600 to 1,200 a month mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, read October 2026.

On an A Level route the pattern is usually fewer products over a longer period: one or two subjects supported steadily rather than a Higher Level plus core components. There is no Extended Essay equivalent, which removes a block. Set against that, A Level content depth means a student who needs support in a subject tends to need it for longer rather than in bursts.

The honest summary is that the Diploma costs more in distinct support products and the A Level route costs more in duration per subject, and for most households the totals land closer together than the structures suggest. What moves the number far more than the route is whether the household bought a diagnosis before buying hours. None of the figures here is an IB Gram price list; they are the published market, with sources, so any quote can be judged against something.

sections.heading: What is the same on both routes
paragraphs: Comparisons tend to exaggerate difference, so it is worth stating what does not change, because that is the part a family can start working on before the decision is even made.

Mark schemes and criteria reward the same behaviours on both routes. Showing method earns marks in every system. Matching the command term earns marks in every system. Quoting the figure from the extract, labelling the diagram, ordering the stages of a process, ranking the sources of error rather than listing them: all of those are route-independent, and a student who learns them in Year 10 carries them through either post-16 programme.

Timed practice marked against a published scheme is the most effective revision method on both routes, and rereading is the least effective on both. Retrieval beats recognition in both systems. Spacing beats blocking in both. Data and graph questions appear across the sciences, geography and economics in both, and improving that one skill lifts several subjects at once regardless of which certificate is at the end.

And the local reality is the same on both. In Ras Al Khaimah the number of people who have taught a particular advanced course is small, specialist capacity tightens as a series approaches, and some of the best-placed local teachers are barred from tutoring students at their own school. That constraint applies to a Higher Level Diploma option and an A Level subject equally, which means the format decision, in-home against online, works out the same way on either route.

sections.heading: Comparing a school's offer before you switch
paragraphs: In a compact emirate the route decision is often a school decision, and switching school for a curriculum is a much larger undertaking than switching a subject. Before doing it, the offer deserves the same scrutiny the system received.

Six questions do most of the work. How many students have completed the final year of this programme at this school, and over how many years? Which subjects and which levels are actually offered rather than listed, and what happens if fewer students choose an option than the timetable needs? Who teaches the subject my child needs at the level they need, and how long have they taught it? What is the school's own internal deadline calendar for coursework? What is the latest inspection outcome? And for a post-16 route, what entries do the school's own courses require from Year 11?

The reason those questions matter more here than in a large market is cohort size. A programme offered to a handful of students is vulnerable to a single teacher leaving, and an option listed in a prospectus may not run if three students choose it. Neither of those is a criticism; both are arithmetic, and a family is entitled to ask about them.

On regulation: private schools in this emirate are regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods as well as regulating provision. That means a programme on offer has been through the emirate authority, and asking for confirmation that the programme is the approved one is an ordinary question rather than an impertinent one.
bullets: How many students have completed the final year here, and over how many years?
Which options actually run, and what happens if too few choose one?
Who teaches my child's subject at that level, and for how long have they taught it?

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and the permit
paragraphs: A page making a route comparison should be comparable itself, so here are the limits that apply here as much as anywhere. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and command term, mark work against the published scheme, test the viability of a coursework decision, review a method, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written.

A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay, A Level coursework or any assessed work, and must not supply text, data or diagrams for submission. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the consequence of buying one falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it, which is why the boundary belongs in a comparison rather than in a footnote.

The materials rule applies on both routes. No tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads; the official source should be referenced and linked instead, which is why this page carries no attachments. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

On who may teach: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutor can promise a grade on either route.

process.title: Describe the student, not the ambition
process.description: Tell us how the last two terms were actually managed: whether several deadlines were held at once or things got finished one at a time at the last minute, and whether revision happened without being told. Those two answers predict route fit better than any grade does.

process.title: Take a free diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis with no card details taken, on real questions from whichever subject matters most. It classifies lost marks into content, method, command term and time, and the written summary is yours whichever route you end up choosing.

process.title: Ask the school the six questions
process.description: Completion numbers, which options actually run, who teaches the subject at the level needed and for how long, the internal deadline calendar, the latest inspection outcome, and what the school's own post-16 courses require from Year 11. All six are ordinary questions.

process.title: Buy the transition block, not a year
process.description: At the fork, the useful purchase is three or four weeks on one named gap: algebra fluency before Higher Level mathematics, or independent writing before an essay-based A Level. It finishes before the new course starts and hands over something written.

process.title: Protect the quieter child's slot
process.description: Where a household runs both routes, the Diploma student will absorb almost all the adult attention in the autumn of the final year. One protected weekly slot for the other child, reduced rather than cancelled in the worst weeks, costs far less than the repair it prevents.

whyPoints.title: The comparison made about students, not schools
whyPoints.description: Both routes work and both are recognised. What differs is what each demands week to week, and the deciding traits are observable by Year 10: consistency across subjects, deadline management, and tolerance for carrying unfinished work.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency stated only where sourced
whyPoints.description: The British-track figures are published and appear here: five subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus an A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E. No IB points threshold appears, because the source used does not state one.

whyPoints.title: The support cost of each route, with the bands named
whyPoints.description: The Diploma costs more in distinct support products and an A Level route more in duration per subject, and the totals land closer together than the structures suggest. The published AED bands are given with their source and the month they were read.

whyPoints.title: What does not change, stated too
whyPoints.description: Method marks, command terms, timed practice against a published scheme and data-handling skill reward the same behaviours on both routes. A student can start on all four before the route decision is made.

whyPoints.title: Both routes fully supportable from Al Dhait
whyPoints.description: Teaching over live video means a Higher Level Diploma option and an A Level subject are equally available here, which is not true of the local in-home pool for several subjects in either system.

whyPoints.title: Comparable limits, including ours
whyPoints.description: No part of assessed work produced, on either route. No syllabus documents or mark schemes as downloads. No promised grades, and no claim of approval from the Department of Knowledge or any awarding body.

faqs.question: Is the IB Diploma or A Levels better for a student in Al Dhait?
faqs.answer: Neither in general; it depends on the student and, in a compact emirate, on which specific school and department are available. The Diploma rewards consistency across six subjects, deadline management and tolerance for carrying several unfinished tasks. A Levels reward depth, independent revision and let a student leave a weak subject behind at 16. A strong teacher in the less ideal route usually beats a weak teacher in the ideal one, which system comparisons rarely admit.

faqs.question: How do I tell which route suits my child?
faqs.answer: Look at how the last two terms were managed rather than at the last two report grades. Did your child hold several deadlines at once, or did things get finished one at a time at the last minute? Did revision happen without being told, or only when a test was imminent? A student who finishes one task before starting another will find the autumn of the Diploma's final year genuinely hard regardless of ability, and that is the single most predictive observation available.

faqs.question: What does the Diploma carry that A Levels do not?
faqs.answer: Six subjects rather than three or four, an internally assessed component in every one of them, a 4,000-word Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and a CAS record. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay have no A Level equivalent and no timetabled lesson on the Diploma either, which makes them the clearest additional workload and the clearest additional support cost of choosing that route.

faqs.question: Can a Diploma student drop a subject they are failing?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the structural fact that decides the route for some students. All six subjects are carried to the end and all six grades count, so a student with one genuinely weak subject has no way around it. On an A Level route the weak subject can be left behind at 16. That is not an argument against the Diploma; it is an argument for being honest about whether one subject is a persistent problem rather than a temporary dip.

faqs.question: Does UAE equivalency treat the two routes the same?
faqs.answer: The published requirements differ and this page states only what a source supports. For the British track: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. For the IB, the source used publishes no points threshold, so none appears here. Confirm your own case with the Ministry or your emirate's attestation channel.

faqs.question: Is it true six IGCSE subjects are needed for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. The published rule on the British track is five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among them. One competitor page ranking for these queries publishes a six-subject figure, which is worth knowing because it circulates. A sensible entry list carries a margin above five anyway, in case one subject goes wrong, but the requirement itself is five and should be confirmed with the Ministry rather than with any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Which route is cheaper to support with tutoring?
faqs.answer: They land closer together than the structures suggest. The Diploma generates more distinct support products: a Higher Level subject weekly, plus internal assessment blocks, plus Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge work. An A Level route generates fewer products but longer durations, because content depth means a student who needs help tends to need it for longer. Using Bestimate's published bands, read October 2026, a weekly mid-market hour is AED 600 to 1,200 a month and specialist exam-year support AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more.

faqs.question: What actually reduces the tutoring bill on either route?
faqs.answer: Buying a diagnosis before buying hours, which matters far more than the route does. The commonest waste in this market is a household booking two sessions a week in September against an undiagnosed problem and finding in January that nothing changed, because nobody established whether the losses were content, method, command term or timing. One session that answers that question redirects everything after it, and at IB Gram it is free with no card details taken.

faqs.question: We have one child on each route. How do we plan the week?
faqs.answer: Decide the shape in September rather than negotiating it each Sunday. The Diploma student needs attention in bursts, with a coursework cluster that saturates six weeks of the final autumn and then a long stretch of paper technique. The A Level student needs steadier attention across both years. Those shapes fit together reasonably well; what collides is adult attention, so the A Level student's weekly slot has to be protected explicitly or it becomes the thing that gets cancelled.

faqs.question: Does Al Dhait's housing help with either route?
faqs.answer: With both, in one respect. Full past papers need ninety uninterrupted minutes in a quiet room, and the district's predominantly villa housing makes that easier than the creek-side apartments do. It also makes two simultaneous online sessions physically possible, which a smaller flat often cannot support. Neither of those changes which route to choose, but both make the final year of either route more practical to run from here.

faqs.question: Should we switch schools to change route?
faqs.answer: Only after asking the receiving school six questions: how many students have completed the final year of the programme and over how many years, which options actually run rather than being listed, who teaches the subject at the level needed and for how long, what the internal deadline calendar looks like, what the latest inspection outcome is, and what their own post-16 courses require from Year 11. Cohort size makes all six more consequential in this emirate than in a large market.

faqs.question: What can my child start working on before the decision is made?
faqs.answer: Four things that pay off on either route. Showing method so that working earns marks rather than the answer alone. Matching the command term exactly, which costs nothing and recovers marks on every paper. Timed practice marked against a published scheme rather than rereading notes. And data and graph handling, which appears across the sciences, geography and economics and lifts several subjects at once. None of those depends on which certificate is at the end.

faqs.question: Is the local teacher shortage different between the two routes?
faqs.answer: No, and that is a useful simplification. In Ras Al Khaimah the number of people who have taught any particular advanced course is small, capacity tightens as a series approaches, and some of the best-placed local teachers are barred from tutoring students at their own school. That applies to a Higher Level Diploma option and an A Level subject equally, which means the format decision between in-home and online works out the same way whichever route a family chooses.

faqs.question: Will a university prefer one route over the other?
faqs.answer: A course specifies its own entry requirements, and those should be read on the institution's own page rather than inferred from a national rule or from a tutoring page. Equivalency is a separate matter from admission: the Ministry's process makes a certificate recognised, and a university then applies its own criteria on top. Both routes are widely recognised, and the sensible sequence is to check the specific courses being considered before the route is chosen rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: Can you help with the Extended Essay if we choose the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary worth stating precisely. A tutor may help narrow a research question so it can be answered inside the 4,000-word limit, explain what each named criterion demands, discuss structure, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor must never write, redraft or complete the essay, nor supply text to paste in. The school provides the supervisor; external support is additional to that rather than a replacement for it, and the student writes every word.

Tell us that, ask the school the six questions in this page, and take a free diagnostic session with no card details taken. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and both routes are fully supportable from here.

intro.heading: The join between two qualifications is a date, not a subject
paragraphs: There is a specific week in a UAE school career when a student stops being an IGCSE candidate and becomes a Diploma student. In practice it falls in June, when the last paper is sat, and the consequences land in September, when six new courses start at once. Between those two points is a summer that most families treat as a holiday and a handful treat as the cheapest academic advantage available. This page is written for the second group and for anyone who wants to join it.

Start with what the two qualifications actually ask. IGCSE is terminal in most subjects: two or three written papers, no coursework, a grade decided in a hall. Cambridge runs June and November series for international centres; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Preparation is therefore front-to-back revision and timed-paper technique, and it finishes cleanly. The Diploma is the opposite shape. Six subjects over two years, each with an internally assessed component marked against published criteria, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay at a 4,000-word limit and Creativity, Activity, Service. Work accumulates from the first month and almost all of its deadlines are set by the school.

That difference in shape is why the transition catches strong students. A child who got a grade 8 in Chemistry 0620 by revising hard in the spring arrives at Higher Level Chemistry where the first consequential task is choosing an Internal Assessment question and collecting workable data, which rewards nothing they practised. A student who is good at exams is not automatically good at projects with distant deadlines, and nobody tells them so in the summer when it could be fixed.

The dates themselves are published and checkable on the IGCSE side. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. On the IB side this page deliberately publishes no specific examination or results date, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically and a wrong date on a planning page is a real harm. UAE schools sit the May session with November available, and your coordinator holds the internal deadline sheet, which is the document that actually governs a Diploma year.

So the brief we work to for a family in Al Hamra Village is this: close the subject gaps in the summer, install project habits before the Diploma needs them, and get the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay decisions made in the first Diploma year rather than the second. IB Gram teaches here one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not place a tutor at a UAE address, and visiting students in person is a service we run only in India. In an emirate with a small pool of Diploma specialists, that is what makes the handover coachable at all.
bullets: IGCSE is terminal and revision-led; the Diploma is cumulative and project-led
The ten weeks after the June papers are the cheapest bridging window available

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.programmesIntro: A handover family is dealing with two systems at once. These four are the ones in play around Al Hamra Village, and each has one feature that matters more than the rest of its prospectus.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subject-by-subject, terminal in most courses, with codes that decide which past papers are the right ones: 0580 Mathematics, 0606 Additional Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology. Tiered subjects set a grade ceiling at entry. For a student heading to the Diploma the significant point is that Extended-tier content, not Core, is what the next qualification assumes.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm the centre's Cambridge timetable zone with the school; Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and says it is essential to use the correct version. For a Ras Al Khaimah family that also means confirming whether the school continues into Years 12 and 13 at all, which is a Year 10 question.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: May/June and November sittings, codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, with a modular pattern available on some courses so units can be banked across sittings. Grades on the 9-1 scale. For the Diploma transition the useful detail is that Pearson's Mathematics A and B routes differ in algebraic demand, and a Diploma maths course assumes the more demanding one.
programmes.countryNote: Work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date. The published history is a safe guide: the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed against descriptors A to D with a Personal Project in the final year. A student arriving at the Diploma from the Middle Years Programme has the opposite problem from an IGCSE student: they are comfortable with extended projects and criteria, and unpractised at timed external papers. Both routes need bridging, in different directions.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah family moves between an IGCSE school and an IB school, the two curricula sequence topics differently and there will be genuine content gaps in maths and science. Those are findable in a diagnostic session and closeable in a summer, provided someone looks.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three usually at Higher Level, scored out of 45, with an internally assessed component in every subject plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay at a 4,000-word limit, and Creativity, Activity, Service. The gap between a predicted and a final score is usually explained by the internal components rather than by the written papers, which is where a first-year plan should concentrate.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session with November available where offered. Ask the coordinator for the internal deadline sheet in the first autumn term: it governs the Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay milestones, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the oral recording windows, and it is the only calendar a tutoring plan should follow.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects where the IGCSE-to-Diploma gap is widest for students on this coast, with what actually has to be bridged in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Assumes Extended-tier algebraic fluency and rewards it continuously. The real gap from 0580 is not topics but speed: a student who rearranges equations slowly will survive Standard Level and struggle at Higher. Additional Mathematics 0606 is the best possible preparation and its absence is the gap most worth closing in a summer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led and technology-led, and the better fit for many students arriving from a Core or a mid-Extended 0580. The decision between this and Analysis and Approaches has to be made before the Diploma begins, because some university courses specify the latter by name. Check the target courses first.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic from 0620 transfers directly and is assumed to be automatic. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are new depth rather than new topics. The genuine novelty is the Internal Assessment: a self-designed investigation with its own criteria, which rewards nothing an IGCSE candidate practised.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circular motion are new; the serious gap is quantitative. Uncertainty propagation and error analysis are assumed from the first term and are barely touched at IGCSE, and they carry marks in both the papers and the Internal Assessment. Six summer sessions on uncertainty is unusually high-value work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume increases sharply and terminology precision matters more. Students coming from 0610 are usually well prepared on content and poorly prepared for an investigation that has to be narrow enough to control, which is where the Internal Assessment is won before any writing happens.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A different discipline from First Language English 0500 rather than a harder version. The Diploma asks for analysis of how texts work on readers, across literary and non-literary material, with an Individual Oral in a school recording window. Students who scored well at IGCSE by writing fluently need to learn to argue instead.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Builds cleanly on IGCSE Economics 0455 where a student took it, and is entirely learnable from scratch where they did not. Diagram accuracy still decides the analysis marks. The new element is internally assessed commentary work spread across the course, which needs scheduling rather than cramming.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Framework-led, and a natural continuation from IGCSE Business Studies 0450. The discipline is applying one correct tool to the stimulus rather than listing several. Higher Level candidates meet a research-based component with its own word limit, criteria and school deadline.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Not a Diploma subject but the single best predictor of comfort in Analysis and Approaches, because it introduces calculus, logarithms and kinematics a year early. Where a student did not take it, a summer block covering differentiation and function transformations closes most of the gap.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Taught alongside both qualifications, since the federal baseline covers Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies for every private school. Support means working with the school's own material and assessment, because using different or additional content without ministry permission is not permitted.

regions.note: Resort-dominated, apartment-heavy, with involved visitor access. Households here travel more in the summer than most, so a plan that survives a trip is worth more than a plan with more sessions in it.

regions.note: The central district holding most of the emirate's schools. Families here are most likely to be changing school for the Diploma years, which makes the bridging question a change-of-curriculum question as well as a change-of-level one.

Content work is diagnosed from the student's own IGCSE papers; habit work means planning something with a distant deadline and actually meeting it. Cheapest high-value intervention in the whole two-qualification route.

This is when the calendar has slack, which is exactly why it is the right time to spend on components.

sections.heading: What "near me" is worth at this point in a school career
paragraphs: The phrase in the search bar is about reach, and reach genuinely matters when a family needs to start quickly. In the handover, though, the clock is unusually generous: the summer gap is known a year in advance, and nobody needs a tutor on the doorstep by Thursday. What is scarce on this coast is not availability but combination. A tutor who can diagnose an IGCSE script and also knows what a Diploma Internal Assessment is marked on is a narrow category anywhere, and Ras Al Khaimah is a small emirate with a small private-school sector.

So the honest reading of this search is that proximity is being used as a proxy for trust. A parent wants someone accountable, who can be checked, who will still be there in three weeks. Those are reasonable requirements and none of them is geographic. They are met by a named tutor who stays the same week to week, a written plan with an end date, and a review against marked evidence rather than against impressions.

There is one way in which distance genuinely argues for online delivery here. Bridging work is at its most useful in the summer, when households on this coast travel, and an in-person arrangement collapses the moment anyone leaves the emirate. A live video session continues from anywhere with a connection, which turns a fragmented ten weeks into a usable block. That is a practical argument rather than a technological one.

IB Gram does not place a tutor at an address in Ras Al Khaimah or anywhere else in the UAE; in-person visiting is a service we run only in India. What a family gets instead is the specific combination this page is about, available in July as readily as in November, and judged on the student's own work rather than on how convenient the arrangement felt.

sections.heading: The handover year, month by month
paragraphs: Laid out as a sequence, the handover is less daunting than it feels, mostly because the heavy items are not where families expect. The spring of the final IGCSE year is the busiest stretch and almost nobody has spare capacity in it. The summer is empty and is where the leverage sits. The first Diploma term looks light and is the single best moment to make component decisions. The second Diploma year has no slack at all and is therefore the worst possible place to start anything.

The table below sets that out with the action for each month-band rather than a description of it. Two rows deserve emphasis. The first is the results row: IGCSE grades arrive in the second half of August, and the Diploma typically starts within weeks. Families who intend to use results to decide subject levels are deciding in a very narrow window, which is an argument for forming a provisional view in June on the evidence of the mocks and the papers as sat.

The second is the first-term row. In the opening months of the Diploma a student has six new courses and very few deadlines, which feels like a quiet term and is actually the most valuable one. This is when an Extended Essay topic can be chosen slowly, when an Internal Assessment question can be narrowed properly, and when a student can learn what criteria-based marking rewards. Every one of those tasks becomes a crisis if it waits until the second year.

A family on this coast can act on this table without buying anything. Ask the school for the internal deadline sheet in September. Write the maths route decision down in June with reasons. Spend two weeks of the summer on whichever gap the IGCSE scripts reveal. Those three steps cost nothing and remove most of the risk from the handover.

sections.heading: Curriculum transition map, subject by subject
paragraphs: Most writing about the IGCSE-to-Diploma jump says that it is a big step and leaves it there. The useful version names the step per subject, because the gaps are specific and several of them are narrow enough to close in a fortnight. One competitor page in this market has a single heading on the subject; nobody has a structured subject-by-subject account, which is why this one is here.

The pattern across sciences is consistent. Content gaps are modest, because IGCSE Extended covers the foundations honestly. The real gaps are quantitative and methodological: uncertainty propagation, experimental design, and the discipline of a self-designed investigation with its own assessment criteria. A student can arrive at Higher Level Physics knowing all the physics they need for the first term and still lose marks from week two because nobody showed them how to handle an error bar.

In mathematics the gap is speed rather than content, and it is the one most worth measuring before the Diploma starts. A student who completes 0580 Extended questions accurately but slowly will cope at Standard Level and find Higher Level relentless. Where Additional Mathematics 0606 was taken, most of the gap is already closed. Where it was not, a summer block on differentiation, function transformations and logarithms does most of the work.

In English and the humanities the gap is a change of discipline. First Language English 0500 rewards fluent, well-structured writing; the Diploma's language courses reward argument about how a text operates on a reader, across literary and non-literary material, with an oral component recorded in a school window. A student who was good at IGCSE English by writing nicely has to learn to analyse, and that transition takes a term rather than a week.

sections.heading: What to actually do with ten free weeks
paragraphs: The summer after IGCSE is the only period in five years when a student has no deadlines and full capacity, and the default use of it is nothing. That is a defensible choice after two years of examined courses, and a complete rest is better than a half-hearted programme. But a fortnight of focused work inside a ten-week break is not a lost holiday, and it reliably changes the first Diploma term.

The content half of a bridging block should be diagnosed rather than assumed. The student's own IGCSE scripts, read properly, say where the weaknesses are, and those weaknesses do not disappear because a new qualification has started. A student who lost marks on rearrangement and indices in June will lose marks on them in Analysis and Approaches in October. Two sessions a week for four weeks on two named gaps is enough to move the needle.

The habit half is less obvious and matters more. The Diploma's distinguishing feature is work with distant deadlines and self-set scope: an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a reflective project. An IGCSE candidate has never had to do that, because every deadline they have met was imposed weekly. So the useful summer exercise is one small project with a question they chose, a deadline they set, and a finished product at the end. The subject barely matters; the experience of scoping and finishing does.

The third element costs nothing: read the assessment criteria for two of the Diploma subjects the student is taking. Not the syllabus, the criteria. A sixteen-year-old who understands before September that their science work will be marked against named criteria with published maximums, rather than against a percentage, starts the course with information that most of their classmates will acquire in February.

sections.heading: Two qualifications, two assessment logics
paragraphs: The deepest difference between IGCSE and the Diploma is not difficulty, it is where the marks live. In an IGCSE subject almost everything is decided in a hall on a named day, which makes revision the dominant activity and makes the final fortnight disproportionately important. In a Diploma subject a meaningful share is decided months earlier, in work produced under the student's own management and marked against criteria the student can read in advance.

That shift changes what good support looks like. For IGCSE, the highest-value tutoring is timed practice marked to the published scheme, because that is the format the grade comes from. For the Diploma, the highest-value tutoring in the first year is criteria literacy and question narrowing, because a well-chosen Internal Assessment question is worth more than any amount of write-up polish applied to a badly chosen one.

It also changes what a parent should ask about. The right question to an IGCSE tutor is which papers they have taught and how they mark. The right question to a Diploma tutor is which criteria they can name for the student's subject and what the mark allocations are. Of the competitor pages researched across these UAE searches, not one names a single assessment criterion by letter. A tutor who can is demonstrating something that cannot be faked.

And the boundary applies on the Diploma side in a way it does not on the IGCSE side. Terminal papers cannot be ghost-written; internally assessed work can. So it needs saying plainly: on an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay a tutor explains the criteria, questions the plan, points out where a conclusion does not follow, and gives feedback on the student's own draft. Nobody at IB Gram writes, rewrites, supplies data for, or completes any of it. One site ranking on these searches sells finished Internal Assessments, and the consequences of that transaction fall on the student.

sections.heading: The maths route decision, made with evidence
paragraphs: Of all the choices in the handover, the maths route is the one most often made for the wrong reason. A student picks Analysis and Approaches because it sounds more serious, or Applications and Interpretation because a friend did, and two years later one of them is in difficulty. The decision deserves evidence, and the evidence exists in June: the student's own IGCSE maths performance, broken down by question type rather than summarised as a grade.

Analysis and Approaches is algebra-heavy and proof-oriented, continuous in its demands, and specified by name as a requirement for some university courses. Applications and Interpretation is statistics-heavy and technology-led, genuinely rigorous, and a better fit for a large number of capable students who are not fast algebraists. Neither is the easy one; they are differently hard, and the Higher Level version of either is a serious undertaking.

The practical test is narrow. Give the student a set of 0580 Extended algebraic manipulation questions and time them. Accuracy with slow speed points towards Applications and Interpretation or towards Standard Level Analysis and Approaches. Accuracy with reasonable speed, plus genuine interest in why a method works, points to Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. Where Additional Mathematics 0606 was taken and went well, that is the strongest available signal.

Then check the destination. If a target degree names Analysis and Approaches, the conversation is about whether Standard Level will satisfy it rather than about avoiding the course. University requirements change, so check the current ones rather than relying on what was true for an older sibling, and check them before the option form goes in rather than in the second Diploma year when changing course is difficult or impossible.

sections.heading: Assembling the equivalency file across both qualifications
paragraphs: A family in Ras Al Khaimah running a child through IGCSE and then the Diploma is also, quietly, assembling a Ministry of Education equivalency file. Equivalency is the process that makes a foreign school certificate usable with UAE authorities and universities. It is not something a tutoring service performs, guarantees or accelerates, and it is not a reason to buy tuition. It is simply a set of requirements that is much easier to satisfy if you know them in Year 9 than in Year 13.

For the British track, the requirements as clarified publicly in July 2026 are five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. That last clause is the one families miss: nine IGCSEs including Arabic and Islamic Education still needs five counting passes from the other seven.

For the American track the requirements are different in kind: English proficiency through IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB Diploma, this page publishes no points threshold, because none has been read on an official Ministry source. A competitor page in this market already publishes a wrong IGCSE subject count; inheriting that error or inventing an IB figure would be worse than saying nothing.

What a family should actually do is three things, none of which involves a tutor. Ask the school which of your child's subjects are the accredited ones. Count the counting subjects while option blocks can still change. And verify any IB equivalency requirement with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly rather than with a tutoring website, including this one.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE to the IB Diploma really?
faqs.answer: Smaller in content than in working style. IGCSE Extended covers the foundations honestly, so most first-term Diploma content is new depth rather than unfamiliar material. The genuine jump is that a Diploma subject includes internally assessed work the student scopes and manages themselves, marked against published criteria, months before any exam. A student who was good at revising for papers has never had to plan something with a distant deadline, and that is the skill the summer before the Diploma should install.

faqs.question: What should my child do in the summer between IGCSE and the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Rest for most of it, then spend about a fortnight on two things. The first is the content gaps their own IGCSE scripts reveal, because weaknesses in rearrangement, indices or uncertainty do not disappear when a new qualification starts. The second is one small self-scoped project with a question they chose and a deadline they set, finished properly. The subject hardly matters; the experience of scoping and finishing is what the Diploma assumes and what no IGCSE candidate has practised.

faqs.question: Should we wait for IGCSE results before choosing Diploma levels?
faqs.answer: Form the view in June and confirm it in August. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached students on 20 August 2026, and Diploma teaching typically begins within weeks of that, which is a very narrow window for a consequential decision. Write down a provisional subject and level plan in June on the evidence of the mocks and the papers as sat, with reasons. Then treat results day as confirmation or a prompt to revise, rather than as the moment the whole decision gets made.

faqs.question: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation for my child?
faqs.answer: Decide on evidence rather than on which sounds more serious. Time a set of 0580 Extended algebraic manipulation questions. Accuracy with slow speed points towards Applications and Interpretation, or towards Standard Level Analysis and Approaches. Accuracy at reasonable speed plus real curiosity about why a method works points to Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, and a good result in Additional Mathematics 0606 is the strongest signal available. Then check whether any target degree specifies Analysis and Approaches by name, because some do.

faqs.question: Does Additional Mathematics 0606 matter if my child is going into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: It is the best single predictor of comfort in Analysis and Approaches, because it introduces calculus, logarithms and kinematics a year early and builds the algebraic speed the Diploma assumes. It is not a requirement, and plenty of students succeed without it. Where it was not taken, a summer block on differentiation, function transformations and logarithms closes most of the gap in six to ten sessions, which is a far cheaper intervention than catching up during a first Diploma term.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject leaves the widest gap into Higher Level science?
faqs.answer: Physics, and the gap is quantitative rather than topical. Uncertainty propagation and error analysis are assumed from the first weeks of a Diploma physics course and are barely touched at IGCSE, and they carry marks in the written papers and in the Internal Assessment alike. A student can arrive knowing all the physics content needed for the first term and still lose marks from week two because nobody showed them how to handle an error bar. Six focused summer sessions is unusually high-value work.

faqs.question: When should the Extended Essay topic be chosen?
faqs.answer: In the first Diploma year, while the calendar still has slack. The essay runs to a 4,000-word limit and the school sets staged draft deadlines that collide in the second year with science Internal Assessment write-ups, the Theory of Knowledge essay and oral components in language subjects. A student entering the second year with a narrowed research question, a working supervisor relationship and some reading behind them is in a different position from one entering it with a title and good intentions.

faqs.question: Is there anyone in Ras Al Khaimah who covers both IGCSE and the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Locally, very few, and that is the honest answer rather than a sales line. The emirate has a comparatively small private-school sector concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, so the number of people here who have taught a Diploma subject at Higher Level and can also diagnose an IGCSE script is small, and most are fully committed. Online one-to-one widens that pool to everyone who does it properly, which is why we teach here by live video rather than by visiting.

faqs.question: What does criterion-based marking change for my child?
faqs.answer: It makes the standard readable in advance, which is an advantage most students fail to take. A Diploma internal component is marked against lettered criteria with published maximum marks, so a student can know before writing what the finished piece has to demonstrate. The practical move is to read the criteria aloud and turn each one into a question the work must answer. Students who write first and check the criteria afterwards produce work that reads well and scores in the middle of the range.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of an Internal Assessment if time has run out?
faqs.answer: No, and the answer does not change with the deadline. A tutor may explain the criteria, question the method, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. Writing a section, rewriting prose, supplying data or editing to completion is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the person who helped. Any provider offering completed assessments is selling an expulsion risk dressed as a shortcut.

faqs.question: How does English change between IGCSE and the Diploma?
faqs.answer: It becomes a different discipline rather than a harder one. First Language English 0500 rewards fluent, well-organised writing and accurate reading. The Diploma's language courses reward argument about how texts work on readers, across literary and non-literary material, with an Individual Oral recorded in a school window and, at Higher Level, an essay with its own internal deadlines. A student who scored well at IGCSE by writing nicely has to learn to analyse, and that shift takes a term of fortnightly work rather than a fortnight.

faqs.question: Will the school change between Year 11 and Year 12 affect the handover?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and it is worth planning for in Year 10 rather than Year 11. Where a Ras Al Khaimah family moves from an IGCSE school to a school offering the Diploma, the two curricula sequence topics differently, so genuine content gaps appear that neither school considers its responsibility. A diagnostic session on the student's own IGCSE scripts will find them, and most are closeable in a summer. Ask any prospective school directly which programmes it is authorised to deliver and at which year groups.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does my child actually need for the Ministry file?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3 for the British track, plus one A Level at grade E or better, or two AS Levels at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, which is the detail that catches families late. One competitor page in this market states that six IGCSE subjects are required; the published rule is five. Ask your school which of your child's subjects are the accredited ones while option blocks can still change.

faqs.question: Can bridging sessions continue while we travel in the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and on this coast that is usually the deciding factor. Households here travel in exactly the weeks when bridging work is most valuable, so an arrangement that requires someone to arrive in person collapses the moment anyone leaves the emirate. A live video session runs from anywhere with a usable connection, which converts a fragmented ten weeks into a block that can actually be planned. Give us the travel dates when the plan is written and the sequence will be built around them.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Diploma subjects at Standard and Higher Level alongside Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE. The match is made on the component that is failing, because a weak Paper 1 and a weak practical component in the same subject are two different problems.

intro.heading: Which paper went wrong is the question worth answering
paragraphs: Al Mamourah is a city-area district of Ras Al Khaimah, close to Al Qusaidat and the creek, with secondary students travelling out to schools concentrated in Al Nakheel, Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab. That geography sets the evening window and nothing else. The question that decides whether tuition works is not where the tutor lives; it is which component of which paper is costing marks and whether anybody available has taught it.

Parents rarely arrive with that information, and it is not their job to. They arrive with a grade, a report comment, or a child who has gone quiet about one subject. The translation from there to a component is the first useful thing a tutor does, and it takes a marked script rather than a conversation. A script shows within minutes whether the student knows the content and loses the method mark, or knows the method and runs out of time, or knows both and answers a question that was not asked.

Those three problems look identical from outside and need entirely different work. Missing content takes weeks of teaching. Missing method lines take a fortnight of habit change. Answering the wrong command term takes three sessions and then applies to every subject the student sits. A tutor who starts from the subject name rather than the component spends the first month finding out which one it was, and in an exam year that month is the budget.

IB Gram matches on the syllabus code, the level or tier, and the failing component, then delivers the lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run in India only. In an emirate where a Higher Level or Extended-tier cohort can number a dozen students, matching on the component is only possible if the pool is national rather than local, which is the whole argument for the format.

The sections below are organised the way an examiner's report is: component weightings and durations, how the practical and investigation components differ across boards, the four English routes and what each assesses, the specific topics where marks go missing with the error named, what a raw mark converts into, the UAE mandatory subjects running alongside the international timetable, the market rates with their publishers named, the academic-honesty boundary, and an honest table of what we can and cannot cover in this emirate.

One caution on dates before the detail. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE centres and the February and March series belongs to India alone. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Diploma candidates at UAE schools sit the May session, and this page publishes no specific IB date, because the board's own site is the only authority and your child's coordinator is the person to confirm them with.
