This is the information a tutor needs before the first lesson, and it is the level of detail this market generally does not publish.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (DP)
subjects.description: Higher Level adds a third paper of extended problem solving that rewards persistence over recall. The recurring losses sit in proof by induction, complex numbers in polar form, and questions asking for justification where the student supplies an answer instead of a reason.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (DP)
subjects.description: Calculator-assumed throughout and statistics-heavy. Marks go missing on unrounded answers, missing units, and modelling questions treated as calculations when the mark scheme wants a comment on how well the model fits the data.

subjects.name: Chemistry (DP)
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the written papers. The scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each, and a design with no genuine independent variable range caps three of those four before any writing.

subjects.name: Physics (DP)
subjects.description: Uncertainty propagation is examinable, routinely under-taught and quick to teach, which makes it the highest-return topic in a short block. Paper 2 rewards rearranging the algebra before substituting numbers, which is a habit rather than a piece of knowledge.

subjects.name: Biology (DP)
subjects.description: The volume of content disguises the real failure, which is command-term discipline on six and eight-mark questions. A student who writes everything known about a process earns the two marks listed and nothing for the remaining page of writing.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Method marks decide the grade. Students who work mentally and write one line lose credit for a correct approach. Algebraic fractions, graph transformations and probability trees without replacement are the predictable losses in local mock scripts.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Potential dividers and series-parallel circuits are where the marks go. Cambridge's alternative-to-practical paper is learnable through a fixed vocabulary about repeats, precision and anomalous results, which makes it the fastest revision win in the subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic under time pressure and organic pathways. The qualitative analysis table is pure recall, worth reliable marks, and routinely skipped in revision because it feels less like chemistry than a calculation does.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Genetics crosses, osmosis write-ups and extended responses. The mark scheme accepts a short set of specific phrases, so teaching the scheme's language outperforms another pass through the textbook by a wide margin.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature (DP)
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen texts are assessed on analysis of how meaning is made rather than on what the text says. Students who summarise content score in the lowest bands regardless of how well they write.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The summary question carries a word ceiling and a content-point tally, so elegant paraphrase can remove the lifted detail the scheme requires. Reading precision rather than expression is the thing being measured.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the international curriculum under the federal rules, and assessed separately from it. Support here is about the school's own scheme and its assessment weightings rather than about an external paper, which makes it a different kind of tutoring brief.

sections.heading: Translating a grade into a component
paragraphs: This is the step that gets skipped, and skipping it is why so many families in Al Mamourah feel that six months of tuition changed nothing. A grade is an aggregate. It tells you the total and hides the shape, and the shape is the only part that can be acted on. Two students with the same overall mark can need entirely different work, and the report card cannot distinguish them.

The translation needs a marked script. From one paper, a tutor can see whether the student attempted every question, whether the working is written or implied, whether marks were lost late in the paper to timing, and whether answers match the command terms. Where the school can release component-level marks for a mock, better still: a strong Paper 1 against a weak Paper 2 is a specific diagnosis, not an impression.

The three failures and their timescales are worth stating plainly. Content gaps take weeks of teaching and respond slowly. Missing method lines take a fortnight of deliberate habit change and respond fast. Command-term errors take about three sessions and then transfer to every other subject the student sits, which makes them the best value work available in a short block. Most students have some of all three, in different proportions.

What a family can do before contacting anybody is collect the evidence: the most recent marked paper, the board and syllabus code from the entry confirmation, the level or tier, and the date of the next assessment. Four pieces of information, all obtainable in two messages to the school, and together they shorten the useful first session from a diagnosis into a plan.

sections.heading: Component weightings and durations, side by side
paragraphs: Parents are told a subject matters without being told how it divides, and the division is where revision time should be allocated. A component worth a third of the grade deserves a third of the preparation, and students routinely spend their effort on the component they find most interesting rather than the one carrying the most marks. The table below exists to make that allocation visible.

Read it as a planning tool rather than a reference. The pattern that matters is relative weight: which component is largest, which is most often neglected, and which rewards technique rather than content. Internal assessments across the Diploma sciences and mathematics carry a meaningful share of the grade and are entirely within the student's control months before any paper, which makes them the most reliable marks on the course.

Durations matter as much as weightings because they govern pacing practice. A student who has only ever done questions untimed has no sense of how long a six-mark answer may take, and discovers it in the hall. Timed practice at the real duration, not at a convenient shortened version, is the single piece of homework most often set and least often done properly.

Confirm any specific figure for your child's subject against the published assessment structure for their syllabus version, because boards revise these and a tutoring page is not where an exam plan should be sourced from. What the table gets right is the shape of the decision: allocate revision in proportion to the marks, not in proportion to comfort.

sections.heading: The experimental components, compared across boards
paragraphs: Science students lose a predictable share of marks in the components that describe practical work rather than in the ones that test theory, and the boards handle this differently enough that a tutor matched to the wrong one wastes the preparation. The content is not the issue; the format is. Each board rewards a particular way of writing about variables, uncertainty and anomalous results.

Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical paper in several sciences, which is highly learnable: the mark scheme accepts a defined vocabulary about controlling variables, repeating readings, improving precision and identifying anomalies, plus the ability to complete and read a results table. A student who learns that vocabulary and practises five past papers typically moves further on this component than on any other in the same time.

Pearson assesses practical skills within its written papers rather than through a separate alternative paper, which spreads the same skills across the course and makes them easier to overlook entirely. The Diploma takes a third approach: a single scientific investigation assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each, where the design decision made before any data is collected determines the ceiling on three of the four criteria.

The practical consequence for an Al Mamourah family is about timing. For Cambridge the work can be done in the final block, because it is paper technique. For Pearson it should be woven through the year. For the Diploma it has to happen before the experiment, which means the highest-value session on the component sits months before any draft exists and is the one nobody books.

sections.heading: The four English routes, and which assesses what
paragraphs: English is where Al Mamourah families most often discover that the subject on the timetable is not the subject being examined. A student can be in English as a Second Language, First Language English, Diploma English A Language and Literature, or Diploma English B, and those four assess different things. Confusing them produces tuition that works on the wrong skill with great diligence.

English as a Second Language measures reading precision and controlled writing. Its summary question has a word ceiling and a content-point tally, which means fluent paraphrase actively loses marks by removing the detail the scheme is looking for. First Language English measures control of register and response to a question about a text, where the commonest failure is answering the text rather than the question that was asked about it.

Diploma English A Language and Literature assesses analysis of how meaning is constructed, in unseen texts and in an individual oral built around a global issue. A student who summarises content, however elegantly, sits in the lowest bands. Diploma English B is a language-acquisition course and assesses comprehension and production rather than literary analysis, so the preparation looks almost nothing like English A's.

The practical instruction is short. Find out from the entry confirmation which of the four your child is actually sitting, then match the tutor to that, because a strong literature teacher is not automatically the right person for an English as a Second Language summary question and the reverse is equally true. This is the subject where the board-and-code discipline recommended throughout this page pays off most visibly.

sections.heading: Where marks actually go missing, topic by topic
paragraphs: Generic advice about revision is useless because the losses are specific and repeat across cohorts. The table below names the topic, the error, and the fix, drawn from the pattern that shows up again and again in marked scripts at this level. It is the kind of detail examiner reports contain and tutoring pages generally do not, and it is worth reading with a script in front of you.

The thing to notice is how many of the entries are habits rather than knowledge. Not writing the substitution line, not labelling an axis, not rounding at the end instead of mid-calculation, not reading the command term: none of those requires teaching new content, and all of them require somebody watching the student work and interrupting. That is precisely what a one-to-one session does and a class of twenty-four cannot.

The second thing to notice is that the fixes are cheap. Most are a single habit, practised deliberately for a fortnight until it stops needing thought. A student who adopts four of these across their subjects recovers a meaningful number of marks without learning anything new, which is why the first block of any plan here starts with a marked script rather than with a syllabus.

Use the table to check the plan you are being sold. If a tutor's proposal for a student losing method marks is a programme of content teaching, the proposal does not match the diagnosis. The questions to ask are which of these errors the script shows, and what the first fortnight is going to do about them.

sections.heading: What a raw mark actually converts into
paragraphs: Families read a mock percentage as though it were a grade, and it is not. Grade boundaries are set after each series by the awarding body, on that series' papers, and they move. A paper that was harder than usual produces lower boundaries; a paper that was easier produces higher ones. A school's mock boundary is an estimate based on previous series and should be read as a range rather than a line.

This matters in two practical ways. First, a student sitting two marks below an internal boundary is not necessarily two marks below the real one, which is why an enquiry about results exists as a route and why a decision about it should rest on the component pattern rather than on the disappointment. Second, chasing a percentage target can distract from the component shape that produces it.

This page publishes no boundary figures and no conversion tables, for a simple reason: grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, they are published by those boards for each series, and reproducing them here would be both a copyright matter and quickly out of date. The place to read them is the board's own site, and the person to interpret them for your child is the exams officer or Diploma coordinator.

What a tutor can do with a mark is more useful than converting it. Read the component split, identify which paper is dragging the aggregate, and target that. A student whose aggregate sits mid-range because one component is strong and another weak has a far better prospect over eight weeks than one whose marks are evenly mediocre, and the aggregate alone cannot tell you which you have.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic education and social studies alongside the timetable
paragraphs: This is one of the largest gaps in the UAE tutoring market and it affects every family on this page. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must otherwise adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those subjects therefore sit on top of the IGCSE or Diploma timetable rather than instead of any part of it.

The practical effect is arithmetic. A Year 11 student in Al Mamourah carrying nine IGCSE subjects plus the mandatory UAE subjects has a fuller week than their nine-subject entry suggests, and a revision plan that counts only the examined international subjects has quietly assumed hours that do not exist. Mapping the real week before planning sessions is a ten-minute job that prevents a term of over-commitment.

Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed version of these requirements, which is useful context even outside Dubai. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least twenty-five minutes. It requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Two further KHDA points are worth knowing because they bound what any tutor can honestly offer. Schools must ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. So support in these subjects means working with the school's own approved material and scheme, not supplying an alternative syllabus.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: The most useful thing about a published rate is not the number; it is whether you can check it. So this section is organised by verifiability. Every band below names the provider or survey that published it, which means you can open their page and see whether it still says what it said. Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in.

The bands, with their sources: budget online and university-student tutors from roughly AED 45-150, with one content platform publishing from AED 45-65 and one learning platform from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150-300, with one UAE agency publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with a UK agency quoting AED 270. Premium named tutors at AED 500-650, with one provider publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 including travel.

For monthly budgeting, surveys put a weekly hour at roughly AED 240-600 for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised monthly packages include online bundles from around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home bundles at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits. None of these figures is an IB Gram price, and nothing here is a quote.

The checks worth running on any quote are three. Does the rate come with a session length attached, since an hour and ninety minutes are different products. Does it come with a session count and a target, since an open-ended weekly slot is not a plan. And is there something you can see before paying, because a free trial lesson on your own material is evidence and a consultation call is a description.

sections.heading: The line on assessed work, and on official materials
paragraphs: A service in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price and ranks for searches a parent in Al Mamourah might run. So the boundary has to be printed rather than implied. A tutor explains the criteria, works through published exemplars, questions whether a design or a topic can carry the required depth, and reads the student's own draft to name the weak criterion. The student produces the work.

Nobody here writes, finishes or edits to completion an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any coursework. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under the board's rules and the penalty falls on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid. That is not a disclaimer; it is the reason the blocks on this page are built to finish two weeks before a school's internal deadline.

There is a parallel rule about materials that parents are rarely told. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. They are cited and linked here rather than reproduced or supplied, because redistributing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure as well. A service offering a mark-scheme bundle as a selling point is offering something it does not own.

The same caution covers examiner claims. Current examiner status is a specific thing that can either be evidenced or cannot, and it grants no access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or unseen paper content. A tutor who has taught a syllabus for years is worth hiring on that basis alone, and a tutor whose main selling point is proximity to the board deserves a direct question about what exactly is being claimed.

sections.heading: What we can and cannot cover in this emirate
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number. The honest version is more useful to a family in Al Mamourah than an implied promise of everything, so here it is as a table: which subjects match quickly, which take longer, and what happens when nobody suitable is available.

The pattern is predictable. Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English and economics match within a few days at both IGCSE and Diploma level. Less commonly taught subjects, Higher Level options with small national cohorts, and anything requiring a specific language of instruction take longer and sometimes cannot be matched at all in a given month. That is a supply fact rather than a policy.

What matters is what happens then. You are told, with a date or an alternative plan, rather than being matched to somebody adjacent to the subject. Six sessions spent discovering that a general science graduate has not taught Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level are six weeks that an exam-year student does not get back, and a clear no in week one is worth more than a comfortable yes.

One structural note to close on. Because delivery is online and one-to-one, the pool is national rather than local, which is precisely why the availability table below has anything in the quick column at all. A service promising in-home coverage across Ras Al Khaimah for these subjects would be promising something the local teaching supply cannot support, and that is the trade this page has been describing throughout.

process.title: Collect four pieces of information
process.description: The most recent marked paper, the board and syllabus code from the entry confirmation, the level or tier, and the date of the next assessment. Two messages to the school produce all four, and together they turn a first session from a diagnosis into a plan.

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: A weak Paper 2 and a stalled investigation design in the same subject need different people and different work. Tell us which component the marks are coming off, or send the script and let the tutor identify it before any teaching is proposed.

process.title: Free trial lesson on your own material
process.description: A real lesson rather than a sales call, run on a question your child got wrong. No payment and no card needed, and you are welcome to watch. What you are judging is how the tutor handles a student who is stuck, which is the part that repeats across every later session.

process.title: A plan matched to the diagnosis
process.description: Content gaps get teaching weeks; method habits get a fortnight of deliberate drilling; command-term errors get three sessions. You get the sequence in writing, with the component target named, so the plan can be checked against the diagnosis rather than taken on trust.

process.title: A marked paper as the measure
process.description: A diagnostic paper at the start and a comparable one six to eight sessions later, both marked against the published scheme, give component-level movement instead of an impression. On a core component the measure is the criterion band rather than a mark.

process.title: An honest coverage answer
process.description: For a Higher Level option with a small national cohort there may be nobody suitable free this month. You hear that, with a date or an alternative, rather than being placed with somebody adjacent. In an exam year a clear no in week one beats a comfortable yes.

whyPoints.title: The component is the unit of work
whyPoints.description: Matching happens on the failing paper or criterion rather than on the subject name. It is slower to arrange and measurably more effective, particularly in an emirate where a Higher Level teaching set can be a single person covering several courses.

whyPoints.title: Specific losses, named with their fixes
whyPoints.description: This page lists the actual errors that repeat in scripts at this level and roughly how long each takes to correct. Most are habits rather than knowledge, which is why one-to-one attention changes them and a class of twenty-four cannot.

whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic education and social studies sit alongside the international curriculum under federal rules, and a revision plan that ignores them has assumed hours that do not exist. No competitor page in this market treats them as part of the timetable.

faqs.question: Is there anyone in Al Mamourah who has actually taught my child's exact paper?
faqs.answer: Possibly not locally, and that is the honest answer. Ras Al Khaimah's private provision is concentrated in a few areas and a Higher Level or Extended-tier teaching set can be one person covering several courses. Because lessons here are delivered one-to-one over live video, the pool is national rather than local, so a tutor who has taught your child's specific component can be matched regardless of where they live. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run in India only.

faqs.question: Which four documents make the first Al Mamourah session productive?
faqs.answer: Four things, all obtainable in two messages to the school: the most recent marked paper, the board and syllabus code from the entry confirmation, the level or tier, and the date of the next assessment. The marked paper matters most, because it shows whether marks are being lost to missing content, to working done mentally without a written method line, or to answering a different question from the one asked. Those three need different plans and look identical from outside.

faqs.question: My child's percentage looks fine but the grade is poor. How?
faqs.answer: Because a percentage is an aggregate and a grade comes from boundaries that are set per series by the awarding body and genuinely move. A mock boundary is an estimate from earlier series rather than a rule. More usefully, an aggregate hides the component shape: a strong paper beside a weak one produces the same total as two mediocre papers and has a far better prospect over eight weeks. Ask the school for component-level marks rather than the overall figure.

faqs.question: Which component is usually the quickest to improve?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge sciences, the alternative-to-practical paper, by a clear margin. Its mark scheme accepts a defined vocabulary about controlling variables, repeating readings, improving precision and identifying anomalies, plus reading and completing a results table. Five past papers with the scheme open typically moves that component further than the same time spent on theory. Across all subjects, command-term discipline is next fastest, usually about three sessions, and it then transfers to every other paper the student sits.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory UAE subjects affect my child's revision time?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most plans ignore it. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside whatever international curriculum they are licensed for, so a nine-subject IGCSE student has a fuller week than nine subjects implies. Mapping the real week before planning sessions takes ten minutes and prevents a term of over-commitment. It also explains why an evening slot that looked free on paper keeps being cancelled in practice.

faqs.question: Can a tutor support Arabic or Islamic education for my child?
faqs.answer: Within limits that are worth knowing. Dubai's regulator requires schools to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, and states that for the mandatory subjects any different or additional content needs prior permission from the Ministry of Education. So honest support means working with the school's own approved scheme and assessment rather than supplying an alternative syllabus, and it is a different kind of brief from preparing an external examination paper.

faqs.question: How do I know which English course my child is actually sitting?
faqs.answer: From the entry confirmation, because the timetable usually shows the word English and nothing useful. There are four plausible courses: English as a Second Language, which measures reading precision and has a word-limited summary; First Language English, which measures register and answering the question about a text; Diploma English A, which assesses analysis of how meaning is made; and Diploma English B, a language-acquisition course. A tutor matched to the wrong one will work very diligently on the wrong skill.

faqs.question: Does the IB investigation really have to be designed before data collection?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the single most expensive thing families learn late. The scientific investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each, and a design with no genuine independent variable range caps three of those four criteria before any writing begins. So the highest-value session on the whole component sits weeks before any draft exists, and it is the session almost nobody books because nothing has visibly gone wrong yet.

faqs.question: Can you supply past papers and mark schemes for us to work from?
faqs.answer: We cite and link them rather than supplying them. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and redistributing them is a copyright matter; for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure as well. Your school's subject teacher or exams officer is the proper route to the material your child is entitled to use, and the boards publish a substantial amount openly on their own sites.

faqs.question: Why is a method mark worth worrying about?
faqs.answer: Because it is free credit a student is declining. On mathematics and physics papers the scheme awards marks for a correct approach even where the final answer is wrong, and a student who works mentally and writes one line forfeits all of it. Across a full paper that habit can cost a grade on its own. The fix is a fortnight of deliberate practice writing the substitution line every time, which requires somebody watching the student work and interrupting.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks enough if the losses are spread across every component?
faqs.answer: Spread evenly across components usually means content coverage, which is the slowest thing to fix, so eight weeks will move it less than it would move a technique problem. It is still worth doing, with the priority on the largest component and on timing, because running out of marks in the final quarter of a paper is recoverable quickly. What eight weeks cannot do is re-teach two years, and any plan claiming otherwise is selling hours rather than diagnosing.

faqs.question: What if nobody is available for a Higher Level option we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date or an alternative plan, rather than matched to somebody adjacent to the subject. Less commonly taught Higher Level options have small national cohorts and the specialists are correspondingly few. Six sessions spent discovering that a general graduate has not taught the course are six weeks an exam-year student does not recover, so a clear no in the first week is more valuable than a comfortable yes that unravels in the second month.

faqs.question: Does online delivery work for a student who needs somebody watching their working?
faqs.answer: It does, with one piece of setup: a document camera or a phone propped over the page so the tutor can see the paper as the student writes. That has to be asked for and arranged in the first session rather than discovered in the fourth. With it, the tutor sees the working line by line and can interrupt mid-calculation, which is the main thing a physically present tutor does and the one advantage worth engineering around.

faqs.question: Can one plan cover both my IGCSE child and my Diploma child?
faqs.answer: One approach, two plans. The diagnostic method is the same for both: get the marked script, translate the grade into a component, and match a specialist to that component. What differs is the calendar and the assessed-work element, because the Diploma child has internal deadlines for core components and the IGCSE child has an entry and a terminal paper. Siblings get separate tutors matched to their own codes, and running the sessions on consecutive slots keeps it to one committed evening.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether the component work is landing?
faqs.answer: By the component, not by the overall mark. If the plan targeted the alternative-to-practical paper, the measure is that paper's mark on a comparable past paper marked to the published scheme. If it targeted command terms, the measure is the long-answer marks across a mixed set of questions. An improvement in the aggregate with no movement in the targeted component means something else changed, and that is worth knowing rather than celebrating.

faqs.question: Is private tutoring in Ras Al Khaimah actually permitted?
faqs.answer: Yes, under a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the ministry has published no amounts, so any figure quoted to you is invented.

The trial lesson is free, runs on your child's own material, and you are welcome to watch it. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time, and if no specialist for your component is free this month we will tell you so.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level and Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE at both tiers. Matching is by syllabus code and component rather than by distance, which is the whole point of the arrangement for a family on the islands.

intro.heading: The radius problem, and what it actually costs a family here
paragraphs: A near-me search is a distance filter, and a distance filter is the wrong tool for this job. It sorts candidates by how far they live from your door, which is a fact about them and tells you nothing about whether they have taught Cambridge 0620 chemistry at Extended tier or marked a Higher Level mathematics exploration against criterion C. On an Al Marjan Island address the filter is unusually brutal: draw a ten-minute circle and it contains resort towers and apartments, no schools and very few teachers.

Widen the circle and the list grows, but so does the price. Every extra kilometre a tutor drives is unpaid time that returns to you as a higher hourly rate. The published UAE market makes the shape of this visible. A qualified subject teacher working online advertises around AED 150 to 300 an hour, as Unitors publishes for IGCSE and IB. Ask for an arrival at a door and the band becomes AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table for the country putting in-home one-to-one at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. You are paying more, from a smaller shortlist, for the same hour of teaching.

That is the argument this page is built on, and it is an argument about value rather than convenience. Specialist subject teachers are genuinely scarce in the northern emirates: the private-school set in Ras Al Khaimah is small and concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, so a family needing Higher Level physics or Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is not choosing between several local candidates. They are choosing between one, none, or somebody who teaches the subject one tier below the level required.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the distance filter entirely. Lessons for families here are one-to-one online tuition over live video, with a shared whiteboard, screen annotation and a recording afterwards. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; in-home visits are a service we run only in India, and we would rather say that in the fourth paragraph than bury it. What replaces the drive is choice: the tutor is selected because they have taught the exact specification your child sits, and their postcode never enters the decision.

The sections that follow are organised around money, because that is what this search cluster is really asking. What a radius buys and what it costs. Which subjects repay paid hours fastest and which do not. What we will tell you if nobody suitable is free, and what happens to the rate then. Who regulates your child's school and why that changes nothing about your tutoring choice but everything about your exam dates. And the equivalency rules that decide whether a set of certificates earned in this emirate opens a UAE university door.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.programmesIntro: Island households split across both of the programmes in this page's title, often inside the same family. The notes below are about what each programme costs in support hours and where that support has to be bought from, rather than a brochure description.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, three at Higher Level, plus the extended essay, theory of knowledge and creativity-activity-service. The support profile is long and shallow rather than short and steep: two years of steady work, with the heaviest demand falling on internal assessment feedback and on Higher Level paper technique in the second year.
programmes.countryNote: This is the level where a radius search fails hardest in the northern emirates. A Higher Level chemistry or mathematics teacher within twenty minutes of Al Marjan Island may simply not exist, and the local substitute is usually a graduate in the subject who has never taught the Diploma. Those are different products and they should not cost the same.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, which is why an MYP grade cannot be read like a percentage. Families often buy support here for the wrong reason, treating a 5 as a failure when it is a mid-band outcome, and under-buy in the year that actually decides the Diploma entry.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest useful money in this programme goes on the transition year. An MYP student moving into Higher Level mathematics or sciences needs algebraic fluency that the criteria do not test directly, and a term of work in the summer before the Diploma is worth more than the same spend in the first term of it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Single-subject courses with codes that decide everything about the match: 0580 and 0606 mathematics, 0625 physics, 0620 chemistry, 0610 biology, 0455 economics. Core and Extended tiers carry different grade ceilings, and the entry your school has made is the first thing a tutor should ask about.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in Ras Al Khaimah sit the June series, with November as the resit route. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after using the wrong zone's version, so dates come from the school's exams officer.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The second board in the emirate, with its own codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1 and, in some subjects, a modular route that lets a unit result be banked. That changes how support should be bought, because a modular entry has more than one deadline to work towards in a single year.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The published record is checkable: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson issues provisional timetables ahead of a series, so always work from the live official document.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.subjectsIntro: IB Diploma subjects first, with the honest note on how many paid hours each tends to need and why. Cost per grade moved varies enormously by subject, and no near-me list will tell you that.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The subject families over-buy and under-target. Higher Level marks concentrate in Paper 3's extended investigations and in proof technique; Standard Level losses are usually algebraic rather than conceptual. A diagnosis on two past papers locates almost all of it, which keeps the hours finite.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and the graphical calculator. Students lose marks to unjustified model choices and to writing conclusions that do not refer back to the context. That is a technique repair, not a content one, and it is among the cheapest grade movements available.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth that punishes shaky algebra, and the data-analysis questions reward a habit rather than knowledge. Pair it with mathematics under one tutor where possible, because the rearranging that fails in physics is usually failing in maths too.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the Higher Level grade, and the internal assessment is where families most often need feedback rather than teaching. Marks are lost in the evaluation section far more often than in the method.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Broad content with precise terminology requirements. The expensive error is buying content hours when the loss is in command-term reading: a student who explains when asked to evaluate will score in the middle band whatever they know.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation marks decide it, and the internal assessment commentaries need a tutor who will question a choice of article rather than suggest one. Higher Level adds quantitative work that catches students who chose the subject to avoid maths.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and Paper 1's unseen analysis are both teachable techniques with a short learning curve and a long practice tail. Buy fewer hours earlier and more marking later; the reverse is the common and expensive mistake.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus material is the whole grade. Students who learn more theory and score the same are losing application marks, and that pattern is visible in a single marked paper.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Study knowledge is necessary and insufficient: the marks sit in using a named study as evidence for a specific argument. One of the subjects where a local generalist and a specialist produce visibly different work.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the extended essay
subjects.description: Not taught so much as supervised, and the support is feedback on the student's own drafting. A tutor questions the research question, names what is unsupported and stops there; the writing belongs to the candidate and nobody else.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE side of the same household, where the cost arithmetic is different: narrower loss patterns, faster diagnosis, fewer hours to a grade.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: The most predictable repair in either programme. Algebraic manipulation, bearings, vectors and the structured longer questions account for most losses, and eight to twelve targeted sessions is a realistic estimate once a paper has been marked properly.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
igcseSubjects.description: Calculus and trigonometric identities with no Core safety net, taken by students heading for Higher Level Diploma mathematics. Few teachers in the northern emirates have taught it, which is precisely where a radius search returns nothing usable.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity costs more marks than any other topic and the alternative-to-practical paper is a separate skill. Expect roughly a third of the hours to go on experimental method rather than content.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
igcseSubjects.description: Mole calculations, ionic equations and qualitative analysis. Students who answer in words where symbols are required bleed marks steadily, and that is a cheap and quick correction.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing technique can be taught in a handful of sessions and then needs marked practice for a term. The money belongs at the back end of the year, not the front.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455)
igcseSubjects.description: A student who can define every term and still sits mid-band is losing the same evaluation marks every time. Several marked attempts fix it; more theory does not.

sections.heading: What a near-me radius buys, and what it costs you in choice
paragraphs: Start with what the search is doing. A near-me query sorts by distance, which is a proxy for convenience and a terrible proxy for competence. On an island with one causeway, convenience and competence point in opposite directions: the people who can reach you easily are the ones who live nearby, and the people who have taught your child's exact course are distributed across the whole country.

The table below sets out what each radius contains. It is not a measurement of a tutor register, because no such register is published for this emirate; it is the practical experience of matching families from these postcodes, and it is deliberately framed as what you give up rather than what you get. Inside twenty minutes you are choosing from a handful of generalists. Inside the emirate you have added some subject teachers and all of them are now quoting travel. Nationally, and online, the constraint disappears and the binding question becomes the evening slot rather than the map.

There is a version of the radius search that works, and it is worth saying so. A primary-age child who needs reading practice and a routine is well served by somebody local, patient and inexpensive, and the subject specialism hardly matters. The radius fails at the top end: Higher Level sciences, Additional Mathematics 0606, Diploma mathematics Paper 3, a first-language English grade stuck in the middle band. Those need somebody who has taught the component, and distance has nothing to do with whether they have.

sections.heading: Cost per grade moved: which subjects repay paid hours fastest
paragraphs: Families budget by subject and almost nobody prices by outcome, which is why two households spending the same amount get very different results. Some grades are cheap to move because the loss pattern is narrow and diagnosable; others are expensive because the thing being bought is judgement, and judgement needs repeated marked attempts rather than explanation.

Mathematics at either level is the clearest example of the cheap end. A student losing marks to algebraic manipulation and to the structure of longer questions can usually be diagnosed in one session and repaired in eight to twelve, because the failure repeats in an identifiable way. First-language English sits at the other end. Nothing is broken in a diagnosable sense; the student writes competently and scores in the middle band, and moving that requires several marked pieces with the same reader. The hours are not wasted, but they are not eight either.

The table is an estimate and says so. Any provider offering you a fixed number of hours to a fixed grade is selling something they cannot deliver, and a grade promise is the one claim we will not make on any page. What a range does is let you decide which subject to spend on first, which is the decision that actually determines whether the money worked. A family with one evening slot and three worries should put it where the loss pattern is narrowest, finish that subject, and then move the slot; the alternative, three subjects maintained at an hour a week each, produces thirty hours per subject across a year and closes none of them.

sections.heading: Coverage and the honest fallback when nobody suitable is free
paragraphs: No competitor in this search cluster discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-local delivery behind a foreign phone number. We would rather publish the limit. There are subject and level combinations where the roster is thin in any given term, and a family in Ras Al Khaimah asking for one of them deserves to know that before they clear an evening.

What happens in practice is one of three things. Either a specialist is available and you are matched within a few days; or the specialist is available at a different time and the question becomes whether your evening can move; or nobody who has taught that component is free, in which case we say so. The third answer is the one that matters, because the alternative, universal in this market, is to put a confident generalist in front of a Higher Level student and hope.

The table sets out where the roster is deep and where it is not. Treat it as a statement about availability rather than about quality: a generalist who is honest about having taught the subject at a lower level is often the right answer for a Standard Level student and the wrong answer for a Higher Level one. The rate does not change because a fallback applies; what changes is what we tell you the session can achieve. Published honestly, a thin month is also useful information for a family: it is the strongest possible argument for booking an autumn slot in a scarce subject rather than appearing in March and discovering that the only remaining option is somebody who has taught the course one level down.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it changes your dates
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools across the seven emirates, and almost nobody in this search cluster names more than one of them. Dubai sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by the UAE government's own information service as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate.

Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education here, and the same government source records that the Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in those three emirates. That is the complete map, and it is worth having because families moving within the country assume the Dubai rules travel with them.

None of this changes which tutor is right for your child. What it changes is your calendar and your paperwork: which authority approves the fee you are paying, which one your school answers to on curriculum and assessment, and which route you will use for attestation later. A tutoring page cannot do any of that for you, and a tutoring company claiming approval from any of these bodies is making a claim it cannot support. IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board approval and does not suggest otherwise.

sections.heading: Equivalency: the five subjects that decide a UAE university application
paragraphs: Certificates earned in Ras Al Khaimah have to be recognised before they open a UAE university door, and the rules for the British track are published and specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details catch families out. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which means a student counting them towards the total may be a subject short without knowing it. And the figure is five, not six: one ranking competitor in this market publishes six, and a family acting on that is being told to buy an unnecessary entry. For the American track the published requirements are different again, with English proficiency met by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB there is no number we will print. The source that sets out the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, and we will not publish one that has not been read on the Ministry of Education's own pages. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or speeds up. Describe it, check it with the authority, and treat any provider offering to handle it as a provider to be wary of.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic education and social studies alongside an international timetable
paragraphs: Families comparing tutoring quotes often leave these three subjects out of the budget entirely, and then discover in Year 10 that they carry real timetable weight. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why every emirate has a mandatory-subject requirement sitting on top of whatever international programme a school is licensed for.

Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed version, and it is instructive even for a Ras Al Khaimah family because it shows how seriously the requirement is treated. Arabic, Islamic education and social or moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic education and social studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and schools are advised that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes.

Two consequences follow for anyone buying support. First, the content is prescribed: using different or additional material without prior permission from the Ministry is not allowed, so a tutor working in these subjects supports the school's own programme rather than importing their own. Second, teachers of Islamic education and Arabic in Dubai schools must hold the regulator's own clearance to teach them, which is a concrete thing to ask about. Neither point is a reason to skip the subjects in a plan; both are reasons to ask a provider a specific question before paying.

sections.heading: The money questions nobody asks until the third term
paragraphs: By March the conversations change. Families who started in September with a general worry arrive with specific, slightly panicked questions, and they are almost always questions that would have been cheaper to ask in October. The commonest is whether to add a second or third subject eight weeks out. The answer is nearly always no: at that point the budget belongs on timed papers and marking in the subject already running, because adding a new diagnosis in April buys an incomplete repair in two places instead of a finished one in a single place.

The second is whether to keep paying after the papers are sat. There is no reason to, and a provider who does not tell you that is being paid for your inertia. We will say when a plan has finished. The third is what happens to the slot during the Holy Month, when evening routines invert and a four o'clock session becomes unworkable; sessions move to a post-Iftar time and the week usually gets lighter rather than heavier, which the plan should anticipate in advance rather than absorb as disruption.

The fourth question is the one worth asking first, in the trial lesson, about what happens if the tutor is wrong for your child. A fair answer names a process and a timescale, inside a fortnight, without buying the term again. A provider who cannot answer it has designed their pricing around you not asking, and on an island postcode where your alternatives are genuinely limited, that is the asymmetry most worth closing before you pay anybody.

sections.heading: Running a Diploma student and an IGCSE student in one household
paragraphs: A good proportion of island families are doing both at once, and the two programmes behave so differently that a single household budget usually gets allocated badly. IGCSE support is a sprint with a finite target: a diagnosable loss pattern, a known number of sessions, a paper in June. Diploma support is a two-year arrangement where the heaviest leverage sits in internal assessment feedback and in Higher Level paper technique, and where the core pieces have internal school deadlines rather than board exam dates.

The practical failure is predictable. The exam-year child absorbs the budget and the younger one loses their slot in February, which is exactly the term in which the IGCSE tier decision and the Diploma subject choices are being made. Protecting the younger slot through the older child's exam run costs less than reinstating it a year later, because a dropped routine is more expensive to rebuild than to maintain.

The table compares the two cost profiles honestly, including where each programme needs fewer hours than families expect. Diploma core supervision is the clearest example: fortnightly feedback on the student's own drafting, over several months, is a small number of sessions with a large effect, and it is the one place where buying more hours actively risks crossing a line that must not be crossed. The more time a paid adult spends with a draft that must be the candidate's own work, the harder it becomes to keep the help on the right side of the academic honesty rules, so the low session count is a feature of the design rather than a limit on the service.

sections.heading: What a trial lesson should prove before you spend anything
paragraphs: A free first session is standard across this market and it is used badly almost everywhere. Most providers treat it as a sales meeting with teaching attached: the tutor talks, the child nods, the parent is reassured, and nothing has been established. A trial should be a diagnosis, and you should finish it holding information you did not have an hour earlier.

The useful version is simple. Your child attempts real past-paper questions at the right tier while the tutor watches and says very little. The tutor then tells you three things: where the marks are being lost, what pattern connects the losses, and roughly how many sessions that implies. If they cannot do the third, they have not done the first. Insist on the subject and tier being correct before the session, because a Core-tier diagnosis on an Extended-tier candidate is worse than no diagnosis at all.

There is one condition worth stating plainly, because caution about the word free is well earned in this market. Our trial is a single lesson with the proposed tutor, before any payment and with no card details taken, and it exists so you can judge the teaching rather than the brochure. If the match is wrong you say so and nothing is owed. That is the whole offer, and anything a provider attaches to the word free that is not visible on the same screen as the word deserves a question.

One more thing a trial should settle, and it is the question island families are least likely to ask: what happens if the match is wrong in week three. Get a named process and a timescale before the first invoice rather than after it.

faqs.question: Why does an IB IGCSE tutor near me search return so little from Al Marjan Island?
faqs.answer: Because the island is residential and the mainland pool is small. There is no school campus on the fronds, so the nearest teacher is already a mainland teacher in Al Hamra, Al Nakheel or Khuzam. The private-school set in Ras Al Khaimah is concentrated in a few districts, and specialist Diploma and Extended-tier teachers are scarce locally in a way they simply are not in Dubai. A radius search is sorting a short list by distance; it is not telling you whether anyone on it has taught the specification your child sits.

faqs.question: Is a nearby generalist ever better than a distant specialist?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific job. A primary or lower-secondary child who needs routine, reading practice and someone patient is well served locally, and subject specialism barely matters. The radius fails at the top: Higher Level sciences, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Diploma mathematics Paper 3, a middle-band first-language English grade. Those need somebody who has taught that component and marked against its scheme, and whether they live twenty minutes away has no bearing on whether they have. Match the choice to the job rather than to the map.

faqs.question: What should we expect to pay for Higher Level Diploma support here?
faqs.answer: The published UAE market puts a qualified subject teacher online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, and specialist IB and IGCSE tutors at AED 200 to 450 or more on Bestimate's 2026 table, while TutorChase quotes AED 270. In-home delivery moves the band to AED 180 to 500. Those are other providers' figures read in October 2026 rather than ours. IB Gram discusses cost against a written plan after the trial lesson, which is the only point at which a number means anything.

faqs.question: How quickly can a specialist be matched for an island family?
faqs.answer: For IGCSE mathematics and the sciences, usually within a few days. For Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Higher Level Diploma mathematics or Higher Level sciences, allow a week or two, because the roster for those is moderate rather than deep in any given term. Theory of knowledge and extended essay supervision should be planned a term ahead and cannot sensibly be arranged in April. If nobody who has taught the component is free, we say so rather than offering a substitute without naming the substitution.

faqs.question: Do you ever tell a family you cannot help?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the part of this page most worth checking against competitors. If a Higher Level psychology or economics request arrives at peak season and no tutor on the roster has taught that course, the honest answer is no rather than a confident generalist. Placing one costs a family a term and then the money again. No provider in the researched UAE market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several hide non-local delivery behind a foreign phone number, which is the same problem wearing a better suit.

faqs.question: Which regulator approves our school in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: The emirate's own Department of Knowledge, which the UAE government's information service describes as regulating private education here. The same source records that the Ras Al Khaimah authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so more than inspection sits with it. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah to its Private Education Authority, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold any approval from a regulator or an exam board?
faqs.answer: No. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any UAE education regulator, from the IB, from Cambridge or from Pearson, and we have no office or centre in the country. We name those bodies on these pages to explain what they govern and where to verify something, which is a different thing entirely. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai would need an educational services permit for a training institute, and describing yourself as approved without holding one is the most dangerous claim in this market.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does our daughter need for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or better, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, which is where families most often come up short without realising. The number is five and not six, despite a ranking competitor publishing six. Check your own case against the Ministry of Education's current guidance, because this is a regulatory process no tutoring company performs or speeds up.

faqs.question: Is there a points figure for IB equivalency we should be working towards?
faqs.answer: Not one we will publish. The sourced guidance we can cite sets out the British and American tracks in detail and states no IB points threshold at all, so any number you see on a tutoring page for that has come from somewhere unverifiable. Ask your school's IB coordinator and check the Ministry of Education's own pages. The same caution applies to IB exam and results dates: the IB's site blocks automated checking, so nothing on this page states a Diploma session date, and your coordinator is the only reliable source for yours.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both our Diploma child and our IGCSE child?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and usually not. A Higher Level chemistry teacher can certainly handle Cambridge 0620 Extended, so where the subjects line up it works and saves a scheduling conversation. Where they do not, two children get half a tutor each. The bigger saving in a two-programme household comes from protecting the younger child's slot through the older one's exam run, because February is exactly when the IGCSE tier decision and the Diploma subject choices are made, and a dropped routine costs more to rebuild than to keep.

faqs.question: Do we need to budget for Arabic and Islamic education as well?
faqs.answer: Many families should, and most leave it out of the plan. Private schools in the UAE must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum under the federal rules, and in Dubai the regulator sets out separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups, prescribed content, and instructional time counted in forty-minute units. Support in these subjects means working with the school's own programme rather than importing other material, because using different or additional content without ministry permission is not allowed.

faqs.question: What does the trial lesson actually have to produce?
faqs.answer: Three things, in writing. Where marks are being lost, the pattern connecting those losses, and an estimated number of sessions to close them. If a tutor cannot give you the third, they have not really done the first. Your child should be working for most of the hour on real past-paper questions at the correct tier rather than listening to an introduction. It is one free session with the proposed tutor, taken before any payment and with no card details, and nothing is owed if the match is wrong.

faqs.question: Should we add a second subject in the last eight weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Eight weeks out, a new subject means a new diagnosis, and a diagnosis that lands in May leaves no time to act on it. The money does more in the subject already running, switched from teaching to timed papers and marking against the official scheme. The exception is where two subjects share a skill that is failing in both, such as graph work or significant figures, in which case one tutor can drill it once and both grades move without a second arrangement being bought.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during the Holy Month in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Evening routines invert, so a four o'clock slot becomes unworkable and a post-Iftar slot becomes the obvious one. Because lessons are delivered over live video there is no travel to reorganise, and the move is a change of time rather than a change of arrangement. The sensible plan also gets lighter rather than heavier for those weeks, with one session instead of two and marked work set across a longer gap. Agree that shape in advance rather than letting it happen as disruption.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the extended essay without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is firm. A supervisor or tutor may interrogate a research question, point out that an argument is unsupported, show how a source should be handled and name what is weak in a draft the student wrote. No tutor may write a student's extended essay, draft their internal assessment or edit a piece to completion, because submitted work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student. Any provider offering finished coursework is selling a risk, not a service.

intro.heading: Al Nakheel is near the schools. That is not the same as near a tutor.
paragraphs: Al Nakheel is the working centre of Ras Al Khaimah: the commercial district, the malls, and most of the emirate's private schooling within a short drive. A family here genuinely does start from a better position than one on Al Marjan Island or in Al Jazirah Al Hamra. School runs are shorter, group classes are at least conceivable, and more teachers live within reach. On paper this is the one neighbourhood in the emirate where the local answer should work.

In practice it rarely does, for a reason that is obvious once stated and almost never stated. Being near the supply of teachers is not the same as having access to it. The teachers who live near Al Nakheel work in the schools near Al Nakheel, and the small number of them with Higher Level or Extended-tier examination experience are the first people every other family in the district approached. Proximity to a fully committed resource is not availability.

So the useful question for a family here is not where but what. There are six distinct ways to buy tutoring in this market and they differ far more from each other than any two neighbourhoods do: a specialist agency, an international marketplace, an independent freelance tutor, a tuition centre running group classes, support through the school itself, and online one-to-one. Each has a characteristic rate, a characteristic failure mode, and a type of family it suits. Almost nobody lays them side by side, because every provider compares itself to an unnamed alternative that happens to look worse. A family who picks the right model for the right problem usually spends less than one who picks the right brand for the wrong model.

This page lays them out. The comparison is at the level of model rather than brand, with rates quoted only where a provider has published them and attributed accordingly, read in October 2026. Where a model has a real advantage over online one-to-one, that is stated: tuition centres are cheaper per hour, school support is often included in fees already paid, and an in-home freelance tutor provides a physical presence that no screen does. Those are not throwaway concessions; they are the cases where we would tell a family to spend their money elsewhere.

And the delivery position, since the URL says tutor near me: IB Gram teaches Al Nakheel students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; in-person visiting is a service we run only in India. The argument this page makes is not that online beats everything. It is that in a small emirate the binding constraint is subject-specific teaching experience, which is the one thing the local models cannot reliably supply and the online model can.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.programmesIntro: A family in Al Nakheel often has a genuine choice of route as well as of provider, because both the British and the IB systems are represented in the emirate. These are the four programmes in play.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal assessment in most subjects, with syllabus codes that determine past-paper selection: Cambridge 0580, 0620, 0625, 0610, 0500, or Pearson 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. Tiered Cambridge subjects fix a grade ceiling at entry. UAE candidates sit June and November; Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only and is irrelevant here.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm your school's Cambridge timetable zone: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed against descriptors A to D, with a Personal Project in the final year. Tuition-centre group classes serve this programme poorly, because criterion-based work is individual by design and a group class defaults to content delivery. One-to-one feedback on the student's own work is the format that matches the assessment.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nakheel families sometimes move a child between a Middle Years setting and an IGCSE one mid-school. The two sequence topics differently, so genuine content gaps appear in maths and science, and neither school treats them as its responsibility.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three at Higher Level, scored out of 45, each with written papers and an internally assessed component marked against lettered criteria, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay at a 4,000-word limit and Creativity, Activity, Service. The internal components are where the grade is quietly decided.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session with November available where offered. No specific IB examination or results date appears here, since the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically; the coordinator's internal deadline sheet is the calendar that matters.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The British-route alternative to the Diploma for Years 12 and 13: three or four subjects in depth, examined terminally, with no equivalent of the Diploma core. It suits a student with clear subject strengths and no appetite for breadth. Entry assumes IGCSE Extended-tier fluency rather than Core.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track expects five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at grade E or better or two AS Levels at the same grade.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.subjectsIntro: Across both systems, these are the subjects Al Nakheel families ask about, with a note on which provider model tends to serve each one best.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Serves adequately in a well-composed group class, because the content is sequential and common errors are shared. It serves badly in a mixed-tier group, which is what small-market centres usually assemble. One-to-one wins where the problem is a specific gap rather than general practice.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Too few candidates in a small emirate for a viable group class, so this is a one-to-one subject by default. Calculus, logarithms and kinematics arrive quickly and a student who is behind on 0580 algebra cannot be carried by a group pace.

subjects.name: Physics, both systems
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended; Diploma HL and SL
subjects.description: The IGCSE written practical paper rewards precise method description and is highly coachable in six sessions, group or individual. Diploma uncertainty handling is individual work, because it has to be practised on the student's own data and corrected line by line.

subjects.name: Chemistry, both systems
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended; Diploma HL and SL
subjects.description: Qualitative analysis recall suits a group; mole arithmetic suits one-to-one, because the error is individual and needs catching in the working. Diploma investigation design is unambiguously one-to-one, as the research question belongs to one student.

subjects.name: Biology, both systems
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended; Diploma HL and SL
subjects.description: The most group-friendly science, because the losses are terminological and shared across a cohort. A well-run group class drilling mark-scheme wording is good value here, and it is the one place in this market where paying less per hour costs little.

subjects.name: English, both systems
subjects.description: Improves only on individual feedback, because the product being assessed is the student's own writing. Group classes can teach structure and technique but cannot mark twelve pieces of writing properly in an hour, which is the activity that actually moves the grade.

subjects.name: Economics (IGCSE 0455 and Diploma)
subjects.levels: IGCSE single tier; Diploma HL and SL
subjects.description: Diagram work is well suited to a group, where seeing six wrong diagrams corrected teaches more than one. Evaluation writing needs individual marking. A split arrangement often makes sense here and rarely gets suggested.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level is the thinnest local supply in the emirate, which decides the model for you: there is no viable group and few freelance options, so an online specialist is usually the only arrangement that reaches the right level of experience.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling, with legitimate use of technology. Interpretation is the recurring loss and it needs individual correction, since the error is a sentence not written rather than a calculation not performed.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
