sections.heading: Being close to the schools, and what it does and does not buy
paragraphs: Living in Al Nakheel confers three real advantages and one illusion. The advantages are short school runs, which protect the early-evening study window; access to a tuition centre on a weekday, which is simply not available to a family on Al Marjan Island; and the presence of more teachers in the surrounding residential streets than anywhere else in the emirate. Those are not trivial and this page is not going to pretend otherwise.

The illusion is that the third advantage converts into availability. The teachers near Al Nakheel teach in the schools near Al Nakheel, and the subset with Higher Level or Extended-tier examination experience is small and was approached first by the families closest to them. A fully committed resource nearby is worth less than an available resource further away, and that is the whole of the comparison this page makes.

The second thing proximity does not change is group viability at the level that matters. A centre can fill a class in IGCSE Biology, because many students take it and the losses are shared. It cannot fill a class in Additional Mathematics 0606 or Diploma Higher Level Chemistry, because there are not enough candidates at one level in one emirate at one hour. So centres in small markets either run mixed-tier groups, which are pitched at nobody, or they decline the subject and offer something adjacent.

The table below sets out the comparison by neighbourhood in the terms that actually matter for choosing a model: what is in reach, whether a group class is viable, and what the evening looks like. Read the final column and the pattern of the whole emirate appears. Al Nakheel has the most options and the same shortage; everywhere else has fewer options and the same shortage.

sections.heading: Six ways to buy tutoring here, side by side
paragraphs: Every provider in this market compares itself favourably with an unnamed alternative. A neutral comparison at model level is more useful and is what follows. The rates are only those a provider has actually published, attributed to that provider and read in October 2026: EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 at the budget online tier, Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, Bestimate's table at AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one and AED 200-450 and above for specialists, and BartyED at AED 650 for examiner-led work.

Read the table by column rather than by row. The replacement-policy column is the one families never ask about and most regret: what happens when a tutor leaves mid-term, which in a freelance arrangement means starting again and in an agency or platform arrangement means a named successor. The permit column matters because the MoHRE private tuition work permit is free and takes two working days, so there is no legitimate reason for an individual not to hold one.

The honest advantages of the non-online models deserve stating. A tuition centre is cheaper per hour and gives a student peers to compare themselves with. School support may already be covered by fees you have paid. An independent in-home tutor provides a physical presence, which genuinely matters for younger children and for some access needs. An international marketplace offers breadth of choice at the cost of any local knowledge at all.

The disadvantage they share in this emirate is the one this page keeps returning to. None of them reliably supplies a person who has taught your child's exact syllabus at your child's exact level to an examination class, because in a market this size that person may not be in it. Online one-to-one does not solve every problem. It solves that one.

sections.heading: Group classes and tuition centres: when they genuinely work
paragraphs: A good group class is an underrated thing and the small-market problem is composition rather than quality. Where eight students are at the same tier in the same subject with the same board, a group class is better value than one-to-one for certain activities: drilling mark-scheme wording, correcting economics diagrams, working through shared misconceptions where seeing six wrong answers teaches more than seeing one. It also gives a student a realistic sense of where they stand, which an isolated one-to-one arrangement does not.

The failure mode is predictable and it is structural. A centre in a small emirate cannot fill eight seats in Additional Mathematics 0606, so it combines tiers, or boards, or year groups. The resulting class is pitched at the middle of a range that does not exist, and the Core student is lost while the Extended student is bored. Nobody is dishonest in this process; the arithmetic simply does not support the class, and the family discovers it in week three.

So the question to ask a centre is narrow and it is not about quality. How many students are in the class, what tier are they, which board, and what year group. A straight answer to those four tells you whether the class will work. Vagueness tells you the composition is the problem, and a centre that will not answer is answering.

There is also a hybrid that almost nobody suggests because no single provider benefits from it. Take the group class for the drill work and buy a smaller amount of one-to-one for the marking-intensive parts: English writing, extended-response evaluation, an investigation question. The total cost is below full weekly one-to-one and the outcome is usually better than either alone, because each format is doing what it is good at.

sections.heading: The school's own support, and the line nobody should cross
paragraphs: The cheapest option in this market is frequently one a family has already paid for. Most schools run some form of additional support: catch-up sessions, revision clubs, departmental clinics, structured intervention for students below target. It is delivered by people who know the scheme of work, the entry tier and the student, and for recently taught content it is often better than anything bought externally.

Its limits are equally clear. It is scheduled to suit the school, not the family. It is usually group-based. It covers what the department has resourced rather than what one student needs, and it cannot give the sustained individual attention an investigation question or a piece of writing requires. And it is available only while a student is at that school, which matters in a transient population.

Then there is the line. Hiring your child's own classroom teacher privately is the arrangement families in small markets drift towards, because the teacher is known, available and already familiar with the child. It should be declined. In Abu Dhabi the education department's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Those rules are reported for specific contexts and should be verified against current policy, but the principle generalises: nobody should be paid privately by a family whose child they also assess.

The practical implication for Al Nakheel is to use the school support that exists, ask the department what it offers before buying anything, and then buy externally only for the things school support structurally cannot do: individual marking of the student's own written work, component coaching, and subject expertise at a level the school's timetable cannot spare.

sections.heading: What the money actually buys in each model
paragraphs: Start with the comparison families actually experience, which is monthly. Bestimate's published monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240-600 at the budget tier, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Market packages seen in the UAE sit inside that: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. The second figure is roughly double the first for half as many contacts.

Translate that into the models. The group class is the cheapest per contact hour and buys shared drill. School support is often already paid for and buys content catch-up. A freelance in-home tutor at AED 180-350, or up to AED 500 at the top of the independent market, buys presence and a known local person. An online qualified subject tutor at roughly AED 150-300 buys the specific syllabus and level. An examiner-led specialist at AED 500-650 and above buys narrow, late-stage expertise, and is wasted on a student whose problem is command terms.

The mistake that costs most in this market is not picking the wrong tier. It is picking any tier before the diagnosis. A family that buys forty hours at AED 200 for a problem that was two sessions of mark-scheme work has spent a substantial sum on the wrong thing, and no provider in the chain had an incentive to say so. Ten minutes with a marked script, before any money moves, is the single highest-return action available.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page, and no price in a currency Ras Al Khaimah families do not transact in. Of the main pages competing for these searches, three publish no AED figure at all, two quote US dollars, and one declines to answer its own pricing question in its own FAQ. Our position is a free trial lesson, then a plan with a target and an end date, then a quote against that plan.

sections.heading: Two routes through Years 12 and 13, compared
paragraphs: Al Nakheel families more often than most have a real choice between the IB Diploma and the British A Level route, because both are represented in the emirate and the commute differences are small. That choice is made at the end of Year 11 and it is harder to reverse than the tutoring decision, so it deserves more than a prospectus comparison.

The Diploma is a breadth qualification with a core. Six subjects, three usually at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay at a 4,000-word limit and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored out of 45. It suits students who are broadly strong, who manage their own deadlines reasonably well, and who want to keep options open. Its characteristic difficulty is load distribution: internal components in six subjects landing alongside the core.

The A Level route is a depth qualification. Three or four subjects examined terminally, no core, no internally assessed components in most subjects. It suits students with clear strengths and a definite direction, and students who perform better in examinations than in sustained independent work. Its characteristic risk is narrowness: dropping a subject at sixteen that a degree course later requires.

The table compares them on the dimensions that matter for a decision, and the row most families skip is the last. Neither route is harder in general; they are harder in different ways, and the right question is which kind of difficulty suits this particular student. A diagnostic conversation with a teacher who has taught both is worth more than any amount of reading, which is also an argument for having somebody independent in the room.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same on every street
paragraphs: The brief for this page was to compare Al Nakheel with the neighbourhood next door and explain why the answer is the same either way. Having done the comparison properly, here is the conclusion. Al Nakheel genuinely has more options: shorter school runs, realistic centre attendance, more teachers nearby. Those options change what a family can conveniently buy. They do not change what is scarce.

What is scarce across the whole emirate is subject-specific examination experience at the top levels. A Higher Level Chemistry teacher who has taken a cohort through to a session, or an Extended-tier physics specialist who knows what the written practical paper pays for, is a small category in a small market, and living closer to the city centre does not create more of them. It only means you are competing for the same few people with more neighbours.

That is why the recommendation is identical for a family in Al Nakheel, in Al Hamra Village and in Al Mamourah. Use the school support you have already paid for. Use a group class where its composition is genuinely right, which means asking about tier, board and year group before enrolling. And for the things that need a specific syllabus at a specific level, or individual marking of the student's own work, buy one-to-one from whoever actually teaches it, which in this emirate usually means buying it online.

The one difference worth acting on is a timing one. Al Nakheel students tend to get home earlier, which means they can take a mid-afternoon session slot. Earlier slots are less contested than evening ones, which genuinely widens the pool of available tutors. It is a small advantage and it is the only one in this comparison that translates directly into access rather than convenience.

process.title: Ask the school what it already provides
process.description: Before buying anything, ask the department what support exists, when it runs and who delivers it. It is often included in fees already paid and is well suited to catching up on recently taught content. Buy externally for what it structurally cannot do.

process.title: Diagnose from a marked script, not from a conversation
process.description: Ten minutes with the actual paper shows whether the problem is content, technique, pacing or command terms. Those four need different work at different prices, and buying before the diagnosis is the most expensive habit in this market.

process.title: Choose the model, then the provider
process.description: Group drill, school support, in-home presence or online specialism solve different problems. Decide which problem you have first. A provider asked to recommend a model will recommend their own; the table on this page is there so you do not have to ask them.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a plan with an end date
process.description: One 45 to 60-minute one-to-one session over live video, no card details, no obligation. What follows should name the target, the number of sessions and how you will know it worked. If it names none of those, it is a standing order rather than a plan.

process.title: Review against marked evidence and change early
process.description: At the end of a block, compare marked work from the start and the finish against the written target. If nothing moved, change the plan or the tutor at week three rather than week twelve. In a small market, the relationship survives that conversation better than the alternative.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Al Nakheel better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and for some activities it is also better teaching: drilling mark-scheme wording, correcting economics diagrams, working through misconceptions where seeing six wrong answers teaches more than one. The question to ask is about composition, not quality. How many students are in the class, which tier, which board, which year group. In a small emirate a centre often cannot fill a class at one tier, so it combines them, and a mixed-tier group is pitched at nobody.

faqs.question: Does living near the schools in Al Nakheel make tutors easier to find?
faqs.answer: It makes convenient options easier to find and does not change what is scarce. The teachers near Al Nakheel work in the schools near Al Nakheel, and the small number with Higher Level or Extended-tier examination experience were approached first by the families nearest them. A fully committed resource nearby is worth less than an available one further away. The one real advantage is timing: students here get home earlier, and earlier session slots are less contested, which genuinely widens the available pool.

faqs.question: What support should we expect from the school before paying for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Ask the department directly what exists: catch-up sessions, revision clubs, subject clinics, structured intervention for students below target. It is delivered by people who know the scheme of work, the entry tier and your child, and for recently taught content it is often better than anything bought externally. Its limits are that it is scheduled for the school, usually group-based, and cannot give sustained individual attention to one student's writing or investigation. Use it first, then buy for what it cannot do.

faqs.question: Can we hire a teacher from our own school privately?
faqs.answer: It should be declined. In Abu Dhabi the education department's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Those are reported for specific contexts and should be checked against current policy, but the principle generalises: nobody who assesses your child should also be paid privately by you. Hire somebody unconnected to the school.

faqs.question: Which is cheapest overall for a family in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Usually a combination rather than any single model. School support costs nothing extra because fees already cover it. A well-composed group class is the cheapest paid hour. One-to-one is bought only for the marking-intensive work: English writing, extended-response evaluation, an investigation question. That split typically costs less than full weekly one-to-one and works better than either alone, and nobody suggests it because no single provider benefits from the arrangement.

faqs.question: What does a replacement policy mean and why should I care?
faqs.answer: It is what happens when a tutor leaves mid-term, which in a transient population happens often. With an independent freelance tutor the answer is usually nothing: you start the search again, mid-year, having lost the continuity that made the arrangement work. With an agency or a platform there should be a named successor with a handover, agreed with you rather than announced to you. It is the question families never ask at the start and most frequently regret not asking.

faqs.question: Should my child take the IB Diploma or A Levels?
faqs.answer: Decide from marks and habits rather than ambition. The Diploma is six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored out of 45, with internally assessed components in every subject; it suits broadly strong students who manage their own deadlines. The A Level route is three or four subjects examined terminally with little internal assessment; it suits clear subject strengths and strong examination performers. Check the requirements of any likely degree course before the decision, because narrowing early can close doors.

faqs.question: Why do some tutors charge AED 650 an hour?
faqs.answer: The top of the published market is examiner-led or named-specialist work: BartyED publishes AED 650, and Bestimate's specialist band reaches AED 450 and above. Whether it is worth it depends entirely on the problem. For narrow, late-stage work with a student whose understanding is already strong, that expertise can matter. For a student losing marks to command terms and omitted working, it is an expensive way to fix something a qualified subject tutor at AED 150-300 fixes just as well. Diagnose before choosing a tier.

faqs.question: Are international tutoring marketplaces worth using from Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: They offer the widest choice, particularly for unusual subjects, and that is a real advantage in a small market. The costs are that rates are often quoted in US dollars rather than dirhams, local knowledge is usually absent, permits are rarely checked, and replacement means browsing listings again yourself. Of the pages researched for these UAE searches, one marketplace page contained no AED figure, no UAE school name, no neighbourhood and no reference to any local regulator at all.

faqs.question: How do I know whether a group class will suit my child's level?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions before enrolling and expect direct answers: how many students, what tier, which exam board, which year group. If those answers are specific and match your child, the class will probably work. If they are vague, the composition is the problem and the class will drift to the middle of a range your child is not in. A centre that will not answer those four questions has answered them. It costs nothing to ask and it saves a term.

faqs.question: Does an in-home tutor have advantages over online for a family here?
faqs.answer: Yes, genuinely, in specific cases. A physical presence matters for younger children, for students who need an adult actively managing attention, and for some access needs. It also suits families who have tried online and found it did not hold the student. What it costs in this emirate is subject precision: published in-home rates run roughly AED 180-500, and the pool willing to visit is the local pool, which at Higher Level and Extended tier is small. The trade is presence against specialism.

faqs.question: What is the first thing we should spend money on?
faqs.answer: Nothing, until a marked script has been read. Ten minutes with the actual paper distinguishes a content gap from a technique habit, a pacing problem from a command-term problem, and those four need different work at different prices. The commonest waste in this market is buying a tier of service before anyone has established what is wrong, which is how a family ends up with forty hours of general support for a problem that was two sessions of mark-scheme work.

faqs.question: Can sessions fit around the Al Nakheel school day?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the timing here is better than elsewhere in the emirate. Short school runs mean many students are home by mid-afternoon, which makes a 3.30pm or 4pm start workable, and those slots are less contested than evening ones. Later sessions to around 9pm suit households with a commuting parent who wants to be present. During Ramadan sessions move after Iftar and shorten to around 45 minutes, which protects concentration better than holding the usual slot.

faqs.question: Which exam series will a Ras Al Khaimah candidate sit?
faqs.answer: June and November for IGCSE, with Pearson International GCSE in May/June and November. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so no candidate here sits it, and revision planners written to that calendar belong to a different country. For the Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session with November available where a school offers it. Also confirm your centre's Cambridge timetable zone with the school, since each of the six zones has its own version of the timetable.

intro.heading: Near me is the wrong question; which paper is the right one
paragraphs: Al Qusaidat is a short drive from Julphar and the older Ras Al Khaimah city grid, and the private schools serving it sit mostly in Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab. That geography produces a specific problem. The emirate's private-school set is small, so a cohort sitting Physics 0625 Extended or Diploma Chemistry Higher Level might number a dozen students, taught by somebody also carrying two other sciences. The teaching is often good. The specialism is thin, by arithmetic rather than by anybody's fault.

Which is why a search for a tutor near me is a reasonable instinct and a poor filter. Distance tells you nothing about whether the person has worked the 0620 qualitative analysis table or the Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3. Those are the questions that decide whether a term of tuition moves a grade. Ras Al Khaimah families who filter by proximity first and syllabus second end up with a general science graduate for a specific paper problem.

IB Gram matches on the syllabus code, the tier or level, and the component that is weak, then delivers the lesson one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run in India only. A family in Al Qusaidat gets whoever has taught the paper, not whoever can reach the roundabout by six. That is the entire trade being offered and it is worth stating in those terms.

This page is built as syllabus content rather than as an argument about delivery. It covers the IGCSE to Diploma bridge subject by subject, the Mathematics route choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, the command terms that quietly decide long-answer marks, the Internal Assessment criteria with their letters and mark allocations, and the word and page limits across assessed components. Those are the five things Ras Al Khaimah parents ask about once the panic about finding somebody local has passed.

One piece of advice before the detail. Bring the marked script. Not the report card, not the predicted grade, not a description of which topics feel difficult, but the actual mock paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it. A marked script shows within five minutes whether a student is losing marks to missing content, to writing answers mentally and skipping the method line, or to answering a question that was not asked. Those three problems look identical in a parent evening conversation and need completely different plans. Every section below is more useful with a script in front of you, and the first thing a good tutor will ask for is the same document.

Ras Al Khaimah also deserves one specific caution about exam dates. Cambridge runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level papers in a June series and a November series for centres here, and the February and March series it offers belongs to India alone. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Diploma candidates at UAE schools sit the May session, and this page deliberately publishes no specific IB date, because the board's own site is the only place those should be read and your child's Diploma coordinator is the person who confirms them.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.subjectsIntro: Each note below names the component where Ras Al Khaimah scripts actually lose marks, with the syllabus code attached. This is the list a tutor needs before a first lesson, and it is more useful than a subject menu.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (DP)
subjects.description: Higher Level sits three papers plus the exploration, and Paper 3 is the extended problem-solving component that most students meet for the first time in a mock. Losses cluster in proof by induction, complex numbers in polar form, and the moment a question asks for justification rather than an answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (DP)
subjects.description: Technology-rich and statistics-heavy, with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout. Students lose marks by giving an unrounded answer, omitting units, or treating a modelling question as a calculation question rather than one requiring a comment on the model's fit.

subjects.name: Chemistry (DP)
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the paper. The scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each, and the commonest failure is an investigation with no genuine independent variable range.

subjects.name: Physics (DP)
subjects.description: Paper 1 multiple choice punishes imprecise definitions and Paper 2 rewards algebraic rearrangement before substitution. Uncertainty propagation is examinable, routinely under-taught, and the fastest marks on the whole syllabus for a student who learns the three rules.

subjects.name: Biology (DP)
subjects.description: The volume of content hides the real issue, which is command-term discipline in six and eight-mark questions. A student who writes everything known about a topic scores the two marks the mark scheme lists and nothing for the rest of the page.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Method marks are the whole game. Students who work mentally and write a single line lose the credit for the correct approach. Algebraic fractions, graph transformations and non-replacement probability trees are where the predictable losses sit in Ras Al Khaimah mock scripts.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic under time pressure, organic reaction pathways and the qualitative analysis table. The analysis table is pure recall and the cheapest marks in the paper; students who skip it in revision are leaving credit untouched on the desk.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity is the recurring problem, particularly potential dividers and series-parallel combinations. The alternative-to-practical paper is learnable through vocabulary about repeats, precision and anomalous results, which makes it the highest-yield revision target in the subject.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Genetics crosses, osmosis practical write-ups and the extended responses. The mark scheme accepts a short list of specific phrases; teaching those phrases is worth more than another reading of the chapter.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The summary question has a word ceiling and a content-point tally. Fluent writers often score poorly because paraphrasing removes the required lifted detail. Reading precision, not expression, is what the paper measures.

subjects.name: Economics (DP and 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the band at both levels. A labelled axis, a shifted curve and a marked new equilibrium earn marks that prose does not. At Diploma level the evaluation sentence must reach a judgement rather than list both sides.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 and DP)
subjects.description: Data representation and network concepts are heavily recalled and heavily mis-remembered, especially hexadecimal conversion. Pseudocode must be internally consistent, which is a writing habit rather than a reading one and only builds by producing code under time.

sections.heading: What a tutor near me actually gets you in a small emirate
paragraphs: In Dubai, filtering by proximity is a reasonable strategy, because the pool behind the filter is deep. Dubai has 227 private schools and 387,441 private-school students across 17 curricula. Ras Al Khaimah's private provision is a fraction of that, concentrated in a handful of places, and the Diploma or Extended-tier cohort in any one subject is small. Filter that pool by distance and you are not choosing between specialists; you are choosing between the two or three people who are free.

The honest version of the in-home question: it exists, it costs more, and the premium pays for travel rather than expertise. UAE rate surveys place in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-500 per hour including the visit, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. In this emirate the extra money buys a shorter list, which is the opposite of what a parent paying a premium expects.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and the matching is done on the syllabus code, the level and the weak component. A student in Al Qusaidat stuck on Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3 gets somebody who has taught that paper. That is the whole argument, and the rest of this page is the syllabus detail that makes it checkable.

If you want the short answer before the detail: send the code, the level or tier, and the marked script or current draft. Everything after that is a conversation about the component rather than about the catchment area.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma bridge, subject by subject
paragraphs: The gap between IGCSE Extended and the Diploma's first term is not evenly distributed. In mathematics it is wide and immediate. In the sciences it is narrower in content and much wider in experimental write-up expectations. In the humanities it is mostly about essay structure and source handling rather than about facts. Treating the transition as one single jump is why so many Diploma students have a difficult first November.

The table below is the version nobody in this market publishes. It names, per subject, what a student arrives with, what the Diploma assumes in the first term, and roughly how long the gap takes to close if it is addressed before Year 12 starts rather than after the first report. The weeks column is deliberately conservative and assumes one session a week with work in between.

Two patterns recur with Ras Al Khaimah students specifically. Students arriving from an Indian-curriculum school are usually ahead on algebraic manipulation and behind on extended written answers. Students arriving from a British-curriculum school are the reverse. Knowing which pattern applies changes what the summer block should contain, and it is visible in ten minutes of looking at a Year 11 script.

The cheapest moment to act on this table is the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, when nothing has gone wrong yet and therefore nobody feels any urgency. Six to eight sessions in that window cost a fraction of the remedial work the same gap generates in the final term of Year 13, and they buy something the later work cannot: a student who starts the Diploma believing they can do the subject. Confidence in the first term determines how much a student volunteers in class, and how much they volunteer determines how quickly the teacher notices a problem. That is the real reason the bridge is worth buying early.

Use the weeks column as a planning figure rather than a promise. A student who does the set work between sessions moves faster than the range suggests; a student who treats the session as the whole of the effort moves slower, and no tutor can compensate for that. The honest version of the arithmetic is that tuition supplies direction and feedback, and the student supplies the hours.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the one decision a Ras Al Khaimah Diploma student cannot easily reverse, and it is usually made in the spring of Year 11 with incomplete information. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented route. Applications and Interpretation is the statistical, modelling, technology-heavy route. Neither is a soft option and both exist at Standard and Higher Level, which means there are four distinct courses hiding behind the word mathematics.

The route matters for university admission rather than for difficulty. Engineering, physics, mathematics and most quantitative economics routes expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and several admissions pages are explicit about it. Medicine, life sciences, business, psychology and design routes generally accept Applications and Interpretation, often at Higher Level. A student who wants engineering and takes Applications and Interpretation has made a reversible mistake only if it is caught in the first term.

The practical test is not which one a student prefers. It is how a student behaved on the 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher paper. A student who wrote full algebraic working and enjoyed the harder manipulation questions belongs in Analysis and Approaches. A student who reached correct answers by calculator and lost method marks belongs in Applications and Interpretation, and will do better there than in a course that punishes exactly that habit for two years.

There is a Ras Al Khaimah-specific wrinkle. Where a school runs only one of the four courses, the choice is made by the timetable rather than by the student, and the family discovers it after enrolment. If your child is aiming at a course with a hard Analysis and Approaches requirement, ask which of the four the school actually offers before Year 12 begins, in writing, and ask whether Higher Level is available in it. A school offering only Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is a perfectly good school that happens to close off a specific university route, and that is a fact to learn in Year 11 rather than in Year 13.

Whichever route is chosen, the exploration sits in both and is worth the same share of the grade. The criteria are identical across all four courses, which means the planning work described later on this page applies regardless of the decision made here.

sections.heading: Command terms, and the marks they quietly decide
paragraphs: Most long-answer marks are lost on the instruction rather than on the content. A student who writes everything they know about osmosis in answer to a question beginning outline has written four paragraphs for two marks. The IB and Cambridge both publish command terms with defined expectations, and almost no revision plan treats them as content to be learned.

The fix is mechanical and fast. For each command term, the student learns the shape of the expected answer: how many distinct points, whether a judgement is required, whether a reason must be attached to each statement. Once that shape is internalised, the student stops producing essays for two-mark questions and stops producing one-liners for eight-mark ones. In Ras Al Khaimah mock scripts this single change is often worth more than any topic revision.

The table below sets out the terms that appear most often and the failure that goes with each. Use it with a marked script beside you. The pattern is usually visible immediately: a student loses marks on the same two or three command terms across every paper, in every subject, because the habit travels.

A worked example makes the size of the problem clear. Take an eight-mark question beginning evaluate. The mark scheme awards credit for points on each side and reserves the top band for a weighted judgement. A student who writes a beautiful page describing both sides and stops reaches the middle band and no higher, however good the content. The missing element is a final sentence that says which consideration outweighs the others and why. One sentence, two marks, repeated across four long questions in a paper. That is a grade boundary's worth of marks lost to a formatting habit rather than to knowledge.

The practice that fixes it is deliberately dull. Short timed bursts: eight questions, mixed command terms, answered to the expected shape rather than to the student's instinct, marked against the published scheme. Three sessions of that changes the habit, and the habit then applies to every subject the student sits, which makes it the highest-leverage work available in a short block.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment criteria, by letter and by mark
paragraphs: Diploma parents in Ras Al Khaimah are frequently told that the Internal Assessment is important without being told how it is marked. It is marked against named criteria, each with its own mark allocation, and the student can read the criteria before starting. That one fact changes the whole exercise from a piece of writing into a specification to be met.

Mathematics is the clearest example. The exploration is marked across five criteria lettered A to E: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics, totalling twenty marks. The largest single allocation sits on use of mathematics, which is also the criterion students most often weaken by choosing a topic that cannot sustain Higher Level content. In the sciences the scientific investigation is assessed across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each, twenty-four in total.

What a tutor does with this is specific and bounded. The tutor explains each criterion, shows what a strong response to it looks like in a published exemplar, reads the student's own draft and names which criterion is under-served. The tutor does not produce the work. Nobody here writes or finishes an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay for a student, because submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice and the consequence lands on the student.

Parents can use the criteria directly, without any subject knowledge. Ask your child to read criterion C aloud and then point to the part of their draft that earns it. If they cannot, the problem is not the mathematics and it is not the writing; it is that the draft was built without reference to the thing marking it. That conversation takes four minutes, requires no expertise, and catches the commonest failure on the component. It works just as well on the sciences criteria and on the Extended Essay, where the published criteria are equally explicit about what each band requires.

One timing note for Ras Al Khaimah families. The deadlines that bite are the school's internal ones, not the board's, and they sit earlier than families expect because the school needs time to mark and moderate. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the internal draft and final dates at the start of Year 12 and write them on the same calendar as the exams, because an assessed component submitted late or unfinished caps a grade in a way no amount of revision later can undo.

sections.heading: Word and page limits across assessed components
paragraphs: Limits are published, enforced, and routinely discovered late. A Diploma student in Al Qusaidat who has written six thousand words of Extended Essay has not written a strong essay; they have written one that has to lose two thousand words in the week before submission, which is a worse edit than the writing it replaces.

The pattern is consistent across components: the limit is part of the task, and the skill being assessed includes selection. An Extended Essay sits at four thousand words. A Theory of Knowledge essay sits at one thousand six hundred. A Mathematics exploration is expected to run around twelve to twenty pages. Knowing these numbers at the start changes how a student plans, which is why the table belongs near the beginning of a Diploma year rather than near the end.

A tutor's role here is planning rather than cutting. The useful session happens before the first draft, when the student maps the argument against the available words and discovers that the research question is too broad to answer in the space. That is a thirty-minute conversation that saves a fortnight, and it is the single highest-value thing tuition does on an assessed component.

A rough allocation helps. For a four-thousand-word Extended Essay, a workable split is roughly four hundred words of introduction and research question, two thousand eight hundred across three or four analytical sections, five hundred of conclusion, and the remainder absorbed by transitions. Write those numbers at the top of the document before the first sentence and the essay stays in shape. Students who do not set an allocation discover in the final fortnight that one section has eaten half the budget, and the edit that follows removes the analysis rather than the padding, because the padding is harder to see in your own writing.

The same discipline applies to the shorter components. An eight-hundred-word Economics commentary holds one diagram and one judgement, not three of each. A one-thousand-six-hundred-word Theory of Knowledge essay holds two knowledge arguments properly developed rather than five sketched. Deciding how many ideas fit is the first act of the task, and it is where tuition earns its fee on these components.

sections.heading: What the market charges, from the cheapest option upwards
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most searches begin. Budget online tutoring and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45-150 per hour in the UAE, with one content platform publishing from AED 45-65 and another from AED 33-52. At that price you are buying homework supervision and general reassurance, which has a real use and is not the same as syllabus specialism.

The next band up is where syllabus knowledge starts. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150-300 per hour, with one UAE agency publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that, IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200-450 and beyond, with a UK-based agency quoting AED 270 and a UAE rate survey showing AED 200-450 or more. Premium named and examiner-track tutors reach AED 500-650, with one provider publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one, including travel, sits at roughly AED 180-500.

Every one of those figures belongs to the provider or survey that published it, not to IB Gram, and none of them is a quote. What we publish is the model: one-to-one, delivered online, with a free trial lesson before any payment. If a page in this market shows you a rate with no source and no date attached, treat it the way you would treat an unsourced number anywhere else.

The question a Ras Al Khaimah family should actually ask is not what the hourly rate is but what the total block costs and what it is supposed to achieve. Ten sessions at a specialist rate with a named component target is a smaller and better-spent sum than thirty sessions at a budget rate with no endpoint, and the second arrangement is the one that quietly runs for two years. Ask for the number of sessions, the target, and the measure that will say whether it worked, then compare the totals rather than the hourly figures.

sections.heading: The honesty line, and why it is on the page rather than in the terms
paragraphs: There is a tutoring service in this market selling finished Internal Assessments at a published price. It ranks. Parents find it. So the boundary needs to be stated plainly rather than assumed: a tutor explains the criteria, teaches the skills, reads the student's draft and says which criterion is weak. The student produces the work. Nobody here produces assessed work on a student's behalf.

This is not squeamishness. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the candidate, not on whoever was paid. A Diploma student found to have submitted purchased work risks the whole Diploma, two years after the decision was made. No fee refund exists that compensates for that, and no tutor absorbs the penalty.

The practical boundary in a session looks like this. Acceptable: explaining what criterion E rewards, working through a published exemplar, questioning whether the chosen topic can sustain Higher Level mathematics, pointing at a paragraph and saying this summarises where the criterion wants reflection. Not acceptable: supplying sentences, restructuring the student's argument into the tutor's own, or editing a draft to a finished state. The difference is visible in a session recording, which is one quiet advantage of lessons delivered over video.

There is a related rule about materials that parents rarely hear stated. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them and link to the official source rather than reproducing or supplying them, because redistributing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure as well. If a tutoring service offers you a bundle of mark schemes as a selling point, it is offering something it does not own.

The same caution applies to anybody described as an examiner. Current examiner status is a specific thing that can be evidenced or cannot, and it confers no access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or unseen paper content. A tutor who has taught a syllabus for years is worth hiring on that basis. A tutor whose selling point is privileged access to the board is making a claim worth a direct question.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor may legally teach in the UAE
paragraphs: Parents in Al Qusaidat can check this in one question, and most never ask it. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. The eligible groups are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

So the question to a prospective tutor is simply whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. The application route is the ministry's own service for private tutor licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone describing the permit as expensive, slow or optional has not looked at the published service.

Two cautions worth carrying. Individuals tutoring without the permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the ministry has not published amounts, so any specific figure you are quoted is invented. And a permit is not an endorsement by anybody: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ministry of Education, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A service using a regulator's name as an adjective is making a claim it almost certainly cannot evidence.

The permit also carries a code of conduct, and one clause of it matters to Al Qusaidat families directly: it bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff set out the same prohibition on paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the tutor's school. So the arrangement that feels most convenient, paying your child's own subject teacher for evening lessons, is the one to avoid, and it is also a poor idea on its merits: the person marking the internal assessments should not be paid to prepare the student for them.

An operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. A tuition centre in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a specific instrument held by specific businesses, and no online matching platform should be describing itself in its language.
bullets: Ask directly whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit
The permit is free, valid two years, and applied for through MoHRE's own channels
No fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as fiction
No regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram, and this page claims none

process.title: Send the code and the level
process.description: Mathematics is four different Diploma courses and at least two different IGCSEs. Send the syllabus code, the level or tier, the board, and the component that is weak. The exams officer or Diploma coordinator has all of it, and getting it right removes the commonest cause of a poor first match.

process.title: Send the marked script or the current draft
process.description: A marked mock paper or a current Internal Assessment draft tells a tutor more in five minutes than a conversation does in thirty. Component marks show whether the problem is content, timing or command-term discipline, and those three need entirely different plans.

process.title: Free trial lesson on your own material
process.description: A real lesson, not a consultation. The tutor works on a question your child got wrong, which is the only part of a first session with predictive value. No payment and no card details are needed to book it, and you are welcome to watch.

process.title: A written plan against the criteria or the paper
process.description: You get the target in writing: which criterion, which paper, which topics, in which order, over how many sessions. For an assessed component the plan includes the school's own internal deadline, because that date controls everything else.

process.title: Session notes you can actually use
process.description: After each lesson, a short note of what was covered, what was set, and what the tutor is watching. Six notes in a row with no movement is a signal to change the match, and having them in writing is what makes that judgement possible.

process.title: An honest answer on availability
process.description: For a thinly taught Higher Level subject there may be no specialist free this month. You will be told that and offered a date, rather than placed with somebody adjacent to the subject. A clear no is more useful in an exam year than a quiet compromise.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the component, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A weak Paper 3 and a weak Internal Assessment in the same subject are different problems needing different people. Matching at component level is slower to arrange and markedly more effective than matching on a subject name, particularly in a small emirate.

whyPoints.title: Criteria and mark allocations in public
whyPoints.description: This page prints the Mathematics exploration criteria by letter with their marks, and the published word limits across components. No competitor page in this market names a single criterion letter. A parent who knows the numbers can judge the tuition.

whyPoints.title: Both boards, properly distinguished
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are not interchangeable, and a tutor who conflates them wastes sessions teaching the wrong question style. Ras Al Khaimah families often have children on both boards, so the distinction is routine here rather than academic.

whyPoints.title: Rates printed with their publisher
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the survey or provider that published it and is presented as the market rather than as our price. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, feedback and questioning on the student's own work. No writing, finishing or editing to completion of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. The malpractice risk sits with the candidate, which is exactly why the boundary is published.

whyPoints.title: One delivery format, disclosed first
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, and home visits are a service we run in India only. You know that before booking rather than after paying.

faqs.question: We searched for a tutor near us in Al Qusaidat. Does distance matter at all?
faqs.answer: For logistics it used to; for teaching quality it does not. Lessons here are delivered one-to-one over live video, so the tutor's location is irrelevant to whether the session happens. What matters is whether they have taught the specific syllabus code and component your child is weak on. In an emirate with a small private-school set, filtering by distance narrows the pool to whoever is free rather than whoever knows the paper, which is the opposite of what a parent paying for specialism wants.

faqs.question: Which IB Mathematics course should my child take after IGCSE Extended?
faqs.answer: Read the IGCSE script rather than asking the student's preference. A child who wrote full algebraic working and enjoyed harder manipulation belongs in Analysis and Approaches. A child who reached correct answers on the calculator and dropped method marks belongs in Applications and Interpretation and will do better there. Then check the intended university course, because engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics routes generally expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level while life sciences, business and psychology routes commonly accept Applications and Interpretation.

faqs.question: How is the IB Mathematics exploration actually marked?
faqs.answer: Against five criteria lettered A to E, totalling twenty marks: presentation worth four, mathematical communication worth four, personal engagement worth three, reflection worth three, and use of mathematics worth six. The largest allocation is on use of mathematics, which is also where most drafts fail, usually because the chosen topic cannot sustain content at the course level. A student who reads the criteria before choosing a topic avoids the single most expensive mistake available on the component.

faqs.question: Is the Extended Essay really capped at four thousand words?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the limit is part of the task rather than an administrative detail. Selection is one of the things being assessed, so an essay that needs two thousand words cut in the final week has already lost the argument it was supposed to sustain. The useful intervention happens before the first draft, mapping the argument against the available words until the research question is narrow enough to answer properly. A Theory of Knowledge essay sits at one thousand six hundred words on the same principle.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor stop on an Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor explains each criterion, works through published exemplars, questions whether the topic can carry the required depth, and reads the student's own draft to say which criterion is under-served. The tutor does not supply sentences, restructure the argument into their own, or edit a draft to a finished state. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under board rules and the penalty falls on the candidate, not on whoever was paid.

faqs.question: Why do my children sit different exam boards at schools in the same emirate?
faqs.answer: Because Ras Al Khaimah's private schools choose their own board, and the emirate's Department of Knowledge approves curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods school by school rather than imposing one. So a family in Al Qusaidat can easily have one child on Cambridge codes such as 0580 and 0625 and another on Pearson codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. The content overlaps; the paper structures and question styles do not, which is why a tutor should be matched per child rather than per household.

faqs.question: What are command terms, and why would they change a grade?
faqs.answer: They are the instruction words that open a question, and both the IB and Cambridge publish what each one requires. Outline wants brief main points; explain wants a reason attached to each statement; evaluate wants strengths and limitations weighed against each other and a judgement. Students who write everything they know lose marks on short questions and run out of time for long ones. Learning the expected answer shape for eight or nine terms is a few hours of work and often moves more marks than topic revision does.

faqs.question: My child is strong in class but weak in the mock. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of three things: timing, method-mark discipline, or command-term handling. All three are invisible in classwork and all three show up immediately on a marked script, which is why we ask for the script rather than the report. A student who knows the content and loses a third of the marks is not short of teaching; they are short of timed practice marked against the published scheme. That is an eight-session problem, not a term-long one.

faqs.question: Does the scientific investigation in IB sciences have criteria too?
faqs.answer: Yes. The investigation is assessed across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks for twenty-four in total. The commonest failure is a design with no genuine independent variable range, which caps the data analysis and conclusion marks before any writing happens. That is why the highest-value session on the whole component is the one held before data collection starts, not the one held when a draft already exists.

faqs.question: How long before a Diploma subject gets beyond fixing?
faqs.answer: Nothing is beyond fixing, but the cost rises sharply once an assessed component is submitted. Content gaps found in Year 12 take weeks. The same gaps found in the final term compete with revision for every other subject. An Internal Assessment already handed in cannot be revised at all. So the honest ordering is: assessed components first, because they have hard deadlines, then content, then paper technique, which responds fastest and can be moved late.

faqs.question: My children are on Cambridge and Pearson codes. Can one approach cover both?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we treat them as separate courses rather than variants. Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and Pearson 4CH1 cover similar chemistry through different paper structures, mark-scheme phrasing and question styles, and the grading scales differ. A tutor matched to the wrong one will teach correct chemistry in the wrong examination idiom, which is a quiet way to waste a term. Send the code from the school's entry confirmation rather than the subject name from the timetable.

faqs.question: Is a fortnightly session enough for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: For maintenance across Years 12 and 13, often yes. A fortnightly slot exists to stop a subject drifting between report cards, which is where most Diploma damage accumulates quietly. It is not enough to close an existing gap, and it is not enough in the final term, when the pattern should step up to weekly. Families who run fortnightly from early Year 12 generally need fewer total sessions than families who start weekly in the final six months.

faqs.question: What happens in the first session for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: The tutor works from the marked script or sets a short timed section, because a conversation about which topics feel hard is the least reliable diagnostic available. From the script the tutor identifies whether the losses are content, method-mark discipline or command-term handling, then names the order of work. You get that in writing after the session. The free trial lesson comes before this and runs on your child's own material, with you welcome to watch.

faqs.question: Do we need tutoring for UAE university equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process and tutoring is not part of it. The published British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify current requirements with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority. IB Gram neither performs equivalency nor guarantees any outcome from it.

faqs.question: Should we use the same person for two Diploma subjects to save money?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually a worse arrangement than it looks. Mathematics and Physics is a plausible pairing; Chemistry and Economics is not. Even where one person can cover both, a single session split across two subjects becomes half an hour of each and a full hour of neither. Two subjects need two slots, and often two tutors, because component-level specialism is the thing being bought and it rarely spans a pair of unrelated syllabuses.

faqs.question: How do we know six sessions have achieved anything?
faqs.answer: By comparing a marked script against a marked script. A diagnostic paper at the start and a comparable paper at session six, both marked to the published scheme, give you component-level movement rather than an impression. The written note after each session tells you what was set and whether it was done. If the second script has not moved and the notes show the work was completed, the match is wrong and should change rather than continue.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.tutorsIntro: Julphar families are matched with tutors who answer verifiable questions with verifiable answers: a syllabus code, a year, a set of papers, a permit. The two grids below cover what is most often requested here across both systems.

intro.heading: Most tutoring claims cannot be checked. Start with the ones that can
paragraphs: Search for a tutor and the results are a wall of assertion: experienced, trusted, highly reviewed, proven. None of it is checkable from a listing, and the research behind this project found worse than vagueness. One provider publishes its own star rating with two different review counts on the same page. Another shows a rating of five from twenty reviews beside a claim about a far larger student body. A third marks up questions in its page code that do not appear on the page at all. A fourth publishes a price in its code that contradicts the price in its text.

So the useful starting point for a family in Julphar is not which claims to believe but which claims can be tested. A syllabus code and a year can be tested. A permit can be shown. A board's own administration pages can be read. A school's inspection outcome can be requested. Almost everything else in this market is a matter of trust, and trust is more sensibly extended to a provider who distinguishes between the two.

Julphar is the old quarter of Ras Al Khaimah around the creek and the historic port, with the shortest school journeys in the emirate and older, denser housing. For a two-system household, running a Diploma student and an IGCSE candidate at once, that means short reliably held sessions work better than long ambitious ones, and the ninety-minute papers need a venue planned rather than assumed.

Delivery is stated plainly, which is itself a verifiable claim. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is the one parents search, and it is answered honestly rather than quietly reinterpreted.

The asymmetry in this page's dates is deliberate and is itself an example of the distinction. Cambridge and Pearson publish exam-administration pages that could be read and dated, so their positions appear with the month they were read and past dates keep their year. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB exam or results date in this project has been verified from the board, and none appears here.

What follows is five comparisons: how the two boards administer a candidate, what can be verified against what must be trusted, a trial lesson against a paid first session, two children where one is ahead, and the options on results day in each system. Each is chosen because it is decidable rather than because it sounds persuasive. Market rates, where they are relevant, are attributed to the provider that published them and dated to the month they were read, which is another instance of the same distinction: a number with a source attached can be argued with, and a number without one cannot.

programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with internal assessment in every subject on school-set deadlines. sections.heading: How the two boards administer a candidate
paragraphs: A two-system household is dealing with two administrative machines, and the parts that can go wrong are administrative rather than academic. This is also the area where everything is published, so a family can be certain rather than hopeful.

On the Cambridge side, the facts that matter are the syllabus code, the tier, the paper numbers, the practical route for each science, and the centre's administrative zone. Cambridge states that every centre is allocated to one of six zones, that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is a published warning and almost no tuition page passes it on. Cambridge runs June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and the February and March series offered in India only.

On the Pearson side, exams run in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. sections.heading: What you can verify against what you must trust
paragraphs: This is the comparison that would most improve the average tutoring decision in this market, and it is simply a sorting exercise. Some claims are checkable in a message or two. Others are matters of judgement. A family that knows which is which spends its scepticism efficiently.

The checkable list is longer than most parents expect. A syllabus code and the year it was last taught. The paper numbers a tutor has worked on. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and can simply be shown. Whether travel is inside a rate. Whether a rate can change mid-term. What happens in week three if the match fails. Whether a provider will state in writing what it will not do with an internal assessment. A school's latest inspection outcome, requested from the school. The board's own series, zones and results dates, read on the board's own pages.

The unverifiable list is where the marketing lives. Experience in general. Trustedness. Self-published star ratings, which the research for this project found contradicting themselves on the same page, including one provider showing two different review counts and another showing a rating from twenty reviews next to a claim about a far larger student body. Student numbers with no method. Success percentages with no n and no date. Examiner status that cannot be evidenced. And any promised grade, which is unverifiable in principle because boundaries are set after a series on the basis of that series' papers.

The practical rule that follows is simple: decide on the checkable list, and treat the unverifiable list as neither evidence for nor against. A provider who volunteers the distinction is giving a family something useful; a provider who fills the page with the second list is telling you which list they would rather be judged on.

sections.heading: A trial lesson against a paid first session
paragraphs: Almost every provider offers something at the start, and the versions differ more than the language suggests. Comparing them properly is worth doing because the first session sets what follows, and because the terms attached to a free offer are the clearest early signal of how a provider behaves.

A free diagnostic session with no card details taken and a written summary afterwards is the most useful version, because the family keeps something of value regardless of what they decide. A free session that requires card details is a subscription with a delay attached, and the condition should be stated on the same screen as the word free. A discounted first session is a legitimate offer and should be described as a discount. A free session conditional on booking a block is a package, not a trial.

What the session itself contains matters more than the price. A sales call wearing the clothes of a lesson is recognisable: it asks about ambitions, explains a method, and produces a recommendation to buy a number of hours. A diagnosis is recognisable too: it works through real questions from the student's own paper, classifies lost marks into content, method, command term and timing, and ends with a written note naming three specific targets. One of those is useful if you walk away. The other is not.

The comparison for a two-system household has an extra dimension. Each child needs a separate diagnosis with a separate subject specialist, because a Diploma Higher Level diagnosis and a Year 10 IGCSE diagnosis are different exercises. A provider offering one combined session across two children and two systems is offering something cheaper to deliver rather than something better.

sections.heading: Two children, one ahead: comparing need against noise
paragraphs: In households running both systems, the decision about where to put limited money and attention is usually made on the basis of whichever child produced the most recent bad mark. That is noise rather than need, and a more deliberate comparison produces a different answer surprisingly often.

Three questions separate need from noise. Is the problem content or technique, because technique responds in weeks and content takes a term. How much of the grade is still movable, which depends on how much course remains and whether internal components have already been submitted. And does anything specific depend on this grade, such as a post-16 entry requirement or an equivalency count. A recent bad mark answers none of those.

Run the three questions across two children and the usual outcome is lopsided. A Diploma student in the final year with coursework already submitted and papers approaching has a technique problem with a short runway, which suits a block. A Year 10 IGCSE candidate with content gaps and eighteen months remaining has the largest movable grade in the household and the cheapest hours available, which suits a weekly slot. Those two conclusions point in different directions from the one a disappointing report would have produced.

The other half of the comparison is attention rather than money. The student generating visible deadlines absorbs almost all of a household's adult attention, which means the quieter child's slot becomes the thing cancelled whenever the louder one has a crisis. A child who learns twice that their work is expendable usually stops raising it, and that is a more expensive outcome than any single bad grade.

sections.heading: Results day compared across the two systems
paragraphs: Both systems produce a fortnight in which consequential decisions are made with little information, and the options are not the same. Knowing which applies to which child before the day arrives is worth more than any amount of reaction afterwards.

On the IGCSE side the sequence is well defined. Ask the school or centre for the component breakdown, marks by paper, before deciding anything. A shortfall concentrated on one paper is a different problem from one spread across every component, and only the first is reliably closed by a short block. Then the options are an enquiry upon results, which is a school process with its own deadline and criteria, a resit in the next series, or accepting the grade. The timing matters: June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 while November 2025 results reached them on 22 January 2026, so a November entry means waiting until January and any receiving institution has to be told in advance.

On the Diploma side the structure is similar and the dates are not publishable here, because none has been verified from the board. The component breakdown is still the first request, an enquiry upon results is still a school process, and a later session exists as an alternative route. The difference is that a Diploma grade sits inside a points total, so a single subject's movement can matter more or less depending on where the total sits relative to an offer, which is a conversation for the coordinator rather than a tutor.

The common error in both systems is reacting to the overall grade rather than to the breakdown, and the common cost is an entry fee spent on a resit that the diagnosis would have advised against. One diagnostic session on the breakdown, before any entry, is the cheapest decision-making hour available in either system.

sections.heading: Effort now against effort later
paragraphs: The last comparison is between two spending patterns that cost the same and produce different results, and it is the one most families get backwards. Early effort compounds and late effort does not, and the reason is structural rather than motivational.

Content learned in the first year of a course is used in the second year as a step inside harder questions, which means a term spent securing it pays twice. Technique learned early is applied to every piece of work afterwards, which means it pays many times. A coursework decision made well in the first year protects a component worth a substantial share of a grade. By contrast, the same hours spent in the final term can only convert knowledge already present into marks, which is valuable and bounded.

There is a market dimension too. Specialist capacity in a small emirate tightens as a series approaches, so a family booking early is choosing from an open diary and a family booking late is choosing from the hours nobody else took. Rates in this market also firm up towards a series for the ordinary reason that demand rises while the same teachers cannot teach more hours. Early booking is therefore both a better educational decision and a cheaper one, which is an unusual combination.

None of that means a late start is pointless. An eight-week block before a series changes technique reliably, and families who arrive with eight weeks should be told that honestly rather than sold a rescue. The point of the comparison is that the same budget placed a year earlier buys considerably more, and that is a decision available to any family reading this in September rather than in April.
