sections.heading: Claims in this market, and what to discount
paragraphs: This section exists because the research behind this project read sixty-odd competitor pages and found a consistent set of patterns that a family can learn to recognise. None of the brands is named here, and no claim is made about any competitor's quality, pricing or legality; what follows is a description of patterns, which is a fair thing to publish and a useful thing to know.

The first pattern is the self-published rating. Several pages show a star rating and a review count that cannot be reconciled, in one case two different review counts on the same page, and in another a rating from a small number of reviews presented beside a claim about a far larger student body. The second is the statistic without method: a success percentage, a satisfaction score, or a median tutor result, with no sample size, no date and no description of how it was measured. The third is the price that contradicts itself, where a figure in a page's underlying code differs from the figure in its visible text.

The fourth is borrowed authority: a regulator's or a board's name placed next to the word approved, accredited or partner where no such relationship exists. That one matters most, because it is the claim a UAE regulator would actually act on. A permit issued to a training institute with premises is a specific thing, and an individual tutor's permit is another specific thing, and neither is a general endorsement of a matching platform. The fifth is the offer to produce assessed work, which the research found openly priced on one page and which transfers the entire risk to the student.

The useful response is not cynicism but a checklist. Discount any rating a provider published about itself. Discount any statistic without a sample size and a date. Discount any claim of approval unless a permit number can be shown. Ask any provider to state in writing what it will not do with an internal assessment. Those four habits remove most of the noise in this market in about five minutes.

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and the permit
paragraphs: A page about verification has to be verifiable itself, so here are the limits that apply here. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and command term, mark work against the published scheme, test whether a coursework topic or method is viable, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written.

A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay, a personal project or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text, data or diagrams for submission. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the consequence of buying one falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it, which is why this limit is published rather than assumed.

On materials: no tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The official source should be referenced and linked instead, which is why this page carries no attachments and asks readers to confirm detail with their own centre. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

On who may teach: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, publishes no rating about itself, and no tutor can promise a grade.

faqs.question: What can a Julphar family actually verify about a tutor?
faqs.answer: More than most parents expect. The syllabus code and the year it was last taught. The paper numbers the tutor has worked on. What happens if the match fails in week three. And whether the provider will state in writing what it will not do with an internal assessment. Decide on those.

faqs.question: Should I trust a tutoring company's own star rating?
faqs.answer: No. The research behind this project found competitor pages in this market publishing ratings that contradict themselves, including one page showing two different review counts and another showing a rating from a small number of reviews beside a claim about a far larger student body. A rating a provider publishes about itself is not evidence either way. If individual dated reviews can be read somewhere independent, read those instead; if they cannot, discount the figure entirely.

faqs.question: Why do no IB exam dates appear on this page?
faqs.answer: Because none has been verified. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB exam or results date in this project has been confirmed from the board itself, and publishing an unverified date that a family plans around would be worse than publishing none. What is safe to state is that UAE schools sit the May session and a November session exists as an alternative route. Take every specific date from your Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge zone, and how do I find ours?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. The board states that it is essential to use the correct version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Ask your exams officer which zone your centre is in, get the centre's own timetable in writing, and revise from that copy rather than from any version found online.

faqs.question: How do I tell a diagnosis from a sales call?
faqs.answer: By what happens in the session and what you keep afterwards. A diagnosis works through real questions from your child's own paper, classifies the lost marks into content, method, command term and timing, and ends with a written note naming three specific targets that is yours regardless of what you decide. A sales call asks about ambitions, explains a method and recommends a number of hours. One of those is useful if you walk away, and the other is not.

faqs.question: Is a free trial lesson always free?
faqs.answer: Not always, and the condition is the thing to look at. A free session with no card details taken and a written summary afterwards is genuinely free. A free session that requires card details is a subscription with a delay attached. A free session conditional on booking a block is a package. All three are legitimate offers; what matters is that the condition appears on the same screen as the word free rather than in a later message.

faqs.question: We have two children on two systems. Who should get the hours?
faqs.answer: Not whoever produced the most recent bad mark, which is noise. Run three questions across both: is the problem content or technique, how much of the grade is still movable, and does anything specific depend on it. A Diploma student in the final year usually has a technique problem with a short runway, which suits a block. A Year 10 candidate usually has content gaps and the largest movable grade in the household, which suits a weekly slot and is the cheaper hour.

faqs.question: How do we stop the quieter child's session from being cancelled?
faqs.answer: By deciding in advance that it is reduced rather than dropped when the other child has a crisis. The student generating visible deadlines absorbs almost all of a household's adult attention, and the predictable result is that the quieter child's slot becomes the thing that gives way. A child who learns twice that their work is expendable usually stops raising it, and two terms of quiet drift costs more to repair than the grade that prompted the crisis.

faqs.question: What should we ask for on IGCSE results day?
faqs.answer: The component breakdown first, marks by paper, before any decision. A shortfall concentrated on one paper is a different problem from one spread across every component, and only the first is reliably closed by a short block. Then ask the exams officer whether the profile makes an enquiry upon results plausible, which is a school process with its own deadline and criteria. Accepting the grade is often the right answer and is almost never offered as one.

faqs.question: Does a November resit delay things?
faqs.answer: Yes, measurably. June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 while November 2025 results reached them on 22 January 2026, so a November entry means waiting until January. That matters if a post-16 place depends on the grade, and the receiving institution should be told in advance rather than asked to accommodate the gap later. Factor the timing into the decision alongside whether a short block can realistically close the specific shortfall.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start tutoring early or later?
faqs.answer: Earlier, on both counts, which is unusual. Content secured in the first year of a course is used as a step inside harder questions later, so it pays twice, and technique learned early applies to every subsequent piece of work. Separately, specialist capacity in this emirate is loosest in September and tightest in the spring, and rates firm up towards a series because demand rises while the same teachers cannot teach more hours. Early booking is both better and cheaper.

faqs.question: Can anyone promise my child a grade?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is structural rather than modest. Grade boundaries are set after a series, once the board has seen how the cohort performed on that particular paper, so an outcome cannot be sold in advance by anybody. A provider offering a promised score, a promised improvement or money back against a result is either misunderstanding that mechanism or hoping the question is not raised. What can honestly be promised is a process, and a process is observable.

faqs.question: A provider says a regulator or board has approved it. What should I ask?
faqs.answer: It means a specific question is worth asking: what is the permit number and who issued it. Permits are specific and are issued to specific entities. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; an individual tutor requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Neither is a general endorsement of a matching platform. IB Gram holds no such approval from any regulator or awarding body and claims none.

faqs.question: Why does this page describe competitor patterns rather than name brands?
faqs.answer: Because the patterns are useful and the names are not. Describing how a self-published rating, an unmethodical statistic or a borrowed-authority claim looks lets a family recognise them anywhere, including here. Naming a brand and making claims about its quality, pricing or legality would be a different kind of statement and not one a tutoring page should make. The research behind this project read sixty-odd pages; what it produced was a checklist rather than a hit list.

faqs.question: What is the single fastest way to filter this market?
faqs.answer: Four questions and about five minutes. Discount any rating a provider published about itself. Discount any statistic without a sample size and a date. Discount any claim of approval unless a permit number can be shown. And ask every provider to state in writing what it will not do with an internal assessment. The last one is the most revealing, because the honest answer is a short list of refusals and the dishonest answer is an offer.

intro.heading: Diagnosis first, and it is quicker than you think
paragraphs: The single most common reason tutoring fails is that nobody established what was wrong. A family worried about Chemistry books two sessions a week in September, and in January the grade is unchanged, because the sessions were spent covering content when the problem was that answers were being written for the student rather than for a marker. That is not a teaching failure. It is a diagnostic failure, and it is avoidable in one session.

A competent subject diagnosis takes about forty minutes and consists of specific checks rather than a general conversation. In Mathematics, can the student factorise and manipulate without a calculator. In Chemistry, can they convert between mass, moles and volume under time pressure. In Biology, do their long answers order a process or just name it. In English, does a reading response analyse how a passage works or retell what it says. Each of those checks produces a yes or no, and between them they tell a family what the next eight weeks should contain.

Khuzam sits inland in Ras Al Khaimah city with a short drive into the emirate's school cluster, so getting to a tutor is not the problem here. The problem is that the emirate's private-school set is small, the Diploma cohort inside it is smaller, and a student can look comfortable in a class of twelve while sitting well below where a national cohort would place them. Small classes are pleasant and they conceal relative weakness, which is a specific risk worth naming.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For diagnostic work the format is an advantage: the script sits on a shared screen, gets annotated live, and the family keeps the annotated copy, which a kitchen-table session does not produce.

This page is written for the household that is running both systems, because the diagnosis differs between them. IGCSE rewards method and specific written moves against a published mark scheme. The Diploma rewards the same plus independent assessed work judged against named criteria. A student can be strong in one and weak in the other, and treating them as a single ability is how a Year 11 success becomes a Grade 11 surprise.

Nothing here promises an outcome. No tutor can promise a grade, because boundaries are set after a series on the basis of that series' papers, and no IB exam or results date appears on this page because none in this project has been verified from the board itself. Cambridge and Pearson positions are sourced from the boards' own exam-administration pages, read in October 2026, and past dates keep their year because that is what makes them checkable. Where a figure or a mark allocation appears, confirm it against the syllabus document or subject guide your own school issues, since both are revised and old copies circulate.
bullets: A subject diagnosis is a set of specific checks, not a general assessment, and takes about forty minutes.

sections.heading: The first forty minutes: what a specialist actually checks
paragraphs: A diagnosis is not a conversation about how a student feels in a subject. It is a short sequence of tasks chosen because each one separates two possible explanations, and the result is a set of yes or no answers that a parent can act on. The whole thing fits inside a single session, which is why it should always come before any package is bought.

The design principle is that each check isolates one variable. Asking a Mathematics student to factorise without a calculator separates algebraic fluency from calculator dependence. Asking a Chemistry student to do a mass-to-moles-to-volume conversion in ninety seconds separates understanding from speed, because almost all of them can do it slowly. Asking a Biology student to describe a process rather than name it separates knowledge from written habit. None of those checks takes longer than five minutes, and together they cover most of the ways a grade goes missing.

What makes the output useful is that it is written down. A verbal impression after a session is worth almost nothing a week later; a short written summary naming three specific targets is a document a family can compare against in January. It is also the document that tells you whether the tutoring is working, because the same named causes either recur in marked work or they stop.

The table lists the opening check per subject and what each result implies. None of it is proprietary and a parent can run several of these at home, which is the point: a diagnosis that only a provider can perform is a sales mechanism rather than a diagnosis.

sections.heading: Two systems, two marking logics
paragraphs: A household running IGCSE and the IB at once is running two different assessment philosophies, and a diagnosis that ignores the difference will misread one of the children. The distinction is not difficulty. It is what the marker is instructed to look for.

An IGCSE paper is marked against a published mark scheme that lists creditable points. Marks exist for identifiable steps, for specific terms, for a labelled feature. The student's job is to produce the listed thing, and the technique that pays is making every creditable step visible. A correct answer with no working can score a fraction of what it deserves, which is why method work is the highest-return intervention at this level.

MYP and Diploma internal work are marked against named criteria with descriptors, which describe a quality of performance rather than a list of points. The student's job is to demonstrate the level described, which usually requires something structural: a justification, a reflection, an evaluation that ranks rather than lists. Marks are not lost one step at a time but a band at a time, and a whole criterion strand left unaddressed costs a predictable chunk.

The practical consequence is that the two children need different coaching. The IGCSE student is taught to write for a mark scheme; the Diploma student is taught to read descriptors and then write to them. Confusing the two produces a Diploma student who shows beautiful working and never addresses a criterion, or an IGCSE student who writes thoughtfully and omits the creditable step.

sections.heading: What a Diploma course assumes you already have
paragraphs: The transition from Year 11 into Grade 11 is where a diagnosis is most valuable and least often performed, because a student who finished IGCSE comfortably is assumed to be ready. What a Diploma course assumes is specific prior knowledge and specific habits, and the gaps are predictable enough to list.

In Mathematics, the assumption is that algebraic manipulation is automatic rather than achievable. A Diploma question will use factorising as a step inside a longer problem, and a student who has to stop and think about it runs out of time. Analysis and Approaches additionally assumes comfort with formal reasoning, which IGCSE barely touches.

In the sciences, the assumption is that recall is already in place and the course can spend its time on analysis, uncertainty and extended evaluation. Students arriving with content secure but no experience of writing a ranked evaluation find the internal assessment much harder than the content. In English, the assumption is that the student can already read for structure and effect, which is the skill the IGCSE reading papers reward and that many students pass without acquiring.

Each of these gaps closes in a defined number of weeks when it is named early, which is the argument for a diagnostic session in the summer between the two courses rather than a rescue in the spring. The table lists the assumption per subject area and the specific prior skill it rests on. None of these is exotic, and none of them is usually stated to a student in the first term of a Diploma course, which is why the gap reads as a general struggle rather than as four specific missing habits.

sections.heading: Command terms: the same word, two different demands
paragraphs: Both systems publish command terms and both expect them to be obeyed, but the lists are not identical and the expectations attached to shared words are not always the same. A student moving between the two, or a household running both, needs to know that the vocabulary is system-specific rather than general English.

The shared terms behave broadly alike. State wants a fact with no reasoning in either system. Describe wants features or stages without cause. Explain wants a mechanism. Where the systems diverge is in the reasoning-heavy terms and in how much structure is expected: Diploma papers lean harder on evaluate, discuss, to what extent and justify, and those expect a stated position supported from both sides, which an IGCSE student can score reasonably well without ever producing.

The practical teaching method is identical in both cases and takes very little time. Take answers the student has already written, cover the marks, and ask them to identify what the term demanded and whether they delivered it. Most students discover within twenty minutes that a measurable share of their lost marks came from answering a different question from the one asked, which is a cheaper realisation than a term of content revision.

Definitions should be checked against the current subject guide or syllabus document for the specific code, because the lists are published per subject and are revised. The table below compares how the heavier terms behave across the two systems.

sections.heading: Diagnostic questions a parent can ask at home
paragraphs: A diagnosis that only a provider can perform is not a diagnosis, so here are the versions a parent in Khuzam can run themselves this week, with no subject expertise required. The aim is not to teach anything but to find out which of four things is going wrong.

Ask to see a recent marked piece of work, and then ask the student to explain, for three of the lost marks, why the mark was lost. If they can say what the marker wanted and why they did not provide it, the problem is habit rather than knowledge, which is good news and quick to fix. If they cannot say what the marker wanted, the problem may be that nobody has ever shown them a mark scheme.

Second: ask them to do one question from a recent paper while you time it, and then ask whether that pace would finish the paper. Students routinely have no idea, and a pacing problem is invisible in homework and decisive in an examination. Third: for any coursework, ask them to state their research question or line of argument in one sentence. Hesitation here is the single most reliable early warning available, because a question they cannot state is a question they cannot answer in 4,000 words.

Fourth: ask what the command term on their last long answer was, and what it demanded. A student who shrugs at that question is losing marks on every paper in every subject, and it is the cheapest thing on this list to correct.
bullets: For three lost marks, can they say what the marker wanted?

sections.heading: The two internal-assessment regimes compared
paragraphs: Internal assessment is where the two systems diverge most, and where a household running both is most likely to apply the wrong standard. IGCSE coursework, where a subject has it, is a defined task with a mark scheme. Diploma internal assessment is an independent piece judged against descriptor bands, and the decision that determines its ceiling is taken before any writing happens.

That asymmetry has a practical consequence for parents. A Year 11 coursework piece can usually be improved by doing more of what the task asked. A Diploma internal assessment frequently cannot, because the ceiling was set by the topic, the method or the article. A Mathematics exploration with no mathematics to develop, a science investigation whose method will not produce analysable data, an Economics commentary built on a thin or stale article: each caps the grade before a word is written, and the only repair is to change the decision.

This is why the highest-value support is early and narrow rather than late and extensive. One session testing viability protects a component carrying a substantial share of the subject grade; the same session six weeks later protects nothing. Confirm mark allocations against the subject guide your school issues, because guides are revised and this page does not reproduce them.

The boundary on help is the same in both systems and worth stating before any of it begins. A tutor may explain criteria, test viability, review a method and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may never write, redraft or complete the work, nor supply text, data or diagrams for submission.

sections.heading: What a small cohort hides
paragraphs: This is a Ras Al Khaimah point rather than a general one, and it is the reason a family here might want an external diagnosis even when nothing appears to be wrong. The emirate's private-school set is small and concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, and a Diploma class may have a dozen students in it or fewer.

Small classes are genuinely good for teaching and genuinely poor for calibration. A student placed third in a class of twelve has a position that carries almost no information about how they would place in a national or international cohort. Report-card comparisons inside a tiny group can describe a student as strong when their absolute performance against a mark scheme is middling, and the discovery arrives with a mock paper late in the course.

The same effect operates on teachers, without any fault on their part. A subject teacher who is the only person in the emirate teaching a particular Higher Level option has no colleague to moderate against on whether a piece of internal work is where it should be. An external specialist who has taught the same component to other cohorts provides exactly that second reading, and in a small emirate it is often unavailable any other way.

None of this is an argument that local schools are weaker. It is an argument that calibration has to come from outside a small cohort, and that an external check once or twice a year is worth more here than weekly tuition bought in a panic later.
bullets: A position inside a class of twelve carries little information about absolute standing.

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and the permit
paragraphs: A page about diagnosis has to be clear about what follows a diagnosis. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain assessment criteria and command terms, mark work against the published scheme, test the viability of a coursework decision, review a method, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written.

A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay, a personal project or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text, data or diagrams for submission. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is an academic integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it.

The materials rule applies across both systems. No tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The official source should be referenced and linked instead, which is why this page carries no attachments and keeps asking the reader to confirm detail against their own school's documents.

On who may teach: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutor can promise a grade.

process.title: Bring a recent marked script per child
process.description: The diagnosis is far quicker and far more accurate with real marked work in front of it. For the Diploma side, bring the current coursework plan as well, because the decision behind it is often what is capping the grade rather than the writing.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: Forty to sixty minutes of subject-specific checks, no card details taken, and a written summary afterwards naming what is wrong and the first three targets. The summary is yours whether or not you book anything else, which is the point of making it free.

process.title: Act on the classification, not the impression
process.description: Lost marks are sorted into content, method, command term and time, and only the first needs teaching. Most students find that the majority of their losses were method and command term, which changes what the next eight weeks should cost as well as contain.

process.title: Separate the two children's plans
process.description: IGCSE coaching is about writing for a mark scheme; MYP and Diploma coaching is about reading descriptors and writing to them. Treating both children as one ability is how a Year 11 success becomes a Grade 11 surprise.

process.title: Re-check once, mid-year
process.description: In a small cohort, calibration has to come from outside, so one further external check against the same criteria tells you whether the recurring causes have changed. That is a cheaper form of reassurance than continuous weekly tuition bought for comfort.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis you can run yourself
whyPoints.description: The opening checks on this page are published, and several can be run at home this week without subject expertise. A diagnosis only a provider can perform is a sales mechanism; one a parent can replicate is a genuine starting point.

whyPoints.title: Both marking logics treated separately
whyPoints.description: IGCSE papers credit identifiable steps; MYP and Diploma internal work is judged against descriptor bands. Coaching the two the same way produces a Diploma student with beautiful working who never addresses a criterion.

whyPoints.title: The transition gaps named in advance
whyPoints.description: A Diploma course assumes algebraic manipulation is automatic, recall is in place, and a student can read for structure and effect. Each gap closes in a defined number of weeks when named in the summer rather than met in the spring.

whyPoints.title: Calibration from outside a small cohort
whyPoints.description: A position inside a class of twelve says little about absolute standing, and a sole subject teacher has no colleague to moderate internal work against. In this emirate an external second reading is often unavailable any other way.

whyPoints.title: Written output, not a verbal impression
whyPoints.description: Every diagnostic session produces a written summary with named causes and three targets, which is a document a family can compare against later. A verbal impression after a session is worth almost nothing a week afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits and no borrowed credentials
whyPoints.description: Explaining criteria, testing viability and feeding back on the student's own draft: yes. Producing any part of assessed work: never. No promised grades, no syllabus documents as downloads, and no claim of approval from any regulator or board.

faqs.question: How long does a proper subject diagnosis take?
faqs.answer: About forty minutes, and it consists of specific checks rather than a general conversation. Each check is designed to separate two explanations: factorising without a calculator separates algebraic fluency from calculator dependence, a timed moles conversion separates understanding from speed, describing a process rather than naming it separates knowledge from written habit. Between them they cover most of the ways a grade goes missing, and the output should be a short written summary rather than a verbal impression.

faqs.question: What can I check at home in Khuzam before booking anything?
faqs.answer: Four things, none needing subject expertise. Ask your child to explain, for three lost marks on a recent script, what the marker wanted and why they did not provide it. Time one question and ask whether that pace would finish the paper. For any coursework, ask them to state the research question in one sentence. And ask what the command term on their last long answer demanded. Hesitation on the third and fourth is the most reliable early warning available.

faqs.question: Why does my child's school report look better than their mock?
faqs.answer: Often because the cohort is small. Ras Al Khaimah's private-school set is compact and a Diploma class may have a dozen students or fewer, so a position inside it carries almost no information about absolute standing against a mark scheme. Comparisons within a tiny group can describe a student as strong when their performance against the published criteria is middling, and the gap shows up for the first time in a timed mock paper late in the course.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE and the IB need different kinds of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the marking logics differ. An IGCSE paper is marked against a published list of creditable points, so the technique that pays is making every step visible: method, intermediate values, units, the term matched. MYP and Diploma internal work is judged against descriptor bands, where marks are lost a band at a time and a whole criterion strand left unaddressed costs a predictable chunk. The same student can be strong at one and weak at the other.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma course assume my child already knows?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. In Mathematics, that algebraic manipulation is automatic rather than achievable, because a Diploma question uses factorising as one step inside a longer problem. In the sciences, that recall is in place so the course can spend its time on analysis, uncertainty and extended evaluation. In English, that the student can already read for structure and effect. Each of those gaps is predictable and closes in a defined number of weeks when it is named early.

faqs.question: When is the best time to check for transition gaps?
faqs.answer: The summer between Year 11 and Grade 11, because it is the only block of time nobody has already claimed and the only period when a student can learn new material without revising old material at the same time. A short diagnostic session plus three or four weeks on one named gap removes the autumn confusion that otherwise gets diagnosed as a general struggle with the Diploma in the following spring.

faqs.question: Can an internal assessment be rescued once it is written?
faqs.answer: It depends what capped it. An IGCSE coursework piece can usually be improved by doing more of what the task asked. A Diploma internal assessment often cannot, because the ceiling was set by the topic, the method or the source material: an exploration with no mathematics to develop, a method that will not yield analysable data, a thin or stale article. The only repair is to change the decision, which is why one early viability session is worth several late ones.

faqs.question: Do command terms mean the same thing in both systems?
faqs.answer: The simple ones broadly do. State wants a fact with no reasoning; describe wants features or stages without cause; explain wants a mechanism. The divergence is in the heavier terms: Diploma papers lean harder on evaluate, discuss, to what extent and justify, and expect a stated position supported from both sides, which an IGCSE student can score reasonably well without ever producing. Check the published list for the specific code or subject, since the lists are per subject and revised.

faqs.question: Is there any point in tutoring if my child is already doing well?
faqs.answer: In a small emirate there can be, and it is a different purchase from remedial work. One external check a year against the published criteria tells a family whether apparent strength inside a cohort of twelve corresponds to absolute strength, and gives a sole subject teacher a second reading on whether internal work is where it should be. That is calibration rather than tuition, and it is cheaper than a panic purchase in the final term.

faqs.question: What should the written summary after a diagnosis contain?
faqs.answer: Three things: the causes of the lost marks, classified into content, method, command term and time; the first three targets in order; and what the next eight weeks should contain. If a provider cannot give you that in writing after a first session, the session was a sales call. The classification matters most, because most students discover that the majority of their losses were method and command term rather than knowledge, which changes both the plan and its cost.

faqs.question: My child panics in timed conditions. Is that diagnosable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually a pacing problem wearing an emotional costume. Students frequently have no idea whether their working speed would finish a paper, because homework is untimed. Timing a single question and extrapolating gives a number, and a number is far less frightening than a feeling. Where the pace genuinely will not finish, the repair is question-selection strategy and method efficiency rather than reassurance, and it responds within a few weeks of deliberate practice.

faqs.question: How do I tell a good tutor from a confident one?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions and one follow-up. Which syllabus code did you last teach and when; which papers did your students sit; which topics did that cohort lose marks on; and do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Then, for Diploma work: have you supervised an internal assessment through to submission, and what did you not do for the student. The last answer is the most revealing one available, and clarity there matters more than confidence anywhere else.

faqs.question: Is proximity worth anything for a Khuzam family?
faqs.answer: Getting to a tutor is not the problem here, since the city school cluster is a short drive away. The problem is how few people in the emirate have taught a particular Higher Level option or a less common IGCSE code, and that some of the best-placed local teachers are barred from tutoring students at their own school. Teaching over live video changes the question from who is nearby to who has taught the course, which is the variable that matters.

faqs.question: Will the tutor talk to my child's school?
faqs.answer: Not on the school's behalf and not in place of it. What is useful and entirely appropriate is for a family to pass on the school's own documents, the subject guides, the internal assessment calendar and the IGCSE codes and tiers, so that the tutoring plan is built around the student's real year rather than a generic one. Any contact with the school is the family's to initiate; a tutor working around the school rather than with it is a warning sign.

faqs.question: Can you promise my child will improve by a grade?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. Grade boundaries are set after a series on the basis of that series' papers, so an outcome cannot be sold in advance. What tuition reliably changes is the precision of practice, the student's reading of command terms and criteria, and the gap between what they know and what reaches the page. That is a smaller claim than a promised grade and it is one a family can verify as the recurring error causes either change or do not.

intro.heading: Two systems, one subject name, and the confusion that costs marks
paragraphs: A family in Mina Al Arab asking for help with chemistry may mean one of at least four things. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 at Extended tier. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1. IB Diploma Chemistry at Standard Level. IB Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level. Those four share a periodic table and diverge in nearly everything that decides a grade: paper structure, what the marking rewards, whether there is an independent investigation, how practical skills are examined, and which past material is even relevant.

A tutor who does not establish which one, in the first conversation, is guessing. And the guess has a cost that shows up late. A student given Cambridge-style structured recall practice for a Diploma paper that wanted extended reasoning will feel well prepared and score poorly. A Diploma-style open investigation offered to an IGCSE candidate wastes hours on something that will never be assessed, because the IGCSE route tests practical understanding through a written paper rather than through a project. The fix costs five minutes and a look at the statement of entry.

This page is therefore organised around the differences rather than around the service. It covers the subjects where the two systems diverge most, the syllabus codes that determine which past papers are the right ones, how practical and coursework elements are handled on each side, and a question nobody in this market addresses: what a tutor may legitimately supply a student, given that syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are the boards' copyright. None of that is advanced knowledge; it is administrative detail that happens to decide outcomes, which is exactly the kind of thing a commercial page usually leaves out.

That last point deserves a sentence here because it is a real distinction between providers. We do not host, reproduce or supply board material as downloads. We reference it, cite the official source, and link out, and the papers a student works from should come from their school or from the board's own channels. A provider handing over folders of scanned material is doing something that is not theirs to do, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one.

On delivery, since the search says near me: IB Gram teaches Mina Al Arab students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not place a tutor at a UAE address, and in-person visiting is a service we run only in India. In a small emirate with a small private-school sector, that is what makes it possible to put an actual Diploma Higher Level specialist and an actual Cambridge Extended specialist in front of two children in the same household, rather than one person approximating both.

sections.heading: What "near me" means when the request is a named syllabus
paragraphs: Proximity solves a real problem: it makes somebody accountable and available. In a small emirate it also creates a different problem, because the smaller the local pool the more likely it is that the person who can reach you teaches the subject generally rather than the syllabus specifically. In Mina Al Arab, where the private-school sector across the whole emirate is modest, the chance that the nearest available tutor has taught the exact specification your child is entered for is not high.

The distinction is not pedantic. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 test much the same physics with different paper structures and different mark-scheme phrasing. Diploma Physics at Higher Level assumes a quantitative treatment of uncertainty that neither IGCSE requires. A tutor teaching physics in general will cover the content and miss the thing the paper actually pays for, and the student will discover that in a hall.

So the honest reframing of the search is this: what you want is not somebody nearby, it is somebody specific. The qualities proximity is standing in for are accountability, consistency and responsiveness, and those come from a named tutor who stays the same, a written plan, and a review against marked evidence. None of the three is geographic.

IB Gram does not place a tutor at an address in Ras Al Khaimah or anywhere in the UAE; in-person visiting is a service we run only in India. What online delivery makes possible in a household running two systems is the thing that matters most here: a Cambridge Extended specialist for one child and a Diploma Higher Level specialist for the other, on the same evening, from two different people who each do one of those things properly.

sections.heading: The same subject under two systems, side by side
paragraphs: Put the two systems next to each other and the pattern is consistent across the sciences. Content overlaps substantially at the foundation. Assessment diverges sharply. IGCSE concentrates almost everything in timed written papers, including the examination of practical understanding, which is typically tested through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than through assessed experimental work. The Diploma splits the grade between written papers and an independent investigation marked against lettered criteria.

That single structural difference changes what good preparation looks like. For IGCSE, time is best spent on timed questions marked to the published scheme, because that is where every mark lives. For the Diploma, the first-year priority is the investigation, because a well-chosen research question is worth more than any amount of write-up polish applied later and because it has a school deadline that the written papers do not.

The second difference is the marking logic. An IGCSE mark scheme awards points for specified content: the named process, the correct unit, the comparison made explicit. Diploma criteria describe a standard of work in bands, and the student is placed in the band their work matches. A student who is excellent at hitting mark-scheme points can produce an investigation that is correct throughout and still land mid-band, because the criteria were asking about something the student never considered.

The table below sets this out. It is deliberately about structure rather than about percentages, because exact weightings belong in the official subject documents your school holds, and publishing them from memory would be precisely the kind of unsourced precision this project avoids. sections.heading: The code problem: which past papers are the right ones
paragraphs: Of all the avoidable failures in tutoring, working from the wrong past papers is the most common and the easiest to fix. A parent says chemistry, a tutor finds chemistry papers, and three months of practice happens against a specification the student is not entered for. The content will mostly overlap. The paper structure, the question phrasing and the mark scheme language will not, and those are what the student is being trained on.

The remedy is a five-minute check at the start. Take the statement of entry, not the textbook, because schools change board between cohorts and shelves lag years behind. Read off the board and the code for each subject. For Diploma subjects, establish the level and the current subject guide, because specifications are revised and material for a previous version teaches an outdated structure. Write all of it down and give it to the tutor.

The second part of the remedy is where the material comes from, and it deserves more attention than it gets. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are the boards' copyright. A tutor who hands over folders of scanned papers is redistributing material that is not theirs, and for unreleased material that is a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright one. The legitimate route is the student's school, which holds access as a centre, and the boards' own published channels.

Our practice, stated plainly: we cite and link official sources, we work from material the student legitimately holds, and we do not host or supply board documents as downloads. That is less convenient than an archive, and it is the correct position. The table below maps the common codes so the first conversation can be specific; the material itself comes from your school.

sections.heading: Practical science: a written paper against an investigation
paragraphs: This is where the two systems diverge most and where preparation most often goes wrong. The IGCSE route generally tests practical understanding through writing: a paper that asks how an experiment would be carried out, what would be measured, which variables controlled, what the sources of error are. It rewards precision of description. A student who can do the experiment but cannot specify it loses marks they would never lose in a laboratory.

The Diploma requires something categorically different: an investigation the student designs, carries out and writes up, marked against lettered criteria with published maximums. Here the marks are decided before the writing. An investigation with one uncontrolled variable - temperature drifting, a concentration prepared imprecisely, a timing method dominated by human reaction - limits the analysis and evaluation criteria permanently, no matter how carefully the report is produced.

Both are teachable and neither prepares for the other. The IGCSE skill is a writing skill: six focused sessions on describing a method to a repeatable standard will usually show up in a mark, which makes it one of the best-value interventions available in the whole qualification. The Diploma skill is a design skill, and the highest-value hour is spent narrowing a research question before anything is measured.

For a household in Mina Al Arab running both, the practical implication is that the two children need different work from different people at different points in the year. The IGCSE candidate needs method-writing practice in the spring of Year 11. The Diploma student needs investigation design in the first year, long before any deadline makes it urgent. Buying the same thing for both, at the same time, is the commonest way two-system households waste money.

sections.heading: Mathematics from 0580 to Analysis and Approaches
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where the two systems join most directly, and where the join is most often mishandled. A Diploma mathematics course assumes Extended-tier fluency, not Core, and assumes it is automatic rather than achievable. A student who rearranges an equation correctly but slowly will manage at Standard Level and find Higher Level unrelenting, because the pace of the course never allows the backlog to clear.

Additional Mathematics 0606 is the bridge and its presence or absence is the single most useful fact about a student entering Diploma mathematics. Where it was taken and went well, calculus, logarithms and kinematics are familiar and the first Diploma term is a continuation. Where it was not taken, there is a specific, finite gap - differentiation, function transformations, logarithmic manipulation - that a focused block closes in six to ten sessions.

The route decision deserves evidence rather than instinct. Analysis and Approaches is algebra-heavy and proof-oriented; Applications and Interpretation is statistics-led and technology-heavy, genuinely rigorous, and the better fit for a large number of capable students who are not fast algebraists. The practical test is narrow: time a set of 0580 Extended manipulation questions. Accuracy with slow speed points one way, accuracy at pace with curiosity about why a method works points the other.

Then check the destination, because some university courses specify Analysis and Approaches by name and requirements change. Check the current ones rather than relying on an older sibling's experience, and check them before the option form goes in. A route change early in the first Diploma year is awkward; a route change in the second year is usually impossible.

sections.heading: English and the humanities: where the discipline changes
paragraphs: In the sciences the two systems differ in assessment. In English they differ in what is being assessed. First Language English 0500 rewards accurate reading and fluent, well-organised writing, and a student who writes clearly tends to do well. The Diploma's language courses reward argument about how texts work on readers, across literary and non-literary material, with an Individual Oral recorded in a school window and, at Higher Level, an additional essay with its own internal deadlines.

The student most at risk in that transition is the one who did well at IGCSE. Fluency was rewarded, so fluency became the strategy, and fluency alone lands mid-band in a Diploma course that wants analysis of technique and effect supported by quotation. The shift takes a term of fortnightly work rather than a fortnight of intensive work, which is why it belongs in the first Diploma year.

In economics and business the continuity is stronger. Diagram accuracy decides the analysis marks on both sides, and an evaluation paragraph that weighs competing effects rather than restating a case separates the top band in both. What the Diploma adds is internally assessed commentary or research work spread across the course, which needs scheduling. A student who treats those as end-of-term tasks meets three of them in the same fortnight as everything else.

Theory of Knowledge has no IGCSE equivalent at all and is therefore the component students handle worst. It is assessed against published criteria on a prescribed title, and the commonest failure is writing about knowledge in general rather than answering the title. A tutor can discuss the title, question the argument and respond to a draft. Nobody writes any part of it, including a paragraph offered as an illustration.

sections.heading: What a tutor may legitimately give a student
paragraphs: This question has two halves and almost nobody in this market addresses either. The first is material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are the boards' copyright. Referencing them, citing them and linking to the official source is legitimate. Hosting them, reproducing them or supplying them as downloads is not, and for unreleased material it carries a malpractice exposure in addition to the copyright problem. A provider with an archive to hand over is not being generous; they are distributing something that is not theirs.

The practical effect for a family is straightforward. The legitimate source of past material is the school, which holds access as an examination centre, and the boards' own published channels. A tutor works from what the student legitimately holds. That is marginally less convenient and it is the correct arrangement, and it is worth knowing which kind of provider you are dealing with.

The second half is assessed work, and the line is sharper on the Diploma side because internally assessed components can be ghost-written in a way that terminal papers cannot. A tutor may explain the criteria, question the plan or the method, point out where a conclusion exceeds the evidence, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite prose, supply data or edit it to completion. Nobody at IB Gram will do any of those things.

This is not an abstract concern in this search market. A site currently ranking on these queries advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale at a published price. The consequences of that transaction fall on the student, not on the seller: submitted work must be the student's own, and a breach is an academic-honesty matter with outcomes that can end a Diploma. Saying so explicitly is one of the few genuine differentiators available on a page like this.

process.description: One 45 to 60-minute one-to-one session over live video, no card details, no obligation. The useful test is whether the tutor can name the criteria or the mark-scheme language for that specific syllabus without looking it up.

process.title: Agree a block per child, with its own target
process.description: Different cadences for different systems: method-writing practice in the IGCSE spring, investigation design in the Diploma first year. One plan covering both children at the same intensity is almost always wrong for at least one of them.

process.title: Review on timed work in the diagnosed area
process.description: At the end of the block the student sits timed questions, or submits a draft against the criteria, and the result is compared with the start. If nothing moved, the plan or the match was wrong. We would rather hear that at week three than at week twelve.

whyPoints.title: Specifications treated as different courses
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1 and Diploma Chemistry are three courses, not three names for one. We establish the board, the code and the level before teaching anything, because practice against the wrong specification feels productive and is not.

whyPoints.title: Two specialists for a two-system household
whyPoints.description: A Mina Al Arab family running an IGCSE candidate and a Diploma student needs two different people who each do one thing properly. Online delivery makes that possible on the same evening; a local search generally produces one person approximating both.

whyPoints.title: Board material cited, never redistributed
whyPoints.description: Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to the boards. We reference and link them and work from material the student legitimately holds. A provider handing over an archive of scanned papers is distributing what is not theirs.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Criteria explained, plans questioned, drafts responded to. No writing, no rewriting, no supplied data, no completion. One site ranking on these searches sells finished Internal Assessments at a published price, and the risk in that sits entirely with the student.

whyPoints.title: Practical skills taught as the two different things they are
whyPoints.description: The IGCSE skill is specifying a method precisely enough to be repeated. The Diploma skill is designing an investigation that can be controlled. Six sessions on the first and one on the second are both cheap, and neither substitutes for the other.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no UAE office. No figure appears on this page without a source and a date.

faqs.question: Does it really matter whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Enough that a tutor should know before the first session. The two boards test much the same content with different paper structures and different mark-scheme phrasing, and past papers have to match the code rather than the subject name: Cambridge 0625 against Pearson 4PH1, Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1. Some Pearson courses also run modularly, with units banked across sittings, which changes the whole shape of a revision plan. Read the board off the statement of entry, because schools change board between cohorts and textbooks lag behind.

faqs.question: How different is Diploma Chemistry from IGCSE Chemistry?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps at the foundation and the assessment diverges sharply. Mole arithmetic appears in both and is assumed automatic at Diploma level. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are new depth rather than new material. The structural difference is the investigation: IGCSE generally tests practical understanding through a written paper, while the Diploma requires a self-designed investigation marked against lettered criteria. A student excellent at IGCSE-style structured recall can score mid-band on that component without ever understanding why.

faqs.question: Where should my child get past papers from?
faqs.answer: From their school, which holds access as an examination centre, and from the boards' own published channels. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the boards' copyright, so a tutor who hands over folders of scanned material is distributing what is not theirs, and for unreleased material that is a malpractice exposure as well as a copyright problem. We cite and link official sources and work from material the student legitimately holds. It is less convenient and it is the correct arrangement.

faqs.question: My two children are on different systems. Do we need two tutors?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, and that is the honest answer rather than an upsell. An IGCSE candidate needs timed-paper technique marked against a specific mark scheme, in the spring of Year 11. A Diploma student needs investigation design and criteria literacy, in the first year, long before anything is urgent. Those are different skills at different times, and one person covering both tends to do each shallowly. Two consecutive one-hour online sessions on the same evening is the arrangement most two-system households in Ras Al Khaimah settle on.

faqs.question: What does the written practical paper reward for a candidate in Mina Al Arab?
faqs.answer: Precision of description. A question asks how an experiment would be carried out, and the marks go to what is varied, what is controlled, what is measured and by what means, in enough detail that someone else could repeat it. Students who have done the experiment lose marks because they summarise rather than specify. It is a writing skill rather than a laboratory skill, which is why six focused sessions on method writing is one of the best-value interventions available anywhere in the IGCSE sciences.

faqs.question: Why does an uncontrolled variable matter so much in a Diploma investigation?
faqs.answer: Because it caps the later criteria regardless of how good the report is. If temperature drifted, or a concentration was prepared imprecisely, or the timing method was dominated by human reaction, then the analysis cannot be sound and the evaluation becomes an account of a flawed design. Those criteria carry stated maximums and no amount of editing recovers them afterwards. This is why the highest-value hour in Diploma science tutoring is spent narrowing and controlling the question before anything is measured.

faqs.question: Does Additional Mathematics 0606 matter for Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: It is the strongest single predictor of comfort in Analysis and Approaches, because it introduces calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and kinematics a year early and builds the algebraic speed the Diploma assumes rather than teaches. It is not a requirement and plenty of students manage without it. Where it was not taken, the gap is specific and finite - differentiation, function transformations, logarithmic manipulation - and a focused block closes most of it in six to ten sessions, best done in the summer.

faqs.question: How do the two grading systems compare?
faqs.answer: They are not really comparable and treating them as such causes confusion in households running both. IGCSE reports 9-1 per subject. The Diploma reports 1-7 per subject with additional points from the core, up to 45 overall. A grade 7 at IGCSE and a 7 in a Diploma subject are different achievements measured against different standards and different cohorts. The useful comparison is against the entry requirement for whatever comes next, not between siblings' report cards.

faqs.question: Which mathematics route should a student coming from 0580 Extended choose?
faqs.answer: Decide on evidence. Time a set of 0580 Extended algebraic manipulation questions. Accuracy with slow speed points towards Applications and Interpretation or Standard Level Analysis and Approaches. Accuracy at reasonable pace, with genuine curiosity about why a method works, points to Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. A good result in Additional Mathematics 0606 is the strongest available signal. Then check whether any target degree specifies Analysis and Approaches by name, because some do and requirements change.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on an Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the legitimate centre of the work. A tutor explains what each criterion rewards, asks questions about the method, points out where a conclusion exceeds the data, and responds in writing to the student's own draft. What a tutor cannot do is write a section, rewrite prose, supply data or edit it to completion, and nobody at IB Gram will. Submitted work has to be the student's own. A provider offering completed assessments is selling an academic-honesty risk that falls on the student.

faqs.question: Our school changed exam board between year groups. What do we check?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry, for every subject, and then the code for each. Paper structures, mark-scheme language and the correct past material all follow from the board, so a change between cohorts invalidates an older sibling's resources entirely. For Diploma subjects, also confirm the current subject guide version, because specifications are revised and material written for a previous version teaches an outdated structure. Five minutes of checking at the start prevents a term of practice against the wrong specification.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge coachable at all?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. The essay responds to a prescribed title and is assessed against published criteria, and the commonest failure is writing about knowledge in general instead of answering the title in front of them. The teachable skill is constructing one argument that a counter-position could genuinely challenge, then testing it with examples that do specific work rather than decorate the prose. A tutor discusses the title, questions the argument and responds to drafts. Nobody writes any part of it, including sample paragraphs.

faqs.question: Why is English harder to transition than the sciences?
faqs.answer: Because the discipline changes rather than the difficulty. First Language English 0500 rewards accurate reading and fluent, structured writing, so a student who writes well does well. The Diploma's language courses reward argument about how texts operate on readers, across literary and non-literary material, with an oral component recorded in a school window. The student most at risk is the one who succeeded at IGCSE through fluency, because fluency alone lands mid-band. The shift takes a term of fortnightly work, not a fortnight of intensive work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in Ras Al Khaimah realistically cover a specific syllabus code?
faqs.answer: Locally, often not, and the reason is the size of the pool rather than anything about the tutors. The emirate has a comparatively small private-school sector, so each specification at each level is taught in a handful of settings, and the few experienced teachers are mostly committed in the evenings. Working over live video widens the choice to everyone who teaches that exact code properly. IB Gram does not place tutors at UAE addresses; in-person visiting is a service we run only in India.

intro.heading: What a syllabus-level tutor does differently in an hour
paragraphs: There are two kinds of tutoring hour. In the first, a tutor re-explains a topic the student has already heard explained, more slowly and more kindly, and everyone leaves feeling better. In the second, the tutor opens a marked paper, finds the three question types that cost the most marks, identifies whether the loss was content, method, command-term misreading or timing, and fixes one of them. Both hours cost the same. Only one of them changes a grade.

The second kind requires something specific: knowledge of the assessment instrument, not just the subject. An IB Diploma student and an IGCSE student in the same house in Seih Al Uraibi are being measured by completely different machinery. The Diploma student has internal assessment marked against criterion letters with published descriptors, papers with fixed percentage weightings that differ between Higher and Standard Level, and a core of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay with word limits that are themselves marked. The IGCSE student has externally examined papers, tiering decisions that cap or raise the available grade, and board-specific conventions that change between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel.

A tutor who knows the subject but not the instrument gives good explanations and leaves marks on the table. A student can understand electrolysis perfectly and still lose half the marks on an electrolysis question because the command term was describe rather than explain, or because the half-equation was written without balancing charge. Those are not knowledge failures. They are instrument failures, and they are the most fixable thing in a tutoring hour. The same pattern shows up in English, where a student who can discuss a poem fluently loses the analysis marks because the answer names the device and never reaches its effect on the reader, and in Economics, where fluent prose sits beneath a diagram with unlabelled axes and earns nothing for the diagram at all.

This page is therefore organised by assessment rather than by neighbourhood. It sets out the paper structures and weightings a Ras Al Khaimah family deals with, the command terms that decide marks, the criterion letters an internal assessment is actually marked against, and a method for working past papers that produces learning rather than a score. Where there is a trap, it is named.

One practical matter first, because the search phrase deserves an honest answer. Near me, in Seih Al Uraibi, returns a small list, and once you narrow it to a named component it gets smaller still. IB Gram does not solve that by sending someone to your address; there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and that service exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is what makes a component-level match possible at all in a market this size.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against lettered criteria by the teacher and moderated externally, and externally examined papers with fixed weightings. The core is where self-managed deadlines bite hardest.

Supervision capacity for the Extended Essay is correspondingly spread, and a supervisor may be allocated outside their subject specialism because the cohort is small.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced throughout, with four criteria per subject group and no external papers unless the school enters students for eAssessment. Students arrive in the Diploma fluent in criteria language and sometimes short on timed-paper stamina, which is the single most common transition problem reported by Diploma teachers.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is sharper here than in a larger market because there are fewer parallel classes to absorb a struggling student. A Seih Al Uraibi student moving from MYP into Diploma Mathematics usually needs algebraic fluency rebuilt before anything else, and it is cheaper to do that in the summer than in November of the first Diploma year.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel
programmes.description: Externally examined at the end of two years. Cambridge subjects are identified by four-digit codes and several are tiered Core or Extended, which caps or raises the available grade. Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1 or 4CH1, and the board's formula-sheet and tiering policies differ from Cambridge's in ways that change revision priorities.
programmes.countryNote: RAK city schools use a mixture of boards, and families often learn which one applies only when the statement of entry arrives. For a tutor this is the first question, not a detail: coaching Cambridge 0580 technique to a Pearson 4MA1 candidate wastes the hours spent on recall the formula sheet would have supplied.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.subjectsIntro: IB Diploma subjects, described by where the marks sit rather than by what the course covers. Weightings differ by level and should be confirmed against the current subject guide through your child's school.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation carry the Higher Level load. The exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Most lost marks in the exploration sit in reflection, where students describe what they did instead of evaluating what it showed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use dominate. Graphical display calculator technique is examinable in itself, and candidates lose marks by presenting a correct result without the command the examiner can see. Modelling questions reward stating assumptions explicitly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth in several topics, and the data-analysis questions punish sloppy uncertainty handling. Definitions are marked literally: a definition of field strength that omits per unit mass or charge earns nothing, however well the student understands it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where Higher Level separates from Standard. Students lose marks writing mechanisms without curly arrows starting from a lone pair or a bond, and on calculations where significant figures are not carried consistently.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem and precision is the solution. Extended-response questions want a named mechanism in sequence, and examiners do not credit paraphrase of defined terms. Statistical reasoning in data questions is routinely weaker than the content knowledge around it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is marked separately from the prose: axes labelled, curves labelled, shift drawn, new equilibrium identified. Higher Level adds quantitative questions where candidates who have practised only essays struggle. Evaluation marks need a stated condition, not a balanced-sounding final paragraph.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus material is the dividing line. Candidates who answer from the textbook rather than from the case lose application and analysis marks even when the theory is right. Tools must be used on the data provided, with a conclusion that follows from it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper-based analysis both reward a line of argument sustained across a text, with quotation followed by effect on the reader. Higher Level adds the essay component, where structure and a controlling thesis matter more than coverage of the work.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed on an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. Students lose marks by writing about the topic rather than about knowledge, which is a habit a tutor can break quickly by making every claim name its knower, its method and its limit.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research essay with a formal supervision process and a reflection requirement. Most weak essays fail on research question scope rather than on writing. A tutor can interrogate the question and the method; the essay itself must be the student's own work.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE side of the same household, described by paper rather than by topic list. Codes are given because the paper structure depends on them.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics 0580 / 4MA1
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Extended candidates lose most marks on functions, graph transformations and conditional probability. Method marks are available almost everywhere, so unshown working is the largest single avoidable loss. Pearson supplies a formula sheet Cambridge does not.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics 0625 / 4PH1
igcseSubjects.description: Circuits are the standard failure point, especially potential dividers and distinguishing potential difference across a component from current through it. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards method writing with named control variables.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry 0620 / 4CH1
igcseSubjects.description: Moles calculations and qualitative-analysis tables carry a disproportionate share of lost marks. Electrolysis half-equations must balance charge as well as atoms, and reaction conditions are asked for far more often than nomenclature.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology 0610 / 4BI1
igcseSubjects.description: Transport, enzymes and inheritance diagrams reward defined vocabulary used precisely. Six-mark questions need a structured mechanism rather than a list, and graph-description questions want the trend quantified from the axes.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics 0455 / 4EC1
igcseSubjects.description: Data-response questions must use the figures in the extract. Candidates import textbook examples and lose application marks. Diagrams are marked on labelling and the position of the new equilibrium, not on neatness.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science 0478
igcseSubjects.description: The board's own pseudocode conventions are examinable, so students who code fluently in Python still lose marks. Trace tables under timed conditions and the validation-versus-verification distinction are the two reliable mark earners.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
igcseSubjects.description: Calculus, logarithms and the binomial theorem at a depth 0580 never reaches, taken as a bridge to A Level. Teaching capacity for this paper in the northern emirates is genuinely thin, which is why it appears on this page at all.

igcseSubjects.name: English First Language 0500 / 4EA1
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing is marked on register and audience, so a strong essay written in place of the requested letter caps its own mark. Analysis answers need quotation then effect, expressed in terms of the reader.
