sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary the mark scheme obeys
paragraphs: The fastest grade improvement available to most students has nothing to do with knowing more. It comes from reading the first word of the question properly. Both the IB and the Cambridge and Pearson boards publish defined command terms, and mark schemes follow them literally rather than generously.

State and describe are not synonyms. State wants a fact with no justification and no credit for extra; describe wants the features in sequence; explain wants a mechanism with a because in it; evaluate wants a judgement with a stated condition; discuss wants both sides before the judgement; justify wants a reason specifically supporting the stated conclusion. A student who explains when the paper said state has written something true that earns nothing extra, and lost the time. A student who describes when the paper said explain has written half an answer and will not see why the mark was withheld.

In the sciences this is compounded by definitional strictness. A Physics definition that omits per unit mass, or a Chemistry answer that gives the reagent but not the condition, is incomplete by the scheme even where the understanding behind it is sound. In Economics an evaluation that lists advantages and disadvantages without arriving at a conditional judgement cannot reach the top band however fluent the prose. In English, analyse requires effect on the reader rather than restatement of the device.

A tutor's job here is mechanical and quick. Take the last marked paper, list every question where marks were lost, and sort the losses into content, command term, method shown and timing. Most students find the command-term column is the largest, and it is the one that closes inside two or three sessions of deliberate drilling.
bullets: State: a fact, no justification, no credit for extra
Describe: features in sequence, no causal mechanism needed
Explain: a mechanism, with causation made explicit
Evaluate and justify: a judgement with a stated condition
Analyse in English: quotation, then effect on the reader

sections.heading: How the papers are weighted, and why that changes a revision plan
paragraphs: Revision time should follow the weighting, and students almost never allocate it that way. They revise what they enjoy, or what they last failed, rather than what is worth the most marks per hour invested. The table sets out the component structures a Seih Al Uraibi family deals with so the allocation can be made deliberately.

Two features of the IB structure matter most. First, internal assessment is worth a meaningful share of the final subject grade and is marked against criteria the student can read in advance, which makes it the most controllable marks on the course. Second, Higher Level is not Standard Level plus an extra paper in every subject; the additional component and the extra depth change what the earlier papers can ask, so an HL student revising from SL material is under-prepared in a way that is invisible until a past paper is attempted.

On the IGCSE side the decisive structural feature is tiering. A Cambridge Core entry caps the available grade; an Extended entry raises the ceiling and raises the difficulty of the questions on the same topics. A tiering decision made in Year 10 on the basis of a bad term can hold down a student who has since improved, and it is worth asking the school to revisit rather than assuming it is fixed. Pearson's single-tier papers in several subjects remove that decision but introduce their own difference, including a formula sheet in maths that changes what has to be memorised.

Confirm every weighting against the current subject guide or specification through your child's school before building a plan on it. Boards revise structures, and a weighting copied from a tutoring page is exactly the kind of detail that goes quietly out of date.

sections.heading: Criterion letters: what an internal assessment is actually marked on
paragraphs: IB internal assessment is not marked out of a number. It is marked against lettered criteria, each with its own descriptors and its own mark allocation, and the student can read those descriptors before writing a word. No competitor page in this market names a single criterion letter, which is remarkable given that this is the most controllable component on the course.

The practical consequence is that a student can audit their own draft. If a criterion rewards personal engagement, a draft with no evidence of independent decision-making cannot score in the top band regardless of how good the mathematics is. If a criterion rewards reflection, a conclusion that summarises what was done rather than evaluating what it showed sits in the middle band by definition. Students lose marks in predictable places, and the places are written down.

This is also where the academic-honesty boundary has to be explicit. A tutor can ask whether the research question is answerable, point at a criterion and ask the student to show where their draft meets it, and explain why a paragraph does not. A tutor cannot write, draft, complete or produce the internal assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed piece. IB Gram does not do that, and at least one provider ranking for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright. That is a malpractice trigger for the student, not a time-saver.

Criterion names and mark allocations differ between subjects and are revised periodically, so take them from the current subject guide via your child's teacher rather than from any website. What does not change is the method: read the descriptors, audit the draft against them, and rewrite the weakest criterion first.

sections.heading: Working a past paper so that it teaches something
paragraphs: Most students use past papers badly, and the failure is consistent enough to be fixed in one session. They do the paper with the book open, stop when they get stuck, check answers rather than mark schemes, and record a score. That produces a number and no learning.

The method that works has four steps and the third is the one everyone skips. Sit the whole paper in the correct duration with nothing open. Mark it against the official mark scheme rather than an answer key, because the scheme shows which words earn the mark and an answer key does not. Then adjudicate honestly, which for most students means having someone challenge their generous self-marking, since the gap between what they meant and what they wrote is exactly where the lost marks live. Finally, re-sit only the questions that were lost, a few days later, cold.

The adjudication step is the argument for a tutor rather than a study group. A student marking alone will award themselves the mark for an answer that contains the right idea in the wrong words, which is precisely the answer an examiner rejects. A tutor who knows the scheme's language will not, and after three or four papers of that friction the student starts writing in the scheme's terms unprompted. That is the point at which past papers stop being assessment and start being teaching.

Volume matters less than parents assume. Six papers worked this way beat twenty papers scored and filed. For a Seih Al Uraibi student with a full school timetable and a commute, six is also achievable in the final weeks, which twenty is not.

sections.heading: Mathematics AA or AI, and the consequence for university
paragraphs: The most consequential subject decision an IB student in Ras Al Khaimah makes is between Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, and it is frequently made on the wrong basis.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-based route, with calculus at its centre. Applications and Interpretation is the statistical and modelling route, with technology use integral to the course. Neither is the easy option; they are different courses with different demands, and a student strong at manipulation and weak at interpretation will find AI harder than AA despite its reputation. The honest test is what the student is good at, cross-checked against what their intended degree requires.

The consequence sits at admission. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and a student arriving with AI can find a course closed regardless of their points total. Requirements vary by university and by year, so the only safe method is to read the current entry requirements for the specific programmes under consideration, including any UAE universities, and work backwards. This is also why the choice should be made in the MYP to Diploma transition rather than revisited in the second Diploma year, when a change is disruptive and sometimes impossible.

For a tutor the difference is practical. An AA student needs proof technique, algebraic fluency and calculus confidence. An AI student needs statistical reasoning, modelling discipline and calculator command fluency, with assumptions stated explicitly. Both need exploration coaching against the criteria, but the content work shares very little.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: A Ras Al Khaimah family comparing two schools is often comparing two boards without realising it, and the difference changes what tutoring has to do.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March sitting is offered to India only, so a RAK candidate sits June with November as the resit route. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in before building a schedule.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and in November each year. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Results timing differs from Cambridge's and affects resit planning: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and those are subject to revision, so any plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than against dates restated elsewhere.

For the student the differences that actually bite are smaller and more specific than the branding suggests: tiering policy, whether a formula sheet is supplied, how practical skills are assessed on paper, and the house style of the mark scheme. Those are the things a tutor matched by board gets right and a tutor matched by subject guesses at.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects running alongside the main course
paragraphs: A student in Seih Al Uraibi is not only sitting IB or IGCSE papers. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, so a second set of assessed subjects runs in parallel all year.

The requirement is federal and the detail is worth knowing because it is tightly specified where it has been published. KHDA's guidance for Dubai, which is the most detailed public statement of how these subjects are organised, requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. It sets Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

One constraint affects tutoring directly: for these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. So support here means working within the school's prescribed material rather than importing an alternative syllabus, which is a narrower brief than parents often expect. KHDA also requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate approval to teach those subjects in Dubai schools, which is a reasonable credential question to ask anywhere.

The practical effect on a revision plan in Ras Al Khaimah is scheduling. Arabic and Islamic Education assessments follow the school's internal calendar, not the board's, and they frequently land in the same fortnight as IGCSE mocks or Diploma internal deadlines. Mapping both calendars onto one sheet in September prevents the collision that otherwise gets discovered in week one of the mock window.

process.description: Command-term losses close fastest, usually in two or three sessions of deliberate drilling. Content gaps take longer and are scheduled around the school's own coverage. Method and working losses are habit, fixed by marking the student's own script against the scheme until the habit changes. Blocks are set against one column, not against a vague improvement.

whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched to a named component and work from the published criteria and mark schemes. Most lost marks in a Seih Al Uraibi student's folder are instrument failures rather than knowledge failures, and those are the fastest thing in the folder to fix.

faqs.question: What does a syllabus-level IB IGCSE tutor near me in Seih Al Uraibi actually do?
faqs.answer: They work from the assessment instrument rather than from the topic list. That means opening your child's last marked paper, sorting the lost marks into content, command term, working shown and timing, then fixing the largest column first. For a Diploma student it also means auditing an internal assessment draft against the published criterion descriptors. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE, which is how a component-level match becomes possible in a market this size.

faqs.question: Why do command terms matter so much on an IGCSE or IB paper?
faqs.answer: Because mark schemes follow them literally. State wants a fact with no credit for extra. Describe wants features in sequence. Explain wants a mechanism with causation made explicit. Evaluate and justify want a judgement with a stated condition. A student who explains when the paper said state has written something true that earns nothing additional and has lost the time. A student who describes when the paper said explain has written half an answer. Deliberate drilling closes this column in two or three sessions, which makes it the cheapest grade movement available.

faqs.question: How should my child in Seih Al Uraibi be using past papers?
faqs.answer: Whole paper, correct duration, nothing open. Then mark it against the official mark scheme rather than an answer key, because the scheme shows which words earn the mark. Then have the self-marking challenged, since students award themselves credit for the right idea in the wrong words, which is exactly the answer an examiner rejects. Then re-sit only the lost questions, cold, a few days later. Six papers worked that way beat twenty papers scored and filed, and six is achievable around a full school timetable.

faqs.question: What is an IB internal assessment marked against?
faqs.answer: Lettered criteria with published descriptors and their own mark allocations, assessed by the teacher and moderated externally. The descriptors are available before the student writes anything, which makes this the most controllable component on the course. Marks are typically lost in predictable places: personal engagement with no evidence of independent decisions, and reflection that summarises what was done instead of evaluating what it showed. Criterion names and allocations differ by subject and are revised, so take them from the current subject guide through your child's teacher.

faqs.question: Can an IB Gram tutor help with my child's Extended Essay in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes. A tutor can interrogate whether the research question is answerable within 4,000 words, ask what evidence would settle it, explain a method and model it on a different topic, and give criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor cannot write, draft, complete or edit the essay to finish. That line is not negotiable: the work must be the student's own, and at least one provider ranking for these searches sells completed internal assessments, which is a malpractice risk for the student rather than a shortcut.

faqs.question: Which maths course should a Diploma student at the coastal campuses choose?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-based route with calculus at its centre; Applications and Interpretation is statistical and modelling-led with technology integral. Neither is easier, and a student strong at manipulation can find AI harder despite its reputation. The decision should be made on demonstrated strengths cross-checked against the current entry requirements of the specific degree programmes under consideration, since several subjects commonly expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Make the choice at the transition year, not in the second Diploma year.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board my child's school in Ras Al Khaimah uses?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry names the board and the syllabus code, and your school's exams officer can confirm it in a sentence before that arrives. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 for Mathematics or 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1 or 4CH1. The answer changes revision priorities materially, because Pearson supplies a maths formula sheet Cambridge does not, and the two boards differ on tiering and on how practical skills are assessed on paper.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level just Standard Level with an extra paper?
faqs.answer: No, and revising from Standard Level material is one of the more damaging mistakes a Diploma student makes. Higher Level adds depth as well as content, and that extra depth changes what the shared papers are allowed to ask, so a question on familiar material can be set at a level Standard Level never reaches. Several subjects also carry an additional component at Higher Level. The gap is invisible until a past paper is attempted under timed conditions, which is the argument for attempting one early rather than late.

faqs.question: Which papers are hardest to find a specialist for near Seih Al Uraibi?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606 is the clearest gap, because the cohort is small and the content reaches calculus and logarithms that 0580 never touches. Computer Science 0478 follows, where the board's own pseudocode conventions and trace tables need someone who has marked the paper. Pearson science codes are thinner locally than Cambridge ones because fewer schools in the emirate use that board. These are precisely the papers where teaching over live video changes the answer from nobody available to somebody available.

faqs.question: Does online delivery work for the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, because that paper tests experimental literacy on paper rather than laboratory handling. It asks candidates to identify variables, write a method with a named control, read a scale correctly, spot an anomalous result and handle uncertainty. All of that is taught with the student's own paper on screen and annotated during the hour. What online cannot replace is the practical work itself, which the school provides. The tutor's job is converting the laboratory time your child has already had into marks on the written paper.

faqs.question: My child understands the content but keeps losing marks. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always an instrument failure rather than a knowledge failure. The common forms are a misread command term, a definition given without the qualifying phrase the scheme requires, a correct answer with no working shown where method marks were available, a reagent named without its condition, or an economics diagram left unlabelled beneath fluent prose. Sorting a marked paper into those categories takes about twenty minutes and usually shows one dominant column. That column, not the subject, is what the next block of sessions should address.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education affect an IB or IGCSE revision plan?
faqs.answer: They affect the calendar, and that is enough to matter. Private schools in the UAE must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum, assessed on the school's internal calendar rather than the board's. In practice those assessments often land in the same fortnight as IGCSE mocks or Diploma internal deadlines. Mapping both calendars onto one sheet early prevents a collision that is otherwise discovered in week one of the mock window, when there is no room left to move anything.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a component-level fix usually take?
faqs.answer: It depends on which column the losses sit in. Command-term and working-shown losses are habit problems and typically close in two or three sessions of deliberate drilling against marked scripts. Content gaps take longer and have to be scheduled around the school's own coverage, because re-teaching ahead of the class rarely sticks. Internal assessment work is bounded by the school's deadline rather than by session count. Any honest answer is a range, and nobody can promise a particular grade from a particular number of hours.

faqs.question: Can a Seih Al Uraibi family be given past papers and mark schemes to work from?
faqs.answer: They can reference and link the official sources, and they can work from the copies your child legitimately holds through school. They should not hand over reproduced papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, because those belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and for unreleased material redistribution is a more serious problem than copyright alone. Any site offering downloadable mark scheme packs is distributing someone else's property, which is a reasonable signal about how it treats other rules too.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial lesson, and is there a catch?
faqs.answer: The first lesson is free and it is used as a diagnosis rather than a sales call. Your child brings marked work, the tutor goes through the questions that lost marks, and you receive a written summary naming the specific weaknesses and the questions they showed up on. There is no obligation afterwards. Our own rate is confirmed in the conversation that follows, with the format and session length stated before anything is agreed, and if no specialist is free for the paper you need we will say so.

intro.heading: Four options, and the one honest way to compare them
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah is the emirate the UAE tutoring market forgets. Of the sixty-odd competitor pages examined for this subject area, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain returned no mentions at all. That absence is a reasonable proxy for the ground truth: the number of resident teachers in this emirate who have marked IB Middle Years Programme mathematics against its published criteria is small, and a family in Al Hamra Village or Mina Al Arab discovers that within a week of starting to ask around.

So the decision in front of a RAK parent is not which tutor to pick from a long list. It is which of four different kinds of help to buy. The first is the school's own provision: an after-school clinic or a subject teacher's lunchtime catch-up, included in fees. The second is a group class at a tuition centre in RAK city, usually four to twelve students across mixed curricula. The third is an independent tutor found through a residents' group or a school parents' channel, working in your home. The fourth is one-to-one teaching over live video with a teacher who may be anywhere.

Each of those options is genuinely better than the others at something. School support is free and aligned to the exact scheme of work your child is following, which no external tutor can match. A centre group class is the cheapest paid option and imposes a weekly routine, which is sometimes the actual problem. A local freelancer is in the room, which matters for a younger or more distractible student. Online one-to-one gives access to a pool of MYP-trained teachers that does not exist within a forty-minute drive of Khuzam, and it marks against the criteria rather than against right answers.

They also fail at different things, and this is where comparison gets useful. A group class cannot change a criterion C habit, because changing it requires someone to read your child's written reasoning line by line every week. School support cannot usually diagnose across year groups, because the teacher running it is working from this term's scheme. A freelance tutor may be excellent and may also be undocumented, which is a question you have to ask rather than assume. And live video needs a stable connection and a parent who protects the slot, which not every household can offer.

IB Gram sells the fourth option only. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, which is stated on every country page we publish. That means this page recommends the other three options where they are the better answer, and explains the permit and verification questions you should ask of any provider, including us. The rest of it covers how MYP mathematics is assessed, how RAK schools place students on the standard or extended route, what the Department of Knowledge actually approves, and what a term of weekly one-to-one work produces week by week.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.programmesIntro: A Ras Al Khaimah MYP family is usually making two decisions at once: how to fill a gap now, and whether the Diploma is the destination at all, given that the nearest alternatives sit in other emirates. These are the three programmes that frame that choice.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, with mathematics assessed continuously against four criteria marked out of eight each rather than through a single terminal paper. The school converts the pattern of criterion levels into the 1 to 7 grade on the report, using its own boundaries. In the final year, mathematics splits into standard and extended routes and some schools enter candidates for on-screen eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: IB provision in Ras Al Khaimah is concentrated in a very small number of schools, with RAK Academy the established continuum option. The consequence is a thin local market in MYP-specific teaching: a maths graduate is findable, a teacher who has marked criterion B is not. Families in Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab are typically forty minutes or more from the schools in RAK city, which narrows the realistic in-home pool further still.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level over two years, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service alongside. Mathematics divides into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation. Which of those a student can take is largely settled by how far their MYP mathematics went, which is why the route placed in MYP 4 or MYP 5 is a Diploma decision in disguise.
programmes.countryNote: RAK families comparing the Diploma against A Levels are often also comparing schools in different emirates, because the local set is small. The maths strand is frequently the deciding factor: a student who has only done standard-route MYP mathematics and then wants Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is starting from behind. Settling that question before Year 11 ends is considerably cheaper than discovering it in the first Diploma term.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary learning across transdisciplinary themes, ending with the Exhibition. Mathematics is embedded in units of inquiry rather than timetabled as an isolated subject for much of the programme, so written fluency on arrival in MYP 1 varies widely between students who have had equally good primary experiences.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah a high proportion of MYP 1 and MYP 2 students have transferred in from Indian or British curriculum primaries in the emirate rather than from a PYP, which produces the opposite problem: strong procedural arithmetic and no experience of being marked on explanation. Those students often lose criterion C marks in their first term simply because nobody has told them that written reasoning is credited.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the specific MYP mathematics requests we receive from Ras Al Khaimah households, listed finely rather than by broad branch, because the choice between a group class and one-to-one usually turns on how narrow the gap actually is.

subjects.name: Simultaneous and linear equations
subjects.description: Elimination, substitution and the graphical method, plus setting up equations from a worded situation. The setting-up step is where marks go: students who can solve a given pair often cannot construct one. A narrow, fixable gap, and a good candidate for a group class rather than one-to-one.

subjects.name: Circle theorems and angle reasoning
subjects.description: Angle at the centre, angles in the same segment, cyclic quadrilaterals and tangent properties, with the reason named for every step. The reasoning, not the answer, carries the communication marks. This is the clearest example of a topic where a tutor must read written work rather than check results.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions and manipulation
subjects.description: Simplifying, adding with unlike denominators, solving equations containing fractions and rearranging formulae with the subject on both sides. The most common single reason a student moved onto the extended route mid-year starts to slide. Needs individual attention because the errors are idiosyncratic.

subjects.name: Logarithms and index laws
subjects.description: Negative and fractional indices, laws of logarithms and solving exponential equations. Extended-route content that most RAK students meet for the first time in Year 11, and the topic that most reliably decides whether Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is realistic in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Vectors in two dimensions
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, addition and scalar multiples, and geometric proof using vector paths. Often taught late in the year under time pressure, so it is frequently the gap a student carries into the Diploma. Short and self-contained enough to fix in three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Cumulative frequency and box plots
subjects.description: Building a cumulative frequency curve, reading the median and quartiles, constructing and comparing box plots and commenting on spread. Marks are lost in the comparison sentence rather than the drawing, which is a communication problem dressed as a statistics problem.

subjects.name: Probability trees and conditional probability
subjects.description: Tree diagrams with and without replacement, and reasoning about dependent events. Students who are fluent elsewhere often stumble here because the method is representational rather than computational. One of the topics where a worked diagnosis in a single session usually settles it.

subjects.name: Modelling and interpretation in context
subjects.description: Choosing a model, applying it to real data, interpreting the result and stating assumptions and limits. The highest-value skill on the page, because the top criterion D bands require the interpretation sentence that most students omit. Cannot be taught at group pace.

subjects.name: On-screen assessment technique
subjects.description: Working accurately in an on-screen environment, managing time across question types and showing method where the interface allows it. Relevant where a school enters candidates for MYP eAssessment, and a skill distinct from the mathematics itself. Worth four or five focused sessions in the term before entry.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.regionsIntro: Ras Al Khaimah is spread out, and distance is the practical reason the four options above do not weigh the same everywhere in the emirate. These are the communities we are asked about, with what the geography does to each choice.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: Central and close to the city's school cluster, so the local freelance and centre options are genuinely available here. The group classes advertised in RAK are mostly within reach of Al Nakheel addresses, which makes this the one part of the emirate where comparing all four options is straightforward.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village
regions.note: A coastal community roughly half an hour south of the main school cluster, with a high proportion of expatriate families on fixed-term contracts. In-home tutoring quotes carry that drive both ways. Continuity through a contract change is the stated priority for most families here, which favours a teacher who is not tied to the emirate.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab
regions.note: Waterfront villas and apartments between the city and Al Hamra. Workable for an in-home tutor based in RAK city but not for one coming from Sharjah or Dubai. Families here commonly run two children on consecutive slots, which is simpler to timetable remotely than around a single visiting tutor's route.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Reclaimed island development with limited residential density and no local tutoring provision at all. Every option except live video involves a causeway crossing in both directions, which is why enquiries from here are almost exclusively about remote one-to-one.

regions.name: Al Dhait
regions.note: Established residential district popular with teaching and medical families, and one of the few areas where a parent might realistically find a qualified neighbour. Worth asking locally first. Where the gap is criterion B or extended-route content, the local pool usually runs out quickly.

regions.name: Khuzam
regions.note: Inland and well connected to the city's schools by the ring road, with a mix of villas and compounds. Evening slots dominate because the school run and the working day finish later than in the city centre. Weekend morning blocks are the most requested windows from Khuzam households.

regions.name: Al Qusaidat and Seih Al Uraibi
regions.note: Older residential areas closer to the city, where group classes at a local centre are the most common paid option and the cheapest. Suitable where the need is routine and discipline rather than a specific criterion. Less suitable for an extended-route student with a content gap.

regions.name: Julphar and the corniche
regions.note: Apartment living near the older commercial core, with families frequently new to the emirate and unfamiliar with the local provision. The first question from this area is usually what the school already offers for free, and it is the right question to ask before paying for anything.

schoolClusters.city: Ras Al Khaimah city and Al Nakheel
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's private schools are clustered within a short radius of the city, covering British, Indian and IB provision, all under the Department of Knowledge. modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across a term
modes.description: A single fixed slot with the same teacher for ten to twelve weeks. The format that changes criterion C and criterion D habits, because those change through repeated correction of the student's own written work rather than through additional content. sections.heading: The four options a Ras Al Khaimah parent is choosing between
paragraphs: Set side by side, the four options stop competing on price and start competing on what they can actually change. That is the comparison worth making, because three of them cost less than one-to-one online teaching and two of them are sometimes the right answer.

School support is the one most families skip and should not. Ask the mathematics teacher directly whether there is a clinic, what it covers and whether your child is already attending. It is free, it follows the exact scheme of work, and in roughly a third of the enquiries we take the honest advice is to exhaust it before paying anyone. Its ceiling is that it is group provision inside a busy week, so it will not read your child's written reasoning line by line.

A tuition centre group class in RAK city is the cheapest paid option, and its real product is routine. For a student who simply is not doing mathematics between lessons, that is a genuine fix. Its limitation is structural rather than a criticism of the teaching: a class covering mixed curricula at a shared pace cannot address an MYP criterion descriptor, and in practice most centres in the northern emirates are staffed for the British and Indian curricula, which dominate enrolment here.

An independent tutor found through a residents' group is the option parents feel best about and verify least. The person may be an excellent teacher. They may also be working without the permit the UAE requires, which is your exposure as much as theirs, and the pool of local candidates who have marked MYP mathematics is very small. The table below puts all four next to each other with market rates attributed to the providers that publish them; the right-hand column is the one to read first.

sections.heading: Why MYP specialist supply is genuinely thin in the northern emirates
paragraphs: This is worth stating because it is the fact the rest of the decision rests on, and because no competitor page in this market says it. Across the sixty-plus ranking pages examined for UAE tutoring queries, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain are not mentioned. The pages exist for Dubai and, less often, Abu Dhabi. The market has not built provision here because the addressable population is small.

The teaching population follows the same curve. IB provision in the emirate is concentrated in a small number of schools, so the number of teachers locally who have taught and marked MYP mathematics is correspondingly small, and most of them are employed full time. Abu Dhabi's own professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the UAE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that addresses the same conflict, so the obvious local candidate is frequently not available to you by design.

What is findable locally is a mathematics graduate, a retired teacher from another curriculum, or an undergraduate at one of the emirate's universities. Any of those can lift arithmetic fluency and drill procedure. None of them, without specific MYP experience, will reliably tell you that your child is capping out in criterion B because the justification is absent rather than wrong, which is the diagnosis that actually moves a grade.

That asymmetry is the whole argument for remote delivery in this emirate, and it is a stronger argument here than in Dubai, where a parent genuinely can find a resident specialist. It also cuts the other way: if the diagnosis turns out to be slow fraction work in MYP 2, a local tutor at a local rate is a perfectly sensible purchase and we will say so. The question the first lesson answers is which of those two situations you are in.

sections.heading: Checking whether a tutor is legally permitted to teach here
paragraphs: If you are considering the freelance option, this is the section to use. Private tutoring in the UAE is not an informal activity. A private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the government states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone telling you a permit costs money, or that permits are only for tutoring centres, is wrong on a point of fact.

The eligible categories are broad, which surprises most parents. According to the government's own guidance, applicants may include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The route is the labour ministry's own service, listed as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a short stated processing time, applied for through the ministry's app, website and e-services system.

The government also states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, and press reporting records that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a figure circulating online as an exact penalty should be treated as unverified. The useful point for a parent is simply that the obligation is real and the permit is free, which removes every reasonable excuse for not holding one.

Asking is not rude and it is the one check a parent can run without expertise. The table sets out the categories and what to ask each. Note also that a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs an educational services permit from the emirate authority. IB Gram holds no such permit and no accreditation from any UAE authority or examination board, and neither does any platform telling you otherwise.

sections.heading: What distinguishes an MYP-trained maths teacher from a maths graduate
paragraphs: Because so much of the RAK decision comes down to who is actually available, it is worth being precise about what the MYP-specific skill is. It is not deeper mathematics. The content of MYP mathematics is well within the reach of any competent graduate. The difference is in what gets credited.

MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The school then converts the pattern of criterion levels across the year into the 1 to 7 grade on the report, using boundaries it sets itself. A tutor working from right answers alone is optimising the first criterion and ignoring three.

In practice that produces a specific and very common failure. A student works with a competent tutor for a term, gets quicker and more accurate, and the report does not move. The parent concludes that tutoring does not work. What has actually happened is that criterion A was never the problem: the student was losing marks for unjustified reasoning in criterion B and for answers without interpretation in criterion D, and nobody was looking at those. A tutor who has marked MYP work opens the first session by asking for the criterion levels rather than the grade.

The test you can apply before committing anything is therefore quite simple. Ask a prospective tutor which criterion they think is losing marks and why, having shown them one marked piece of work. A specialist will name one and give a reason tied to the writing on the page. A generalist will talk about topics. Both answers are informative, and one of them is worth two hundred dirhams an hour more than the other.
bullets: Four criteria, each marked out of eight, converted by the school into a 1 to 7 grade
Criterion A rewards fluency; criteria B, C and D reward written reasoning
A term of accurate drilling can leave the report unchanged

sections.heading: MYP 5, eAssessment and the standard or extended placement
paragraphs: In the final MYP year, two things happen that a Ras Al Khaimah parent should understand before choosing any option above. Mathematics divides into a standard and an extended route, and some schools enter candidates for the IB's on-screen eAssessment while others award the programme on internally assessed work alone. Schools in this emirate differ on the second point, and the school office is the only reliable source for what yours does.

The placement decision is the one with lasting consequences. Extended covers the standard content plus additional material, which usually means logarithms, further index work, harder algebraic fractions, two-dimensional vectors and additional trigonometry depending on the scheme of work. A student who completes the standard route and then takes Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the Diploma starts with a real content deficit, not merely a pace adjustment. Given that the Diploma options available locally are limited, that can also become a school-choice question.

If your child is entered for eAssessment, a distinct skill enters the picture: working accurately in an on-screen environment under timed conditions. That is separate from mathematical ability and it is coachable in four or five focused sessions. It is also the one part of the MYP where exam technique behaves like IGCSE exam technique, which widens the pool of tutors who can help with it.

The practical sequence for a RAK family is to establish in September which route the school has placed the child on and whether eAssessment applies, then decide how to spend money. A placement on extended with a shaky algebraic-fractions base is a narrow-gap block of three or four sessions. A student on standard who wants Higher Level Analysis and Approaches later is a term of weekly work. A student who is coping but not writing up their reasoning is a criterion C problem and the cheapest fix on this page.

sections.heading: The RAK Department of Knowledge and what it actually approves
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah has its own education regulator, and that is unusual among the northern emirates. The UAE government's guidance states that the Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate, while the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi has the Department of Education and Knowledge and Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority.

The scope is wider than inspection. The same guidance records that the authorities in Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a meaningful detail for a parent: the curriculum your child is taught and the fee you are charged have both passed through an emirate-level approval process, not only a federal one. It is also a fact that no competitor page in this market mentions, which tells you how little attention the northern emirates get.

Alongside whichever international curriculum a school is licensed to teach, the federal baseline applies: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations. For an MYP family this means the timetable is fuller than the IB subject list suggests, and the week has less slack in it than a plan for three tutoring sessions assumes. One protected slot that survives the term is worth more than an ambitious schedule abandoned in week four.

What none of this makes anybody is accredited. IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from the Department of Knowledge, the Ministry of Education, the IB organisation or Cambridge, and any tutoring provider implying such a relationship is making a claim worth checking against the authority's own register. What a parent can verify is an individual tutor's permit, the school's own position on eAssessment, and the quality of the marking in a free first lesson.

sections.heading: What a term of weekly one-to-one actually produces, week by week
paragraphs: If you choose the fourth option, this is what you are buying, laid out so that you can tell in week six whether it is working rather than hoping it is. The shape below is the one we use for an MYP 4 or MYP 5 student whose grade has slipped a band or two, which is the most common RAK enquiry.

The first fortnight is diagnostic and is where parents often expect too little. By the end of week two there should be a named criterion, a named cause and a rough number of weeks attached. If a tutor has not produced that, more sessions will not produce it either. Weeks three to six are habit weeks: written reasoning, notation, interpretation sentences. These are the weeks where nothing dramatic appears to happen and the grade changes afterwards.

Weeks seven to ten are content weeks, when the specific topic gaps get closed, and this is where extended-route students need the most time. The final fortnight is timed practice against the school's own assessment format. Running that sequence in reverse, which is what happens when a family starts in the fortnight before a report, is the single most common reason tutoring disappoints: timed practice on a student who has not fixed their written reasoning just produces faster unjustified answers.

The evidence column in the table is deliberately concrete, because a parent should be able to check it without understanding the mathematics. A marked piece of work with reasoning written out looks different from one without. If week six arrives and nothing in that column has appeared, the right response is to change the teacher or the plan, not to add a second session.

sections.heading: Where tutoring stops and the student's own work begins
paragraphs: Whichever of the four options a RAK family chooses, one rule applies to all of them. IB academic-honesty requirements mean assessed work must be the student's own, and the consequences of a breach fall on the student rather than on whoever supplied the help. That makes the boundary a practical matter rather than a philosophical one.

A tutor may teach the mathematics, work through unrelated examples of the same type, explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning is thin or the communication unclear. A tutor may not author any part of a submitted task, supply the generalisation for an investigation, rewrite an explanation, or polish a draft into something the student could not have produced alone. The test a parent can apply after a session is whether their child can explain every line of what will be handed in.

This matters in the UAE market specifically because some providers openly sell completed assessed work, including Diploma internal assessments at four-figure prices. An offer phrased as done-for-you is a reason to stop the conversation, not a service tier. The same boundary applies to the MYP Personal Project in the final year: planning, process and reflection coaching is legitimate; producing the artefact or the report is not.

On the same basis we do not supply IB syllabus documents, past examination material or mark schemes. Those are copyright material properly accessed through your child's school and the official site, and a provider offering you a folder of them is offering something they are not entitled to distribute. It is a small test and a revealing one.

process.title: Ask the school first
process.description: Before paying anyone, ask your child's mathematics teacher what catch-up provision exists, what it covers and whether your child is attending. It is free and scheme-aligned, and in a meaningful share of enquiries it is enough on its own. Where it is not, you at least arrive at the next conversation knowing what has already been tried.

process.title: Send marked work and the criterion levels
process.description: Send one recent marked MYP maths task and the latest report showing criterion levels rather than only the grade. Fifteen minutes of reading real work replaces a fortnight of guessing, and it is what lets the first lesson be diagnostic instead of introductory.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a named outcome
process.description: A full one-to-one lesson over live video at no charge, with no card details taken. The output to expect is a named criterion, a named cause and a rough number of weeks. If the honest answer is that a group class or the school clinic would fix this, we will tell you that instead.

process.title: Choose the shape, not just the tutor
process.description: A narrow topic gap is three or four sessions and then nothing. A habit problem in written reasoning is a term of weekly work. An assessment a fortnight away is an intensive. Picking the wrong shape is the most common way families overspend, and the diagnosis is what decides it.

process.title: Check the evidence at six weeks
process.description: Compare the school's own criterion levels before and after, not a tutor's report on progress. If one criterion has moved and another has not, the plan changes. If nothing has moved in six weeks of weekly work, the teacher changes rather than the hours increasing.

whyPoints.title: The comparison includes what we do not sell
whyPoints.description: School clinics, centre group classes and local freelance tutoring are all on this page with their genuine advantages, because a parent cannot make a decision from a page that only describes one option. Where another option is the better fit, the first lesson is where you will hear that.

whyPoints.title: Access, not proximity
whyPoints.description: The binding constraint in Ras Al Khaimah is the number of resident teachers who have marked MYP mathematics, which is small. Remote one-to-one changes the pool rather than the price of the drive, and that matters more here than in Dubai where a resident specialist is genuinely findable.

whyPoints.title: Permit facts you can verify yourself
whyPoints.description: The private tuition permit position is set out with the resolution that created it and the fact that it is free for two years, so you can check any tutor including ours. We claim no accreditation from any UAE authority or examination board, because we hold none.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level diagnosis in the first lesson
whyPoints.description: The first session produces a named criterion and a named cause from marked work, not a general impression. That is what makes a six-week review possible, and it is why a term of accurate drilling that leaves the report unchanged should not happen twice.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their source and date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. Several competitor pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a RAK family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated plainly
whyPoints.description: If no MYP mathematics specialist is free at your slot, we say so at the trial stage rather than filling the hour. That disclosure is uncommon in this market and it is cheaper for you than discovering a mismatch in week three.

faqs.question: Which is the better first move in Ras Al Khaimah: the school's own catch-up, a group class, or a private tutor?
faqs.answer: Start with the school, because it is free and follows the exact scheme of work your child is being taught. Ask the mathematics teacher what clinic provision exists and whether your child is attending it. If the problem is that your child does no mathematics between lessons, a group class at a local centre is the cheapest fix and the routine is the product. Move to one-to-one when the problem is specific: a named criterion losing marks, an extended-route content gap, or written reasoning that is thought but never recorded. Those three cannot be fixed at group pace, which is the only real dividing line between the options.

faqs.question: Why are there so few MYP maths tutors actually living in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Because IB provision in the emirate is concentrated in a very small number of schools, so the population of teachers who have taught and marked MYP mathematics here is small, and most of them are employed full time. There is a second constraint: the UAE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct addressing conflicts of interest, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, so the obvious local candidate is often unavailable by design. What is findable locally is a maths graduate or an undergraduate, which helps with fluency and drill but not with criterion-level diagnosis.

faqs.question: Does a group class at a tuition centre in RAK work for MYP mathematics?
faqs.answer: For some problems, yes. If your child is simply not practising between school lessons, a weekly class imposes the routine and that is often the whole issue. It is also the cheapest paid option, with market group rates running roughly AED 45-150 per student per hour. What it cannot do is address an MYP criterion descriptor, because that requires someone reading one student's written reasoning every week. Most centres in the northern emirates are staffed for the British and Indian curricula, which dominate local enrolment, so ask directly whether anyone there has marked MYP work before paying for a term.

faqs.question: How do I check that a freelance tutor in Ras Al Khaimah is allowed to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask to see their private tuition work permit. The UAE introduced it under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and the government states it is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one. Eligible categories are broad and include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The government also states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published. A tutoring centre with premises needs a separate permit from the emirate authority.

faqs.question: What exactly does an MYP-trained maths teacher do that a maths graduate does not?
faqs.answer: They mark against the four criteria rather than against right answers. MYP mathematics is assessed on knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each marked out of eight, and the school converts that pattern into the 1 to 7 grade on the report. A graduate tutor optimises the first criterion. The failure that produces is specific and common: a term of accurate work, a faster student, and a report that has not moved, because the losses were in unjustified reasoning and uninterpreted answers. Ask any prospective tutor to name a criterion from one marked piece of work.

faqs.question: Does my child's school in Ras Al Khaimah enter students for MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Schools differ, and the school office is the only reliable source. Some IB schools enter final-year MYP candidates for on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, while others award the programme on internally assessed work alone. The answer changes what is worth paying for. If your child is entered, on-screen assessment technique becomes a distinct coachable skill: working accurately in the interface, managing time across question types and showing method where the format allows. That is usually four or five focused sessions and it behaves much more like IGCSE examination technique than like the rest of the MYP, which widens the pool of tutors who can help with it.

faqs.question: My daughter has been put on extended mathematics in MYP 5 and is struggling. Is that the wrong route?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and the answer depends on which part is hard. Extended adds content to the standard route, commonly logarithms, further indices, harder algebraic fractions, two-dimensional vectors and extra trigonometry, so a student who is coping conceptually but drowning in algebraic fractions has a narrow, fixable gap rather than a wrong placement. A student who is losing marks across all four criteria is a different case. The question to settle is where she is heading: if Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the destination, extended is close to a practical prerequisite, and dropping to standard now buys relief this year at a cost in two.

faqs.question: We are in Al Hamra Village on a two-year contract. What happens to continuity if we move?
faqs.answer: This is the most common reason families here choose remote teaching over a local tutor, and it is a sound reason. A tutor who drives to your villa in Al Hamra is specific to that address; a teacher working over live video is not tied to the emirate or the country, so a mid-contract relocation does not restart the relationship. For an MYP student that matters more than it sounds, because the criterion C and criterion D habits that take six weeks to change are exactly what gets lost when a tutor is replaced. If you expect to move, say so at the trial stage so the match accounts for the time zone you are heading to.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Ras Al Khaimah, and what does the regulator control?
faqs.answer: Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate. Its remit is broader than inspection: the UAE government records that the Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Elsewhere the picture differs, with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority in Dubai, the Department of Education and Knowledge in Abu Dhabi, and the federal Ministry of Education supervising Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None of this makes any tutoring provider accredited; IB Gram holds no permit or relationship with the Department of Knowledge or any examination board.

faqs.question: How will I know after six weeks whether the tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: Use the school's own criterion levels, not the tutor's report. Six weeks is long enough for written reasoning habits to change and short enough to act if they have not. The concrete evidence is visible without understanding the mathematics: homework that shows justified steps rather than bare answers, and context questions that end with a sentence on what the answer means and what limits it. If a criterion level has moved, continue. If one has moved and another has not, change the plan. If nothing has moved in six weeks of weekly work, change the teacher rather than adding a second session.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough, or should we book two from the start?
faqs.answer: One well-placed weekly session with work done in between moves more than two sessions with nothing between them, and that holds for most MYP cases. The losses at this stage are usually habits rather than content gaps, and habits change through repeated correction of the student's own written work, not through extra contact hours. Two or three sessions a week make sense in two situations: an internal assessment or eAssessment entry a fortnight away, or a student placed on the extended route mid-year with genuine content to cover. Outside those, the second weekly session usually buys reassurance for the parent rather than progress for the student.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP Personal Project in the final year?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes; with the product, no. Planning, setting criteria for success, structuring the process journal, managing the timeline and reflecting on what happened are all legitimate coaching, and students genuinely benefit from someone asking hard questions early. What a tutor must not do is author any part of the report, produce the artefact, or edit a draft into something the student could not have written alone. IB academic-honesty rules require the work to be the student's own, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student. Any offer phrased as done-for-you should end the conversation rather than start a negotiation.

faqs.question: What does the first lesson cost if we decide not to continue?
faqs.answer: Nothing, and no card details are taken beforehand. The trial is a full one-to-one lesson over live video, and its purpose is to produce something you can use with or without us: a named MYP criterion, the cause behind it, and a rough number of weeks. If the honest conclusion is that the school's own clinic or a local group class would fix this, you will hear that in the first lesson. If we do not have a suitable MYP mathematics specialist free at your preferred slot, you will hear that too, rather than being matched with whoever is available.

faqs.question: Can sessions be arranged around a long school run and the RAK working day?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth planning around the bus rather than the bell. Children travelling from Al Hamra, Al Marjan Island or Mina Al Arab to the city school cluster are often not home before four, and the first hour afterwards is the worst time to attempt investigation work. Slots that survive a full term are usually later weekday evenings or a longer weekend morning block, and weekend mornings are the most requested windows from this emirate. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and the productive part of the day moves, so most families switch to a late-morning or post-iftar slot agreed a fortnight ahead.

faqs.question: Are there IB MYP mathematics tutors available for students outside Ras Al Khaimah city?
faqs.answer: Yes, because delivery does not depend on geography inside the emirate. Al Marjan Island, Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab have little or no local tutoring provision, and every option other than live video involves a drive in both directions that ends up in the hourly rate. Remote one-to-one prices the same for an Al Dhait family as for an Al Marjan Island family, since no travel is being bought. The practical requirements are a stable connection, a quiet room and a parent who protects the slot in the calendar, which is a smaller ask than it sounds but not a trivial one.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Middle Years Programme subjects to students in Ras Al Khaimah over live video. Each works from the criterion descriptors your child's school uses to mark, rather than from an examination paper that does not exist at this stage.

intro.heading: The question is not whether to hire a tutor, but which of four things to buy
paragraphs: Almost nobody searches for an IB MYP tutor in Ras Al Khaimah as a first move. By the time a parent types that phrase, something has already happened: a report arrived with a 4 in a subject that used to read 6, or a teacher wrote a comment about "inconsistent application of criterion C" that nobody at home could decode. The sensible next step is rarely obvious, because the Middle Years Programme does not produce the artefacts parents know how to read. There is no percentage. There is no past paper to work through. There is a grid of letters and a number between one and eight.

So the real decision is a choice between four things, and they are not interchangeable. The first is the support the school already owes you, which is free and underused. The second is a group class at a tuition centre in Al Nakheel or Al Dhait, which is cheap per hour and usually built around an examination syllabus rather than MYP criteria. The third is a freelance tutor who drives to the villa, often shared between two or three families on the same street. The fourth is a subject specialist working one-to-one over live video, which is what IB Gram arranges.

Each of those four is the right answer for somebody. A Year 7 student who has simply stopped doing the set work does not need a specialist; they need the school's homework club and a parent who checks the planner. A MYP 5 student whose science teacher has left mid-year and whose criterion D marks have collapsed does need a specialist, and in the northern emirates that person is unlikely to live within driving distance. Ras Al Khaimah has a small private-school set concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, and the pool of adults who have marked MYP sciences against the published descriptors is correspondingly small.

That scarcity is the whole reason this page exists in the form it does. In Dubai, a parent choosing between a local visiting tutor and an online specialist is choosing between two reasonably deep pools. In Ras Al Khaimah, the local pool for a specific MYP subject at a specific year level is often one person or none. Comparing the four options therefore gives a different answer here than it would in Jumeirah, and anybody who tells you otherwise has not tried to staff a MYP 5 integrated sciences slot north of Umm Al Quwain in February.

What follows is the comparison, the parts of the Middle Years Programme that make it different to teach, what the market charges around the emirate in dirhams, and what the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge actually controls at your child's school. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors at the door are a service we run only in India, and saying so plainly is more useful to you than a promise we would have to break.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: Ras Al Khaimah families meet the Middle Years Programme either inside an IB continuum school or when transferring from a British or Indian stream. The programmes below are the ones that sit either side of MYP, because a middle-years decision is almost always also a decision about what comes next.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of concept-led study across eight subject groups, marked against four published criteria per subject on a 1-8 strand scale. Teachers set the tasks; the IB sets the criteria. The programme ends with the Personal Project in MYP 5, and schools may enter students for IB-set on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the MYP Certificate. Nothing in MYP produces a transcript grade a university reads, which changes what tutoring is for.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah the MYP cohort inside any single school is small, so a year group often runs one teaching set per subject with no streaming. A student who is ahead and a student who is behind sit in the same room with the same task. That is the specific gap one-to-one support fills here, and it is a different gap from the one a Dubai family describes.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subject groups, three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Assessment switches to externally marked examinations in a May session for schools in this hemisphere, with internal assessment contributing a published share of each subject grade. The jump in written volume from MYP 5 is the single biggest complaint we hear from Year 12 students.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah students who continue into the Diploma usually do so at the same campus they were already attending, which means the MYP 5 subject choices effectively set the Diploma option blocks. Getting MYP 5 mathematics and sciences to a secure level is therefore a decision about Higher Level availability two years later, not just about this year's report.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year examined alternative most Ras Al Khaimah schools run instead of MYP 4 and 5. Assessment is by externally marked papers in a June or November series, with a Core or Extended tier in Cambridge syllabuses that sets a ceiling on the achievable grade. Students transferring in from MYP meet timed papers and mark schemes for the first time, which is a skills change rather than a content change.
programmes.countryNote: Several families in the emirate move a child from an MYP stream into an IGCSE stream at the end of MYP 3, usually because a sibling is already in the British system or because a planned relocation makes examined qualifications simpler to carry. The transition work is mostly about examination technique, not about catching up on content.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's primary framework, ending in the Year 6 exhibition. Reporting is descriptive rather than graded, so parents arriving into MYP 1 meet a numbered scale for the first time and frequently misread it. Support at this stage is almost entirely about reading fluency and secure number facts, both of which predict MYP performance better than anything a middle-years tutor can repair later.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Ras Al Khaimah school runs the full continuum, the move from the Year 6 exhibition into MYP 1 happens on the same campus with the same staff, which hides the change in assessment language. Parents often ask for MYP support in the first term of Year 7 when the actual issue is that nobody explained what a criterion level means.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP subject groups are taught through concepts and contexts rather than a content checklist, so a tutor has to work from your child's own unit planner and task sheet. The subjects below are the ones Ras Al Khaimah families ask about most for MYP 3 to MYP 5.

subjects.name: Mathematics (MYP)
subjects.description: Four branches: number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability. Criterion A rewards knowing and understanding, criterion B investigating patterns, criterion C communicating, criterion D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most lost marks sit in B and D, where students produce a correct answer with no general rule and no evaluation of its validity.

subjects.name: Integrated Sciences (MYP)
subjects.description: Criterion B asks the student to design a method with a clear variable structure; criterion C asks them to process and present data and then interpret it. Students lose heavily by describing a graph instead of explaining it, and by writing a conclusion that restates the hypothesis rather than testing it against the evidence collected.

subjects.name: Biology (MYP 4-5)
subjects.description: Cells, systems, ecology and genetics taught through global contexts. The written tasks demand scientific vocabulary used precisely, and criterion D requires a reasoned position on the implications of science for people and the environment. A student who revises definitions but never practises the evaluative paragraph plateaus at a 5.

subjects.name: Chemistry (MYP 4-5)
subjects.description: Bonding, moles, rates and energetics, with laboratory work feeding criteria B and C. The common failure is arithmetic in mole calculations combined with units dropped halfway through. Working accurately with significant figures is a criterion C issue rather than a content issue, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Physics (MYP 4-5)
subjects.description: Forces, energy, waves, electricity and the relationship between equations and physical meaning. Students who can rearrange a formula often cannot say what it predicts, which is exactly what criterion A probes at the higher levels. Graph-gradient interpretation is the single most profitable thing to practise before MYP 5 ends.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Four criteria covering analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Marks are lost in criterion A when a student summarises a text instead of analysing how meaning is constructed, and in criterion C when a creative response ignores the stated audience and purpose. The paired text analysis is the task most worth rehearsing.

subjects.name: English Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehension of spoken and written text, plus speaking and writing in the target language, graded against the phase the student is placed in. A phase placement that is too low flatters the report and hides a problem; a placement that is too high produces consistent 3s and 4s from a capable student. Both are worth checking.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: History, geography and economics content delivered through investigation. Criterion B is an investigation plan with a research question the student formulated, and criterion D asks for a substantiated argument. Source evaluation that names provenance, purpose and limitation earns marks that most students leave on the table.

subjects.name: Design (MYP)
subjects.description: The design cycle: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. Every criterion rewards documented process, so a strong product with a thin design folder scores poorly. Students need to be taught that the folder is the assessment, not the artefact, and that is usually news to them.

subjects.name: Arabic (Language Acquisition or Language A)
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the MYP in every UAE private school as a federal requirement, with separate provision for Arabic speakers and non-Arabic speakers. Support has to match the stream the school has placed the student in, and a tutor who teaches first-language Arabic to an acquisition-phase student wastes the hour.

subjects.name: Mathematics Extended (MYP 5)
subjects.description: The extended pathway adds content aimed at students heading for Higher Level mathematics in the Diploma. A student kept in standard mathematics through MYP 5 can still take Analysis and Approaches, but the first term of Year 12 is noticeably harder. The decision point is usually in MYP 4, earlier than parents expect.

subjects.name: Personal Project (MYP 5)
subjects.description: A self-directed project assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, supported by a process journal and a supervisor at school. A tutor may teach project-management habits, question an argument and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not contribute content to the report or the product.
