A student who collects those consistently is insulated from boundary movement in a way that one aiming at a remembered number is not.

faqs.question: What are the Pearson codes and why do they matter?
faqs.answer: They identify what a student is actually sitting, which a school report does not. 4MA1 is Mathematics A across two papers with Foundation and Higher tiers; 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 are the separate sciences across two written papers each; 4SC1 is Science Double Award; 4EA1 is English Language A; and Business, Economics, History and ICT carry their own codes. Get the complete list in writing from your exams officer, because past papers are useless without it.

faqs.question: Is Further Pure Mathematics worth taking?
faqs.answer: It depends on one thing: whether your child's algebra is fast rather than merely correct. Further Pure introduces calculus and trigonometric identities assuming manipulation is already automatic, so a student who copes with the main paper by working slowly and carefully will struggle, not because the ideas are beyond them but because the pace assumes fluency. Fix the fluency first with short frequent algebra sets, and the new content lands much faster. It is also among the least widely taught courses in this emirate.

faqs.question: Is rereading notes a waste of revision time?
faqs.answer: Largely, yes, and it is the commonest method because it feels productive. Material becomes familiar and familiarity gets mistaken for recall. What works is retrieval, closing the book and writing down what can be remembered before checking, which is unpleasant precisely because it exposes the gaps; spacing, returning to a topic after a gap rather than blocking it in one evening; and timed practice marked against the published scheme, which is the only method that tests what the exam tests.

faqs.question: What is the single most efficient hour of IGCSE revision?
faqs.answer: An hour on data and graph questions, because they appear in Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography and Economics and reward the same handful of moves: read the scale, calculate rather than eyeball a gradient, quote the figure, state the trend with its cause, suggest an improvement. Improving that one skill lifts five subjects at once, which no single-subject revision plan can match. It is also the skill most students have never practised deliberately in any subject.

faqs.question: How many subjects should my child actually enter?
faqs.answer: At least five countable ones, with a margin. UAE equivalency on the British track requires five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, so a sensible list carries more than the minimum in case one subject goes wrong. Above that, the binding constraint is attention: a marginal subject nobody revises can cost more in other grades than it adds. Ask your child why each subject is on the list.

faqs.question: Is it true that six IGCSE subjects are needed for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. The published requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. One competitor page ranking for these queries states six. Confirm your own case with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation channel rather than with any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Can a tutor cover a subject for only four sessions?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Business, Economics, History, Geography or ICT that is often the right purchase rather than a compromise. The content volume is modest, the losses are usually a specific writing move, and the block should have an end date written into it from the start. A provider that converts every request into a standing weekly arrangement is managing its revenue; a short block that stops when the technique holds is what the subject actually needs.

faqs.question: Does living in Al Dhait affect how we revise?
faqs.answer: In one practical respect. Full past papers need ninety uninterrupted minutes in a quiet room, and Al Dhait's predominantly villa housing makes that easier to arrange than the creek-side apartments do. That matters because a complete paper is the only thing that tests pacing and the decision about which question to leave, neither of which shows up in a short weekday session. Put the full papers at the weekend and keep the weekday evenings for question groups.

faqs.question: Will my child's ICT or Geography coursework be a problem?
faqs.answer: Only if the help crosses a line. Where an IGCSE subject carries a coursework component, a tutor may teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria require, discuss structure and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may never write, redraft or complete the work or supply text for a student to paste in. Ask any provider what they will not do, in those words, and expect a clear and short answer.

faqs.question: Can we get past papers and boundary tables from the tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutor should supply them. Reproducing or distributing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure. Work is done against material the student legitimately holds through their school, marked against the published scheme in the session, with the official source referenced and linked. Boundary tables are also, as this page argues, a poor planning tool in any case.

faqs.question: For an Al Dhait candidate, which Pearson and Cambridge windows apply?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results on 22 January 2026. For Cambridge, June and November, with the February and March series offered in India only. Ask the exams officer which zone your Cambridge centre sits in, because the board states the correct zone timetable must be used.

intro.heading: A tutoring plan is a calendar before it is a syllabus
paragraphs: Ask a family in Al Hamra Village what they want from an IGCSE tutor and the answer is usually a subject. Ask when the exam is and the real brief appears. Thirty weeks out, the sensible plan covers content and builds habits. Eight weeks out, content work is mostly a distraction and the plan is technique, timing and the three topics losing the most marks. Three weeks out, it is pacing and sleep. Same child, same subject, three completely different pieces of work, and the only thing that distinguishes them is the date. So the first question we ask a family on this coast is not which subject but which week, because that single answer decides everything else in the plan.

The fixed points come from the boards and they are published. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in three windows across the year. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and in November, with provisional timetables released ahead of each series and a final version after. Everything else in the year - mocks, internal cut-offs, revision blocks - is arranged by schools and families inside those two windows.

One correction belongs here because it circulates widely in online revision guides. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. A candidate in Ras Al Khaimah does not sit it, and a plan built around a February exam window is a plan for another country. The UAE candidate's series is June, with November available as the resit and tier-correction route. If a tutor or a downloaded revision planner mentions February papers, that tutor is working from the wrong calendar.

The historical dates are worth writing down because they are checkable and because they settle an argument families have every year. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Read those together and the November route stops looking like a free second attempt: it produces a grade in January, which is after a great many application deadlines have closed.

What follows is the year read backwards, the timetable-zone trap that genuinely costs candidates exams, what Pearson's modular option does to a revision schedule, and an honest account of what each remaining window can achieve. IB Gram teaches Al Hamra Village students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we place no tutor at a UAE address, and visiting students in person is a service we run only in India. The practical effect is that a plan can start the week it is agreed rather than when someone is free to drive down the coast.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ha.programmesIntro: Four stages sit inside the window this page describes, and each has a date that matters more than its content. Here is what each one asks of a student on this coast.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The years in which the IGCSE tier decision is actually made. Checkpoint tests run in three windows across the year and schools use the results to stream students towards Core or Extended entry. The content is modest; the habits are not. Algebraic rearrangement, unit discipline, reading a graph and writing a conclusion that references data are the four skills that decide how Year 10 feels.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah, where the private-school sector is smaller than Dubai's, a child's set placement in Year 9 is harder to change later because fewer parallel classes exist. Al Hamra Village families should ask in Year 9 which tier the school is pointing at and what evidence would move the decision.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two or three written papers per subject in most cases, with syllabus codes that matter for past-paper selection: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English, 0455 Economics. Tiered subjects fix a grade ceiling at entry. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones and states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. Ask your school in Ras Al Khaimah which zone it sits in and get the dates from the school rather than from a search result. This is the single cheapest piece of risk management in the whole year.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: May/June and November sittings, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4BI1 Biology. Some courses run in a modular pattern, meaning units can be sat and banked across sittings rather than all in one block. Grades are reported on the 9-1 scale. Pearson publishes a provisional timetable well ahead of each series and then a final version closer to it.
programmes.countryNote: The modular option is a genuine planning tool for a Ras Al Khaimah student who is strong in one unit and weak in another, because it lets the weak unit have a whole extra term. Confirm with the school whether your child's course is actually being run modularly; many schools choose the linear route regardless.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The destination that makes the IGCSE tier decision consequential. AS sciences and A Level Mathematics assume Extended-tier fluency, not Core, and the first term exposes any gap in moles, algebra or graph work within weeks. Entry requirements are usually stated in grades, which means the ceiling set by an IGCSE tier entry can close a route two years before anyone looks at it.
programmes.countryNote: For students on this coast, continuing into Years 12 and 13 sometimes means a longer commute or a change of school, which is a decision worth making in Year 10 rather than after results. The Ministry of Education equivalency route for the British track also expects one A Level at grade E or better, or two AS Levels at the same grade, alongside five IGCSE passes.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ha.subjectsIntro: Each subject has its own point in the calendar where it becomes urgent. These are the IGCSE courses Ras Al Khaimah families ask about, with the component that decides the outcome and when it bites.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: No coursework, so the entire grade sits on timed papers plus the tier decision. That makes the spring mock the most informative document of the year: an Extended-entered student scoring mid-range and a Core-entered student scoring at the top need entirely different work in the weeks that follow.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Sat alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics, and the subject most often started too late. Calculus, logarithms and kinematics arrive at pace, and a student who is still shaky on 0580 algebra in the spring term will not catch both in one run-in. Sequence this one early.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper is the most improvable component in the whole qualification because it tests method writing rather than recall, and six focused sessions on describing a procedure precisely will usually show up in a mark. Electricity and electromagnetism remain the biggest content losses.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic and ionic equations separate the Extended cohort, and qualitative analysis is the cheapest block of marks on the paper, so it is the first thing to secure when the calendar is tight. Organic chemistry pays better once the calculation work is reliable, not before.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: A volume subject rather than a difficult one, which makes it the most responsive to a structured eight-week schedule. Marks come from the mark scheme's own terminology, so the productive drill is writing to the scheme rather than rereading notes, and that habit takes about two sessions to install.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: One or two grades spanning all three sciences, with its own content list and its own exclusions. The calendar trap is revising from single-science materials, which wastes weeks on topics that will not be examined. Check the syllabus code before any past-paper plan is built.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading marks are where the grade moves, not vocabulary. Students lose them by summarising when the question asks for the effect of a writer's choices. One piece of the student's own writing marked properly each fortnight through the spring term is worth more than any amount of model-answer reading.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Often needed as evidence of English proficiency later, so the grade has a life beyond the certificate. Writing tasks are assessed against a register and a word count that candidates routinely overshoot, and the listening paper rewards reading the questions before the recording begins.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Terminal assessment, diagram-led. An unlabelled axis or a curve shifted the wrong way loses the analysis marks whatever the prose says, and the top band needs evaluation that weighs rather than restates. Both are teachable inside a six-week block if the diagrams come first.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Second Language (Cambridge 0508 / 0544)
subjects.description: Taught alongside the licensed curriculum in every UAE private school as part of the federal baseline covering Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies. Worth knowing for planning: Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five accredited subjects the Ministry of Education requires for British-track equivalency.

regions.note: Resort-dominated and apartment-heavy, with the most involved visitor access in the emirate. The relevant calendar effect is that any arrangement depending on a third party arriving on time will slip, and in a run-in week a slipped session is a lost session.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ha.modesIntro: Three formats, chosen by how many weeks remain rather than by preference. The number of weeks is the only input that genuinely changes what a plan can deliver.

modes.title: Term-length weekly, running ahead of class
modes.description: One or two hours a week from the start of a term, deliberately covering topics shortly before the school teaches them so that class time becomes the second pass rather than the first. This is the only format that reliably moves a grade by more than one step, and it needs a term or more to do it.
bullets: Sequenced from the school's own scheme of work
Mock and entry dates built into the plan from week one
Written review every four to six weeks against named topics

modes.title: Eight-week run-in built from timed papers
modes.description: Two or three hours a week, each session anchored to a timed section of a real past paper marked against the published scheme. New content only where a gap is blocking a paper. The weekly output is a ranked list of what is costing the most marks, which is also the agenda for the following session.
bullets: Zone-correct timetable confirmed before the plan is written
Marks tracked by topic rather than as a percentage
Deliberate taper across the final ten days

modes.title: Three-week triage
modes.description: The format for a family who arrives very late. No new content at all. The work is pacing, command terms, the two highest-value topics and a rehearsal of the actual paper under time. Expectations are set honestly at the first session: this protects marks that are being thrown away rather than adding knowledge.

sections.heading: The Cambridge and Pearson year counted backwards, term by term
paragraphs: Read forwards, a school year looks like three terms and an exam at the end. Read backwards from the paper, it looks like a sequence of closing doors. The tier decision closes first, in Year 9 or early Year 10. The entry deadline closes months before the papers. The mock window passes, and with it the last good diagnostic. Then the taper, then the hall. Each of those has a thing that should already be done by the time it arrives, and the table below states what.

The entry deadline is the line in that table that families most often meet too late. In a tiered Cambridge subject, entry fixes the grade ceiling: a Core entry in Mathematics 0580 caps the grade at a 5 on the 9-1 scale, and the exam cannot award above the tier regardless of how well it is sat. A student whose ability becomes obvious in the spring term is a student whose ceiling was set before anyone noticed. Nothing a tutor does in April changes that, and anyone who implies otherwise is selling.

The second most-missed line is the mock. A mock sat under genuine conditions and marked to the published scheme is the most useful document a family will see all year, and it arrives with enough runway to act on. A mock treated as a formality, half-marked and returned in a pile, produces a grade and no information. If one thing on this page is worth doing this week, it is asking the school when the mocks fall and making sure the marked papers come home.

The final line is the one nobody plans: the taper. The fortnight before the first paper should reduce load rather than increase it. Students who cram in that window perform worse than students who revisit two named weak topics, sleep properly and walk in having already sat that paper several times under time. Building the taper into the plan in advance is the difference between a schedule that is followed and one that is abandoned in a panic.

sections.heading: The timetable-zone trap, and how a candidate loses a whole paper
paragraphs: This is the most concrete piece of risk on the page and it is almost never mentioned by anyone selling tutoring. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, publishes a timetable per zone, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. It also states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong version. That is not a disclaimer buried in small print; it is a plain warning about a real failure mode.

The way this happens is mundane. A parent searches for the exam timetable, finds a version, and builds a revision plan on it. A tutor does the same. Three months later a student peaks a week early or, worse, prepares for a paper on the wrong day. The dates in two zones can differ, and the student in Ras Al Khaimah who downloaded a version intended for another zone has no recourse. The fix costs one email: ask your school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in and take the dates from them.

Pearson's equivalent risk is different in shape. Pearson publishes a provisional timetable well ahead of each series and then a final version, and the provisional one can be revised. Any plan built from a restated date on somebody's web page is therefore built on a snapshot. The published history gives the pattern safely: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The sensible habit is to plan from months and to confirm specific days against the live official timetable.

For a tutoring plan the practical consequence is that the calendar check belongs in week one, not week six. Before any topic sequencing, we want the board, the tier, the subject codes and the zone, taken from the school. A plan that is one week out of phase in its final fortnight wastes the most valuable fortnight in the year, and it is entirely avoidable.

Cambridge says it cannot accept responsibility for a wrong-zone error
Get the zone and the dates from your school's examinations officer

sections.heading: Pearson's modular option, and what banking a unit does to a schedule
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE candidates normally sit a whole subject in one series. Some Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses can be taken in a modular pattern, with units sat and banked across sittings. Those two sentences describe genuinely different planning problems, and a family whose child sits Pearson modularly has an option that a Cambridge family does not.

The option is useful when a student's strength is uneven. A candidate who is confident on one unit and badly behind on another can sit the strong unit, bank the result, and give the weak unit an additional term of preparation rather than meeting both in the same fortnight. That is a real reduction in peak load, and peak load is what causes the collapse in the final weeks. It also gives a student a real grade in hand, which does more for confidence than any amount of encouragement.

It has costs too, and they should be stated. Banking a unit means sitting an examination earlier, in a term that would otherwise be used for teaching, and it commits the student to a result before they have finished growing into the subject. Where a student is improving quickly, sitting early locks in a weaker performance. The decision needs the school's view, because the school controls whether the course is actually being run modularly at all; plenty of schools choose the linear route whatever the specification allows.

The table below sets the two sequencing patterns side by side. The column that matters for a family in Al Hamra Village is the last one: what each pattern asks of a tutoring plan. A linear plan concentrates support in one run-in. A modular plan needs two smaller run-ins and a quieter middle, which for a working household is often the easier shape to sustain.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, six weeks, three weeks: an honest account of each
paragraphs: Families arrive at different distances from the paper and deserve a straight answer about what each distance can buy. Eight weeks is a good position. It is enough to diagnose properly from a marked mock, drill three or four high-cost topics, install mark-scheme discipline, teach command terms, and sit several full papers under time with a week to taper. Most of the marks recovered in that window are technique marks, which is why the gain can be larger than parents expect.

Six weeks narrows the ambition to two or three topics plus technique. The diagnosis has to come from work that already exists rather than from a fresh assessment, and nothing gets taught twice. It still works, and a well-run six-week block is a better use of money than a vague term of weekly sessions, because the target is explicit and the end is visible.

Three weeks is triage and should be sold as triage. No new content. The work is a full paper under conditions in week one, a stop rule for when to abandon a question, the two highest-value topics, command terms, and rehearsal. The honest framing is that this protects marks currently being thrown away. It does not add knowledge, and a provider who promises otherwise at three weeks is making a claim nobody can keep.

What none of these windows can do is substitute for the two-year course. A student who has never met electromagnetic induction, mole calculations and differentiation will not acquire all three alongside everything else, however good the tutor. Saying so at the first conversation is part of the job, and it is also why the most valuable thing a family in Al Hamra Village can do is read the calendar in the autumn rather than in the spring.

sections.heading: Results arithmetic: August grades, January grades, and what each one is good for
paragraphs: Results dates are not administrative trivia; they decide which doors a grade can open. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those two facts together determine the whole shape of the resit conversation for a candidate in Ras Al Khaimah, and they are published rather than inferred.

The June pattern is simple. A grade awarded in August is available for a sixth-form or Year 12 place starting the following month, for an application that closes in the autumn, and for the Ministry of Education equivalency file. It is the grade that does everything. The November pattern is not simple: the grade exists in January, which is after a great many application deadlines and after most school places have been allocated. It is still worth having, and for a tier correction it may be the only route, but it is a repair rather than a plan.

There is a second, quieter consequence. A student who sits in November and waits until January to know the outcome spends the autumn term in uncertainty, often while beginning an AS Level course that assumed a different grade. Where a November entry is the right call, the sensible accompanying decision is to agree with the school in advance what happens under each outcome, rather than treating January as a surprise to be dealt with when it arrives.

The table turns this into a planning sequence. The useful habit it encourages is working backwards from the thing the grade is for - a school place, a course entry requirement, an equivalency file - rather than forwards from the exam. That is a five-minute exercise and it frequently changes which series a family chooses.

sections.heading: Making the spring mock genuinely diagnostic
paragraphs: A mock is the only full rehearsal most students get, and the information in it is in the pattern of lost marks rather than in the grade. Four patterns recur and each wants a different response. Marks scattered thinly everywhere points to fluency, and the answer is volume of timed practice rather than teaching. Marks clustered in two or three topics points to targeted teaching, which is the classic eight-week shape.

An unfinished final section is a pacing problem. The fix is a stopwatch, a stop rule for abandoning a question, and practice at reading a whole paper before starting, not more content. And full marks on recall questions with nothing on extended responses is a command-term problem: a student treating describe, explain, compare and evaluate as synonyms will lose the same marks in every paper in every subject until someone puts a mark scheme in front of them and shows the difference. That is a two-session fix worth more than a term of revision.

To get that information out of a mock, three things have to happen. The paper has to be sat under real conditions, including timing. It has to be marked against the published scheme rather than impressionistically. And it has to come home. A school that returns a grade without the script has given the family a number and withheld the data, and it is entirely reasonable to ask for the paper.

So the request we make of every family in Al Hamra Village is the same: send the marked mock, not a description of it. Where no mock exists, the first session includes a timed section so that the plan is built on evidence. It takes twenty minutes and it prevents the most common failure in tutoring, which is a tutor teaching the topic the parent named rather than the topic the marks point to.

sections.heading: Ramadan, travel and the real shape of a Ras Al Khaimah school year
paragraphs: A revision schedule has to survive the actual year rather than an idealised one. Private schools here teach the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the licensed international curriculum, because the federal baseline covers Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and the Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate including the approval of curricula, programmes and assessment methods. The practical consequence is a fuller timetable than the exam entries suggest and a homework load to match.

Ramadan reshapes the day. School hours shorten, attention moves either early or well after sunset, and a mid-afternoon session that has worked all year stops working. The answer is planned rather than improvised: shift sessions after Iftar, shorten them to around 45 minutes, and accept that a shorter focused session beats a long one at the wrong hour. Families who arrange this before the month begins keep their momentum; families who try to hold the old slot generally lose three or four weeks.

Travel is the other recurring interruption on this coast, where plenty of households leave during breaks and sometimes during term. An online plan survives that intact, because a Tuesday session can happen from anywhere with a connection. Continuity matters more than intensity in the final term, and a kept session during a trip is worth more than two extra ones on return.

Put it together and the year has a shape. Cover content while the timetable is stable in the autumn and winter. Use the mock to set the plan. Shorten and move sessions through Ramadan if it falls in the run-in. Confirm the zone timetable with the school before the final fortnight is designed. Then taper. None of that depends on anyone being nearby; all of it depends on someone knowing which paper your child is sitting and when.

process.description: The marked paper shows in minutes whether the problem is content, technique, pacing or command terms, and those four need different work. Where no mock exists yet, the first session starts with a timed section so the plan rests on evidence rather than impression.

process.description: One 45 to 60-minute one-to-one session over live video, no card details and no obligation. What follows is a plan with weeks in it: what each week covers, when the full papers happen, and when the taper starts. A plan without dates is a subscription.

process.title: Protect the schedule through Ramadan and travel
process.description: Both are predictable, so both get planned for rather than reacted to. Shorter post-Iftar sessions during Ramadan, kept slots during trips, and a written taper for the final ten days. Continuity through the disruptions is worth more than extra hours around them.

process.title: Decide the series before the deadline, not after results
process.description: The June-or-November question is answered before the entry deadline, with the school, on the evidence of the mock. Deciding after results in August means a scramble; deciding in advance means the November route is a plan rather than a consolation.

Confirming the zone before the plan is written costs one email and protects the most valuable fortnight of the year.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on short windows
whyPoints.description: Eight weeks buys technique, topic repair and rehearsal. Three weeks buys pacing and command terms. Neither buys a two-year syllabus. We say which window you are in at the first conversation rather than discovering it together in week five.

faqs.question: When does my child's IGCSE entry deadline fall, and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, with the school setting an internal cut-off earlier still. It matters because entry fixes the tier, and in a tiered Cambridge subject the tier fixes the grade ceiling: a Core entry in Mathematics 0580 caps the achievable grade at a 5 on the 9-1 scale however well the paper is sat. A student whose capability becomes obvious in the spring term had their ceiling set the previous autumn. Ask the examinations officer for the internal deadline early in the year, not late.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge timetable zone and how do I find ours?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each. It states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The way to find yours is to ask your school's examinations officer, not to search for a timetable. This is the cheapest piece of risk management available in the whole year and it takes one email.

faqs.question: Does a student in Ras Al Khaimah ever sit the February or March Cambridge papers?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series, with November as the resit and tier-correction route, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. This matters because revision planners and tutor guides written for the Indian calendar circulate widely online, and a plan peaking for February papers is a plan for a different country. If someone mentions February papers for your child, they are working from the wrong calendar.

faqs.question: Is a November entry worth it if June does not go well for my child?
faqs.answer: As a response to a result, often yes. As a hedge planned in advance, rarely. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November grade is a January grade, which lands after many application deadlines and most school place allocations. It earns its place in two cases: correcting a tier where a Core-capped candidate needs a higher grade for an AS Level course, and repairing one subject that has blocked a route. In both the work is narrow and well suited to a short block.

faqs.question: What can eight weeks of tutoring realistically do before the papers?
faqs.answer: A good deal, provided the eight weeks are spent on the right things. It is enough to diagnose properly from a marked mock, drill the three or four topics costing the most marks, install the habit of writing to the mark scheme, teach command terms and sit several full papers under time with a week left to taper. Most recovered marks in that window are technique rather than knowledge. What it cannot do is teach a two-year syllabus that was never learned in the first place.

faqs.question: Our child is three weeks from the first paper. Is there any point starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the goal stated honestly as triage. Three weeks protects marks currently being thrown away rather than adding knowledge. The work is a full paper under conditions in week one, a stop rule for abandoning a question that is eating time, the two highest-value topics, command-term discipline and rehearsal. Nothing new gets introduced after the halfway point. A provider who promises a transformation at three weeks is making a claim they cannot keep, and the honest version is worth more.

faqs.question: What does Pearson's modular option change for a revision plan?
faqs.answer: It splits one large peak into two smaller ones. Where a Pearson course is run modularly, units can be sat and banked across sittings, so a student who is strong on one unit and behind on another can bank the strong one and give the weak one an extra term rather than meeting both in the same fortnight. The cost is that an early sitting locks in an earlier standard, which is a poor trade for a student improving fast. The school decides whether the course runs modularly at all.

faqs.question: Which mock paper pattern should worry us most?
faqs.answer: An unfinished final section, because it means marks are being lost to pacing rather than to knowledge and the student may not realise it. The response is a stopwatch, a rule about when to abandon a question and practice reading the whole paper before starting. The second pattern to take seriously is full marks on recall questions with nothing on extended responses, which signals that describe, explain, compare and evaluate are being treated as synonyms. That is usually a two-session fix.

faqs.question: Can we get the actual mock script back from the school?
faqs.answer: It is entirely reasonable to ask, and worth insisting on. A grade without the script is a number with the data withheld, and the information a family needs is in the distribution of lost marks: which topics, which question types, whether marks went missing at the start of long questions or at the end, whether the last pages are blank. Twenty minutes with the marked paper produces a better plan than an hour of conversation about how the term has gone, and it costs nothing.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a revision schedule in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: It moves it rather than interrupting it. School hours shorten, attention shifts either early or well after sunset, and an afternoon slot that worked all year stops working. The pattern that holds is shorter sessions after Iftar, often around 45 minutes rather than a full hour, arranged before the month begins. Families who plan the shift keep their momentum through what is often the most important stretch of the run-in; families who try to hold the old slot typically lose three or four weeks of it.

faqs.question: We travel during term. Will that break a tutoring plan on this coast?
faqs.answer: Not an online one. A Tuesday session can run from anywhere with a usable connection, which is one of the practical reasons we do not place tutors at UAE addresses at all. Continuity matters more than intensity in a final term: a kept session during a trip is worth more than two extra ones on return, because the value comes from acting on feedback between sessions rather than from total hours. Tell us travel dates when the plan is written so the sequence allows for them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if our school does not offer a subject my child wants?
faqs.answer: Teaching it, yes; entering for it, no. A private-candidate entry has to be arranged through a centre willing to accept external candidates, and that arrangement needs to be in place well before the entry deadline rather than discovered late. The teaching side works well online, since the subject is taught to the published syllabus with past papers from the correct code. Start with the centre question, because without a seat in an examination room the teaching has nowhere to go.

faqs.question: Do we need to confirm the exam board as well as the subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and from the statement of entry rather than the textbook. Schools change board between cohorts and shelves lag behind. The board decides paper structure, mark-scheme wording and which syllabus code past papers must come from: Cambridge 0625 against Pearson 4PH1, Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1. A tutor working from the wrong code is teaching a similar subject rather than the one your child sits, and the difference shows up in the exam rather than in the sessions.

faqs.question: Why not just hire someone local in Al Hamra Village for the run-in?
faqs.answer: Because the run-in is exactly when subject precision matters most and proximity matters least. Ras Al Khaimah has a comparatively small private-school sector, so the number of people here who have taught your child's exact subject and tier to an examination class is small, and the few who have are usually already booked every evening. Online one-to-one keeps the speed that made the search urgent while widening the choice of tutor. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; this is live video teaching.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ha.closingBody: An IGCSE plan is only as good as the calendar it is built on. We will say plainly what the remaining weeks can achieve and what they cannot, and you can test the match with a free trial lesson before committing. Lessons for Al Hamra Village students are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the school day, shortened after Iftar during Ramadan and kept running through travel.

intro.heading: Al Mamourah against the next street over, and why it barely matters
paragraphs: Al Mamourah sits in the Ras Al Khaimah city area, a few minutes from Al Qusaidat, Julphar and the older residential grid behind the creek. Ask three families in these three districts where they look for IGCSE help and you will get three answers framed around geography: somebody nearby, somebody who can come after work, somebody a neighbour used. None of those answers describes a difference that affects a grade.

Here is the part that surprises people. The honest comparison between Al Mamourah and Al Qusaidat, or between either and Al Dhait, produces almost no difference at all. The same schools serve them, mostly in Al Nakheel, Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab. The same buses run. The same evening window opens around five. And the same scarcity applies: a subject with a dozen Extended-tier candidates in the emirate has a dozen candidates' worth of specialist teaching available locally, wherever the family happens to live.

Which means the comparison worth making is not between neighbourhoods. It is between exam boards, between tiers, between delivery formats, and between provider models. Those four comparisons genuinely change outcomes, they are all answerable with published facts, and almost nobody in this market publishes them. So this page is built as a set of tables rather than as prose about an area, because the area is the least informative variable in the whole decision.

A word on the delivery format, stated early rather than buried. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one and live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run in India only. In-home tutoring exists in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel; what that premium buys in Ras Al Khaimah is a shorter list of available teachers, which the tables below set out plainly.

The nine comparisons that follow are: the city-area neighbourhoods against each other, the provider models against each other, Cambridge against Pearson for the same subject, Core against Extended, online against in-home against small group, the market rate bands with their publishers named, Ras Al Khaimah against Dubai on tutor supply, the tutor permit categories, and the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements by curriculum. Each one is a table with information in every cell.

Read them in any order. If you are short of time, the tier comparison and the board comparison are the two that most often change what a family does next, because a student entered for the wrong tier or taught in the wrong examination idiom is losing marks for a reason that has nothing to do with how hard they are working.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ma.programmesIntro: Three programmes produce the comparisons on this page, and a family in Al Mamourah may be dealing with two of them at once across siblings at different schools.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with Core and Extended tiers across most subjects. Core covers less content and caps at grade C; Extended runs the full A* to G range. The syllabus code is the operative detail rather than the subject name, because 0580 Mathematics, 0606 Additional Mathematics and 0607 International Mathematics are three different courses sitting behind one word.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah centres sit the June and November series. The February and March series Cambridge offers belongs to India alone and should never appear in an Al Mamourah plan. Each centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct zone version of the timetable, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same certificate name reached through different papers. Codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4BI1 Biology sit on a 9 to 1 grading scale, with Foundation and Higher tiers in mathematics rather than Core and Extended. Several subjects use fewer, longer papers than the Cambridge equivalent, which changes how a mock should be timed.
programmes.countryNote: International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates show the cycle; Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so plan from the live official file.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The two years that decide the tier entry. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and produce a diagnostic report rather than a certificate. A Year 9 report showing weak algebraic fluency is the earliest and cheapest warning available that 0580 Extended will be a struggle two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Al Mamourah families overwhelmingly treat Year 9 as a quiet year and start tuition in Year 11. Reversing that order costs less and works better: eight weeks of algebra at Year 9 removes the gap that otherwise absorbs an entire exam-year budget. Checkpoint is also the only low-stakes external data point most students here generate before the IGCSE series itself.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The common next step for a Ras Al Khaimah student who does not move into an IB school. Three or four subjects rather than ten, with AS available as a halfway point. Entry is constrained by IGCSE grades, so the grades out of Year 11 set the ceiling on what is available in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: This matters to the Ministry of Education equivalency file as well as to admissions. The published British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than E or grade 3.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ma.subjectsIntro: Each subject below names the board codes together, because the comparison between them is the thing an Al Mamourah parent most often needs and least often gets.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended sits two papers; Pearson 4MA1 Higher sits two papers of different length and question weighting. Both reward written method lines over mental arithmetic. The practical difference is question style rather than content, which is exactly why a tutor must be matched to the code.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Both extend into calculus and are taken alongside the main mathematics entry by students heading to A Level. Differentiation of composite functions is the common failure point. A student comfortable with 0580 Extended can still find these unfamiliar because the command terms want proof-shaped answers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical component carry the losses on both boards. Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical paper with a learnable vocabulary about repeats, precision and anomalous results; Pearson handles practical skills differently, which changes what revision should target.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic under time pressure and organic pathways decide the grade on both. Cambridge's qualitative analysis table is pure recall and the cheapest marks available in the paper. Students who revise only the calculations leave those marks untouched.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty, and the mark schemes accept a short list of specific phrases. Genetics crosses and osmosis write-ups are where marks go missing, and the fix is learning the scheme's language rather than rereading the chapter.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Reading precision rather than fluency is what the paper measures. The summary question has a word ceiling and a content-point tally, so a student who paraphrases elegantly can lose the lifted detail the scheme requires. Speaking is a separate endorsement on 0510.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response reward control of register above range of vocabulary. The commonest loss is a student answering the text rather than the question. Past papers with the published scheme open is close to the whole intervention.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the band. A labelled axis, a shifted curve and a marked new equilibrium score where prose does not. In the longer questions evaluation must reach a judgement rather than list both sides of an argument.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the case study separates grades. Students who revise definitions score the first mark and stop; the rest require naming the business in the stem and using its figures. Break-even and cash-flow calculations are reliable marks that get skipped in revision.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Data representation and networking are heavily recalled and heavily mis-remembered, hexadecimal conversion most of all. Pseudocode must be internally consistent, a habit built by writing code under time rather than by reading it.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study specificity carries the top band: a named place with a figure and a date outscores a general description every time. Map and graph skills are the most teachable part of the syllabus and routinely the least practised.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two awards, so breadth beats depth. Students lose marks preparing each strand as though it were a full single subject. The tutor's job is triage: which topics are examined thinly and which carry real weight.

sections.heading: Al Mamourah against its neighbours, compared honestly
paragraphs: Start with the comparison that parents actually make, so it can be put aside. The question is whether living in Al Mamourah rather than Al Qusaidat, Julphar or Al Dhait changes what IGCSE support is available or sensible. The answer is almost no, and the table below shows why: the school clusters are shared, the commutes differ by minutes rather than by half-hours, and the local supply of Extended-tier specialists is identical because it is an emirate-level constraint rather than a district-level one.

What does differ slightly is timing. A family commuting to Al Hamra Village loses more of the evening than one schooled in Al Nakheel, which pushes the realistic start of a session later. In Al Dhait, activities rather than travel decide which evening is free. Those are real differences and they affect scheduling, not tutor choice. Nobody should pick a different tutor because they live three kilometres further from the creek.

The reason this matters is that proximity-based searching produces a false sense of having compared something. A parent who has rung four people who can reach Al Mamourah has compared availability, not expertise. A parent who has asked four people which syllabus code they have taught and seen a marked script has compared the thing that moves marks. The second list is usually shorter and almost always better.

So the recommendation for Al Mamourah is the recommendation for the whole city area: choose on the board, the code and the component, and accept that the delivery will be online because that is what makes choosing on those three things possible in a northern emirate. The rest of this page compares the variables that actually vary.

A tuition centre with premises has fixed overheads and tends to fill seats, which pushes towards small groups. sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson for the same subject
paragraphs: This is the comparison that most often explains a disappointing mock, and most Al Mamourah parents have never been shown it. The two boards award a qualification with almost the same name and assess it differently enough that a tutor who knows one and not the other will teach correct content in the wrong examination idiom. Content overlap is high; paper structure, grading scale, tiering and question phrasing are not.

The grading difference alone changes how a predicted grade should be read. Cambridge runs A* to G with Core entries capped at C. Pearson runs 9 to 1, with 9 above the old A* and no simple one-to-one mapping between the scales. A parent told their child is predicted a 6 and comparing it with a sibling predicted a B is comparing two different currencies without an exchange rate.

Tiering works differently too. Cambridge splits most subjects into Core and Extended with separate papers. Pearson mathematics uses Foundation and Higher tiers; several Pearson sciences are untiered. That changes the entry decision and it changes what a mock result means, since a strong performance on a Foundation paper and a weak one on a Higher paper can produce the same raw mark and entirely different grades.

For a tutor, the practical consequence is specific. Question stems differ in length and in how much scaffolding they offer. Mark schemes differ in the phrases they accept. The number and duration of papers differ, which changes pacing practice. Send the code from the school's entry confirmation rather than the subject name from the timetable, and the first session starts in the right place.

sections.heading: Core against Extended, and the cost of the wrong entry
paragraphs: A tier decision made quietly in Year 10 can cap a grade two years later, and families in Al Mamourah frequently discover the cap at the point of applying for a sixth-form place. Core and Extended are not easier and harder versions of one paper; they are different entries with different content, different papers and a different grade ceiling. A Core entry cannot produce a B however well the student performs.

The decision should be made on evidence rather than on temperament. A Year 9 Checkpoint report or an internal assessment showing fluent algebraic manipulation points to Extended. A student who reaches correct answers but cannot show method, or who runs out of time consistently, may genuinely be better served by Core in that subject while sitting Extended in others. Mixed entries across subjects are normal and often the right answer.

What makes this urgent is the entry window. The tier is part of the entry the school submits to the board months before the first paper, so the conversation has to happen inside that window rather than in the spring. A family who decides in March that Extended was the right call for chemistry has made a correct decision too late to act on in that series.

Use it with a marked script and the school's entry deadline in front of you, and the conversation with the subject teacher becomes a short one.

sections.heading: Online against in-home against small group
paragraphs: This is the comparison the market mostly refuses to make honestly, usually because the page is selling one of the three. So here is the honest version, including what each format does better. A tutor physically present can read a student's written working upside down on the desk and interrupt mid-line. That is a genuine advantage and online delivery replaces it with a document camera or a phone propped over the page, which has to be asked for and set up.

What online gives back is a deeper pool, a shared screen on the actual past paper with annotations saved afterwards, no travel cost in either direction, a session that still runs when the family is travelling or the road is closed, and a written record. In Ras Al Khaimah the pool argument is decisive rather than marginal, because a student sitting Computer Science 0478 or Economics 0455 at Extended tier may have no local specialist within a reasonable drive at all.

Small group deserves its own column because it is cheaper and genuinely suits some students. A group of three working through past papers with a good teacher is a sound arrangement for a student who is broadly on track and needs structure. It is a poor arrangement for a student with a specific component problem, because the group moves at the group's pace and the specific problem is nobody else's.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE and does not run group classes on these pages; the service is one-to-one over live video. The table includes in-home and group anyway, with published rate bands, because a comparison that omits the alternatives is advertising rather than information.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Most rate comparisons in this market stop at the number. The more useful question is what the difference between two numbers actually buys, and for the in-home premium the answer is uncomfortable: it buys a journey. UAE rate surveys place in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is not better teaching; it is the tutor's evening spent in a car.

Working through the bands with their publishers named: budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45-150, with one platform publishing from AED 33-52 and one content site from AED 45-65. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150-300, with a UAE agency publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with a UK agency quoting AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with one provider publishing AED 650.

Monthly figures are often the more honest comparison because they expose the total. Surveys put a weekly hour at roughly AED 240-600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages include online bundles from around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home bundles at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits.

All of these belong to the provider or survey that published them. None is an IB Gram price and nothing here is a quote. sections.heading: Ras Al Khaimah against Dubai, on tutor supply
paragraphs: The argument for online delivery is much stronger here than it is two hours down the coast, and it is worth seeing the numbers that make it so. Dubai's private sector reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. Dubai also added seven new private schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

Ras Al Khaimah's private-school set is a fraction of that, concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab. The consequence is not worse teaching; it is less redundancy. In Dubai a parent who cannot find a 0625 Extended specialist in one direction tries another. In Al Mamourah there may be one obvious person and they may be fully booked, which converts a preference for local delivery into a constraint on quality.

This is the comparison that should settle the format question for most families here. A Dubai parent choosing in-home over online is choosing between two deep pools. A Ras Al Khaimah parent making the same choice is choosing between a deep pool and a shallow one. Both are legitimate decisions; only one of them is usually being made with the information in front of the person making it.

It also explains why the eighteen gaps in this market are gaps. Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain appear essentially nowhere in the competitor pages that rank for these searches, and ADEK is named by none of them. Pages written about Dubai and lightly relabelled do not describe the problem a family in Al Mamourah has, which is why this one is built around the emirate's actual constraints.

sections.heading: The tutor permit categories compared
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit, and the categories are worth comparing because parents assume a school teacher automatically qualifies and that a student never could. Both assumptions are wrong. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years.

The eligible groups named on the federal portal are teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service listing covers issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a two-working-day completion time.

Two constraints sit alongside eligibility. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published, so a specific figure quoted to you is invented. And the permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school, which matches ADEK's professional-ethics position for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi.

A business is a different matter again. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any UAE regulator or examination board, and this page claims none.

sections.heading: Equivalency compared across curricula
paragraphs: If your child intends to apply to a UAE university, the certificate has to be made equivalent by the Ministry of Education, and the requirements differ by curriculum. This is one of the clearest gaps in the market: several competitor clusters do not mention equivalency at all, and one ranking page publishes the wrong subject count for the British track, which is the kind of error a family acts on.

The published British-track rule asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The exclusion is the part families miss: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

The American track is different in kind rather than in degree. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB, this page publishes no points threshold, because none has been read on the Ministry's own site and an unverified figure on a page like this would be a liability rather than a service.

Two cautions to carry. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, does not submit it on your behalf and guarantees no outcome from it; it is a Ministry process and the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority is where it should be verified. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression, whatever urgency anybody attaches to it.

process.title: Send the board and the code
process.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different courses. Take the code from the school's entry confirmation rather than the subject name on the timetable, and include the tier. That single detail removes the commonest cause of a poor first match and of a wasted first month.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a report
process.description: A marked mock paper shows in five minutes whether the losses are content, missing method lines, or answering the wrong command term. A report comment shows none of that. Component marks are what set the order of work, and they are usually already in the school's hands.

process.description: You get the number of sessions, the target, the order of topics and the date the block finishes. Compare total block cost against that target rather than comparing hourly rates, because an hourly rate with no endpoint is the easiest thing in this market to quote and the least informative.

process.title: Notes after every session
process.description: What was covered, what was set, what the tutor is watching next. Six notes with no movement in a marked script is a signal to change the match rather than to add sessions, and having it in writing is what makes that judgement possible.

process.description: For a thinly taught subject at Extended tier there may be nobody suitable free this month. You will hear that, with a date or an alternative, rather than being matched to somebody adjacent. In an exam year that honesty is worth more than speed.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether we live in Al Mamourah or Al Qusaidat for finding a tutor?
faqs.answer: Hardly at all. The two districts share bus routes, school options and the same evening window that opens around five once the school run is done. The supply of Extended-tier subject specialists is an emirate-level constraint rather than a district-level one, so the answer to the same question is the same in both places. What does differ is scheduling: a family commuting to Al Hamra Village loses more of the evening than one schooled in Al Nakheel, which pushes the session start later.

faqs.question: Where do I look up whether Al Mamourah schools use Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the entry confirmation, which carries the board and the syllabus code for every subject. Do not rely on the timetable, because it usually shows subject names only, and the name is the part the two boards share. The distinction matters: Cambridge grades A* to G with Core capped at C, Pearson grades 9 to 1, and the paper structures, mark-scheme phrasing and tiering differ. A tutor matched to the wrong board teaches correct content in the wrong examination idiom.

faqs.question: Is a Cambridge grade 6 the same as a Pearson grade 6?
faqs.answer: No, and the question itself shows why the comparison trips families up. Cambridge uses letters, A* to G, with Core entries capped at C. Pearson uses numbers, 9 to 1, where 9 sits above the old A*. There is no clean one-to-one mapping between the two, so comparing a predicted 6 on one board with a predicted B on the other is comparing currencies without an exchange rate. Ask the school which board, then read the prediction against that board's own scale.

faqs.question: Which is better value in Ras Al Khaimah, a group class or one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong. A small group of three working past papers with a good teacher suits a student who is broadly on track and needs structure, and it costs less per hour. It suits a student with a specific component problem poorly, because the group moves at the group's pace and that problem belongs to one person. One-to-one is the format to buy when a marked script shows a particular paper or topic cluster failing rather than a general lack of practice.

faqs.question: What does paying for a home visit actually get us here?
faqs.answer: A journey, mostly. Published UAE rates put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The difference pays for the tutor's time in the car rather than for better teaching. In Ras Al Khaimah it also narrows the pool, because the people who can reach Al Mamourah on a weekday evening are a short list and the people who have taught your child's exact syllabus code are a different one.

faqs.question: Can my child sit Core in one subject and Extended in another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and mixed entries across subjects are normal rather than a compromise. The tier is set per subject when the school submits the entry, so a student can sit Extended in mathematics and Core in a subject they do not intend to continue. What matters is making the decision inside the entry window on evidence from a marked script, because a Core entry caps the grade at C however well the student performs on the day.

faqs.question: Which provider model should a Ras Al Khaimah family actually choose?
faqs.answer: Decide what you need before comparing brands. A marketplace is cheap and puts the whole selection risk on the parent. A freelance tutor may be excellent and is a single point of failure with no replacement mid-term. A centre with premises tends towards small groups because of its overheads. An agency does the matching and charges for it. An online platform widens the pool and rules out in-home delivery. Each is a reasonable answer to a different question, and the mistake is choosing without knowing which you bought.

faqs.question: Why is online delivery a stronger argument in RAK than in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because of redundancy. Dubai reported 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, so a parent who cannot find a specialist in one direction tries another. Ras Al Khaimah's private provision is concentrated in three areas, which means there may be one obvious local person for a given syllabus code and they may be fully booked. A Dubai family choosing in-home picks between two deep pools; a family here picks between a deep pool and a shallow one.

faqs.question: Can a university student legally tutor my child in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the permit. The federal portal lists university students among the eligible applicants for the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, alongside registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, and school students aged 15 to 18. The permit is issued by MoHRE free of charge for two years. Whether a university student is the right tutor for an Extended-tier component problem is a separate question from whether they may lawfully do it.

faqs.question: Will five passes be enough when my child applies inside the UAE?
faqs.answer: The published British-track equivalency rule asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking tutoring page currently states six subjects, which is wrong. Verify the current rule with the Ministry of Education or the emirate attestation authority, since no tutoring page is the authority on it.

faqs.question: Does my child's Cambridge centre zone change anything for us?
faqs.answer: It changes which timetable you should be reading. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in, then take the timetable from the board's own site rather than from an aggregator page, and plan revision in the paper order it shows.

faqs.question: Our two children sit different boards - can one evening cover both?
faqs.answer: Yes, as consecutive one-to-one slots rather than a shared lesson. Two children at different schools on different boards need their own tutors matched to their own codes, but running those slots back to back means one committed evening instead of two. That is a common arrangement in Al Mamourah households, where siblings are frequently split across Cambridge and Pearson, and it is usually the difference between the second child's sessions happening and quietly lapsing.

faqs.question: Is an alternative-to-practical paper something a tutor can prepare online?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the better uses of an online session. The component rewards a fixed vocabulary about variables, repeats, precision and anomalous results, plus the ability to read and complete a results table, and all of that is paper-based work on a shared screen. What an online session cannot substitute for is handling apparatus in the school laboratory, which belongs to the school's own teaching and should not be outsourced to tuition in the first place.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks left. Which comparison on this page matters most?
faqs.answer: The tier comparison, then the format comparison, and nothing else. At eight weeks the entry is fixed, so the useful question is whether the plan matches the tier your child is actually sitting and whether the sessions can realistically happen in the evening window you have. Everything else on this page is a decision for a family with a year or more in hand. Open with a full paper sat to time, set the topic order from its component marks, and stop adding new content in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Do you offer in-home lessons if we pay the premium?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE at any price; home visits are a service we run in India only. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market does exist here and published rates run roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel, so the option is real and available elsewhere. We state the limit on the page rather than after a payment, because the alternative is a family waiting for somebody who was never coming.

faqs.question: How should we compare two quotes we have received?
faqs.answer: On total block cost against a named target, not on hourly rate. Ask each provider how many sessions, aimed at which component, and what evidence will show whether it worked. Ten sessions at a specialist rate with a defined target is usually a smaller and better-spent sum than an open-ended cheap weekly slot that runs for two years. An hourly rate quoted without a session count or an endpoint is the easiest number in this market to publish and the least useful one to compare.
