intro.heading: The cost question, answered before anything is sold to you
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry that reaches us from Al Marjan Island begins with price, and almost none of the pages competing for this search will answer it. Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages in the UAE publish no figure at all; two quote US dollars, a currency no family here transacts in. One agency's own frequently-asked-questions block poses the question "how much does a tutor cost" and then declines to say. So this page starts with numbers, attributes every one of them to whoever published it, and then explains what sits behind the gap between the cheapest band and the dearest.

The headline is simple. A university-student tutor working online in this market advertises from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. A qualified subject teacher online sits around AED 150 to AED 300. Ask for someone to arrive at a door and the published range moves to AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table for the UAE putting in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. A named premium tutor can publish AED 650. The same teaching hour therefore costs between AED 45 and AED 650 depending on who is selling it and how they get to you.

Al Marjan Island sharpens that gap more than most addresses in the emirate. The island is four reclaimed fronds reached by a single causeway off the Al Hamra coast road, which means a tutor living in Al Nakheel, Al Uraibi or Al Dhait is looking at twenty-five to forty minutes each way on a weekday evening. That is unpaid time for them and it has to be priced into the hour you buy. A tutor who can sell three or four consecutive online hours between five and nine in the evening does not need to charge what a tutor who can physically fit two of them does.

This is also where the honesty has to be plain. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Our lessons here are one-to-one online tuition over live video, with a shared whiteboard and a recording of the session. We are making the case for that format on the evidence above rather than apologising for it, because the alternative on an island postcode is paying a travel premium for a smaller pool of subject specialists.

The rest of the page is arranged the way a careful family actually spends. What the market charges, with sources. What the drive costs, in minutes and in dirhams. Monthly budgets rather than hourly rates, because nobody buys a single hour. The questions that separate a fair quote from a bad one. The exam calendar that decides whether money spent in February is early or late. And the two things that make a cheap tutor expensive: a tutor with no permit, and a tutor willing to cross a line on coursework that can cost your child a qualification.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of single-subject courses, each examined separately, with syllabus codes that matter more than the brand name: maths 0580, physics 0625, chemistry 0620, biology 0610, English first language 0500. Most subjects run a Core and an Extended tier with different grade ceilings, and the tier your child's school entered them for is the first thing a tutor needs to know.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable for each. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after working from the wrong zone's timetable, so a Ras Al Khaimah family should take dates from the school's exams officer rather than from a tutor's memory.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board you will meet in this emirate, with its own codes: 4MA1 for maths, 4PH1 for physics. Some subjects are offered in a modular shape, so a student can bank a unit result and carry it forward rather than sitting everything in one window. That changes the arithmetic of how many paid hours are needed and when.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The published results history is checkable: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables well ahead of a series, so link the live PDF rather than trusting a date on any tutoring page.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, with Checkpoint tests offered in March, May and October. Families on the island often start here because an hour a week in Year 8 costs the same as an hour a week in Year 11 and buys considerably more. The content is thinner, so the hour goes into fluency rather than into damage control.
programmes.countryNote: Spending in Years 7 to 9 is the cheapest spending available to a Ras Al Khaimah family, because the tier decision at the end of Year 9 sets a grade ceiling. A child placed into Core maths rather than Extended cannot be awarded above grade C on the Cambridge scale, and no amount of money spent in Year 11 undoes that entry.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where many island IGCSE students go next, at the RAK Academy international campus or outside the emirate. Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus three core pieces, and the cost profile is different: two years of steady support rather than a sprint, with the internal assessment and extended essay needing feedback rather than hours of teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma support is the one place where budget tutoring reliably wastes money in this emirate. A generalist can supervise homework; only someone who has taught the subject can tell a Higher Level student which of their exploration's marks are already lost. Price the Diploma by the term, not the hour.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ma.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Marjan Island families ask for most, with the syllabus code and the honest note on where the paid hours go. The subject matters to the budget: a maths repair is linear and predictable, a first-language English repair is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most predictable spend of the lot. Marks concentrate in algebraic manipulation, bearings and vectors, and the longer Paper 4 structured questions. A diagnostic hour on two past papers will usually locate the whole problem, which is why maths rarely needs an open-ended commitment.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Higher Level Diploma maths or A-Level. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive with no Core safety net. Fewer tutors in this emirate have taught it, which is exactly where an online roster beats a local search.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism cost more marks than any other topic, and the alternative-to-practical paper is a separate skill from the theory. Budget roughly a third of the hours for practical-method questions rather than content.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative-analysis tables are where grades are made. Students who can describe a reaction in words and not in symbols lose marks steadily across all three papers, and that is a cheap fix once identified.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively approachable, which is why families underspend on it. The marks go on precise terminology and on data-handling questions about unfamiliar experiments. Flashcards do not fix either.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading-for-ideas questions reward a technique that can be taught in a handful of sessions and then needs practice. This is the subject where parents most often buy too many hours too early and too few in the final term.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510)
subjects.description: A different paper from first-language English with its own mark scheme, and the one most often mismatched by a generalist tutor. Listening and speaking components carry weight that written practice alone will not move.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation half of the longer answers decide the grade. Students who can define every term and still score in the middle band are almost always losing the same four evaluation marks each time.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: A case-study paper that punishes generic answers. The paid hours should go on applying theory to the printed business rather than on learning more theory, which is the opposite of how most revision guides are organised.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and data representation. The paper rewards exact notation, so a tutor who codes professionally but has not taught 0478 will often coach a style the mark scheme does not credit.

sections.heading: What the Ras Al Khaimah market actually charges, with sources
paragraphs: A qualified subject teacher working online in the UAE advertises between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour. That is the band to hold in your head, because almost everything below it buys supervision rather than teaching, and almost everything above it is buying either travel or reputation. The table attributes each band to whoever published it, with the date we read it, so you can check the claim rather than take ours.

Reading it from the cheap end upwards is more useful than the other way round. The AED 45 to 150 band exists and it is not a scam: a capable undergraduate can keep a Year 10 student working through homework and can re-explain a topic the school rushed. What that band does not reliably include is mark-scheme literacy, which is the ability to look at a four-mark answer and say precisely which mark is missing and why. That skill is what the AED 150 to 300 band is actually for, and it is the difference between a child who understands physics and a child who scores well in 0625.

Above AED 300 the money is mostly buying one of two things. Either a tutor is physically travelling, in which case you are funding their unpaid drive to the causeway, or they are selling a name. Examiner branding is worth something when it is current and evidenced, and worth nothing when it is a line on a website. Ask when they last marked, for which board, and for which component. A tutor who cannot answer that precisely is charging a premium for a credential they cannot show you.

sections.heading: Pricing the causeway: what the drive onto the island costs you
paragraphs: Al Marjan Island has one road in. Whatever the traffic is doing on the Al Hamra coast road, a tutor coming from the city centre is committing an hour of their evening to travel before a single minute of teaching happens. Nobody absorbs that for free, and the honest version is that it appears in your hourly rate rather than on a separate line of the invoice.

The arithmetic is worth doing out loud. A tutor who works five to nine on a weekday can sell four online hours. Add a forty-minute drive out and back plus the setup either side, and the same evening yields two in-home hours. To earn the same amount they must charge roughly double, which is exactly the gap between the AED 150 to 300 online band and the AED 180 to 500 in-home band that Bestimate and the independent home-tutor market publish. The premium is not greed; it is geometry.

The second cost is less visible and more annoying. A physical session is fragile. Weather, road works at the Al Hamra junction, a late school bus or a tutor's own traffic turns a session into a refund argument or a loss. An online slot in the same situation moves by ninety minutes and still happens. Across a thirty-week school year, the number of sessions that actually take place is a bigger lever on outcomes than the hourly rate you negotiated in September. A family who loses four physical sessions to the coast road has paid the travel premium and received thirteen per cent less teaching for it, which is the quiet way an in-home arrangement becomes the dearest option on the island rather than merely the dearer one.

sections.heading: The three places Al Marjan Island families lose money
paragraphs: The first is spreading a budget too thin. A family with AED 1,200 a month to spend will often buy an hour a week of maths, an hour of physics and an hour of chemistry. Three subjects each get thirty hours across a school year, which is enough to keep a topic list from growing and not enough to shrink one. The same budget on one subject, with marked work between sessions, moves that subject properly and then releases the slot for the next. Sequential beats simultaneous, and it is the single most expensive instinct to argue a parent out of.

The second is buying hours before a diagnosis. A tutor who starts teaching in the first session is guessing. The useful first hour is a student sitting two past-paper questions badly while someone watches, because the loss pattern is almost never what the school report says it is. We see children described as weak at algebra who are actually losing marks to units and significant figures across every subject, and that is four sessions of work, not forty.

The third is paying for content a child already has. By February of Year 11 most students have been taught everything; what they lack is the ability to convert knowledge into marks under timed conditions. Hours spent re-teaching the syllabus in the final term are hours spent on the part the school already did. The money belongs on timed papers, on marking against the official scheme, and on the specific command terms that are costing marks. That is cheaper than it sounds, because it is finite.

sections.heading: Monthly budgets, because nobody buys a single hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutors advertise and monthly outlay is how families actually decide. Bestimate's UAE estimates for a weekly one-hour session land at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packaged offers circulate too: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Packages are worth reading carefully rather than dismissing. Eight sessions for AED 799 is about AED 100 a session, which is good value if the sessions are sixty minutes with a subject teacher and poor value if they are forty-five minutes with whoever was free. The number that matters is not the monthly figure but the cost per teaching hour with a named tutor you have met. Ask for that explicitly and the comparison between two providers becomes possible in about thirty seconds.

Set the budget against the term rather than the month, because tutoring demand is seasonal and your child's need is not flat. A sensible Ras Al Khaimah plan spends lightly from September to December, steps up for the January and February mock window, peaks in the eight weeks before the paper, and stops. Spreading the same total evenly across the year costs identical money and achieves less, because the expensive weeks are the ones nearest the exam. Written down as a term budget rather than a monthly direct debit, the plan also becomes something you can stop, which is the feature families value most once the paper has been sat.

sections.heading: Four questions that separate a fair quote from a bad one
paragraphs: Every provider sounds similar on a website and stops sounding similar under four questions. The first is which syllabus code the tutor has taught, not which subject. "IGCSE physics" is not an answer; "Cambridge 0625 Extended, including the alternative-to-practical paper" is. A tutor who has taught 4PH1 and not 0625 is a good tutor for a different child, and in an emirate where specialist subject teachers are genuinely scarce locally this is the question that matters most.

The second is what happens between sessions. A rate that includes setting and marking written work is a different product from a rate that covers the hour alone. Compare two quotes without establishing that and you will pick the wrong one. The third is what a cancellation costs, in both directions, and the fourth is how a change of tutor works if the match is wrong in week three. A provider with no answer to the fourth question is hoping you will not ask it.

There is a fifth question worth asking about any UAE tutoring business, and it is about the permit rather than the price. Private tutoring here is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. Anyone offering private lessons without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A provider who treats that as an irrelevance is telling you something about how they treat everything else.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees in this emirate, and who approves them
paragraphs: A tutoring bill only makes sense against the school bill. Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which the UAE government's own information service describes as regulating private education in the emirate. Ras Al Khaimah's authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so fee setting here is a regulated act rather than a school's unilateral decision.

That matters to a family budgeting for both. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the following academic year, under an economic incentives package. Ras Al Khaimah families cannot read that announcement as applying to them, because their fees sit with their own regulator; what they can take from it is the principle that the fee line is approved and checkable rather than arbitrary, and so is worth querying.

Set against a school fee, a year of one-subject tutoring at the mid-market monthly band is a meaningful but not enormous addition, and it is the only part of the education bill a family controls month to month. That is the argument for spending it deliberately. The households that get the most from it are not the ones that spend the most; they are the ones that spend in the eight weeks where the spending converts into marks, and stop in the months where it does not.

sections.heading: The exam calendar that decides whether your money is early or late
paragraphs: Tutoring money has a shelf life. The same AED 1,000 buys considerably more in the eight weeks before a paper than in the eight weeks after the previous one, and the calendar is what tells you which eight weeks you are in. Cambridge International runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

One thing to be clear about, because it catches families who have moved here from India: Cambridge's February/March series is offered in India only. A Ras Al Khaimah candidate sits June, with November available as the resit route. If you read a tutoring page quoting an early-spring exam window and a November entry deadline to a UAE family, you are reading a page written for a different country.

The second thing is that Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's version. Dates therefore come from your child's exams officer, never from a tutor. What a tutor should give you instead is the shape of the run-up counted backwards from the paper, which is what the table below does. Pearson behaves the same way: it publishes provisional timetables for a series well in advance and then issues a final version, so the only safe practice is to link the live official document rather than restate dates that can still be revised. Read backwards, the run-up has three money decisions in it: whether to book a slot in the autumn, whether the mock results justify stepping up, and when to switch the spending from teaching to marking.

sections.heading: Is the person you are paying legally permitted to tutor here?
paragraphs: This is a cost question as much as a compliance one, because the cheapest quote in the market is often cheap for exactly this reason. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the application runs through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system under the service name "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", with a stated two-working-day completion time.

The eligibility list is broader than most families expect. It includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Because the permit costs nothing and takes two working days, a tutor without one has no economic excuse, and the UAE's position is unambiguous: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so nobody should be quoting you an amount.

One boundary deserves naming because it affects who you should even ask. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's school. That is reported policy rather than wording we can quote verbatim, and it is worth verifying against the current document, but the principle is sound everywhere: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to pay privately.

sections.heading: What no amount of money should buy: the coursework line
paragraphs: There is a market in this region for completed assessed work, and it is priced openly. One site in this search cluster advertises finished internal assessments at a four-figure dirham sum. A family comparing quotes needs to understand that this is not an expensive version of tutoring; it is a different transaction with a different risk, and the risk sits entirely with the student.

The rule is not complicated. A tutor teaches, explains, questions, models a technique and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write a student's coursework, does not draft their internal assessment and does not edit a piece to completion. Under the IB's academic honesty rules, submitted work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the consequence lands on the candidate rather than on the person who was paid. No price makes that a good purchase.

The same boundary applies to materials, and it is worth knowing because some providers advertise it as a feature. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A tutor can work through them with a student in a session and can point you to the official page; reproducing them as downloads is copyright infringement. If a provider's selling point is a library of other people's documents, they are offering you something they are not entitled to give. Saying this plainly costs us a selling point that two competitors in this search use freely, and it is still the right way round.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: Send the subject, the board, the syllabus code if you know it, the tier, and the school. For an Al Marjan Island family that is usually a RAK Academy or city-centre entry, and the code decides which tutors are even a candidate. Getting this right in the first message removes a week of mismatched trials.

process.title: A free trial lesson, used as a diagnosis
process.description: One free session with the proposed tutor, spent watching your child attempt real past-paper questions rather than being taught at. You end it knowing the loss pattern and the number of sessions it implies. If the match is wrong, you have spent nothing and you say so.

process.title: A written plan with a number of hours on it
process.description: Before the first paid session, a short plan naming the topics, the components and an estimated range of sessions. An estimate can be wrong and an open-ended commitment cannot be checked, so we give you the former. You decide the budget against it.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked work between
process.description: A fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, work set after each session and marked before the next, and a topic list that visibly shrinks. The recording stays available to you. Progress is reported against the plan rather than as a general impression.

process.title: Step up for the eight weeks that matter, then stop
process.description: Move to two sessions a week for the pre-series block, switch from teaching to timed papers and marking, and finish. Continuing past the paper costs money and buys nothing. We will tell you when that point has arrived.

whyPoints.title: The rates on this page are other people's, with dates
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider that published it and the month we read it. We do not present market bands as our price, and we do not publish a rate card we would have to defend against a currency we do not quote in. Our own cost comes up in the consultation, against the plan.

whyPoints.title: Distance stops filtering your shortlist
whyPoints.description: Specialist subject teachers are genuinely scarce in the northern emirates. Searching for someone who will drive to the island narrows the pool to whoever is nearby and willing; searching the roster for a 0606 or 4PH1 teacher does not. That is the practical argument for online delivery here, and it is the one we are making.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis before a commitment
whyPoints.description: The first session exists to find the loss pattern, not to start the syllabus again. Families who know that their child is losing marks to units and command terms rather than to content buy four sessions instead of a term, which is a worse outcome for us and the right one for them.

whyPoints.title: Sessions that survive a Ras Al Khaimah week
whyPoints.description: Nothing about a live video lesson depends on the coast road, a school bus or the weather. A slot that has to move moves by ninety minutes and still happens. Across a school year the count of sessions that actually took place matters more than the rate you agreed in September.

whyPoints.title: The boundaries are written down, not implied
whyPoints.description: We say plainly what a tutor may not do with coursework, we do not supply other people's mark schemes as downloads, and we claim no regulator or board approval, because IB Gram holds none. On a page full of numbers, those are the claims most worth checking.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE home tutor in Al Marjan Island cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Treat AED 150 to 300 an hour as the band for a qualified subject teacher working online, which is where Unitors publishes its IGCSE and IB rates. Ask for someone to travel to the island and the published market moves to AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's UAE table at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking 200 to 500. Below AED 150 you are generally buying supervision rather than mark-scheme teaching. Those are other providers' figures, read in October 2026, not ours; IB Gram's own cost is discussed against a written plan after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home rate higher than an online rate for the same teacher?
faqs.answer: Because travel is unpaid time that still has to be paid for. A tutor working five to nine on a weekday can sell four consecutive online hours. Add twenty-five to forty minutes each way to Al Marjan Island plus setting up either side and the same evening yields two. To earn the same income they must charge roughly double, which is exactly the gap between the published online and in-home bands. The premium funds the drive, not better teaching. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE at all; our lessons here are one-to-one online.

faqs.question: Is AED 45 an hour ever a sensible choice for a Year 10 student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for a narrow job. A capable undergraduate at the bottom of the market can keep a child working, re-explain something the school covered too fast, and hold a homework routine together. That is real value for a Year 9 or early Year 10 student who is coping but drifting. What that band rarely includes is the ability to look at a four-mark answer and name the missing mark. If the problem is marks rather than effort, the cheap hour will not find it, and six months of it costs more than eight sessions with someone who can.

faqs.question: Should we pay per hour or buy a monthly package for a child on the island?
faqs.answer: Compare them on one number: the cost per teaching hour with a named tutor you have met. A package advertised at AED 799 for eight sessions is about AED 100 a session, which is good if those are sixty-minute sessions with a subject teacher and poor if they are forty-five minutes with whoever is free. Packages also need an exit. Ask what happens if the tutor is wrong in week three, and whether unused sessions survive a pause. If either answer is vague, pay by the hour until you trust the arrangement.

faqs.question: Do the AED figures quoted on this page include VAT?
faqs.answer: We cannot tell you, and neither can most of the pages quoting them. The bands here are other providers' published rates read in October 2026, and few of them state their tax treatment. We are deliberately not stating how UAE value added tax applies to tuition, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance rather than for a tutoring page. What you should do is simple: ask any provider, in writing, whether the number they quoted is the number you will be charged. A quote that cannot answer that is not a quote.

faqs.question: How many paid hours does repairing one IGCSE subject usually take?
faqs.answer: Far fewer than most families expect, once the problem is named. A maths grade held back by algebraic manipulation and Paper 4 structured-question technique is often eight to twelve sessions of targeted work. A physics grade held back by the alternative-to-practical paper can be six. What takes a term is re-teaching a syllabus the school has already taught, which is why the diagnostic hour matters so much: it is the difference between buying a finite job and buying an open-ended arrangement. Ask for an estimated session range in writing before you start.

faqs.question: Does sharing one paid hour between two children on the island save money?
faqs.answer: Only if their entries match, and on Al Marjan Island they frequently do not. Two siblings in the same year group at the same school taking the same tier of the same syllabus code can share an hour productively. Two children a year apart, or one on Cambridge 0580 and one on Pearson 4MA1, will each get half a session rather than a shared one. The honest saving usually comes from a different direction: one tutor covering two related subjects for the same child, which removes the duplicated diagnosis rather than halving the attention.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates around Ras Al Khaimah rise closer to the June series?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than prices visibly jumping. From February onwards the tutors who have taught your child's syllabus code are the ones already booked, and what remains is either a different specialism or a higher band. The practical effect on a family budget is the same as a price rise: you pay more for a worse match. Booking the slot in the autumn and running lightly until the mock window costs less across the year than appearing in March with eight weeks to go, which is also when the teaching has to be replaced by marking.

faqs.question: What is the single most common way island families waste tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Spreading a budget across three subjects at once. An hour a week in each gives every subject about thirty hours across the year, enough to stop a topic list growing and not enough to shrink one. The same money on one subject, with work set and marked between sessions, closes that subject and frees the slot. Families resist it because three worrying subjects feel like three problems, but they usually share one cause: units, command terms, or timed-paper technique that fails everywhere. Fix the cause in one subject and the others improve without being bought.

faqs.question: Can we start with one subject now and add another later in the year?
faqs.answer: That is the sequence we would recommend anyway, and it is the cheaper order. Start with the subject where the gap between current and target grade is widest, run it until the topic list is short, then move the slot. If you add a second subject it should be because the first no longer needs the hour, not because the worry list grew. The one exception is a pre-series block in the final eight weeks, where two subjects can share timed-paper practice because the work has stopped being teaching and become marking.

faqs.question: Does a tutor charge for a session cancelled because of the causeway traffic?
faqs.answer: With an in-home arrangement, that depends entirely on a policy you should read before paying anything, and the fair version binds both sides equally. It is also the strongest practical argument against buying travel at all on an island postcode: weather, road works at the Al Hamra junction or a late school bus turns a physical session into a refund conversation. A live video lesson in the same situation moves ninety minutes later the same evening. Across thirty weeks, the number of sessions that actually happened matters more than the hourly rate.

faqs.question: How does a year of tutoring compare with what we already pay in school fees?
faqs.answer: One subject at the mid-market band is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month on Bestimate's UAE estimates, so a focused two-term plan is a meaningful addition to a school bill rather than a rival to it. The difference is control. Private school fees in Ras Al Khaimah are approved by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves curricula and assessment methods, so the fee line is largely fixed once you have chosen a school. The tutoring line is the part of the education budget a family can switch on and off by month.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects tend to need the most paid hours?
faqs.answer: First-language English and the essay-weighted humanities, because the skill being bought is judgement rather than content and judgement takes practice to shift. Economics 0455 is the classic case: a student who can define every term and still sits in the middle band is usually losing the same evaluation marks every time, and that takes several marked attempts to correct. Maths and physics are the opposite. The loss pattern is usually narrow, diagnosable in one session, and fixable in eight to twelve, which makes them the cheapest grades to move.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Al Nakheel cheaper than one-to-one for an island family?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and the comparison is not really about the hour. A group class at a centre splits a teacher's attention across the room and adds the same drive you were trying to avoid, this time in both directions and at a fixed time you cannot move. A centre earns its place when a child needs structure and company more than diagnosis. If the problem is a specific loss pattern in a specific component, a group rate is cheap money spent on the wrong thing, and the drive makes it dearer than it looks.

faqs.question: What does IB Gram actually charge, and how do we find out?
faqs.answer: We do not publish a rate card on these pages, deliberately. Our cost depends on the subject, the level, the number of sessions your written plan calls for and whether you are buying a term or a pre-series block, and a single number on a page would be either misleading or useless. The route is a free trial lesson with the proposed tutor, a written plan with an estimated session range, and then a figure against that plan. You see the teaching before you see a price, and you owe nothing if the match is wrong.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ma.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, then decide what to spend
ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ma.closingBody: If you have read this far you already know more about what IGCSE tuition costs around Ras Al Khaimah than most of the pages selling it will tell you. The next step is cheap and specific. Send the subject, the board, the syllabus code and the tier, and we will put a tutor who has taught that exact specification in front of your child for a free trial lesson, delivered one-to-one over live video at a Gulf Standard Time slot that fits an Al Marjan Island evening. You end that session with a loss pattern, an estimated number of hours and a number to decide against. If the match is wrong, you say so and you have spent nothing.

intro.heading: What an Al Nakheel parent is actually buying
paragraphs: Al Nakheel sits at the commercial centre of Ras Al Khaimah city, on the inland side of the creek, with apartment blocks along the main roads and villa streets behind them. The families living there send children to a mix of Indian-curriculum campuses in the city, British-curriculum campuses a few minutes away, and the RAK Academy group out at Al Hamra and Khuzam. That mix is the reason the phrase 'IGCSE home tutor in Al Nakheel' gets typed so often. A parent whose child has just been entered for Cambridge papers wants somebody who knows those papers, and the local pool of people who do is small.

The honest answer to the search is that distance is the wrong variable to optimise. Ras Al Khaimah is not Dubai: there is no dense layer of freelance subject specialists circling the neighbourhood waiting to be booked. If you insist on a tutor who can park outside the building, you are choosing from whoever happens to live within a short drive and is free at six in the evening, and you will usually end up with a generalist who teaches four subjects. If you drop the travel requirement, you choose from people who teach one subject on one syllabus and have marked hundreds of scripts on it.

IB Gram is built on the second choice. Lessons for Al Nakheel students are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen and a tablet the tutor writes on so your child sees the working appear line by line. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. That is stated plainly here because the alternative, discovering it after payment, is how families lose trust in a platform.

What follows is the comparison a parent in this part of the city actually needs. It sets Al Nakheel against Al Uraibi and Al Mairid next door and against Khuzam to the south, prices what the local market charges in AED, counts the Cambridge and Pearson exam series backwards from the papers themselves, and explains where the Ministry of Education's equivalency rules bite when IGCSE subjects are chosen in Year 9. The conclusion is the same from any of those postcodes, and the page shows the working rather than asserting it.

Nothing on this page quotes an IB Gram price list, because the first conversation is a free trial lesson and a short call about your child's actual papers. The AED figures below are market figures, attributed to the providers who published them, so you can check them against whatever quote you have in hand. Where a number comes from a Ras Al Khaimah listing rather than a UAE-wide average, the page says which, because the emirate sits below the Dubai rate for the same subject.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-na.programmesIntro: Al Nakheel children arrive at IGCSE from three directions: a Cambridge lower-secondary programme, an Indian middle school, or an IB Middle Years Programme at one of the RAK Academy campuses. The entry point changes what the first six weeks of tutoring have to do, so it is worth naming which one applies before booking anything.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses examined at the end, with a Core tier capped at grade C and an Extended tier reaching A*. Most Al Nakheel students take between six and nine subjects. The decisions that matter are made in Year 9: which tier, whether to take separate sciences or a co-ordinated award, and whether maths runs alongside Additional Maths 0606. Each of those choices changes the papers sat and the ceiling available.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A Ras Al Khaimah school and a Dubai school may therefore sit the same paper on different days. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in before you plan revision around any published date.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other British-track route, graded 9 to 1 and tiered Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended. Maths A runs as 4MA1 with two two-hour papers worth half the grade each, which rewards a student who can work steadily for two hours more than one who sprints. Science codes start 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The content overlaps Cambridge heavily, but the question style and the mark scheme wording do not.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates, which is what makes them checkable; for the series your child is entered for, use the live official timetable rather than a figure copied onto a tutoring page.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The RAK Academy campuses run the IB continuum, so a number of children in the city follow MYP rather than IGCSE through Year 11. MYP marks arrive as criterion letters against published descriptors rather than as percentages, and the eAssessment at the end of MYP 5 is a different animal from a Cambridge paper. Families who transfer into an IGCSE cohort mid-course feel the gap immediately in the way questions are phrased.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Nakheel household the practical question is whether a Year 11 transfer is worth it. Moving from MYP into a Cambridge Year 11 means learning a mark scheme in one year rather than two, and the subjects where that is hardest are maths and the sciences, where the IGCSE papers assume two years of notation practice. A term of focused one-to-one work on command terms and paper technique usually closes more of the gap than extra content coverage does.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-na.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Nakheel families ask for by name, with the syllabus codes attached, because a tutor who knows 0580 and a tutor who knows 4MA1 are preparing a student for different papers. Each description says where the marks actually go missing rather than restating the topic list.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended candidates sit a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper under the current syllabus, which caught out a generation of students trained only on the calculator route. Marks go missing on exact-value work with surds, on bounds, and on the multi-step algebra questions that carry method marks a student never writes down.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A-Level maths or an IB Higher Level course. The jump is calculus and trigonometric identities. Students who coast through 0580 often stall here because 0606 expects algebraic fluency to be automatic rather than reconstructed each time from first principles.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper, a longer theory paper worth roughly half the grade, and a practical component taken either as a laboratory test or as the alternative-to-practical written paper. The alternative paper is where Ras Al Khaimah students lose most: it tests experimental reasoning on paper, and it cannot be revised by rereading notes.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Electrolysis, moles and organic chemistry account for most of the lost marks. Mole calculations fail on units rather than on chemistry, and organic questions fail on functional-group naming. Both respond quickly to one-to-one work because the error is specific and visible in the student's own script.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: The content volume makes this feel like a memory subject, and students revise it as one. The marks sit in the extended-response questions on transport, homeostasis and inheritance, where a described mechanism earns marks and a named structure does not. Genetics diagrams are the single most recoverable topic.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language 0500
subjects.description: Two papers: reading and directed writing, then composition. The directed-writing task is scored on audience and register as well as content, and Al Nakheel students who write fluent but undirected prose lose the register marks every time. The fix is a handful of annotated rewrites, not more reading.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: A short-answer paper and a structured-essay paper. Almost all recoverable marks are in diagram work: a correctly labelled and shifted curve scores, a described shift does not. Evaluation marks in the final part of each question are left on the table by students who explain both sides without reaching a judgement.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two two-hour papers, equally weighted, graded 9 to 1. The Higher tier question order ramps steeply in the last third, so pacing work matters as much as content. Students moving from Cambridge find the wording terser and the number of marks per question larger.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: A long first paper and a shorter second one, with practical skills assessed in the written papers rather than in a laboratory test. Equations are provided differently from Cambridge, which changes revision priorities: a student switching boards mid-course must relearn what is given and what must be recalled.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: A double award covering biology, chemistry and physics across shared papers, chosen by students who need science breadth without three separate subjects. The risk is that one weak discipline drags the whole award, and because it is examined jointly, a parent cannot see which discipline is failing without looking at the component marks.

sections.heading: Al Nakheel against Al Uraibi: the comparison parents actually run
paragraphs: The first thing a family does when a tutor search fails is widen it to the next district. From Al Nakheel that means Al Uraibi, Al Mairid and Khuzam. The reasoning is sound in a big city and wrong in this one. Those districts are minutes apart, they feed the same campuses, and crucially they draw their freelance tutoring from the same handful of people. Widening the radius by three kilometres does not add a Chemistry 0620 specialist to the list; it adds the same generalists you already found, at a slightly higher rate because the drive is longer.

The table below sets the three districts against each other on the variables that actually differ: how far the school run is, what the evening road looks like, whether a quiet study space is likely, and what the local tutoring supply looks like. The last column is the one that matters, and it reads the same in every row. That is the finding, not a disappointment: it means the decision for an Al Nakheel family is not where to look but what format to buy.

Read the table and then read the row for the district you live in. If your conclusion from the first three columns is that an in-home tutor is feasible, the fourth column tells you what you will actually get: somebody local, pleasant, teaching several subjects, who has not marked a 0625 alternative-to-practical paper. If your conclusion is that it is not feasible, you arrive at the same place by a shorter route. Either way the next move is a trial lesson with a specialist, run over video, at a time that fits around the drive.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what it costs
paragraphs: Put the two formats side by side on money and the gap is not subtle. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in the UAE are quoted in the AED 150-300 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, with travel folded into the fee, is quoted at AED 180-500: Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts the band at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. The same tutor, in other words, costs more when a car is involved, and in Ras Al Khaimah the car is involved for longer than it would be in Dubai.

What does the premium buy? Three real things. A tutor in the room can see a page the student is hiding, can take a book off the shelf, and cannot be unplugged by a dropped connection. Those are genuine advantages and anybody who tells you otherwise is selling. What it does not buy is subject depth, because the pool it draws from is defined by geography. A family paying the top of the in-home band in this emirate is paying a travel premium on a generalist, which is the worst trade available on this page.

The second table prices the formats a household here can actually book, including the group option that the tuition centres in the city offer. Treat every AED figure as a market figure published by the provider named, not as an IB Gram price. IB Gram's own first step is a free trial lesson and a short conversation about your child's papers, and the rate is agreed after that, once it is clear which subject specialist the student needs and how many sessions a week the exam timetable justifies.

sections.heading: Why the answer is the same from either postcode
paragraphs: The comparison collapses because the thing a Year 10 student needs is not proximity. It is somebody who has read the examiner's report for the paper your child is sitting and can say, in one sentence, which of the six recurring errors is costing the grade. That person exists in small numbers, and they are distributed across the world rather than across Ras Al Khaimah. A search filtered by postcode filters them out first.

There is a second reason, and it is about the school rather than the tutor. Ras Al Khaimah's private-school sector is smaller than Dubai's, which means subject sets are smaller. A Year 11 economics group of five or six is normal here. Small sets are good for attention and bad for calibration: the student has no sense of where they sit, and the teacher has few scripts to compare against. An external specialist who has marked a hundred scripts on 0455 restores the calibration that a set of five cannot provide, and that has nothing to do with which district the family lives in.

Third, availability. The local answer fails most often not on quality but on diaries. The one person in the city who teaches Extended maths well is booked from five until nine, four nights a week, by February of Year 11. Online, the constraint lifts: a tutor in another time zone is free at seven in the evening Gulf time because it is the middle of their afternoon. For a family in Al Nakheel, Al Uraibi or Khuzam, that is the difference between starting tutoring in October and starting it in March.

sections.heading: The Cambridge and Pearson series, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Almost no tutoring page in this market names an exam series at all, which is strange, because the series is the only fixed point in the year. Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series exists but is offered to India only, so a Ras Al Khaimah candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

Counting backwards from the paper is more useful than counting forwards from today. Entry deadlines sit months before the exam because the centre has to submit a cohort, order papers and book rooms. Results then arrive months after: Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates are quoted because they are checkable; for the series ahead, use the official timetable your school's exams officer works from, since provisional timetables are revised.

The table turns that into a sequence a parent can act on. Every row is a milestone somebody else controls, with the thing your child should have finished by then. The zone point in the last row is the one families miss: Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable per zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask the school which zone it sits in, in writing, and plan from that document only.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and who may legally tutor them
paragraphs: Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education locally and, along with Sharjah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection alone, and it is worth knowing because it means curriculum and fee questions have a local address rather than a federal one. Dubai's schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to SPEA, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately, through employment law rather than education law. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an exact figure is guessing.

Two practical consequences for an Al Nakheel family. The first is that 'is the tutor licensed' is a fair question with a checkable answer, and the MoHRE service to look for is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. The second is that IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and does not claim one: there is no KHDA permit, no ADEK registration and no Department of Knowledge listing behind this page. A platform that implies otherwise is making the most dangerous claim available in this market.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch in coursework
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than it once did, but practical components, directed-writing tasks and school-set assignments still count, and the boundary matters. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the mark scheme, work through a published exemplar and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write, draft or complete the work, and IB Gram does not sell that at any price. One ranking site in this market openly sells finished Internal Assessments; for a student, buying one is a malpractice finding and the loss of the qualification.

The line is easier to hold when it is operational rather than moral. Ask for the feedback in writing, so the comments sit next to the student's draft and you can see what changed. Ask the tutor to annotate against criteria rather than rewriting sentences. If a session produces prose the student cannot explain back to you, something has gone wrong regardless of who typed it. A good tutor leaves a trail of the student's own improving attempts, which is also exactly what a school asks for if a question is ever raised.

There is a related point about past papers and syllabus documents. IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus material, mark schemes or past papers. Those are the boards' copyright, and your school has legitimate access to them. A tutor should be working from the papers your child's teacher has already issued, or pointing you to the official source, rather than handing over a folder of scanned material of unclear provenance.

sections.heading: Equivalency: the five subjects that decide a UAE university application
paragraphs: Subject choices made in Year 9 in Al Nakheel have a consequence most families meet four years later, at the Ministry of Education equivalency stage. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects.

That exclusion is the detail that catches people. A student with six IGCSEs, two of which are Arabic and Islamic Education, has four that count, not six. It is a paperwork problem created years earlier by a timetable decision, and it is entirely avoidable if somebody checks the count in Year 9. At least one competing tutoring site tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required; the published rule is five, with those two excluded, and getting that right matters more than any tutoring claim on this page.

On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published on the sources behind this page, so none is stated here: verify it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and no tutoring is required for it. Describing it is as far as this page goes.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond those subjects, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. So an Al Nakheel child on a Cambridge timetable is also carrying a second, parallel set of subjects, usually taught in Arabic and usually assessed differently from everything else on the report.

Dubai's regulator has published the most detailed version of these requirements, and while those guidelines are KHDA's rather than Ras Al Khaimah's, they show the shape of what schools are working to. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, prohibiting combined classes because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. It sets Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, and it calculates instructional time in forty-minute lesson units, advising a minimum of twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. It also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from the authority to teach those subjects.

For tutoring, two things follow. The first is that the use of any different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so nobody should be offering a parallel Arabic or Islamic Education syllabus of their own invention. The second is that for an Arabic-first-language student in Al Qusaidat or Al Mamourah, support in these subjects is a different request from IGCSE physics help, and it should be scoped as such rather than bundled into a general package.

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is short on purpose. You describe the subject, the board and the specific problem, in whatever detail you have: 'Year 10 Chemistry 0620, Extended, failing on moles' is more useful than 'needs help with science'. A free trial lesson is scheduled with the tutor who looks like the right fit. You and the student decide after that lesson, not before it. If the fit is wrong, a different tutor is proposed rather than the first one being defended.

The honest part is what happens when the specialist you need is not available. On a narrow subject at a specific level, there are evenings when nobody suitable has a free slot in the window a Ras Al Khaimah family can use. The options at that point are a waiting period of a week or two for a named tutor, a different time slot that is less convenient, or a tutor with adjacent rather than exact specialism, clearly labelled as such. What should not happen is a general tutor being presented as a subject specialist, and the way you test that is to ask which papers they have taught and what the last examiner's report said.

Payment follows the trial, not the enquiry, and the AED figures earlier on this page are the market's rather than a price list. A short call establishes how many sessions a week the exam timetable justifies, which is a different number in October than it is six weeks before a June paper. For most Al Nakheel families the answer is one session a week for two terms and two a week in the final stretch, which is less than the monthly packages of AED 1,599-1,799 that in-home providers quote for four two-hour visits.

process.description: Name the board, the syllabus code if you have it, the tier and the specific failure. A parent who writes '0580 Extended, non-calculator paper, surds and bounds' gets matched in one pass. A parent who writes 'maths help' gets matched in three.

process.description: You are told who the tutor is, which syllabus they teach, and why they fit this particular problem. If the honest answer is that only an adjacent specialist is free this week, you are told that too rather than discovering it in the first lesson.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the student in the room
process.description: Sixty minutes with the actual tutor on the actual material. The point is the student's reaction, not the parent's. Children in Al Nakheel who have sat through a bad tuition centre class can tell within twenty minutes whether this one is different.

process.title: A weekly slot that survives the school run
process.description: The slot is set around the drive home, clubs and prayer times, in Gulf Standard Time. Families travelling to the coastal campuses usually land on seven in the evening; city-school families can start earlier. The slot holds through the term rather than moving weekly.

process.title: Written notes, then a review before the series
process.description: Each session leaves annotated working and a short note of what to practise. Before the June or November papers, the tutor and the family review whether the session count still matches the timetable, and adjust rather than drift.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: A tutor matched to 0625 is a different person from a tutor matched to 4PH1, even though both teach physics. Equations provided, practical assessment and question style all differ. Matching on the code is the single highest-value thing a platform can do, and it is the thing a postcode search cannot.

whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not visit homes in this country; that service exists only in India. Saying so on the page costs some enquiries and saves every family a wasted conversation.

whyPoints.description: Every rate band on this page names who published it and when. Three of six competing pages audited in this market publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams. A figure you can check is worth more than a figure that flatters.

whyPoints.description: Teaching, modelling and feedback on the student's own work; never writing it. That boundary is stated rather than implied because the alternative, which is openly sold elsewhere in this market, ends a student's qualification rather than improving it.

whyPoints.description: Series are named by month, not month and year, so nothing on this page quietly expires. Where a date is quoted it is a past one, cited because it can be verified, and the live timetable is always the school's rather than ours.

whyPoints.description: Subject sets in Ras Al Khaimah are small. A tutor who has marked many scripts on the same syllabus gives a student the comparison a group of five cannot, which often matters more than extra content coverage.

faqs.question: Can I actually get an IGCSE home tutor to come to our flat in Al Nakheel?
faqs.answer: Independent home tutors do operate in Ras Al Khaimah city, and the market rate for in-home one-to-one in the UAE is quoted at AED 180-500 an hour with travel folded in. IB Gram is not one of them: lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video, and in-home visiting is offered only in India. The practical trade is subject depth against proximity. A local visiting tutor is usually a generalist covering several subjects, while an online match is made to the exact syllabus code your child sits. For most Al Nakheel families chasing a specific paper, the second is the better buy.

faqs.question: Is tutoring in Al Nakheel any different from tutoring in Al Uraibi or Khuzam?
faqs.answer: Not in any way that changes your decision. The three districts are minutes apart, feed overlapping campuses and draw freelance tutoring from the same small pool of people. Widening a search from Al Nakheel to Al Uraibi adds travel time, not expertise. What does differ is practical: Khuzam families living near the British School campus can often start a session at five, while children travelling to the Al Hamra campuses rarely start before seven. So the postcode changes the timetable, not the shortlist of people who genuinely know Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4MA1.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge IGCSE series do students in Ras Al Khaimah sit?
faqs.answer: June and November. Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so it does not apply to a UAE centre. Most schools here enter the main cohort for June and use November as the resit route. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable per zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exams officer which zone it sits in and plan from that timetable.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does an Al Nakheel student need for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. A competing tutoring site in this market states six, which is wrong, and a student relying on it could find two of their subjects do not count. Check the total in Year 9 rather than in Year 13, and verify on the ministry's own pages.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Ras Al Khaimah need a permit from anyone?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you read online with caution. The MoHRE service is listed as private tutor licensing and is applied for through its app or website.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tutors charge around Ras Al Khaimah city?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market figures give you the bands. Budget online tutoring runs AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one, travel included, is quoted at AED 180-500. Specialist exam-year tutoring reaches AED 200-450 and above, and one premium provider publishes AED 650. Those are other people's rates, cited so you can compare. IB Gram agrees a rate after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a list.

faqs.question: My son is in a Year 11 economics set of five. Is a small class a problem?
faqs.answer: It cuts both ways. Attention per student is excellent, and that is real. What a set of five cannot give him is calibration: he has no sense of where a grade-A answer sits relative to his own, and his teacher has few scripts to compare against. On IGCSE Economics 0455 that shows up in the evaluation marks at the end of each structured question, where a student explains both sides and never reaches a judgement. A tutor who has marked many scripts on that paper supplies the comparison the set cannot. It is one of the clearest cases for outside help in a small emirate.

faqs.question: Will live video lessons work in a shared Al Nakheel apartment?
faqs.answer: Usually, with two adjustments. Headphones solve most of the noise problem, and a wall or a window behind the student rather than a corridor solves the rest. The bigger issue is the table: a laptop on a sofa produces a slumped student and an unreadable camera angle. A hard surface, the device at eye level and a paper notebook beside it change the lesson more than any software setting. Tutors share a screen and write on a tablet, so your child watches the working appear rather than listening to it described, which is the part that makes video workable for maths and the sciences.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths, physics and chemistry for the same child?
faqs.answer: Someone can, and that is how most local in-home tutoring in the emirate is sold, because a visiting tutor needs enough work within driving distance to make the trip pay. It is rarely the right answer. The mark schemes differ, the practical assessment differs, and the recurring errors differ: moles and units in 0620, experimental reasoning in 0625, exact-value algebra in 0580. Matching a specialist per subject costs the same per hour and buys a sharper diagnosis. Sessions can still be stacked on one evening so the family keeps a single fixed slot in the week.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my daughter sits Cambridge or Pearson papers?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the syllabus code on her entry, not the subject name. Cambridge codes are four digits, as in 0580 for maths and 0625 for physics. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes start with a figure and letters, as in 4MA1 for Maths A and 4PH1 for physics. The distinction is not cosmetic. Grading runs A*-G on Cambridge and 9-1 on Pearson, tiering is Core and Extended against Foundation and Higher, and the equations provided in the physics papers differ. A tutor matched to the wrong code will teach the right content and the wrong exam.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a directed-writing task my child has to hand in?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the task type, work through a published exemplar, explain how audience and register are credited, and give written feedback on your child's own draft. A tutor will not write it, draft it or edit it to completion, and that is not a service IB Gram sells. Keep the feedback in writing so the comments sit beside the draft and you can see what the student changed. If a session produces prose your child cannot explain back to you, something has gone wrong irrespective of who typed it. A trail of improving drafts is also what protects the student if the school ever asks.

faqs.question: We may move our daughter from MYP into a Cambridge Year 11. How hard is that?
faqs.answer: Harder in presentation than in content. MYP reports against criterion descriptors; a Cambridge paper rewards a specific mark-scheme vocabulary and a specific amount of written working. A student who understands the physics can still lose half the marks by answering in MYP style. The subjects where the gap is widest are maths and the separate sciences, where IGCSE assumes two years of notation practice. A term of focused work on command terms, working-out conventions and timed questions usually closes more of the distance than racing through extra content does.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tutoring in Al Nakheel six weeks before a paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the goal changes. Six weeks is not enough to reteach a two-year syllabus, and anyone promising that is overselling. It is enough to do error-type work: sit the student down with their own marked papers, sort the lost marks into four or five recurring categories, and drill those categories under time. On 0580 that is often exact values, bounds and multi-step method marks. On 0620 it is units in mole calculations. Narrow, diagnosed work in the final weeks moves grades more reliably than broad revision does, because it targets marks the student is currently giving away.

faqs.question: Do you teach Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Those sit on a separate track and should be scoped separately. Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside its licensed international curriculum, and the content is set centrally: the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. So nobody should be offering an invented parallel syllabus. For an Arabic-first-language student, support in these subjects is a different request from help with physics, taught in Arabic and assessed differently. Ask for it as its own stream rather than folding it into a general package.

faqs.question: What if the tutor you match us with is not right for my child?
faqs.answer: You say so and a different one is proposed. That is why the first lesson is a free trial and why the student's reaction matters more than the parent's. The common mismatch is not competence but pace: a tutor who has taught the top of the Extended tier for years can move too fast for a student who is rebuilding confidence. Tell us which it was, because that detail makes the second match better. What should not happen is the first tutor being defended at length. If the specialist you need has no free slot in a Gulf-time evening, you will be told that rather than offered a substitute presented as the real thing.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-na.closingHeading: One trial lesson tells you more than three weeks of searching

The alternative takes an evening to test. Tell us the board, the syllabus code and the specific place the marks are going, and a specialist in that paper runs a free lesson with your child at a Gulf Standard Time slot that fits around the drive home. You decide afterwards. Nothing is charged before the lesson, and no tutor will ever be sent to a Ras Al Khaimah address.
