intro.heading: The Al Qusaidat IGCSE year, counted backwards
paragraphs: Al Qusaidat sits inland from the Ras Al Khaimah corniche, close to Julphar and the older residential grid behind it. Families here send children across the emirate for school rather than around the corner, which means a weekday evening already carries a thirty to fifty minute return journey before anyone opens a textbook. That single fact decides most of what follows on this page. An IGCSE home tutor in Al Qusaidat is a sensible thing to want; a second car journey after the first one is not, and the market in this emirate is thin enough that the search often ends with whoever is free rather than whoever knows the syllabus.

So this page is written as a calendar instead of a sales pitch. The IGCSE year has fixed hinge points that nobody in Al Qusaidat controls: the school's internal entry submission, the mock window, the coursework or practical deadlines where they apply, the published exam timetable, results day, and the enquiry-about-results window after it. Work forwards from today and tuition looks optional. Work backwards from the first paper and it becomes obvious which eight weeks matter and which three are already spent.

Ras Al Khaimah private schools answer to the Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. What it does not do is sit your child's exams. Cambridge International runs the IGCSE, O Level and International A Level papers in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Those four windows are the only ones that matter to a Year 10 or Year 11 student in this emirate.

IB Gram matches Al Qusaidat students to subject specialists and delivers every lesson one-to-one over live video. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated plainly because the alternative is a parent waiting at the gate for somebody who was never coming. What you get instead is a specialist chosen for the syllabus code rather than the postcode, which in a northern emirate with a small teaching pool is the difference between a Chemistry 0620 tutor and a general science graduate.

The sections below give you the June series counted backwards as a dated table, the November route for a resit, what the market actually charges in AED with the source named, who is legally permitted to tutor in the UAE, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that decides whether five IGCSEs are enough. Read the calendar table first. If your child's first paper is eight weeks away, the rest of the page tells you what to do with those weeks.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-qu.programmesIntro: Al Qusaidat students arrive at IGCSE from three directions: a Cambridge lower secondary route, a Pearson route, or a transfer from an Indian or American school mid-stage. The programmes below are the ones that decide which papers your child actually sits and when the entry has to be in.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers, with Core and Extended tiers in most subjects. Core caps at grade C; Extended runs the full A* to G range. Subject codes matter more than subject names: 0580 Mathematics is a different animal from 0606 Additional Mathematics, and a tutor who has not worked the specific code will teach around the edges of it.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah centres sit the June and November series. The February/March series Cambridge runs is offered to India only, so no Al Qusaidat student should be planning around it. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Linear and modular routes to the same certificate, with codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics and 4CH1 for Chemistry. Papers are shorter and more numerous than the Cambridge equivalents in several subjects, and the grading runs 9 to 1 rather than A* to G, which changes how a predicted grade should be read.
programmes.countryNote: International GCSE is available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those past dates show the shape of the cycle; always check the live timetable, because Pearson publishes provisional versions that can be revised.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The two years before IGCSE decide which tier a student is entered for. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and produce a diagnostic report rather than a certificate. A Year 9 report that shows weak algebraic fluency is the cheapest possible warning that 0580 Extended will be a struggle, and it arrives two years before anyone has to act on it.
programmes.countryNote: Al Qusaidat families often treat Year 9 as a quiet year and start tuition in Year 11. Reversing that order is both cheaper and more effective: eight weeks of algebra in Year 9 removes the problem that otherwise consumes a whole exam-year budget. Checkpoint is also the only low-stakes external data point most RAK students generate before the IGCSE series itself.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The usual next step for a Ras Al Khaimah student who does not move to an IB school. AS sits at the halfway point and can be cashed in or carried forward to the full A Level. Subject choice at this stage is constrained by IGCSE grades, so the grades your child takes out of Year 11 set the ceiling on the Year 13 options.
programmes.countryNote: This matters for equivalency as well as admissions. The UAE Ministry of Education's British-track route asks for proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE or GCSE passes. A student who drops out after Year 11 with five passes and no AS has only part of the file.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-qu.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Qusaidat and wider Ras Al Khaimah families ask for most, with the syllabus code attached because that is what a tutor needs before the first lesson. Each note names where the marks actually go missing rather than describing the subject in general terms.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Extended Paper 2 and Paper 4 reward method marks that students throw away by not writing the intermediate line. The recurring losses sit in algebraic fractions, transformations of graphs, and the probability tree where a branch is not replaced. Timed paper work under exam conditions fixes more of this than another worked example does.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics. Calculus arrives early and the differentiation of composite functions is where most of the damage happens. A student comfortable with 0580 Extended can still find 0606 unfamiliar, because the command terms expect a proof-shaped answer.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical paper account for a disproportionate share of lost marks. Students can state Ohm's law and still mis-read a potential divider. The alternative-to-practical paper is learnable in a way the theory is not, because it rewards a fixed vocabulary about precision, repeats and anomalous results.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic reaction pathways carry the grade. The common pattern in Ras Al Khaimah mock scripts is a student who can balance an equation but cannot convert between mass, moles and concentration under time pressure. Qualitative analysis tables are pure recall and are usually the fastest marks available.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Marks go missing on genetics crosses, osmosis experiment write-ups and the long answers where a student lists facts instead of answering the command term. Teaching the mark scheme's language is worth more than another pass through the textbook.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension is scored on precision of lifting, not on fluency. The summary question has a word limit and a content-point tally, and students who write beautifully often score poorly because they paraphrase away the required point. Speaking is a separate endorsement in 0510.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response reward control of register above vocabulary range. The commonest loss is a student who answers the text instead of the question. Past-paper work with the published mark scheme open is the whole intervention here.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the grade. A correctly labelled axis and a shifted curve with a new equilibrium marked earns marks that an essay of prose does not. Evaluation in the longer questions must be a judgement, not a list of both sides.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Application to the case study is the differentiator. Students who revise definitions score the first mark and then stop; the remaining marks require the answer to name the business in the stem and use its numbers. Calculation questions on break-even and cash flow are reliable marks that get skipped.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory on data representation and networks is heavily recalled and heavily mis-remembered, particularly hexadecimal conversion and the difference between a router and a switch. Paper 2 pseudocode must be syntactically consistent, which is a habit built by writing it, not reading it.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Case-study specificity carries the top band. A named place with a figure and a date outscores a general description every time. Map and graph skills in Paper 2 are the most teachable section of the whole syllabus and routinely the least practised.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Covers biology, chemistry and physics in two GCSEs worth of content, so breadth beats depth. Students lose marks by preparing as though each strand were a full single subject. A tutor's job here is triage: which topics are examined thinly and which carry the weight.

sections.heading: What a search for an IGCSE home tutor in Al Qusaidat usually means
paragraphs: A parent in Al Qusaidat typing this phrase is almost never shopping for a service category. They have seen a mock result, a report comment, or a child who has stopped opening a particular folder, and the exam is close enough to count in weeks. The word home in the search is about logistics: nobody wants a fourth journey in a day that already contains a school run both ways.

The honest answer has two halves. In-home tutoring genuinely exists in the UAE and the market for it is real, with rates that reflect travel as much as teaching. Independent UAE rate surveys put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-500 per hour including the visit, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The travel premium is between a third and double the online rate, and in Ras Al Khaimah it buys a smaller pool of available teachers rather than a larger one.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and that is a deliberate model rather than a limitation we are apologising for. A family in Al Qusaidat looking for Chemistry 0620 Extended help gets a tutor chosen for that code. A family relying on who can drive to Al Qusaidat on a Tuesday evening gets whoever is within range, which in this emirate is a short list.

The rest of this page is built on that. The calendar decides the plan, the subject decides the tutor, and the delivery format is settled: online, one-to-one, with a free trial lesson before any commitment so you can watch the first session rather than take a description of it on trust.

sections.heading: The June series counted backwards from the first paper
paragraphs: This is the table nobody in this market publishes. Work forwards from today and every month looks like it has room in it. Work backwards from the first written paper and the sequence is rigid: the entry is already gone, the mocks are the last external data point, and the final eight weeks are the only period in which timed paper technique can still be changed.

Read the middle column as a window rather than a fixed date, because the school sets its internal deadlines and the board sets the exam window, and the two are not published on the same calendar. The one date you should confirm directly with your child's exams officer is the internal entry submission, because that is the only step in the chain where a missed deadline cannot be recovered without an extra fee and sometimes not at all.

The point of the table is the right-hand column. Each row names the thing that should already be true by that stage, which converts a vague worry about exams into a short list of checks. If your child is eight weeks out and has never sat a full paper to time, that is the gap, and it is a gap that eight weeks can genuinely close. If the coursework row is still open four months out, that is a different and more urgent problem, because an unsubmitted assessed component is a capped grade rather than a weak one.

Print the table, mark today's position on it, and the conversation with your child changes from how much revision are you doing to which of these rows is not yet true. Parents in Al Qusaidat who do this in the autumn almost never need an eight-week emergency block in the spring, because the two expensive failures in an IGCSE year are a missed entry decision and a mock sat without preparation, and both of them sit above the halfway line on this table.

sections.heading: Zones, and the mistake that costs a whole paper
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and publishes a separate version of the timetable for each. The organisation states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That is unusually direct language from an examination board and it is there because the error happens.

The error is easy to make from Al Qusaidat. A parent searches for the IGCSE timetable, finds a PDF, and pins it to the fridge. The paper times on it belong to a different zone, the family plans an afternoon around a morning paper, and nobody discovers the mismatch until the hall is already sealed. The fix takes one message: ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in, then download the matching timetable from the board's own site rather than from a results-aggregator page.

Private candidates in Ras Al Khaimah carry this risk more than school candidates, because there is no form tutor repeating the dates in registration every morning. If your child is entering as a private candidate through an accepting centre, the zone question goes in your first email to that centre, not your last. The same discipline applies to Pearson: provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and can be revised, so the live official PDF is the only version worth trusting.

There is a second, quieter version of the same mistake. A student revising from a timetable with the wrong paper order prepares the components in the wrong sequence, peaks on the wrong day, and arrives at the harder paper already spent. Getting the zone right is therefore a revision-planning decision as much as an attendance one, and it is the first thing a tutor should ask for before writing any dated plan.

sections.heading: November as a route, not a rescue
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah candidates have two full Cambridge sittings a year and Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November. That second window changes the arithmetic of a disappointing June, and most families in Al Qusaidat do not know it exists until they need it. A June grade that sat two marks below a boundary does not require a repeated school year; it requires a focused five months on the one component that went wrong.

The November route works best when the decision is made on component evidence. A statement of results that shows a strong Paper 4 and a weak Paper 2 points at timing and arithmetic under pressure, which is a technique problem. The same overall grade built from an even spread across components points at content coverage, which takes longer. Those two students need different plans and should not be given the same eight-week block.

There is a trade-off worth saying out loud. A November resit sits in the middle of the first term of the next course, so a student carrying it is revising an old syllabus while starting a new one. For one subject that is manageable. For four it is not, and a family choosing to resit four subjects in November usually ends the term behind on both fronts. The table below sets out what each route actually fixes.

One practical note for Al Qusaidat families specifically. If the current school does not enter candidates for the November series in that subject, the route becomes a private-candidate entry through an accepting centre, which you arrange and pay for yourself. Ask that question before building a five-month plan, because the answer decides whether the plan is possible at all and it takes a single email to the exams officer to settle.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in the northern emirates
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number a household budget actually contains. A single weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor sits in the AED 600-1,200 band per month on UAE rate surveys, and an exam-year specialist block runs AED 1,000-2,000 or more. Monthly packages advertised in this market include online bundles from around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home bundles at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits.

Working down from there: a budget online or university-student tutor is advertised from roughly AED 45-150 per hour, with platforms publishing starting points as low as AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150-300, with one UAE agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors run AED 200-450 and above, with one UK-based agency quoting AED 270. Premium named or examiner-track tutors reach AED 500-650, with one provider publishing AED 650.

These are market figures, attributed to the providers and surveys that published them, not an IB Gram price list. What we do publish is the model: one-to-one, online, with a free trial lesson before any payment so the first session is evidence rather than a promise. Nothing on this page should be read as a quote; ask for one and it comes with the session length and the subject attached, which is the only way an hourly rate means anything.

sections.heading: Why online one-to-one beats a local visit in this emirate specifically
paragraphs: The argument for online delivery is weaker in Dubai than it is here, and it is worth being precise about why. Dubai has 227 private schools and 387,441 private-school students across 17 curricula, which produces a deep local teaching pool. Ras Al Khaimah's private-school provision is a fraction of that size, concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab. A student in Al Qusaidat sitting Computer Science 0478 or Economics 0455 may have no local specialist within a reasonable drive at all.

That is the real comparison. Not online versus in-person in the abstract, but a subject specialist reachable by video against a generalist reachable by car. For Mathematics 0580 the local pool is adequate and the choice is genuinely about preference. For a less commonly taught subject at Extended tier, the choice is between a specialist and nobody, and the honest recommendation is the specialist.

There are things a visit does better and pretending otherwise is not useful. A tutor in the room can see a student's written working upside down on the desk and intervene mid-line. Online, that requires a document camera or a phone propped over the page, and it requires asking for it. What online gives back is a shared screen on the actual past paper, a written record of every session, no travel cost in either direction, and a session that still happens when the Hajar road is closed or the family is travelling.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to tutor your child in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted, and it is permitted through a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone telling you the permit costs money, or that it is optional, is wrong on a point of fact that is published on the federal portal.

The eligible categories are wider than most parents expect: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a two-working-day completion time.

Two things follow for a family in Al Qusaidat. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has not published the amounts, so nobody should be quoting you a figure. And a school teacher is not a free pass: the permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Asking your child's own teacher for paid lessons is the one arrangement to avoid, and asking a tutor whether they hold the MoHRE permit is a reasonable first question.

sections.heading: The Department of Knowledge, and what a RAK regulator actually controls
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah has its own education regulator, which is more than most of the UAE tutoring market seems to know. The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate, and like Sharjah's authority it approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone: the curriculum your child's school runs and the fee it charges both pass through the emirate's own authority.

It is worth knowing the full map, because families move between emirates and the rules move with them. Dubai's private schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A parent told that one Dubai framework applies across the country is being told something untrue.

What none of these bodies do is accredit a tutor. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and any tutoring service claiming otherwise should be asked to produce the permit number. A permit for a training institute with premises in Dubai is a specific KHDA instrument with its own application sequence; it is not something an online matching platform can imply it holds.

There is one federal rule that reaches every emirate, including this one. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must otherwise adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. For an Al Qusaidat family that means those subjects sit on top of the IGCSE timetable rather than instead of it, so a Year 11 week contains more scheduled lessons than the IGCSE subject list alone suggests. Factoring that in is the difference between a revision plan that fits the week and one that quietly assumes hours the student does not have.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E: the equivalency rule most parents get wrong
paragraphs: If your child intends to apply to a UAE university, the certificate has to be made equivalent by the Ministry of Education, and the British-track rule is specific. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The part families get wrong is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A student in Al Qusaidat taking five IGCSEs where one is Arabic has four that count, not five, and discovers it at the application stage rather than at the entry stage. One ranking tutoring site currently publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced rule is five, excluding those two.

Two cautions. The American-track requirements are different again: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and at least 450 in SAT Math. And there is no published IB points threshold we are willing to repeat, because it has not been read on the Ministry's own site. IB Gram does not perform equivalency and does not guarantee an outcome from it; the process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, and that is where it should be verified.

sections.heading: An eight-week block, session by session
paragraphs: Most Al Qusaidat families arrive with roughly eight weeks and one subject. Here is what that block should contain, because the shape matters more than the hours. Session one is a full past paper sat to time, with the phone away. It is unpleasant and it produces the only honest map of where the marks are. Sessions two to four work the three weakest topic clusters from that script, using questions rather than explanations.

Sessions five to ten alternate: one session on a topic, one session on a timed component, so that technique and content build against each other instead of one waiting for the other. By session eleven the student should be marking their own work against the published scheme with the tutor present, because reading a mark scheme is a learnable skill and the student who can do it has a revision tool that outlasts the tuition.

Sessions thirteen to sixteen are whole papers under time, marked and discussed, with no new content introduced. If a gap appears in the last fortnight it gets a note and a two-minute recap, not a lesson, because reopening content late reliably costs more marks than it recovers. The block ends two weeks before the first paper, deliberately, so the final fortnight belongs to the student. The free trial lesson happens before any of this, so you can see the tutor work with your child before committing to the block.

Two things will tempt you off this shape. The first is adding a second subject in week three because the first one is going well; resist it until the block is finished, since two half-blocks reliably underperform one whole one. The second is skipping the diagnostic because the mock result already exists. Use the mock if it was sat to time and marked to the published scheme, and sit a fresh paper if it was not, because an inflated internal mark is the single most common reason an eight-week plan targets the wrong topics.

process.description: Early in the engagement your child sits a full past paper under exam conditions. The tutor marks it against the published scheme and reports component by component. This is what sets the topic order for everything that follows, and it is usually the first time a family sees where the marks actually go.

process.description: The plan is written back from your child's first paper and the school's internal deadlines, not forward from today. You get the sequence in writing: which topics in which weeks, which papers on which dates, and when the block stops.

process.description: What was covered, what was set, and what the tutor is watching. It takes a minute to read and it is the record that lets you tell whether six sessions have moved anything. If they have not, say so and the match changes.

process.description: For a thinly taught subject at Extended tier there may be no immediate match. You are told that rather than placed with a generalist, and offered a date or a different plan. Being told no is more useful than being quietly downgraded.

whyPoints.title: The calendar comes first
whyPoints.description: Every plan here starts from the series your child is entered for and works backwards. That sounds obvious and almost nobody does it; the usual pattern is a weekly slot with no end date and no relationship to the exam window. A block with a defined finish concentrates the work.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: A tutor matched to 0620 Extended has worked that mark scheme. A tutor matched to chemistry has not necessarily seen a Cambridge qualitative analysis table. In a small emirate the difference between those two is the whole argument for online delivery.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what a tutor may not do
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on a student's own work. Nobody here writes or completes coursework, an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay. Services that sell finished assessed work exist in this market and using one is a malpractice risk carried entirely by the student.

whyPoints.title: One format, stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one and live over video. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses and we do not let a family find that out after paying. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and saying so on the page is less expensive for everyone than saying it on the phone.

whyPoints.title: Regulators named, never claimed
whyPoints.description: This page explains what the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and the Ministry of Education each do. It claims approval from none of them, because IB Gram holds none. The most dangerous phrase in UAE tutoring marketing is a regulator's name used as an adjective.

faqs.question: Can we get an IGCSE home tutor who comes to our house in Al Qusaidat?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. In-home tutoring does exist in the Ras Al Khaimah market and published rates run roughly AED 180-500 per hour including travel, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. In a small emirate the practical effect of insisting on a visit is a shorter list of available teachers, so a student sitting a thinly taught subject at Extended tier usually ends up with a generalist instead of a specialist.

faqs.question: When do Ras Al Khaimah students actually sit their IGCSE exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and both are available to UAE centres. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. The February and March series Cambridge offers is for India only, so it should not appear in any Ras Al Khaimah plan. Confirm the exact paper dates on the correct zone version of the timetable through your child's exams officer, because every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and each zone has its own timetable.

faqs.question: How far before the exam does the entry have to be submitted?
faqs.answer: Months, and it is the school that submits it rather than the parent. In practice the final entry for a June series closes roughly five months before the first paper, which is why a decision about tier or about adding a subject has to be made in the autumn rather than in the spring. Ask your child's exams officer for the internal submission date, in writing. It is the only step in the whole sequence where a missed deadline cannot be fixed later without extra cost, and in some cases cannot be fixed at all.

faqs.question: My child is eight weeks from the first paper. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change shape. Eight weeks is enough to move timed-paper technique, mark-scheme literacy and three weak topic clusters, which between them account for a large share of recoverable marks. It is not enough to re-teach two years of content, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling hours. The block should open with a full paper sat to time, use the resulting component marks to set the topic order, and introduce no new content in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Is my child entered for the right tier, and who decides that in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Core covers less content and caps at grade C; Extended runs the full A* to G range and is the tier most UAE sixth forms expect for a subject a student intends to continue. The tier is part of the entry, so changing it is a conversation with the exams officer inside the entry window rather than a decision made in the spring. A student entered for Core who later needs a B has to resit at Extended in a later series, which is why the tier decision deserves more attention than it usually gets.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Ras Al Khaimah families most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Mathematics 0580 Extended, Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620 account for most requests, with English as a Second Language 0510 close behind. The pattern is less about difficulty than about staffing: in a small private-school set, one teacher may cover several sciences, and a subject with a dozen candidates gets a dozen candidates' worth of attention. Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 and Economics 0455 are the subjects where a family in Al Qusaidat is least likely to find a local specialist at all.

faqs.question: Does an online lesson work for a subject with a practical paper?
faqs.answer: For the assessment, yes, and better than most parents expect. The practical and alternative-to-practical components reward a fixed vocabulary about variables, repeats, precision and anomalous results, plus the ability to read and complete a results table. All of that is paper-based and can be worked through on a shared screen. What an online session cannot replace is time in the school laboratory handling the apparatus, which is the school's job and should not be outsourced to tuition in the first place.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should we book for one subject?
faqs.answer: One a week if the exam is a term or more away, two a week inside an eight-week exam block. Three is rarely useful, because the work between sessions is where the improvement happens and a student with three sessions has no time to do it. For two subjects, run them on different days with different tutors rather than splitting one session, since a split hour ends up being thirty minutes of revision in each and a full hour of neither.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is legally allowed to teach my child here?
faqs.answer: Yes to the permit and no to the cost. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the ministry has not published the amounts.

faqs.question: Can we ask my child's own school teacher to tutor privately instead?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the rules, it is a poor arrangement on its own terms: the person marking your child's internal assessments should not also be paid to prepare them for it. A separate specialist gives you an independent read.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with coursework if my child's subject has it?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the skills, explains the assessment criteria, and gives feedback on work the student has written. Nobody here produces assessed work for a student. That boundary is not a policy preference: submitting work that is not your own is malpractice under board rules and the consequence falls on the student, not on the tutor. Services in this market do sell completed coursework and Internal Assessments, which is exactly why the boundary is stated on the page rather than buried in terms.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial, and what happens in it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a real lesson rather than a sales call. The tutor works on your child's own material, usually a question from a recent paper or a topic from this week's class, and you are welcome to watch. No payment is taken and no card is needed to book it. What you are judging is how the tutor behaves when your child gets something wrong, because that is the part of a session that repeats forty times over a block and the part a brochure cannot show you.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for an Al Qusaidat student?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics, the three separate sciences, and English, usually within a few days. For a thinly taught subject at Extended tier it can take longer, and if there is no suitable specialist available you will be told that rather than placed with somebody adjacent. A plan with a date attached is more useful than an immediate match with the wrong person, particularly in an exam year where six wasted sessions are six weeks you do not get back.

faqs.question: Does tuition have to stop during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: No, but the timing moves. School days shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window shifts to the late evening, so sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot. Because lessons are delivered online there is no travel to arrange around prayer times or iftar, which is one of the practical advantages of the format in this market. Families who plan the Ramadan schedule two weeks ahead rather than week by week lose far fewer sessions, and the same applies to the mid-term and summer breaks.

faqs.question: Do five IGCSEs give my child UAE university equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 is the published British-track requirement, but Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A student with five passes where one is Arabic therefore has four that count. The British track also asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify the current rule with the Ministry of Education or the emirate attestation authority, since IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: What should we do with the statement of results when it arrives?
faqs.answer: Read it component by component rather than as a single grade. A strong Paper 4 beside a weak Paper 2 points at timing and arithmetic under pressure, which a focused November block can fix. An even spread across components at a low level points at content coverage, which takes longer. That distinction decides whether an enquiry about results, a single-subject November resit, or a different route altogether is the sensible next step, and it is invisible if you only look at the letter.

Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and we will tell you before you book if the specialist your child needs is not available this month.

intro.heading: Most of the marks are won on paper
paragraphs: Families understandably worry that online tuition cannot support IGCSE sciences, because the laboratory is the visible part of the subject. The arithmetic says otherwise. In Cambridge sciences the laboratory work is assessed through one component out of three, and even that component may be a written paper rather than a practical test depending on what the centre entered. Everything else, and a very large share of the available marks, is reading, calculating, graph work and explanation on paper.

The first thing to establish is therefore administrative. Cambridge science candidates sit either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the centre chooses. If your centre entered the written alternative, the entire practical component is a paper exercise about reading somebody else's experiment, and a shared screen is a better place to teach it than a bench. If your centre entered the practical test, the laboratory work happens at school with school equipment regardless of who tutors, and a tutor's contribution is the recording, the uncertainty treatment and the write-up.

Julphar is the old quarter of Ras Al Khaimah, built around the creek and the historic port, with the shortest school journeys in the emirate and older, denser housing. The journey advantage means a session can start early; the housing means it should be short and reliably held rather than long and ambitious. Forty-five minutes is enough for every kind of work described on this page except a complete timed paper.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For written practical work, graph questions and language papers the format is an active advantage: the paper sits on a shared screen, is annotated live against the published scheme, and the family keeps the annotated copy.

The second half of this page is about skills that cross subjects. Graph and data questions appear in Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography and Economics in substantially the same style, and they reward the same handful of moves. Significant figures and uncertainty rules cost marks in every science paper and are almost never taught explicitly. An hour on either lifts several subjects at once, which no single-subject revision plan can match.

Everything here should be confirmed against your own centre's entry and the current syllabus document, because boards revise them. Cambridge and Pearson positions come from the boards' own exam-administration pages, read in October 2026. Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only; a centre in Ras Al Khaimah enters June and November. That correction matters because revision guides written for an India audience circulate here freely, and a family planning a schedule around a February window is planning around a window their child will never sit. Past dates on this page keep their year because the year is what makes them checkable, and future series are named by month only so that nothing here becomes wrong a year from now without anybody touching it.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves carry the heaviest content losses. The practical component rewards apparatus discipline or written method critique depending on the centre's entry, and graph work appears in every paper rather than only in the practical one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry remain the wall, and conversions break down under time rather than in principle. Practical work centres on observation, inference and the language of a test result: a precipitate described rather than merely noticed.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Long answers reward sequencing as much as naming. Practical questions are heavy on variables and on the distinction between a control and a controlled variable, which students confuse routinely and which costs a mark every time.

subjects.description: Reading and writing, listening, and speaking. Writing is marked on content and language separately, so register and task conventions cost content marks independently of fluency. Listening must be practised at exam speed with no pauses.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
subjects.description: Assesses reading, comprehension and extended writing in Standard Arabic. Home speakers lose marks on register and on the conventions of the required text type rather than on vocabulary, which is a different problem from fluency.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: A foreign-language paper with reading, writing, listening and speaking components. Taken by non-Arab students, and the marks sit in prescribed structures and topic vocabulary rather than in free expression. Confirm the code with your centre.

subjects.name: French, Spanish and German (Cambridge 0520, 0530, 0525)
subjects.description: Four skills assessed, with the writing and speaking components rewarding specific structures and tenses rather than volume. Frequently taken as a fifth or sixth subject and rarely revised, which makes it an efficient target.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The current Cambridge structure includes a non-calculator paper in each route; Pearson sits two papers of equal weight. Graph work, significant figures and multi-step method discipline carry across into every science paper.

subjects.name: Geography and Economics
subjects.description: Both carry data and graph questions in the same style as the sciences, which is why the cross-subject skills on this page matter. Geography adds case-study specificity; Economics adds labelled diagrams and extract figures.

sections.heading: Practical science without a lab: the two routes
paragraphs: This is the question every family asks about online science tuition, and it has a precise answer rather than a reassuring one. Cambridge science candidates sit either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the centre decides which. Establish that first, in writing, because it determines what half of the preparation should be.

Where the centre entered the alternative-to-practical paper, the practical component is entirely written. The examination asks a candidate to read somebody else's experiment: identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables, spot the flaw in a described method, read a scale to the correct precision, tabulate results with units in the headings, plot points and draw an appropriate line, calculate a gradient, state a conclusion that the data supports, and suggest an improvement that addresses a named weakness. Every one of those is a paper skill and every one is better taught with the question on a shared screen than with apparatus on a bench.

Where the centre entered the practical test, the laboratory work happens at school with school equipment, as it must. A tutor's contribution is the part students lose marks on anyway: recording to an appropriate precision, consistent units, sensible table layout, and an evaluation that ranks sources of error rather than listing them. Pearson assesses practical knowledge inside its written papers instead, which makes the same written skills decisive on that board regardless of route.

The table sets out what each route examines and where the marks go. Confirm your centre's entry before building a plan around either, because a term spent rehearsing apparatus technique for a candidate entered on the written alternative is a term spent on a skill nobody will assess.

sections.heading: Significant figures, units and uncertainty
paragraphs: These are the rules that cost marks in every science paper on both boards and that almost nobody teaches explicitly, because they feel like administration rather than science. They are worth a session on their own, and the gain shows on the next paper rather than next term.

The recurring failures are consistent. Rounding in the middle of a multi-step calculation, which propagates an error into the final answer and loses the accuracy mark even when the method was right. Dropping units in a table heading, where the scheme expects them, and then adding them inconsistently in the answer. Quoting an answer to more figures than the data justifies, or to fewer than the mark scheme expects, when the convention is usually to work to the precision the question's data supports and to state what has been assumed. And treating uncertainty as a formality rather than as a quantity that can be estimated and then used.

The teaching method is unglamorous. Take a student's own marked calculations, identify every mark lost to rounding, units or precision rather than to physics or chemistry, and total them. Most students are surprised by the figure, and surprise is what changes a habit. Then rewrite three answers correctly, which takes ten minutes and generalises immediately.

One caution: conventions on significant figures and acceptable tolerances are specified by the board in the mark scheme for each paper, and they differ between questions. The correct approach is to read the scheme rather than apply a universal rule, which is another reason to mark work against the published scheme instead of an answer key.
bullets: Never round in the middle of a multi-step calculation.
Units belong in table headings, and consistently in the answer.
Work to the precision the data supports and state what has been assumed.
Read the mark scheme's tolerance for each question rather than applying one rule.

sections.heading: Graph work: the skill that appears in five subjects
paragraphs: Of all the cross-subject skills available at IGCSE, graph and data handling has the best return per hour, because the same small set of moves is rewarded in Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography and Economics. A student who improves at it improves in five subjects simultaneously, and almost no revision plan is organised to take advantage of that.

The moves are specific and learnable. Choose a scale that uses most of the available grid rather than a convenient one. Label both axes with a quantity and a unit. Plot to the nearest small square rather than approximately. Draw the line the data supports, which may be a straight line of best fit or a curve, rather than joining the points. Calculate a gradient from two widely separated points actually on the line, showing the coordinates used. Read an intercept where one is asked for. Describe a trend and then give its cause, because the description alone rarely earns the mark.

The identical pattern appears outside the sciences in a form students do not recognise. A Geography climate graph, an Economics data-response table and a Biology rate-of-reaction curve all ask the same four things: read accurately, calculate rather than estimate, quote the figure, and explain the cause. Practising them together rather than subject by subject is the thing that makes the skill transfer.

The table lists the question types by what they reward. It is worth running a student through one of each in a single session, because the recognition that these are the same question in different clothing is itself most of the improvement.

sections.heading: Languages at IGCSE: three different examinations
paragraphs: Language entries are where families are most likely to be unaware of what their child is actually sitting, because the labels sound similar and the papers are not. First language, second language and foreign language qualifications assess different things and reward different preparation, and a student in the wrong one is a surprisingly common situation in this market.

A first language paper, such as Cambridge 0500 for English or 0508 for Arabic, assesses reading comprehension and extended writing at native-speaker level, with marks for analysing how a text works and for writing to a specified form. A second language paper, such as Cambridge 0510 or 0511 for English, assesses reading and writing, listening and speaking, with content and language marked separately, so register and task conventions cost content marks independently of fluency. A foreign language paper, such as Cambridge 0544 for Arabic, 0520 for French, 0530 for Spanish or 0525 for German, assesses four skills around prescribed topic vocabulary and structures, where accuracy in a small range beats ambition across a wide one.

The practical consequences differ sharply. A fluent home speaker entered for a first language paper loses marks on register and analytical vocabulary rather than on understanding, and needs analytical teaching. A strong writer entered for a second language paper loses content marks by ignoring the form of a report or an email, and needs task discipline. A student on a foreign language paper usually needs structures drilled and topic vocabulary secured, which is the most mechanical and fastest-improving of the three.
Confirm the code with your exams officer, because the labels in a school report do not distinguish reliably between these. The table sets out what each type assesses and where the marks go.

sections.heading: When each topic is taught, and when the gap surfaces
paragraphs: A particular pattern recurs in this market and it looks mysterious until the teaching sequence is laid out. A student is fine through Year 10, then struggles in Year 11, and the household concludes that the course has suddenly become harder. Usually what has happened is that a Year 10 topic was never secured and the Year 11 content assumes it.

The sequence is predictable because schemes of work are. Electricity and waves in Physics are usually taught early, and almost everything later assumes them. Moles and stoichiometry in Chemistry sit in the first year, and organic chemistry and quantitative questions in the second year assume fluency with them. Algebraic manipulation in Mathematics is Year 9 and Year 10 work, and every multi-step question afterwards uses it as a step rather than as the point. In Biology, cell structure and transport are early and the later physiology assumes them.

The practical consequence is that a Year 11 problem is frequently a Year 10 diagnosis. Teaching the Year 11 content harder does not fix it, and this is why a term of conscientious tuition can produce no change: the sessions were spent on the material the student was struggling with rather than on the material underneath it. A diagnostic session that works backwards is what separates the two.

sections.heading: Rewriting an answer: a worked method
paragraphs: This is the most transferable thing a tutor does and it takes about eight minutes per answer. Most students have never seen it done, and the first time they do it they usually find two or three marks they already knew.

The method has five steps. Take a question the student has already answered and had marked. Cover both their answer and the awarded marks, and read only the question, noting the command term and the number of marks available. Predict what the scheme will credit, in a list, one item per mark. Then uncover the published scheme and compare it with the prediction. Finally, rewrite the answer to deliver each credited item explicitly, in the scheme's own vocabulary where it uses a technical term.

What makes this work is that it separates knowing from scoring. A student who predicted four of five credited items but delivered two of them has a writing problem, which is fixable in weeks. A student who predicted one of five has a content or comprehension problem, which takes longer. The exercise diagnoses and treats in the same ten minutes, which almost nothing else in revision does.

The rule on materials still applies. Work from papers and schemes the student legitimately holds through their school. No tutor should reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads; the official source should be referenced and linked instead. That is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.
bullets: Read only the question: note the command term and the marks available.
Predict the credited items, one per mark, before looking at anything.
Compare the prediction with the published scheme.

sections.heading: The three question styles students never practise
paragraphs: Revision tends to cover topics, and papers tend to contain question styles. Three styles appear reliably and are almost never practised deliberately, which means a well-prepared student can still meet them for the first time in the examination.

The first is the unfamiliar context: a question that applies a known idea to a situation the student has never seen, such as a circuit in a device nobody studied or a reaction in an industrial process the textbook skipped. The content is familiar and the dressing is not, and students who have only practised textbook-shaped questions freeze. The treatment is deliberate exposure: five questions in unfamiliar contexts on content the student already knows.

The second is the synoptic question, which requires two parts of the syllabus at once: energy and electricity together, or genetics and variation together. Topic-by-topic revision actively prepares students badly for this, because it trains retrieval of one box at a time. The treatment is to practise questions that deliberately cross two topics, which is also a good use of a short session.

The third is the extended-response question with a high mark allocation, where the marks are structured and a student who writes an unplanned paragraph collects some of them by luck. The treatment is two minutes of planning: list the credited items first, then write. That habit alone usually moves an extended-response score more than any amount of additional content revision, and it is the clearest example of why practising styles matters as much as practising topics.

sections.heading: Honesty, materials and the permit
paragraphs: A tutor may teach content, explain what a command term demands, work through past questions, mark answers against the published scheme and give written feedback on the student's own work. Where an IGCSE subject carries a coursework component, support means feedback on a draft the student has written, never production of the work.

No tutor should reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The official source should be referenced and linked instead, which is why there are no attachments on this page and why it repeatedly asks readers to confirm codes, structures and practical routes with their own centre. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications through the smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

No tutor can promise a grade, because boundaries are set after a series on the basis of that series' papers. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none; describing what a regulator or a board does is not the same as being endorsed by it.

faqs.question: Can online tuition cover IGCSE practical science from Julphar?
faqs.answer: It depends on which component the centre entered, and that is worth one email to establish. If your centre entered the alternative-to-practical paper, the entire practical component is written: identifying variables, spotting a flaw in a method, reading a scale, tabulating with units, plotting, calculating a gradient and suggesting an improvement. A shared screen suits all of that better than a bench. If the practical test was entered, the laboratory work happens at school and a tutor works on the recording and the write-up.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a control and a controlled variable?
faqs.answer: A controlled variable is a factor kept the same across every trial so that it cannot explain the result, such as temperature or concentration. A control is a separate trial run without the factor being tested, to show what happens in its absence. Students use the two terms interchangeably and lose a mark almost every time a practical question appears, in all three sciences. It is a five-minute correction that recurs on every paper afterwards.

faqs.question: How many marks does my child lose to rounding and units?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect, and the number is worth calculating. Take a set of marked calculations and total every mark lost to rounding mid-calculation, missing or inconsistent units, or an answer quoted to the wrong precision, rather than to the chemistry or physics itself. Most students are surprised by the figure, and surprise is what changes the habit. Conventions and tolerances are specified per question in the mark scheme, so the fix is reading the scheme rather than applying one universal rule.

faqs.question: Which single skill improves the most IGCSE subjects at once?
faqs.answer: Graph and data handling, because Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Geography and Economics all ask for it in substantially the same style. The moves are specific: choose a scale that uses the grid, label both axes with quantity and unit, plot to the nearest small square, draw the line the data supports rather than joining points, calculate a gradient from two widely separated points with the coordinates shown, and state a trend with its cause. Three or four sessions on it lifts five subjects.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Economics data answer score badly when the maths is right?
faqs.answer: Usually because the figure from the extract was paraphrased rather than quoted. Data-response marks in Economics, and comparable marks in Geography and Biology, frequently require the actual number to appear in the answer, with units. The second common loss is comparing two data sets in two separate paragraphs instead of holding both in one statement with a figure for each. Both are mechanical fixes and both transfer straight into the science data questions.

faqs.question: Is my child entered for the right English paper?
faqs.answer: Worth checking, because the labels in a school report do not distinguish reliably. Cambridge 0500 First Language English assesses reading analysis and extended writing at native-speaker level; 0510 and 0511 English as a Second Language assess reading, writing, listening and speaking with content and language marked separately. A fluent home speaker in a second language entry, or a developing writer in a first language entry, is a common and expensive mismatch. Ask the exams officer for the code.

faqs.question: What do foreign language papers actually reward?
faqs.answer: Accuracy within a prescribed range rather than ambition beyond it. Cambridge 0544 Arabic as a Foreign Language, 0520 French, 0530 Spanish and 0525 German each assess four skills around set topic areas and structures, and the marks go to secure tenses, correct structures and topic vocabulary used properly. A student reaching for complex constructions they cannot control scores less than one deploying simpler ones accurately. Confirm the code, because entries vary by centre.

faqs.question: Why is my child fine in Year 10 and struggling in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually because a Year 10 topic was never secured and the Year 11 content assumes it. Electricity and waves in Physics, moles and stoichiometry in Chemistry, algebraic manipulation in Mathematics and cell transport in Biology are all taught early and used as foundations later. Teaching the Year 11 material harder does not fix that, which is why a term of conscientious tuition can produce no change. The diagnosis has to run backwards before the teaching runs forwards.

faqs.question: What is the fastest way to improve an extended-response answer?
faqs.answer: Two minutes of planning before writing. High-mark questions have structured mark schemes, and a student who writes an unplanned paragraph collects some credited items by luck. Listing the credited items first, one per mark, and then writing to deliver each explicitly, usually moves an extended-response score more than any amount of extra content revision. It is also the clearest demonstration that practising question styles matters as much as practising topics.

faqs.question: How does the answer-rewriting exercise work?
faqs.answer: Five steps and about eight minutes. Take a question the student has already answered and had marked. Cover both the answer and the awarded marks, and read only the question, noting the command term and the marks available. Predict the credited items, one per mark. Uncover the published scheme and compare. Then rewrite to deliver each item explicitly in the scheme's own vocabulary. A student who predicted four and delivered two has a writing problem, which is fixable in weeks.

faqs.question: What are synoptic questions and why do they catch students out?
faqs.answer: They require two parts of the syllabus at once, such as energy and electricity together or genetics and variation together. Topic-by-topic revision prepares students badly for them, because it trains retrieval of one box at a time and these questions ask for two boxes simultaneously. The treatment is deliberate: practise questions that cross two topics on purpose, which also suits a short session well because the content is already known and only the combination is new.

faqs.question: Where should a Julphar student sit a full timed paper?
faqs.answer: Somewhere other than a busy flat, because an interruption at minute fifty destroys the pacing information the paper exists to produce. The school library, a relative's home, or an early weekend morning before the household wakes all work. Julphar's advantage is the shortest school journeys in the emirate, which makes an early weekday slot easy; its constraint is older, denser housing, which makes the ninety-minute sitting the thing to plan a venue for.

faqs.question: Can a 45-minute session cover practical paper work properly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it suits the format well. A single practical-style question with its mark scheme takes twenty to thirty minutes to attempt, annotate and rewrite, which fits comfortably and produces something concrete: a named reason a mark was lost. What forty-five minutes cannot do is test pacing across a complete paper, so the long sittings go elsewhere in the week. For a dense Julphar household, short and reliably held beats long and frequently cancelled.

faqs.question: Which exam windows apply to a Ras Al Khaimah science candidate?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge, June and November, with the February and March series offered in India only, so revision material written for an India audience names a window your child will not sit. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Ask your Cambridge centre which of the six administrative zones it sits in, because the board states the correct zone timetable must be used.

faqs.question: Will a tutor supply practical papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and none should. Reproducing or distributing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure. Work is done against material the student legitimately holds through their school, annotated on a shared screen against the published scheme, with the official source referenced and linked. The annotated copy of the student's own work is theirs to keep afterwards.

intro.heading: The code decides what is worth practising
paragraphs: There is no such thing as IGCSE Maths. There is Cambridge 0580, which splits candidates into Core and Extended and sits different papers for each, and there is Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1, which uses Foundation and Higher tiers and a different paper structure again. A student practising the wrong one is preparing conscientiously for an examination they will not sit, and this is the most common single waste of effort in the subject.

The same is true across the sciences. Cambridge Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 each run a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and then either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, with the practical route chosen by the centre. Pearson's 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 assess practical knowledge inside two written papers of unequal length. Those are genuinely different examinations that happen to cover similar content.

Khuzam sits inland in Ras Al Khaimah city, a residential district with a short drive into the emirate's school cluster. The practical consequence of being here is that the local tutoring pool is small and weighted towards the most widely taught subjects, so the question of whether a tutor has actually taught your child's code matters more than it would in Dubai, where several candidates exist for most things.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For IGCSE work that is not a compromise: most of a useful session is a question, a mark scheme and a pen, annotated live on a shared screen and kept afterwards, which is closer to how examiners work than a dining table is.

The second half of this page is about method marks, which is where the real grades live. A mark scheme awards credit for identifiable steps, not for the right answer alone, and a student who writes a correct answer with no working loses marks they fully earned in their head. Teaching a student to write for a marker rather than for themselves is the fastest improvement available in any IGCSE subject, and it is almost never taught explicitly.

Everything here should be confirmed against your own centre's entry and the current syllabus document, because boards revise assessment structures. Cambridge and Pearson positions below come from the boards' own exam-administration pages, read in October 2026. One correction worth stating before anything else: Cambridge offers the February and March series to candidates in India, and a centre in Ras Al Khaimah enters June and November. Revision material written for an India audience circulates widely here, and a family working to those dates is working to a calendar their child will never sit. Past dates on this page keep their year because that is what makes them checkable; future series are named by month only, so nothing here goes stale without anybody touching it.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Naming a process earns one mark; ordering its stages earns the rest, and most lost marks sit in that second half. Extended genetics needs a Punnett square drawn properly rather than reasoned about aloud.

subjects.name: Physics, Chemistry and Biology (Pearson 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1)
subjects.description: Two written papers of unequal length, with practical knowledge assessed inside them. Preparation therefore centres on method critique and data interpretation in written form rather than on apparatus handling.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: A reading paper and a directed writing and composition paper. Marks are lost by retelling the passage instead of analysing how it works, and by writing more than the time allows rather than spending four minutes planning.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510)
subjects.description: Reading and writing, listening, and a speaking component. Writing is marked on content and language separately and the task types are prescriptive, so register matters as much as fluency. Listening practice has to be done at exam speed.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: A bridge to A Level Mathematics or a Higher Level Diploma course, introducing calculus and trigonometric identities early. This is where a weak Year 9 algebra foundation stops being hideable.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450, 0455)
subjects.description: Both are application papers. Business marks come from using the business in the stimulus rather than the theory in the textbook; Economics marks come from labelled diagrams and from quoting the figure in the extract.

sections.heading: Cambridge Mathematics 0580: the tiers and the papers
paragraphs: Start with the entry, because nothing else in this subject makes sense without it. Cambridge 0580 runs two routes. The Core route covers a reduced syllabus and is capped below the top grades. The Extended route covers the full syllabus and reaches the top of the scale. They sit different papers, which means the past papers a family downloads are either the right ones or a complete waste of a term.

Cambridge revised the 0580 assessment structure, and the current pattern includes a non-calculator paper in each route alongside a calculator paper. That change matters more than it sounds, because a generation of students learned to route every calculation through a device. Surds, factorising, simultaneous equations and fraction arithmetic done by hand are a different skill from the same operations done on a screen, and a student can lose a grade on the non-calculator paper while performing adequately everywhere else. Confirm the current paper pattern with your exams officer rather than with any website, including this one.

The second structural point is where the marks sit. The longer structured paper in each route carries multi-step questions, and multi-step questions award method marks for identifiable steps. A student who produces the right answer with no working can score a fraction of the available marks, and a student who produces the wrong answer with correct working can score most of them. That asymmetry is the single most exploitable fact in IGCSE Mathematics.

The practical consequence for a Khuzam family is a two-part plan: confirm the route and the paper pattern in writing, then spend the term on the papers actually entered, with every answer written out as a marker would want to read it.

sections.heading: The Cambridge sciences: 0625, 0620 and 0610
paragraphs: The three Cambridge sciences share an assessment shape, which makes them easy to plan together and easy to misunderstand together. Each runs a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper, and then either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, with that last choice made by the centre rather than by the student or the family.

That practical decision is worth establishing before any preparation begins, because the two routes test different things. The alternative-to-practical paper is entirely about reading somebody else's experiment: identifying the controlled variable, spotting a flaw in a method, reading a scale correctly, plotting results and suggesting an improvement. Those are written skills. The practical test is about handling apparatus under timed conditions, which has to be practised with equipment at school.

Content losses are predictable and subject-specific. In Physics the heaviest are electricity and waves, with explanation questions answered by writing an equation rather than a sentence. In Chemistry it is moles and stoichiometry, where a student who balances equations confidently cannot convert between mass, moles and volume under pressure. In Biology it is the second half of long answers: naming a process earns a mark and sequencing its stages earns the rest, and students routinely stop after the name.

The table lines up the components with what each tests and what the realistic preparation looks like. Confirm your centre's practical route in writing before building a plan around either possibility, because a term spent rehearsing apparatus technique for a candidate entered on the written alternative is a term spent on a skill that will not be assessed.
