sections.heading: Pearson's codes, and why the papers are not interchangeable
paragraphs: Families who discover their child is entered with Pearson rather than Cambridge often assume the difference is cosmetic. It is not. The number of papers, the way practical skills are assessed, the tier structure and the grade scale all differ, which means past-paper practice does not transfer in either direction.

Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 sits two papers of equal weight, with Foundation and Higher tiers, and the Foundation tier is capped below the top grades. The sciences, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4BI1 Biology, each sit two written papers of unequal length, with the longer carrying the larger share, and practical knowledge is assessed inside those written papers rather than through a separate practical or alternative-to-practical component.

The grade scale is the other visible difference. Cambridge IGCSE reports grades A* to G. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports grades 9 to 1. For a family in Ras Al Khaimah with children on both boards, or a student sitting some subjects privately, that produces a certificate set in two different currencies, which is confusing at exactly the moment it needs to be clear.

What rescues the comparison is equivalency, because the Ministry's published requirement is expressed in a way that covers both. The British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. That is a floor rather than a target, and it is worth knowing in Year 10.

sections.heading: What the grade scales actually mean for a family here
paragraphs: Grade scales look like administration and behave like strategy, because the tier ceiling and the equivalency floor between them define the usable range of outcomes for any entry. Getting this right in Year 10 avoids a specific and common disappointment: a student who performed well inside a tier and still cannot do what the family assumed the certificate would allow.

Two ceilings matter. Cambridge's Core route is capped below the top grades, and Pearson's Foundation tier is likewise capped below the top of the 9 to 1 scale. A student entered on the lower route who performs excellently receives the capped grade, not the grade their performance would have earned at the higher tier. There is nothing unfair in that, and it is not reversible after entries close.

One floor matters. The Ministry's published equivalency requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, plus an A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E. That floor is low relative to what most families aim for, which is useful to know because it separates two different anxieties: whether a certificate will be recognised, and whether it will open a particular post-16 course. Those have very different answers.

It is also worth noting that one competitor page ranking for these queries tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required. The published rule is five. Where this page states an equivalency figure it is taken from a sourced report, and for the IB no points threshold is published here because the source used does not state one. Confirm your own case with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation channel; no tutoring provider performs or underwrites equivalency, and tuition is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: English: what the papers actually reward
paragraphs: English is the subject where a confident student is most likely to be scoring below their ability, because fluency and mark-earning are not the same thing. The papers reward specific moves, and a student who writes well without making those moves lands in the middle bands and cannot see why.

Cambridge First Language English 0500 sits a reading paper and a directed writing and composition paper. The reading responses reward analysis of how the passage works: what the writer is doing with structure, word choice and tone, and what effect that produces. Students retell the passage instead, which is a summary of something the examiner has already read. On the writing side, the task type is prescriptive: a directed writing task has an audience, a purpose and a form, and ignoring them loses content marks that quality of prose cannot recover.

Cambridge English as a Second Language 0510 assesses reading and writing, listening, and speaking. Writing is marked on content and language separately, which means a fluent writer who misses the register of a report or an email loses the content half of the available marks. Listening is the component students neglect because it feels passive, and it has to be practised at exam speed rather than with pauses.

The repair in both is mechanical and quick: take answers the student has already written, identify what the task demanded, and rewrite one paragraph to deliver it. Four or five sessions of that changes how a student reads a question, which transfers to every paper afterwards, including the ones in other subjects.
bullets: Reading responses: analyse how the passage works, do not retell it.
Directed writing: audience, purpose and form are marked, not optional.
0510 writing is marked on content and language separately; register costs content marks.

sections.heading: Method marks: why working earns more than answers
paragraphs: This is the section that moves grades, and it is the one almost nobody teaches explicitly. A mark scheme does not award credit for being right. It awards credit for identifiable steps, and it describes those steps in specific language. A student who understands this writes differently within a fortnight.

Consider the arithmetic of a five-mark multi-step question. The scheme typically allocates marks for a correct method, for a correct intermediate value, and for the final answer with its unit. A student who does the whole thing mentally and writes one number can earn one mark out of five while having answered it correctly. A student who sets out the method, shows the intermediate value and gets the final arithmetic wrong can earn four. Across a paper, that difference is a grade.

The same logic applies outside mathematics. In the sciences a mark is often awarded for the mechanism rather than the outcome, so an answer that states the result without the cause scores nothing even when the result is right. In Economics a mark is available for the labelled axis, the shown shift and the marked new equilibrium, each of which a student can earn before any analysis happens. In every case the marks are there to be collected by a student who writes for a reader rather than for themselves.

Teaching it works best on the student's own old answers. Cover the marks awarded, have them predict where the scheme would have given credit, then compare. The discovery that most of their lost marks were available rather than unknown is uncomfortable and it is the reason the habit sticks.

sections.heading: Mapping topics onto papers
paragraphs: Revision almost always follows the textbook, which is the order the content was taught rather than the order the examination uses. A more useful map runs the other way: start from the paper, work out which topics appear in it and in what style, and revise in that structure.

The reason this matters is that question style varies by component more than families expect. A multiple-choice paper rewards breadth and elimination technique. A structured theory paper rewards depth and written mechanism on a narrower set of topics. A practical-style paper rewards method critique and data handling regardless of topic. A student who revises content uniformly across all of them spends the same effort on everything and prepares properly for none of it.

Building the map takes one session and a past paper. Go through a recent paper, list every topic that appears, note the style of question it appeared as, and compare that against the student's own confidence list. The mismatches are the revision plan. Topics that appear frequently and in demanding styles get the time; topics that appear rarely and in simple styles do not.

The table is a worked example of the shape rather than a syllabus listing. Build your own from your own papers, because the frequency pattern depends on the code and the series. It is also worth repeating the exercise once in the autumn and once about eight weeks before the papers, since the second pass is made against a student who has changed and will usually move two or three topics up or down the list.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do, materials and the permit
paragraphs: Three boundaries belong on a page that goes this far into assessment detail. The first is academic. A tutor may teach content, explain what a command term demands, work through past questions, mark answers against the published scheme and give written feedback on the student's own work. A tutor may never produce work that will be submitted, nor supply text for a student to copy. Where an IGCSE subject carries a coursework component, support means feedback on a draft the student has written.

The second is materials. No tutor should reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The correct approach is to reference the official source and link to it, which is why this page has no attachments and repeatedly asks the reader to confirm structures with their own centre. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material a malpractice exposure.

The third is who may teach, and it is checkable in exactly the way a syllabus code is. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee against it and a two-working-day completion time, which means a tutor who does not hold one has been stopped by neither cost nor delay. Eligibility is broad rather than restrictive, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so the amounts that circulate in parent groups here have no source behind them. Ask about the permit in the same conversation in which you ask whether a tutor teaches 0580 or 4MA1. Both answers take ten seconds, and a hesitation on either one is informative.

And one on claims. No tutor can promise a grade, because boundaries are set after a series on the basis of that series' papers. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the paper numbers
process.description: Ask the exams officer in writing for the awarding body, the syllabus code, the entry tier, the paper numbers and, for the sciences, whether the centre has entered the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Those five facts decide what is worth practising at all.

process.title: Bring a recent marked script
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis with no card details taken, and it is far more useful with a marked paper in front of it. The tutor classifies lost marks into content, method, command term and time, and writes it up. Most students find that the majority were method marks.

process.title: Drill the method before the content
process.description: Where the diagnosis says the knowledge is present, the first block is about how answers are written: working shown, intermediate values recorded, units carried, command terms matched. That is the cheapest grade movement available and it transfers to every subject.

process.title: Build the topic-to-paper map
process.description: One session with a past paper produces a list of which topics appear, in what style, and how often, compared against the student's own confidence. The mismatches are the revision plan, which is a better plan than the textbook order.

process.title: Fix the slot and protect it
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, starting as early as the Khuzam school run allows and ending before Maghrib rather than against it. One weekly slot that never moves builds more across a term than three that are cancelled twice a month.

whyPoints.title: Codes before claims
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610 and 0500; Pearson 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the entire seven-page competitor area cluster researched for this project, which is why this page leads with them.

whyPoints.title: Method marks taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: A mark scheme credits identifiable steps rather than correct answers, so a student who shows method on a wrong answer can outscore one who writes a right answer bare. Teaching that habit is the fastest grade movement available in any IGCSE subject.

whyPoints.title: Grade scales and the equivalency floor, stated correctly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge reports A* to G and Pearson 9 to 1, and the Ministry's British-track requirement is five subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure; the published rule is five.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer on practical science
whyPoints.description: Where the centre enters the alternative-to-practical paper, the assessment is entirely written and a shared screen suits it better than a bench. Where a practical test is entered, lab work happens at school and tuition contributes the recording, the uncertainty and the write-up.

whyPoints.title: Supply treated honestly in a small emirate
whyPoints.description: The local pool in Ras Al Khaimah is weighted towards the most widely taught subjects. Teaching over live video replaces a drive into the city cluster with a subject panel, which matters most for the codes nobody locally has taught.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on materials and claims
whyPoints.description: No syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes supplied as downloads; the official source is linked instead. No promised grades, no self-published ratings, and no claim of approval from any regulator or awarding body.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal for preparation. The number of papers differs, practical skills are assessed differently, the tier structures are not the same, and the grade scales differ: Cambridge reports A* to G while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1. Past-paper practice does not transfer in either direction, so a family working from the wrong board's material is preparing conscientiously for an examination their child will not sit. Ask the exams officer in writing for the board and every syllabus code.

faqs.question: Can a right answer still score one mark out of five?
faqs.answer: Because a mark scheme credits identifiable steps rather than correct answers. On a five-mark multi-step question the scheme typically allocates marks for a correct method, a correct intermediate value, and the final answer with its unit. A student who does it mentally and writes one number can score one mark out of five while being entirely correct, and a student who shows the method and makes a final arithmetic slip can score four. Across a paper that difference is a grade.

faqs.question: Has Cambridge changed the Mathematics 0580 papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge revised the 0580 assessment structure, and the current pattern includes a non-calculator paper in each route alongside a calculator paper. That matters because many students have learned to route every calculation through a device, and hand algebra, surds, factorising and fraction arithmetic are a different skill. Confirm the current paper pattern with your exams officer rather than relying on any website, including this page, because structures are revised and old material circulates freely.

faqs.question: What does the Core route in Cambridge 0580 actually cap?
faqs.answer: It covers a reduced content list and is capped below the top grades, and that cap cannot be lifted after entries close. There is a genuine argument for the lower route: a student entered above their level meets questions they cannot attempt for a year, loses confidence and often ends below where the lower route would have placed them. The mistake is not choosing it, but choosing it without knowing what it closes at post-16 level, which in Ras Al Khaimah is a narrower market than in Dubai.

faqs.question: How do I find out which practical route my child's centre entered?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer directly, because it is a centre decision rather than a student one. Cambridge science candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and the two examine different things. The alternative paper is entirely about reading somebody else's experiment: controlled variables, flaws in a method, reading a scale, plotting and interpreting results. The practical test is about handling apparatus under timed conditions, which has to be practised with school equipment.

faqs.question: With the lab at school, what can a screen-based tutor add in the sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arguably better than a tutor at a kitchen table. Everything that paper examines is written: identifying what was controlled, spotting a flaw in a method, reading a scale correctly, plotting results, interpreting a trend and suggesting an improvement. Those skills are taught with the paper on a shared screen, annotated live and kept afterwards. Where a practical test is entered instead, the laboratory work happens at school and tuition contributes the recording, uncertainty and write-up.

faqs.question: Which topics genuinely deserve the most revision time?
faqs.answer: Build the map from a past paper rather than from the textbook. Go through a recent paper, list every topic that appears and the style of question it appeared as, then compare that against your child's own confidence list. The mismatches are the plan. In practice electricity and waves in Physics, moles and stoichiometry in Chemistry, and algebraic manipulation in Mathematics absorb the most time in most plans, because they appear frequently and in demanding styles.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does UAE equivalency actually need?
faqs.answer: Five, on the British track, at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. That precision matters because a competitor page ranking for these queries states that six subjects are required. Confirm your own case with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation channel; no tutoring provider performs or underwrites the process.

faqs.question: My child writes well in English but scores mid-band. Why?
faqs.answer: Because fluency and mark-earning are different things. The reading responses reward analysis of how a passage works, what the writer is doing with structure, word choice and tone, and students retell the passage instead. On the writing side the task is prescriptive: a directed writing task has an audience, a purpose and a form, and ignoring them costs content marks that quality of prose cannot recover. The repair is to rewrite one paragraph of an existing answer to deliver what the task actually demanded.

faqs.question: Is listening practice really worth session time in 0510?
faqs.answer: Yes, because it is the component students neglect on the assumption it is passive. The listening paper runs at exam speed with no pauses, and a student who has only practised with a finger on the pause button is practising a different task. Short, frequent, full-speed practice with the transcript checked afterwards is the method that works. Writing in 0510 is also marked on content and language separately, so register and task conventions cost content marks independently of fluency.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix a method-mark habit?
faqs.answer: Usually a fortnight to change how a student writes and six to eight weeks for it to show reliably under exam pressure. The teaching method is to use the student's own old answers: cover the marks awarded, have them predict where the scheme would have given credit, then compare. The discovery that most of their lost marks were available rather than unknown is uncomfortable, which is precisely why the habit sticks once it lands.

faqs.question: Is there a tutor in Ras Al Khaimah who has taught my child's code?
faqs.answer: For Mathematics and the sciences at the commonest codes, often yes. For less widely taught subjects, Additional Mathematics, or a code entered privately, the local pool thins quickly, because the emirate's private-school set is small and concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab. Teaching over live video replaces a drive into the city cluster with a subject panel, so the question becomes who has taught the code rather than who lives near Khuzam.

faqs.question: Should we practise with papers from older series?
faqs.answer: Selectively, and with one caution. Older papers are useful for content practice and for building volume, but where a board has revised an assessment structure the older papers may not match the format your child will sit, which is currently a live issue in Cambridge Mathematics. Use the most recent series for format and timing practice, and older ones for topic drilling. Work from material the student legitimately holds through their school rather than from files passed around.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do with an IGCSE coursework component?
faqs.answer: Teach the underlying content, explain what the assessment criteria demand, discuss structure, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may never write, redraft or complete the work, nor supply text for a student to paste in. That boundary is the same across every board, and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student rather than on whoever sold the help. Ask any provider what they will not do, and expect a clear answer.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach IGCSE in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-khuza.closingHeading: Send the code; bring a marked script
ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-khuza.closingBody: Two things make the first session useful. The awarding body, syllabus code, entry tier, paper numbers and the centre's practical route, requested in writing from your exams officer. And a recent marked script, so the tutor can classify where the marks actually went: content, method, command term or time. The session is free and no card details are taken. Most Khuzam families discover the majority of their lost marks were method marks, which is the cheapest thing in the subject to fix. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: An IGCSE is a twenty-month project that most families manage for eight weeks of it
paragraphs: The structure of a two-year IGCSE course is known before it starts. Year 10 introduces most of the content. Year 11 finishes it, runs the mocks, and delivers the papers. The entry decisions, including tier, happen between those two points. Nothing about that sequence is hidden, and yet the overwhelming majority of tutoring enquiries arrive in the last twelve weeks, when the cheapest and most effective interventions have already expired.

This page is an attempt to say what each term is good for, because the same money spent at different points in the project buys very different things. A block in the autumn of Year 10 can change which tier a child is entered for, which changes the grade ceiling for the whole qualification. A block in the spring of Year 11 can recover technique marks and improve pacing. Both are worthwhile. Only one of them can change what the student is allowed to achieve. Families who understand that difference spend less and get more, which is the only genuinely useful thing a page like this can tell them.

The fixed external points are published. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in three windows. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and in November, publishing a provisional timetable ahead of each series and a final one closer to it. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and schools set an internal cut-off earlier still. One correction while we are here: Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so no candidate in Ras Al Khaimah sits it.

The post-results part of the calendar is the piece nobody writes about, and it is genuinely useful. Results arrive, and then there is a short window in which a school can request a review of marking on a candidate's behalf. Those windows are tight, they are administered through the centre rather than the family, and a parent who does not know they exist discovers them after they have closed. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the review window opened and closed inside the weeks that followed.

Finally the delivery question, since the URL says home tutor. IB Gram teaches Mina Al Arab students one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not place a tutor at a UAE address; in-person visiting is a service we run only in India. For a twenty-month plan that format matters practically rather than philosophically: a plan spanning two academic years, a summer, several trips abroad and a Ramadan survives when it does not depend on anybody driving down the coast road at five o'clock.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-mina-.programmesIntro: Four stages sit inside a twenty-month IGCSE project and its approaches. Each has a term where support is cheap and effective, and a term where it is expensive and marginal.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The streaming years. Checkpoint tests run in three windows and schools use them to decide who is pointed towards Core and who towards Extended. Content is light; the four habits that matter are algebraic rearrangement, unit discipline, reading data from a graph and writing a conclusion that refers to the evidence. A Year 9 student without those will meet the gap again in Year 10 science, and by then it costs more to close.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah, where schools run fewer parallel sets than in Dubai, a Year 9 placement is harder to revise later simply because there may be nowhere to move to. Ask in Year 9 which tier the school expects, and what evidence would change it.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10
programmes.description: Most of the content is introduced here and almost nobody buys tutoring. That is the inefficiency this page is about. Work in Year 10 is cheap because there is no deadline pressure, it compounds because the content is foundational, and it generates the evidence a school needs if a tier decision should be revised. Subjects with heavy cumulative structure, chiefly mathematics and the sciences, benefit most.
programmes.countryNote: For a Mina Al Arab family the practical Year 10 move is a short diagnostic block in the autumn term, then targeted work on whatever it reveals. Two named gaps closed in Year 10 are worth more than eight weeks of general revision in Year 11.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11
programmes.description: Content completion, mocks, entries and the papers. Tier is confirmed at the entry deadline and the ceiling closes with it. Support here is technique, pacing, command terms and the three or four topics costing the most marks, diagnosed from a marked mock. Effective and worth doing, but working inside limits set the previous year rather than resetting them.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm the centre's Cambridge timetable zone before designing the final fortnight. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, says it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The destination that gives the tier decision its weight. AS sciences and A Level Mathematics assume Extended-tier fluency, and entry requirements are stated in grades, so a ceiling set by a Core entry can close a route two years before anyone examines it. The first term of AS Chemistry revisits moles and bonding at a depth that exposes any gap within weeks.
programmes.countryNote: Where continuing locally is not possible, a change of school or a longer commute becomes part of the plan, and that is a Year 10 conversation. Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track also expects one A Level at grade E or better, or two AS Levels at the same grade.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-mina-.subjectsIntro: Each subject has a term in which tutoring is cheap and effective. These are the IGCSE courses Ras Al Khaimah families ask about, with the right moment to start each one.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most cumulative subject on the timetable and therefore the one where early work compounds hardest. A gap in indices or rearrangement in Year 10 reappears in trigonometry, in algebraic fractions and in every science. Start in the autumn of Year 10 if you are starting anywhere.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Needs 0580 Extended to be solid before it is useful, so it is the one subject where starting too early is possible. The right window is the second half of Year 10 into the first term of Year 11, once algebra is automatic rather than effortful.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity rewards early work because it is conceptually awkward and taught once. The alternative-to-practical paper, by contrast, is a late-term target: it tests precise method writing, which is a skill that can be installed in six sessions whenever they happen.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic belongs in Year 10, because everything quantitative afterwards depends on it. Qualitative analysis is the opposite: pure recall, cheapest to secure in the final weeks, and the first thing to drill when a family arrives late.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty, so it tolerates a late start better than any other science. A structured eight-week programme on terminology and mark-scheme wording works. Starting earlier still is better, but biology is the subject least damaged by waiting.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Has its own content list and its own exclusions, so the first task in any term is confirming the code and building the past-paper plan from it. Revising from single-science material is the recurring waste here and it costs weeks nobody has.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Improves on a slow curve, which makes it a Year 10 subject. One piece of the student's own writing marked properly each fortnight across two years moves a grade more reliably than any intensive block. Reading marks, not vocabulary, are where the grade sits.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Often needed later as evidence of English proficiency. Listening and reading respond to technique quickly; writing to a set register and word count takes longer. Start the writing work early and leave the listening drill for the final term.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram-led and learnable from scratch inside one year, which makes it the most forgiving option subject on this list. The marks sit in accurate diagrams and in evaluation that weighs rather than restates, and both can be taught in a six-week block.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Second Language (Cambridge 0508 / 0544)
subjects.description: Taught alongside the licensed curriculum, since the federal baseline covers Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies for every private school. Support works with the school's own material, because using different or additional content without ministry permission is not allowed.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village
regions.note: A gated community to the south with a campus inside it, so parents hear about assessments early and informally. Families here tend to make contact in Year 10, which is the term when contact is most useful.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Apartment-heavy and resort-oriented, with a high share of households who travel through the summer. A two-year plan here needs to assume interruption rather than hope for continuity, which online delivery handles and in-person arrangements do not.

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: The central district with most of the emirate's schools. Mock windows arrive earliest here because the larger schools run tighter internal assessment cycles, so a Year 11 spring plan has less runway than it looks.

regions.name: Khuzam
regions.note: Inland and close to the city, with short school runs. Early study evenings make it the easiest cluster for two short weekly sessions sustained across a whole academic year rather than one intensive term.

regions.name: Al Dhait
regions.note: Established inland villa districts where a parent is often commuting south. Supervised study shifts later, which matters less for a Year 10 plan built on consistency than for a Year 11 plan built on timed papers.

regions.name: Al Qusaidat and Julphar
regions.note: Older districts near the creek with the emirate's heaviest late-afternoon traffic. Any arrangement requiring arrival slips here, and a slipped session in a mock fortnight is a lost session rather than a late one.

regions.name: Al Mamourah and Seih Al Uraibi
regions.note: Lower-density areas with small school-age populations, so group revision at a single subject and tier does not assemble. One-to-one across two years is the only format that genuinely exists here.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-mina-.modesIntro: Over twenty months a family will usually want two of these three, not all of them, and the choice depends on which year the plan starts in.

modes.title: Year 10 foundation block
modes.description: A short diagnostic followed by targeted work on two named gaps, usually a fortnightly hour rather than a weekly one. Cheap, low-pressure and compounding, because the content being secured is the foundation everything in Year 11 is built on. It also generates the evidence a school needs if a tier decision deserves revisiting.

modes.title: Sustained fortnightly across both years
modes.description: The quiet option almost nobody chooses and the one that works best in English and mathematics. One hour a fortnight for twenty months, with the student's own written work marked each time. Low total cost, high total hours, and improvement on the curve those subjects actually move on rather than in a spike.

modes.title: Year 11 run-in
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week for six to ten weeks, built from timed past-paper sections marked to the published scheme, with a taper in the final fortnight. The familiar format, and effective within its limits: it recovers technique marks and improves pacing, but it works inside a tier decision made the previous year.

sections.heading: Which term each subject actually needs
paragraphs: Tutoring is usually bought by urgency and should be bought by subject structure. A cumulative subject, where each topic depends on the last, rewards early work enormously because the alternative is building on sand for eighteen months. A recall-heavy subject rewards late work, because the knowledge needs to be fresh on the day and securing it a year early wastes most of the benefit. Mathematics is the first kind. Qualitative analysis in chemistry is the second.

The table below assigns a window to each subject and says why. The column that matters is the last one: what it costs to start later than the recommended term. In mathematics the cost is compounding, which is why a Year 10 gap in rearrangement reappears in trigonometry, in algebraic fractions, in the physics equations and in every graph question for two years. In biology the cost is close to nothing, because the subject is volume rather than dependency and an eight-week programme can still cover it.

That difference should change how a family spends. A household in Mina Al Arab with a budget for sixty tutoring hours across two years will get far more from forty of them in Year 10 mathematics and twenty in a Year 11 biology run-in than from sixty hours spread evenly across both subjects in the spring of Year 11. The arithmetic is unglamorous and it is the single largest efficiency available in this market.

It also changes the conversation about tier. A student who closes two mathematics gaps in the autumn of Year 10 and then performs on Extended-tier questions has produced exactly the evidence a school needs to reconsider an entry decision. That is a specific, finite piece of work with a defined output, and it is worth more than any amount of general support later, because it alters the ceiling rather than the performance under it.

sections.heading: What a Year 10 family can still change, and a Year 11 family cannot
paragraphs: This is the section families wish they had read a year earlier. Some decisions have windows, and the windows close in order. A frank list of what is still available at each point does more for a household than any amount of reassurance, and it is not a list anyone selling tutoring usually publishes, because most of the items on it reduce how much tutoring a family needs to buy.

In Year 9 and early Year 10, nearly everything is open: subject choices, tier expectation, set placement, and whether to add Additional Mathematics. In the middle of Year 10, subject choices have firmed but tier is still genuinely movable with evidence. By the entry deadline in Year 11, tier is fixed and the grade ceiling with it. After the papers, the only remaining levers are a review of marking inside a short window and a November resit.

The practical consequence is that the value of a tutoring hour declines across the project while its price does not. An hour in October of Year 10 can contribute to a decision worth two grades. An hour in April of Year 11 can recover technique marks inside a fixed ceiling. Both are real; they are not equivalent, and the family paying the same rate for each deserves to know which they are buying.

The table states each window with the action that is still possible and the one that is no longer. The most useful line for most readers is the one about tier evidence in the middle of Year 10, because it describes work that is short, specific, and consequential, and it is almost never bought.

sections.heading: The private-candidate route, and the centre problem
paragraphs: Some families on this coast need a subject the school does not offer, or need to sit a qualification outside a school altogether. That is the private-candidate route, and the teaching side of it works perfectly well. The administrative side is where it fails, and it fails for one reason: the examination seat. A candidate needs a centre willing to accept external candidates, and that arrangement has to exist before the entry deadline rather than being discovered after it.

The sequence runs in an order that surprises people. Find the centre first. Confirm which subjects and which boards it will accept external entries for, because a centre offering Cambridge may not accept Pearson entries and may not run every component. Establish what it charges and when it needs the entry. Only then plan the teaching, because a flawless year of preparation with no seat in an examination room produces nothing at all.

There are components that complicate it further. Subjects with speaking tests, practical arrangements or coursework may be unavailable to private candidates at some centres, or available only in specific configurations. That is the question to ask early and in writing. A family who assumes the component will be fine and discovers in the spring that it cannot be assessed has lost the series, not the component.

For a Mina Al Arab household the realistic version is that the centre conversation happens in the city, in the autumn, with the examinations officer of a school willing to take external entries. It is an administrative task with a deadline, not an academic one, and it should sit on the household calendar well before any teaching plan is built around it.

sections.heading: Results day and the fortnight after it
paragraphs: Most writing about IGCSE stops at the exam. The weeks after results are a live part of the calendar with real options in them, and they are compressed. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. The centre receiving results a day before the candidates is not a quirk; it is how the system works, and it means the school is the party with the information and the authority.

Two things can happen in the window that follows. A school can request a review of marking where there is reason to think a script has been marked inconsistently, and the deadlines for that are short and administered through the centre. A family cannot submit one directly; it goes through the examinations officer, which is why knowing the window exists is the whole of the advantage. The second option is a November entry, which for Pearson delivered results to students on 22 January 2026 in the most recent completed cycle.

Both decisions need the same input, and it is an input a family can prepare in advance: a clear view of which grade is blocking which route. A grade that is disappointing but sufficient needs no action. A grade that closes a specific AS Level course or sits below a stated entry requirement is worth asking the school about immediately, in the first days rather than the second week.

The table lays out the sequence. The useful habit it encourages is deciding in advance what each outcome would mean, so that results day is a confirmation rather than a scramble. Families who have done that act inside the windows. Families who have not generally find out about them afterwards, from someone else's conversation at the school gates.

sections.heading: Clashes, double paper days and the fortnight that breaks students
paragraphs: In the examination fortnight the problem stops being knowledge and becomes stamina and sequencing. A candidate with nine subjects will meet days with two papers, consecutive days with heavy papers, and gaps of four days in the middle where the temptation is to do nothing. None of that is visible when a revision plan is written in February from a generic timetable, and all of it is visible once the correct zone timetable is in front of you.

This is the practical reason the zone check matters beyond the risk of missing a paper altogether. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable per zone, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone. A revision plan sequenced against the wrong version has the student peaking for the wrong subject on the wrong day, which is a silent failure rather than a dramatic one.

With the right timetable, the planning is simple and worth an hour. Mark the double days and reduce the revision load the evening before them. Identify the longest gap and plan what goes in it, because an unplanned four-day gap in the middle of a fortnight is where confidence drains. Put the subjects with the heaviest recall load, qualitative analysis in chemistry for example, immediately before their papers rather than two weeks earlier.

The last piece is the thing families most often get wrong: the final evening before a paper should be short and light. Students who revise late into the night before an early paper lose more to fatigue than they gain from the extra hour, and the effect is largest on exactly the long structured papers where marks are most available. Writing that rule down in advance, as part of the plan, is what makes it survive the week.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the summer and the real Ras Al Khaimah year
paragraphs: A twenty-month plan has to survive two summers, at least one Ramadan and a quantity of travel. Private schools here teach the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the licensed international curriculum, since the federal baseline covers Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, so the timetable is fuller than the exam entries suggest and the homework load is heavier than a comparison with a British school implies.

Ramadan shortens school hours and moves concentration either early or well after sunset. The arrangement that holds is planned rather than improvised: sessions move after Iftar and shorten to around 45 minutes, which protects focus better than a full hour at the wrong time. For a Year 11 candidate whose run-in overlaps Ramadan, deciding this in advance is worth three or four weeks of effective preparation.

The summer between Year 10 and Year 11 is the other asset nobody uses. It is not a time for new content, but a fortnight on whichever two gaps the Year 10 assessments exposed, done in the morning with no deadline pressure, changes the autumn term substantially. Households in Mina Al Arab and on Al Marjan Island travel heavily in those weeks, which is precisely why an arrangement that continues from anywhere with a connection is worth more here than one requiring a doorstep.

Put it together and the twenty months have a shape that any family can run without buying a thing. Fix the four habits in Year 9. Diagnose in the autumn of Year 10 and close two gaps. Use the summer on whatever remains. Confirm entries, tier and the zone timetable in the autumn of Year 11. Diagnose from the mock, run eight focused weeks, then taper. Know the review-of-marking window before results arrive. That sequence is the plan; a tutor is one of the tools inside it.

sections.heading: Where the money gets wasted in this market
paragraphs: Published rates in the UAE tutoring market, read in October 2026, run like this. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students or recent graduates, is advertised from AED 45-65 by EdFlik and from AED 33-52 by Tutopiya. Qualified subject tutors online run roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Named IGCSE and A Level specialists are published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, and examiner-led premium work at AED 650 by BartyED. In-home one-to-one visits sit at roughly AED 180-350 on Bestimate's table and up to AED 500 from independent tutors. Every one of those is the provider's own figure, not ours.

The waste in this market is not usually the hourly rate. It is the timing and the format. A household that buys forty hours of general support in the spring of Year 11 at AED 200 an hour has spent a substantial sum inside a fixed grade ceiling, on a plan diagnosed from a parent's impression rather than from a marked script. The same money placed in the autumn of Year 10, on two named gaps, with the tier decision still live, buys something structurally different.

The second source of waste is the two-hour in-home block, which exists because a two-hour visit justifies a drive rather than because two hours is a good unit for a fifteen-year-old. Market monthly packages make the difference visible: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Twice the money for half as many contacts, and the second hour of a double session is routinely worth much less than the first.

The third is buying hours without a target. A block that cannot be judged will not be stopped, which is how a six-week plan becomes a two-year subscription. Our position is a free trial lesson, then a block with a stated goal and an end date, then a review against marked evidence. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page and no price in a currency Ras Al Khaimah families do not transact in; two of the pages competing for this search quote US dollars, and three publish no price at all.

process.title: Tell us which year the student is in, first
process.description: Year 10 autumn and Year 11 spring are different projects with different ceilings, and the recommendation changes completely between them. We would rather talk you out of an expensive late block and into a cheap early one than the other way round.

process.title: Send the most recent assessments or the marked mock
process.description: In Year 10 that means school assessments and classwork; in Year 11 it means the mock script. Either way the evidence shows whether the problem is a foundation gap, a technique habit or pacing, and those need different work at different costs.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a term-by-term plan
process.description: One 45 to 60-minute one-to-one session over live video, no card details, no obligation. What follows names the subject, the window, the number of sessions and what will have changed at the end. A plan without those four things is a standing order.

process.title: Confirm the administration while the teaching runs
process.description: Entry deadline and tier with the examinations officer, the centre's Cambridge timetable zone, and a private-candidate centre where one is needed. None of that is academic work and all of it can sink a good year if it is left to the spring.

process.title: Know the post-results window before results arrive
process.description: Ask the school in advance how a review of marking is requested and what the deadline is. The window is short, it runs through the centre rather than the family, and the parents who use it are the ones who knew about it in July.

whyPoints.title: Advice that reduces what you need to buy
whyPoints.description: Most of this page describes things a family can do without a tutor: fix four habits in Year 9, diagnose in Year 10, confirm the zone timetable, know the review window. We would rather be the provider that said so than the one that sold sixty hours in the spring of Year 11.

whyPoints.title: Subject structure, not urgency, decides the plan
whyPoints.description: Mathematics compounds and rewards early work; biology is volume and tolerates a late start; qualitative analysis is recall and is cheapest in the final weeks. Spending by structure rather than by panic is the single largest efficiency available in this market.

whyPoints.title: The administration treated as part of the job
whyPoints.description: Entry deadline, tier, board, timetable zone, and a private-candidate centre where one is needed. These are the things that silently cost a series, and they are checked in week one of a plan rather than discovered in the spring.

whyPoints.title: A plan that survives two summers and a Ramadan

faqs.question: Should a Mina Al Arab family hire a tutor in Year 10 or wait for the mocks?
faqs.answer: For mathematics and the sciences, yes, and it is the cheapest decision in the whole project. Year 10 work has no deadline pressure attached to it, it compounds because the content is foundational, and it produces the evidence a school needs if a tier decision should be revisited. An hour in October of Year 10 can contribute to a decision worth two grades. An hour in April of Year 11 recovers technique marks inside a ceiling that was already fixed. Both are useful; they are not equivalent.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject is most damaged by starting tutoring late?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, because it is the most cumulative subject on the timetable. A gap in indices or algebraic rearrangement does not stay local: it reappears in trigonometry, in algebraic fractions, in every physics equation and in every graph question, for two years. First Language English is the second, for a different reason - writing improves on a slow curve and cannot be compressed into a run-in. Biology is the most forgiving, because it is volume rather than dependency and eight structured weeks can still cover it.

faqs.question: How does my child sit an IGCSE subject the school does not teach?
faqs.answer: As a private candidate, and the first task is the examination seat rather than the teaching. You need a centre willing to accept external entries for that board and that subject, confirmed in writing, with its fees and its deadline, before any teaching plan is built. Ask specifically about speaking tests, practical arrangements and coursework components, because some centres cannot assess them externally. A flawless year of preparation with no seat in an examination room produces no grade at all.

faqs.question: Can we ask for a paper to be remarked if a grade looks wrong?
faqs.answer: A review of marking is requested by the school on the candidate's behalf, inside a short window after results, not by the family directly. That is why knowing the window exists is the whole advantage: Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the review deadlines fall in the weeks after. Ask your examinations officer in July how the process works at your centre, so that in August you are making a request rather than learning the rules.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer between Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: Rest, mostly, then spend about a fortnight on whichever two gaps the Year 10 assessments exposed. Morning sessions, no deadline pressure, two named topics rather than general revision. It is not a time for new content and it should not be a programme. Households in Mina Al Arab and on Al Marjan Island travel heavily in those weeks, which is one practical reason our sessions run over live video: a plan that continues from anywhere beats one that stops at the airport.

faqs.question: When is the tier decision actually final?
faqs.answer: At the entry deadline in Year 11, which sits months before the papers with a school cut-off earlier still. Until that point a tier can be moved with evidence. After it, the grade ceiling is fixed: a Core entry in Mathematics 0580 caps the achievable grade at a 5 on the 9-1 scale regardless of how the paper is sat. If you think your child is entered below their capability, the useful work is a short block producing Extended-tier performance on real questions, done before the deadline rather than argued after it.

faqs.question: How should the examination fortnight itself be planned?
faqs.answer: From the correct zone timetable, an hour of work, done in advance. Mark the days with two papers and reduce the load the evening before them. Identify the longest gap and decide what goes in it, because an unplanned four-day gap is where confidence drains. Place recall-heavy topics such as qualitative analysis immediately before their paper rather than a fortnight earlier. And write down that the final evening is short and light, because that rule only survives the week if it was agreed before it.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge timetable zone matter for revision rather than just for dates?
faqs.answer: Because sequencing depends on it. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A plan sequenced against the wrong version has a student peaking for the wrong subject on the wrong day, which is a quiet failure rather than an obvious one. Ask your examinations officer.

faqs.question: Is fortnightly tutoring across two years better than weekly for one term?
faqs.answer: In English and mathematics, often yes, and it usually costs less in total. One hour a fortnight for twenty months, with a piece of the student's own work marked every session, matches the curve those subjects actually improve on. It also survives travel and Ramadan because the cadence is loose enough to absorb a missed week. Intensive blocks suit technique problems and recall subjects. Slow-curve subjects suit slow cadence, and almost nobody buys them that way.

faqs.question: Does a November entry make sense for a single weak subject?
faqs.answer: It is the case where November genuinely earns its place. One grade blocking a specific route, with everything else settled, is a narrow repair job well suited to a six-to-eight-week block over the summer and early autumn. The constraint is timing: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so the grade exists in January, after many application deadlines. Decide it with the school before the entry deadline rather than treating it as something to consider once results disappoint.

faqs.question: How do we keep a two-year plan going through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: By moving it rather than pausing it. School hours shorten, concentration shifts either early or well after sunset, and a mid-afternoon slot that worked all year stops working. Sessions move after Iftar and shorten to around 45 minutes, which holds focus better than a full hour at the wrong time. Arrange it before the month begins. For a Year 11 candidate whose run-in overlaps Ramadan, that single planning decision is worth three or four weeks of effective preparation.

faqs.question: Our school's mocks are early. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and usually in your favour. Larger schools in Ras Al Khaimah city tend to run tighter internal assessment cycles, so the mock lands sooner and the diagnostic information arrives with more runway. The risk is treating an early mock as a dress rehearsal for which nothing has been covered yet, which produces a demoralising grade and little information. Ask what the mock covers, make sure the script comes home marked, and build the eight-week plan from the distribution of lost marks.

faqs.question: Do we need to confirm the board as well as the tier?
faqs.answer: Yes, from the statement of entry rather than the textbook, because schools change board between cohorts. The board determines paper structure, mark-scheme wording and the syllabus code past papers must come from: Cambridge 0620 against Pearson 4CH1, Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1. Some Pearson courses also run modularly, with units banked across sittings, which changes the whole shape of a revision plan. A tutor working from the wrong code is teaching a similar subject rather than the one your child sits.

faqs.question: Why teach Mina Al Arab students online rather than visiting?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, one practical and one about supply. A twenty-month plan spans two summers, a Ramadan and a good deal of travel, and an arrangement that depends on someone arriving at a gate does not survive them. And Ras Al Khaimah has a comparatively small private-school sector, so the number of people here who have taught your child's exact subject and tier to an examination class is small and mostly committed. IB Gram does not place tutors at UAE addresses; in-person visiting is a service we run only in India.

intro.heading: Seih Al Uraibi, Al Nakheel, Al Dhait: the same search, the same answer
paragraphs: Parents in Seih Al Uraibi rarely search once. They search for an IGCSE home tutor in Seih Al Uraibi, then they search Al Nakheel, then Al Dhait, then Khuzam, on the theory that one of those districts must have more teachers in it. It is a reasonable theory and it is wrong, and the reason it is wrong is worth setting out plainly before anything else on this page.

Ras Al Khaimah is a small private-school market. The emirate's international schools cluster in three places: the Indian and British campuses behind the city centre, the RAK Academy campuses at Al Hamra and Khuzam, and a handful of standalone schools serving the villa districts. The teachers in those staff rooms are the local tutoring pool, and almost all of them are already teaching a full timetable. Spread that pool across Cambridge and Pearson, across Core and Extended tiers, and across eleven or twelve subjects, and the number of people within driving distance of Seih Al Uraibi who have actually marked IGCSE Physics 0625 Paper 4 to a mark scheme is very small. In two or three subjects it is zero.

Moving your search one district over does not change that arithmetic. Al Nakheel has more apartment blocks and a slightly larger school cohort, but it draws on the same staff rooms. Al Dhait is further inland and adds commuting time to the same list of names. Al Hamra Village has the IB continuum campuses and therefore more Diploma teachers, which does nothing for an IGCSE Chemistry problem. The comparison that parents keep running between neighbourhoods returns the same shortlist with the travel figures rearranged.

What does change the arithmetic is removing distance from the problem. If the tutor does not need to reach Al Uraibi at all, your shortlist stops being everyone within a twenty-minute drive and becomes everyone who teaches that paper. That is the whole of IB Gram's case here. Lessons are one-to-one, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and pretending otherwise on a Ras Al Khaimah page would be a promise nobody could keep.

The rest of this page is the comparison you were going to run anyway, done properly: what the districts around Seih Al Uraibi actually offer, what tutoring costs across this market in AED, how an in-home hour compares with an online hour once travel is priced in, and the two exam timetables a RAK family has to track. Every figure carries its source. Nothing on this page is an IB Gram price list. Read it as a decision aid rather than a brochure: if the conclusion does not fit your child, the figures are still yours to use elsewhere, and the sources are named so you can check every one of them yourself.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-seih-.programmesIntro: An IGCSE search in Ras Al Khaimah normally covers three stages of the same British-curriculum route: the lower secondary years that feed into it, the two IGCSE years themselves, and the post-16 choice that follows. Each needs different work from a tutor.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary (Years 7-9)
programmes.description: The three years before option blocks are chosen. There is no external exam, so weak algebra, weak written structure and weak practical technique travel forward invisibly. The repair work in Year 10 is almost always Year 8 content: fractions and indices in maths, rearranging formulae in science, paragraph control in English. Tutoring at this stage is cheap compared with the Year 11 version of the same problem.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah city the Year 9 to Year 10 step is where most families first look for help, because cohorts in the Indian and British campuses behind the city centre are large enough that individual attention thins out. A Seih Al Uraibi student who was comfortable at Year 8 can arrive in Year 10 with a fast-moving Extended syllabus and no spare teacher time.

programmes.name: International GCSE (Years 10-11)
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined entirely at the end on papers set by Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel. Each subject has its own paper structure, its own tiering, and its own command-term vocabulary. Grades are reported 9-1 or A*-G depending on board and subject, and the grade on the certificate is what MoE equivalency and university admissions read.
programmes.countryNote: RAK schools run a mixture of boards, and families often do not know which one their child is entered for until the statement of entry arrives. That document carries the syllabus code. Getting it right matters in Seih Al Uraibi as much as in Dubai: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different papers with different formula sheets, and a tutor coaching the wrong one wastes the term.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma routes after Year 11
programmes.description: IGCSE grades decide which post-16 subjects a student can take. Most A Level science and maths courses expect a grade 6 or 7 at IGCSE in the same subject, and the IB Diploma expects comparable attainment for Higher Level. A near-miss in Year 11 closes doors that were open in Year 10, which is the practical argument for intervening early rather than after results day.
programmes.countryNote: For a Seih Al Uraibi family the post-16 choice frequently involves a journey. The IB continuum campuses sit at Al Hamra and Khuzam, so a Diploma route means a daily drive out of the city. Families who want A Levels in the city have fewer option blocks to choose from, which makes the Year 11 grade profile more decisive here than in a larger market.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the British curriculum
programmes.description: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. So an IGCSE student also carries Arabic, and Islamic Education where applicable, assessed on a separate internal calendar from the Cambridge or Pearson timetable.
programmes.countryNote: These subjects sit under the federal Ministry of Education framework in the northern emirates. For a Year 11 student in Seih Al Uraibi the clash is practical: Arabic assessments often land in the same fortnight as IGCSE mock papers, and the revision plan has to allow for both rather than discovering the overlap in week one of the mock window.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-home-tutor-in-seih-.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Ras Al Khaimah families ask about most, with the part of each syllabus where marks actually go missing. Board and code are named because the paper structure differs between them.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended candidates lose marks on functions, transformations of graphs, and the conditional-probability branches of tree diagrams. Pearson 4MA1 supplies a formula sheet Cambridge does not, so recall expectations differ. Method marks are available on almost every question, and most lost marks here are unshown working rather than wrong answers.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity is the standard failure point: series and parallel circuits, potential dividers, and the difference between potential difference across a component and current through it. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards experimental literacy rather than theory, and students who have never written a method with a named control variable lose those marks outright.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and the qualitative-analysis tables carry a disproportionate share of lost marks. Extended candidates also need electrolysis half-equations and the reactivity series applied rather than recited. Organic chemistry is usually fine on nomenclature and weak on reaction conditions, which is exactly what the longer-mark questions ask for.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Transport in plants, enzyme graphs and inheritance diagrams reward precise vocabulary, and examiners do not accept loose paraphrase for terms like osmosis or active transport. Six-mark questions need a structured answer with a stated mechanism, not a list of remembered facts.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The reading-comprehension exercises punish lifting whole sentences from the passage when the question asks for two specific details. Summary tasks have a word limit that is marked. The speaking component is assessed separately and students rarely practise it under timed conditions until the week before.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed-writing tasks are marked on register and audience as much as on content, and a student who writes a good essay instead of the requested letter caps their own mark. The analysis questions need quotation plus effect, in that order, with the effect expressed in terms of the reader rather than the writer's intention.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450 / Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study application is where grades separate. Students know the theory of cash flow and break-even and then answer in the abstract, when the mark scheme wants the numbers from the stimulus material used. Evaluation marks require a judgement with a stated condition, which is a skill that has to be taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455 / Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is non-negotiable: axes labelled, curves labelled, shifts drawn and the new equilibrium marked. Many candidates write competent prose around a diagram that earns nothing. The data-response questions reward reading the figures in the extract rather than importing a textbook example.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / Pearson 4CP0)
subjects.description: Pseudocode under timed conditions is the main gap, together with trace tables and the difference between validation and verification. Students who have coded in a real language often lose marks writing syntactically valid Python where the paper expects the board's own pseudocode conventions.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger candidates as a bridge to A Level. Calculus, logarithms and the binomial theorem appear at a depth 0580 never reaches, and the step up catches students who were comfortable with Extended maths. Local teaching capacity for this subject in the northern emirates is genuinely thin.

sections.heading: Seih Al Uraibi against the next district over: what actually differs
paragraphs: A parent comparing districts wants to know whether a different postcode produces a different shortlist. Across Ras Al Khaimah city it does not. The table below sets out the four variables that genuinely change between these neighbourhoods, and the one that does not.

What changes is travel. The run back from the city-centre campuses to Al Dhait is materially longer than the run to Seih Al Uraibi, and the run to Al Hamra Village is longer again. That difference decides what time a session can realistically start, and it decides how much an in-home tutor has to charge to make the evening worth their while. It is a real difference and it is worth pricing.

What does not change is the pool of people who have taught a particular IGCSE paper. Ras Al Khaimah's private schools draw their staff from the same labour market, the schools themselves are shared across all of these districts, and a Pearson 4CH1 specialist either lives in the emirate or does not. No amount of moving the search radius creates one. That is why the recommendation at the end of each row below is identical, and why the comparison a parent runs across six browser tabs returns one answer.

The sensible use of this table is not to pick a district. It is to see how much of the problem is distance and how much is supply, and then to stop paying for the part that online delivery removes for free.

sections.heading: Why the answer is the same whichever district you search
paragraphs: The arithmetic behind that table deserves to be spelled out, because it is the part no tutoring site will tell a parent. Start with the subject your child needs. Then narrow to the board: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. Then narrow to the tier, Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. Then narrow to the paper, because a tutor who is strong on 0580 Paper 2 and weak on Paper 4 is not the tutor you need for Extended. Then narrow to people free in the hour after your child's school day who are not already teaching it somewhere.

Each narrowing step cuts the list by more than half. In Dubai, which had 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 according to the Dubai Media Office, a list that starts in the thousands survives that process. In Ras Al Khaimah the list starts small. By the time you have specified Pearson 4PH1 Paper 2 and a 4.30pm slot, there may be nobody in the emirate who fits, and there is certainly nobody within fifteen minutes of every one of these districts.

This is the gap online delivery closes, and it closes it in one step. Remove the travel requirement and the final narrowing disappears. Your child's tutor needs to know the paper and be awake at the right hour on Gulf Standard Time, and that is a far larger group than the set of people willing to drive to Al Uraibi on a Tuesday. The tutor is matched to the statement of entry rather than to the map.

That is not a sales argument so much as a supply argument, and it applies with more force in the northern emirates than anywhere else in the UAE. A Dubai Marina parent trading in-home for online gains convenience. A Seih Al Uraibi parent trading in-home for online gains access to subjects that are not locally staffed at all.

paragraphs: Most competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. Here are the AED figures, attributed, so a Seih Al Uraibi parent can see where any quote they receive sits.

Read the table from the cheapest row down rather than from the premium end, because the cheap end is where most families start and where most of the disappointment happens. Budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 150 an hour buys a capable graduate who can explain content. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 on their own pages. At that level you are paying for someone to re-teach a topic, which is useful if the problem is that your child missed a fortnight of school and useless if the problem is that they cannot convert knowledge into marks under a mark scheme.

The qualified-subject-tutor band, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online, is where paper-level work becomes realistic. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The in-home band sits higher, AED 180 to 500 an hour, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home at AED 180 to 350 with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. Specialist exam-year tutors run AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase lists AED 270. The premium end, AED 500 to 650 and up, is quoted by BartyED at AED 650.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. These are market figures from the sources named, not IB Gram prices. Our own rate is confirmed in the consultation that follows the free trial lesson, with the format and the session length stated before anything is agreed.

sections.heading: An in-home hour against an online hour, priced honestly
paragraphs: Comparing formats only means something if the comparison includes what each one costs in time as well as money. For a family in Seih Al Uraibi the time cost of the in-home model is invisible on an invoice and significant in practice.

The in-home premium is not profit. It is the tutor's journey, and on a weekday evening in Ras Al Khaimah city that journey is twenty to forty minutes each way. A tutor charging AED 300 for a ninety-minute visit is being paid for closer to two and a half hours of their evening, which is why the per-hour figure sits above the online band for the same qualification. Nobody is overcharging; the travel is real and somebody pays for it.

What the premium buys is a person in the room. For a Year 7 student who needs supervision as much as teaching, that is worth paying for. For a Year 11 student who needs someone who has marked Extended papers to a scheme, it is the wrong thing to buy, because the money is going into a car journey instead of into subject expertise. IB Gram's position is stated plainly rather than hedged: there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and lessons for Seih Al Uraibi students are delivered one-to-one over live video.
