sections.heading: The two exam timetables a Ras Al Khaimah family tracks
paragraphs: A British-curriculum student in the UAE sits papers set by one of two boards, and their calendars are not the same. Knowing which one applies is the first thing a tutor should establish, and the statement of entry answers it.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. One point matters enormously for UAE families and is misreported constantly: the February and March sitting is offered to India only. A Ras Al Khaimah candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your child's school knows its zone; a tutor planning a revision schedule should ask.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Results timing is worth knowing in advance because it decides when a resit decision has to be made: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, and those can be revised, so a plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than against dates copied from a page like this one.

Counted backwards from a June series, the shape of the year is consistent: entries are confirmed by the school months in advance, mocks fall in the winter term, the final content coverage finishes in spring, and the last six to eight weeks are past papers under timed conditions. The table turns that into milestones. Dates for a specific series must always be checked against the board's own timetable page and your school's exams officer.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what it changes for you
paragraphs: Parents in the northern emirates often assume the Dubai rules they read about online apply to them. They do not, and the difference occasionally matters.

The UAE has five bodies regulating private schools. Dubai sits under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, which likewise regulates private education in the emirate. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in those three emirates.

For a Seih Al Uraibi family the relevant authority is the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge. Its remit is broader than inspection: the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So curriculum and fee decisions at your child's school pass through the emirate regulator, not only through the school's own management. If you are comparing a RAK school with a Sharjah or Dubai one, you are comparing schools under different authorities with different published reports.

One caution belongs here because the opposite claim is common in this market. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or endorsed by the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International, Pearson or the IB. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is information. Implying it has blessed a tutoring company is not, and a parent should treat any such claim as a reason to ask for the permit number.

sections.heading: Is a private tutor in Ras Al Khaimah legally permitted to teach?
paragraphs: This is a fair question to ask anyone a family is about to invite into their home or onto a video call, and the answer is specific in the UAE.

Private tutoring is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a tutor who tells you it costs money to obtain is mistaken. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific figure a parent reads online should be disregarded, including the amount that circulates on tutoring blogs. There is also a professional boundary worth knowing: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so treat it as a reason to ask the question rather than as a settled wording.

A separate rule applies to organisations rather than individuals. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit is a specific thing issued to institutes with premises, and no tutoring company should describe itself as KHDA approved without holding it.

sections.heading: Coursework, mark schemes and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less internally assessed work than the IB Diploma, but it carries some, and the boundary between teaching and doing is the same in both.

A tutor can teach a method, model a worked example on a different question, mark a student's own attempt against the published criteria, and explain why a paragraph or a calculation did not earn the mark. A tutor cannot write, complete, draft or produce the student's coursework, their exploration, or any assessed piece. IB Gram does not offer that and will not, and parents should know that at least one provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's qualification at risk, not a shortcut.

There is a related restriction on materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A tutor should reference and link them, and work from the copies a student legitimately has through their school, rather than hand out reproduced packs. Any site offering downloadable mark schemes is distributing someone else's copyright, and for unreleased material it is worse than that.

The practical version of all this, for a Year 11 student in Seih Al Uraibi, is a session where the student brings their own marked work, the tutor reads the examiner's comments with them, and the next attempt is the student's. That is slower than being handed an answer and it is the only version that survives the external papers in June.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: what an IGCSE certificate has to show
paragraphs: Families planning a UAE university route need the Ministry of Education's equivalency rules, and this is one of the areas where a ranking competitor publishes the wrong number.

On the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for that count. One competitor page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five, and the exclusion of Arabic and Islamic Education from the count is the part families most often miss when choosing options in Year 9.

For the American track the same clarification sets out English proficiency as a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that source, so no IB equivalency figure should be published without a Ministry of Education page to support it. If your child is on the Diploma route, ask the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly.

Two honest caveats. Equivalency and attestation are processes run by the authority, not by a tutoring company, and IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees them; we can describe the requirement and point you to the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression. Anyone telling a parent in Seih Al Uraibi that it is has turned a regulatory process into a sales line.

faqs.question: Can I get a home tutor who comes to our house in Seih Al Uraibi?
faqs.answer: Tutors who travel to homes do exist in Ras Al Khaimah city, and market rates for that service run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting in-home at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching AED 500. IB Gram is not one of them. We deliver one-to-one tuition to Seih Al Uraibi students over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is a limitation worth stating plainly rather than discovering after booking.

faqs.question: Is the tutoring pool in Al Nakheel or Al Dhait any better than in Seih Al Uraibi?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the main finding of this page. All of these districts send children to the same cluster of private schools, and those staff rooms are the local tutoring pool. Al Nakheel has a denser cohort and therefore more parents competing for the same names. Al Dhait adds twenty to thirty minutes of driving to an identical shortlist. Khuzam has more IB staff nearby, which helps a Diploma family and does nothing for an IGCSE Chemistry problem. Searching the next district over rearranges the travel figures without adding specialists.

faqs.question: Which board is my child entered for, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry from your child's school names the board and the syllabus code. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0580 for Mathematics or 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look like 4MA1 or 4CH1. If the statement has not arrived, the school's exams officer can confirm it in a sentence. It matters more than parents expect: Pearson supplies a formula sheet in maths that Cambridge does not, so recall expectations and revision priorities differ between the two.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams actually happen for a student in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March sitting is offered to India only, which is a point several tutoring sites get wrong for Gulf families. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and in November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Always work from the board's live official timetable and your school's exams officer, since provisional timetables are revised.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for IGCSE tuition in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: budget online tutoring runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Exam-year specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. IB Gram's own rate is confirmed after the free trial.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Ras Al Khaimah need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so ignore the amounts that circulate online.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with exams in a few months. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: It is late but not pointless, provided the work changes shape. With a short run-in there is no time to re-teach a syllabus, so the sessions should be diagnostic from the first hour: find the three or four question types that cost the most marks in the mocks, fix those, and spend the remaining weeks on whole papers under timed conditions marked against the official scheme. That is a different plan from a year-long content programme, and anyone promising a particular grade from a standing start is not being straight with you.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a local tutor for around Ras Al Khaimah city?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606 is the clearest gap, because it is taken by a small number of strong candidates and needs calculus and logarithms at a level 0580 never reaches. Computer Science 0478 is next, where pseudocode conventions and trace tables need someone who has marked the paper. Pearson science papers are thinner locally than Cambridge ones simply because fewer RAK schools use that board. These are exactly the subjects where removing the travel requirement changes the answer from nobody to somebody.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates the schools Seih Al Uraibi children attend?
faqs.answer: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit includes approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, Abu Dhabi under ADEK, Sharjah under SPEA, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. For tutoring the practical effect is indirect: it shapes your school's calendar and reporting. No regulator approves or endorses a tutoring company, including IB Gram, and any claim otherwise deserves scrutiny.

faqs.question: What may an IGCSE tutor in Seih Al Uraibi do with marked coursework, and what not?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the method, model a worked example on a different question, mark your child's own attempt against the published criteria, and explain where the marks went. A tutor cannot write, draft or complete the assessed work. One provider ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments; that is an academic-integrity breach that risks the student's qualification. Tutors should also reference rather than redistribute syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes, which belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a Seih Al Uraibi student need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five. The British-track rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A ranking competitor page in this market states six, which is wrong. Equivalency is run by the Ministry of Education, not by any tutoring company, so verify the current requirement through the official channel.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start for a family in Seih Al Uraibi?
faqs.answer: If your child attends one of the city-centre campuses, a 4.15pm start is comfortable once the ten-to-fifteen-minute run home is done. Families driving back from the RAK Academy campuses at Al Hamra usually settle on 5.30pm or later, and Al Marjan Island households later still. Because lessons are delivered over live video, the only constraint is when your child is home and ready, not when a tutor could reach your street. Arabic assessment weeks and sport fixtures are worth flagging when the slot is agreed.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IGCSE subjects for a student in Seih Al Uraibi?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be checked rather than assumed. Maths and Physics pair naturally, and so do Business Studies and Economics. Chemistry and Biology look adjacent and are taught by different specialists more often than parents expect, because the mark schemes reward different skills. The test is whether the tutor has taught both papers to a scheme, not whether they are confident in both subjects. Where the answer is no, two tutors in alternating weeks usually beats one tutor stretched.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a practical subject like IGCSE Physics?
faqs.answer: For the written papers, yes, and that is where the marks are. The alternative-to-practical paper tests experimental literacy on paper: identifying variables, describing a method, reading a scale, spotting an anomalous result and handling uncertainty. All of that can be taught over live video with the student's own paper on screen. What online cannot replace is laboratory handling itself, which the school provides. A tutor's job is to make sure the practical work your child has already done converts into marks.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no tutor free for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You are told. For a scarce paper such as Additional Mathematics 0606 or a less common Pearson science code, there may be no specialist available in the week you ask. The honest options are to wait for the right match, to start on a related paper where the diagnosis still helps, or to look elsewhere. Being offered a near-enough tutor for a scarce subject is how families lose a term, so availability is disclosed rather than smoothed over.

intro.heading: What an online IGCSE lesson actually is, once you look inside the hour
paragraphs: Online tutoring is described almost everywhere as a convenience and almost nowhere as a method. That is the wrong way round. The reason a live video lesson works for a Year 11 student in Ras Al Khaimah is not that nobody has to drive; it is that the tutor can see the student's working appear line by line, stop at the exact moment a sign error is made, and keep the paper, the mark scheme and the student's own script on screen at the same time. In a room with a shared exercise book, a tutor sees the finished answer. On a shared digital page, they see the thinking.

The mechanics are simple and worth knowing before you book. The tutor writes on a graphics tablet, so maths and science working appears in handwriting rather than as typed text. The question paper is screen-shared from the student's own specification. The student writes on paper and shows it to the camera, or writes on the shared page directly, depending on the subject and on what they will do in the exam hall - pen on paper is what gets examined, so most sessions keep that habit. Nothing exotic is involved and nothing needs installing beyond a browser-based meeting room.

What changes for families in this emirate is reach. Ras Al Khaimah's school-age population is spread across roughly forty kilometres, from the northern strip at Al Rams through the city districts to Al Hamra Village and Al Marjan Island, and the private-school set is small. For Extended-tier Chemistry 0620, Additional Mathematics 0606 or Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 taught with the right scope, the number of specialists within driving distance is often zero. Live video makes that question irrelevant, which is the actual argument for the format here.

It also has limits, and this page states them. Laboratory work belongs in a laboratory; what a screen teaches is the assessed version of practical skill - results tables, sources of error, controlled variables, the alternative-to-practical paper. Young children who cannot yet hold their own attention usually need an adult beside them rather than on a screen. And a connection has to be good enough, which in most of the emirate it is, but not in every household at 7pm. IB Gram teaches UAE families online only; we do not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE, because in-home visiting is a service we run only in India.

The rest of this page is operational detail: the anatomy of a session, the equipment table, how each examined component is handled remotely, what to expect of connections and timing in Gulf Standard Time, how recordings and a minor's personal data are treated under the UAE's data protection law, how an hour of individual attention compares with an hour in a group of six, and what changes for a private candidate studying outside a school.

Entries are made through the centre your child's school holds, and that centre is allocated to one of six Cambridge administrative zones, each with its own timetable version. Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after the wrong zone timetable was used, so the exams officer, not a tutor, is the authority on dates.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, taught live
programmes.description: Grades run 9 to 1 and the specifications differ from Cambridge's: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. There is no separate practical examination in the international sciences, so practical understanding is taught as it is assessed - inside written questions, with real data sets on screen.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs series in May or June and again in November, and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each one. For a Ras Al Khaimah student, the November route is the practical reason to confirm early whether the school's centre is entering candidates for it, since a private-candidate entry elsewhere carries its own earlier deadline.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: Remote sessions at this stage are short and frequent rather than long: thirty to forty minutes, one topic, with the student writing while the tutor watches. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and give a diagnostic that maps onto the topics an IGCSE paper will examine two years later.
programmes.countryNote: This is the age group where a parent being within earshot helps, which is easy in an apartment in Al Nakheel and equally easy in a villa in Mina Al Arab. Families here commonly run a fortnightly slot through Years 7 and 8 and move to weekly when Year 10 starts, keeping the same tutor.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The route many Ras Al Khaimah students take after Year 11, and the one where remote teaching is least disputed, because the work is already independent. Sessions revolve around past questions, worked derivations and extended writing, with the student's own script on screen beside the mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: Because the emirate also has IB continuum provision on the southern coast, families here often compare an A Level route in the city against a Diploma place closer to home. A summer of bridging work in mathematics is the usual request either way, and it runs well remotely in July and August when schools are closed.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject uses the screen differently. The notes below describe what a live session in that subject looks like, rather than restating the syllabus content.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The purest fit for a shared page. The tutor writes on a graphics tablet while the student works on paper and shows it to the camera, so a missing line of method is caught as it happens rather than after the answer is wrong. Non-calculator practice is set as written homework.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Calculus and trigonometric identities need worked derivations, which is exactly what a shared handwritten page does well. Sessions typically run a full hour here rather than forty-five minutes, because a derivation interrupted halfway is worse than one not started.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Circuit diagrams are drawn live and annotated by both people, which is hard to do over a book. The describe-an-experiment questions are taught from real data on screen: a named measurement, a repeated reading, a stated control.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Mole calculations are set out in steps on the shared page so the method is visible and markable. Organic mechanisms are drawn rather than described, and results tables from past practical papers are worked through as data-handling exercises.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Diagram labelling and answer length are the two recurring issues, and both are easier to drill on screen because the mark scheme can sit beside the student's answer. Genetics crosses are built live rather than copied from notes.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Session one is a scoping exercise: establishing what the double award excludes, so no time is spent on single-science content. Thereafter the pattern follows the three sciences in rotation, with one component per session.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: The student's writing is shared on screen and annotated against the published criteria, which is faster and clearer than reading aloud. Reading-paper work uses the extract on screen with the question beside it, so analysis is anchored to the text.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Listening practice runs well online because the audio is clean and can be replayed with the note-taking visible. Speaking components are rehearsed on camera, which most students find a closer simulation of the assessment than a conversation across a table.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: The subject that benefits most from screen sharing, because the assessment is practical software work. Spreadsheets and document production are built in front of the student and then rebuilt by them while the tutor watches.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / Pearson 4CP0)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables on a shared page, with the student filling in each row as the algorithm runs. Programming practice uses a shared editor so an error can be found by the student rather than announced by the tutor.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450 / Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study work is done with the case on screen and the answer being typed or written beside it, so every paragraph can be checked against the business in front of the student rather than against business in general.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams are drawn by the student on the shared page while the tutor marks the labels, which is where the easy marks are lost. Evaluation language is then built into written answers one paragraph at a time.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Connection, rooms and timing across Ras Al Khaimah
ras-al-khaimah/igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Remote lessons depend on three household things rather than on geography: a stable connection, a room where a door closes, and a slot that survives the week. These are the local patterns we see across the emirate.

regions.name: Al Nakheel and Al Mairid
regions.note: Apartment living in the city core. Connections are generally good; the constraint is usually a quiet room rather than bandwidth, and a headset solves more problems here than any upgrade to the internet package.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village and Al Jazirah Al Hamra
regions.note: Villa communities with stable fixed-line service. The practical issue is distance from the router in a large house, which a mesh extender or moving the session to a room nearer the hub resolves quickly.

regions.name: Mina Al Arab and Hayat Island
regions.note: Newer housing with good connectivity. Households here often have two children needing the same evening window, so one session at 5pm and one at 6.15pm works better than trying to run both at once in the same room.

regions.name: Al Marjan Island
regions.note: Newer builds and a mixed resident population. Sessions here are the clearest case for remote delivery in the emirate: a single causeway means a visiting tutor's arrival time is never reliable, while a video call is.

regions.name: Khuzam and Al Dhait
regions.note: Dense family districts inland of the city with short school runs. Early slots from 4.30pm are realistic here and are taken first in September; families booking in January are generally choosing from after 6pm.

regions.name: Al Qusaidat, Al Rams and Sha'am
regions.note: The northern strip, where the school run alone can take twenty-five minutes each way. A 6pm start is the realistic one, and it is also the hour when the Gulf-wide evening demand peak is at its highest.

regions.name: Digdaga, Al Ghail and the inland belt
regions.note: Furthest from the school clusters. Fixed-line service is generally adequate for video; where it is not, a session runs over a mobile connection with video off for the tutor and the shared page carrying the lesson.

regions.name: Households that travel between emirates
regions.note: Families splitting the week between Ras Al Khaimah and Dubai or Sharjah for work keep one slot rather than two, because the lesson follows the laptop. This is the single most common reason parents here give for choosing remote teaching over a local arrangement.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways to run remote sessions, chosen by age and by how far away the series is. All are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: Standard live session, 45 to 60 minutes
modes.description: The default. Marked practice from last week is reviewed in the first ten minutes, one error type is taught, the student works on paper while the tutor watches through the camera, and a question set is agreed for the week. A short note follows the same day naming what was covered and what to practise.
bullets: Graphics tablet and shared page for handwritten working
Question paper on screen from the student's own specification
Written session note the same day, not a weekly summary

modes.title: Short frequent sessions, 30 to 40 minutes
modes.description: For Years 7 to 9, for students who lose concentration before the hour is up, and for the fasting month, when two short sessions beat one long one. Each session covers a single topic with a clear finish point, which also makes the homework easier to set and to check.
bullets: One topic per session, with a defined end point
Suits younger students and the Ramadan weeks
Easier to reschedule within a busy school week

modes.title: Paper and review pairs
modes.description: Used in the run-in to a series. The student sits a timed paper alone, uploads a photograph of the script, and the session that follows is spent on the marking. Two sessions a week in this shape produce more than four hours of teaching at the same point in the year.

sections.heading: The first ten minutes, and what the rest of the hour contains
paragraphs: A live session that starts with how was your week has wasted the most valuable ten minutes available. The shape we use starts with the student's own marked work from the previous session: the tutor has it on screen, has read it before the lesson, and opens by naming what went right and which single error is being taught today. That sets the agenda in two minutes and tells the student that what they did between sessions is the point of the arrangement.

The middle of the hour is teaching, and the format differs by subject. In mathematics and the sciences the tutor writes on a graphics tablet while the student works on paper and holds it to the camera, or writes directly on the shared page. The reason for keeping pen on paper is not nostalgia: the exam is handwritten, and a student who has only ever typed working loses time and layout marks in the hall. In the essay subjects the student's own paragraph is shared on screen and annotated against the published criteria, line by line, which is faster and more honest than reading aloud.

The last ten minutes set the work for the week. A question set, a page reference in the student's own textbook, and where relevant a timed section to sit alone. This is the part that is most often skipped and that most determines whether anything changes, because an hour a week of excellent teaching with no practice between sessions moves a grade slowly if at all.

Then the note. You get a few lines the same day: what was covered, what the student is practising, and anything that needs the school's input - a missing textbook, a coursework deadline, a tier question. Short on purpose. A page-long report nobody reads is a worse product than four honest lines.
bullets: Opens on last week's marked work, which the tutor has read in advance
Handwritten working stays handwritten, because the exam is
Closes with a specific question set, not a general instruction to revise
A short written note reaches you the same day

sections.heading: The equipment that matters, and the equipment that does not
paragraphs: Families routinely over-buy for online tutoring and under-think the room. The honest list of what affects a lesson is short, and most households in Ras Al Khaimah already have all of it. A laptop or tablet with a working camera, a pair of wired earphones with a microphone, a notebook and pen, and a door that closes. That is the whole requirement for a secondary student.

What makes a visible difference beyond that is lighting and camera angle, because the tutor needs to see the student's written working. A phone propped on a stand beside the notebook as a second camera is the single cheapest upgrade available, and it turns a lesson where the tutor sees a face into one where they see the method. A graphics tablet on the student's side helps in maths-heavy subjects but is a convenience rather than a requirement; the tutor's tablet is the one that matters.

What does not matter: a premium internet package, a large monitor, a dedicated desk setup, or any paid software. Our sessions run in a browser-based meeting room, and video quality beyond a basic standard changes nothing about teaching. Where a connection is genuinely weak, the fix is to turn the student's video off and keep the shared page, which uses almost no bandwidth and preserves the part of the lesson that carries the teaching.

One point about phones. A session taken entirely on a phone, held in one hand, is a session in which the student cannot write. If a phone is the only device, use it as the camera and write on paper beside it; do not try to work on the screen. Families with two children sharing one laptop are better off staggering sessions by an hour than running them simultaneously in the same room, where the audio alone makes both worse.

sections.heading: How each examined component is taught through a screen
paragraphs: The useful question is not whether online teaching works in general but what happens to each examined component. IGCSE grades are built from distinct pieces - multiple choice, structured theory, extended writing, practical or alternative-to-practical papers, and in a few subjects coursework - and remote teaching suits some of them better than others. The table below is the honest version, including where the answer is that the school does it and we do not.

The component that causes most anxiety is the science practical, so it is worth being precise. Cambridge sciences carry either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, worth roughly a fifth of the grade; Pearson's international sciences have no separate practical exam and assess practical understanding inside the written papers. In both cases what earns marks is a specific, teachable set of moves: naming the measuring instrument, identifying the independent and controlled variables, spotting an anomalous result, explaining why a reading was repeated, and reading a results table carefully. All of that is taught from real data on a screen. The hands-on laboratory work stays at school, where it belongs, and no amount of video replaces it.

Coursework is the other component that needs care. Where a school runs the coursework option in Geography or History rather than the alternative paper, the rules on help are strict, and a tutor's job is to teach the criteria and question the student's own draft. Nobody here writes, redrafts or completes any part of assessed work. Two sites competing for this search sell exactly that, which is a malpractice trigger for the student and not a service we offer at any price.

For the written components, remote teaching has a genuine advantage that in-person work does not: the mark scheme, the question and the student's answer can all be visible at once, and the student can see the marker's logic being applied to their own words. That is the mechanism behind most of the grade movement we see, and it has nothing to do with convenience.

sections.heading: Timing, connections and the Gulf evening peak
paragraphs: Scheduling is the most underrated part of remote tutoring and the thing most likely to break a plan. Every UAE family wants the same window: after the school run, before dinner, between roughly 4.30pm and 7.30pm Gulf Standard Time. That is three hours of demand against a whole week of supply, and the strongest subject specialists are booked inside it first. A family in Khuzam that fixes a Tuesday 5pm slot in September usually keeps the same tutor until the exams. A family that starts looking in March is choosing from what remains.

The northern areas have a narrower window still. From Al Qusaidat, Al Rams or Sha'am the school run alone can take twenty-five minutes each way, which makes a 4.30pm start unrealistic and a 6pm one sensible - and 6pm is the busiest hour in the whole week. The practical answer is often a weekend morning session instead, which is usually easier to staff and, for a tired fifteen-year-old in exam term, frequently more productive than a weekday evening.

On connections, the requirement is lower than families assume. A lesson needs the shared page to stay live; it does not need broadcast-quality video. Where a household's service struggles at peak, turning the student's camera off while keeping the second camera on the notebook keeps the teaching intact at a fraction of the bandwidth, and a mobile hotspot is an adequate fallback for a single session. The time to discover this is during the free trial rather than in week nine of a plan.

One scheduling habit is worth copying. Fix the slot for the term rather than agreeing it week by week. Negotiating a time every Sunday produces drift, missed sessions and a tutor who eventually gives the slot to someone else; a fixed time with two planned exceptions written in at the start survives the term intact.
bullets: The 4.30pm to 7.30pm Gulf Standard Time band is the scarce resource, not the tutor

sections.heading: Recordings, safeguarding and a child's personal data
paragraphs: A lesson involving a minor on video raises real questions, and parents in the UAE are entitled to specific answers rather than reassurance. Our position is: sessions are one tutor and one student, a parent may sit in or be within earshot at any time and does not need to ask, and the meeting room is not a public link that can be joined by anyone who finds it.

Recording is only done on a parent's written instruction, for that family's own revision use, and a recording made that way is not shared with anyone else or used for marketing. If you would rather nothing was ever recorded, say so at the start and nothing will be. Where a recording exists, you can ask for it to be deleted and it will be.

On data, the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the governing framework, and the honest version of our practice is a short list. We collect what is needed to teach: the student's year group, subjects, syllabus codes and tier, the scripts and work you send us, the session notes, and a parent's contact details. We do not need a child's photograph, their full school report history or their examination candidate number, and we do not ask for them. You can ask what is held, ask for it to be corrected, and ask for it to be deleted, and the privacy link on every page explains how.

Two practical points parents often raise. First, scripts and work you send are used for teaching that student and for nothing else; they are not published as examples. Second, a tutor should never ask a student to move the conversation to a personal messaging account. Communication about lessons goes through the arrangement you booked, with a parent copied in, which is both a safeguarding norm and a simple way of keeping a record.
bullets: One tutor, one student; a parent may be present at any time
Recording only on written instruction, never shared onward, deletable on request
Minimal data: year group, subjects, codes, the work you send, session notes
No side channels: lesson communication stays in the booked arrangement

sections.heading: What an hour buys in each format
paragraphs: The comparison parents actually need is not online against in-person. It is minutes of individual attention against the cost of the hour, and feedback latency against the student's error rate. A group class of six is not a worse product than one-to-one teaching; it is a different one, and for a student who shares the class's gap it can be the better buy. For a student whose marks are leaking in four specific places, it is usually the wrong instrument.

Think of it as attention arithmetic. In a sixty-minute class of six, a student receives on average ten minutes of individual attention, and the pace is set by the group's median. In a one-to-one session, all sixty minutes respond to that student's work, and the pace is set by their error rate. At published market rates - roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for group and budget provision against AED 150 to 300 for qualified one-to-one online teaching - the group seat is cheaper per hour and the one-to-one hour is cheaper per minute of attention. Those are market figures from published provider rates, not our price list.

Feedback latency is the second axis and the one nobody mentions. In a class, written work is marked between sessions if at all, and a misconception can run for a fortnight. In a live one-to-one session with the student writing on camera, an error is caught in the sentence it appears in. For technique problems - missing method, misread command words, unfinished papers - that difference is the whole mechanism by which a grade moves.

None of which means more hours is better. Three one-to-one hours a week in one subject, with no practice between them, produces less than one hour plus homework. The limiting factor is almost always the student's independent work, which is why our sessions end with a specific question set rather than an instruction to revise.

sections.heading: Private candidates and students studying outside a school
paragraphs: A small but growing group of families in the northern emirates are not working from a school timetable at all: children taught at home, students repeating a single subject after a move, and families between schools after relocating to Ras Al Khaimah mid-year. Remote teaching is the obvious format for them, and the complications are administrative rather than educational.

The first is entry. A private candidate needs an examination centre willing to accept the entry, and the deadlines for private entries fall earlier than for school candidates. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January, as November 2025 results did on 22 January 2026 - and entries for a window like that are settled with the centre months earlier, in the first half of the year. Cambridge works the same way across its June and November series. Finding the centre therefore comes before any teaching plan, because the centre determines which series, which subjects and which components are available at all.

The second is practical components. Not every centre offers the practical test for Cambridge sciences, and where it is unavailable the alternative-to-practical written paper is the route. That is a better outcome than it sounds - the alternative paper is a written assessment of practical understanding and suits remote preparation closely - but it has to be established before the entry rather than discovered afterwards.

The third is pacing. A student without a school timetable has no external deadlines, and the thing that fails is not the teaching but the practice. Private-candidate plans therefore carry more structure, not less: a written topic order with week numbers, a timed paper every fortnight from the halfway point, and a parent who sees the marked scripts. We will say honestly at the enquiry whether a subject can be taught well to a private candidate in the time available, because the alternative is a family paying for an entry that was never realistic.

sections.heading: Regulation: what a remote tutor working with UAE families must hold
paragraphs: Parents ask whether the permit rules apply to a tutor teaching over video, and it is a fair question because the rules were not written with a camera in mind. The position to work from is the published one. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure you see quoted.

MoHRE's own service for it is listed as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a stated completion time of two working days. That is the official route, and it is the thing to ask a tutor about rather than a certificate of some other kind.

There is a second rule worth knowing even though it applies elsewhere in the country. In Abu Dhabi, press-reported professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Whatever emirate you live in, the general principle holds: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to pay privately, and a provider offering that arrangement is offering you a problem.

What IB Gram is not, finally, needs saying plainly on a page about regulation. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ministry of Education, from any emirate authority including Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, or from Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. We name those bodies on this page because what they do affects your decisions, not because any of them endorses us. A tutoring company describing itself as approved by a regulator is telling you something about its honesty rather than its credentials.

process.title: Check the room before the tutor
process.description: Before the trial, pick where the lesson will happen: a surface big enough for a notebook, a door that closes, earphones with a microphone, and a phone on a stand beside the page as a second camera. Ten minutes of setup prevents most of what families later blame on the format.

process.title: Send the specification and the scripts
process.description: The statement of entry with the syllabus code and tier, plus two recent marked scripts. Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different jobs, and the scripts tell the tutor where the marks are going before a single minute of the trial is spent asking.

process.title: Free trial, which doubles as a technical check
process.description: One free lesson per subject, no card details taken, with the tutor who would keep the slot. It teaches something real and it tells you how your connection, your room and your child handle the format at the hour you actually want.

process.title: Fix the slot for the term
process.description: Agree one time in Gulf Standard Time and keep it, with known exceptions written in from the start. Week-by-week scheduling is the single most common reason a remote plan quietly loses four sessions a term.

process.title: Read the session notes
process.description: A few lines reach you the same day: what was covered, what the student is practising, anything the school needs to resolve. Reading them takes a minute a week and is how you keep the arrangement honest without sitting in every lesson.

whyPoints.title: The tutor sees the working, not the answer
whyPoints.description: A shared handwritten page plus a camera on the notebook means a method error is caught in the line where it happens. That is the mechanism behind grade movement in maths and the sciences, and it is harder to achieve across a kitchen table.

whyPoints.title: Specification-matched, not school-matched
whyPoints.description: Lessons are planned against the code and tier on the statement of entry. In an emirate where a given specification may have no local specialist at all, that match matters more than proximity.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the laboratory
whyPoints.description: Practical skill is taught as it is examined - variables, repeats, anomalous results, results tables - and the hands-on work stays at school. We do not claim a screen replaces a laboratory bench.

whyPoints.title: Clear rules on recording and data
whyPoints.description: Recording only on written instruction, never shared onward, deletable on request. We collect the minimum needed to teach and name it, under the framework of Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling treated as part of the teaching
whyPoints.description: The scarce resource is the 4.30pm to 7.30pm window, not goodwill. Slots are fixed for the term, with the known interruptions written in, which is what keeps a twenty-week plan intact.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals
whyPoints.description: No regulator and no examination board approves or endorses IB Gram, and we never imply otherwise. The permit question that does matter - MoHRE's private tuition work permit - is one you should ask any tutor, including ours.

faqs.question: What does my child actually need in front of them for a live lesson?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet with a working camera, wired earphones with a microphone, a notebook and pen, the calculator their exam allows, and a room where a door closes. The one upgrade worth making is a phone on a small stand beside the notebook as a second camera, so the tutor sees the written working rather than only a face. Nothing needs installing beyond a browser. A premium internet package, a large monitor and paid software change nothing about the teaching, and a session taken on a hand-held phone is a session in which the student cannot write.

faqs.question: How does a tutor see my son's working if he is writing on paper?
faqs.answer: Through a second camera angle. A phone propped beside the notebook, or a laptop positioned so the page is in frame, shows the working as it is produced. The tutor writes on a graphics tablet at their end, so both people are drawing on a shared surface in handwriting rather than typing. This matters more than it sounds: method marks are awarded for steps on a page, and a tutor who only sees the final answer is reviewing homework rather than teaching. We keep pen and paper precisely because the exam is handwritten.

faqs.question: Is a shared whiteboard enough for maths, or should he be typing equations?
faqs.answer: A shared handwritten page is better than typed equations for IGCSE work, because the student has to produce handwritten mathematics under time in the exam hall. Typing trains a different skill and hides layout problems that cost marks: cramped working, steps in the wrong order, no equals signs aligned. The tutor's graphics tablet keeps the demonstration handwritten too, so what the student sees modelled is what they will be asked to produce. Typed working is useful in one place only - programming in Computer Science, where a shared editor is the right tool.

faqs.question: What happens to the science practical work if lessons are remote?
faqs.answer: The hands-on work stays in the school laboratory, and we do not pretend otherwise. What is taught remotely is the component that is actually examined. Cambridge sciences carry either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper worth roughly a fifth of the grade, and Pearson's international sciences assess practical understanding inside the written papers. The marks go to naming the measuring instrument, identifying controlled variables, explaining a repeated reading, spotting an anomalous result and reading a results table. All of that is taught from real data on screen, and it is where most students are losing marks.

faqs.question: Will lessons be recorded, and who else can watch them?
faqs.answer: Only if you ask for it in writing, and then only for your family's own revision use. A recording made that way is not shared with anyone else and is not used for marketing or training. If you would prefer nothing is ever recorded, say so at the start and nothing will be. Where a recording exists you can ask for it to be deleted at any point. Sessions themselves are one tutor and one student in a private room, not a public link, and a parent is welcome to sit in or be within earshot without asking first.

faqs.question: What information do you hold about my daughter, and can I have it removed?
faqs.answer: We collect what is needed to teach: her year group, subjects, syllabus codes and tier, the scripts and work you send, the session notes, and a parent's contact details. We do not ask for a photograph, a full report history or a candidate number. Under the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection you can ask what is held, ask for corrections and ask for deletion, and the privacy link on every page sets out how. Scripts you send are used for teaching her and nothing else; they are never published as examples.

faqs.question: Our internet drops in the evening. Can a session survive that?
faqs.answer: Usually, because the part of the lesson that carries the teaching uses very little bandwidth. The shared page and the audio are what matter; video is a comfort. If the connection struggles, the fix is to turn the student's camera off, keep the second camera on the notebook if possible, and carry on. A mobile hotspot is an adequate fallback for one session. The free trial is the right moment to test this at the hour you actually want, rather than discovering it in week nine of a plan.

faqs.question: Which evening times are genuinely available in Gulf Standard Time?
faqs.answer: Every UAE family wants roughly 4.30pm to 7.30pm, so that window is the scarce resource rather than the tutors themselves. Inside it, the earliest slots go first and they go in September. For families on the northern strip, where the school run alone takes twenty-five minutes each way, a 6pm start is realistic and is also the busiest hour of the week. A weekend morning session is usually easier to staff and, for a tired fifteen-year-old in exam term, often more productive than a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Can two of my children share one session to save money?
faqs.answer: It can work for siblings close in ability sitting the same specification, and it is cheaper than two individual sessions. The trade-off is real: the pace follows the slower of the two, individual attention halves, and a student with a specific error pattern gets perhaps thirty minutes of relevant teaching in an hour. Where siblings are in different years or different tiers, a shared session usually helps neither. Staggering two shorter individual sessions an hour apart is the arrangement most families here settle on after trying both.

faqs.question: Does remote teaching work for a student who is easily distracted?
faqs.answer: Sometimes better than a room, sometimes worse, and the trial lesson is how you find out rather than a brochure. What helps is structure: a shorter session of thirty to forty minutes with one topic and a defined end point, a camera on the page so the tutor can see when attention goes, and a parent within earshot rather than in the room. What does not help is a ninety-minute block, a phone in the other hand, or a session in a room with a television. For students who need an adult physically beside them, a local arrangement is the better answer and we will say so.

faqs.question: How quickly will I know whether the tutor is the right match?
faqs.answer: After the trial you should be able to answer two questions: did the tutor name specific errors from the scripts, and did they teach something in the hour rather than interview you. If either answer is no, the match is wrong regardless of credentials. Beyond the trial, the honest window is two or three sessions, which is enough to see whether the student does the practice and whether the written notes describe something recognisable. Changing tutor at session three costs you nothing; changing at session twelve costs a month of a plan.

faqs.question: We moved to Ras Al Khaimah mid-year and my son has no school place yet. Can he still prepare?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the first task is administrative rather than educational. A candidate without a school needs an examination centre willing to accept a private entry, and private deadlines fall earlier than school ones. In the UAE the realistic choices are a June series and a November series, and the entry for either closes with the centre months ahead of the first paper, so the series you are aiming at is usually decided a term or two before any revision starts. The centre also determines whether a practical test is available or whether the alternative-to-practical paper applies. Settle those questions first, because they decide which subjects and series are realistic, and then the teaching plan is straightforward.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor legally teach a student who lives in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring here is regulated by permit rather than by format. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private lessons without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so ignore quoted amounts. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Ask any tutor about their permit, local or remote.

faqs.question: Are you approved by Cambridge or by the education authority here?
faqs.answer: No, and any tutoring company telling you otherwise is worth a second look. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the IB, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority, including the Department of Knowledge that regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah. Those bodies appear on this page because what they do affects your decisions - which authority approves your school's curriculum and fees, which board your child is entered with, which permit a tutor needs. None of them endorses us, and we do not describe ourselves as if they did.

faqs.question: What do I receive after each lesson?
faqs.answer: A few lines the same day: what was covered, what the student is practising before the next session, and anything that needs the school's input, such as a missing textbook or a coursework deadline. It is deliberately short, because a page-long report nobody reads is worse than four honest lines. At the six-week point you get a longer review comparing the current list of recurring errors with the one written after the first session, which is the part that tells you whether the arrangement is working.

You will learn more in that hour than from any description of the method: whether your connection holds, whether your child works on camera, and whether the tutor can name specific errors rather than general weaknesses. intro.heading: Four ways to get IGCSE help in Ras Al Khaimah, and what actually separates them
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah is a small market for a specialised job. The emirate's private schools sit mostly in a band running from Al Nakheel and Khuzam in the city out to Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab on the southern coast, and between them they offer a handful of IGCSE subject menus rather than the fifty-campus spread Dubai has. That matters the moment your child needs help with Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 rather than general study support. The number of people in driving distance who have taught that exact specification to that exact tier is small, and in some subjects it is close to nobody.

So the real decision here is not whether tutoring helps. It is which of four options you are buying. The school's own revision clinic is free, is run by the person who sets the mock, and is almost always a group. A tuition centre in the city gives you a room, a timetable and a teacher covering six children at once at a lower hourly figure. A freelance tutor contacted through a neighbourhood group may be excellent and may be a university student with a fortnight of experience; the permit position and the subject depth are both on you to check. One-to-one online teaching costs more per hour than a group seat and less than an in-home visit once travel is priced in, and it is the only one of the four where the pool you choose from is not limited by who lives within half an hour of your villa.

The honest version of the trade-off is this. Group teaching is efficient for content coverage and poor at diagnosing one student's specific error pattern. A local freelance visit buys presence in the room and costs you travel time inside the fee. Online one-to-one buys the subject specialist and asks the student to work on a screen with a shared document and a graphics tablet. For a Year 11 student eight months from a June series, the thing that moves the grade is usually not the format at all: it is whether somebody has read their last two mock scripts question by question and knows which four topics are costing them marks.

IB Gram delivers teaching to families in Ras Al Khaimah online, over live video, with one tutor and one student. We do not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate limit rather than a gap. It means a family in Al Marjan Island and a family in Al Rams are offered the same Physics 0625 specialist, and that a subject with three capable teachers in the whole northern emirates is not rationed by postcode.

What follows is the detail a parent needs before paying anybody: what the four options cost in AED, how to tell a Cambridge entry from a Pearson one, what the tier on the entry form does to the grade ceiling, where marks are lost in each of the main subjects, and the entry deadline that sits months before the exam and quietly removes options when it passes.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Ras Al Khaimah schools run IGCSE as a two-year Year 10 to Year 11 course, usually after a Lower Secondary or Checkpoint phase and usually feeding into either International A Levels or the IB Diploma. Support is organised around those four stages because a Year 9 problem and a Year 11 problem need different teaching.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is a two-year, subject-by-subject qualification taken one syllabus at a time, each with its own code: 0580 Mathematics, 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0450 Business Studies, 0478 Computer Science. Grades are reported A* to G. Most syllabuses are examined entirely at the end of Year 11, with the sciences adding a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper worth a fifth of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: The British-curriculum schools in Ras Al Khaimah run Cambridge entries through their own exam centre, and the centre is allocated to one of Cambridge's six administrative zones. The zone decides which version of the timetable applies, and Cambridge states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your school's exams officer which zone it sits in.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE covers the same age group with different specifications and a different grade scale: 9 to 1, where 9 is the top grade. Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics is 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A is 4EA1. The sciences have no separate practical exam; practical understanding is assessed inside the written papers, which changes how a student should revise for them.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE series in May and June and again in November, which gives a Ras Al Khaimah student who narrowly missed a grade a resit route in the same calendar year rather than a twelve-month wait. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Results from the June 2026 series reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE are where the gaps that later cost grades are created: negative indices, rearranging formulae, writing a method rather than an answer, reading a question for its command word. Cambridge offers Checkpoint tests in March, May and October as a diagnostic rather than a certificate, and the feedback they return maps cleanly onto the topics an IGCSE paper will ask about two years later.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah this is the cheapest intervention available, because a Year 8 student needs one session a fortnight rather than the three a week an exam-year panic requires. Families in Al Dhait and Khuzam often start here after a Checkpoint report, use two terms to close an arithmetic or writing gap, and then stop until options are chosen in Year 9.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is one of the two routes out of IGCSE in this emirate, alongside International A Levels. It asks for six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The step up is less about new content than about new formats: internal assessments with published criteria, a 4,000-word research essay and papers that reward argument rather than recall.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah has an IB continuum campus on the Al Hamra side of the emirate, so an IGCSE student here may be weighing a Diploma place against an A Level route in the city or in Sharjah. The subject that most often decides it is mathematics: a 9 or A* at Extended tier makes Analysis and Approaches realistic, while a 6 or B usually points to Applications and Interpretation.

ras-al-khaimah/igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Ras Al Khaimah families ask about most, with what each one is actually assessed on and where the marks tend to go. Every subject is taught against the specification your child is entered for, Cambridge or Pearson, not against a generic syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers, each worth half the grade. From the 2025 Cambridge syllabus one paper in each tier pair is sat without a calculator, while Pearson's Mathematics A allows a calculator in both. Marks are lost on method presentation, on exact-value work and on the multi-step problems that sit at the back of every paper.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Higher Level or A Level mathematics. Two papers of two hours each, covering calculus, trigonometric identities, series and vectors. It is the single best preparation for a Diploma Analysis and Approaches course, and the subject where a strong IGCSE student most often meets genuine difficulty for the first time.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Cambridge splits the grade across a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper. Pearson's 4PH1 has two written papers and no practical exam. Electricity circuits, moments and the describe-an-experiment questions are where most of the lost marks sit.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade more than any other topic, and organic chemistry decides whether the top band is reachable. The practical or alternative-to-practical component rewards students who can read a results table and identify a source of error, which is a trainable skill rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively easy to under-prepare. The marks are in precision: naming the correct process, using the command word the question asked for, and writing an answer whose length matches the mark allocation. Genetics and transport in plants produce the most predictable errors.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a double award, common where a timetable cannot fit three separate science blocks. It needs a tutor who knows which parts of the single-science syllabuses are out of scope, because revising from 0625 or 0620 material wastes weeks on content that will not be examined.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: A reading paper and a writing paper, each half the grade. The reading marks go on summary and on close analysis of how a writer achieves an effect; the writing marks go on structure and register. Both are taught, not innate, and both improve fastest when a student marks their own work against the published criteria.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing and listening components with a speaking element, taken by many students in Ras Al Khaimah whose school language is English but whose home language is not. Exam technique carries real weight here: the listening paper rewards note-taking discipline and the writing task rewards hitting the stated purpose and audience.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450 / Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Paper 1 takes short answers and data response; Paper 2 is a case study issued in the exam. Marks are lost by students who explain a concept correctly but never apply it to the business in front of them. Application and evaluation are where the top two bands live.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper and a structured-question paper, with diagrams carrying marks of their own. Students who can draw a correctly labelled market diagram and then write a sentence about what the diagram shows pick up marks their classmates leave on the table.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / Pearson 4CP0)
subjects.description: Two written papers: computer systems, then algorithms, programming and logic. There is no coursework. Pseudocode and trace tables are the two skills that separate grades, and both are practised rather than read.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460) and History (Cambridge 0470)
subjects.description: Both carry a skills or source paper plus an alternative-to-coursework option that schools in the UAE commonly choose. Source handling in History and the geographical-skills paper in Geography are the two components where a term of targeted work shifts a grade most reliably.

sections.heading: What a Ras Al Khaimah parent is really choosing between
paragraphs: There are four realistic ways to get IGCSE support in this emirate, and they differ far more in what they are good at than in what they cost. The school's own clinic is free and is taught by the person who writes the mock, which is a genuine advantage; it is also a group of eight to fifteen students moving at one pace, and it stops when term stops. A city tuition centre sells a seat in a class, typically four to eight students, at the lowest hourly figure in the market. A freelance tutor contacted through a community group is the most variable option available: some are experienced teachers with a permit, some are undergraduates with a fortnight of practice, and the difference is not visible in the advertisement.

One-to-one teaching delivered online is the fourth option and the one this site provides. Its advantage is not the technology. It is that the pool of available teachers is not limited to people living within half an hour of your door, which in Ras Al Khaimah is the binding constraint on every other option. For Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 or Additional Mathematics 0606, the question is whether anyone nearby has taught that specification at that tier in the last three years. Often the honest answer locally is no.

The AED figures below are market rates published by providers in this region, not an IB Gram price list. They are included because three of the six largest competitor pages in this search publish no price at all, and a parent comparing four options needs numbers. Our own pricing is quoted after a free trial lesson and depends on subject, tier and session length, which is why it is not in the table.

One warning that applies to every option. Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and people tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted as unverified.

sections.heading: Check which IGCSE your child actually sits before you book anybody
paragraphs: Parents in Ras Al Khaimah routinely book a tutor for the wrong qualification. The phrase IGCSE covers at least two different exam boards with different specifications, different paper structures and different grade scales, and plenty of schools in this emirate enter students for a mixture: Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson for mathematics is a common pattern. A tutor who revises the wrong specification can spend a whole term on content that will not be examined.

The document that settles it is the statement of entry, issued by the school's exams officer. It lists each entry code: 0580 and 0620 are Cambridge, 4MA1 and 4CH1 are Pearson Edexcel. If you cannot find it, the grade scale on the last report is a reliable second clue, because Cambridge IGCSE still reports A* to G while Pearson's International GCSE reports 9 to 1. A report carrying both scales usually means both boards are in play.

The difference is not cosmetic. Cambridge sciences carry either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper worth a fifth of the grade; Pearson's international science specifications have no separate practical exam and assess practical understanding inside the written papers. Cambridge mathematics from the 2025 syllabus includes a paper sat without a calculator; Pearson's Mathematics A permits a calculator in both papers. A student who has revised arithmetic fluency for the wrong board has wasted the effort, and one who has not revised it for the right board has a problem.

Series availability differs too, and that matters for resits. Cambridge runs June and November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson runs International GCSE in May or June and again in November. For a student who misses a grade by two marks, a November series is the difference between a retake inside the same academic year and a twelve-month wait.
