faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start for a child living in Mina Al Arab?
faqs.answer: For secondary students, 17:30 is the first slot that produces a full lesson. Bus pickups on Hayat Island start around 06:45 and secondary students are rarely home before 15:00, so a 16:00 start catches a child who has been awake for ten hours. Primary children finish earlier and often do well at 16:00 for a short session. Diploma students with a late period usually settle on 18:00. The useful window on this coast runs roughly 17:30 to 20:45 on a school night, and families who protect it keep the arrangement running into March.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to a villa in Mina Al Arab or on Hayat Island?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for Ras Al Khaimah families is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Independent in-home tutors do work in Ras Al Khaimah and that arrangement is legal where the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit. The practical limit on this coast is subject depth: the number of people who can teach Higher Level Chemistry and will drive to the southern coast weekly is very small, so the choice is made on availability rather than on the subject your child actually sits.

faqs.question: How long is the drive from Mina Al Arab to a tuition centre in the city?
faqs.answer: Twenty to twenty-five minutes each way to Al Nakheel outside peak hours, and longer between 16:00 and 18:30 when the school run and the working day overlap. Including parking and waiting, a weekly 90-minute lesson in the city centre costs roughly an hour of car time on top of the lesson, or close to thirty hours over a 30-week school year. For a specialist in Sharjah or Dubai the figure is two to three hours a week, which is usually why that arrangement stops by November rather than being formally ended.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Year 10 student on this coast start with?
faqs.answer: Two, in one subject, for the first half-term. One session a week maintains a subject but rarely repairs one, because there is no second contact point to check whether the method actually transferred. Three or more only makes sense as a short block before mocks, with an end date agreed when it is booked. Starting with two in a single subject also keeps the diagnosis clean: if the grade moves, the approach is working, and a second subject can be added in the next term rather than everything changing at once.

faqs.question: Can two siblings in the same Mina Al Arab household share a session?
faqs.answer: Not usefully, unless they sit the same syllabus at the same level in the same year, which is uncommon. Two children on different boards need different papers, different command-term practice and different pacing, and a shared hour gives each of them half a lesson. Separate shorter sessions work better and often cost less in total than one long shared one. Where siblings do overlap, the sensible shared element is a timed paper sat side by side at the weekend, with the teaching handled separately afterwards.

faqs.question: What happens to our weekly slot during Ramadan in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: It moves, and the move is agreed before Ramadan begins. Private schools shorten the day, so children are home by early afternoon, and fasting teenagers are at their least alert between two and five. Post-iftar slots from around 20:30 work well for secondary students, while primary children often do better with a late-morning session on the shortened day. The schedule reverts to the term pattern afterwards. Families who renegotiate after the first missed lesson usually lose three sessions before settling, which is the avoidable part.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working in Ras Al Khaimah need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted at no charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published. Ask any individual tutor to show the permit before a first lesson.

faqs.question: Is a single 90-minute session better than two 45-minute ones for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: For Year 11, two shorter sessions usually beat one long one, because maths technique needs a gap in which the student attempts work alone and finds out what they cannot do. A single 90-minute block tends to become the tutor demonstrating for an hour. The exception is past-paper work: a full timed paper needs an uninterrupted block, so a sensible Year 11 pattern is two teaching sessions midweek plus one longer weekend slot for a timed paper and its review.

faqs.question: What internet connection does a live video lesson in Mina Al Arab need?
faqs.answer: A standard home fibre or 5G connection is sufficient. The demanding part is not video quality but shared screen work, where a tutor writes on a visible whiteboard while talking. A wired connection or a position close to the router removes most problems. Headphones matter more than most families expect, because a child working in a living room with siblings nearby will stop speaking, and a session where the student stops speaking has stopped being one-to-one teaching.

faqs.question: My son finishes school at 15:15 and is finished by five. How do we fit a lesson in?
faqs.answer: Feed him, let the school day settle, and start at 18:00. The collapse at five is normal after a day that began with a 06:45 bus, and it is not evidence that he cannot work in the evening. Most Diploma students on this coast are at their best between six and eight once they have eaten. If the evening genuinely does not work, a Friday or Saturday morning session is the stronger alternative to forcing a slot into the hour when he is least able to use it.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue while we travel out of Ras Al Khaimah over the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the summer is when the format earns its keep. Lessons run over live video, so they continue from wherever the family is, with the slot adjusted for the timezone difference and agreed before departure. Families who spend July and August abroad commonly use that period for the work there is never time for in term: the step up from MYP into Diploma maths, or the Year 10 content a Year 11 student never properly secured. Two sessions a week through August is a common pattern.

faqs.question: How late in Year 13 can a Diploma student on this coast start subject support?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, but what is achievable narrows. Starting in September of Year 13 leaves time to change content understanding across a subject. Starting in January means working on paper technique, question selection and the specific topics where marks are being dropped, which can still move a grade. Starting after study leave begins is damage limitation. Nobody should promise a particular grade at any of those starting points, and anyone who does is selling you something other than teaching.

faqs.question: What does IB and IGCSE tutoring cost per hour around Mina Al Arab?
faqs.answer: No rate table is published for Ras Al Khaimah, so the available figures are Dubai ones. Named providers publish bands of AED 45-150 for budget online tuition, AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180-500 for in-home visits where travel is priced in, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, with one premium provider publishing AED 650. Treat those as a ceiling for this emirate. IB Gram quotes after a consultation and arranges a trial lesson before any commitment to a term.

faqs.question: Who checks that the tutor actually knows the syllabus my child sits?
faqs.answer: The syllabus code does, and it is checked at matching rather than afterwards. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are different papers with different practical arrangements, and a tutor who has taught one is not automatically fluent in the other. Matching starts from the code on the entry statement, the level, and the specific topics the last report or mock flagged. The trial lesson is where that is tested: a tutor who cannot describe the paper structure in the first ten minutes is the wrong match.

faqs.question: Do you work with students at the RAK Academy and Indian School campuses?
faqs.answer: Students supported across Ras Al Khaimah attend the RAK Academy campuses at Al Hamra and Khuzam, RAK English Speaking School, and the Indian-curriculum campuses around Al Nakheel, as well as schools in Sharjah and Ajman where families make that commute. Those schools are named here as local context only. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to, endorsement from or commercial relationship with any of them, and no claim of accreditation from the Department of Knowledge or any examination board.

intro.heading: The course your child is on has a number, and it matters
paragraphs: Seih Al Uraibi sits in the established belt of Ras Al Khaimah city, a mixed residential district of villas, older apartment blocks and small commercial streets close to the creek and the main routes south. Children here attend the city-centre campuses, the Khuzam campus inland, and in a smaller number of cases the coastal schools, which means neighbouring households are frequently on different examination boards without knowing it.

That is the recurring problem in this district, and it is administrative rather than academic. A family buys a revision guide, downloads past papers, hires a tutor, and does all three for the wrong specification. Cambridge Physics 0625 and Pearson International GCSE Physics 4PH1 cover broadly similar content and assess it through different components, with different paper structures, different practical arrangements and different tiering. Practising one does not prepare a student for the other.

Nothing about the error is visible while it is happening. Content is being learned, questions are being answered, a tutor is turning up. The discovery usually comes in a mock, when a student meets a paper that does not look like anything they have practised, and by then a term has gone. It is the single most avoidable loss in the local market and it costs nothing to prevent: ask the school for the entry statement, which lists every subject with its code.

The second thing families here consistently find out too late is how the examination machinery works. What a grade boundary is, and why a mark of 70 is not 70 per cent. How a practical component is assessed when a student is tutored outside school. Whether a single paper can be resat. How many series a year each board runs, and what a November entry involves. None of this is secret and almost none of it is explained to parents.

This page sets all of it out: the two boards compared code by code, how practical science is actually credited, the tier decision and its grade ceiling, what a boundary is and how it moves, the resit routes, what to spend money on, and the independent work no school can do for a student. Tuition for Seih Al Uraibi families is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service offered only in India.

One orientation point, because the two are routinely confused. Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for schools in this emirate. Examination administration is a separate matter entirely and sits with Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, whose own published pages are the authority on any date, deadline, component rule or boundary.

ras-al-khaimah/seih-al-uraibi.programmesIntro: Three examination systems appear in this district, and each has its own administrative logic. The differences between them cause more lost marks locally than any single topic does.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Four-digit syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: One Cambridge administrative detail matters more in this region than most families realise. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable has been used. Ask your school which zone its centre sits in.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes combining digits and letters, such as 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4BI1 Biology. Pearson International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, with provisional timetables published ahead of each series.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's published dates show how early the real deadlines sit. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Because provisional timetables can be revised, a revision plan should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed components are marked by teachers against published criteria and then moderated, alongside terminal papers sat in the May session at almost every UAE school.
programmes.countryNote: No IB session or results date is published on this page. The IB's own assessment pages are the authority, and dates should be confirmed with your school's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from any tutoring site. What can be said confidently is that UAE schools sit the May session and that internal deadlines run many months ahead of it.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria marked out of eight, reported on a 1-7 scale, with an optional eAssessment at the end of MYP 5 delivered through on-screen examinations and ePortfolios.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP student moving into Year 10 IGCSE in this district meets a published mark scheme for the first time. The change is in format rather than content: method marks, command terms and working to time on a full paper. A term of timed practice in Year 10 handles it, and it is much better done then than discovered in a Year 11 mock.

ras-al-khaimah/seih-al-uraibi.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is listed with both boards' codes where they differ, because that is the level at which a revision plan has to be correct. The description names the component where the two boards diverge most.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended, Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Both boards tier the subject and both cap the grade on the lower tier, but the tier names, paper pairings and formula provision differ. Practising Cambridge Extended papers for a Pearson Higher entry trains the right content and the wrong paper, which is the most common version of this error locally.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The clearest divergence is the practical route. Cambridge offers centres a practical test or a written alternative-to-practical paper depending on arrangements; Pearson handles practical understanding within its own paper structure. A student must know which applies before any practical revision begins.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same divergence on the practical component, with the additional difference that question styles in extended response are not interchangeable. Moles and stoichiometry gate the rest of the course on either board, so that is where a diagnosis starts regardless of code.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Highest content volume of the sciences on both boards. The difference shows in extended-response question style and in how data-handling questions are framed, so past-paper practice has to come from the correct board to train the right answer shape.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Two Cambridge variants of the same subject with different speaking endorsement arrangements. A family that does not know which code the student is entered for cannot know whether a speaking component is being assessed, which is a question worth settling in Year 10.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Assessment structures differ substantially between boards, including the weighting of coursework where a centre offers it. The marking criteria are what a student should be writing to, and those are board-specific documents rather than general good-writing advice.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions used in question papers are board-specific, which surprises students who have practised on the other board's material. Trace tables and algorithm discipline carry a large share of marks and are highly trainable once the convention is right.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Command terms and case-study formats differ, and the proportion of the grade carried by data response varies. Students who answer at a uniform depth lose marks in both directions, which is a board-specific technique problem rather than a content one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Included because Year 11 students in this district are choosing between IGCSE tiers that determine whether this course stays open. Proof and calculus heavy, with marks lost in unstructured later questions and in the exploration's reflection criterion.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. Calculator operation errors account for a real share of lost marks, particularly in hypothesis testing, which makes calculator-specific practice part of any serious preparation.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum and taught to prescribed content. Where it is also examined at IGCSE, the code and the entry route are worth confirming early, since Arabic is excluded from the Ministry's five-subject equivalency count.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson compared, code by code
paragraphs: Both boards are respected, both are widely accepted by universities, and neither is meaningfully easier than the other. What differs is structure, and structure is what a student practises. The useful comparison is therefore not about standards but about components: how many papers, what each one does, how practical understanding is credited, and how the tiers are named and paired.

Codes are the entry point. Cambridge uses four digits, so 0580, 0625, 0620 and 0610 are mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology. Pearson International GCSE uses a digit and letters, so 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 are the equivalents. A family that knows those two patterns can read an entry statement and immediately see which board each subject sits with, including the mixed cases where a school uses different boards for different subjects.

The divergence that costs the most marks is the practical component in the sciences. Cambridge offers centres a choice between a practical test and a written alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson credits practical understanding within its own paper structure. A student revising for one when entered for the other has practised a component that does not exist on their paper, which is a loss no amount of content knowledge compensates for.

The second divergence is tiering. Cambridge names its mathematics tiers Core and Extended; Pearson names them Foundation and Higher. Both cap the grade available on the lower tier, and both make the decision in Year 10. The paper pairings and formula provision differ, so practice material has to match the tier as well as the board. The table sets out the pairs most often confused in this district.

sections.heading: How science practicals are credited, and what that means for online tuition
paragraphs: This is the question every family asks when tuition moves to video, and it deserves an unambiguous answer. Practical work is done at school, in the school laboratory, under the school's arrangements. No tutoring arrangement, in person or online, substitutes for that, and any provider implying otherwise is misdescribing what a school examination requires.

What is assessed in the examination, in both boards, is the student's written understanding of experimental work: identifying independent, dependent and control variables; explaining why a step improves the data; handling repeats, means and anomalies; drawing and reading graphs; calculating and expressing uncertainty; and suggesting a specific improvement rather than a generic one. All of that is written work, and all of it can be taught precisely over a shared screen.

It is also the most recoverable block of marks on a science paper, because the language is rarely taught explicitly. In a busy practical lesson the activity consumes the time, so students learn to do experiments and not to write about them. The characteristic marked answer describes the procedure, which earns little, instead of justifying it, which earns the marks. Two or three focused sessions change it.

The one thing to establish first is which practical route applies. Cambridge centres may use a practical test or the written alternative; Pearson credits practical understanding within its own structure. A student preparing for the wrong one has prepared for a paper they will not sit. Ask the school's examinations officer, and get it in writing alongside the syllabus code.

sections.heading: The tier decision and the grade ceiling it sets
paragraphs: In tiered subjects the entry a school makes determines the highest grade available before a single revision session happens. Cambridge mathematics 0580 runs Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher. The lower tier in each case caps the outcome, and the upper tier adds content as well as difficulty.

The decision is taken by the school on the basis of Year 10 performance and is often communicated as an administrative note rather than as the strategic choice it is. Families in this district frequently learn which tier applies only when the entry statement appears, by which point moving up means covering content the lower set never saw while the upper set is a term ahead.

Neither tier is correct for every student, and the honest framing matters. A lower-tier entry achieved comfortably is a better outcome than an upper-tier entry that collapses, and for a student who needs five subjects at no less than grade E or 3 for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a secure lower-tier pass may be exactly the right plan. The mistake is letting the decision happen by default.

Three questions settle it, asked before February of Year 10. Which tier is my child currently entered for. What marked evidence is that based on. What would have to change for the other tier to be viable. A tutor's job at that point is to say honestly whether the gap is closable in the time available, not to encourage the entry that generates more sessions.

sections.heading: What a grade boundary is, and why a mark is not a percentage
paragraphs: Very few parents in this district have had this explained, and it changes how a mock result should be read. A raw mark on an examination paper is not a percentage of an outcome. Each board converts raw marks into grades using boundaries set after the papers have been sat and marked, and those boundaries move between series because papers vary in difficulty.

The practical consequences are three. A mark that earned one grade last June may sit in a different band this June, so a student revising against last year's boundary is aiming at a moving target. A school mock marked against last year's boundaries is giving an indication rather than a prediction. And a student two or three marks below a boundary has not failed at understanding the subject; they have failed to collect three marks, which is a very different problem and usually a technique one.

This is also why counting marks beats reading grades when working out what to do. A paper that shows twelve marks lost to pacing and eight to method not shown is telling you where three grade boundaries' worth of marks are sitting, available, with no new content required. A grade on its own tells you none of that.

Boards publish boundary information after each series, and schools can access component-level marks. What should not happen is a tutoring provider reproducing or circulating boundary tables, syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because the boards hold copyright in all of them. The correct practice is to reference and link the official source, which is also the only version guaranteed to be current.

sections.heading: Resits, retakes and the two series a year
paragraphs: A disappointing result in June does not mean waiting a year. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June and a November series, and Pearson International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. That gives a student in this district a realistic second attempt within months rather than at the next annual cycle.

The decision about what to resit should be made from component marks rather than from the overall grade. A single unexpectedly weak component is a different problem from a subject that underperformed throughout, and the two justify entirely different amounts of work. The school's examinations officer can access the component breakdown, and it is the first thing to request after results.

Review and enquiry-about-results processes exist on both boards with their own short deadlines, and they close quickly after results are released. That ordering matters: read the component marks, ask the examinations officer whether a review is warranted and what the deadline is, then decide about a resit, then start any equivalency paperwork. Families who do these in a different order routinely miss the review window.

A resit entry has the same deadline logic as a first entry, which means months of lead time, and in the UAE it also means picking between two sittings rather than finding the next available one. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series here; the February/March series is offered to India only, so a candidate in Seih Al Uraibi who has just missed a grade is choosing between November of the same year and June of the next, not between February and June. Entries for a November resit are settled well before the autumn half-term, and entries for a June sitting close in the spring, months ahead of the papers. The exact dates come from the centre, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six timetable zones. Pearson's published figures give the concrete version of the same gap: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series which can be revised, so the live official timetable is the only safe reference.

The bands below carry the provider that publishes them and should be read as a ceiling rather than a local quote. The more useful question in this district is not what to pay but what to pay for, because several of the problems on this page cost nothing to fix.

Three things are free. Asking the school for the entry statement with syllabus codes. Asking which practical route applies to each science code. Asking the examinations officer which zone the centre sits in and for the component breakdown after results. Any family that does those three has eliminated the most expensive errors in the local market without spending anything.

What is worth paying for is narrower. Board-specific paper technique, where the mark scheme wording is read alongside the student's own answers. The written practical and data skills block, which is the single largest recoverable block on a science paper. And marked timed papers, because marking is the part that produces the result and the part that costs a tutor real time outside the session.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed hourly rate on these pages, and does not sell syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or boundary tables, because the boards hold copyright in all of them and the official versions are free to access. Pricing is quoted after a consultation and a trial lesson is arranged before any commitment.

sections.heading: If the budget covers two subjects, which two?
paragraphs: Most families in this district can fund one or two subjects rather than nine, which makes triage the real decision. It is usually made on anxiety, which selects the subject the student complains about most, and that is rarely the subject where the available marks sit. A better rule is to put money where recoverable marks are dense and the repair is fast.

Three things make a subject a good candidate. There are marks visibly lost to technique rather than to missing content, which the marked paper shows. The repair has a short timescale, such as paper pacing or practical writing, rather than a term of content rebuilding. And the subject matters to the next step, either because it is required for a sixth-form route or because it is one of the five subjects counted for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track.

Three things make a subject a poor candidate for paid support right now. The student is already secure and merely anxious. The content has not yet been taught, so a mock showing gaps is showing a timetable rather than a weakness. Or the whole subject needs rebuilding from an insecure foundation, which is real work and should be started in Year 10 rather than funded as an emergency in the spring of Year 11.

The triage below is the version that works in practice. Write every subject into one of the four rows using the marked paper rather than impressions, and fund from the top. A family that does this usually ends up funding a different pair of subjects from the one they arrived intending to fund, which is the point of doing it at all.

sections.heading: The independent work the school cannot do for your child
paragraphs: Everything above is administrative knowledge, and administrative knowledge only converts into marks through work the student does alone. That is the part of the course that was always designed to be independent, and it is where the gap between a well-taught class and a strong result actually sits.

The quantities are worth stating. Schools typically work through two or three past papers per subject in class across an exam year, which is enough to show the format. A student aiming at the top grades needs eight to twelve full papers per subject, sat to time and marked against the official scheme. That difference is not a criticism of any school; a class of twenty-five cannot be individually marked at that volume by one teacher.

The same applies to mark scheme literacy. Nobody is formally taught to read a mark scheme, yet it is the single document that explains how credit is awarded, and it is published free by the board. A student who reads the scheme alongside their own answer learns in ten minutes what a term of general advice does not convey. This is independent work by design, and almost nobody does it unprompted.

The honest conclusion for a family in Seih Al Uraibi is that tuition is most useful as a structure for that independent work rather than as a substitute for it. A tutor who marks papers, reads schemes with the student and sets specific practice between sessions is adding the thing the school has no capacity for. A tutor who re-explains content in a weekly hour is duplicating what the school already does well.

process.title: Get the entry statement in writing
process.description: Every subject with its syllabus code, from the school's examinations officer. Cambridge codes are four digits; Pearson International GCSE codes combine digits and letters. This single document prevents the most expensive error available in this district and costs nothing to obtain.

process.title: Confirm the practical route for each science
process.description: Whether a practical test or a written alternative applies, and which zone the centre sits in for timetabling. Both answers come from the examinations officer, and both determine what a student should be practising rather than what they assume they should.

process.title: Send the marked paper and the component marks
process.description: A marked mock shows where marks are going; component marks after a live series show which paper underperformed. Together they tell a tutor what to teach in the first session rather than in the third.

process.title: Trial lesson against the real paper
process.description: One session before any commitment, worked on the student's own marked paper from the correct specification. A tutor who cannot describe that paper's structure and weightings in the first ten minutes is not matched to the code, whatever their general subject knowledge.

process.title: Review at the next timed paper
process.description: Progress is measured on a full paper sat to time and marked to the official scheme, not on how sessions feel. If the marks lost by category have not moved by the second review, the approach changes rather than the student being asked to revise harder.

whyPoints.title: The code comes before the subject
whyPoints.description: Matching is done against the syllabus code and paper structure on the entry statement. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 assess similar content through different components, and practising the wrong one looks like progress right up until the mock.

whyPoints.title: Practical skills taught as written skills
whyPoints.description: Practical work stays at school. What tuition covers is the written component both boards credit: variables, justification, reliability, graph work, uncertainty and specific evaluation. It is the largest recoverable block on a science paper and is rarely taught explicitly.

whyPoints.title: Marks counted, not grades discussed
whyPoints.description: A raw mark is not a percentage, and boundaries move between series. Work is planned from marks lost by category on a real paper, which is where the available improvement is actually visible.

whyPoints.title: Official sources referenced, never redistributed
whyPoints.description: Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and boundary tables are the boards' copyright and are free from the boards themselves. They are linked, not supplied, and no family should ever buy them from a third party.

whyPoints.title: Resit decisions made from component marks
whyPoints.description: Both boards run two series a year, so a second attempt is months away rather than a year. The decision about what to resit is made from the component breakdown, and review windows are short, so the order of those steps matters.

whyPoints.title: Plain about what IB Gram is
whyPoints.description: An independent tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises and no accreditation from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Schools named on this page are local context only.

faqs.question: What is the actual difference between Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Structure rather than standard. Both are widely accepted and neither is meaningfully easier. Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0580 and 0625; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. The differences that matter in practice are the number and function of papers, how practical understanding is credited in the sciences, how the tiers are named and paired, and the pseudocode and command-term conventions used in question papers. Practising one board's papers does not prepare a student for the other's.

faqs.question: What does it mean if a school says a course is modular?
faqs.answer: It refers to whether components can be sat at different points rather than all at the end, and arrangements differ by specification and by what a centre offers. The authoritative answer for your child's course is the specification document on the board's own website plus the centre's own entry policy, because a board can offer flexibility that an individual school chooses not to use. Ask the examinations officer directly which components are being entered and in which series, and get the answer in writing alongside the codes.

faqs.question: Could two subjects at the same school sit with two different boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this district it happens more often than families realise. A school may use Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson for mathematics, or the reverse, and the entry statement is the only reliable record. It matters because revision material, past papers and tutoring all have to match each subject's own board. A single tutor can cover subjects across both boards, but they need to know which is which before the first session rather than discovering it halfway through a term.

faqs.question: How are science practicals assessed if my child is tutored online?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself is done at school, in the school laboratory, under the school's arrangements, and no tutoring substitutes for that. What the examination assesses is the written understanding of experimental work: naming variables, justifying method steps, handling repeats and anomalies, graph work, uncertainty, and suggesting a specific improvement. All of that is written and all of it can be taught precisely over a shared screen. Confirm first which practical route applies to your child's code, since Cambridge and Pearson handle it differently.

faqs.question: What is a grade boundary and why does it change every year?
faqs.answer: A boundary is the raw mark at which one grade becomes the next, and boards set them after papers have been sat and marked, so that a grade means the same thing even when one series' paper proves harder than another's. That is why a mark which earned one grade last June may fall in a different band this June. It also means a school mock marked against last year's boundaries gives an indication rather than a prediction, and it is worth asking which boundaries were applied.

faqs.question: Does a mark of 70 mean my son scored 70 per cent?
faqs.answer: No. A raw mark is the number of marks collected on that paper, not a percentage of anything, and it is converted to a grade using the boundaries set for that series. Papers also differ in total marks available, so the same raw mark means different things on different components. The useful figure is the component breakdown, which shows which paper underperformed, and then the marked paper itself, which shows the questions where the marks went.

faqs.question: Can a student resit a single paper rather than a whole subject?
faqs.answer: What can be re-entered depends on the specification and on the centre's entry policy, so the authoritative answer comes from the board's specification document and your school's examinations officer. The prior question is what should be resat, and that is answered from the component breakdown rather than the overall grade: a single unexpectedly weak component justifies a very different amount of work from a subject that underperformed throughout. Request those component marks as the first step after results.

faqs.question: Is a November resit better than waiting for the following June?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for two reasons. The content is still recent, and the student is still in the habit of working to that paper. Cambridge runs June and November series and Pearson runs May/June and November, so a second attempt is months rather than a year away. The constraint is the entry deadline, which sits well before the papers, and the preparation window being shorter than it looks. Decide quickly after results, once the component marks are in front of you.

faqs.question: Where do I find the official syllabus document for my child's course?
faqs.answer: On the board's own website, free. Cambridge publishes syllabuses by code on cambridgeinternational.org and Pearson publishes specifications on its qualifications site, along with past papers and mark schemes. Those are the definitive versions, and they are the only ones guaranteed to be current. No family should ever pay a third party for them, and a provider circulating them as downloads is infringing the board's copyright, which for unreleased material also carries a malpractice exposure.

faqs.question: Which of the two boards is easier?
faqs.answer: Neither, in any way that is useful to plan around. Both are standard-maintained qualifications with boundaries set after marking, so a difference in paper difficulty in one series is corrected at the boundary stage. What does differ is fit: a student who writes well under time pressure may find one board's extended-response style more comfortable, and a student who prefers structured calculation may prefer the other's paper pattern. In any case the board is chosen by the school, not the family, so the practical task is to prepare for the one on the entry statement.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tuition cost for a family in Seih Al Uraibi?
faqs.answer: No rate table is published for this emirate, so the figures available are Dubai ones and should be read as a ceiling. Named providers publish AED 45-150 an hour for budget online tuition, AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180-500 for in-home visits with travel priced in, and AED 200-450 or more for a specialist. Before spending anything, collect the three free items: the entry statement with codes, the practical route for each science, and the component marks after any series.

faqs.question: Our school changed boards between Year 10 and Year 11. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Get the new entry statement immediately and treat the change as a technique problem rather than a content one. The content overlap between the two boards is high; the paper structures, practical arrangements and question conventions are not. The practical steps are to discard past-paper material from the previous board, confirm the practical route for each science under the new one, and spend a short block on the new paper structure and its mark scheme wording before resuming ordinary revision.

faqs.question: Do you provide mark schemes and past papers to families?
faqs.answer: They are linked from the boards' own sites rather than supplied, because Cambridge, Pearson and the IB hold copyright in their syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and boundary tables. The official versions are free to access and are the only ones certain to be current. What a tutor adds is the marking: your child's own attempt marked against the published scheme, with the wording read alongside their answer so they can see exactly where credit was available.

faqs.question: How many papers does one IGCSE subject involve?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject, board and tier, which is why the specification document is the thing to read rather than a general rule. A tiered subject typically pairs two papers at each tier; the sciences add a practical component through either a practical test or a written alternative depending on the board and the centre; some languages add a speaking endorsement. The component weightings matter more than the count, because they tell a student where revision time should go, and they are published in the specification.

faqs.question: Can my child be entered for a subject the school does not teach?
faqs.answer: Through a recognised examination centre that accepts private candidates for that specification, with the entry made by the board's published deadline. The administration belongs to the family: finding a centre, making the entry, arranging any practical or speaking component, and paying the centre's fees. Cambridge also allocates centres to administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone timetable can mean a missed exam. A tutor can teach the syllabus and track the deadlines; nobody can register a candidate on a family's behalf.

ras-al-khaimah/seih-al-uraibi.closingHeading: Start with the code, then the component, then the marks
ras-al-khaimah/seih-al-uraibi.closingBody: Three free pieces of information eliminate most of what goes wrong in this district: the entry statement with syllabus codes, the practical route for each science, and the component breakdown after any series. Send us those and the last marked paper, and we will match a tutor who knows that specification's paper structure and mark scheme wording. Lessons are one-to-one over live video with shared screen working, past papers drawn only from the correct specification, and official documents linked rather than redistributed.

sharjah.tutorsIntro: The teachers below work the IB Diploma and Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE specifications your child is actually sitting. Each one teaches a short list of subjects at a named level rather than everything on a timetable, and each works with Sharjah families in the evening slot that survives the school run.

intro.heading: Start with the inspection report, not the tutor search
paragraphs: Most tutor searches in this emirate start in the wrong document. A parent types a phrase, collects five names and five hourly rates, and chooses on price or on who lives nearest. The more useful paper is already in the house. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, SPEA, which is a separate body from Dubai's KHDA and Abu Dhabi's ADEK, and its judgement on your child's school carries subject-level detail underneath the headline band. That detail tells you which departments catch a slipping student early and which ones will not.

A band describes systems, not children. A school judged Good can hold a Chemistry teacher who has marked Higher Level papers for a decade, and a school judged Very Good can have lost its only Mathematics Analysis and Approaches specialist in August. Read the report backwards instead: find the subject group your child sits at Higher Level or at Extended tier, read the attainment and progress line for it, and hold that against the predicted grades on the last report card. Where the two disagree, the school is either being generous or carrying your child on momentum, and that gap is the conversation a first tutoring call should be about.

Geography then decides what is possible. Al Nahda sits on the Dubai border at Al Qusais and empties into the heaviest school-run corridor in the country, so a three o'clock pickup in Dubai can put a family back indoors at half past four with a tired student and a full evening still to run. Al Majaz and Al Taawun send children in both directions across the Al Mamzar crossing. Muwaileh and University City feed large Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools within a few minutes of each other. Kalba and Khor Fakkan are under the same regulator but an hour and more of mountain road away from all of it, and IGCSE tuition in Al Nahda and tuition on the east coast are not the same logistical problem at all.

Our answer to both problems is the same. Tuition for families here is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and matched on the specification rather than on the postcode. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature: an online IB tutor in Sharjah can be the person who taught Physics Higher Level for fifteen years and knows how Paper 3 is marked, instead of the one teacher prepared to drive to Al Suyoh at six in the evening. The pool a family chooses from stops being a function of the traffic.

What follows is the reference material competitors in this market leave out. The AED bands the UAE tutoring market charges, with each figure attributed to whoever published it. The exam year counted backwards from results day. The internal assessment criteria by letter with their mark allocations. What Ministry of Education equivalency asks of an IB or IGCSE leaver. The line a tutor must not cross on coursework. None of it is a price list, because our own numbers depend on level and frequency and belong in a conversation, not in a table pretending to be a quote.

sharjah.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover almost every internationally schooled child in the emirate: the three IB programmes running in continuum schools, and Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE in the much larger British-curriculum set. Each one fails students in a different place, so each one needs a different kind of hour.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units rather than subject textbooks, and it reports on approaches to learning as much as on content. Parents moving in from an Indian or British primary often read a PYP report and cannot find the marks. There are none to find. What matters at this stage is reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining a method out loud, because all three are assumed by the Middle Years Programme and none of them is retaught.
programmes.countryNote: Several continuum schools in the emirate run the PYP and then hand students on to the MYP in the same building, which hides gaps for years. A Year 5 student in Al Zahia or Aljada who cannot yet hold two steps of a method in working memory will look fine in a unit of inquiry and will struggle badly in MYP 3 mathematics. Short, frequent sessions work far better at this age than a weekly hour.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against four criteria per subject on a one-to-eight scale, and those criterion scores convert to a grade through published boundaries. The usual shock is the criterion that rewards investigation and reflection rather than correct answers. A student who is strong at the mathematics and weak at explaining the mathematics will sit at a five. MYP 5 also carries the ePortfolio and the personal project, both of which are assessed on process and both of which reward early planning.
programmes.countryNote: Families here often move a child from MYP 5 into a Diploma Programme at a different school, sometimes across the border into Dubai, and the two institutions do not use the same internal standards. An MYP 5 seven in sciences is not a promise of a Diploma six. The reliable check is a past Diploma Paper 1 under timed conditions before the option forms are signed, which in this emirate usually means February of MYP 5.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Grades run one to seven, with up to three further points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix, for a maximum of forty-five. Internal assessment is typically a fifth of a science or mathematics grade. The Diploma punishes a student who is behind in two Higher Levels simultaneously, because the coursework deadlines of both land in the same fortnight of DP2.
programmes.countryNote: An IB Diploma tutor in Al Majaz or Al Khan is usually asked for in October of DP2, which is late but survivable, or in February, which is not. The emirate has fewer Diploma cohorts than Dubai, so a student taking an unusual combination such as Higher Level Economics with Higher Level Physics may be the only one in the year group with that timetable. Live video is the practical way to reach a teacher who has taught exactly that pairing.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum students here sit eight to ten IGCSEs across two years, at Core or Extended tier with Cambridge and at Foundation or Higher tier with Edexcel. The syllabus code on the exam entry matters more than the subject name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 cover similar ground and examine it differently, with different paper structures and different formula support. Grades are reported nine to one, with grade four as the standard pass reference point.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in Muwaileh and along the University City Road corridor enter students with Cambridge in some subjects and Edexcel in others, which is legitimate and frequently missed by a tutor who asks only which school a student attends. An IGCSE tutor in Muwaileh should know the board and the tier before the first lesson, and a parent can get both from the statement of entry rather than from the textbook cover.

sharjah.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Sharjah families ask for most, at the levels they ask for them. A request for an IB Maths AA tutor in Sharjah is really a request for one of four different courses, so the level and the board come first and the teacher comes second.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level sits on proof, calculus and complex numbers, and Paper 3 asks for extended reasoning with no obvious route in. Marks disappear in the middle of long questions where method is implied rather than written. The twenty-mark exploration is where a student can bank security early, and criterion D, reflection, is where most of this emirate's cohorts lose it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and graph theory, with the graphic display calculator treated as part of the method rather than a convenience. Students who switched from Analysis and Approaches in DP1 usually arrive fluent in algebra and unpractised at interpreting output in context, which is exactly what the papers reward. Check which course UAE and overseas engineering admissions expect before switching.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Higher Level additions in fields, induction and quantum physics are conceptually separate from the Standard Level core, so a student cannot revise their way across the gap. Paper 2 long questions are lost on units, significant figures and unstated assumptions far more often than on the physics itself. The scientific investigation is marked on research design before any data exists.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the two topics that separate a five from a seven, and both reward drawing before writing. Data-based questions require fluency with the data booklet, which is a trainable skill and rarely trained. Students here frequently ask for help on the investigation after collecting unusable data, which is six weeks too late.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. The command terms do the work: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate carry different mark expectations, and a correct answer written to the wrong command term earns nothing. Higher Level adds depth in plant biology and genetics that Standard Level students never see, so cross-level study groups mislead everyone involved.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal assessment commentaries on published news articles carry twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade and thirty per cent at Standard Level. Diagrams must be labelled fully and must be referred to in the prose. Higher Level Paper 3 is quantitative and is where students who treated economics as an essay subject run out of time.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The tools, techniques and theories list is examinable and finite, and candidates lose marks by answering from general business sense instead of from it. Paper 1 works from a pre-released case study that rewards months of preparation and usually gets days. Higher Level extension topics appear in Paper 2 section C with no warning.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, and the guiding question is a gift that most candidates ignore. The Higher Level essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words is twenty per cent of the grade and is written in DP2 alongside everything else. Second-language speakers need the analytical vocabulary taught explicitly rather than absorbed.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended tier reaches to grade nine and Core caps at grade five, so tier choice decides a ceiling before any revision happens. Both papers are calculator and non-calculator split, and the formula support is thinner than most students expect. Working shown earns method marks even when the final answer is wrong, which is the cheapest grade gain available.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper is a distinct skill from the theory papers: it tests apparatus, variables, anomalous readings and graph plotting. Students taught online practise it on scanned past papers and often outscore classmates who did the experiments and never analysed them. Electricity and circuit calculations are the single largest source of lost Extended marks.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, a different formula sheet from Cambridge and a question style that leans more on multi-step problems in context. A student moving school mid-Year 10 between a Cambridge centre and an Edexcel centre is changing specification, not just teacher, and needs the differences mapped rather than assumed away.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic A is for first-language speakers and Arabic B for additional-language learners, and placing a student in the wrong one wastes two years. The Diploma Arabic B assessments reward prepared text types and consistent register. For many families in the emirate this is the subject with the widest gap between home fluency and written examination performance.

sharjah.regionsTitle: Districts we work with across the emirate
sharjah.regionsIntro: Sharjah is not one tutoring market. A district's schools, its commute and the hour at which a student is finally free decide what a weekly session can look like, and those three things differ sharply between the corniche, the University City corridor and the east coast.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Dense apartment blocks along the lagoon with schools within walking distance, so the school run is short and a session can realistically start at half past four. Families here are split between Sharjah schools and a Dubai commute, which is why two siblings in one flat often need different slots.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Straddles the Dubai border at Al Qusais and carries the heaviest cross-emirate school traffic in the country. A three o'clock pickup in Deira or Al Qusais regularly turns into ninety minutes of road, so evening slots from six work and afternoon slots quietly collapse.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Lagoon-side towers close to the Al Mamzar crossing, with a mixed Indian and Arab expatriate population and a strong British-curriculum pull. IGCSE requests dominate here, usually in mathematics and the separate sciences, and usually in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

regions.name: Al Taawun and Al Qasimia
regions.note: Older high-rise districts feeding both local schools and Dubai campuses across Al Mamzar. Two working parents is the norm, so the viable window is often after seven in the evening, which rules out most tutors who are also full-time classroom teachers in the same time zone.

regions.name: Muwaileh and University City
regions.note: The emirate's largest concentration of school places, with Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum campuses minutes apart along University City Road. Mixed-board entries are common here, so the statement of entry matters more than the school name when matching a tutor.

regions.name: Aljada, Al Zahia and Al Mamsha
regions.note: Newer master communities with younger cohorts moving through the Primary and Middle Years Programmes. Demand is heaviest for MYP mathematics and sciences, and Diploma specialists are genuinely scarce within driving distance, which is where live video stops being a preference.

regions.name: Tilal City, Sharjah Garden City and Al Suyoh
regions.note: Villa communities out along the Emirates Road corridor where the school run is a highway run in both directions. Seven o'clock starts are standard, and a session that has to survive a forty-minute drive at both ends rarely survives the term.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan and Kalba
regions.note: East-coast exclaves under the same regulator as the city, separated from it by the Hajar mountain road. The local pool of Diploma subject specialists is very thin, so Khor Fakkan online tuition is often the only route to a Higher Level Chemistry or Economics teacher at all.

sections.heading: What SPEA inspects, and how to read the verdict
paragraphs: SPEA licenses, inspects and approves fees for private schools across the emirate, including the east-coast exclaves at Kalba and Khor Fakkan. An inspection looks at students' attainment and progress subject group by subject group, at the quality of teaching and assessment, at the curriculum, at how well the school protects and supports its students, and at leadership and management. The overall judgement is the band parents repeat to each other at the gate. The subject-level lines underneath it are the part that should change what a family does next, and almost nobody reads them.

The national school inspection framework runs on six bands from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The top two describe a school whose systems notice a slipping student before the parent does. Good and Acceptable describe schools where that noticing depends on the individual teacher your child happens to have. Weak and Very Weak describe a school working through an improvement plan, which is a reasonable thing for a school to do and an unaffordable thing for a Year 11 or DP2 cohort to wait for. None of the bands says anything about one child in particular.

So read it as a map of risk. Take the subject your child sits at Higher Level or at Extended tier, read the attainment and progress judgement for that subject group, and compare it with the predicted grade on the most recent report card. Agreement means the school's internal standard is calibrated and you can trust the prediction. Disagreement means one of the two is wrong, and the exam will decide which. Ask the school directly for its most recent SPEA inspection report: the emirate does not maintain a school-by-school public archive in the form Dubai parents have grown used to.

sections.heading: Three authorities and one awarding body: who governs what
paragraphs: A family in this emirate deals with more education bodies than a family in Dubai does, and they are routinely confused with one another. SPEA licenses and inspects the school. If the sibling crosses the border to a Dubai campus, that school answers to KHDA and is inspected by its own framework on its own cycle, which is why two report cards from the same household are not on a shared scale. The federal Ministry of Education does not inspect your private school here, but it is the body that decides whether a foreign leaving certificate counts as equivalent to the UAE secondary certificate.

The private-tutoring permit is a fourth thing again. It is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and every government source we could check states that it is granted free of charge. A tutor who is employed elsewhere needs their employer's no-objection as part of the application. We have deliberately not published a figure for penalties: the reporting on this says the ministry did not specify the fine amounts, and a number circulating online that cannot be traced to a ministry statement is not something to plan around.

The IB, Cambridge and Pearson are awarding bodies, not regulators. They set the specification, write and mark the papers, and moderate internal assessment. A query about a mark goes to the awarding body through the school's exams officer, on the awarding body's own deadline, and not to SPEA. Knowing which door to knock on saves a term: the table below is the version of this a parent can keep.

sections.heading: Ministry equivalency: the paperwork an IB or IGCSE leaver needs
paragraphs: Equivalency is the Ministry of Education recognising a foreign school-leaving certificate as equal to the UAE secondary certificate. A family heading straight to a British or North American university often never needs it. A family applying to a UAE federal or public university, applying for a government scholarship, or expecting the student to work in the public sector or a licensed profession here almost certainly does. MoE equivalency for IB students is not difficult, but it is sequential, and every step of it depends on documents that are easier to collect while the family is still in the country.

The failure mode is always timing. Transcripts need attestation, attestation takes a queue, and the queue is slower from abroad than from Sharjah. A transfer certificate from a previous school in another country, unattested at the time of the move, becomes a two-month problem three years later. On the British route the subject count is the trap: a student who quietly dropped a science in Year 12 can find the count no longer satisfies the condition, long after the decision could have been changed.

Treat the published conditions as live rather than settled. They have been revised more than once, the detail differs between the IB route and the Cambridge or Edexcel route, and a school office repeating what was true three years ago is a common source of bad advice. Ask for the current requirement in writing, dated, and keep it. The table is the shape of the process, not a substitute for that document.

sections.heading: What one-to-one tuition costs in this market, in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six agency pages ranking for tuition queries in this country publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency any family here transacts in. So here are the bands, in AED, with the source of each figure named. They are market rates. They are not our rate card, and no page that gives you a single number for a category this wide is telling you anything useful.

Two things move a rate more than anything else. Format is the first: an hour in which a tutor travels carries the travel inside the price, which is most of the gap between the online bands and the in-home bands. Level is the second: Higher Level Diploma sciences and mathematics cost more than IGCSE in every published list, because the teaching pool is smaller. Monthly packages are common and worth comparing carefully. Published examples include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Ask three questions of any quote. Is the price per hour or per session, because a ninety-minute session quoted as a session price is a different number. Is VAT included or added. And what happens if you stop after one lesson. Our own model is a free trial lesson and a consultation that sets level and frequency first, because a rate quoted before anyone has seen the student's marked work is a guess with a decimal point on it.

sections.heading: A tutor in the room or a tutor on the screen: the arithmetic here
paragraphs: Home tuition is a real service with real advantages, and it deserves an honest answer rather than a dismissal. A tutor sitting beside a twelve-year-old can see a pencil hesitate. A parent can hear the lesson from the next room. For a primary-age child with a short attention span, that physical presence is worth something no camera supplies. What it costs is the gap between roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour online and roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, plus the forty to ninety minutes of road that the tutor either charges for or absorbs by teaching fewer students.

The second cost is choice, and in this emirate it is the larger one. Dubai has enough Diploma cohorts that someone who has taught Chemistry Higher Level for a decade probably lives within a reasonable drive of most districts. Here the number of Diploma cohorts is smaller, and on the east coast the mountain road makes the question academic. A family in Kalba choosing from tutors willing to drive to Kalba is not choosing from teachers of their child's subject. They are choosing from drivers who also teach.

Which is why IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one tuition over live video, with a shared screen, an annotated past paper and a file left behind after every session. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody will be sent to an address in this country. The comparison below is the case on its merits: same hour, wider pool, lower price, better record. Decide it on the rows rather than on the word.

sections.heading: The exam year counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what decides whether tuition arrives in time to matter. Count backwards. IB papers run through May with results released in early July. Cambridge and Edexcel's June series is the one almost every school here enters, with results in August. The October and November series exists for resits and November-entry candidates, with results in January. Cambridge's February and March series runs for India only and is not available to centres in this country, which catches out families who move here from Mumbai or Delhi mid-cycle.

Registration is owned by the school's exams officer, not by you, and the internal deadline for it sits months before the exam. A resit decision taken in February for a June series is usually a decision taken after the entry closed. The same is true at the other end: the window for an enquiry upon results after August or July is short and runs on the awarding body's clock, so the question to ask the exams officer is not whether a remark is possible but by which date the request must reach them.

Then there is Ramadan, which in these years falls across the stretch between mocks and study leave. School days shorten, energy drops in the afternoon and the evening reorganises itself around Iftar. A Ramadan tutoring schedule in Sharjah that pretends none of this is happening will be abandoned by the second week. Ours moves to post-Iftar slots at forty-five minutes rather than sixty, keeps the frequency, and returns to full length afterwards. Frequency protects a student's momentum far better than length does.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria by letter, and the marks students leave behind
paragraphs: Internal assessment is the one part of a Diploma grade that can be secured calmly, months before any exam, and it is the part most families treat as an afterthought. It is marked by the school's own teacher and then externally moderated by the IB, which means a generous internal mark can be scaled down across a whole cohort. A high mark from a school is therefore not a banked grade. A piece of work that scores well against the published descriptors is.

Those descriptors are public, they are organised by criterion letter, and each letter carries a stated number of marks. That is the whole trick. A student who knows that the mathematics exploration gives six marks for use of mathematics and three for reflection will not spend a fortnight on presentation. A student who knows the scientific investigation gives equal weight to research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation will not collect data for three weeks before deciding what the question was.

The pattern across cohorts here is consistent and it is not a content problem. Marks go in criterion D of the mathematics exploration, where students describe what they did instead of reflecting on what the result meant. They go in criterion D of the scientific investigation, where weaknesses are listed without a realistic improvement attached. They go in the economics commentaries, where a correct diagram is never referred to in the prose. A tutor's job on all of these is to mark the student's own draft against the letters and hand it back, which is also the only thing a tutor is permitted to do.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may touch and what stays the student's
paragraphs: One agency in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750. That is not tutoring, and a student who submits one is exposed to a malpractice finding that can cost the whole diploma rather than one subject grade. The supervisor signs a declaration that the work is the student's own, and moderators read thousands of scripts a season and recognise an adult's register in a sixteen-year-old's essay. There is no version of this that is a shortcut. It is a risk transfer from the seller to your child.

The permitted ground is wide and most families underestimate it. A tutor can teach the skill the task requires, model the same technique on a completely different dataset or text, ask the questions a good supervisor would ask, mark a draft against the published criteria and explain why a criterion scored what it scored, and teach referencing to the school's required style. What a tutor cannot do is write a sentence that goes into the submission, restructure a draft line by line, supply the data, or choose the research question outright. The test is simple: could the student explain and defend every decision in an oral?

Artificial-intelligence tools now sit inside the same question, and the school's own policy governs them. The IB's position is that use must be acknowledged and that unacknowledged generated text is misconduct. Extended Essay support in Sharjah that leans on a generator to produce a literature review is the same breach as buying one, with a worse writing style. Our coaching assumes the student writes, the tutor questions and marks, and the record of drafts shows exactly that progression if anyone asks.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Studies and UAE Social Studies around a Diploma timetable
paragraphs: Every internationally schooled child in this country carries subjects that sit outside their examined programme. The Ministry of Education requires private schools to teach Arabic, with Arabic A for first-language speakers and Arabic B for additional-language learners, and Islamic Education for Muslim students; Moral, Social and Cultural Studies appears alongside them at defined stages. The precise point at which each requirement ends varies by cohort and has been revised, so confirm the current rule with the school office rather than with another parent.

These subjects rarely appear in a tutoring conversation, and they are frequently the reason a conversation was needed. They occupy real periods in the week, they carry homework and assessment, and they appear on the school report that a parent reads for signs of trouble. A DP1 student with three Higher Levels, an Extended Essay, Arabic B and Islamic Education has a week with no slack in it. The subject that gives way is usually the Higher Level with the latest deadline, which is how a student arrives in October of DP2 two topics behind in mathematics.

They also matter to the equivalency record described earlier, because enrolment and assessment in the mandated subjects form part of what the Ministry examines. A student who joined a school here in Year 10 from overseas can carry gaps that nobody notices until a university application. The practical response is to timetable around them honestly: put the tuition slot where the week actually has room, keep sessions shorter and more frequent rather than long and heroic, and treat Arabic as a subject to be planned for rather than absorbed.

The trial lesson is a real lesson with real content, not an introduction, and the student's view of it counts more than yours. A bad fit here costs an hour instead of a term.

whyPoints.description: The first questions are the board, the syllabus code and the tier: Cambridge 0580 or Edexcel 4MA1, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Core or Extended. Schools in Muwaileh regularly split entries across two boards, and a tutor who assumed the board from the school name teaches the wrong paper structure for a term.
