faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Sharjah, and does it change how I pick a tutor?
faqs.answer: Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by SPEA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which is separate from Dubai's KHDA and Abu Dhabi's ADEK. It inspects schools rather than tutors, so there is no such thing as a regulator-endorsed private tutor here. What it changes is where you start. The subject-level attainment and progress judgements in your school's inspection report tell you which departments are strong and which depend on one teacher, and that is the gap tuition should be aimed at. Ask the school for its most recent report and read the subject lines rather than the overall band.

faqs.question: What do the six inspection bands in a school report actually mean for my child?
faqs.answer: The national framework runs from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable to Weak and Very Weak. They describe the school's systems, not your child. Outstanding and Very Good mean the school usually spots a slipping student before you do, so predicted grades tend to be reliable. Good and Acceptable mean that depends on the individual teacher. Weak and Very Weak mean an improvement plan is running, which a Year 11 or DP2 student cannot afford to wait for. Use the band to judge how much to trust the prediction, then check the prediction against a timed past paper.

faqs.question: Can I see my own school's SPEA inspection report before I enrol?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly and ask for the most recent one with the subject-level detail, not a summary slide. The emirate does not maintain the school-by-school public archive that Dubai parents are used to browsing, so the school office is the practical route. A school confident in its report will share it. If a school will not, that is information too. Read the attainment and progress lines for the subject group your child will sit at Higher Level or Extended tier, because that is the part that affects your decision rather than the headline judgement.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tutors charge per hour in this emirate in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published market rates across the country run from about AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget online tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for a tutor who travels to a home, AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500 to 650 or more at examiner level. EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65, Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are other providers' numbers. Ours follow a free trial lesson and a consultation.

faqs.question: Is a tutor physically in the room worth the extra AED an hour here?
faqs.answer: For a young child with a short attention span, sometimes. For a Diploma or IGCSE student, the money buys travel rather than teaching. The gap between roughly AED 150 to 300 online and AED 180 to 500 with a visit is the car. More importantly, this emirate has fewer Diploma cohorts than Dubai, and on the east coast the mountain road makes local choice almost theoretical. A family choosing only from tutors willing to drive to their district is choosing from drivers who also teach, rather than from teachers of their child's subject.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private-tutoring permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and every government source we could check states that it is granted free of charge. A tutor already employed elsewhere needs their employer's no-objection as part of the application. You can simply ask a tutor whether they hold a current permit and under what name. We have not published penalty figures here, because the reporting on this states the ministry did not specify the fine amounts, and an unverified number is not something to plan around.

faqs.question: We live in Al Nahda and my daughter's school is in Dubai. When can a session realistically start?
faqs.answer: Later than you think. A three o'clock pickup in Al Qusais or Deira regularly turns into ninety minutes of road at that hour, which puts a tired student indoors at half past four with homework still to do. Sessions from six in the evening hold through the term; sessions at four quietly collapse by October. If both parents work, a seven o'clock start with a forty-five minute session is more durable than a longer slot earlier. The point of online delivery here is that the tutor's own commute never enters the calculation.

faqs.question: How should a tutoring schedule change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, afternoons are low on energy, and the evening reorganises around Iftar. A schedule that ignores all three is abandoned by the second week. We move sessions to post-Iftar timing, shorten them from sixty minutes to forty-five, and keep the frequency unchanged, because frequency protects momentum far better than length does. This matters most in February and March, which is exactly the stretch between mocks and study leave when past-paper discipline decides outcomes. Agree the arrangement before Ramadan starts rather than renegotiating it mid-month.

faqs.question: Does my child need Ministry equivalency after finishing the IB Diploma here?
faqs.answer: If they are going straight to a university abroad, usually not. If they are applying to a UAE federal or public university, seeking a government scholarship, or expecting to work in the public sector or a licensed profession here, then yes. MoE equivalency for IB students needs the IB transcript, the diploma record and an attested school letter. The common failure is timing: attestation takes a queue, and the queue is far slower once the family has left the country. Start the week July results are confirmed, while the school office is still accessible.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Studies fit around a Diploma or IGCSE timetable?
faqs.answer: They occupy real periods, carry homework, and appear on the school report. The Ministry requires private schools to teach Arabic, with Arabic A for first-language speakers and Arabic B for additional-language learners, and Islamic Education for Muslim students, with Moral, Social and Cultural Studies alongside at defined stages. The stage at which each requirement ends has been revised, so confirm the current rule with the school. Practically, a DP1 week with three Higher Levels plus these subjects has no slack, and the subject that gives way is the Higher Level with the latest deadline.

faqs.question: Which internal assessment criteria cost students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Criterion D, twice over. In the mathematics exploration, reflection carries three marks and students describe what they did instead of reflecting on what the result meant. In the scientific investigation, evaluation carries six and students list weaknesses without attaching a realistic improvement. In economics, the commentaries lose marks on unlabelled diagrams that are never referred to in the prose. In the Extended Essay, criterion C, critical thinking, carries twelve of thirty-four marks and typically receives a quarter of the student's time. All four are fixable in a fortnight if caught before the final draft.

faqs.question: What exactly is a tutor allowed to do with an IA or an Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the skill the task needs, model the method on entirely different material, ask the questions a good supervisor asks, mark the student's own draft against the published criteria and explain each mark, and teach referencing in the school's style. A tutor may not write a sentence for the submission, restructure a draft line by line, supply data, or choose the research question. One agency in this market sells completed assessments at around AED 3,750; a student who submits one risks a malpractice finding against the whole diploma, not one grade.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Read the statement of entry rather than the textbook cover. It names the board, the syllabus code and the tier, which is what a tutor actually needs: Cambridge Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier is a different paper structure and a different formula provision from Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 at Higher tier. Several schools along the University City Road corridor enter students with Cambridge in some subjects and Edexcel in others, legitimately, so one answer for the whole timetable is often wrong. Check subject by subject before booking anything.

faqs.question: Mocks are six weeks away and the marks are poor. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the scope narrowed hard. Six weeks is enough to fix command-term errors, method marks that were never written down, and two or three topics that carry disproportionate paper weight. It is not enough to reteach a two-year syllabus, and anyone saying otherwise is selling. We start from the last marked script, not the report card, and work backwards from the paper that carries most marks. The honest ceiling is a grade, sometimes two in a subject where the gap is technique rather than content.

faqs.question: Does live video work for a student in Khor Fakkan or Kalba?
faqs.answer: It works better there than almost anywhere else in the emirate. Both towns sit under the same regulator as the city and an hour or more of mountain road away from its tutoring pool, so the realistic local choice of a Higher Level Chemistry or Economics teacher is close to none. Khor Fakkan online tuition removes the drive from the equation entirely: the student sees the same shortlist an Al Majaz family sees, at the same hours, with a shared screen, annotated past papers and a file left behind after each session.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's subject combination?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting someone who nearly fits. A student taking Higher Level Economics with Higher Level Physics may be the only one in their year group with that pairing, and the right teacher for each is two different people with two different slots. If one of them has no availability for a few weeks, we tell you the date, and you can decide whether to wait or to start with the other subject. A generalist booked into a Higher Level slot wastes a term that an exam year does not have.

sharjah.closingHeading: Start with the report, then book one trial lesson
sharjah.closingBody: Two documents decide most of this. The subject-level lines in your school's inspection report, which tell you where the school is strong and where it depends on one teacher, and your child's most recent marked script, which tells you whether the gap is content or technique. Send us both and we will go through the script question by question on a thirty-minute call, and tell you honestly if the school has it in hand. If tuition is the right answer, you get a short list of teachers who work that specification at that level, a free trial lesson, and a weekly slot set around the commute you actually have.

sharjah/al-juraina.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the subjects Al Juraina households most often price up: IGCSE Mathematics and the separate sciences, Diploma Biology and Chemistry at both levels, and Internal Assessment supervision. Rates depend on subject, level and the balance of teaching to supervision, which is what the consultation establishes.

intro.heading: Why the quotes you have collected disagree so violently
paragraphs: Al Juraina is one of the older established residential districts of central Sharjah, sitting inland of the creek among the commercial and light-industrial spine of the city. It is a long-settled area rather than a new development, with villa households whose children attend a wide spread of schools and whose parents have usually been doing this for a while. The enquiries we get from here are, more than from anywhere else in the emirate, framed around price.

That framing is reasonable, because the published spread is absurd. A parent who rings four providers for help with Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry will be quoted figures from under AED 50 an hour to over AED 600, and every one of those quotes is real. Published UAE rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33-52 at the budget end of one online platform to AED 650 for a premium named tutor at another, which is a tenfold spread for what sounds like the same hour of the same subject.

Almost none of that spread is explained by the subject. It is explained by who is teaching, how they are employed, and whether they are travelling. A university student revising alongside your child sits at the bottom. A qualified subject teacher working online sits in the middle. An in-home visit costs roughly a third more than the equivalent online rate, and that third is fuel and driving time rather than teaching. A named specialist with examining experience sits at the top, and in the eight weeks before a written series they are scarce enough to hold that price.

The more important number, and the one nobody quotes, is the number of hours. A correctly diagnosed technique problem - command terms on Paper 2, method marks not shown, pacing across a full paper - can resolve in eight to ten sessions. The same student with a tutor re-teaching content they already knew can absorb forty sessions and finish in the same place. That is a four-fold difference in total cost, which dwarfs the difference between a mid-band and a specialist rate. Ask what the hours are for before you negotiate what they cost.

Everything below is a breakdown rather than a pitch. There is a table of provider models with the published rate for each, a table of what moves a quote, a table of the extras that appear on bills, and a two-year worked example. We do not publish an IB Gram price list on these pages, because the honest figure depends on subject, level and how much of the work is supervision. Delivery is one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, as home visits are a service we run only in India.

sharjah/al-juraina.programmesIntro: Cost behaves differently by programme, and not in the way parents expect. The note under each programme is about what drives the bill rather than what the course contains.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: The cheapest programme to support, because supply is deep. Mathematics, the separate sciences and English are staffed at every price point, which means a parent genuinely has choice and the mid-band is competitive. The cost risk here is not the rate, it is buying support in six subjects when two are the problem, which happens frequently in Year 11 when panic arrives.
programmes.countryNote: Published figures put a qualified online IGCSE tutor around AED 150 upwards. The cost-sensitive decision in Al Juraina households is usually how many subjects to support rather than at what rate, and the answer is almost always fewer than the family first proposes. Confirm the board and syllabus code before paying anyone, because teaching the wrong paper structure wastes the opening sessions.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most expensive programme to support, for two reasons. Specialism is narrower, so the rate sits in the specialist band rather than the qualified-tutor band, and the programme runs two years with coursework in the middle, so the natural engagement is longer. A two-year Diploma plan is the largest tutoring commitment most families ever make, which is why it deserves a worked total rather than a monthly figure.
programmes.countryNote: Published figures put IB specialist support around AED 200-450 and above per hour. The cost lever specific to the Diploma is the balance between teaching hours and supervision hours: supervision on an Internal Assessment is a handful of well-placed sessions rather than a weekly commitment, and families who understand that distinction spend considerably less.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Inexpensive to support and frequently over-bought. The marks in the MYP sit in criterion literacy rather than content, so a small number of sessions explaining exactly what each criterion rewards produces more movement than a term of general subject work. Families who buy weekly MYP tutoring for two years are usually paying for reassurance rather than for a measurable gap.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Juraina households with several children, the honest advice is to spend the MYP budget on building algebraic fluency in MYP 4 and 5. That is what keeps the harder Diploma mathematics route open later, and repairing it in DP1 costs several times as much because the rate band is higher.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Mid to upper band, with cost concentrated into the months before a series. Because the assessment is almost entirely terminal written papers, the efficient spend is on timed paper practice with individual marking rather than on content teaching, which the school covers well. That makes a short intensive at a higher rate better value than a cheap year-long arrangement.
programmes.countryNote: For families planning UAE university entry, the published British-track equivalency route asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3 plus one Advanced Level subject at E or above or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. That is a document requirement, not a reason to buy tutoring.

sharjah/al-juraina.subjectsIntro: The note against each subject below is about cost: how many sessions the common problem in that subject usually takes, because that is the figure that determines what you spend rather than the rate.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The cheapest subject to support because supply is deepest. The commonest problem, method marks lost through working not being shown, takes four to six sessions. Students who need the whole Extended syllabus rebuilt are a different and much longer proposition, which is why the distinction matters before buying.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The practical paper is the high-yield, low-cost fix: three to five sessions on experimental method language, control variables and systematic error. Electricity and electromagnetism as a content rebuild is a longer and more expensive piece of work, so diagnose which one you are buying.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Reacting masses and limiting reagents are the usual gap and they take three to four consecutive sessions, close together rather than weekly, because the method decays. Buying a weekly slot for a year to fix a calculation is the classic over-purchase in this subject.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Terminology to the syllabus wording plus data interpretation, typically four to six sessions. Inexpensive to fix and commonly diagnosed as a general weakness, which turns a short job into a long one at the parent's expense.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: Data-handling technique is the efficient target, around six to eight sessions, with Internal Assessment supervision costed separately as two to four sessions per draft. Content teaching across the whole course is the expensive option and rarely the necessary one.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are a genuine content block and price accordingly. The Internal Assessment analysis criterion, by contrast, is a short fix: uncertainty treatment explained once and applied to the student's own data.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 3 investigation technique at Higher Level takes six to ten sessions and sits in the specialist rate band. Standard Level proof and reasoning work is shorter and cheaper. Knowing which of the two you are buying changes the total by a large multiple.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator and statistical-function fluency is one of the cheapest wins in the Diploma, often two or three sessions, because the content is not the obstacle. Modelling interpretation takes longer. Both are worth separating on a quote.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis needs 90-minute sessions to be worth buying at all, and typically six to ten of them. It is the subject where a cheap short session is most clearly false economy, because a plan that never becomes a marked paragraph teaches nothing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation structure are quick. The Higher Level quantitative paper is a specialist job in a scarce band. Pricing these as one subject is how families end up paying a premium rate for diagram practice.

subjects.name: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay supervision
subjects.description: Costed as a small number of well-placed sessions rather than a weekly slot: narrowing the question at the start, then criterion feedback on the student's own draft. Four to six across a project is a common shape. Nothing is authored for the student.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies
subjects.description: Low rate and short sessions, two or three times a week at thirty to forty-five minutes, working on the school's own material. Cheap to maintain and expensive to rescue, which argues for starting it before a report card forces the issue.

sections.heading: What each provider model charges, with the source named
paragraphs: Every competitor page researched for this project compares itself against an unnamed set of other platforms. That is not a comparison, it is a straw man. The table below compares provider models instead - agency, marketplace, independent tutor, tuition centre, school-run support - and quotes published figures only where a provider published them, with the month they were read. We do not comment on any competitor's quality or legality, only on their own stated prices.

The structural point is that each model carries a different cost base. An agency adds a matching and quality layer and charges for it. A marketplace is cheaper per hour and leaves verification to you. An independent tutor keeps the whole fee and may or may not hold the MoHRE permit, which is worth asking about. A tuition centre spreads a teacher's hour across several students, which is why the per-student rate is lowest and the attention per student is too.

School-run support is the one model most families forget to price, and it is frequently free or near-free. Many schools run revision sessions, clinics or coursework drop-ins that cover exactly what a parent is about to pay for. Asking the school what it already provides, before buying anything, is the first cost-saving step and it costs nothing. We would rather say that than pretend private tutoring is the only route.

One honest note about our own position in that table. IB Gram is a matching platform rather than an employer of tutors, delivery is online one-to-one, and we do not publish a fixed hourly rate on these pages because the figure depends on subject, level and the teaching-to-supervision balance. The consultation gives you the band before you commit. That is a less satisfying answer than a number, and it is the accurate one.

sections.heading: What actually moves a quote up or down
paragraphs: Parents often treat an hourly rate as a fixed property of a tutor, when much of it is a property of the booking. Session length, time of day, distance, notice period, subject scarcity and whether the work is teaching or supervision all move the number, and some of them move it a long way. Knowing which levers exist means a family can reduce the bill without reducing the quality, which is a better outcome than negotiating a specialist down to a generalist's rate.

The largest single lever is subject scarcity, and it is largely outside your control. Physics at Higher Level in the spring term prices towards the specialist and premium bands because the pool is small and demand concentrates. The second largest is travel, and it is entirely within your control: choosing an online format removes roughly the difference between the AED 150-300 and AED 180-500 published bands, because that difference is substantially the drive.

The third lever is the one families underuse. A 90-minute booking is normally priced below two separate 60-minute sessions, and for a student above about sixteen working on extended written output, the longer session is also pedagogically better. That is an unusual case of the cheaper option being the better one, and it is worth asking about explicitly rather than assuming the quote is per hour regardless of block length.

The lever that should never be pulled is credential. Paying a budget rate for a tutor who does not know the specific board and level is not a saving; it is a different purchase that happens to cost less. Published budget bands buy homework supervision and content revision, which is genuinely useful for some students and genuinely useless for a Year 11 candidate losing marks on practical-paper method language.

sections.heading: The extras that appear on a tutoring bill
paragraphs: A quoted hourly rate is not always the whole figure, and the additions are rarely hidden so much as unmentioned. The table below lists what we see in this market, how each one is usually treated, and the question to ask before the first session. None of these items is unreasonable in itself; the problem is discovering them in month three rather than in the first conversation.

Materials are the commonest. Some providers charge for a workbook or a question bank; others use the school's own material and the board's published resources. Our position is the second, and there is a reason beyond cost: we do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, so the material a student works from should be what they legitimately hold through their school, referenced against the official source.

On tax, this page will not state the VAT treatment of tuition fees as a fact, because doing so accurately requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and we are not going to invent one. The useful question for a parent is narrower and entirely answerable: ask any provider whether the price they quoted you includes VAT, and get the answer in writing before you pay. A quote that is silent on the point is a quote you cannot compare.

On the word free, one caution. If something is offered at no charge with a condition attached - a trial of a certain length, one per family, eligibility limits - the condition should be stated on the same screen as the offer. Our own introductory session is at no charge, one per family, about thirty minutes, with the student present, and those are all the conditions there are. Any offer where the conditions are harder to find than the word free is worth reading twice.

sections.heading: Two worked totals: a term of IGCSE support and a two-year Diploma plan
paragraphs: Hourly rates are hard to budget from. The table below converts the published bands into two realistic shapes: a term of targeted IGCSE support, and a structured two-year Diploma arrangement. The figures are built from market bands read in October 2026, and they are illustrative arithmetic rather than a quote from us. Your own number depends on subject, level and the hour count, which is exactly the point.

The IGCSE example is deliberately small, because for most of the problems on this page it should be. A diagnostic block of three sessions, then eight targeted sessions on one component, is eleven sessions. At the qualified-tutor band that is a defined and modest commitment with a clear end, and it is the shape that fixes a practical-paper problem or a method-marks problem. Compare that with a weekly slot in three subjects for a full year, which is roughly ninety sessions, and the difference is not marginal.

The Diploma example is larger and should be, because the commitment is genuinely two years with coursework in the middle. The structure that keeps it predictable is to separate the three uses of an hour: weekly teaching in term time, a small number of supervision sessions clustered around the school's internal deadlines, and an intensive phase in the final weeks. Families who buy a flat weekly commitment for two years instead usually pay more and get less in the final term, when they need the hours most.

For wider context on the cost of education in the region, Dubai's regulator confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in that emirate would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Fees at Sharjah private schools are approved by the emirate's own authority rather than by Dubai's, so that measure does not apply here, but it is a published anchor worth knowing when the household budget is being set.

sections.heading: Cheap tutoring, legal tutoring, and the question to ask
paragraphs: Price and permit are separate questions that parents sometimes merge. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. Because the permit costs nothing, a low rate is not evidence that someone lacks one, and a high rate is not evidence that they hold one.

The eligibility list is wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is accessed through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the route to point any independent tutor at if they do not hold one.

No fine schedule is published. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and figures circulating online could not be verified, so treat any specific amount you read as unsourced. Separately, a school teacher tutoring their own enrolled students raises a professional-ethics issue rather than only a permit one: Abu Dhabi's regulator has rules barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit carries a code of conduct addressing the same point.

A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal category and needs its own permit from the relevant authority. IB Gram holds no permit, approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, SPEA, ADEK, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we state that plainly rather than borrow authority we do not have. Any provider claiming regulator approval for tutoring should be asked to show the permit number.

sections.heading: Where online changes the arithmetic for an Al Juraina household
paragraphs: The cost case for online delivery in this district is narrower and more honest than the usual version. Al Juraina is central, so the drive from much of the city is not long, and an in-home tutor here is not facing the journey they would face out at Tilal City. The travel premium exists but it is at the lower end of the published range rather than the top.

Where the arithmetic genuinely changes is in what the money buys. For a mainstream IGCSE subject, both formats will find you a competent tutor and the comparison is mostly about the travel component. For a scarce combination - Physics at Higher Level, the quantitative Economics paper, Internal Assessment supervision in a specific discipline - the local pool is small, and a family paying an in-home rate often ends up with a generalist, which is paying more for less. That is the real cost argument.

The second place the arithmetic changes is reliability. A session that starts ten minutes late because of traffic loses the part where the previous week's work is checked, and three of those across a term is a session's worth of consolidation gone without appearing on any bill. Removing travel removes that leak. It is a small effect per session and a real one across a two-year Diploma.

To be explicit: IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE and nothing here is an offer to send anyone to a Sharjah address. Home visiting is a service we offer only in India. What we sell is one-to-one tuition over live video with a shared screen and a saved board. If an adult in the room is what your child needs, the independent in-home market exists at the published AED 180-500 band, and in a central district like this one you should be negotiating the travel component down.

sections.heading: The one thing nobody should be paying for
paragraphs: A cost-focused page has an obligation to name the purchase that is never worth making. One of the pages competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price of several thousand dirhams. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, the consequence falls on the candidate rather than the seller, and it can end a Diploma candidature. No price makes that a reasonable transaction.

Legitimate coursework support costs far less and does more. A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain what each assessment criterion rewards in plain language, help narrow a research question until it is answerable inside the word limit, challenge whether a claim in a draft is actually evidenced, point out that data carries no uncertainty treatment, and read a draft against the published criteria and name the weak criterion. Four to six sessions across a project is a common shape, which is a fraction of the cost of a bought document.

What a tutor must not do is author any part of a submission - not a paragraph, not a methodology, not a conclusion, not a results set. We say this at the start of every supervision block and we say that anything the student did not write has to come out before submission. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or boundary tables; we cite the official source and work from material the student legitimately holds.

There is a cost argument even here. A student who has had sections written for them learns nothing about criterion literacy, which is the same skill that lifts their written papers. So the bought document is not only a risk, it is a worse purchase than the supervision it replaced, at several times the price.

sections.heading: How to buy this sensibly, in order
paragraphs: First, ask the school what it already provides. Revision sessions, subject clinics, coursework drop-ins and past-paper access are frequently included in fees and frequently unused. This costs nothing to establish and occasionally ends the conversation, which is a result we are happy to report.

Second, buy a diagnosis before buying hours. Three or four sessions to establish which component is losing marks costs less than a month of weekly lessons and determines whether the answer is eight sessions or forty. That single decision has a larger effect on your total than any negotiation over the hourly rate, and it is the step families under pressure most often skip.

Third, separate teaching from supervision on the quote, and ask what the hours are for. A specialist used on one identified component for four to eight sessions costs a fraction of a year-long weekly commitment and frequently produces the same mark movement. Ask whether a 90-minute booking is priced below two hours, because for a student above sixteen it often is and is also better teaching.

Fourth, establish the terms before paying: materials, VAT, notice period for cancellation, what happens to unused sessions, and what happens if the match is wrong. Then test the match. Our introductory session is at no charge, one per family, about thirty minutes, with the student present, and if the pairing does not work we change the tutor. If a scarce subject carries a wait we will tell you in that first conversation rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: Why do two tutors quote completely different prices for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Because the rate reflects who is teaching and whether they travel, not what is being taught. Published UAE figures read in October 2026 run from AED 33-52 at one budget platform to AED 650 for a premium named tutor elsewhere. A student or graduate tutor sits at the bottom, a qualified subject teacher online in the middle at AED 150-300, an in-home visit at AED 180-500 because the rate absorbs the drive, and a scarce Higher Level specialist at AED 200-450 and above. Ask what credential and what format each quote assumes.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to get IGCSE help in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Ask the school what it already provides, because revision sessions and subject clinics are often included in fees and unused. If private help is still needed, the cheapest effective shape is a three-session diagnosis followed by eight targeted sessions on the one component that is losing marks, at the qualified-tutor band of AED 150-300 an hour. That is eleven sessions with a defined end, against roughly ninety for a weekly slot in three subjects across a year at the same rate.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper tutor cost more in the end?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, because the total is driven by the hour count rather than the rate. A correctly diagnosed technique problem can resolve in eight to ten sessions. The same student with a tutor who re-teaches content they already knew can absorb forty and finish in the same place, which is a four-fold difference in total cost at any rate band. Published budget bands typically buy homework supervision and content revision rather than exam technique at a named board and level, which is a different purchase that happens to be cheaper.

faqs.question: What should we ask before paying for a block of sessions?
faqs.answer: Five things. Does the quoted price include VAT. What materials will my child need to buy. What notice avoids a cancellation charge. What happens to sessions we have paid for and not used. And what happens if the match is wrong. Two quotes cannot be compared until all five are answered, preferably in writing. Then ask the question that matters most: what are these hours intended to fix, and how will we know whether it worked.

faqs.question: Are monthly tutoring packages good value in the UAE?
faqs.answer: They are the cheapest per hour and the least flexible. Published examples in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour home visits. The problem is that the academic year takes weeks back: mock fortnight, study leave, school revision programmes, Ramadan timings and holidays. A package that assumes four usable weeks every month will have unused sessions, so ask what happens to them before committing.

faqs.question: Does a quoted tutoring price include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing. This page deliberately does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a fact, because doing so accurately needs a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than a tutoring provider's assertion. What you can and should establish is narrower: whether the specific figure you were quoted is the figure you will pay. A quote that is silent on the point is not comparable with one that is explicit, and the difference can be material across a two-year arrangement.

faqs.question: How many sessions will my child actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the type of problem, and the ranges are reasonably predictable once it is diagnosed. Science practical-paper method language usually takes three to five sessions. Showing working to secure method marks takes four to six. Command-term discipline on extended responses takes four to eight. Higher Level mathematics Paper 3 technique takes six to ten. Internal Assessment criterion work takes two to four sessions per draft. Content gaps are open-ended, which is why finding out which kind you have is worth paying for first.

faqs.question: What extras get added to a tutoring bill?
faqs.answer: Materials and workbooks, VAT where it is not in the quote, travel or distance surcharges on in-home arrangements, late-cancellation charges, and sometimes peak-season rates in the weeks before a series. None is unreasonable in itself; the problem is meeting them in month three. Our own position on materials is to work from the school's own resources and the official published sources, partly on cost and partly because we do not reproduce or distribute board papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put two children in the same session?
faqs.answer: Cheaper, yes, and usually a false economy if the two children have different problems. One-to-one means one student, and the diagnosis that makes the hour worth buying is specific to them. Where siblings are at the same stage, on the same board and with the same component weakness, a shared session can work. Where they are not, you are paying for an hour in which each child receives half the attention on work that is only half relevant. Separate shorter sessions usually beat one shared longer one.

faqs.question: What happens to sessions we have paid for but not used?
faqs.answer: It varies between providers, which is exactly why it should be settled before payment rather than discovered later. Some expire at the end of a month, some roll forward, some are forfeited after a notice period. Monthly packages are the most exposed to this, because the academic calendar reliably removes weeks through mocks, study leave and holidays. Ask the question in the first conversation and get the answer in writing; a provider who will not answer it clearly has told you something useful.

faqs.question: Should we pay per session or per month?
faqs.answer: Per session for anything short or targeted, which covers most of what this page recommends. Per month only when you are confident the sessions will actually be used, which in practice means a steady teaching term rather than a spring term full of mocks and study leave. Monthly packages are cheapest per hour, and the saving is real, but it disappears the first time three sessions go unused. Match the payment shape to the calendar rather than to the headline rate.

faqs.question: Does the price go up closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: In the market, yes. Demand for specialists concentrates into the eight to twelve weeks before a written series, and the scarce combinations - Physics at Higher Level, quantitative Economics, Computer Science - price towards the specialist and premium bands at exactly that point. The practical response is to secure a scarce slot in the autumn term, when both availability and rates are better. A slot that is unavailable in February cannot be created in February at any price, which is the market saying the same thing.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre cheaper than a private tutor in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and it is the lowest visible option in the market, because a teacher's hour is divided between several students. What you give up is the thing that makes one-to-one worth buying: individual script analysis against the mark scheme. A centre group class is good value for content coverage and poor value for a specific component problem. The sensible question is which of those two your child needs, which is a diagnostic question rather than a pricing one.

faqs.question: How much of an in-home rate is the travel?
faqs.answer: Roughly the difference between the published bands. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150-300 an hour; in-home one-to-one with travel included sits at AED 180-500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table listing 180-350 and individual listings reaching 500. Most of that gap is driving time and fuel rather than teaching. In a central district like this one the drive is shorter than it would be inland, so the travel component should be at the lower end, and it is a reasonable thing to raise when negotiating.

faqs.question: What does a two-year Diploma support plan cost in total?
faqs.answer: It depends on structure more than on rate. A predictable shape is around 28 weekly teaching sessions across DP1 term time, 8 to 12 supervision sessions clustered on the school's internal coursework deadlines, and 16 to 24 sessions in a final intensive phase, at the specialist band of AED 200-450 and above. A flat weekly commitment for two years costs more and typically leaves too little budget for the final term, when the hours actually convert into marks. We do not publish a fixed rate; the consultation gives you the band.

sharjah/al-juraina.closingHeading: Get the diagnosis priced before the hours
sharjah/al-juraina.closingBody: If you are comparing quotes, the most useful thing you can do is make them comparable: ask each provider whether the price includes VAT, what materials are needed, what notice avoids a charge, what happens to unused sessions, and what the hours are intended to fix. Then buy a short diagnosis before a block, because whether the answer is eight sessions or forty moves your total far more than the rate per hour does. Our introductory session is at no charge, one per family, with the student present. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video.

sharjah/al-khan.tutorsIntro: The tutors shown here teach the evening and weekend slots Al Khan families actually ask for, in the subjects that dominate enquiries from this part of the lagoon: IGCSE maths and sciences by board, and Diploma sciences in the run-up to a May sitting.

intro.heading: The Al Khan week, hour by hour
paragraphs: Al Khan is a compact coastal district wrapped around the lagoon, hemmed in by Al Khan Street on one side and the Al Taawun and Al Majaz approaches on the other. It is a short distance from almost everything in central Sharjah and a long time from any of it between 7am and 9am, and again between 5pm and 8pm. Tutoring here lives or dies on the clock rather than on the quality of the tutor, which is the opposite of what most families expect when they start looking.

Work backwards from a normal weekday. The bus or the car leaves between 6:45am and 7:15am depending on whether the school is inside Sharjah or over the Dubai line. The school day finishes somewhere between 1:40pm and 3pm. A child on a bus route that loops through Al Majaz and Al Taawun before reaching Al Khan does not walk through the door until well after 3:30pm, and then needs to eat. A parent driving back from a Dubai office reaches the building between 6:30pm and 7:30pm.

That leaves a genuine working window of roughly 6:30pm to 9pm, narrower for younger children who are finished by eight. It is a small window and it is contested: it is also when siblings need attention, when football practice happens, and when the family eats. Booking the hour is therefore the first decision, not the last one, and defending it for a whole term is the thing that separates arrangements that work from arrangements that lapse in October.

Saturday is the exception and the opportunity. On a Saturday morning the child is rested, a parent is usually in the building, and ninety minutes of concentration is genuinely available. That is the slot for the work that cannot be done at the end of a school day: a whole past paper sat to time, an Internal Assessment draft, a long piece of writing. It is also the slot that fills first in every subject, which is why families who ask in September get it and families who ask in February do not.

The second Al Khan-specific factor is distance to school. Families here send children to schools spread from Al Qasimia and Al Majaz through to Muwaileh and across the border into Dubai. A twelve-minute journey and a thirty-five-minute journey produce completely different children at 6pm. A tutoring plan that does not ask how long the child has been travelling is guessing.

IB Gram's answer is to deliver lessons one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Al Khan address, and home visiting is a service run only in India. The direct consequence is that the booked hour is a taught hour: no late arrival because the Al Wahda interchange was blocked, no shortened session because the tutor has somewhere to be at eight, and no restriction of the tutor pool to those who happen to live within a fifteen-minute drive of the lagoon.

sharjah/al-khan.programmesIntro: Al Khan enquiries concentrate in three programmes, and each has a different relationship with the calendar. The point of the summaries below is when the pressure arrives, not what the programme claims to develop.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Examined by syllabus code rather than by subject name, with Core and Extended tiers in sciences and maths that cap the attainable grade. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For an Al Khan family that means the zone timetable from the child's own school, not a timetable found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Available in May or June and again in November each year, graded 9 to 1, with formula provision and paper structures that differ from the Cambridge equivalent in the same subject. Some Pearson qualifications are modular, which changes when revision has to peak.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson published a November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and sent June 2026 results to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026. Because provisional timetables are revised, an Al Khan family should work from the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com rather than from a date copied onto a tutoring page.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across two years, three at Higher Level, with internal assessment in each subject plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Internal deadlines set by the school usually sit a long way before anything the IB itself publishes, which is what catches families out.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. IB session and results dates are not restated here because they must be confirmed against ibo.org or the school's Diploma coordinator before a family plans around them. The school's internal assessment calendar is the document an Al Khan tutoring plan should actually be built from.

sharjah/al-khan.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often requested from Al Khan addresses, with the technique failure that costs marks in each. Lessons are delivered over video, so availability depends on the subject and level rather than on the neighbourhood.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended candidates meet functions, matrix transformations and histograms with unequal class widths; Core candidates never see them. The tier decision is made by the school in Year 10 and quietly sets the grade ceiling for the whole qualification.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers, with a formula sheet provided that changes what has to be memorised. Candidates who have practised only Cambridge papers lose time adjusting to the question order and the proportion of marks carried by method.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper is where marks go missing: candidates describe a method without naming a control variable or a repeat reading. Electricity circuits and moments remain the two topics that produce the widest mark spread.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations and electrolysis dominate lost marks at Extended tier, and the qualitative analysis tables have to be learned rather than reasoned. Precise language about ions and half-equations is worth more than extra content.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: A long syllabus where candidates know the material and answer imprecisely. Examiners want the structure named, the process named and the consequence stated, and a script describing a change without a mechanism earns little.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level load, and the internally assessed investigation decides a fifth of the grade on the strength of a research question chosen months earlier.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circular motion defeat capable students because the algebra and the physical reasoning have to run together. Paper 1 rewards recognising which relationship applies before any calculation starts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level Paper 3 asks for extended unseen problem solving and cannot be prepared for by topic revision alone. Proof, complex numbers and advanced calculus are the recurring trouble spots.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marks come from applying a tool to the stimulus organisation and reaching a defended judgement, not from reproducing the tool. Candidates who list advantages and disadvantages without concluding plateau around the middle of the range.

subjects.name: English as a second language and English A
subjects.description: Reading-for-detail and summary questions reward precision over fluency at IGCSE, while DP English A requires an argument about how a text works. Both respond well to short, frequent sessions rather than long ones.

regions.name: Al Qasba and the Sharjah corniche

sections.heading: What a weekday in Al Khan does to a tutoring slot
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a family in Al Khan can do before contacting any tutor is to write out their actual weekday. Not the idealised one. The one with the bus loop, the younger sibling's pickup, and the drive back from the office. Nearly every failed tutoring arrangement in this neighbourhood failed because the hour was chosen optimistically.

The clock below is the composite of what Al Khan households describe. It is not universal, but the shape holds: a long morning departure, an early school finish undone by a slow bus route, a dead hour when a child is home and nobody else is, and a short genuinely usable evening. The dead hour between 4pm and 5:30pm looks like an opportunity and usually is not, because an eleven-year-old who has been awake since six is not available for new learning.

Two practical rules come out of this. The first is that a session booked at a time a parent cannot be in the building should only be booked for a student old enough to run it themselves, which in practice means Year 11 upwards. The second is that the length of the session should follow the year group rather than the price list: forty-five minutes for a Year 7 pupil at 7pm is more productive than ninety.

The third, less obvious rule is to leave the slot alone once it works. Families who move a lesson around the week to accommodate everything else end up with a tutor who sees the child irregularly and a child who never builds the habit. A slightly inconvenient fixed hour beats a convenient floating one.

sections.heading: Session length and frequency by year group
paragraphs: Most families buy the session length the provider leads with, which is usually sixty minutes, and most of them should not. Attention span and the amount of content that needs covering both scale with age, and in a neighbourhood where lessons happen late in the evening the mismatch is amplified.

A Year 7 or Year 8 pupil at 7pm has perhaps forty minutes of genuine concentration left. Buying ninety produces thirty-five minutes of teaching and fifty-five minutes of supervised fatigue. Two short sessions across the week also give the child two chances to practise something and two chances to be corrected, which is worth more than one long exposure.

By Year 10 and 11, sixty minutes is the right unit for a single subject, with a longer Saturday session when past papers are being sat. In the Diploma, ninety minutes becomes genuinely useful because Higher Level problems and Internal Assessment work do not fit into an hour once the first ten minutes have gone on reviewing homework.

Frequency is the other lever, and it is the one families reach for last. Going from one session a week to two in a single subject, for the eight weeks before a mock, usually does more than adding a second subject. The table sets out the pattern that works in this neighbourhood at each stage.

One further adjustment is worth making in Al Khan specifically. Because the usable evening is short and shared with everything else in the household, the session should start with marked homework rather than with new content. Ten minutes spent going through what the child got wrong since last week is the highest-value part of the hour, and it is the part that gets cut when a session starts late. Protecting it is a scheduling decision as much as a teaching one.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the exam: what is actually dated
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names an exam session, an entry deadline or a results date. That absence is strange, because the deadlines that matter most to a family are the administrative ones, and they fall months before anyone starts revising.

Cambridge publishes the shape clearly, as long as you read it for a series an Al Khan candidate can actually be entered for: June or November, not the February and March sitting Cambridge offers to centres in India. For a June series, final entries close in the spring - roughly four months before the first paper, on a date the centre prints on the statement of entry - forecast grades follow on Cambridge's published deadline for that series, the papers fall in June on the centre's zone timetable, results reach Cambridge Direct in August and certificates arrive later in the year. Pearson supplies the hard numbers for the same lag on its own route: its November 2026 International GCSE papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, its June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 grades did not reach students until 22 January 2026. The gap between the entry deadline and the first paper is a term or more, which means a decision about tiering or about adding a subject belongs in the autumn, not in the exam term.

Pearson works to a different rhythm. International GCSE exams are available in May or June and again in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and those can be revised, so the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com is the only safe reference.

For the IB Diploma the honest position is that UAE schools sit the May session and that specific session and results dates must be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org before a family plans around them. What is reliably true is that the school's own internal deadlines for Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge arrive long before anything external, and those are the dates that should drive a tutoring schedule.

sections.heading: Why a visiting tutor's hour is not the same hour
paragraphs: Parents comparing an advertised in-home rate with an advertised online rate are usually comparing two different products. The in-home figure buys travel as well as teaching, and in central Sharjah at seven in the evening the travel is not trivial.

Run the arithmetic honestly. A tutor driving from Al Majaz or Al Nahda to Al Khan at peak time spends twenty to forty minutes each way. That hour and a bit is unpaid time the tutor has to recover somewhere, which is why market in-home rates sit higher: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors asking up to AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online.

The travel also caps how many sessions a visiting tutor can deliver in an evening, which is why the 7pm slot is the hardest to get and the 5pm slot is offered first. Families accept a 5pm start to secure a good tutor and then discover that nobody is home to supervise it. The constraint is the tutor's diary, not the child's readiness.

None of this makes in-home tutoring a bad product. For primary-age homework support within a short walk it is often the sensible choice. It becomes a poor choice at the point where the subject is specialised, because the tutor pool shrinks to whoever can reach the building, and a Higher Level specialist is rarely in that set. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE and does not pretend to; lessons for Al Khan families are delivered one-to-one over live video.

sections.heading: Is a visiting tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody in this market answers, and it is one a parent can check. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published, any specific amount quoted to you is unverified.

Eligibility is broader than most families assume. The published list includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two working day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two conditions matter in practice. The permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi the education regulator's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. A tutoring arrangement that involves your child's own classroom teacher, paid privately, is the arrangement to avoid regardless of emirate. Ask, rather than assume.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it requires an educational services permit from the relevant authority. IB Gram holds no such permit and no regulator approval of any kind, and does not describe itself as approved, accredited or licensed by SPEA, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or any examination board.

sections.heading: Which subjects Al Khan families ask for, and in which term
paragraphs: Demand from this neighbourhood is seasonal in a way that is predictable enough to plan around. Knowing when the queue forms is useful, because the good slots in a scarce subject are taken by the families who asked in September.

September and October bring Year 10 and Diploma year one enquiries, usually prompted by a new teacher, a harder syllabus or a first assessment that went badly. This is the cheapest and most effective moment to start, because there is time for content repair rather than triage. It is also when tier decisions for Cambridge sciences are still open.

January and February bring the largest wave, driven by mock results. These enquiries are almost always about technique rather than content: a child who knows the chemistry and cannot structure a six-mark answer. Eight to twelve weeks is enough to change that if the work is paper-based from the first session.

March onwards is the sprint, and the honest advice shifts. With six weeks left, adding three subjects spreads the effort so thin that nothing moves. One subject, twice a week, on past papers, with a hard taper in the final ten days, is the plan that produces a change. Sciences and maths dominate requests from Al Khan throughout; Arabic and English second language cluster in the autumn when reports land.

The quiet season is June to August, and it is underused. A family that books four or five sessions across the summer in a subject the child will meet in September arrives in the autumn with the first unit already understood rather than already behind. For a pupil moving from Year 9 into Year 10, or from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma, those few summer hours are worth more than the same money spent in a February panic.

sections.heading: What online delivery fixes for an Al Khan family, and what it does not
paragraphs: The case for video delivery in this neighbourhood is mostly about time. It removes travel from both ends of the hour, which means the 7pm slot is actually available, the session starts on the minute, and a tutor in a different city or time zone can hold it. It also widens the choice of tutor from those who will drive to the lagoon to those who teach the exact syllabus code the child is entered for.

There are practical requirements. The child needs a quiet room and a device with a working camera, which in a shared apartment takes planning. A stable connection matters more than a fast one. A graphics tablet or even a phone propped over a notebook makes maths sessions far better, because the tutor needs to see working rather than answers.

There are also genuine limits, and a page that pretends otherwise is not worth reading. A video tutor cannot replace laboratory bench time; practical skills can be taught as method, variables, uncertainty and data analysis, but the hands-on hours belong to the school. A child under about ten usually needs an adult nearby for the first few sessions. And a student who will not engage with a screen will not engage with a screen, which is a reason to use the trial lesson as a real test rather than a formality.

IB Gram does not visit homes anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is offered only in India. That is said plainly before any payment, because several providers in this market route UAE parents to overseas numbers without disclosing where delivery actually happens.

sections.heading: Booking a slot in Al Khan that survives the whole term
paragraphs: The mechanics matter more than the marketing. A tutoring arrangement in this neighbourhood typically ends not because the tutor was poor but because the slot was wrong, so the sequence below front-loads the scheduling decision.

Start by naming two viable hours in the week, with the honest constraints attached: who is home, how long the child has been travelling, and what else is in that slot. Then bring the statement of entry so the board, syllabus code and tier are known. Those two pieces of information, the hour and the code, determine the match almost entirely.

Take a trial lesson and judge it on diagnosis. A tutor who finishes by naming a specific misconception, a missing prerequisite or an untaught technique has told you something. One who reports that the session went well has not. Then run three or four sessions as a diagnostic block before committing to a term, and ask for the plan in writing.

Set the review against the next school assessment rather than a number of weeks, and ask what happens if a session is missed, whether the same tutor is held for next term, and whether homework is marked. If a specialist is not available at your hour, expect to be told so rather than offered a generalist. That answer is the clearest signal of how a provider will behave later.

Two small habits keep the arrangement alive through the term. Read the session note each week, even briefly, because a note that stops naming specifics is an early warning. And tell the tutor about school events before they happen rather than after: a trip week, a mock block, a sports fixture. A tutor who knows a mock is in nine days spends those nine days differently, and in a neighbourhood where the usable evening is this narrow, nine days of focus is most of what a term has to give.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a tutoring session can realistically start on a weekday in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: For a child at a school inside central Sharjah, around 6pm. For a child travelling to Muwaileh or across into Dubai, 6:30pm or later. The bus route home often loops through Al Majaz and Al Taawun, so a 2:40pm school finish can still mean a 3:45pm arrival, and the hour after that is for eating rather than learning. Students in Year 11 and above can use a late afternoon slot productively without an adult present. Below that, the 6:30pm to 8pm block and Saturday morning are the two that work.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to apartments in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service run only in India. Lessons for Al Khan families are delivered one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing for past papers. The reason is practical rather than ideological: removing the drive means the 7pm slot is actually available, the session starts on time, and the choice of tutor is not limited to those who can reach the lagoon in the evening traffic.

faqs.question: How much more does an in-home tutor cost than an online one in this part of Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour, against AED 180 to 350 for in-home one-to-one in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with independent home tutors asking up to AED 500. The gap is mostly travel, which the invoice does not itemise but the rate absorbs. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring runs AED 200 to 450 and above in either format. IB Gram quotes after a consultation rather than publishing a flat hourly rate.

faqs.question: When does the Cambridge entry deadline fall for an Al Khan candidate, and why does it matter so early?
faqs.answer: Your child will sit either the June series or the November series, and for a June sitting the final entry closes in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper; November carries its own, earlier deadline. The exact day is not a national date you can look up - it is the one the centre names and the statement of entry records, so ask the school for it in writing. It matters because tier and subject decisions close at that point: a candidate entered for Core cannot be moved to Extended afterwards, and the grade ceiling is therefore fixed months before anyone sits a paper. Forecast grades follow later, on Cambridge's published deadline for the series. Ask for the centre's own zone timetable in the same message.

faqs.question: My child sits Pearson Edexcel rather than Cambridge. Does the tutoring plan change?
faqs.answer: Yes, in ways that are invisible from the textbook. Pearson International GCSE papers differ in count, in formula provision and in how practical skills are examined, and some qualifications are modular, which changes when revision has to peak. Pearson runs May or June and November series, with a November 2026 final timetable from late October to 19 November 2026. Because provisional timetables can be revised, work from the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com. The first thing a tutor should ask for is the specification code, not the subject name.

faqs.question: How long should a session be for a Year 8 child in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: Forty to forty-five minutes, twice a week, rather than ninety minutes once. A twelve or thirteen year old who left home before seven in the morning has limited concentration left at 7pm, and buying a longer session usually buys supervised fatigue rather than teaching. Two shorter sessions also create two chances to practise and two chances to be corrected, which matters more at this stage than coverage. By Year 10 an hour is the right unit, with a longer Saturday session once past papers start.

faqs.question: We want help in four subjects at once. Is that sensible before an exam series?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and especially not with fewer than ten weeks left. Four subjects at one session each consumes four evenings and produces shallow work in all of them, because exam technique improves through repetition in a single subject rather than through exposure across many. The pattern that moves a grade is one or two subjects, twice a week, entirely on past papers, with the rest handled by the school. Add a third subject only after the first has stabilised against a school assessment.

faqs.question: Is a tutor in Sharjah required to hold a permit, and can I ask to see it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat a specific figure with scepticism. Asking to see the permit is reasonable.

faqs.question: Can a teacher from my child's own Al Khan school tutor them privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: That is the arrangement to avoid. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi the education regulator's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the rules, it creates a conflict in which the person setting and marking the assessment is also paid to prepare the child for it. A tutor with no connection to the school gives an independent read on where the marks are actually being lost.

faqs.question: How do practical science skills get taught if lessons are over video?
faqs.answer: Method, variables, uncertainty, graph work and data analysis all teach well on screen, and those are where most practical marks are actually awarded. Cambridge alternative-to-practical papers test exactly that: naming a control variable, justifying a repeat reading, identifying a systematic error. What video cannot replace is bench time with apparatus, which belongs to the school laboratory. A tutor who claims otherwise is overselling. The honest division is that the school provides the hands and the tutor provides the reasoning.

faqs.question: What should I watch for in a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis. A useful trial ends with the tutor naming something specific: a confused definition, an untaught technique, a prerequisite missing from two years earlier. That tells you they were listening to the child rather than delivering a lesson. Watch also for whether they asked which board and code your child sits before teaching. If a trial is advertised as free, the condition attached to it should be stated before you book. Rapport matters, but on its own it predicts very little.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to move a lesson during a busy week?
faqs.answer: Ask about this before you start, because policies differ widely. A reasonable arrangement allows a session to be moved with notice measured in a day or two, holds the regular slot for the following week, and is clear about what happens when a session is missed without notice. The thing worth protecting is the slot itself: families who shuffle the hour around the week end up with irregular contact and a child who never builds the habit. One fixed, slightly inconvenient hour outperforms a convenient floating one.

faqs.question: Will a tutor know the mock and Internal Assessment dates my child's school uses?
faqs.answer: Only if you provide them, and that is the right way round. Schools in Sharjah set their own mock windows and their own internal deadlines for Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, and those dates sit a long way before anything the awarding bodies publish. Send the school's assessment calendar at the start and the tutoring schedule can be built backwards from it. A tutor working from a generic UK half-term calendar is planning around the wrong year.

faqs.question: Do you tutor the Arabic and Islamic Education subjects my child takes alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a separate stream with its own tutors. These subjects are mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and they are frequently the lowest grades on an otherwise strong report. In Dubai, the KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Tutoring follows the same distinction, and short frequent sessions work better here than long ones.

faqs.question: If no tutor is available in a scarce Higher Level subject at our hour, what then?
faqs.answer: You should be told that plainly rather than offered a generalist. Some Higher Level subjects have no UAE-based specialist free in the 7pm to 9pm Sharjah window. The two honest options are a waiting position until a slot opens, or a tutor in another time zone whose working day covers a Sharjah evening. Ask who the tutor is, what they have taught and at what level, and ask it before any payment. A provider that cannot answer specifically is answering the question anyway.

sharjah/al-khan.closingBody: In Al Khan the scarce resource is not a good tutor; it is the ninety minutes between a parent getting home and a child needing to sleep. Name the two hours in your week that genuinely work, send the statement of entry so the board and syllabus code are known, and the match becomes a narrow search for a specialist who teaches that code at that hour. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, entry deadlines on this page come from Cambridge and Pearson publications, and the student writes every word of their own assessed work.
