sections.heading: The boundary on coursework, stated plainly
paragraphs: Because so much of this page is about the Internal Assessment, the boundary needs stating without hedging. Assessed coursework must be the student's own work and the student signs a declaration confirming it. One of the pages competing for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments at a published price. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate, not the seller. That is sufficient reason to rule out any provider who offers it.

Legitimate supervision is specific and does more good than parents expect. A tutor can teach the underlying content, translate each criterion into plain language, help narrow a research question until it is answerable inside the word limit, challenge whether a claim is supported by the data, point out that a results table carries no uncertainty treatment, and read a draft against the published criteria and name which criterion is weak and why. Every one of those is teaching.

What a tutor must not do is author any part of the submission - not a paragraph, not a methodology, not a conclusion, not a results set. We say this to students at the start of a supervision block, and we say that anything they did not write has to come out before submission. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we cite the official source and work from material the student legitimately holds through their school.

There is a quieter reason this matters for the subject of this page. A student who has had sections written for them learns nothing about criterion literacy, which is exactly the skill that would have lifted their written papers too. Supervision done properly transfers; a finished document does not.
bullets: Allowed: content teaching, criterion translation, evidence challenge, criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft
Not allowed: authoring any part of a submission, supplying results, rewriting to completion
Official papers, schemes and boundary tables are cited, never redistributed
Criterion literacy learned properly also lifts the written papers

sections.heading: Starting from a returned paper rather than from a subject name
paragraphs: The first thing to send is not a description of the problem but two recent pieces of marked work, ideally including a full paper or a mock script. From those we can usually say within one reading which component the marks are leaving from, whether the pattern is knowledge, technique or pacing, and roughly how long the repair takes. That is a more useful starting point than any conversation about which topics feel hard.

We then match a tutor who teaches that exact board and level, and run an introductory session at no charge - one per family, about thirty minutes, with the student present. The point is to test whether this particular pairing works and to put the script on the screen together. If the match is wrong we change it rather than suggest another week, because mismatched pairings do not improve with persistence.

If no specialist is free we say so immediately. For mainstream combinations it is rare; for scarce Higher Level subjects in the weeks right before a written series it happens, and the wait is usually one or two weeks. Where no UAE-based specialist is available we offer one from our wider pool, which is centred on India and includes tutors who have taught these syllabuses to international cohorts for years. Delivery is unchanged because it was always online over live video.

Finally, timing. A technique problem identified in November for a May series has time to be fixed and then practised, which is the sequence that actually changes a grade. The same problem identified in April can be mitigated but not rebuilt. And once the entry deadline has passed, the tier is fixed, so the plan has to make the most of the papers your child is actually sitting.

process.title: Send two marked scripts
process.description: A full paper or mock script is worth more than any description of the difficulty. We read it to sort lost marks into knowledge, wrong-question and pacing, because those three have different remedies and only one of them is fixed by revision.

process.title: Confirm board, level and syllabus code
process.description: Taken from the exam entry rather than the textbook cover. Cambridge 0620 and a Pearson chemistry specification set out the same chemistry in different papers, and teaching the wrong structure wastes the opening weeks of any arrangement.

process.title: Agree which component the work targets
process.description: We name one component and one type of loss as the goal for the first block, so progress can be measured in marks on that component rather than in topics covered. Vague briefs produce vague outcomes at any hourly rate.

process.title: Meet the tutor at no charge
process.description: One introductory session per family, roughly thirty minutes, with the student present and the script on the shared screen. If the pairing does not work we change the tutor, and there is no obligation to book a block afterwards.

process.title: Review against marks, not hours
process.description: Every few weeks we check the targeted component's marks on fresh timed work. If the marks have not moved, we change the method or the tutor rather than adding hours, which is how families avoid buying a term of sessions that were never going to work.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before hours
whyPoints.description: A short block establishes which component is losing marks before anyone commits to a term. It frequently reduces the total needed, and it occasionally shows that supervised independent practice, which costs nothing, is the honest answer.

whyPoints.title: Official schemes, not paraphrases
whyPoints.description: Written work is marked against the board's own published scheme so the student sees the exact wording that earns the mark. We cite and reference official material rather than redistributing it, which is both a copyright position and a quality one.

whyPoints.title: Specialists chosen by syllabus
whyPoints.description: The tutor teaches the precise board, level and paper structure your child sits. For scarce Higher Level combinations, an online match from a national pool is materially better than whoever specialises in it within driving distance of a southern Sharjah address.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The AED bands here name the source that published them and the month they were read. We publish no satisfaction percentages, student counts or ratings, because the underlying data for such claims cannot be produced.

whyPoints.title: An explicit coursework line
whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own drafts, with nothing authored on their behalf at any stage. Stated here because a provider competing for these searches sells the opposite and the risk lands on the student.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what tutoring cannot fix
whyPoints.description: A three-Higher-Level workload problem, a tier locked at entry, or a student who needs sleep rather than sessions are not solved by buying hours. We will say so, including when it means a shorter engagement than you expected.

faqs.question: What does a Sharjah school class of twenty-four not have time to do?
faqs.answer: Read each student's full paper line by line against the mark scheme. That takes roughly forty minutes per student per paper, which is about sixteen hours for one class and one paper, and no teaching load accommodates it. Schools cover the syllabus well and mark homework reliably. What falls off the end is individual script analysis and full-length timed practice, which is usually limited to two mocks a year. Those two gaps are where most of the marks in this page's case studies are lost, and they are exactly what a one-to-one hour can supply.

faqs.question: Should my child sit IGCSE Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: It depends on autumn-term attainment, and the decision is effectively locked at entry rather than at the exam. A UAE candidate is entered for the Cambridge June series, or for November if a retake is the plan, and entries for either close well ahead of the papers, so the tier is settled while the teaching is still going on. Core caps the available grade, so a student comfortably near the top of Core past papers is being limited by the tier. Extended rewards a stronger cohort, so a student scoring far below on Extended practice may finish lower than Core would have placed them. We can give an evidence-based view from the student's own marks; the school holds the decision.

faqs.question: How much of the Diploma grade comes from the Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: In most Diploma subjects the Internal Assessment carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of the subject grade. It is marked by the teacher against published criteria and then externally moderated. The reason it matters out of proportion to its weight is that students approach it with the least information about how it is judged, so the marks are often avoidably low. Criterion literacy, which means knowing specifically what the analysis and evaluation criteria reward, is the difference between a mid and a high mark, and it is rarely taught explicitly.

faqs.question: Which Internal Assessment criterion loses the most marks?
faqs.answer: In the sciences it is usually the analysis criterion, because data is presented without uncertainty treatment, and then the evaluation criterion, because limitations are listed generically rather than tied to the method actually used. In mathematics the equivalent loss is on personal engagement and on reflection that restates results instead of interpreting them. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards and read a draft against the published criteria to name the weak one. The writing itself has to remain the student's own work throughout.

faqs.question: Why did my son get a 6 in class tests and a 4 in the mock?
faqs.answer: Almost always because class tests assess a single recent topic and a mock assesses the whole course under time with mixed question types. Three things separate the two: pacing across a full paper, selecting a method when the question does not signal which topic it belongs to, and sustaining accuracy in the final third when concentration drops. None of these shows up in an end-of-unit test. The remedy is full timed papers with individual marking, not more topic revision, which is the work most students have already been doing.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a command term and a topic?
faqs.answer: The topic is what the question is about; the command term is what you are required to do with it. State, describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify and discuss ask for different things and carry different mark allocations. A question saying evaluate that receives a thorough explanation scores a fraction of the available marks even when every sentence is correct. This is the single largest source of lost marks on extended-response papers in our experience, and it is drillable in short bursts rather than requiring more content knowledge.

faqs.question: Does a Higher Level subject really need twice the work of Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Not twice, but substantially more, and the difference is structural rather than a matter of effort. Higher Level adds syllabus content, adds paper time, and in several subjects adds an extra paper. The practical implication is the combination rather than the single subject: three Higher Levels that all demand long written answers create a workload problem no amount of tutoring resolves. If that is the situation, the honest advice is sometimes to change the combination in DP1, before coursework has accumulated and the change becomes disruptive.

faqs.question: My daughter understands the content but runs out of time in papers. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: Timed practice with a stopwatch and a deliberate decision rule, not more revision. The specific habits that buy time are reading the whole paper first, allocating minutes by marks available, and leaving a question that is not moving after a set period rather than fighting it. Students resist the last one most and it recovers the most marks. A paper where the first six questions are strong and the final two are blank is a pacing problem, and it typically responds within four to six sessions of structured timed work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's work using the official scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, and marking against the board's own published scheme rather than a tutor's impression is the point of the exercise. The value is that the student sees, on their own sentence, the gap between what they wrote and the wording that earns the mark. We reference official schemes and work from material the student legitimately holds through school. We do not reproduce or distribute board papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which is both a copyright position and a reason to get the material from the school's own channels.

faqs.question: What does a predicted grade actually mean at a Sharjah school?
faqs.answer: It is a professional judgement about where the student is now, based on performance to date, rather than a projection of where they will finish. Read literally it causes unnecessary alarm or unwarranted comfort. Read properly it prompts a better question: which component is holding this prediction down, and what mark on that component would move it. A predicted 5 driven by an unwritten Internal Assessment is a different problem from a predicted 5 driven by consistently weak Paper 2 responses, though the report shows the same number.

faqs.question: Is it a problem if my child has never sat a full paper under time?
faqs.answer: It is one of the commonest reasons a capable student underperforms. Schools typically run two mocks a year, which may be the entire quantity of complete timed papers a student sits before the real series. Pacing, method selection under pressure and the discipline of abandoning a stuck question are learned by doing. A student who has sat eight marked papers by April is in a materially different position from one who has sat two, even where the classroom teaching was identical. Increasing that count is usually the first thing a plan should do.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether to drop a Higher Level subject to Standard?
faqs.answer: Look at written output rather than understanding. If the student can explain the material but consistently fails to finish extended answers in time across more than one subject, the issue is total load rather than ability in any single subject. Make the change in DP1 where possible, because coursework accumulates and a later change wastes work already done. We can set out what the student's component marks suggest; the decision sits with the family and the school, which knows the cohort and the teaching.

faqs.question: What should a student in Al Nouf be doing in the fortnight after mocks?
faqs.answer: Working through the returned script rather than starting a fresh revision cycle. The mock has just generated the most useful diagnostic document of the year, and most students read the total and file it. Sort the lost marks into knowledge, wrong-question and pacing, look at unawarded marks inside answers that were broadly right, and pick one component to work on. One session doing that is worth more than a fortnight of general revision, because it tells you where the next three months of effort should go.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for practical science subjects?
faqs.answer: For the assessed practical components, yes, because what those papers test is written: experimental design, control of variables, identification of systematic error, and precise method description. None of that requires a bench. The hands-on work your child does in the school laboratory is not replaced, and should not be. What a session adds is the mark-scheme language that turns a competent experiment into a high-scoring answer, which is the part most often missing from a returned practical paper.

faqs.question: How many weeks does it take to fix an exam technique problem?
faqs.answer: It depends on the component, and the ranges are fairly predictable. Science practical-paper language usually takes three to five sessions. Showing working to secure method marks takes four to six. Command-term discipline on extended responses takes four to eight. Higher Level mathematics Paper 3 investigation technique takes six to ten. Internal Assessment criterion work takes two to four supervision sessions per draft. Content gaps, by contrast, are open-ended, which is why diagnosing which kind of problem you have is worth doing before buying a term of hours.

sharjah/al-nouf.closingHeading: Send the script, not the symptom
sharjah/al-nouf.closingBody: If your child understands the subject and the marks say otherwise, the fastest route to an answer is a marked paper rather than a description. Send two recent pieces of work with the board, level and syllabus code from the exam entry, and we will tell you which component the marks are leaving from, whether the pattern is knowledge, technique or pacing, and roughly how many sessions that repair usually takes. The introductory session is at no charge, one per family, with the student present and the script on the shared screen. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video.

sharjah/al-qasimia.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Diploma and IGCSE subjects for central Sharjah families, including students sitting papers as external candidates. Each teaches a named syllabus at a named level and works from the student's own scripts.

intro.heading: The administration that decides a result
paragraphs: Al Qasimia is central Sharjah: dense apartment blocks between the creek and the inland roads, the university at one edge, Rolla and the old commercial quarter within walking distance, Al Majaz and Al Nahda next door. School runs here are short by UAE standards. What makes a tutoring conversation at this address different is not the commute but the paperwork, because central Sharjah has a high concentration of families whose children are sitting examinations in arrangements nobody fully explained to them.

Three situations recur. A student is entered for a subject by a centre and the family has never seen the statement of entry. A student wants to sit a subject the school does not teach, and nobody has told them whether that is possible. A student has had a result they did not expect and the window for doing anything about it is already closing. All three are administrative, all three are solvable, and all three are almost completely absent from every page competing for this search.

Start with the one that costs whole subjects. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the board states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone — and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. That is a single clerical error with the weight of a whole qualification behind it. Ask the examinations officer at your child's school which zone the centre sits in, write it down, and use only that timetable.

Then the entry clock, and the first thing to get right is which series your child is even in. Cambridge examines IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, and a UAE centre works to those two; the February-March series that some search results throw up is offered in India only and is not available to a candidate sitting in Sharjah. The clearest confirmable worked example of how early the clock starts is Pearson's. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series; the November 2026 final written timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entries for each of those series closed months before the first paper, and Cambridge's June and November entries sit in the same relationship to their papers, with the exact closing date printed on the statement of entry your centre issues. Those dates mean the decisions that shape a result — subject, tier, board, series — are taken months before anybody is revising.

We should be clear about delivery before anything else: lessons for an Al Qasimia family are delivered online, one to one, over live video, with the student's own script on a shared screen. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We also do not send families syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables — those belong to the boards, and we link their official pages instead.
bullets: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones; the wrong zone timetable can cost a whole paper
UAE candidates sit Cambridge in June or November; the February-March series is offered in India only
A subject the school does not teach may still be sittable through an approved centre
Enquiries about a result are initiated by the centre, inside a short published window

sharjah/al-qasimia.programmesIntro: Central Sharjah carries a wide curriculum mix inside a small area, and that mix is why entry arrangements rather than content tend to be the first thing worth checking. These four programmes cover nearly all of our Al Qasimia enquiries.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses identified by a syllabus code, examined in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Several subjects are tiered, so a Core entry caps the grade while Extended runs the full range. Every candidate is entered through a centre allocated to one of six administrative zones.
programmes.countryNote: The practical Al Qasimia question is which centre holds the entry and which zone it belongs to. Centres in different zones sit the same syllabus on different days with different papers, so a student practising from the wrong zone's timetable can arrive on the wrong morning. The examinations officer, not the subject teacher, is the person who can answer this.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Linear in most subjects, with codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4EA1, examined in May/June and November each year. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then a final one, so any date a page quotes without linking the live official timetable may already be out of date.
programmes.countryNote: Several central Sharjah schools run Pearson in some subjects and Cambridge in others, sometimes within the same science department. A family revising from material bought by subject name rather than by code can spend a whole term practising the wrong paper structure. Read the code off the statement of entry and buy nothing that does not match it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, to a maximum of 45 points. Registration runs through an IB World School rather than through any general external route, and every subject carries an internally assessed component with a school deadline months ahead of the papers.
programmes.countryNote: The IB's own exam dates are not something we publish. The organisation blocks automated access to its site, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools overwhelmingly sit the May session; the date your child needs is the one their IB coordinator gives them, and that is the only source worth relying on.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Studied in depth after IGCSE, examined in June and November series alongside the IGCSE timetable, with the same zone allocation rules applying. For UAE equivalency on the British track, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, sits on top of the five-subject GCSE or IGCSE requirement.
programmes.countryNote: Central Sharjah families sometimes choose A Levels precisely because the external route is better established than for the Diploma, which matters where a school does not offer a subject a student needs. Whether a given centre accepts external candidates in a particular subject is a question for that centre, and the answer varies by subject and by series.

sharjah/al-qasimia.subjectsIntro: Our Al Qasimia enquiries are weighted towards the examined academic subjects, often with a specific component in mind rather than a whole course. Each entry below says what is assessed and where marks go.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: IGCSE Core and Extended; DP AA and AI
subjects.description: The tier decision caps the IGCSE grade and is made by the school, usually in Year 10. At Diploma level the Analysis and Approaches Higher Level third paper is worth 20% and is the least rehearsed component in the programme because it sits at the end of the schedule.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge offers both a practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which one a centre uses changes what to practise. At Diploma level the papers carry 36% and 44% with the scientific investigation at 20%.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and qualitative analysis at IGCSE. Students memorise the tests then cannot explain an observation, which is exactly what the longer questions ask. The two boards sequence organic chemistry differently.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The volume of content misleads students into revising terminology. The examined skill is applying a known principle to unfamiliar data, and it is practisable weekly from early in the course rather than in the final term.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus earns the marks, not definitions. The Diploma research project is internally assessed with a strict word limit and must be built on a real organisation with accessible information.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks prose cannot: correctly labelled axes, the correct shift, the new equilibrium identified. The internally assessed commentaries fail when students choose news articles with no identifiable mechanism in them.

subjects.name: English
subjects.levels: First Language 0500 / 0990; ESL 0510 / 0991; DP Language A
subjects.description: First Language English and English as a Second Language are different qualifications with different ceilings, and the entry is chosen by the school. Read which code is on the statement of entry before buying any support.

subjects.name: Accounting
subjects.description: A subject where method marks dominate and presentation is assessed. Students lose marks on layout and on balancing conventions rather than on the arithmetic, which makes it unusually responsive to a few sessions of disciplined practice.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory papers plus an internally assessed solution the student develops and documents. Able programmers lose marks on success criteria and the evidenced process rather than on the code.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: A student speaking a dialect at home and examined in Modern Standard Arabic sits between the two routes. The placement should rest on written evidence, and any support has to work from the school's own approved material.

sharjah/al-qasimia.regionsTitle: Al Qasimia and the central Sharjah districts around it
sharjah/al-qasimia.regionsIntro: Al Qasimia sits in the dense centre of the emirate, with short runs in most directions and the schooling choices of several neighbouring districts within reach. These are the ones that come up when we plan a term here.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: On the lagoon directly west, with a much higher share of children bussed into Dubai. An Al Qasimia family schooling locally has two usable hours more in the evening than an Al Majaz family with a Dubai place.

regions.name: Rolla and the old centre
regions.note: The commercial quarter immediately adjacent, with long-established schools and a high proportion of families whose children are sitting external or late entries. Walkable school runs, so the constraint here is study space rather than travel.

regions.name: Al Nahda, Sharjah
regions.note: Towards the Dubai boundary, where cross-border schooling is routine. Families comparing a central Sharjah school place with a Dubai one usually find the entry arrangements easier to manage locally.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Coastal, with a mix of local campuses and Dubai bus runs. Activity blocks rather than road conditions decide the evening here, which makes a defended weekly slot more important than an early one.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: The inland school belt, dense with campuses across several curricula. Al Qasimia families with a Muwaileh place have the most predictable run in the emirate and the widest choice of entry arrangements.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: The higher-education cluster inland. Relevant to Al Qasimia families because it is where a conversation about destinations and entry requirements becomes concrete rather than abstract.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Lagoon-side towers with a heavily mixed intake. Households here commonly run the international curriculum and the mandatory subjects in parallel, each with its own homework rhythm.

regions.name: Al Qasimia Corniche
regions.note: The creekside strip at the edge of the district itself. Apartment living, so a quiet room at seven in the evening is often harder to arrange than the tutoring slot is.

modes.description: A single session, sometimes just a conversation, whose purpose is to establish which centre holds the entry, which codes are on it, which zone timetable applies, what the tier is and when the next deadline falls. Families regularly discover something here that changes the plan entirely.

modes.description: A standing weekly slot aimed at a specific component rather than a whole subject: the alternative-to-practical paper, the data-analysis question, the extended response, the directed writing task. Narrow targets move marks faster than general revision does.

sections.heading: What an Al Qasimia tutoring search is usually trying to fix
paragraphs: Enquiries from central Sharjah divide differently from those we get elsewhere in the emirate. In the lagoon districts the first problem is usually the commute. Here it is usually an arrangement: something about the entry, the centre or the series that nobody explained, and that has quietly narrowed what is still possible. We spend the first part of these conversations establishing facts rather than diagnosing teaching needs, because the teaching plan depends on facts the family often has not been given.

The most common version is a tier. A parent believes their child is working towards a grade in the seven-to-nine range and the child has been entered for a Core paper that cannot award it. Nobody lied to anyone; the school made a placement decision in Year 10 on the basis of an assessment, and the entry was submitted months later without the word Core appearing in any conversation with the family. Finding out costs one question. Finding out in October rather than in March is the difference between a reviewable decision and a settled one.

The second is the missing subject. A student wants Further Mathematics, or Accounting, or a language the school does not teach, and has been told it cannot be done. Sometimes that is true for that school. It is frequently not true in general: Cambridge and Pearson both operate routes for candidates entered through an approved centre, and whether a particular centre accepts external candidates in a particular subject in a particular series is a question with a concrete answer. The IB is different, and we say so plainly: Diploma registration runs through an IB World School, and there is no equivalent general external route, so confirm anything in that space with an IB coordinator.

The third arrives in late August or late January, when results land. A grade is a mark against a boundary, not a percentage, and a result one mark below a boundary is a different situation from one ten marks below. Both have routes available, both routes are initiated by the centre rather than by the family, and both windows are short and published by the board. Families who do not know that lose the option by default, which is the worst way to lose anything.

sections.heading: Which centre entered your child, and which zone timetable it uses
paragraphs: A candidate does not sit a Cambridge examination as an individual. They sit it as a candidate of a centre, and the centre's administrative zone decides which version of the timetable applies. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination because the wrong version was used. The board could not be clearer, and almost no parent in this market has heard of it.

The practical risk is not theoretical. A family looks up the timetable, finds a date, plans the revision calendar around it, and the centre is in a different zone sitting that paper on a different day with a different question paper. In the best case somebody notices in March. In the worst case the student arrives for a paper that was yesterday. The fix takes one email: ask the examinations officer which zone the centre is allocated to, then download only that zone's timetable and work from nothing else.

The same conversation answers two other useful questions. Which syllabus codes is the candidate entered for — and they should be read, not assumed, because 0620 and 4CH1 are different Chemistry courses and 0654 is a double award while 0653 is single. And which practical arrangement applies in the sciences, because Cambridge offers a practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper, and most international centres use the alternative. That changes what a student should be practising from the start of Year 10.

Write all of it on the front of the folder: centre, zone, codes, tier, practical route. It takes five minutes and it is the cheapest intervention available to any family on this page. Everything a tutor does afterwards is more effective because the target is correct.

sections.heading: The entry clock, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: The dates that constrain a result are entry dates, not examination dates, and they sit much earlier than families expect. Pearson's published timetable is the clearest worked example available, because every date in it can be checked against the board's own page: the November 2026 International GCSE written papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entries for each series had closed months earlier. Cambridge's June and November series behave the same way for a Sharjah candidate: entries and forecast grades are collected well before the papers, and the exact dates for your centre are on the statement of entry rather than on any page like this one. The decisions that shape the result — which subjects, which tier, which board, which series — are therefore locked in while the student is still in the middle of the course.

Pearson works on its own cycle. Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for future November series, which is exactly why any page quoting a date without linking the live official timetable should be treated as unreliable: provisional dates are revised.

For the IB we publish no date at all. The organisation returns an error to automated requests, so nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and we will not put an unverified session or results date on a page that families plan around. UAE schools sit the May session overwhelmingly. The specific dates come from your child's IB coordinator, and that is the only source we would tell you to rely on.

What to do with this: build the term around the next deadline rather than around the examination. In September the next deadline is usually an entry or a tier decision. In November it is often a forecast-grade evidence point. In February it is an internal coursework deadline. Each of those is a different brief for a tutor, and a family that plans from the paper date alone spends the autumn doing work that would have been more valuable in the spring.

sections.heading: Sitting a subject the school does not teach
paragraphs: This comes up more in central Sharjah than anywhere else we work, because the district has a wide range of schools and a lot of ambitious students whose school does not offer the one subject they need. The answer is not uniform, and getting it right requires asking the right body rather than the nearest adult.

For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications, candidates are entered through a centre, and some centres accept candidates who are not their own students for some subjects in some series. Whether yours will is a question for that centre's examinations officer, and the answer depends on the subject, the practical requirements and the series. A subject with a practical test is harder to arrange than one assessed entirely by written paper, which is one reason the sciences are the most common refusal and mathematics, accounting and languages the most common acceptance.

For the IB Diploma the position is different and simpler. Registration runs through an IB World School; there is no general external route of the kind the other boards operate. If a student needs a Diploma subject their school does not teach, the realistic options are the school-supported self-taught route where it applies, a different subject choice, or a conversation with the IB coordinator about what the school can arrange. We would rather tell you that plainly than let you spend a term pursuing something that does not exist.

If an external entry is available and you decide to pursue it, the sequence matters. Confirm the centre will accept the entry before buying teaching, because the entry deadline is the binding constraint and it is months ahead of the paper. Establish the practical arrangement next. Then buy full-syllabus teaching rather than top-up support, since there is no class covering the content. The table sets out who is responsible for each step, because the most common failure here is everybody assuming somebody else is handling it.

sections.heading: Results day, boundaries and the window that closes quietly
paragraphs: A grade is a mark measured against a boundary set after the papers are marked. That is why a target expressed as a grade is less useful than one expressed as a mark: the grade is the output of a calculation nobody can see in advance, and the mark is the thing a student controls. It is also why a result one mark short of a boundary is a different problem from one twelve marks short, even though both look the same on a certificate.

The routes available after results exist, they are initiated by the centre rather than the candidate, and the windows are short. Both Cambridge and Pearson operate post-result services for reviewing marking, and both publish service descriptions and deadlines for each series. We will not state those deadlines here, because they change by series and a wrong date on a page like this would cause real harm. What we will tell you is the shape: the window is measured in weeks, not months; the centre has to submit the request; and there is normally a cost and a possibility that a mark can move in either direction. Ask the examinations officer for the current service dates on the day results arrive, not a fortnight later.

Retakes are the other route, and they are a planning decision rather than an emergency one. Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson runs May/June and November. A student who misses a boundary in June has a November option in several subjects, and the useful question is whether the gap between the two is long enough to change the outcome. Eight weeks of targeted work on the two components that failed is usually more valuable than retaking the whole subject with the same preparation.

This is where a tutor is most useful and most often bought too late. The post-results fortnight is when the decision gets made and the four weeks after it are when the work has to start. Families who wait until the new academic year settles have lost the most productive part of the window.

sections.heading: What tuition costs around Al Qasimia, and when in the year to buy it
paragraphs: Market bands in dirhams, with the source of each figure, read in October 2026. These are the market, not an IB Gram price list: our own arrangement starts with a free consultation and a trial session, and the figure that applies depends on the subject, the level and how scarce the specialism is. We publish these because three of the six pages ranking for this kind of search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote dollars.

The timing question matters more here than the rate. The same money buys very different amounts depending on when it is spent. Autumn money buys entry decisions and tier reviews, which are the highest-leverage purchases available because they change what grade is possible at all. Winter money buys component technique, which moves marks reliably. Spring money buys timed practice, which is useful. Money spent in the four weeks before a paper buys reassurance, which is worth something to a family but very little to a grade.

A low rate in this market usually means a university student, often working without the private-tuition work permit that national rules require. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, on the government's own account, subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you either.

For context against the dominant number in a family budget: Dubai's regulator reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, and confirmed in May 2026 that fees in that emirate would not rise for 2026-27 under an economic incentives package. Tutoring is usually a small fraction of what a household already spends on school, and judging an hourly rate against that total is more honest than judging it alone.

sections.heading: One-to-one online against a central Sharjah tuition centre
paragraphs: Al Qasimia has more tuition centres within walking distance than almost any district in the country, and that is a genuine alternative rather than a straw man. A group class at a local centre is cheaper per hour, it gets a child out of the apartment, and for some students the structure of turning up somewhere at a fixed time is itself the thing that works. We are not going to pretend that model has no merit.

What it does not do is target a component. A group class teaches the syllabus at the pace of the group, which means a student who is losing marks on the alternative-to-practical paper, or on directed writing, or on Paper 3 technique, sits through content they already have. The arithmetic is straightforward: a cheaper hour that addresses the wrong thing costs more than an expensive hour that addresses the right one. For students whose problem is a general content gap, the centre is often the better buy. For students whose problem is specific, it is not.

On the in-home question, which is what the search term implies: an in-home market exists in Sharjah and publishes rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — that service exists only in India — so the comparison here is between two models rather than a pitch for one. From Al Qasimia the travel objection is weaker than from the outer districts, because the district is central and a local tutor is genuinely findable. The constraint is the match: a general subject tutor is available nearby, a specialist in a particular component at Higher Level under the current guide usually is not.

sections.heading: Coursework, honesty and the documents we will not send you
paragraphs: Two boundaries apply to everything on this page, and both are worth stating before anybody books anything. The first is authorship. A tutor may teach a concept, read the published criteria with the student, read what the student has produced and say which band it currently sits in and why, ask the questions a good supervisor would ask, and teach the student how to redraft. A tutor may not become the author: no text for submission, no data, no graphs to be pasted in, no ready-made research question, no restructuring until the voice has changed. Internally assessed work is declared as the student's own, and a tutor who crosses that line creates a malpractice risk the student carries, not the tutor.

The second is copyright and material. We do not send families syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, they are published on the boards' own sites, and we link there instead. A tutoring service that emails you a folder of scanned mark schemes is telling you how it treats other people's rules, which is information about how it will treat yours.

There is a specific version of this worth naming for Al Qasimia, because the district has a lot of tuition centres and a lot of informal arrangements. Some operators in this market sell completed internal assessments outright at prices in the low thousands of dirhams. That is not an aggressive tutoring service; it is an academic-integrity breach that triggers malpractice procedures and can cost a student their diploma. If anybody offers it, the correct response is to end the conversation, because the offer tells you what else they would do.

One last boundary. The private-tuition work permit in the UAE carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's authority has professional-ethics rules to the same effect for schools in that emirate. Whatever emirate your child is schooled in, hiring their own subject teacher privately is not a route worth pursuing — and a tutor who offers it has told you something about their judgement before the first lesson.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Qasimia, in the right order
paragraphs: The order matters more here than the content of any individual session, so here it is. First establish the facts: centre, zone, codes, tier, practical arrangement, next deadline. That is one conversation with the examinations officer and it costs nothing. Second, look at the most recent marked script and find the repeated loss. Third, buy the narrowest intervention that addresses it. Families who reverse that order buy a term of general tutoring and then discover a tier problem in March.

Our first call is a free consultation and it is mostly these questions. We will tell you whether we can cover the subject at the level in question, and if we cannot we say so rather than offering something adjacent. For common combinations a match takes a few days. For scarce ones — external-candidate subjects, Higher Level sciences under the current guides, less widely taught languages — it takes longer and sometimes cannot be done this term. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, we will offer one from the wider pool delivering the same one-to-one online lesson from another time zone, disclosed before anything is booked, including what it means for an evening slot in central Sharjah.

Then the arrangement itself is deliberately plain: one slot, one target, one term, a review at the halfway point against something measurable. A timed paper marked to the real mark scheme is the best review instrument available and it costs one session. We send a written note after each lesson naming what was covered and what to practise, and we agree a stop date at the outset so the pattern ends when it has done its job.

If you take one thing from this page, make it the zone question. Ask the examinations officer which administrative zone your child's centre is allocated to, download that timetable, and discard every other version. It is a five-minute task that protects a two-year course, and nobody else competing for this search will have told you to do it.

process.title: Establish the facts before buying teaching
process.description: Which centre holds the entry, which administrative zone it is in, which syllabus codes are on the statement of entry, whether the tier is Core or Extended, and which practical arrangement applies. One conversation with the examinations officer settles all five, and it changes what is worth buying.

process.title: Find the repeated loss in the marked work
process.description: Send the most recent returned script with the teacher's annotations. We look for the comment that appears three times rather than at the grade, because that is the brief. A single identifiable component failing is a much cheaper problem to solve than a general sense of being behind.

process.title: Buy the narrowest intervention that fits
process.description: A component block rather than a whole-subject course, a diagnostic rather than a term, an administrative conversation rather than a lesson. We would rather sell you one session that resolves the question than twelve that work around it, and we will say when the honest answer is to buy nothing.

process.title: Review against a timed paper, then stop or continue
process.description: At the halfway point of the term, sit one paper under timed conditions and mark it against the real conventions. That is the only review instrument that tells you anything, and it costs a single session. The review can end the arrangement, and when it should, we say so.

whyPoints.title: We start with the entry, not the syllabus
whyPoints.description: Centre, zone, code, tier and practical arrangement decide what grade is reachable at all. Asking those five questions costs nothing and changes the plan more often than any teaching decision that follows. Most pages competing for this search do not mention a single one of them.

whyPoints.title: Dates come from the boards, or not at all
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson publish their calendars and we quote them with the source. The IB blocks automated access to its site, so we publish no IB session or results date and tell you to get it from your child's coordinator. A page that invents a date families plan around is doing real harm.

whyPoints.title: External and retake routes explained honestly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson entries run through a centre, and whether a given centre accepts external candidates varies by subject and series. The IB Diploma runs through an IB World School with no equivalent general route. We tell you which of those applies rather than letting you chase something that does not exist.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries a source and a date
whyPoints.description: The AED bands name the provider that published them and the month they were read; the permit and regulator statements name the authority. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no student count and no star rating, because we cannot show you the data behind one.

whyPoints.title: The material stays where it belongs
whyPoints.description: We link the boards' own pages for syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes rather than sending copies, and we do not produce assessed work. Both of those are rules we would keep whether or not anybody checked, and they are the two things the weakest operators in this market break first.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam centre and zone my Al Qasimia child is entered through?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer, not the subject teacher, because entries are an examinations-office function. You want two answers: which centre holds the entry, and which of Cambridge's six administrative zones that centre is allocated to. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Write the zone on the front of the folder and download only that timetable. It takes five minutes and protects a two-year course.

faqs.question: Can my child sit an IGCSE subject their Sharjah school does not teach?
faqs.answer: Often, but it depends on the centre. Cambridge and Pearson candidates are entered through a centre, and some centres accept candidates who are not their own students for some subjects in some series. Written-paper subjects such as mathematics, accounting and languages are the usual acceptances; subjects with a practical test are the usual refusals. Ask the centre's examinations officer directly, and confirm the entry before buying any teaching, because the entry deadline is the binding constraint. The IB Diploma is different: registration runs through an IB World School with no general external route.

faqs.question: When did entries actually close for the next series?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families expect, and the series matters as much as the date. A Sharjah candidate sits Cambridge in the June series or the November one, and entries for either close months ahead of the papers, with forecast grades collected before the examinations begin. Pearson's Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November series, and its November 2026 final written timetable ended on 19 November 2026, with entries long closed by then. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, and Cambridge timetables are split across six administrative zones, so always work from the live official timetable for your centre's zone rather than from a date quoted on a page. If you want a tier revisited, raise it in the autumn, before the entry goes in.

faqs.question: My child's result was one mark below a boundary. What can we do?
faqs.answer: Something, and quickly. Both Cambridge and Pearson operate post-result services for reviewing marking, and both publish the service descriptions and deadlines for each series. The request is submitted by the centre rather than by you, there is normally a cost, and a mark can in principle move in either direction. We deliberately do not quote the deadlines here because they change by series and a wrong date would cause real harm. Ask the examinations officer for the current service dates on the day results arrive, not two weeks later.

faqs.question: Is a retake in the next series worth it?
faqs.answer: It depends on the distance from the boundary and on what the destination actually requires. Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson runs May/June and November. A student a few marks short in one or two components usually does better with eight weeks of targeted work on exactly those components than with a full repeat of the course. A student a long way short has a content problem rather than a technique problem, and that takes a term. Before committing, read the receiving institution's own admissions page and check the grade is genuinely required.

faqs.question: Do your tutors visit homes in central Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For an Al Qasimia family every lesson is delivered online, one to one, over live video, with the student's own script on a shared screen. An in-home market does exist in Sharjah, publishing rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour, and because Al Qasimia is central a local general tutor is genuinely findable. What is harder to find locally is a specialist in one component at Higher Level, which is what the online match is for.

faqs.question: Is a local tuition centre cheaper than one-to-one for an Al Qasimia student?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and for some students it is the better choice. A group class gets a child out of the apartment, provides structure and teaches the syllabus at the pace of the group. What it cannot do is target a component. If your child is losing marks on the alternative-to-practical paper, or on directed writing, or on Paper 3 technique, a cheaper hour spent on content they already have is not a saving. Centres suit broad content gaps; one-to-one suits specific, diagnosed losses and scarce subjects.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1?
faqs.answer: They are different Chemistry qualifications from different boards, with different paper structures, different practical arrangements and content sequenced differently, particularly in organic chemistry. Cambridge tiers its entry into Core and Extended; Pearson's International GCSE is linear in most subjects. The consequence for a family is practical: past papers and revision material from one are of limited use for the other. Read the code off the statement of entry and buy nothing that does not match it. This is the single most common wasted term we see.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Sharjah need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own service. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The government states that individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion.

faqs.question: What should I ask the examinations officer before the autumn term ends?
faqs.answer: Five things, in one email. Which centre holds my child's entry. Which Cambridge administrative zone the centre is allocated to. Which syllabus codes my child is entered for. Whether each entry is Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. And which practical arrangement applies in the sciences, a practical test or the alternative written paper. Those five answers determine what grade is reachable, what past papers are relevant and what to prepare. Asking in October gives you options; asking in March usually gives you information about a decision already made.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school in Al Qasimia?
faqs.answer: If the campus is in Sharjah, the emirate's own authority does. On the UAE government's own account it regulates private education in the emirate, and Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — a broader remit than inspection alone. If your child attends a campus in Dubai, Dubai's authority applies instead, whatever your home address. Ask the school which authority licenses it, then read that authority's material rather than whatever a search returned first.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an internal assessment that is due soon?
faqs.answer: Inside a boundary we set out first. A tutor may read the published criteria with the student, read what the student has produced, say which band it sits in and why, teach the missing skill, and ask the questions a supervisor would ask. A tutor may not supply text, data or graphs, write a research question, or restructure a draft until the voice has changed. With six weeks a great deal can be done honestly. With six days the honest work is securing whichever criteria the existing material can still reach, which is usually more than families fear.

faqs.question: Can you email us the mark schemes for my child's Al Qasimia centre?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth explaining why rather than just declining. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. They are published on the boards' own sites, and we link there instead of distributing copies. A tutoring service that emails you a folder of scanned mark schemes has told you how it treats other people's rules. What we will do is teach your child to use official material properly, which is a different and more useful thing than owning more of it.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a tutor for a student in Al Qasimia?
faqs.answer: For common combinations — IGCSE Mathematics Extended, Diploma Biology Standard Level, English — usually within a few days. For scarcer requirements it takes longer and sometimes cannot be done this term: external-candidate subjects, Higher Level sciences under the current guides, Accounting at A Level and less widely taught languages are the recurring ones. We say so on the first call rather than offering a generalist. Where no UAE-based specialist is free we will offer one from the wider pool, delivering the same online lesson, and disclose the time-zone consequences before anything is booked.

Each one teaches a named syllabus, not a general subject.

intro.heading: Who lives in Al Rahmaniya, and what their school year looks like
paragraphs: Al Rahmaniya sits inland, on the Maliha Road side of Sharjah, where the emirate thins out from apartment blocks into plotted villa and townhouse communities. The households here split into two fairly distinct groups. The first is settled: Emirati and long-resident Arab expatriate families in large villas, often with three or four school-age children spread across primary and secondary, and usually with at least one child sitting a board exam in any given year. The second is newer and smaller, families who bought or rented into the master-planned communities that have gone up around this belt over the past few years, many of them moving out from Al Majaz, Al Khan or Al Nahda for space.

Those two groups ask for different things. The settled villa household tends to want one tutor who can hold several subjects together across siblings, with a schedule that survives a long school run and a single evening window. The newer household is more often mid-transition: a child who finished Year 8 in one curriculum and walked into IGCSE Year 10 in another, or a student who arrived in DP1 after a different Grade 10 system entirely. Both end up on the same search page, but the first needs capacity and continuity and the second needs diagnosis.

The academic pressure points follow from that. In the settled households, the recurring one is the jump from IGCSE to the Diploma Programme, where a student who collected A grades on 0580 Extended Maths discovers that Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes a fluency the IGCSE course never asked for. In the newer households it is more often Year 10 itself: a student who has never sat a structured, timed, command-term paper being asked to produce one every fortnight. Neither problem is a knowledge gap in the ordinary sense. Both are a technique gap, and technique is what responds fastest to one-to-one work.

Geography shapes the timetable more than parents expect. Al Rahmaniya households drive to schools in Muwaileh, University City, Al Khan and Al Jazzat, and a meaningful minority drive across to Dubai using Emirates Road. That means the school run does not finish when the bell does. A child who gets home at 16:20 on a good day and 17:15 on a bad one cannot hold a fixed 16:00 slot, and a tutor who has to be physically present loses the hour anyway in travel. Online delivery removes the travel from both sides of the arrangement, which is the practical reason it works out here rather than an abstract argument about technology.

The regulator for your child's private school is the Sharjah Private Education Authority. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and, according to the UAE government's own portal, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than parents assume: it means the subject menu at a Sharjah school is approved locally, not set by the exam board alone. If your child is dropping a subject, adding one, or moving between Core and Extended tiers, the school's answer sits inside a framework SPEA has signed off, and knowing that changes the question you ask at the parent meeting.

sharjah/al-rahmaniya.programmesIntro: Al Rahmaniya children sit three programme families between them, and the tutoring differs sharply by programme rather than by subject. What follows is what each one actually demands of a student in this part of Sharjah, including the part the school timetable does not cover.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, and converts those criteria into a 1-7 grade through a school-set boundary table. Students lose marks less on content than on criterion language: a Criterion D response in Sciences that discusses an experiment without evaluating its implications scores low however accurate the chemistry is. Tutoring at this stage is mostly teaching students to read the criterion strand they are being judged against and answer that strand on purpose.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Rahmaniya families the MYP years matter because this is where the Diploma subject choice is quietly decided. A student who has never been pushed in MYP Mathematics arrives at Analysis and Approaches without the algebraic fluency the course assumes. We use MYP 4 and 5 as the window to build that, rather than discovering the shortfall in DP1 term two.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE is where most Sharjah tutoring demand sits. Cambridge syllabuses run on codes - 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology - and Pearson runs its own, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics. The two boards split the same subject differently: paper counts, tiering, calculator policy and practical assessment all vary. A tutor who teaches the wrong board's structure wastes a term teaching the right content in the wrong shape.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah schools in and around this belt use both boards, and some run Cambridge in the sciences with Pearson in Mathematics. The first thing we confirm for an Al Rahmaniya enquiry is the syllabus code on the student's own exam entry, taken from the school, not from the textbook cover. That single check removes the commonest cause of wasted early sessions.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade, marked by the teacher and moderated externally. The structural difficulty is not any single component but the overlap: four internal deadlines, a 4,000-word essay and mock exams frequently land inside the same six weeks of DP2.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in this part of Sharjah are often the first in their family to sit the IB, which means the parent cannot calibrate whether a predicted 5 is a problem. We spend the first session mapping the student's actual component marks against the published assessment weightings, so the conversation moves from a vague grade to a specific paper.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Several Sharjah schools run International A Levels instead of the Diploma, usually three or four subjects taken linearly or modularly depending on the board. The assessment is narrower and deeper than the IB: no Internal Assessment in most subjects, no Theory of Knowledge, and a far heavier weighting on terminal written papers. Students who coasted through IGCSE on recall find the step into AS analysis the sharpest single jump in the British track.
programmes.countryNote: For equivalency purposes the A Level route matters to Al Rahmaniya leavers heading to UAE universities. The Ministry of Education's British-track rule asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE subjects. That makes the AS year a document requirement as well as an academic one.

sharjah/al-rahmaniya.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Al Rahmaniya households request most, with the part of each that actually costs marks. Nothing here is a general description of the subject; it is where a student in Year 10 or DP2 loses the grade they were predicted.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks go missing in the proof and reasoning strands rather than in computation. At HL, Paper 3 asks students to extend an unfamiliar result under time pressure, which rewards practice at reading a stem and deciding what is being asked. Most sessions here are about method selection, not arithmetic.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The Extended tier punishes students who cannot handle multi-step problems with no scaffolding. Transformations, functions and the harder trigonometry questions are where the grade boundary between a 7 and a 9 actually sits. Core-tier students more often lose marks on accuracy and units than on concepts.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism cause the most trouble, closely followed by the practical paper, where students describe a method without controlling a variable or identifying a systematic error. Learning the mark-scheme language for experimental design lifts practical scores faster than more content revision.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations are the standard failure point, and students who can balance equations often still cannot set up a limiting-reagent problem. Organic chemistry is usually taught late in the school year, which is why so many Sharjah enquiries about 0620 arrive in February.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: The HL extensions in energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are the separating topics. Students lose Internal Assessment marks under the analysis criterion for presenting data without uncertainty treatment, which is a technique problem a tutor can fix quickly without touching the student's own write-up.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Paper 2 extended-response questions reward candidates who answer the command term they were given. A question that says 'explain' and receives a description scores a fraction of the available marks. We work from the student's own returned papers so the diagnosis is based on their marks, not a generic weakness list.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: The volume of defined terminology is the first hurdle and data-based questions are the second. Students who can recall a process often cannot read a graph with two y-axes under exam conditions. Sessions here are usually split between consolidating the terminology and drilling unfamiliar data.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: The Higher tier has two equally weighted papers and no coursework, so pacing matters more than on some other boards. Students coming from a Cambridge textbook meet unfamiliar question styles in the later sections, which is why confirming the board before the first session is not pedantry.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of an unseen text is where the marks are won. Students from Sharjah schools frequently write fluent content summaries and score poorly because they have not addressed authorial technique. The Individual Oral needs a global issue narrow enough to argue in ten minutes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries more marks than students expect, and an unlabelled axis costs the same whatever the prose says. At IB HL the quantitative paper trips candidates who have revised theory only. IGCSE 0455 rewards structured eight-mark evaluations with a conclusion that actually decides something.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools under the federal framework, and it is the subject most often left to look after itself until a report card arrives. Streams for first-language and additional-language learners are taught separately and need different tutors.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Supervision support, not production. We help a student narrow a knowledge question, test whether an essay's claims can be evidenced, and read a draft against the published assessment criteria. The argument, the sources and the words remain entirely the student's own.

sharjah/al-rahmaniya.regionsIntro: Al Rahmaniya sits inside a wider inland and central Sharjah belt, and families move between these areas more than the map suggests. Each one changes the realistic lesson slot, because each one has a different school-run pattern.

regions.name: Sharjah Garden City
regions.note: Villa communities on the same inland corridor, with school runs that mostly head towards Muwaileh and University City. Afternoon returns here land late enough that a 17:30 or 18:00 slot is the first honest option on a weekday.

regions.name: Tilal City
regions.note: A newer plotted development further out along the inland route, where families tend to have younger children and a longer bus journey. Primary-age tutoring here works best at weekends rather than squeezed into a weekday evening.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: Townhouse and apartment communities closer to University City Road, which shortens the run to several of the bigger Sharjah schools. Students here can often hold a 16:30 slot, the earliest in this cluster.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Dense school territory, with several of the emirate's larger private schools inside a short radius. Traffic around dismissal is the constraint rather than distance, so parents here prioritise a slot that does not collide with the pick-up window.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Home to the university campuses and a number of schools, which makes the afternoon road pattern unusually busy in both directions. Older siblings studying locally often share a household study window with a DP student.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Central, apartment-dominated and a common previous address for families who have moved inland. Many Al Majaz children commute into Dubai schools, which pushes homework and tutoring into a narrow post-19:00 window.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Coastal and central, with a mix of apartment towers and older villas. Families here are the most likely in Sharjah to be weighing a Dubai school against a Sharjah one, and tutoring often has to bridge a mid-year move.

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: A large mixed-use development with a growing share of young families and a school on site. Demand here skews towards primary and MYP support rather than Diploma work, and weekend morning slots fill first.

schoolClusters.city: Inland and central Sharjah schools
schoolClusters.note: These are the schools Al Rahmaniya households name most often when they enquire, spread across Muwaileh, University City, Al Jazzat and the central districts. Programme menus change between academic years, so confirm the current curriculum and exam board directly with the school before buying a single textbook.
schools: The American School of Creative Science, Sharjah

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools reached on the Emirates Road commute
schoolClusters.note: A minority of Al Rahmaniya families drive across the emirate line each morning, and for them the tutoring timetable has to survive a return journey that varies by forty minutes depending on the day. These schools sit under KHDA rather than SPEA, which changes the inspection framework a parent reads.

sharjah/al-rahmaniya.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Al Rahmaniya enquiry. All three run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen and a saved board, so the student keeps the written record of every session rather than a page of their own hurried notes.

modes.title: Weekly subject tuition
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, a fixed weekly slot held for the academic year. This is what the multi-sibling villa household usually wants, because the slot becomes a fixture the family can plan around. Progress is tracked against the school's own assessment calendar, so the work in a given fortnight matches what the class is being graded on rather than running on a separate schedule.

modes.description: Three to four sessions with a defined question to answer: is this a content gap, a technique gap, or a tier mismatch. The output is a written view a parent can take to a school meeting, including which paper the marks are actually being lost on. Families mid-transition into IGCSE or DP1 usually start here rather than committing to a year of weekly slots.

This is the format that suits a student whose content knowledge is sound and whose exam output is not.
