sections.heading: Testing a shortlist in one trial lesson: the questions that actually separate tutors
paragraphs: A free trial lesson is only useful if you know what you are testing. Most parents use it to see whether their child liked the tutor, which is worth something but is the weakest available signal; a pleasant hour and no grade movement is the most common outcome in this market. Use the trial to test specification fluency, diagnostic ability and honesty about what they cannot do. Those three predict the next six months better than rapport does.

Bring one artefact: your child's most recently marked school paper, with the marks still on it. Ask the tutor to read it live and tell you the three places your child is losing marks and why. A specialist will separate a knowledge gap from a command-term failure within a few minutes and will tell you which one is cheaper to fix. A generalist will talk about confidence. Both answers are real, but only one of them is a plan.

Then ask the questions a brochure cannot answer. Which paper is worth 20% on this specification? What does Paper 6 ask a candidate to do that a practical test does not? What is the tier decision on 4MA1 and who makes it? Which topic in this syllabus does my child's school usually teach last, and does that matter for a February series? And the one that matters most: what would make you tell me my child does not need tutoring in this subject?

Finally, settle the commercial terms in the same conversation, before anyone is emotionally invested. Per hour or per session. What happens to a missed lesson. Whether the rate changes in the exam term. How progress will be reported and how often. Whether the rate quoted includes any tax the provider is obliged to charge, which is a question for the provider rather than for a web page, since UAE tax treatment should be confirmed against the Federal Tax Authority rather than asserted by a tutoring site.

whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning and written feedback on the student's own work, with a hard line against producing assessed work. A page in this search sells completed Internal Assessments; the student who buys one carries the malpractice risk, not the seller.

faqs.question: Why do two IGCSE tutor quotes in Sharjah differ by AED 200 an hour?
faqs.answer: Because they are quoting different tiers, formats and subjects. Published UAE market bands run from AED 45-150 an hour for a budget online or university-student tutor, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200-450 or more for an IGCSE or A Level specialist, with premium named tutors quoted as high as AED 650. In-home rates of AED 180-500 include the tutor's travel. Add subject scarcity, how close the series is, and whether the quote is per hour or per 90-minute session, and a AED 200 gap stops being mysterious. Ask which tier, which format and which basis before comparing.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book an IGCSE tutor based in Sharjah or one based in Dubai?
faqs.answer: For online lessons, location stops being a pricing input, which is the main commercial argument for them. For in-person lessons it matters a great deal: a Dubai-based tutor crossing into Al Nahda or Al Majaz at peak is pricing an hour of driving into the session, and published in-home bands of AED 180-500 reflect that. The more useful question is which tutor has taught your child's exact syllabus code. Online delivery widens the pool from whoever is drivable to whoever is qualified, and for families in Kalba or Khor Fakkan that is the difference between a specialist and nobody.

faqs.question: Does a tutoring rate quoted in Sharjah include tax?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, because it changes the real cost. This page will not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees as a fact: that should be confirmed against the Federal Tax Authority rather than asserted by a tutoring website, and a provider should be able to tell you whether a quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive and whether they hold a tax registration number. The same applies to anything described as free. If a trial lesson is free, confirm the length, the eligibility and whether any card details are required before it.

faqs.question: How many hours of IGCSE tutoring does a Sharjah Year 11 student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the diagnosis rather than the subject. A student losing marks to command-term misreading can be moved substantially in six to eight focused sessions, because the fix is technique. A student with genuine content gaps across a two-year syllabus needs weekly work across a full term or more. One marked past paper usually settles which situation you are in. The expensive mistake is buying a package of ten before anyone has diagnosed the loss pattern, then discovering in week six that the problem was timing. Diagnose first, buy second, and review against marked work every four to six weeks.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tutoring rates in Sharjah rise closer to the June series?
faqs.answer: Effective rates stiffen because supply collapses rather than because anyone posts a new price. In the eight to ten weeks before a series, the specialists in Extended Maths, triple science and thin-cohort subjects have no good slots left, so what remains is either a less experienced tutor at the same money or a scarce specialist at the top of the band. Booking in September for a June series means buying in a soft market. For the November series, with Pearson's November 2026 timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, serious preparation starts in August.

faqs.question: Is a Sharjah tuition centre group class better value than one-to-one lessons?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is whether your child's problem is shared. Group classes are priced well below one-to-one and work when a whole cohort needs the same syllabus coverage in the same order, which is common in breadth revision. They work poorly for a diagnosed individual weakness, because the pace cannot stop on your child's specific error. A reasonable pattern is group revision for coverage plus a small number of one-to-one sessions on the two components actually dragging the grade. Centres with premises and staff need an educational services permit, which is a different thing from a tutor's permit.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Sharjah, and does that change what a tutor should teach?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and in Sharjah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is broader than inspection alone. For tutoring it means the specification your child is examined on has been approved, so a tutor who proposes working from a different board's material because it looks similar is making a decision that belongs to the school. Confirm the board and the syllabus code with the school, then insist the tutoring matches it. SPEA does not regulate what a private tutor charges you.

faqs.question: How do I check an IGCSE tutor is permitted to tutor privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and it is applied for through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a published two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so distrust any specific amount quoted at you.

faqs.question: My child's Sharjah school uses Edexcel rather than Cambridge, so does the price change?
faqs.answer: The tier bands are the same, but the shortlist is not. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, use two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them, while Cambridge Extended sciences use a multiple-choice paper at 30%, a theory paper at 50% and Paper 6 Alternative to Practical at 20%. Maths differs too: 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher with two equally weighted papers, while 0580 splits into Core and Extended routes and requires a non-calculator paper. A tutor fluent in one board is not automatically fluent in the other, so ask which they have taught.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children in the same house sitting different boards?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is worth asking, but do not assume it. A tutor who has taught both Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 can switch between them, and in Sharjah households with children at different schools this is a common request. Where it breaks down is in thin-cohort subjects and in set-text-dependent subjects like Literature, where the texts differ by school. The practical arrangement that works is consecutive one-to-one slots rather than a shared session, because the two children are almost never losing marks in the same place.

faqs.question: What should a free trial lesson prove before I agree to a Sharjah rate?
faqs.answer: Three things, none of them rapport. First, specification fluency: the tutor should name the paper weightings on your child's exact syllabus code without looking them up. Second, diagnosis: given one marked school paper, they should identify three loss points and say which is cheapest to fix. Third, honesty about limits: ask what would make them recommend against tutoring, and listen to whether an answer exists. Settle the commercial terms in the same conversation, including whether the rate is per hour or per session and what happens to a missed lesson.

faqs.question: Will a budget-tier tutor be enough for IGCSE Extended Mathematics?
faqs.answer: For a secure student who needs structure and homework accountability, often yes, and the published budget band of roughly AED 45-150 an hour makes that an efficient choice. For a student losing marks across algebraic fractions, non-calculator technique and multi-step problem solving under time pressure, usually not: the work needs someone who has marked against the board's mark scheme and knows where method marks are awarded. The honest test is the trial lesson with a marked paper in hand. A budget tutor who diagnoses accurately is better value than a specialist who teaches content your child already has.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor mark coursework before my child submits it?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read the student's own draft and give written feedback on it, explain the criteria, question the argument and set a working schedule. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it to completion, or supply text for submission, and no reputable provider should offer to. One page competing for this search sells completed Internal Assessments; the student who submits bought work carries the malpractice consequence, not the seller. Note also that most current IGCSE specifications put the marks in written papers and in components such as Paper 6, so paper technique is usually where tutoring money works hardest.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's IGCSE subject in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a realistic match time rather than placing a generalist. Thin-cohort subjects are the ones affected: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Further Pure 4PM1, Computer Science 0478, and some language specifications. Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the alternative is a specialist elsewhere teaching on Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed before anything is booked rather than concealed behind an international phone number. The practical advice is to ask early: scarce-subject availability in the ten weeks before a series is the hardest thing to find in this market.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our building in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, and does not operate an office, centre or branch in the country; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Sharjah families are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that your shortlist is not limited to tutors within a drivable radius, which matters most in Halwan, Al Dhaid, Kalba and Khor Fakkan, where a specialist for a thin-cohort subject is unlikely to live nearby. The practical cost is that you need a quiet room and a stable connection.

faqs.question: How does an IGCSE grade affect Ministry of Education equivalency in the UAE?
faqs.answer: On the British track, published requirements ask for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects, and one ranking competitor publishes a higher subject count that does not match the published rule. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, and no provider performs or guarantees the process. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

intro.heading: What 0606 adds to a Sharjah family's tutoring bill, and why
paragraphs: Most families in this emirate meet Additional Mathematics 0606 twice. The first time is a line on a Year 10 options sheet that nobody reads closely. The second is a parents' evening in Year 11, when a maths teacher says the words "she is coping with 0580 but 0606 is slipping", and a household that had budgeted for one maths subject discovers it has two. That is the moment this page is written for, and the first honest thing to say is that the second subject does not cost half as much to support as the first. It usually costs more per hour, because fewer people in the Sharjah market teach it.

The arithmetic is worth doing before the first phone call rather than after the third invoice. Published rates for a qualified subject tutor working online across the UAE sit at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE support from AED 150. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table running to AED 450 plus for exam-year specialists. Those are market figures from the providers and the rate survey named, not an IB Gram price list. What this page does with them is translate them into the number a family actually pays, which is monthly.

Monthly is the unit that matters because 0606 is not a subject that responds to a single rescue session. It is a syllabus built on fourteen topic areas where almost every one depends on fluency with indices, surds and algebraic fractions established months earlier. A weekly hour across two terms is cheaper in total than a panic block in April and it produces a different outcome, which makes the monthly band the figure to compare between providers. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

Sharjah complicates the picture in a way Dubai does not. A large share of households in Al Nahda, Al Majaz and Al Khan send children to campuses across the border in Dubai, so the school day ends later than the postcode suggests and the realistic start time for a weekday session drifts towards 18:00 or later. Meanwhile the pool of people in this emirate who have actually taught two full 0606 cohorts is small. Those two facts together are why an in-home maths tutor is quoted higher here than the mileage alone would justify, and why online delivery changes the price as well as the logistics.

So the page below is ordered as a cost argument. It prices a plan by the month, explains why a 0606 hour carries a premium over a 0580 hour, separates the travel component from the teaching component, lays out five ways to buy help from cheapest to dearest, shows which topics the money is actually spent on, and finishes with what a parent in this emirate can check for themselves before paying anyone. IB Gram delivers all of it as one-to-one online tuition over live video; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and no tutor will be sent to a Sharjah address.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths.programmesIntro: Additional Mathematics 0606 sits in the middle of a route, not at the end of one. These are the stages either side of it, with what each costs a Sharjah household in time and attention.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: A second, separate Cambridge IGCSE taken alongside Extended Mathematics 0580 rather than instead of it. Two papers of two hours, 80 marks each, equally weighted, calculator permitted. Content covers functions, quadratics, indices and surds, polynomials, logarithms and exponentials, straight-line graphs, circular measure, trigonometry, permutations and combinations, series, two-dimensional vectors, and differentiation and integration. Graded A* to E only.
programmes.countryNote: A minority of Sharjah timetables carry it. Where it appears it is usually offered to a single top set, often taught in fewer periods than 0580 gets, which is precisely why private support is bought for it more often per candidate than for any other Cambridge maths code in this emirate.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, Extended tier
programmes.description: The compulsory maths qualification almost every Cambridge candidate in Sharjah sits. The Extended tier is the prerequisite in practice for Additional Mathematics, because 0606 assumes Extended algebra is already automatic rather than something to be reasoned out. Where a student is still working slowly through surd manipulation or algebraic fractions in 0580, that gap surfaces as a calculus problem a term later.
programmes.countryNote: Support for 0580 and 0606 is often sold as two separate weekly hours in this market. It does not have to be. A single specialist hour that treats the 0580 algebra as the warm-up for the 0606 technique is both cheaper and more coherent, and that bundling decision is the single biggest lever a Sharjah family has over the monthly figure.

programmes.name: Cambridge AS and A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The qualification 0606 was designed to feed. Pure Mathematics 1 revisits differentiation, integration, circular measure, series and trigonometric identities at greater depth and with stricter notation. A student who has sat 0606 arrives having already met every one of those ideas once, which changes the first term of Year 12 from an introduction into a consolidation.
programmes.countryNote: For Sharjah families planning a UK or Gulf engineering or economics route, this is where the 0606 spend is recouped. AS Mathematics 9709 preparation is substantially easier to resource locally than 0606 itself, so the expensive year is Year 11, not Year 12.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The other common destination. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level opens with function notation, transformations, sequences and series, then moves quickly into differentiation. None of that is new to a 0606 candidate. The adjustment is to the IB's command terms and to an internal assessment that has no equivalent in the Cambridge system.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah households switch board between Year 11 and Year 12, usually by moving to a Dubai Diploma campus. A 0606 grade travels well into that move; what does not travel is the assumption that the Cambridge exam technique will score in an IB paper, and that is worth one honest conversation before Year 12 starts.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths.subjectsIntro: 0606 is fourteen topic areas, and tutoring money is not spent evenly across them. This is where the hours actually go, ordered roughly by how much private support a Sharjah candidate typically needs per topic.

subjects.name: Differentiation
subjects.description: The product, quotient and chain rules, stationary points, increasing and decreasing functions, rates of change and small increments. The single largest consumer of tutoring hours in the syllabus. Students usually acquire the rules quickly and then lose marks for a term because they cannot rewrite an expression into a differentiable form first.

subjects.name: Integration
subjects.description: Indefinite and definite integration, area under a curve, kinematics applications. Marks are lost to omitted constants of integration, limits substituted in the wrong order, and the assumption that an area below the axis contributes positively. Usually the second-heaviest block of paid hours after differentiation.

subjects.name: Indices, surds and algebraic fractions
subjects.description: Not a glamorous topic area and not where parents expect to spend money, but the hidden tax on everything else. A student who cannot turn one over the square root of x into x to the power of minus a half will be unable to differentiate it, and the symptom presents as a calculus failure rather than an algebra one.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and trigonometric identities
subjects.description: Identities, equations over a stated interval, amplitude and period, and graphs of the three principal functions. The recurring loss is finding one correct solution and stopping, when the question asks for all solutions in a given range. Easily diagnosed from a marked paper and relatively cheap to fix once seen.

subjects.name: Circular measure
subjects.description: Radian measure, arc length, sector area and composite shapes. The degree-to-radian switch is where most of the damage happens, because a calculator left in degree mode produces an answer that looks plausible and scores nothing. Typically one or two sessions, not a term.

subjects.name: Functions and inverse functions
subjects.description: Domain and range stated properly, composite functions, inverses, the modulus function and graph transformations. Notation is assessed here as strictly as method. Students who write a composite the wrong way round lose the marks even where the arithmetic that follows is sound.

subjects.name: Logarithmic and exponential functions
subjects.description: Laws of logarithms, solving exponential equations, and linearising a relationship to find constants from a straight-line graph. The graph-linearising question is a reliable source of lost marks because it requires a student to decide what to plot before any calculation starts.

subjects.name: Series and binomial expansions
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric progressions, sums to infinity, and the binomial expansion including the term-independent-of-x question. Often left until late in Year 11 and then crammed, which is the expensive way to learn it. Cheaper to take two early sessions in the autumn term.

subjects.name: Permutations and combinations
subjects.description: Arrangements, selections, restrictions and the repeated-items case. Distinctive because success depends on reading precisely rather than on technique. A student who is strong at calculus can still score badly here, and the fix is a specific style of question practice rather than more teaching.

subjects.name: Vectors in two dimensions
subjects.description: Position and displacement vectors, magnitude, unit vectors, and velocity problems involving relative motion. A compact topic area with a predictable question style, usually covered in one or two sessions once the notation is settled.

subjects.name: Quadratic functions, equations, inequalities and graphs
subjects.description: Completing the square, the discriminant, intersections of a line and a curve, and inequalities involving a modulus. The discriminant conditions are a frequent source of lost marks because students solve the equation rather than answering the question about the number of roots.

subjects.name: Factors of polynomials and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: The factor and remainder theorems, cubic factorisation, and simultaneous equations where one is non-linear. Mechanically straightforward and well taught in most Sharjah classrooms, so rarely worth buying separate hours for unless a marked paper shows otherwise.

sections.heading: The bill nobody planned for when 0606 appeared on the timetable
paragraphs: A household supporting one Cambridge maths subject has a predictable cost. A household supporting two does not, because the second subject behaves differently in the market. Extended Mathematics 0580 is taught in every Cambridge school in the emirate, which means supply is deep, rates are competitive and a parent can choose on price. Additional Mathematics 0606 is taught in a minority of Sharjah timetables, often to one set, sometimes in fewer periods than 0580 receives. Supply is thin, and thin supply is what a premium is made of.

The practical consequence is that the first three quotes a parent collects for 0606 will come back wider apart than three quotes for 0580 would. One will be from the budget end of the market, where published online rates start around AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. One will be from a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300. One will be from a specialist agency at AED 270 or above. Those are three different products, and the gap between them is not padding.

What turns that spread into a decision is knowing what a 0606 hour has to contain. It is not revision company. A student who can state the chain rule and still cannot differentiate a quotient involving a surd needs someone who recognises that the obstacle is index notation, not calculus, and who will spend twenty minutes on algebraic rewriting before touching a derivative. That diagnosis is what separates the AED 60 hour from the AED 270 hour, and it is diagnosable in a single trial lesson rather than guessable from a profile.

The rest of this page prices that choice out. It starts with the monthly figure, because the hourly rate is the number providers advertise and the monthly total is the number families actually live with.

sections.heading: What a 0606 plan costs by the month, not by the hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how this market advertises and monthly totals are how households budget, so the table below converts the published bands into the second form. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Read the table as a comparison frame rather than a price list. Every figure in it is attributed to the provider or the rate survey that published it, and IB Gram's own arrangement is a free trial lesson followed by a plan agreed with the family — not a published tariff. The column that usually changes a decision is the last one, because the cheapest monthly figure and the cheapest route to a grade are frequently not the same row.

One number in the table deserves separate mention: the hours remaining. A family that starts a weekly hour in October has roughly thirty sessions before a June series. A family that starts in April has six. The April family will pay a higher hourly rate because intensive work is priced higher, buy fewer hours, and ask those hours to cover the whole calculus block. That is the most expensive version of this purchase available, and it is reached by waiting rather than by choosing.

For a Sharjah household running two Cambridge maths codes at once, the monthly figure is also where bundling shows up. Two separate weekly hours with two separate tutors is two monthly fees. One specialist hour that opens with the 0580 algebra a 0606 question will need is one fee, and in most cases the better lesson.

sections.heading: Why an hour of 0606 is priced above an hour of 0580
paragraphs: Parents reasonably expect two Cambridge maths codes to cost about the same to support. They do not, and the reasons are worth knowing because two of them are negotiable and one is not.

The reason that is not negotiable is the size of the teaching pool. Extended Mathematics is sat by almost every Cambridge candidate in the emirate, so anyone who has taught IGCSE maths has taught 0580. Additional Mathematics is an optional second subject offered by a minority of schools, so the set of people who have taken a cohort through both papers and seen where that cohort lost marks is far smaller. A Cambridge IGCSE maths tutor in Al Majaz is a straightforward search. A 0606 specialist in the same postcode frequently is not, and scarcity prices itself.

The second reason is that 0606 overlaps with AS-level content, which means the tutors who are genuinely comfortable with it are usually also teaching AS Mathematics 9709 or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Those are higher-rate engagements. An hour sold to a 0606 candidate is an hour not sold at a sixth-form rate, and quotes reflect that. The third reason is preparation load: the two papers reward exact-form answers and complete solution sets over stated intervals, so a tutor who marks properly is spending time outside the session on work a parent never sees.

Two of those three are negotiable in practice. Bundling 0580 and 0606 into one weekly specialist hour reduces the total fee without reducing contact time on either, because the algebra one subject needs is the algebra the other is assessed on. And starting early converts specialist hours from scarce exam-season inventory into ordinary autumn-term inventory, which is a different price in every tutoring market there is.

sections.heading: The travel line: an in-home maths tutor in Sharjah against the same hour online
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real and legitimate market in this emirate and parents are right to ask about it. Published figures put an in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Set against a qualified online rate of AED 150 to 300, the difference is not a quality difference. It is a logistics charge, and the table below separates it out so a family can decide whether to pay it.

In Sharjah that charge buys something specific, and it is worth being precise about what. It buys a tutor physically present in the room, which helps a younger or less organised student stay on task. It costs three things: money, the tutor's travel window either side of the hour, and the available pool. A tutor who will drive to Tilal City at 17:30 on a Tuesday is selected from the people willing to make that drive, not from the people who have taught 0606 twice. For a niche syllabus code, that constraint is the whole argument.

The timing arithmetic is sharper here than almost anywhere else in the UAE. A family in Al Nahda whose children attend a Dubai campus often sees the bus arrive after 16:30. An in-home session booked for 17:00 on the corniche side of Al Khan starts late because the tutor is in the same traffic the bus was. By the time the hour genuinely begins it is 17:25, and the hour is billed from 17:00. Online, the same session starts when the student sits down.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India, and no tutor will be sent to a Sharjah address. What a Sharjah family gets instead is access to the specialist rather than to whoever is within a twenty-minute drive, which on a subject taught by a handful of people in the emirate is the more valuable thing to be buying.

sections.heading: Cheapest first: five ways to buy 0606 help in this emirate
paragraphs: Most pages about tutoring costs start with the premium option and work down. This one goes the other way, because a family deciding how to spend AED 600 a month needs to know what the cheap options genuinely deliver before being shown what AED 1,800 adds. Three of the five rows below cost nothing or almost nothing, and at least one of them should be exhausted before any money changes hands.

The free options are real. Cambridge publishes the syllabus for 0606 on cambridgeinternational.org, which states exactly what is assessed in each topic area; reading it with a child for twenty minutes removes a surprising amount of anxiety and shows precisely which of the fourteen areas have not yet been taught. Most schools in this emirate run some form of maths support session, and the maths department will usually say, if asked directly, whether the problem is a topic gap or a pace problem. That answer determines which of the paid rows is appropriate and is worth more than the first paid session.

What the paid rows buy, in ascending order, is diagnosis. A budget tutor at the AED 45 to 150 band will answer the question a student brings. A qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 will sequence teaching ahead of the school. A specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above will look at a marked paper, identify that the lost marks are index notation rather than calculus, and change what is taught. The price difference tracks that difference, and a trial lesson is how a parent tells which one they are actually being offered.

The row families most often get wrong is the group option. Small-group tuition at two to four students lowers the per-student rate, and for a well-taught subject with a broad cohort that trade is often sensible. For 0606 in Sharjah it rarely works, because the cohort is small, the students in it are at different points in the calculus, and assembling three candidates on the same syllabus code in the same week is harder than it sounds.

sections.heading: Where the money actually goes: the calculus block and the eight weeks around it
paragraphs: Across a full year of 0606 support, spending is not evenly distributed and should not be. A family that understands which weeks are expensive can plan the budget rather than react to it. In this syllabus the costly stretch is the eight to ten weeks in which differentiation and integration are taught, and the reason is that those weeks expose every earlier gap at once.

Here is the mechanism. Differentiation itself is a short list of rules that a capable Year 11 student can learn in two sessions. What takes ten weeks is the rewriting that has to happen first: turning a root into a fractional index, splitting a fraction into separate terms, recognising that a product has to be expanded before it can be differentiated term by term. All of that is 0580 Extended algebra. A student who has been reasoning it out slowly rather than performing it automatically will appear to have a calculus problem, and a tutor who treats the symptom will bill hours against the wrong topic.

That is why an 0606 calculus tutor online is worth paying more per hour than a general maths tutor, and why the trial lesson matters more than the profile. The question to listen for in that first session is not whether the tutor can differentiate — everyone can — but whether they ask the student to simplify before differentiating, and whether they notice the hesitation when the student does it. The tutors who do that convert a ten-week problem into a four-week one, and that is where the premium pays for itself.

The weeks either side of the block are cheaper and should be budgeted as such. Circular measure, vectors and the polynomial work are compact, well taught in most Sharjah classrooms, and rarely need more than a session each. Permutations and combinations needs question practice rather than teaching. Series needs two early sessions in the autumn so it is not being met for the first time in April. Planning around that shape is how a family spends AED 700 a month for eight months instead of AED 1,800 a month for three.

sections.heading: Paying twice: 0580 and 0606 in the same series, one tutor or two
paragraphs: A Sharjah candidate sitting Additional Mathematics is almost always sitting Extended Mathematics 0580 in the same series. That means four written papers in one subject area, and it raises the question most directly responsible for an inflated monthly figure: does the family buy two weekly hours from two tutors, or one from one?

The case for two is honest and occasionally correct. The papers differ in style, the 0580 Extended papers reward breadth and careful arithmetic across a wide syllabus while the 0606 papers reward technique and exact presentation, and a student genuinely behind on both may need separate time. Where a child is at risk of a grade 4 or 5 in 0580 rather than chasing an A in 0606, the two subjects have different problems and splitting them can be sensible.

The case for one is stronger for most families, and it is cheaper. The 0606 content assumes 0580 Extended algebra is automatic, so a well-built single hour uses the first fifteen minutes on the exact 0580 skills the 0606 work will need next, then spends the rest on the technique. The student gets both subjects taught by one person who can see which is causing the other to fail. The household pays one monthly fee. And the written work comes back marked by someone who knows what the student did last week, which is not true of two tutors who never speak to each other.

There is a scheduling argument as well, and in this emirate it carries weight. Two weekly sessions means two slots to protect in a week that already contains Arabic and Islamic education homework, a Dubai school run and, for many families, a bus that returns after 16:30. One slot survives a busy term. Two tend to become one anyway, usually the wrong one, with the fee still being paid for both.

sections.heading: What a Sharjah parent can verify before paying anyone
paragraphs: Almost everything in a tutoring pitch is unverifiable, and almost everything that matters is checkable. The table below is the short list of things a parent in this emirate can confirm independently, with where to confirm them. None of it takes more than an evening, and doing it before the first payment is the cheapest insurance available in this market.

Start with the permit position, because it is the one most providers are vague about. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered through MoHRE, whose service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting an amount is guessing. Because it is free, a tutor's permit costs a family nothing and should never appear as a line in a quote.

Next, the regulator. Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for the emirate's private schools. That is a school-level remit, not a tutoring one: SPEA does not set what a private tutor may charge, and no tutoring provider — IB Gram included — may describe itself as holding an approval or accreditation from SPEA, from the Ministry of Education or from Cambridge. IB Gram holds none of those, and a page claiming otherwise is the clearest warning sign in this SERP.

Finally, check the materials question, because it separates teaching from selling. Cambridge syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are Cambridge's copyright material and are distributed through schools and the official site. A tutor refers to them, cites them and works from them; a provider that offers to supply a bundle of them as a download is telling you something about how it operates.

sections.heading: Does the 0606 spend pay? AS 9709, Maths AA HL and the equivalency count
paragraphs: The honest answer to whether an expensive Year 11 is worth it depends on where the student is going in Year 12, and for Sharjah families there are three realistic destinations. Each changes the calculation.

If the destination is Cambridge A Level Mathematics 9709, the return is direct and measurable in time. Pure Mathematics 1 revisits differentiation, integration, circular measure, series and trigonometric identities, with stricter notation and harder questions. A 0606 candidate has met every one of those ideas already, which turns the first term of Year 12 into consolidation rather than first contact. Families who skipped 0606 frequently buy that term back in paid support instead, which means the cost does not disappear — it moves.

If the destination is the IB Diploma, the return is real but partial. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level opens with functions, transformations, sequences and series and moves quickly into calculus, so the content advantage holds. What does not transfer is exam technique: the IB's command terms, its mark-scheme conventions and its internal assessment have no Cambridge equivalent. Budget for a short adjustment period in Year 12 rather than assuming the Cambridge habits will score.

If the destination is a UAE university and Ministry of Education equivalency, 0606 is a useful subject but not a required one, and this is where families should be careful with what they read. The British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competitor page ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring provider performs or can promise, and nothing on this page should be read as implying that tutoring is needed to obtain it.

process.title: Send the marked paper, not the report card
process.description: A school report says a grade. A marked 0606 paper says which topic area lost the marks and whether the cause was method, notation or algebra underneath. Photograph the most recent one and send it with the enquiry. It is the single thing that makes the first session useful rather than exploratory.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson and watch for one thing
process.description: The trial lesson is one hour, online, with no card required and no obligation. Watch whether the tutor asks the student to simplify an expression before differentiating it, and whether they notice any hesitation. That behaviour, not the profile, is what distinguishes a specialist from a competent generalist on this syllabus.

process.title: Agree the plan shape and the monthly figure
process.description: Decide between a weekly hour to the series, a bounded topic block or a pre-series intensive, and fix the number of sessions a month so the cost is known rather than accumulating. Ask whether 0580 can be folded into the same hour; for most candidates it can, and that is the largest single saving available.

process.title: Hold one slot, in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Pick a time that survives a bus arriving after 16:30 and an evening containing Arabic and Islamic education homework. For most Sharjah families with children at Dubai campuses that means 18:00 or later. One protected slot a week outlasts two optimistic ones, and it is cheaper.

process.title: Review at week six against written work
process.description: Six sessions in, look at marked questions rather than impressions. Exact-form answers presented correctly, complete solution sets over a stated interval, constants of integration present. If those are moving, the plan is working. If they are not, change the tutor rather than adding hours to the same arrangement.

whyPoints.title: The rate bands on this page are attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is traceable to the provider or the rate survey that published it — EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. None of them is an IB Gram price. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: Subject-matched rather than distance-matched
whyPoints.description: Additional Mathematics is on a minority of Sharjah timetables, so a tutor chosen from those within driving distance of Tilal City or Kalba is chosen from a very short list. Online delivery removes geography from the selection and puts the choice back on who has taught both 0606 papers.

whyPoints.title: One hour can carry both maths codes
whyPoints.description: Most Sharjah 0606 candidates are also sitting 0580 Extended in the same series. Where the same specialist covers both, the algebra one subject needs becomes the warm-up for the other, the household pays one monthly fee, and the marked work is seen by someone who remembers last week.

whyPoints.title: What a tutor will and will not do is stated
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, marks, and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody here will produce assessed work for a student, and no Cambridge syllabus, past paper, mark scheme or grade-boundary table will be supplied as a download — those are the awarding body's to distribute, and schools already have them.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that accounts for a Sharjah week
whyPoints.description: Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time around a school day that for many families ends in Dubai, and can shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. A session that survives the term is worth more than a session that looked convenient when it was booked in September.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, in either direction
whyPoints.description: No tutor can guarantee a grade in a Cambridge examination and any page selling one should be read carefully. What can be shown is movement in marked written work week by week, which is the only honest evidence available before results day and the thing to ask any provider for.

faqs.question: What should a Sharjah family budget per month for Cambridge IGCSE Additional Maths 0606 support?
faqs.answer: Work from the monthly bands rather than the hourly ones. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. For 0606 specifically, most families land in the middle or upper band because the subject is taught by fewer people. Advertised packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are published market figures, not an IB Gram tariff; our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a plan agreed with you.

faqs.question: Is 0606 tutoring priced differently from 0580 tutoring in the Sharjah market?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and by more than parents expect. Extended Mathematics 0580 is sat by almost every Cambridge candidate in the emirate, so supply is deep and rates are competitive. Additional Mathematics is an optional second subject carried by a minority of Sharjah timetables, so the pool of tutors who have taken a cohort through both papers is small. Scarcity shows up in the quote. The content also overlaps with AS-level work, so the tutors comfortable with it can often sell the same hour at sixth-form rates. Bundling both codes into one specialist hour is the most reliable way to bring the monthly total back down.

faqs.question: How much of an in-home rate in Sharjah is the drive rather than the teaching?
faqs.answer: A useful amount. Published in-home one-to-one rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Qualified online rates sit at AED 150 to 300. The gap is largely movement, not teaching quality, and in outlying communities such as Tilal City or Sharjah Garden City it widens because a tutor is pricing the better part of an hour each way. There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice: a session booked for 17:00 in Al Khan traffic often starts at 17:25 and is still billed from 17:00.

faqs.question: Can we buy 0606 help by the topic instead of committing to a whole term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a strong candidate with one visible hole it is often the cheaper choice. A bounded block of four to six sessions aimed at a single topic area — most commonly differentiation and integration together — keeps the spend known and finishes. The condition is that the diagnosis has to be right before the block starts, which is why we ask for a marked school paper rather than selling a separate assessment. Where a marked paper shows losses spread across several topic areas, a block will not fix it and a weekly hour across the year costs less per mark gained.

faqs.question: Do tutoring providers in Sharjah quote per sixty minutes or per lesson for maths?
faqs.answer: Both conventions are in use, which makes advertised rates hard to compare. A rate quoted per lesson can mean 45, 50, 60 or 90 minutes, and a monthly package quoting a number of sessions tells you nothing until the session length is stated. Before comparing two quotes, get the session length in writing and convert both to a cost per sixty minutes of contact time. This is the most common reason a cheaper-looking package turns out to be dearer, and it costs nothing to check. Our sessions are stated as 60-minute hours and the monthly figure follows from the number agreed.

faqs.question: Does the AED figure quoted by a maths tutor include tax?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, because practice varies and the published rates on this page are taken from competitor listings that do not consistently state it. The UAE VAT treatment of tuition is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring page, so we will not characterise it here; the authority's own guidance is the place to confirm it. What we can say is that any figure we quote you for a plan is stated as the amount you pay, with nothing added at invoice, and that a provider unwilling to confirm the same in writing is telling you something useful.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper 0606 tutor at AED 60 an hour ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being honest about when. Budget online rates start around AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya, and at that price a capable student who simply needs company while working through set problems may be well served. What the band does not reliably buy is diagnosis — recognising that a student's calculus failure is actually index notation, and changing what is taught as a result. If the problem is motivation or organisation, the cheap row works. If the problem is a prerequisite gap, it will consume months without finding it.

faqs.question: How many hours does a 0606 candidate in Sharjah usually need before the series?
faqs.answer: There is no single figure, but the shape is predictable. A weekly hour started in October gives roughly thirty sessions before a June series, which is enough to meet each topic area shortly before or alongside the school and to spend eight to ten of those weeks on differentiation and integration. Started in April, the same weekly pattern gives about six sessions, which is why families in that position buy intensives at a higher rate instead. The cost difference between those two routes is larger than the cost difference between a budget tutor and a specialist, which makes timing the more important decision.

faqs.question: We have two children on Cambridge maths. Does the second child cost the same?
faqs.answer: Per hour, broadly yes — one-to-one teaching is one-to-one teaching, and a second child in a different year group needs their own hour. Where households do save is in coordination rather than discount: one provider, one marking convention, one set of slots to protect in a week that already contains Arabic and Islamic education homework and a school run. If both children are in the same year and on the same syllabus code a shared session is theoretically cheaper, but the 0606 cohort is small and two siblings are rarely at the same point in the calculus, so it seldom teaches well.

faqs.question: Why is a 0606 specialist harder to price in Sharjah than in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the market is thinner in both directions. Dubai has 227 private schools across 17 curricula, which supports a visible tutoring market with competing published rates. Sharjah's private sector is smaller, a minority of its campuses enter candidates for Additional Mathematics at all, and a significant share of households attend Dubai schools from Al Nahda or Al Khan rather than locally. The result is fewer local quotes to compare and a wider spread between them. Online delivery is what levels this: the rate is set by who has taught the syllabus, not by who lives within driving distance of your community.

faqs.question: Does the Sharjah Private Education Authority set what a private maths tutor can charge?
faqs.answer: No. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and, like Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools. That remit covers schools, not individual tutoring arrangements, so a tutor's hourly rate is a matter between the tutor and the family. Private tutoring is governed separately, through the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds an approval or accreditation from SPEA, and any page suggesting otherwise should be treated with real scepticism.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson for 0606 cover, and is there a condition attached?
faqs.answer: One hour, online, one to one, with no card required and no obligation to continue. It is best spent on a marked school paper you send in advance: the tutor works through two or three questions the student lost marks on and says where the loss actually came from. The thing to watch for is whether the tutor asks the student to simplify an expression before differentiating it. That single behaviour separates a 0606 specialist from a competent general maths tutor, and it is visible in sixty minutes. After the trial you decide the plan shape and the monthly figure, or you decide nothing.

faqs.question: If we stop 0606 support after a month, what have we actually paid for?
faqs.answer: Four sessions and, if the arrangement was built properly, four pieces of marked written work you keep. That is the test to apply when comparing providers: ask what remains in your possession after a month. Annotated questions showing where marks were lost, and a note of which topic areas have been covered, are useful to the school and to any tutor who comes next. An arrangement that leaves nothing behind has sold you attendance. We agree plans by the month rather than by the term for this reason, and nothing here is tied to an outcome.

faqs.question: Does a tutor's permit cost money that ends up in our hourly rate?
faqs.answer: It should not, because the permit is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page — Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing — lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. So a licensing line in a quote has nothing behind it. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start 0606 in Year 10 or to wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Starting earlier is almost always cheaper in total, for a reason that has little to do with hourly rates. The expensive part of 0606 is the eight to ten weeks of differentiation and integration, and what makes those weeks long is unfinished 0580 Extended algebra underneath them. Two or three Year 10 sessions spent making index and surd manipulation automatic shorten that block materially. Waiting until Year 11 means buying the same algebra at a calculus-session rate, inside a timetable that also contains nine other subjects. The cheapest version of this purchase is small and early, not large and late.

faqs.question: Which 0606 topics are worth paying a specialist for, and which can the school handle?
faqs.answer: Pay for differentiation and integration, and for the index and surd work that sits beneath them — that is where a specialist changes the outcome rather than the atmosphere. Trigonometric identities and the graph-linearising logarithm question are mid-cost: worth a session or two each. Circular measure, two-dimensional vectors and the factor and remainder theorem are compact, well taught in most Sharjah classrooms and rarely need paid hours. Permutations and combinations needs question practice rather than teaching. Planning spend against that shape is how a family runs eight months of support instead of three months of intensive.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths.closingHeading: Start with the marked paper, then decide the monthly figure
sharjah/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths.closingBody: If Additional Mathematics has just appeared on your child's timetable in Sharjah and you are trying to work out what it will cost, do two things before comparing quotes. Photograph the most recent marked 0606 paper, and take a free trial lesson with no card required. The marked paper tells a specialist whether the problem is calculus or the algebra beneath it, and the trial tells you which of the market's three price tiers you are actually being offered. Lessons run online, one to one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Send the paper and we will suggest a plan shape and a monthly figure you can hold to.

intro.heading: What 0610 biology help costs in Sharjah, before anyone quotes you
paragraphs: Start with the number, because that is the question. Across the UAE market a qualified biology tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. Unitors, the only agency in this search result that publishes a rate at all, lists IGCSE support from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist exam-board work. Budget providers go lower: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to AED 52 an hour. Once a tutor drives to a villa in Al Majaz or an apartment in Al Nahda, Bestimate's Dubai rate table for 2026 puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors ask AED 200 to AED 500. Those are market figures, attributed, not an IB Gram price list.

Three of the six pages currently ranking for biology tutoring queries in this region publish no price whatsoever, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Sharjah family budgets in. A page that will not answer the first question a parent asks is not being discreet; it is making you ring a sales line to find out. So the rate table two screens down is the first thing on this page, with the provider model in one column and the source of each figure in another.

The second thing worth knowing is that the hourly rate is the least interesting part of the cost. A 0610 candidate sitting the Extended route takes Paper 2, Paper 4 and then either Paper 5 or Paper 6. That is three separately weighted components, and the practical component carries twenty per cent of the grade on its own. Buying twenty hours of general biology revision and never touching experimental design is how families spend AED 4,000 and watch the grade move by nothing. The useful question is not what an hour costs but which component the hour is aimed at.

Sharjah shifts the arithmetic in ways a generic Dubai page will not tell you. A large number of families living in Al Nahda, Al Taawun and Al Majaz send children to schools across the border in Dubai, and the Sharjah to Dubai evening return is the reason a 4pm slot is fiction for many households. Tutors who drive are pricing that commute into the rate whether or not they itemise it. An online slot at 7.30pm after Maghrib costs the family nothing in travel and costs the tutor nothing in travel, which is the single clearest reason online rates sit below in-home rates in this emirate.

Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That matters to a tutoring budget because the school's fee is the larger number on the same household spreadsheet, and because the subject your child sits is set by the school's Cambridge entry, not by a tutor's preference. Everything on this page is built around that order of operations: find out what the school has entered, work out which component is weakest, then price the hours.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-tut.programmesIntro: 0610 does not sit on its own. A Sharjah student arrives at IGCSE biology from a middle-school programme and leaves it for a sixth-form route, and the price of tutoring changes at each boundary. These are the stages either side of the syllabus this page is about.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE (Years 10–11)
programmes.description: The two years in which 0610 is taught and examined. Schools enter candidates for either the Core route or the Extended route, and that decision usually lands in Year 10. Core caps the available grades; Extended opens the top grades but adds supplement content across every topic, from transport in plants to selection and evolution. Most tutoring demand in Sharjah concentrates in the second half of Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah's private schools follow a range of curricula under SPEA, and the British-curriculum schools in Muwaileh, Al Ruqa Al Hamra and University City are where Cambridge IGCSE entries cluster. Ask the school office which route your child is entered for and which series, June or November. A tutor cannot plan a 0610 programme without those two facts, and the answer is written on the entry, not on the report card.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary science
programmes.description: The three years before 0610 begins. Science is usually taught as one combined subject, with biology, chemistry and physics interleaved rather than separated. Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October. Students who arrive in Year 10 without the habit of writing a reason after a statement are the ones who lose Paper 4 marks later, because the command word 'explain' is worth more than the command word 'state'.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run a transition year where science splits into three subjects partway through Year 9. Families in Al Qasimia and Halwan often ask whether to start tutoring then. The honest answer for most students is no: the cheaper intervention is a term of writing practice in September of Year 10, before the 0610 content load makes everything feel urgent and before the exam-year rate inflation described further down this page.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Biology
programmes.description: Where a strong 0610 grade leads. AS and A Level biology assumes fluency in the Extended material, particularly cell structure, transport, enzymes and genetics, and it assumes a student can design an experiment without being told what the variables are. The jump catches out candidates who scored well on 0610 multiple choice and poorly on the practical components, because that balance reverses at A Level.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families aiming at medicine or dentistry in the Gulf or the UK are usually working to an A Level biology plus chemistry combination, and the Year 11 to Year 12 summer is when the gap shows. Tutoring priced at the specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450 and above, per Bestimate's 2026 figures, is normally aimed at this stage rather than at 0610.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Biology
programmes.description: The other common post-IGCSE route, offered by a smaller number of Sharjah schools. DP biology adds an internally assessed investigation the student designs and writes themselves, which changes what a tutor is allowed to do: coaching the process and giving feedback on the student's own draft is permitted, producing any part of the work is not. The content overlap with 0610 Extended is real but the assessment culture is different.
programmes.countryNote: Victoria International School of Sharjah is the emirate's most visible IB school, and some families move from a British-curriculum IGCSE into an IB Diploma at a different school entirely. If that is the plan, the 0610 topics worth over-investing in are genetics, ecology and the data-handling skills in Paper 4, because all three recur immediately in DP year one.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-tut.subjectsIntro: Biology 0610 is the subject on this page, but almost no Sharjah family books one subject. These are the IGCSE subjects most often requested alongside it, with what each one actually assesses and the point at which marks tend to go missing.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Six components, of which a candidate sits three. The practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper carries twenty per cent. Marks are lost most often on experimental design, on graph work where the axes are chosen badly, and on explanation questions answered with a description instead of a mechanism.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: The usual second science. Moles and stoichiometry are where the grade is decided, and the practical paper mirrors 0610's in structure, so a student who can plan a biology investigation usually transfers that skill. Organic chemistry nomenclature is the common late-stage gap.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Formula selection and unit discipline decide most grades. Candidates who are strong in biology often struggle here because physics rewards rearranging an equation under pressure rather than recalling a labelled process. Electricity and waves are the two topics most frequently requested.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: From the 2025 series the papers split into a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper at both tiers. That change matters to biology candidates too, because the arithmetic in a magnification or rate-of-reaction calculation has to be done without a calculator in some school assessments.

subjects.name: Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: One grade covering all three sciences, chosen by students who need breadth rather than depth. The biology content is a reduced version of 0610, so a tutor working across both has to be precise about which syllabus statements are in scope. Entering the wrong syllabus is a surprisingly common and expensive error.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Reading and writing across two examined papers, with an optional coursework portfolio route. Biology candidates who lose marks for vague explanation often have a writing problem rather than a biology problem, and the two subjects respond to the same fix: say the mechanism, in order, with the connectives.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper and a structured paper, weighted thirty and seventy per cent. Popular as a fourth or fifth option in Sharjah's British-curriculum schools. The diagram work and the evaluation language are the two things tutoring usually targets.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, the second a case study issued in the exam room. Application to the given business is where candidates leak marks, writing textbook definitions when the question wanted the figures from the case.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Computer systems in one paper, algorithms and programming in the other. Cambridge pseudocode conventions are examined, so a student who codes fluently in Python can still underperform on the written paper.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508)
subjects.description: Sat alongside the international curriculum because Arabic is a mandatory subject in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. Reading comprehension and formal writing registers are the common tutoring requests, and schools organise first-language and additional-language groups separately.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-biology-0610-tut.regionsIntro: Sharjah is not one commute. The emirate runs from Al Nahda, which is effectively a Dubai suburb, out to Al Dhaid in the interior and across to Khor Fakkan on the Gulf of Oman. Where a family lives decides what time a lesson can realistically start.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Dense apartment blocks on the Dubai border. Many children here are driven into Dubai schools, which puts them home late and makes a 7.30pm or 8pm online slot the first workable one on a school night.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Older villa and tower mix around Khalid Lagoon, within short reach of several British-curriculum schools. Afternoon slots from 5pm are usually feasible here, which is why in-home tutors quote Al Majaz more cheaply than the outlying districts.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Home to a cluster of large private schools and a young family population. Sibling bookings are common, and parents often want two consecutive one-to-one slots rather than a shared lesson, because 0610 Core and Extended cannot be taught in the same hour.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Built around the Sharjah higher-education campuses. A useful source of science graduates, which is part of why the budget end of the Sharjah tutoring market is well supplied with university-student tutors at the AED 45 to AED 150 band.

regions.name: Al Khan and Al Taawun
regions.note: Corniche-side towers with heavy evening traffic along the lagoon. Families here report that a tutor driving in from Dubai arrives late often enough to matter, which is a scheduling argument for video lessons rather than a sales one.

regions.name: Halwan and Al Qasimia
regions.note: Central, mostly Arab and South Asian expatriate households, with children split across Cambridge, CBSE and MoE-curriculum schools. A tutor working here needs to confirm the exam board before the first lesson, not assume it.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan and Kalba
regions.note: The east-coast exclaves, still regulated by SPEA but roughly two hours from the city by road. In-home tutoring at a sensible rate is essentially unavailable here; a live video lesson is the only way a 0610 specialist reaches a student in Kalba at all.

regions.name: Al Dhaid
regions.note: Inland agricultural town in the emirate's interior. Same point, more sharply: distance prices in-home tutoring out of reach, and online delivery removes the geography from the decision entirely.

sections.heading: What the Sharjah market charges for IGCSE biology support, in AED
paragraphs: A qualified biology tutor working online in the UAE is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour as of October 2026. Below that band sit university-student and budget-platform tutors from about AED 45 an hour; above it sit subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and premium named tutors above AED 500. In-home delivery adds a travel premium that the published figures put at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour. Each figure in the table is attributed to the provider or rate survey that published it.

Read the table by provider model rather than by brand. The thing that separates a AED 60 lesson from a AED 270 lesson is rarely the subject knowledge in the room, because a biology graduate knows the Core syllabus perfectly well. It is whether anything happens between the lessons. At the budget end you buy sixty minutes of talking. At the specialist end you buy sixty minutes plus a marked set of Paper 4 questions, a note on which syllabus statements were missed and a plan for the following week. Both are defensible purchases; they are not the same purchase.

Monthly packages are common in this market and worth comparing carefully. Published examples include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Divide before you decide: the first works out near AED 100 an hour, the second near AED 200 to AED 225. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed AED rate on this page, and a page that quoted one without knowing the component, the route and the number of weeks left would be guessing. What we do publish is the trial: one free trial lesson per student, no card details collected before it, and the tutor's subject history shown in advance. The rate for a continuing programme is agreed after that lesson, once there is a diagnosis to price against.

sections.heading: Seven things that move a 0610 quote in this emirate specifically
paragraphs: Two Sharjah families can receive quotes AED 120 apart for the same subject in the same week, and the difference is almost never arbitrary. Seven variables account for most of the spread, and six of the seven are things a parent can influence before asking for a price. The table sets out the direction and the rough size of each effect.

Timing is the largest lever. Demand for biology tutoring in the Gulf peaks between January and the start of the June Cambridge series, and rates follow demand in any market. A family that books a weekly slot in September pays the standing rate; a family that calls in April is buying from a shrinking pool of available hours, often at a premium, and is also buying less time to work with. The cheapest exam-year decision available to a Sharjah parent is made in the autumn term.

Geography is the second lever, and it only bites on in-home delivery. A tutor quoting for a villa in Al Dhaid or an apartment in Kalba is quoting for three or four hours of their evening, not one, and the rate reflects that honestly. Online delivery removes the variable: a student in Khor Fakkan and a student in Al Majaz are quoted the same, and both are matched from the same pool of 0610 specialists rather than from whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive.

The remaining levers are about scope. Core and Extended are different syllabuses in practice and the Extended route needs more hours. A practical component is slower to fix than a recall gap because it needs the student to produce written plans that someone then marks. Two siblings in consecutive slots is cheaper per child than two separate bookings. And a tutor asked to cover biology and chemistry in one hour is being asked to do neither properly, which usually costs more in the end than booking two shorter sessions.

sections.heading: The six components of 0610, and which three your child will sit
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 is assessed through six components, and no candidate sits all six. A Core candidate takes Paper 1, Paper 3 and then either Paper 5 or Paper 6. An Extended candidate takes Paper 2, Paper 4 and then either Paper 5 or Paper 6. The school decides the route and decides whether the cohort sits the practical test or the written alternative, and both decisions are made before a parent is usually told about them. Confirm the current component structure and the school's entry on cambridgeinternational.org and with the exams officer.

The weightings are the part families misjudge. The theory paper carries half the grade, the multiple-choice paper thirty per cent and the practical component twenty per cent. Twenty per cent is a grade boundary and a half. A candidate who can recite the whole syllabus and has never drawn a results table with the independent variable in the first column is throwing away a fifth of the marks before the paper starts. That is also the component most easily fixed by tutoring, because it is a set of conventions rather than a body of knowledge.

Paper 5 and Paper 6 are not interchangeable in how they are prepared for even though they carry the same weight. Paper 5 is a timed practical in a laboratory with apparatus in front of the candidate; Paper 6 is a written paper about practical work, where the candidate plans investigations, completes tables, plots graphs and comments on sources of error. Paper 6 is entirely teachable over video, because the whole task is on paper. Paper 5 preparation online concentrates on the recording, the processing and the written commentary, with the handling practice done in the school laboratory where it belongs.

This table is the reference a parent can take to a school meeting. It is also the reason this page does not sell a flat package of hours: a Core candidate two terms out with a weak Paper 6 and an Extended candidate six weeks out with a weak Paper 4 are two different jobs, needing different numbers of hours at the same hourly rate.
