sharjah/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-t.programmesIntro: Where a student sits in the chemistry sequence changes what counts as evidence of progress. These are the stages this page connects, with what a Sharjah family should expect to see at each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry
programmes.description: Separate-sciences chemistry across twelve topic areas: states of matter; atoms, elements and compounds; stoichiometry; electrochemistry; chemical energetics; chemical reactions; acids, bases and salts; the Periodic Table; metals; chemistry of the environment; organic chemistry; and experimental techniques and chemical analysis. Assessed in a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component.
programmes.countryNote: Most Sharjah candidates meet it as one of three separate sciences in Years 10 and 11. The evidence a family should expect here is concrete: marked theory answers, a list of topic areas covered, and a visible improvement in equation writing within the first month.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Science
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course, where particles, reactions and the Periodic Table appear without the quantitative treatment 0620 adds. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October. Progress at this stage shows up in recording habits — units written down, observations described in chemical rather than everyday language.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 is where the arithmetic that later blocks mole calculations can be fixed cheaply. Sharjah families who use a few sessions here on ratio and proportion in a chemical context see a measurably easier Year 10.

programmes.name: Cambridge AS and A Level Chemistry 9701
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation, which assumes the 0620 Extended treatment of bonding, stoichiometry, energetics and organic chemistry and then raises the quantitative and mechanistic demand considerably. Evidence of readiness is not a grade but a specific capability: performing mole calculations without prompting and writing mechanisms as a sequence rather than a result.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah students moving into Year 12 locally or at a Dubai campus most often struggle with the volume of written explanation rather than the content. A 0620 candidate whose answers have been marked against the scheme arrives with that habit already formed.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Chemistry
programmes.description: The other Year 12 destination, at Standard or Higher Level. The content overlap with 0620 Extended is substantial at the start, but assessment differs: the IB defines its command terms, and there is an internal investigation the student designs and writes themselves, which has no Cambridge equivalent.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Sharjah family moves to a Dubai Diploma campus after Year 11, the useful preparation is not more content but the habit of designing and recording an investigation. A tutor supports that process and gives feedback; the work itself must be the student's own.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-t.subjectsIntro: Chemistry progress does not appear evenly across the syllabus. These are the twelve topic areas with the evidence each one produces, ordered by how quickly movement becomes visible.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry and mole calculations
subjects.levels: 0620 Extended, with simpler treatment at Core
subjects.description: Relative formula mass, moles from mass, reacting ratios, limiting reagents, concentration and percentage yield at Extended. The clearest progress indicator in the syllabus: a student either completes the three-step route from mass to moles to ratio to mass, or stalls at a specific step that a marked script identifies precisely.

subjects.name: Chemical equations and state symbols
subjects.description: Writing and balancing symbol equations, ionic equations at Extended, and state symbols. The earliest visible improvement in any 0620 arrangement, usually within two to three sessions, which makes it the first thing to check if a family is unsure whether sessions are working.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and salts
subjects.description: Reactions of acids, preparing a soluble salt, titration and the pH scale. The salt-preparation question has a fixed answer structure — react, filter, evaporate, crystallise — and progress shows as a complete sequence replacing a partial one. Marks here are sequential, so partial answers score poorly.

subjects.name: Experimental techniques and chemical analysis
subjects.description: Separation methods, purity, and the named tests for ions and gases. Progress is directly countable: a student can list the reagent, the observation and the conclusion for a given ion, or cannot. Writing that a solution turned cloudy where a white precipitate was required is the classic unscored answer.

subjects.name: Atoms, elements and compounds
subjects.description: Atomic structure, isotopes, ionic and covalent bonding, and the structures of giant lattices. Explanations here are formulaic and therefore improve quickly once the sentence shapes are learnt: a property is explained by a structure, and a structure is described in terms of particles and the forces between them.

subjects.name: The Periodic Table and group trends
subjects.description: Group I and Group VII trends, the transition elements and the noble gases. A copy of the Periodic Table is printed in the examination paper, so this area rewards interpretation rather than memorisation. Progress shows as a student reading a trend off the table instead of trying to recall it.

subjects.name: Chemical reactions, rates and reversible reactions
subjects.description: Rate of reaction, the effect of concentration, temperature and surface area, catalysts, and reversible reactions with equilibrium at Extended. Progress appears as the pairing of a graph with a particle-level sentence; a student who draws the right curve and cannot explain it is halfway there and the marked script says so.

subjects.name: Chemical energetics
subjects.description: Exothermic and endothermic changes, energy level diagrams, and bond-making and bond-breaking at Extended. A small area with clean marking points. The recurring loss is an energy diagram drawn correctly and labelled incompletely, which is a one-session fix and a visible one.

subjects.name: Electrochemistry
subjects.description: Electrolysis of molten and aqueous substances, electrode products and half equations at Extended. Progress is checkable question by question: the student identifies the ions present, predicts the product at each electrode, then writes the half equation. Each step appears separately on a marked script.

subjects.name: Metals and extraction
subjects.description: Reactivity series, extraction of iron and aluminium, alloys and rusting. The industrial questions demand exact conditions and named substances, so progress shows as precision replacing approximation. Marks are lost to a correct process described without the raw materials or the temperature.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.description: Homologous series, naming, isomerism at Extended, reactions of alkanes, alkenes and alcohols, and polymers. Often taught last, which makes it the area where a late arrangement produces the most visible gains simply because the student has not yet forgotten it.

subjects.name: Chemistry of the environment
subjects.description: Water treatment, air quality, fertilisers and the greenhouse effect. Descriptive and bounded, and therefore a reliable late-revision target. Progress is easy to evidence here because the questions reward specific named substances rather than general reasoning.

sections.heading: What should arrive each week, and when a family should start asking
paragraphs: The single most useful question a parent can ask a tutoring provider is not about qualifications or rates. It is: what will I have in my hands after four weeks? A good answer is specific and physical — four marked pieces of written work, a list of topic areas covered, and a note of which question types have moved. A vague answer is itself information.

There is a reason to be firm about this in chemistry particularly. The subject divides into discrete, checkable capabilities, so an arrangement that cannot produce weekly evidence is choosing not to. Balanced equations with state symbols. A mole calculation completed from mass to mass. A named ion test written as reagent, observation and conclusion. A salt preparation given as a complete four-step sequence. An energy level diagram labelled fully. None of those requires a chemistry degree to check for presence or absence on a page.

The timing matters as much as the content. Equation writing and the simpler ion tests should show movement within two to three sessions, because they are recall and convention rather than reasoning. Mole arithmetic takes longer — typically four to six sessions before the three-step route runs without prompting, because it depends on ratio fluency the student may not have. Written explanation on the theory paper moves next. The practical component conventions move quickly once addressed but are often addressed last. A family that knows that order can tell the difference between a plan that is working slowly and one that is not working.

The table below sets out what a twelve-week arrangement should produce. It is deliberately written as a checklist a parent can hold a provider to, including ours. If week six passes with nothing in the second column, that is the moment to change the arrangement rather than to add hours to it.

sections.heading: Reading a marked 0620 script without knowing any chemistry
paragraphs: Parents routinely assume they cannot judge chemistry work. In fact four checks are available to anyone, and together they tell you most of what you need to know about whether an arrangement is doing its job.

The first is marks available against marks taken. Every question carries a number in brackets. On a marked script, count how many of those brackets are fully satisfied and how many are partially satisfied. A student losing one mark on many questions has a different problem from one losing all marks on a few: the first is precision, the second is content. Over three scripts the pattern is obvious even to a reader who cannot follow a single equation.

The second is whether the annotation names something. Useful marking identifies the missing marking point — state symbols absent, reagent not named, moles not converted back to mass. A tick, a cross and a number at the bottom do not tell a student what to do differently next week, and a tutor who returns work in that form is recording a result rather than teaching. This is the clearest single quality signal in the whole arrangement, and it costs nothing to check.

The third is the length of answers over time. In 0620 a long answer is frequently a weak answer, because a six-mark question wants six distinct statements rather than a paragraph on the topic. Shorter, more structured answers appearing across successive scripts is real progress, and it is one of the few things visible at a glance. The fourth is the covered-topic list: twelve topic areas, each marked covered, partly covered or outstanding. If no such list exists after a month, nobody is planning the sequence, and the chance of the organic chemistry area being met for the first time in April rises sharply.

sections.heading: Mole calculations: real progress and the false signal that imitates it
paragraphs: Stoichiometry is where the most 0620 tutoring hours go and where the evidence is most often misread. The misreading has a specific shape, and recognising it saves Sharjah families a term of comfortable illusion.

The route a question demands is three steps: convert the given mass to moles using the relative formula mass, apply the reacting ratio from the balanced equation, then convert the resulting moles back into the quantity asked for. A student who has been taught well performs all three unprompted. A student who has been coached rather than taught performs all three when a tutor is present and stalls at step two when alone, because the ratio has to come from an equation they must balance themselves. In the session it looks identical. On an unsupervised script it does not.

This is why the evidence that matters is written work completed between sessions rather than work completed inside them. The test is simple: set two comparable questions, one worked together in the session and one set for the week. If the second comes back complete, the capability is real. If it comes back stalled at the ratio, the session was company rather than teaching, and the remedy is to spend two sessions on balancing equations before returning to stoichiometry at all. That is a diagnosis a marked script makes and a conversation cannot.

The second common false signal is arithmetic rescue. Many students who appear to have a mole problem have a ratio and proportion problem from several years earlier. The symptom is the same and the fix is not. A tutor who notices this will say so, and families in Aljada or Al Zahia with younger children often find that two or three sessions on proportion in Year 9 removes the whole issue before it ever presents as chemistry.

sections.heading: The practical component as a progress record
paragraphs: The practical component carries 20% of the 0620 grade, and it is the easiest part of the subject to evidence because almost all of its marks follow recording conventions rather than experimental flair. Whether the centre enters the practical test with apparatus or the written alternative to practical, the skills assessed are the same family: measuring, tabulating, plotting, concluding and improving.

What makes it good evidence is that every convention is a yes-or-no on the page. Units belong in the table heading rather than beside each value. Readings are recorded to a consistent precision. A graph has a sensible scale and a drawn line of best fit rather than points joined in sequence. An anomalous reading is circled and named as anomalous. A conclusion refers to the data rather than to what the student expected. A suggested improvement is specific enough that someone could act on it — repeat and average, insulate the container, use a burette rather than a measuring cylinder — instead of a general wish to be more accurate. A parent can audit all six of those without any chemistry.

The named tests for ions and gases sit alongside this and are the purest recall in the syllabus. The marking convention is three parts: the reagent added, the observation, and the conclusion drawn. A student who writes that the solution turned cloudy has recorded an everyday observation where a white precipitate was required, and will not be awarded the mark no matter how well they understand the chemistry. Progress here is countable in the most literal sense — how many tests can be written correctly this week against last week.

Preparing all of this over live video is not a compromise, because the assessed object is a written record rather than a manipulation. The student performs or describes, records in their own hand, photographs the page, and the tutor marks what is actually there. For east-coast families in Kalba or Khor Fakkan, with no realistic local alternative, this is also the only version that happens weekly rather than occasionally.

sections.heading: Mark movement against grade movement, and why the grade lags
paragraphs: A pattern that unsettles families more than it should: twelve weeks of visible improvement in marked work, followed by a school report showing the same grade as before. It is usually not a contradiction, and understanding why protects a plan that is actually working from being cancelled.

Grades are bands. A student can gain a substantial number of marks and remain inside the band they started in, particularly in the middle of the range where the bands are narrow in mark terms but wide in capability terms. That is why mark movement is the leading indicator and the grade is the lagging one. The honest way to judge an arrangement at week twelve is to compare two comparable scripts and look at the mark gap, not to wait for a letter to change. A provider who directs you to the letter instead of the marks is choosing the slower, vaguer evidence.

There is a second reason the grade lags in 0620 specifically. The theory paper carries 50% of the grade and it is the component that improves last, because written explanation depends on everything else being secure first. A student usually gains on multiple choice and on the practical component before the theory marks move, so the overall picture improves in a sequence rather than all at once. A school assessment taken mid-sequence reports the average and therefore understates what has happened.

The third factor is what the school is actually measuring. School assessments differ in difficulty, in coverage and in whether they are tiered to match the entry. A February test covering organic chemistry, which the tutoring has not yet reached, will report badly regardless of how much stoichiometry has improved. This is why the covered-topic list matters: it tells you whether a disappointing school mark was about progress or about sequence. The table below sets out how to read the two together.

sections.heading: SPEA, the school report and what each document can actually tell you
paragraphs: Sharjah families usually hold three kinds of paper about their child's chemistry: the school's own assessment data, published regulator material about the school, and whatever a tutor provides. They answer different questions, and treating one as a substitute for another is how parents end up either complacent or alarmed without cause.

Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools in the emirate. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge holds a similar remit; Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools to ADEK, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. What that material tells a parent is about the institution — its curriculum approval, its oversight, its standing. It does not report on one child's chemistry and should not be read as if it does.

The school's assessment data is the only source that reports on the child inside the taught course, and it is authoritative on three things in particular: the tier the child is entered at, which practical component the centre will enter, and the order in which the twelve topic areas are being taught. All three are worth asking the examinations officer or head of science directly, because all three change what a tutoring plan should do next. Core entry caps the grade at C in a tiered Cambridge subject, and a family planning towards A Level Chemistry should know that early rather than in April.

A tutor's evidence is narrower and more frequent: this week's marked work, these question types, this list of topics covered. Its value is that it is weekly, which no school report is. Its limit is that it only sees what the tutor sets. No tutoring provider holds any approval, accreditation or licence from SPEA, from the Ministry of Education or from Cambridge — IB Gram holds none of them — and no provider's internal evidence is a substitute for the school's view of the taught course. Used together, the three sources are complementary, and reading them in that order prevents most of the panic that accompanies a single disappointing mark.

sections.heading: What evidence nobody can honestly produce
paragraphs: An audit of what should arrive is only half of it. The other half is knowing which forms of evidence do not exist, because a provider offering them is telling you something important about itself.

No provider can produce a guaranteed grade, and none should offer one. No tutor can promise a particular outcome in a Cambridge examination, and a page offering one should be read with real scepticism rather than relief. The same applies to a promised number of grades of improvement, or to a refund tied to a result. What can honestly be offered is weekly marked evidence and the freedom to stop when that evidence goes flat, which is a stronger protection than a promise that cannot be enforced.

Nobody can honestly publish a satisfaction figure or a success rate without stating how many students it covers, over what period, and how it was measured. A percentage with no number of students behind it is decoration. Three of the competitor pages researched for this market show self-asserted star ratings, and one shows two different review totals on the same page. A provider that cannot show the underlying data should not be publishing the headline, and we do not.

Nobody should be supplying Cambridge syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are the awarding body's copyright material, distributed through schools and published on the official site; a tutor references them and works from the copies the school already holds. And nobody should be producing a student's own assessed work. In 0620 that question arises mainly around practical write-ups and set problem sheets: a tutor teaches a question type, marks the student's attempt and gives feedback, and the writing stays the student's. Any provider blurring that line is creating a problem for the student that no grade improvement would be worth.
bullets: No guaranteed grades, no promised grade jumps, no refunds tied to a result
No statistic without the number of students, the period and the method
No bundled syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes or boundary tables as downloads
No producing assessed work: a tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on the student's own

sections.heading: Permits, verification and the two checks worth making first
paragraphs: Before the evidence question comes a simpler one: is this arrangement legitimate. Two checks answer it, and both are free.

The first is the permit position. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered through MoHRE, whose service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. It is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has not published a fine schedule, so any page quoting an amount is inventing it. Because the permit is free, it should never appear as a charge in a quote.

There is a related point that Abu Dhabi families meet more often than Sharjah ones but which is worth knowing anywhere in the UAE. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Marketing a child's own classroom teacher as their private tutor is therefore not something any provider should be doing.

The second check is on the claims themselves. Ask whether the provider asserts any approval, accreditation or licensing from a regulator or an awarding body. The correct answer is that it does not, because independent tutoring providers do not hold those. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises, with initial approval followed by permit and licence steps and an annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry; it is not something an online tutoring platform holds. A provider claiming regulator approval is making the single most dangerous claim available in this market, and spotting it is a better use of five minutes than reading any list of testimonials.

process.title: Send the marked chemistry paper, all pages
process.description: Photograph the whole marked script rather than reporting the grade. The distribution of lost marks across question types is the diagnosis: one mark lost on many questions is a precision problem, all marks lost on a few is a content gap. That distinction decides what the first session does.

process.title: Confirm the tier, the component and the teaching order
process.description: Ask the school three things: Core or Extended, practical test or alternative to practical, and the order the twelve topic areas are being taught in. The third is the one families forget, and it is what stops a February school test on organic chemistry being mistaken for evidence that the plan has failed.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson to test the marking
process.description: One hour, online, no card required, no obligation. Take a question the student lost marks on and watch what the tutor does with it. Useful marking names the missing marking point; a tick, a cross and a total does not. That single behaviour predicts the quality of every piece of evidence that follows.

process.title: Agree what arrives each week, in writing
process.description: A marked piece of written work, an updated covered-topic list, and a note of which question types moved. Agree it before the first paid session, because an arrangement that has not committed to producing evidence will not start producing it in week eight when you ask.

process.title: Audit at week six, decide at week twelve
process.description: At week six check that marks on comparable tasks are moving and that set work completed unsupervised matches work done in session. At week twelve compare the re-test against the original script. If the gap is flat, change the arrangement rather than adding hours to the same one.

whyPoints.title: Written work comes back named, not scored
whyPoints.description: Annotation identifies the specific marking point that was missing — state symbols absent, reagent unnamed, moles not converted back. A student can act on that next week. A number at the bottom of a page records a result and teaches nothing, and it is the commonest weakness in tutoring arrangements of every price.

whyPoints.title: Unsupervised work is the test that counts
whyPoints.description: Stoichiometry done beside a tutor and stoichiometry done alone are different capabilities that look identical in a session. Set tasks completed between sessions are what distinguish them, which is why they are marked separately and why a flat result there triggers a change of approach rather than more hours.

whyPoints.title: A covered-topic list exists from week one
whyPoints.description: Twelve topic areas, each marked covered, partly covered or outstanding, updated weekly. It tells a family whether a poor school mark reflects progress or sequence, and it prevents organic chemistry and the environment topics being met for the first time weeks before a series.

whyPoints.title: The practical component is treated as 20%
whyPoints.description: Table headings, precision, lines of best fit, named anomalies, data-based conclusions and actionable improvements. These are conventions rather than chemistry, they improve within a session or two, and they are the most auditable marks in the subject for a parent who did not study the subject.

whyPoints.title: Subject-matched rather than distance-matched
whyPoints.description: Separate-sciences chemistry specialists are thinly spread across this emirate, and for families in Kalba, Khor Fakkan or the outlying villa communities the local pool is very small. Delivering online removes geography from the decision and puts it back on who has marked these papers.

whyPoints.title: Stopping is part of the arrangement
whyPoints.description: Plans are agreed by the month and the evidence is weekly, so a family that sees flat marked work can end the arrangement rather than wait out a term. No grade is promised and no refund is tied to an outcome, because neither can be honestly enforced; the protection is the evidence and the exit.

faqs.question: What should we actually receive after each 0620 session?
faqs.answer: Three things, and all three are physical. A piece of the student's own written work marked against the published scheme, with annotation that names the missing marking points rather than only the loss. An updated note of which of the twelve topic areas have been covered, partly covered or not yet reached. And a short statement of which question types moved and which did not. After four weeks that is four marked pieces and a covered-topic list, which is enough for a parent or a school to audit. A provider that cannot describe this before the first paid session is unlikely to produce it later.

faqs.question: How do we tell in week three whether chemistry support is working?
faqs.answer: Look at equation writing, because it moves first. Within two or three sessions a student receiving real teaching should be balancing symbol equations and including state symbols without being reminded. That is checkable on a page by anyone. What should not be expected by week three is fluent mole arithmetic, which usually takes four to six sessions because it depends on ratio confidence the student may not yet have, or improved theory-paper explanations, which move last. Judging week three against the slowest indicator produces unnecessary alarm; judging it against equations gives a real answer early.

faqs.question: My daughter's marks moved but her grade did not. Is that progress?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Grades are bands, and in the middle of the range a student can gain a meaningful number of marks and stay inside the band they started in. Mark movement on comparable tasks is the leading indicator; the grade is the lagging one. In 0620 there is a second reason for the lag: the theory paper carries 50% and improves last, because written explanation depends on the content and the arithmetic being secure first. So multiple-choice and practical-component marks typically rise before the overall picture changes. Compare two comparable scripts rather than waiting for a letter to move.

faqs.question: What can a parent who never studied chemistry check on a marked script?
faqs.answer: Four things, none of which need any chemistry. Count the marks available in brackets against the marks awarded, and look at the pattern — one mark lost on many questions is a precision problem, all marks lost on a few is a content gap. Check that the annotation names what was missing rather than only recording the loss. Watch whether answers get shorter and more structured over successive scripts, which in this subject is improvement. And ask for the covered-topic list and see what is still outstanding. Three scripts read this way tell you most of what you need.

faqs.question: Which 0620 skill shows progress earliest?
faqs.answer: Writing and balancing symbol equations, including state symbols. It is convention and practice rather than reasoning, so it responds within two or three sessions, and it is visible to a non-specialist on the page. The named ion and gas tests move almost as fast, because they are pure recall in a fixed three-part form: reagent, observation, conclusion. Those two are therefore the right things to check first when a family is unsure whether an arrangement is working. Mole calculations, electrolysis half equations and theory-paper explanation all take longer and should not be used as an early test.

faqs.question: Our son says the sessions are going well but the school test said otherwise. Which do we believe?
faqs.answer: Neither, on its own — compare them. The first thing to check is the covered-topic list against what the school test examined. A test on organic chemistry when the sessions have been working through stoichiometry will report badly regardless of real progress, and that is a sequencing mismatch rather than a failure. The second check is whether work completed between sessions, unsupervised, matches work completed inside them. A student who is strong beside a tutor and stalled alone has been coached rather than taught, and that pattern explains most of these disagreements.

faqs.question: How should a tutor evidence work on the practical component?
faqs.answer: Through the student's own tables, graphs and written conclusions, marked for conventions. Six of those conventions are checkable by anyone: units in the table heading rather than beside each value, consistent precision down a column, a sensible graph scale with a drawn line of best fit, an anomalous point circled and named, a conclusion that refers to the recorded data, and an improvement specific enough to act on. Each improves within a session or two of being addressed. For the named tests, the countable evidence is how many can be written correctly as reagent, observation and conclusion this week against last.

faqs.question: Can we see a record of which 0620 topics have been covered?
faqs.answer: You should be able to, and you should ask for it in week one rather than week ten. The syllabus has twelve topic areas, and a running list marking each covered, partly covered or outstanding does two jobs. It shows whether the sequence is sensible, and it explains a disappointing school mark on a topic the sessions have not yet reached. Without it, nobody can tell those two situations apart. It also prevents the common late problem of organic chemistry and the environment topics being met for the first time a few weeks before the papers.

faqs.question: Is a weekly test the right way to measure 0620 progress?
faqs.answer: A short weekly task is, a weekly test usually is not. What produces useful evidence is two or three past-paper questions of the same type as the ones the student lost marks on, completed unsupervised and marked against the scheme. That is comparable week to week and it isolates a capability. A broad weekly test mixes topics the sessions have covered with topics they have not, so the score moves for reasons unrelated to the teaching and tells a family very little. Comparable tasks, marked consistently, are what let you see a trend rather than noise.

faqs.question: What does flat progress after six sessions mean, and what should we do?
faqs.answer: It means the arrangement is not working, and the right response is to change it rather than to add hours to it. Before changing, check two things. Has the work been set and completed unsupervised, or has everything been done in session? And has the marking named the missing marking points, or has it only recorded scores? If either answer is unsatisfactory the problem may be the method rather than the match. If both are sound and the marks are still flat after six comparable tasks, the tutor is not the right fit and continuing is spending money on hope.

faqs.question: Does the school's report tell us anything a tutor's marking does not?
faqs.answer: Yes, three things, and they are the three that matter most for planning. The school is authoritative on the tier your child is entered at, which caps the grade at C on the Core route in a tiered Cambridge subject. It is authoritative on whether the centre enters the practical test or the written alternative. And it knows the order the twelve topic areas are being taught in. A tutor's marking is weekly and specific but only sees what the tutor sets. Published regulator material from SPEA or KHDA concerns the school as an institution and reports on neither.

faqs.question: How long before mole calculations start showing up in marks?
faqs.answer: Typically four to six sessions, and the reason for the lag is worth knowing. The route is three steps — mass to moles, apply the reacting ratio, convert back — and the middle step requires the student to balance an equation themselves. Students who are shaky on ratio and proportion from earlier years can do the first and third steps and stall reliably at the second. If marks have not moved after six sessions, the honest next step is usually two sessions on balancing equations and proportion before returning to stoichiometry, rather than more stoichiometry practice on top of an unfinished foundation.

faqs.question: What progress evidence should we show the chemistry teacher at school?
faqs.answer: The marked written tasks and the covered-topic list, and nothing else. A teacher can read annotated work immediately and will often tell you something useful in return — that the question types being practised are the right ones, or that the class is about to move into a topic the sessions should reach first. That conversation is more productive than a report of how the sessions feel. It also keeps the school's view of where the student actually is intact, which matters because the school makes the tier and component decisions and needs to see the student's unassisted work.

faqs.question: Is a predicted grade from a tutor worth anything?
faqs.answer: Very little, and it should not be relied on for any decision. Predictions for a Cambridge series come from the school, which has the full cohort context and the forecast-grade obligation; the school submits those forecasts to the board ahead of the June papers, on a date the exams officer can give you, and the same applies to the November series that candidates here use as the resit route. A tutor sees one student and the work that tutor has set, which is too narrow a base for a grade prediction and too easy to use as a sales instrument. What a tutor can honestly provide is the mark movement on comparable tasks and the list of topics still outstanding. Those support a decision; a predicted letter does not.

faqs.question: What evidence would tell us to stop paying?
faqs.answer: Four signals, any one of which is sufficient. Marks flat across six comparable, unsupervised tasks. Work returned as scores rather than named marking points, after you have asked for the latter. No covered-topic list a month in. Or a persistent gap between performance in session and performance alone, which means the student is being carried rather than taught. Plans here are agreed by the month precisely so that this decision stays available. No grade is promised and no refund is tied to a result, because neither could be honestly enforced; the real protection is weekly evidence and a short exit.

faqs.question: Does writing fewer words in a chemistry answer count as progress?
faqs.answer: In 0620, frequently yes. A six-mark question wants six distinct statements, each naming a substance, a condition or an observation, and the marks are awarded where those statements appear. A long general paragraph about the topic can contain one of them and bury the rest. So an answer that becomes shorter and more structured across successive scripts is usually an answer that is scoring more, and it is one of the few improvements a parent can see at a glance. The exception is the explain questions where a cause and a consequence are both required; there, two clauses are the minimum rather than one.

Send the most recent marked chemistry script and take a free trial lesson, with no card required, to see what the marking actually looks like. Lessons run online, one to one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-computer-science.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 for Year 10 and Year 11 students in Sharjah. Each one works in pseudocode as well as a real language, marks full past papers against the published mark scheme, and sends the annotated script back to you rather than a summary of it.

intro.heading: What a 0478 tutor should be able to show you after four weeks
paragraphs: Most families in Sharjah hire a Computer Science tutor on a feeling. The Year 11 report said "inconsistent", the mock came back at a 5, and something has to change before the series. Four weeks later the same parents cannot say whether anything has changed. The lessons happened, the student says they were useful, and the next mock is months away. That gap is what this page is built to close. A 0478 tutor who is working properly leaves a paper trail, and the paper trail is readable by someone who has never written a line of Python.

The trail has four parts. A marked past-paper script carrying the mark scheme's own wording in the margin. A running error log that names the topic and the command word rather than the question number. A list of the specific things the student could not do in week one, with dates against the ones that have since been cleared. And a stated target for the next sitting that is a number rather than an adverb. If none of that exists by the fourth lesson, the money is buying company instead of teaching.

0478 is easier to audit this way than most subjects, because the grade is assembled from two written papers and nothing else. There is no portfolio, no separate practical examination and no split into Core and Extended tiers: every candidate sits the same two papers, each carrying 75 marks and half the grade. A marked script is therefore not a proxy for progress. It is the same instrument the examiner will use. Confirm the component structure for your child's specific series on cambridgeinternational.org, since Cambridge revises syllabuses on a published cycle and the version in a second-hand revision guide may not be the one being sat.

Sharjah adds one practical constraint worth naming early. SPEA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, regulates private schools in the emirate, and a large share of Sharjah households send children across the border to Dubai schools, driving out from Al Nahda, Al Majaz or Al Taawun and queueing back along Al Ittihad Road in the evening. A tutor who has to find parking in Al Qasimia at 16:30 cannot realistically begin before 17:30. Running the lesson over video takes the drive out of the arithmetic and returns that hour to the student.

IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE: that is a service offered only in India, and a Sharjah family is matched with a 0478 specialist for online IGCSE Computer Science tuition in Sharjah instead. The practical effect is that the pool stops being whoever teaches Computer Science within a twenty-minute radius of Al Khan. It becomes whoever can mark a Paper 2 script properly, wherever that person lives, at an hour that fits a Sharjah school day.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-computer-science.programmesIntro: 0478 sits inside a Cambridge pathway that most Sharjah schools run from Year 7 through to Year 13. Knowing which rung your child is on changes what a weekly hour should be spent on, because a Year 9 student is still building notation habits while a Year 11 student is usually losing marks on content they already know.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Computing
programmes.description: The pre-IGCSE stage, where students meet selection, iteration, simple data types and the idea that a computer stores everything as binary. Schools treat it with very different levels of seriousness: some run it as a timetabled subject with written assessment, others fold it into a general ICT or digital-literacy slot. The difference shows up immediately in Year 10, because a student who has never written a condition inside a loop starts 0478 roughly a term behind one who has.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools in Muwaileh and Al Zahia run computing as a carousel subject in Years 7 and 8, rotating with design technology. Work out from your child's timetable how many taught hours of computing they actually had before Year 10, because that number predicts the first term of 0478 far better than the end-of-year grade does.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science
programmes.description: The syllabus this page is about. Ten topic areas split across two written papers: computer systems in Paper 1, and algorithms, programming, databases and Boolean logic in Paper 2. Each paper runs 1 hour 45 minutes and carries 75 marks, so the two halves of the course cannot be traded off against each other. A student who is strong on hardware and weak on trace tables loses a clean half of the available marks, and no amount of extra theory revision recovers them.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah centres sit 0478 in the standard Cambridge series, and the entry is made by the school rather than by you. Ask the examinations officer in writing which series your child is entered for and which timetable zone the centre belongs to, because the Cambridge IGCSE 0478 entry deadline falls months ahead of the exam and a zone mix-up is the one administrative error Cambridge will not absorb.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE (9-1) Computer Science
programmes.description: The same subject content reported on the 9 to 1 grade scale rather than A* to G. Schools choose between the two codes for reporting and comparability reasons, not because the course is different, and the teaching, the papers and the revision are effectively interchangeable. Parents hit this when a tutor advertises 0478 and the school's reports show 0984, or when a past paper downloaded from the wrong code's folder uses an unfamiliar grade boundary table.
programmes.countryNote: If your child's Sharjah school reports Computer Science as a 7 or an 8 rather than an A or a B, the entry is almost certainly 0984. The teaching plan does not change, but the conversation about a target grade does: a 6 under 9 to 1 is not the same thing as a C, and translating between the two scales by eye is where a lot of Sharjah parents mis-set expectations.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science
programmes.description: The continuation route, and the reason a weak 0478 grade matters beyond Year 11. 9618 assumes fluency in the things 0478 only introduces: data representation, abstraction, file handling and structured programming in a chosen language. A student who scraped through 0478 by memorising theory and avoiding the programming questions tends to meet a wall in the first term of AS, because the written paper there assumes code can be read as well as recalled.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah's A-Level provision in Computer Science is thinner than Dubai's, and some families end up choosing between a school that offers 9618 and one that offers a stronger overall sixth form. Fixing the Paper 2 weakness during Year 11 keeps that option open rather than closing it quietly, which is a better reason to work on algorithms now than the Year 11 grade by itself.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-computer-science.subjectsIntro: 0478 is published as ten numbered topic areas, and the numbering is useful to a parent because it is the vocabulary a tutor should be using in the error log. Below is what each one actually assesses and where Sharjah students most often lose marks inside it, which is a more honest map of the course than a list of lesson titles.

subjects.name: 1.1 Data representation
subjects.description: Binary, hexadecimal, two's complement, character sets, sound and image representation, and file compression. Marks go missing on the conversion arithmetic under time pressure and on explaining why a system uses hex rather than binary, which is an explanation question dressed as a conversion question.

subjects.name: 1.2 Data transmission
subjects.description: Packet structure, serial and parallel transmission, simplex and duplex, USB, and error-checking methods including parity, checksum, echo check and check digit. Students who have memorised the list still lose marks because the question asks which method catches which type of error, not what the methods are called.

subjects.name: 1.3 Hardware
subjects.description: The CPU, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, registers, embedded systems, input and output devices, and the full range of storage and virtual memory. The reliable loss here is describing a device instead of explaining why it suits a stated scenario, which is the difference between two marks and five.

subjects.name: 1.4 Software
subjects.description: System and application software, operating systems, interrupts, high and low-level languages, compilers, interpreters and assemblers. The compiler-versus-interpreter comparison appears in some form in most series, and answers that describe both without ever comparing them score about half of what is available.

subjects.name: 1.5 The internet and its uses
subjects.description: URLs, HTTP and HTTPS, browsers, DNS, cookies, digital currency and blockchain, plus cyber-security threats and the countermeasures for each. The security section rewards precision: naming a threat is one mark, explaining the mechanism and the specific countermeasure is where the rest sit.

subjects.name: 1.6 Automated and emerging technologies
subjects.description: Sensors and control systems, robotics, and artificial intelligence including machine learning. Short, often underestimated, and a frequent source of cheap marks for a student who can describe a feedback loop with a named sensor and a named actuator rather than in general terms.

subjects.name: 2.1 Algorithm design and problem-solving
subjects.description: Decomposition, flowcharts, structure diagrams, pseudocode, trace tables, validation and verification, and test data selection. Trace tables are the single most diagnostic question type on the paper: a student who cannot complete one cannot reliably debug, and the marks reflect that.

subjects.name: 2.2 Programming
subjects.description: Variables, constants, data types, the three control structures, string handling, arrays, procedures, functions and file handling, written in pseudocode or a permitted language. The most common failure is syntactically valid code that answers a slightly different question from the one asked.

subjects.name: 2.3 Databases
subjects.description: Single-table databases, field types, primary keys, and SQL using SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, SUM and COUNT. A small topic with a predictable question, routinely dropped because it sits at the end of the syllabus and gets taught in the week before study leave.

subjects.name: 2.4 Boolean logic
subjects.description: Logic gates, logic circuits from a written scenario, truth tables and logic expressions. Mechanical and learnable, and therefore the cheapest marks on Paper 2 to secure: Boolean logic in 0478 rewards a student who has drawn thirty circuits far more than one who understands the theory abstractly.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-computer-science.modesIntro: Three ways Sharjah families use 0478 support, and all three run as one-to-one lessons over live video. The right one depends on how far away the series is and whether the problem is content the student has never met or content they have met and cannot reproduce under timed conditions.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through Year 10 and Year 11
modes.description: A fixed hour each week, following the school's own order of teaching rather than a parallel syllabus. The tutor sees the exercise book and the last class test, works the current topic to the standard the paper asks for, and sets a short timed task for the following week. Progress is recorded in a dated error log that stays with the student across the two years, which is what makes a Year 11 conversation about target grades evidence-based rather than hopeful.

Families use this when the content is broadly there and the marks are not, which is the most common shape of an exam-year problem.

sections.heading: The evidence a 0478 tutor should produce, week by week
paragraphs: Ask for the evidence before you ask for the price. A tutor who cannot describe what will exist on paper after four lessons is describing an intention, not a method, and intention is what every page in this search result already sells. The table below is the standard we hold a 0478 match to in Sharjah, and it is deliberately written so that you can check it without understanding the subject.

The first lesson should be spent partly on diagnosis. Not a conversation about how the student finds Computer Science, but a section of a past paper attempted cold and marked, with the lost marks tallied against the ten syllabus areas. That tally is almost always a surprise. A student who says they are weak on programming frequently turns out to be losing more marks on data transmission and the compiler comparison, because those feel easy and are therefore never revised.

From week two the useful artefact is the error log. The entry should name the topic and the command word, so a line reads "2.1, complete the trace table, lost 3 of 4" rather than "question 5b". Logs built that way group themselves, and the grouping is the teaching plan. Logs built around question numbers are unusable a fortnight later and tell a parent nothing.

By week eight there should be a full paper, sat in one sitting, marked question by question. That is the number you can compare with the school's mock, and the first point at which the word progress means anything specific. If the twelfth week arrives with no written plan for the final stretch, the honest reading is that nobody is steering.

sections.heading: How the 0478 grade is actually built
paragraphs: Two papers, no coursework, no tiering. That single sentence explains more about how to plan 0478 tuition than anything else on the syllabus, and it is worth stating because parents arriving from a science subject reasonably assume there is a practical component to worry about and parents arriving from maths assume there is a Core and an Extended route to choose between. Neither is true here.

Paper 1 covers the computer-systems half of the syllabus: the first six topic areas, from data representation through to automated and emerging technologies. Paper 2 covers the second four: algorithm design and problem-solving, programming, databases and Boolean logic. Each paper is scheduled at 1 hour 45 minutes, carries 75 marks and contributes half the grade. There is no mechanism by which a strong Paper 1 rescues a poor Paper 2.

That symmetry has a blunt consequence for how a weekly hour is spent. The theory half is examinable by reading and recall, and a motivated student can improve it substantially alone with a textbook and past questions. The algorithms half is not: it needs someone to watch the student attempt a trace table and say where the reasoning broke. If a tutor is spending most of the hour on Paper 1 content, the hour is being spent on the half the student could have covered without paying for it.

Check the current component details for the series your child is entered for on cambridgeinternational.org rather than taking them from a revision guide. Cambridge publishes syllabus updates on a cycle, past versions of 0478 differed in how the programming content was assessed, and second-hand material circulating in school WhatsApp groups is frequently a syllabus version or two behind.

sections.heading: Pseudocode, trace tables and the gap between coding and examined programming
paragraphs: The most frequent 0478 enquiry from Sharjah parents is some version of this: my child writes games in Python at home, so why is Paper 2 a 4? It is a fair question and the answer is structural. 0478 does not primarily examine whether a student can produce working code. It examines whether a student can read an algorithm written by somebody else, predict exactly what it does, find the flaw and describe the fix, and much of that happens in Cambridge's own pseudocode rather than in any language the student has chosen.

Cambridge pseudocode has fixed conventions: specific keyword capitalisation, declared data types, particular loop forms, and an array-indexing convention that can differ from the one a self-taught Python user assumes. A student who treats it as approximate English loses marks on the detail. A student who treats it as a small formal language with its own rules stops losing them, usually within a handful of sessions, because the content was never the problem.

Trace tables are where this becomes measurable. A trace table asks the student to record every variable's value at every step of an algorithm, in order. It is unforgiving, entirely mechanical, and the fastest diagnostic available: a student who cannot complete one cannot predict what their own code does either, which is why their debugging is guesswork and their programming answers drift away from the question. Drilling trace tables fixes two question types at once.

The practical plan is narrow. Take the standard algorithms the syllabus expects, dry-run each one on paper, then amend them to a stated new requirement rather than rewriting them from nothing. Exam programming questions almost always ask for an amendment or a completion. A student who has only ever written programs from a blank file has practised the one thing the paper rarely asks for.
bullets: Pseudocode conventions learned as rules, not approximated from Python habits
Trace tables completed to the last row, every time, before anything else
Standard algorithms amended to a new requirement rather than rewritten
Data-type declarations and array indexing checked line by line
Every answer re-read against the words of the question before it is handed in

sections.heading: The six computer-systems topics and the marks each one quietly costs
paragraphs: Paper 1 looks like the easier half and behaves like it right up to the point marks are counted. The content is finite, the questions are predictable in shape, and most students feel reasonably confident. The losses are therefore not dramatic: they are two marks here, three there, spread across six topic areas, and they add up to a grade without ever producing a question the student remembers getting wrong.

Data representation leaks marks through arithmetic under time pressure and through explanation questions disguised as conversions. Asking why a developer uses hexadecimal is not asking for a conversion, and an answer that converts a number scores nothing. Data transmission leaks them through the error-checking methods: students memorise parity, checksum, echo check and check digit as a list, then meet a question asking which one detects which category of error, and the list does not help.

Hardware is the biggest single reservoir of avoidable loss, because describe and explain are marked differently and students default to describing. A question that supplies a scenario, a warehouse or a hospital monitor, is asking for the link between the device's properties and that scenario's needs. Software loses marks on the compiler and interpreter comparison, which turns up in some form in most series and attracts answers that describe both without comparing them. The internet section rewards precision about mechanisms: naming a threat earns the first mark, explaining how it works and what specifically prevents it earns the rest.

Automated and emerging technologies is short, often rushed at the end of Year 11, and quietly generous. A student who can describe a closed feedback loop with a named sensor and a named actuator, and distinguish robotics from machine learning in concrete terms, tends to clear it. Treating it as the last two lessons before study leave is how those marks get left behind.
bullets: 1.1: practise conversions to time, and read explanation questions twice
1.2: learn error-checking methods by what each one detects, not as a list
1.3: answer the scenario the question gives, rather than describing the device
1.4: build one explicit compiler-versus-interpreter comparison and reuse it
1.5: pair every named threat with its mechanism and its countermeasure
1.6: do not leave sensors, actuators and machine learning to study leave

sections.heading: What 0478 support costs around Sharjah, and what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Begin with the figure nobody in this search result publishes: the difference between an online hourly rate and an in-home one. Market data for the UAE puts in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Qualified subject tutors working online are published lower, from about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The gap between those two bands is the travel premium, and it is worth asking what it buys.

It buys presence in the room, which for some students genuinely matters. What it does not buy is subject depth, because the premium is paid for geography. A Sharjah family paying the in-home band is selecting from the people willing to drive to Al Khan at 17:00, and in a subject as narrow as Computer Science that pool may contain nobody who has marked a 0478 Paper 2 against the mark scheme. Paying more for a smaller pool is the specific trade this market makes without naming it.

At the cheaper end, EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, usually for university-student or generalist tutors. For Paper 1 theory that can be adequate. For Paper 2 it rarely is, because the tutor needs to have been marked on pseudocode themselves. Specialist IGCSE and A-Level rates run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the named-examiner end. 0478 sits comfortably in the specialist band and almost never needs the premium one.

All of those are other providers' published rates as at October 2026, quoted so you have a frame of reference, and they are not IB Gram's price list. Ask any tutor whether the quote is per hour or per session, whether VAT is included, and what happens to a prepaid block if the match is wrong. Those three questions move the real cost more than the headline rate does.

sections.heading: Grade movement: reading a 0478 mock mark honestly
paragraphs: A mock mark is a weak instrument used carelessly and a strong one used properly, and the difference is almost entirely about whether you know what was sat. Two 0478 mocks a term apart can be a full paper against a single section, an untimed attempt against a timed one, or a teacher-written paper against a Cambridge one. Comparing the percentages without knowing which is comparing nothing, and it is how a family concludes that tuition is working when the only thing that changed was the difficulty of the paper.

So the first question about any mark is what produced it. Which paper, which series, how long was allowed, and was it marked against the published mark scheme or against a teacher's judgement. A tutor who marks to the mark scheme and shows you the annotation is handing you a mark you can line up against the next one. A tutor who reports a percentage is handing you a feeling with a number attached.

Second, look at where the marks moved rather than whether the total did. A student can gain six marks on Paper 1 recall while losing four on trace tables and show a two-mark improvement that conceals a worsening problem. The error log exists precisely for this: it lets you see that the 2.1 entries have stopped recurring, or that they have not. Topic-level movement is the signal. The total is the noise.

Third, be realistic about what a few weeks can move and refuse any claim beyond that. No tutor can promise a grade, and a confident number attached to a specific outcome is the clearest signal to walk away. What can be stated honestly is narrower and more useful: that a named error has stopped recurring across three marked scripts, and that the student is now completing trace tables unaided. Those are checkable. A promised grade is not.

sections.heading: SPEA, the Sharjah school map and what a parent can check
paragraphs: Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Its remit is wider than inspection: SPEA approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in the emirate's private schools, which is a stronger form of oversight than parents arriving from other systems tend to assume. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a particular curriculum beyond Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must work within the Ministry of Education's general regulations.

For a 0478 family the practical consequence is that your school's curriculum offer, including which exam board and which syllabus codes it enters candidates for, sits inside an approved programme rather than being chosen freely each year. That is why a school can decline a request to enter a candidate for an additional subject, and why the answer to "can my child add Computer Science in Year 11" comes from the school's approved programme rather than from the examinations officer's goodwill.

What you can verify yourself is narrow but useful. The emirate's regulator publishes the school listing, so a school's name and status can be checked against the authority's own records rather than against a tutoring agency's logo wall. Your child's own school can tell you the exam board, the syllabus code, the series entered and the timetable zone, and all four should be in writing. If an agency names a school in a way that implies a relationship, ask the school.

Sharjah households that send children to Dubai schools live under two regulators at once. One child may be at a SPEA-regulated school in Al Majaz and another at a KHDA-regulated school across the border, with different term dates, different inspection frameworks and sometimes different exam boards for the same subject. Mapping that before you plan a revision calendar saves a genuine amount of friction in the exam term.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines, Cambridge zones and what a Sharjah candidate must have done by when
paragraphs: Nobody in this search result publishes an exam calendar, which is odd, because the deadlines are the part of the process that actually goes wrong. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Entries are made by the centre, not by you, and they close months before the first paper is sat.

Take the June series and count backwards, because that is the session a Sharjah candidate is entered for, with November as the resit route; the February and March series exists for India only and no centre here uses it. Final entries close in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper, on a date your centre prints on the statement of entry. Forecast grades follow weeks before the papers. The written period then runs inside the June window set by your centre's zone timetable, results appear on Cambridge Direct in August, and certificates reach the centre some weeks after that. The shape of that timeline is the point. What a candidate sits is decided months before the first paper, which means a tutoring plan built in April is working inside choices already made in the spring.

The zone issue is less known and more dangerous. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong one. A revision schedule built from a timetable PDF found online, rather than from the one the centre confirms, is a real risk rather than a theoretical one.

Families whose children sit Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers instead work to a different calendar: May/June and November series each year, with the November 2026 timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live PDF rather than a restated date, including on this page.
