sections.heading: Permits, honesty boundaries and what a 0478 tutor will not touch
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit rather than left open. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through MoHRE, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody.

The official route is MoHRE's own service page, "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of that kind and should never be described as having one: it is a matching platform delivering lessons over video, with no office or centre in the UAE.

There is a separate rule parents should know about. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. Verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document before relying on it, but the direction is clear enough that "your child's own teacher, privately" is not something to arrange.

The honesty boundary on the work itself is simple and we state it rather than leaving it vague. A tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write the coursework, the project or the answers a student hands to a teacher, and will decline if asked. For 0478 that mostly concerns school-set programming tasks: the tutor will read the student's code, ask what each line does, point at the line that fails and let the student fix it. Nor will a tutor supply Cambridge past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables as downloads. Those are Cambridge's to publish, and the right move is to cite cambridgeinternational.org and work from what your centre provides.

process.title: Tell us the paper, not just the subject
process.description: Send the syllabus code, the series your child is entered for, the last mark and which paper the losses sit on. "Year 11, 0478, Paper 2 at 38 out of 75, trace tables" produces a match in a different league from "needs help with Computer Science". The code matters because 0478 and 0984 report differently and ICT 0417 is a separate subject.

process.title: A free trial lesson with a diagnostic attached
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, no card details taken, and the condition is simply that it is one lesson. Ask for it to include a cold attempt at a past-paper section, marked. That turns a get-to-know-you call into the first piece of evidence, and it tells you within an hour whether the tutor marks to the scheme or to an impression.

process.title: The first marked script
process.description: After the trial, you should receive the annotated script and a topic tally of the marks lost, mapped to the ten 0478 areas. Read it even if the subject is unfamiliar. The annotation tells you whether the tutor is working from the mark scheme's language or from their own, which is the single most reliable quality signal available to a non-specialist.

process.title: A weekly rhythm with a dated log
process.description: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, a short timed task between sessions, and an error log updated with dates. The slot matters in Sharjah: an Al Nahda family commuting back from a Dubai school needs a later start than an Al Khan family, and a slot set optimistically is a slot that gets cancelled.

process.title: A written plan for the final stretch
process.description: Ten to fourteen weeks out, the log should turn into a one-page plan: named topics against dates, which papers will be sat and when, and what gets dropped if time runs short. If a tutor cannot produce that page, you are funding weekly lessons rather than a route to the series, and the two are not the same purchase.

whyPoints.title: Marking, not reassurance
whyPoints.description: Sessions produce a marked script annotated in the mark scheme's own words and an error log naming topics and command words. The point is that a parent who has never written code can still audit the work. Reassurance is free everywhere; marked evidence is the thing worth paying for and the thing most of this search result does not describe.

whyPoints.title: 0478 by syllabus code, not by subject label
whyPoints.description: Matching happens on the code and the paper, because "Computer Science" covers 0478, 0984, ICT 0417 and AS 9618, and a tutor comfortable with one is not automatically useful on another. Telling us the code is how a Sharjah family avoids paying specialist rates for a generalist who last saw pseudocode in a different syllabus version.

whyPoints.title: Pseudocode treated as its own language
whyPoints.description: The gap between writing Python and scoring on Paper 2 is pseudocode conventions and trace tables, and both are teachable in weeks rather than terms. Tutors drill them until completing a trace table is mechanical, because that one skill carries the algorithm questions, the debugging questions and the programming amendments at the same time.

whyPoints.title: Gulf Standard Time, and no drive
whyPoints.description: Lessons run live online over video at a time set around a Sharjah school day, which means the Al Ittihad Road queue is not part of the arithmetic. The hour that an in-home arrangement spends on travel is spent on the paper instead, and the tutor pool is national rather than whoever lives near Al Taawun.

whyPoints.title: Boundaries stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor marks and teaches the student's own work and will decline to produce work that gets submitted. No past papers or mark schemes are supplied as downloads, no regulator approval is claimed, and no grade is promised. Several pages in this search result do the opposite on at least one of those counts, which is a risk carried by the student.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 tiered into Core and Extended?
faqs.answer: No. Unlike Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 or the sciences, 0478 has no Core and Extended split. Every candidate sits the same two written papers, each carrying 75 marks and half the grade, so there is no tier decision for a parent to make and no ceiling on the attainable grade built into the entry. That changes how tuition is planned: the work is about covering ten topic areas to the same depth for everyone, rather than deciding which route suits a student. Confirm the current structure for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org, because Cambridge revises syllabuses on a published cycle.

faqs.question: Which programming language should my child use for the 0478 programming questions?
faqs.answer: The written papers are answered in Cambridge's own pseudocode or in a permitted high-level language, and the choice usually follows whatever the school teaches, most often Python, Java or Visual Basic. The language matters less than people expect. What is examined is the logic, the control structures and the ability to read and amend somebody else's algorithm, and the pseudocode conventions carry marks of their own. A student fluent in Python who has never written Cambridge pseudocode still loses marks on notation. Ask your school which language it teaches, then treat pseudocode as a second one to learn properly.

faqs.question: What should exist on paper after four weeks of 0478 lessons?
faqs.answer: Four things. A marked cold diagnostic from the first lesson with the lost marks tallied against the ten syllabus areas. A dated error log naming the topic and command word behind each loss. A second timed attempt on those same topics, marked against the published mark scheme, so movement is measurable rather than felt. And a short statement of what has cleared and what has not. If the only artefacts after four weeks are session notes and a verbal impression, you have no way to judge the work, which is the position most families in this market end up in.

faqs.question: How is the 0478 grade divided between the two written papers?
faqs.answer: Evenly. Paper 1, Computer Systems, covers the first six syllabus areas and carries 75 marks. Paper 2, Algorithms, Programming and Logic, covers the remaining four and also carries 75 marks. Each paper is scheduled at 1 hour 45 minutes and contributes half the final grade, with no coursework component anywhere in the course. The practical consequence is that a strong theory performance cannot compensate for a weak algorithms performance, which is why a tutoring plan weighted towards Paper 1 content tends to produce a disappointing result. Verify the component details for your series on cambridgeinternational.org.

faqs.question: My son can code in Python but loses marks on pseudocode. Why does that happen?
faqs.answer: Because the paper is not mainly testing whether he can produce working code. It tests whether he can read an algorithm written by somebody else, predict exactly what it does, find the flaw and amend it, often in Cambridge pseudocode with its own keyword and data-type conventions. Self-taught Python habits transfer imperfectly: array indexing, declared types and loop forms all differ in small ways that cost marks. The fix is short and specific. Treat pseudocode as a separate small language with rules, and drill trace tables until completing one is automatic. Most students close this gap in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge IGCSE 0478 still include pre-release material before the examination?
faqs.answer: This is exactly the kind of detail that has changed between syllabus versions, so do not take it from a revision guide or a school WhatsApp group. Earlier versions of the course handled the programming element differently from the current one, and material circulating second-hand is frequently a version or two out of date. Check the syllabus document for the specific series your child is entered for on cambridgeinternational.org, and ask your school's examinations officer to confirm what the centre has been sent. Planning a revision timetable around a component that no longer exists wastes weeks that a Year 11 candidate does not have.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my daughter's 0478 mock mark has genuinely moved?
faqs.answer: Ask what produced each mark before comparing them. Which paper, which series, how long was allowed, and was it marked against the published mark scheme or a teacher's judgement. Two mocks a term apart are often not comparable at all. Then look at where the marks moved rather than at the total: a six-mark gain on recall alongside a four-mark loss on trace tables shows as a small improvement while concealing a worsening problem. Topic-level movement recorded in the error log is the signal you want. A single percentage, with no record of what was sat, tells you almost nothing.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0478 the same qualification as 0984 Computer Science?
faqs.answer: The subject content is effectively the same; the reporting scale differs. 0478 reports on the A* to G scale and 0984 on the 9 to 1 scale, and schools choose between them for comparability and reporting reasons rather than because the course changes. Teaching, past papers and revision are interchangeable in practice, but grade boundaries and target-setting are not: a 6 under 9 to 1 is not a C, and translating between the scales by eye is where expectations get mis-set. If your child's reports show numbers rather than letters, the entry is almost certainly 0984.

faqs.question: Should my child take 0478 or Cambridge IGCSE ICT 0417 at a Sharjah school?
faqs.answer: They are different subjects with different demands, and the choice is usually made by the school's option blocks rather than by the family. 0478 is a computer-science course built on algorithms, programming, logic and how systems work, assessed by two written papers. ICT 0417 is about using applications competently and includes practical assessment of software skills. A student who enjoys building things and does not mind abstraction belongs on 0478; one who prefers applied, document-based work often does better on 0417. If AS Computer Science 9618 is a possibility later, 0478 is the sensible preparation.

faqs.question: Can a 0478 tutor teaching from outside the UAE work legally with my child?
faqs.answer: The UAE permit framework applies to individuals providing private tutoring in the UAE: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone offering private tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted figure with suspicion. The honest position for a cross-border online tutor is to ask the provider directly how the arrangement is structured, and to check MoHRE's own private tutor licensing page rather than relying on a tutoring website's summary.

faqs.question: What does SPEA actually control in my child's Sharjah school?
faqs.answer: More than parents usually assume. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the school's curriculum offer sits inside an approved programme rather than being set freely each year. Federally, private schools must follow Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies and work within the Ministry of Education's general regulations, but are otherwise free on curriculum choice. For a 0478 family the practical effect is that whether a subject can be added in Year 11 is a programme question, not a favour the examinations officer can grant.

faqs.question: How late can a 0478 session start for a family driving back into Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: Later than most schedules assume. Al Nahda households commuting from Dubai schools can be home after 16:30 on a heavy evening, and a slot set at 16:30 is a slot that gets cancelled. Because lessons run over live video rather than requiring anybody to travel, start times through to about 21:00 Gulf Standard Time are workable, and a weekend morning slot is frequently more reliable than any weekday one during term. Set the time around the actual arrival, not the hoped-for arrival: a consistent 18:00 beats an optimistic 17:00 that happens two weeks in three.

faqs.question: What does an hour of 0478 support cost in the Sharjah market?
faqs.answer: Other providers' published rates as at October 2026 give the frame. Generalist online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE and A-Level tutors run AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270, and named-examiner rates reach AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the rate. Those are the market's numbers, not a quote from us.

faqs.question: Will a 0478 tutor fix my son's school programming task for him?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers to. A tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student has produced; writing or completing work that a student submits is not something we do, and it exposes the student rather than helping him. On a school-set programming task the tutor will read his code, ask what each line is doing, point at the line that fails and let him fix it. That produces a student who can debug the next one. Nor will a tutor supply Cambridge past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because those are Cambridge's to publish.

faqs.question: When does the entry close for the Cambridge series my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: Months before the first paper, and the centre makes the entry rather than you. For the June series that a candidate here sits, entries close in the spring, forecast grades follow weeks before the papers, the written period falls in the June window on your centre's zone timetable, results appear on Cambridge Direct in August and certificates follow some weeks later; the November series runs on the same pattern shifted round the year and is the normal resit route. Ask your examinations officer in writing which series your child is entered for and which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre belongs to, because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

intro.heading: Why a student who understands economics writes answers that score in the middle
paragraphs: Economics is the subject where confidence and marks part company most reliably. A Year 11 student in Muwaileh or Al Majaz can explain, in conversation, why a rise in interest rates slows consumer spending, and then lose five of the eight marks available for writing the same thing. Parents reasonably conclude the problem is understanding. It almost never is. Cambridge 0455 awards marks for a specific sequence of written moves, and a student who has not been shown that sequence will keep producing answers that are true, interesting and unrewarded.

The structure of the assessment explains why. Every 0455 candidate sits two papers. Paper 1 is multiple choice: 45 minutes, 30 marks, 30% of the grade. Paper 2 is structured questions: two hours fifteen minutes, 90 marks, 70% of the grade, made up of one compulsory data-response question worth 30 marks and then a choice of three structured questions from four, each worth 20 marks. The syllabus is not tiered — there is no Core or Extended route — so every candidate faces the same papers, and the grade runs A* to G.

Inside a Section B structured question the marks come in four ascending parts, typically two, four, six and eight. That shape is the single most useful thing a candidate can internalise, because each part wants a different behaviour. The two-mark part is a definition, written precisely. The four-mark part asks for explanation with a reason attached. The six-mark part usually wants analysis, often with a diagram that is then referred to. The eight-mark part wants two sides and a judgement. A student who writes the same kind of paragraph four times collects a predictable fraction of the available marks each time.

The syllabus itself has six sections: the basic economic problem; the allocation of resources, including how the market works and market failure; microeconomic decision makers; government and the macroeconomy; economic development; and international trade and globalisation. Those six do not behave the same way. Two of them account for most of the grade movement in a typical Sharjah cohort, two are taught so late that they are regularly under-revised, and one has a wider spread of marks within it than any other. Treating the syllabus as a flat list is why revision plans fail.

There is one more thing specific to writing economics in this emirate, and it is an advantage rather than a problem. Candidates are asked to apply ideas to real economies, and Sharjah's own — a trade and manufacturing emirate with free zones, a working port and a large student population — supplies usable examples that a student actually understands. Using them well is a technique, and it is not about memorising statistics. Lessons here run online, one to one, over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, which are a service we provide only in India.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-economics-0455-t.programmesIntro: Economics is chosen at a point in a student's route and leads somewhere specific. These are the stages this page connects, with what a Sharjah family should expect at each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics
programmes.description: Two papers: a 45-minute multiple-choice paper worth 30% and a two-hour-fifteen structured-questions paper worth 70%, the latter comprising a compulsory 30-mark data response and three 20-mark questions chosen from four. Six syllabus sections run from the basic economic problem through to international trade and globalisation. No coursework, no tiering.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah, 0455 is usually an option subject taken alongside the sciences or alongside Business Studies rather than instead of it. That means a candidate often meets it with fewer timetabled periods than a core subject receives, which is why so much of the private support in this emirate is aimed at answer technique rather than content.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies
programmes.description: The subject families most often weigh against Economics. It examines how firms are organised and managed — marketing, operations, finance, people — with case-study material, where 0455 examines how markets and economies behave. Both are written subjects with no coursework, and the two are frequently taken together.
programmes.countryNote: The practical difference for a Sharjah student is the kind of thinking each rewards. Economics asks for a causal chain and a judgement about an economy; Business Studies asks for a recommendation about a firm, justified from the case material. Students who prefer diagrams and mechanisms tend to prefer Economics.

programmes.name: Cambridge AS and A Level Economics 9708
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation, which revisits every 0455 section at greater depth and raises the demands on evaluation and on diagram accuracy considerably. The biggest change is in the essay: an A-Level answer sustains an argument across pages rather than across a paragraph.
programmes.countryNote: For Sharjah students heading to a local or Dubai sixth form, the 0455 habit worth building now is the two-sided eight-mark answer. That habit transfers directly; memorised content does not, because the content is retaught at greater depth in Year 12 anyway.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Economics
programmes.description: The other Year 12 destination, at Standard or Higher Level, with its own command terms, a heavier emphasis on real-world examples and an internal assessment in which the student comments on published news articles using economic theory. There is no Cambridge equivalent to that component.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families moving to a Dubai Diploma campus after Year 11 should know that the internal assessment is the student's own work. A tutor teaches the theory and gives feedback on a draft; the commentary itself must be written by the candidate, and that limit is set by the IB.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-economics-0455-t.subjectsIntro: 0455 is six syllabus sections and a small set of transferable writing skills. These are the topic areas and skills a tutor works through, ordered by how much of the grade usually turns on each.

subjects.name: Government and the macroeconomy
subjects.description: Government aims, fiscal and monetary policy, supply-side measures, economic growth, employment and unemployment, inflation and deflation. The largest and most heavily examined section, and the one where causal chains are longest. Most eight-mark questions in a series draw on it, so weakness here caps a grade.

subjects.name: The allocation of resources
subjects.description: Demand and supply, price determination, price elasticity of demand and supply, market economic systems, market failure and mixed economies. The diagram-heavy section. Marks are lost both to diagrams drawn incorrectly and to diagrams drawn correctly and then never referred to in the written answer.

subjects.name: Microeconomic decision makers
subjects.description: Money and banking, households, workers, trade unions and firms, including costs, revenues, objectives and market structure. The section with the widest internal spread of marks: students are usually comfortable with households and workers and much weaker on the firms material, particularly economies of scale and the cost curves.

subjects.name: International trade and globalisation
subjects.description: Specialisation, free trade, protection, exchange rates and the current account of the balance of payments. Taught last in most schemes of work and therefore revised least. Exchange rates in particular are a reliable late-course gap, and the questions on them follow a predictable pattern once seen.

subjects.name: Economic development
subjects.description: Living standards, poverty, population, differences in development between countries and the role of aid and investment. Descriptive rather than mechanical, which makes it one of the better returns on late revision time. The recurring loss is a list of features where a comparison with a cause was required.

subjects.name: The basic economic problem
subjects.description: Scarcity, choice, opportunity cost, factors of production and production possibility curves. Taught first, assumed afterwards, and quietly responsible for lost definition marks all the way through the course. Opportunity cost in particular is defined loosely by most students and precisely by the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Definitions and the two-mark part
subjects.description: Almost every structured question opens with a definition worth two marks. Written precisely it is the quickest mark in the paper; written as an example or a paraphrase it earns one mark or none. Over a whole paper this single habit is worth a meaningful fraction of the Section B total.

subjects.name: Diagrams and their use in an answer
subjects.description: Axes labelled, curves labelled, the shift drawn and the new equilibrium marked. Then — the part students omit — a sentence in the prose that refers to the diagram and explains what it shows. A diagram that is never mentioned in the writing has done only half its work.

subjects.name: Elasticity calculations and interpretation
subjects.description: Price elasticity of demand and of supply, the formulas, the sign and what the number means for a firm's revenue. The calculation is straightforward arithmetic; the marks are lost on dropping the negative sign, on confusing elastic with inelastic, and on failing to state the consequence after the number.

subjects.name: The eight-mark evaluative part
subjects.description: Two sides argued and a judgement reached. The judgement has to be a judgement — it depends on, it is more likely where, in the short run as against the long run — rather than a restatement. Students who present one strong side score in the middle of the band however well they write it.

subjects.name: The data-response question
subjects.description: Compulsory, extract-based and worth a third of the whole paper. Marks live in the supplied material: figures quoted from the extract, trends described from the data, and conclusions anchored to what is in front of the candidate rather than to what they revised.

subjects.name: Paper 1 multiple choice
subjects.description: Thirty items in 45 minutes with no credit for working. Worth auditing by wrong-answer type rather than by score: a student missing items in one syllabus section has a content gap, while one missing items scattered across sections usually has a definitions problem.

sections.heading: The six syllabus sections, and the two that decide most grades
paragraphs: A revision plan that treats the 0455 syllabus as six equal parts will allocate time badly, because the sections are not equal in how often they are examined, how long their causal chains run, or how much marks move when a student improves in them. The table below sets out the six with what each actually costs.

Two sections carry most of the grade movement. Government and the macroeconomy is the largest and most frequently examined, and it supplies the material for a high proportion of eight-mark evaluative parts in any series — fiscal policy, monetary policy, inflation, unemployment, growth. A student who is weak here is capped, because the hardest-marked parts of the paper keep returning to it. The allocation of resources is the other: demand, supply, price determination, elasticity and market failure, and it is where almost every diagram in the subject lives.

Two sections are usually under-revised for structural rather than intellectual reasons. Economic development and international trade sit at the end of most schemes of work, which means they are taught in the spring of Year 11 and revised once, hurriedly. Exchange rates are the clearest example: the questions follow a recognisable pattern, the content is finite, and candidates lose marks on them every series simply because they met the topic three weeks before the paper.

The remaining two behave differently again. The basic economic problem is taught first and then assumed, and its definitions — scarcity, opportunity cost, the factors of production — leak marks all the way through the course because nobody revisits them. Microeconomic decision makers has the widest internal spread: students are generally sound on households, workers and trade unions and distinctly weaker on firms, costs, revenues and economies of scale. Knowing that in advance is worth several sessions of exploratory teaching.

sections.heading: Definitions: the quickest marks in the paper, and the ones most often skipped
paragraphs: Almost every Section B structured question in 0455 opens with a two-mark definition. Over a paper where a candidate answers three such questions, plus definition-style marks inside the data response, that is a non-trivial block of the total available, and it is the easiest block in the subject to secure. It is also the block Sharjah students most often forfeit, for a reason that is more about habit than ability.

What happens is this. A student who understands a term well gives an example instead of a definition. Asked to define opportunity cost, they write that if you spend money on one thing you cannot spend it on another, which is an illustration rather than a definition and typically earns one of the two marks. Asked to define inflation, they write that prices go up, where the mark scheme wants a sustained rise in the general price level. The economics is present. The precision is not, and precision is what the two marks are for.

The fix is unglamorous and reliable. Build a list of the definable terms section by section — there are not many more than sixty across the whole syllabus — and practise writing each one in a single precise sentence, not reciting it aloud. Written is the operative word: a student who can say a definition and cannot write it under pressure will not score it. Fifteen minutes a week on this produces more marks per minute than any other activity in 0455 revision, which is why it is the first thing a session should check rather than the last.

There is a second-order benefit worth knowing. Precise definitions make the longer parts easier, because a four or six-mark explanation that begins from an exactly stated term stays on track. Much of what looks like weak analysis in a marked script is actually an answer that drifted because the opening term was vague. A tutor who starts with definitions is not avoiding the hard parts; they are removing the commonest cause of them going wrong.

sections.heading: Elasticity: the calculation, the sign, and the sentence that must follow
paragraphs: Price elasticity is where numerical and written economics meet, and it loses marks in three distinct places. Each is specific enough to diagnose from a marked script, which makes it a good illustration of how 0455 support should work.

The first loss is arithmetic framing. Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price, and students who substitute absolute changes rather than percentage changes produce a number that is simply wrong. The remedy is a fixed working layout: percentage change in quantity, percentage change in price, divide, state. Written out every time, including when the student thinks they can do it mentally, because under exam pressure they cannot.

The second is the sign. Price elasticity of demand is normally negative because price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions, and candidates who drop the sign or treat the value as negative when interpreting it get tangled. The convention a student needs is to calculate with the sign, then interpret the magnitude: a value whose size exceeds one is elastic, below one is inelastic. Income elasticity behaves differently again, where the sign itself carries the meaning and distinguishes a normal good from an inferior one. That distinction is examined and is routinely muddled.

The third loss is the most expensive and the least obvious: stopping at the number. A question that asks for an elasticity calculation almost always wants the consequence stated — what happens to the firm's total revenue if it raises the price, and why. A candidate who computes correctly and writes nothing after it has taken the calculation mark and left the application marks on the table. The habit to build is a mandatory sentence after every number: therefore, because demand is inelastic, a price rise increases total revenue. One session on that single habit moves marks across both papers.

sections.heading: The causal chain, and the middle step students leave out
paragraphs: If there is one diagnosis that fits more middling 0455 scripts than any other, it is the missing middle step. A student is asked to explain how a rise in income tax might reduce inflation. They write that higher income tax reduces inflation. Both ends of the chain are correct, the economics is sound, and the answer earns a fraction of the available marks because the mechanism between the ends was never written down.

The full chain has three or four links: income tax rises, so disposable income falls, so consumer spending falls, so aggregate demand falls, so the general price level rises less quickly. Each link is a separate marking point, and an examiner can only award what is on the page. Students leave the middle out because to them it is obvious, and the more able the student the more likely they are to omit it. This is why strong students plateau in economics while weaker ones who write methodically do not.

Teaching it is mechanical in the best sense. Take a policy, draw four boxes, and require a sentence in each. Then do it again for monetary policy, for a supply-side measure, for a change in the exchange rate, for a tariff. After six or seven of these the student stops needing the boxes, because the shape of an economics explanation has become the shape they write in. That is a two-to-three-session intervention with an effect that runs across every section of the syllabus.

The chain also sets up the eight-mark part, which is the other place Sharjah candidates plateau. An eight-mark question wants two chains — one supporting, one qualifying — and then a judgement. The judgement is where most answers fail, because a restatement is offered instead: having argued both sides, the student concludes that there are arguments on both sides. A real judgement says what it depends on. It depends on the size of the tax change. It is more likely to work where demand is interest-sensitive. In the short run it reduces spending; in the long run it may reduce investment and growth. Those are judgements, and they are learnable phrases attached to a learnable habit.
bullets: Write every link: tax rises, disposable income falls, spending falls, demand falls, prices rise less quickly
Each link is a separate marking point and only what is written can be awarded
Able students omit the middle most often, which is why they plateau
An eight-mark judgement states what the outcome depends on, not that both sides exist

sections.heading: Microeconomic decision makers: the section with the widest spread
paragraphs: Section three of the syllabus — money and banking, households, workers, trade unions and firms — behaves unlike the other five, because students are not uniformly weak or strong in it. They are reliably comfortable in its first half and reliably shaky in its second, and a plan that treats the section as one block spends its time in the wrong place.

The comfortable half covers money and banking, household spending and saving decisions, the factors influencing an individual's choice of occupation, wage determination and the role of trade unions. This material is intuitive, connects to things a sixteen-year-old observes directly, and is generally well taught. Where marks are lost it is to the usual culprits: a definition given as an example, or a list of factors offered where an explanation of one factor was required.

The shaky half is firms. Classification by size and the ways of measuring it, the causes and effects of growth in firm size, internal and external economies and diseconomies of scale, fixed and variable costs, total and average cost and revenue, and the objectives of firms. This is the most technical material in the syllabus outside elasticity, it is often taught quickly late in Year 10 or early in Year 11, and the cost-and-revenue arithmetic catches out students who are otherwise strong. Economies of scale in particular is examined often and answered vaguely — a student who can name purchasing, technical, financial and managerial economies and explain one properly is immediately ahead of the median script.

For a Sharjah candidate, this section has a practical advantage: the emirate's own economy supplies examples a student can picture. Firms growing, firms of different sizes, the difference between a small workshop and a large manufacturer are all observable here, which makes the abstract material easier to hold. That is a teaching advantage rather than an exam requirement, and it is one of the reasons this section repays targeted sessions so well.

sections.heading: Economic development and international trade: taught last, revised least
paragraphs: Sections five and six sit at the end of almost every scheme of work, and the consequence is predictable: they are taught in the final months of Year 11, revised once in a hurry, and then examined at the same standard as material the student has had two years with. This is a planning problem rather than a difficulty problem, and it is the easiest structural gain available in 0455.

Economic development covers living standards and how they are measured, poverty and its causes, population characteristics and change, differences in development between countries, and the role of aid and foreign investment. The material is more descriptive than mechanical, which is why it rewards late revision well. The characteristic loss is a list where a comparison was wanted: asked why living standards differ between two countries, a student produces features of each rather than causes of the difference. Fixing that is a matter of question-stem reading and one or two marked attempts.

International trade and globalisation covers specialisation, the benefits and costs of free trade, methods and reasons for protection, exchange rates and their effects, and the current account of the balance of payments. Exchange rates are the specific weak point, and the reason is that the reasoning runs in two directions at once: a depreciation makes exports cheaper abroad and imports dearer at home, with effects on the current account that depend on elasticities. Students who have met this three weeks before the paper cannot hold both directions. Students who met it in a session in January can.

The practical recommendation for a Sharjah family is to buy these two sections early rather than late — a handful of sessions in the winter term on development and exchange rates, well before the school reaches them, so that the school's own teaching lands as consolidation. That is cheaper than an April intensive and considerably more effective, and it is the sort of plan that only gets made if someone has looked at the scheme of work rather than at the revision guide.

sections.heading: Writing about an economy the student actually lives in
paragraphs: 0455 asks candidates to apply economic ideas to real economies, and students who do that concretely write better answers than students who stay abstract. Sharjah is unusually good material for this, and using it well is a technique worth teaching explicitly.

The emirate's economy is a trade and manufacturing economy with a working port, free zones at Hamriyah and the Sharjah Airport International Free Zone, a substantial industrial base, and a large university population in University City. Every one of those is a usable illustration. Specialisation and the benefits of trade become concrete when the example is a port handling goods that are not consumed locally. Economies of scale become concrete when the example is a manufacturer whose unit costs fall as output rises. The effect of an exchange-rate movement on an exporter becomes a question about firms the student can name rather than a textbook abstraction.

There is an important limit, and it is the opposite of what students assume. Cambridge rewards the mechanism, not the statistic. A candidate does not need to know a growth rate, a trade figure or an inflation number for the UAE, and inventing one is worse than omitting it. What earns marks is an accurate chain of reasoning applied to a plausible real context. So the instruction to a student is: name the kind of firm or the kind of market, explain the mechanism in full, and leave the numbers alone unless a figure is supplied in the extract. If a student does want to use a published figure, it should come from an official source they can cite, and the habit of checking is worth more than the figure.

This also pays off in the data-response question, which is compulsory and worth 30 marks of the 90 on Paper 2. That question hands the candidate figures in an extract, and the marks are for using those figures — quoting them, describing the trend they show, and anchoring the conclusion in them. A student practised at applying mechanisms to a real context moves naturally into that mode, while one who has only revised definitions tends to answer the data-response question from memory and ignore the material in front of them.

sections.heading: The repair order after a disappointing 0455 mock
paragraphs: When a mock comes back lower than expected, the instinct is to revise everything again. That is the least efficient response available, because 0455 losses have distinct signatures and each signature has a different repair. The table below sets out the order we would work in, with what each repair involves and roughly how long it takes.

The ordering principle is marks per hour. Definitions come first because they are the quickest marks in the paper and because precise definitions improve the longer parts as a side effect. Causal chains come second because they affect every section of the syllabus simultaneously. Judgement phrasing for the eight-mark parts comes third, since it is a narrow habit with a wide effect. Only after those three does it make sense to address content gaps in specific sections, because a student with content gaps and poor answer structure will not show any benefit from content teaching alone.

The data-response question deserves its own place in the order and usually gets missed. It is compulsory and carries a third of Paper 2, and students who score poorly on it are frequently answering from revision rather than from the extract. That is one of the cheapest repairs in the subject: two marked attempts in which the student is required to quote at least three figures from the supplied material are normally enough to change the habit.

Paper 1 is last in the order, not because it does not matter — it is 30% of the grade — but because its weaknesses are usually symptoms of the others. A wrong-answer audit sorted by syllabus section will show either a cluster, which means a content gap worth teaching, or a scatter, which almost always means imprecise definitions and will improve on its own once the definition work is done. Auditing by type rather than counting the score is the difference between useful information and a number.

sections.heading: SPEA, the school, and the entry questions worth asking
paragraphs: 0455 is an option subject, which means the school has made several decisions about it that affect what support is useful. Three questions to the school settle all of them, and none of them is a difficult conversation.

The first is whether Economics sits in the same option block as Business Studies. In many Sharjah schools it does, which forces a choice; in others a student can take both. Families who intend both should confirm it before assuming it. The second is the scheme of work: which of the six sections are being taught when, and particularly when economic development and international trade are scheduled. That answer is what allows a plan to put sessions ahead of the school rather than behind it. The third is which series the candidate will be entered for, because Cambridge entry deadlines fall months before the papers: a June entry closes in the spring, and the November series, which candidates here use as the resit route, closes in the preceding months on a date the centre holds. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a timetable built on it belongs to a different country. Each centre is also allocated to one of six administrative zones, with Cambridge stating plainly that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

The regulatory layer sits above all of that and is worth understanding for what it does not do. Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools in the emirate. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge holds a comparable remit, Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools to ADEK, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. Those bodies oversee schools. None of them regulates or endorses private tutoring, and no tutoring provider — IB Gram included — holds an approval, accreditation or licence from any of them.

Private tutoring is governed separately, through the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE's service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing with a two-working-day completion time, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since the ministry has published no fine schedule, any page quoting an amount has invented it.

process.title: Send the marked Paper 2 script, all parts
process.description: Photograph the whole marked script rather than reporting the grade. What matters is which of the two, four, six and eight-mark parts lost marks, because each signals a different repair. A script where the two-mark parts scored poorly is a definitions problem and a cheap fix; one where only the eight-mark parts failed is a judgement problem.

process.title: Ask the school for the scheme of work
process.description: Find out when the six syllabus sections are being taught, and especially when economic development and international trade are scheduled. Those two are taught last in most schools, and knowing the date is what makes it possible to cover them in a session before the class reaches them rather than three weeks before the paper.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson on an eight-mark part
process.description: One hour, online, no card required, no obligation. Bring one eight-mark answer the student lost marks on. Watch whether the tutor rebuilds the causal chain link by link and shows where a judgement should sit. A tutor who re-explains the economics instead has not diagnosed anything.

process.title: Work the repair order, not the syllabus
process.description: Definitions first, then causal chains, then judgement phrasing, then the data-response habit, then any content gap in a specific section. Teaching content to a student whose answer structure is the problem produces no visible change, which is how families conclude that tutoring does not work in this subject.

process.title: Review at week six on paired answers
process.description: Compare two eight-mark answers on comparable questions, six sessions apart, both marked. Look for two chains and a judgement rather than for a higher number. If the structure has appeared, the marks follow at the next assessment. If it has not, change the arrangement rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis by question part, not by topic
whyPoints.description: A 0455 script tells you which of the two, four, six and eight-mark parts failed, and that is a more useful fact than which topic the question was about. Sessions start from that breakdown, because the repair for a missing definition and the repair for a missing judgement share nothing.

whyPoints.title: The neglected sections are planned for
whyPoints.description: Economic development and international trade sit at the end of nearly every scheme of work and are revised once. Covering exchange rates and development in the winter term, ahead of the school, is one of the cheapest structural gains in the subject and it only happens if someone looks at the scheme of work.

whyPoints.title: Causal chains written out, link by link
whyPoints.description: The missing middle step is the commonest diagnosis in this syllabus and it affects every section at once. Four boxes, one sentence each, repeated across six or seven policies until the shape is the shape the student writes in. Two or three sessions, and the effect shows up everywhere.

whyPoints.title: Real context without invented statistics
whyPoints.description: Sharjah's port, free zones and manufacturing base make good illustration material, and Cambridge rewards an accurate mechanism applied to a plausible context. It does not require a growth rate or a trade figure, and inventing one is worse than leaving it out. Any published figure a student uses should come from a source they can cite.

whyPoints.title: Marked against the published criteria
whyPoints.description: Written answers come back annotated with the marking points that were and were not present, which is the only pre-results evidence available in an exam-only subject. No tutor can promise a grade in a Cambridge series; a marked pair of comparable answers six weeks apart is what can honestly be shown.

whyPoints.title: Subject-matched rather than distance-matched
whyPoints.description: Economics is an option subject, so specialists are thinly spread across this emirate and almost absent from the east-coast communities. Delivering online removes geography from the choice and puts it back on who has marked Section B answers against the criteria.

faqs.question: Which of the six 0455 syllabus sections carries the most marks?
faqs.answer: Government and the macroeconomy is the largest and most frequently examined, and it supplies the material for a high proportion of the eight-mark evaluative parts in any series — fiscal and monetary policy, inflation, unemployment and growth. The allocation of resources is the second heaviest and is where almost every diagram in the subject lives. A student weak in those two is effectively capped, because the hardest-marked parts of Paper 2 keep returning to them. The basic economic problem is small in content but leaks definition marks all year, so it repays attention out of proportion to its size.

faqs.question: How many marks does a definition earn in 0455, and does it have to be exact?
faqs.answer: Almost every Section B structured question opens with a two-mark definition, and precision is exactly what those marks are for. An example is not a definition: writing that inflation means prices go up typically earns one of the two marks, where a sustained rise in the general price level earns both. There are not many more than sixty definable terms across the whole syllabus, so the work is finite. Practise writing them rather than reciting them, because a student who can say a definition aloud and not write it under pressure will not score it in the paper.

faqs.question: My son can draw a demand and supply diagram but still loses the marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Most often because the diagram is never used. A correctly drawn diagram with labelled axes, labelled curves, the shift shown and the new equilibrium marked earns its own marks, but the analysis marks come from the prose that refers to it. Candidates draw the diagram, then write a paragraph that would read identically if the diagram were not there. The habit to build is a mandatory sentence after every diagram: as the diagram shows, the curve shifts right, so equilibrium price falls and quantity rises. That is a single-session fix with an effect across the whole paper.

faqs.question: How is price elasticity of demand marked in 0455, and does the negative sign matter?
faqs.answer: The calculation is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the percentage change in price, and using absolute changes instead of percentage changes produces a wrong number. The sign matters: price elasticity of demand is normally negative because price and quantity move in opposite directions, and students who drop it get tangled when interpreting. Calculate with the sign, then interpret the magnitude — a size above one is elastic, below one inelastic. Income elasticity is different again, where the sign itself distinguishes a normal good from an inferior one, and that is examined and routinely muddled.

faqs.question: What is the middle step that students leave out of economics answers?
faqs.answer: The mechanism between cause and effect. Asked how a rise in income tax might reduce inflation, a student writes that higher income tax reduces inflation — both ends correct, nothing in between. The full chain is: tax rises, so disposable income falls, so consumer spending falls, so aggregate demand falls, so the general price level rises less quickly. Each link is a separate marking point and an examiner can only award what is written. Able students omit the middle most often because to them it is obvious, which is precisely why strong candidates plateau in this subject.

faqs.question: Does my daughter need to memorise real economic statistics for 0455?
faqs.answer: No, and attempting it is a poor use of revision time. Cambridge rewards an accurate mechanism applied to a plausible real context, not a recalled figure, and inventing a statistic is worse than omitting one. What earns marks is naming the kind of market or firm and then explaining the chain of reasoning in full. The exception is the data-response question, which supplies figures in an extract and expects the candidate to quote and use them. If a student does want to cite a published figure elsewhere, it should come from an official source they can name.

faqs.question: Can a student use Sharjah or UAE examples in a 0455 answer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually improves the writing. Sharjah's working port, its free zones at Hamriyah and the Sharjah Airport International Free Zone, and its manufacturing base all illustrate specialisation, trade and economies of scale in a form a sixteen-year-old can actually picture. A concrete example keeps a causal chain honest, because it is harder to skip a step when describing something real. The rule is to name the type of firm or market and explain the mechanism, and to leave numbers out unless they are supplied in the extract or come from a source the student can cite.

faqs.question: Which 0455 section is taught last, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: International trade and globalisation, usually with economic development just before it, and it matters a great deal. Both sit at the end of most schemes of work, which means they are taught in the spring of Year 11 and revised once in a hurry, then examined at the same standard as material the student has had two years with. Exchange rates are the specific casualty, because the reasoning runs in two directions at once and a student who met it three weeks before the paper cannot hold both. Covering these early, ahead of the school, is the cheapest structural gain available.

faqs.question: What should we fix first after a disappointing 0455 mock?
faqs.answer: Work in order of marks per hour rather than revising everything. Definitions first, because the two-mark parts are the quickest marks in the paper and precision there keeps the longer answers on track. Causal chains second, because the missing middle step affects every section simultaneously. Judgement phrasing for the eight-mark parts third. Then the data-response habit of quoting figures from the extract. Only after those four does teaching content in a weak section produce a visible change, because a student with structural problems shows no benefit from content teaching alone.

faqs.question: Why do students score lower on the data-response question than on the essays?
faqs.answer: Because they answer it from revision instead of from the extract. The compulsory data-response question carries 30 of the 90 marks on Paper 2, and its marks live in the supplied material: figures quoted, trends described from the data, conclusions anchored to what is on the page. A candidate who has revised thoroughly often writes a good general answer that ignores the extract and scores in the middle. Two marked attempts in which the student is required to quote at least three figures from the material is normally enough to change the habit permanently.

faqs.question: Is Economics 0455 a sensible choice alongside the sciences and Additional Maths?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the deciding factor is usually writing load rather than difficulty. 0455 has no coursework, so every mark is sat in the exam room, and Paper 2 asks for two hours fifteen minutes of structured written answers. A student already carrying three sciences and two maths codes is adding a subject whose demands are verbal rather than numerical, which some find a relief and others find the opposite. The elasticity and cost-and-revenue arithmetic is well within Extended Mathematics. Ask the school whether Economics and Business Studies sit in the same option block before assuming both are available.

faqs.question: How much writing does a 0455 candidate actually have to produce in Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Enough that stamina is a real factor. Paper 2 runs two hours fifteen minutes for 90 marks: a compulsory 30-mark data-response question and then three structured questions chosen from four, each worth 20 marks and each built from parts of roughly two, four, six and eight marks. That is a substantial amount of structured prose, and candidates who have only ever answered single parts in homework find the full paper a shock. Sitting one complete timed Paper 2 before the mock is worth more than any amount of topic revision, and it costs nothing beyond the paper.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge 0455 include any coursework or controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: No. Both components are written examinations sat at the end of the course: the multiple-choice paper worth 30% and the structured-questions paper worth 70%. There is no portfolio, no controlled assessment and no practical element, so every mark is earned in the exam room. That has one clear implication for tutoring: the work is entirely about preparation and technique, and no question arises of a tutor contributing to assessed work. It also means mock performance under timed conditions is the only realistic predictor available before the series.

faqs.question: How should a tutor use a 0455 essay the school has already set?
faqs.answer: As the material, with the writing left to the student. A good session takes the question, rebuilds the causal chain the answer needed, shows where a judgement should sit, and then has the student rewrite it themselves. What a tutor should not do is draft the answer or dictate it: the school needs to see where the student actually is, and work submitted as the student's own has to be theirs. The same applies to materials — Cambridge syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes belong to the awarding body, are published on the official site, and the school already holds copies.

faqs.question: What does the school decide about 0455 that we should ask about?
faqs.answer: Three things, all factual and quickly answered. Whether Economics sits in the same option block as Business Studies, which decides whether both are possible. When the six syllabus sections are scheduled, especially economic development and international trade, which is what lets sessions run ahead of the class rather than behind it. And which series the entry is for, together with the centre's Cambridge administrative zone — entry deadlines fall months before the papers, and Cambridge states that using the wrong zone timetable is a risk it cannot take responsibility for.

faqs.question: Is 0455 worth taking if my child will study engineering rather than economics?
faqs.answer: That is a judgement for the family and the school rather than something this page should answer, but two factual points help. 0455 is a full IGCSE and counts as one of a candidate's subjects, and under the British-track Ministry of Education equivalency rule a student must present five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. So the subject can serve that purpose regardless of the degree intended. Verify any equivalency requirement on moe.gov.ae, and note that tutoring is in no way required for the process.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-economics-0455-t.closingHeading: Send one eight-mark answer and we will show you what it was missing
sharjah/cambridge-igcse-economics-0455-t.closingBody: If your child understands economics and the marks do not show it, the diagnosis is usually visible in a single answer. Photograph one eight-mark part the student lost marks on, along with the marked script it came from, and take a free trial lesson — one hour, online, with no card required. In that hour a specialist will rebuild the causal chain link by link, show where the judgement should have sat, and tell you which of the six syllabus sections to work on first. Lessons run online, one to one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

intro.heading: Where the money goes in English, and why it is not where parents expect
paragraphs: English is the subject Sharjah families most often buy badly. Not because they overspend, though some do, but because the thing being purchased is unclear. In maths or chemistry an hour buys teaching: a method is explained, practised and checked. In 0500 a substantial part of the value is in marking — someone reading a 500-word composition closely against published criteria and saying exactly which of the available marks were not taken. Marking takes time outside the session, it is invisible on an invoice, and it is the first thing a cheap arrangement quietly stops doing.

This matters because of how the paper is built. Cambridge 0500 is assessed across two written papers of 80 marks each, carrying 50% of the grade apiece. Paper 1 is Reading, two hours, covering comprehension and a directed response, analysis of a writer's use of language, and a summary. Paper 2 is Directed Writing and Composition, also two hours: a directed writing task worth 40 marks, then one composition chosen from a descriptive or narrative option, also worth 40 marks, of which 24 are for content and structure and 16 for style and accuracy. Some centres enter a coursework portfolio in place of Paper 2. There is no Core or Extended tier in 0500 — every candidate sits the same papers, and the grade runs A* to G.

Two of those components respond to teaching and two respond to marking, and the budget should follow that split rather than the clock. The summary question and the language-analysis question have techniques that can be taught in a few sessions and then practised cheaply. The composition and the directed writing improve almost entirely through a redraft cycle: write, be marked precisely, rewrite the same piece, be marked again. That cycle is the expensive part, and a provider charging only for contact time is either absorbing the marking or not doing it.

The Sharjah market makes the choice wider than it looks. Published online rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, with Unitors listing IGCSE support from AED 150. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits including travel run roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350. Those are market figures from the providers and rate survey named, not an IB Gram price list.

The order of this page follows the money. It begins with what costs nothing, moves to what the local market charges and why English sits where it does in that range, works out where a limited budget should go between the two papers, covers the entry decision between 0500 and 0510 that changes the budget entirely, prices the redraft cycle honestly, and ends with the checks a Sharjah parent can make for free. Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, which are a service we provide only in India.

Treating the two as one subject is a common and expensive error.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student takes both, one specialist covering both in a single weekly hour is materially cheaper than two arrangements, and the Paper 1 analysis work transfers. Ask any provider directly whether the same tutor is comfortable with both before paying for two.

programmes.name: Cambridge AS and A Level English Language 9093
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation for students who want to keep the subject. It raises the analytical demand considerably and introduces directed writing for specified audiences and purposes. A 0500 candidate who has been marked against criteria rather than corrected for grammar arrives with the habit that matters.
programmes.countryNote: For Sharjah families with a sixth form in view, the useful 0500 spend is on the composition redraft cycle rather than on last-minute exam technique, because the redraft habit is what Year 12 depends on and the technique is not.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-english-first-la.subjectsIntro: 0500 breaks into a small number of assessed tasks, and they do not cost the same to improve. This is where a budget actually goes, ordered from the cheapest marks to recover to the dearest.

subjects.name: The summary question
subjects.description: The cheapest marks in the syllabus to recover. It rewards selecting the relevant points from a passage and expressing them concisely in the student's own words. It is a technique, not a talent: identify, condense, avoid quotation, watch the length. Two or three sessions and some unsupervised practice usually settles it for good.

subjects.name: Comprehension and short-answer reading
subjects.description: Short responses where marks are lost to answering a different question from the one asked, or to giving one point where two were required. Cheap to improve because the fix is reading the question stem carefully and checking the mark allocation. Rarely needs more than a session plus practice.

subjects.name: Writer's effects and language analysis
subjects.description: The question that separates grades. It asks what the writer's choice of words achieves, not what the passage says. Students who paraphrase the content score poorly however well written their answer. Mid-cost: the technique can be taught in two or three sessions, but it needs several marked attempts before it holds under exam pressure.

subjects.name: Directed writing
subjects.description: Writing to a specified form, audience and purpose from supplied material. Marks follow convention as much as quality: the form has to be recognisable, the audience addressed and the supplied material used rather than ignored. A structural fix, which makes it faster and cheaper to improve than the free composition.

subjects.name: Descriptive composition
subjects.description: Twenty-four marks for content and structure, sixteen for style and accuracy. The expensive component, because it improves through redrafting rather than instruction. Students who write fluently and score in the middle are almost always losing structure marks, not accuracy marks, which is counter-intuitive and only visible in criteria-based marking.

subjects.name: Narrative composition
subjects.description: The alternative composition option, marked on the same split. The recurring loss is a plot that consumes the word count without any crafted writing in it. Improvement comes from fewer events and more deliberate sentences, which is a hard thing to accept and a cheap thing to teach once accepted.

subjects.name: Style and accuracy, the sixteen marks
subjects.description: Sentence variety, punctuation under pressure, paragraph control and vocabulary used precisely rather than decoratively. This is the part parents assume is the whole subject. It is sixteen marks out of forty, and spending the entire budget here while the structure marks leak is the most common misallocation in 0500 support.

subjects.name: The coursework portfolio route
subjects.levels: 0500 Component 3, where a centre offers it
subjects.description: Where a school enters coursework in place of Paper 2, the assessed work is produced over time under the school's supervision. Tutoring here is tightly bounded: a tutor may teach and discuss, but the writing must be the student's own, and that limit is not negotiable under the awarding body's rules.

subjects.name: Speaking and listening
subjects.description: Reported separately and not part of the 0500 grade itself. Worth knowing because families occasionally pay for support here believing it will move the English grade. It will not. Confirm with the school what is being entered before any money is spent on it.

subjects.name: Reading speed and stamina
subjects.description: Not an assessed objective but a real constraint: two hours, three question types and a long passage to work from. Students who run out of time lose marks on the final question regardless of ability. Timed practice costs nothing beyond the paper it is written on and is the cheapest intervention available.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-english-first-la.regionsIntro: What English support costs and what is available locally varies across the emirate, mostly because of travel and the size of the local tutoring pool. These are the communities this page is written for.

regions.name: Al Majaz and Al Qasba
regions.note: Central Sharjah, where in-home English tutoring is most actively advertised and quoted rates are most visible. Competition keeps prices comparable here, which makes it the easiest part of the emirate in which to shop on price rather than availability.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Dense apartment living on the Dubai boundary with many children at Dubai campuses. Supply is plentiful but heavily weighted to the budget end of the market, so the useful question here is what the fee includes rather than what it is.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Several Cambridge centres and a large Year 10 and 11 population. The local pattern is a confident speaker with a middling composition mark, which is a structure problem and the one most likely to be mispriced as a grammar problem.

regions.name: University City and Al Nouf
regions.note: Proximity to the higher-education cluster makes cheap undergraduate tutoring easy to find for English specifically. That genuinely works for timed reading practice and summary technique; it does not reliably work for criteria-based composition marking.

regions.name: Al Khan and Al Taawun
regions.note: Coastal and committed to the Dubai commute, so an in-home session booked at 17:00 often starts late and is still billed in full. For a subject where the value sits partly in marking done outside the session, that lost time is expensive.

regions.name: Tilal City and Sharjah Garden City
regions.note: Outlying villa communities where in-home quotes rise fastest because a tutor prices the drive as well as the hour. Online delivery removes that line from the invoice without changing what happens to a marked composition.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan, Kalba and Dibba Al Hisn
regions.note: East-coast communities under SPEA with little local English tutoring supply at specialist level. Working over live video is the only arrangement here where a weekly redraft cycle actually runs for a full term.

schoolClusters.note: Students we support in Sharjah attend Cambridge and British-curriculum schools across the emirate. Each campus decides whether it enters the coursework portfolio or Paper 2, and whether an individual student is entered for first-language or second-language English — both decisions change what support is worth paying for.

sections.heading: The cheapest useful thing you can do for 0500 costs nothing
paragraphs: Two interventions in this subject are free and both outperform a month of poorly targeted paid sessions. They are worth doing before any provider is contacted, partly because they work and partly because they tell you what you actually need to buy.

The first is a timed composition written at home. Two hours, one past-paper question, no help, no phone. Most Sharjah students have never done this, because school conditions are different and homework is untimed. What comes back answers the question nobody can answer from a report: does the student run out of time, or produce a fluent piece that lacks shape, or write carefully and accurately with nothing much happening in it. Those are three different problems with three different price tags, and confusing them is how families spend AED 800 a month on grammar for a student whose structure marks are the ones leaking.

The second is a direct question to the English department. Ask three things. Is the child entered for first-language English 0500 or second-language English 0510. Does the centre enter the coursework portfolio or Paper 2. And on the most recent composition, were the marks lost mainly in content and structure, which carries 24 marks, or in style and accuracy, which carries 16. English teachers answer that third question readily and precisely, and the answer determines what a tutor should be doing. Many families never ask it and pay for months of work aimed at the wrong half of the mark scheme.

A third free step is nearly as useful: read the published marking criteria for the composition with the student. Not the syllabus, the criteria. Seeing that nearly two-thirds of the marks are for content and structure reframes the subject for a student who believes English marks are awarded for vocabulary. That conversation costs twenty minutes and changes what the student does in the exam room.

sections.heading: Teaching time or marking time: what the fee actually covers
paragraphs: English is priced like other subjects and consumed differently, and that mismatch is responsible for most disappointing English arrangements in this market. An hour of maths tutoring is an hour of work. An hour of 0500 tutoring that includes a properly marked composition is an hour of contact plus thirty to forty minutes of close reading against criteria, which somebody has to absorb.

There are three ways providers handle this and they are worth distinguishing before signing anything. Some price contact time only and mark nothing, which is cheap and appropriate if the student needs reading technique rather than writing development. Some price contact time and absorb light marking, which usually means corrections and a comment rather than criteria-based assessment. Some charge for marking separately, per piece, which is transparent and often the best value for a student whose problem is purely the composition. The table below sets the three out with the question to ask each.

The practical consequence for a Sharjah family on a budget is that the cheapest route is frequently a hybrid. Buy a small number of technique sessions for the reading paper, where contact time is the thing that helps. Buy marking by the piece for the composition, where the marking is the thing that helps. That combination costs less than a weekly hour across a year and targets both halves of the paper. It requires a provider willing to sell it that way, which is itself a useful filter.

One warning about the cheapest end. At published budget rates of roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, criteria-based composition marking is not realistically included, and a provider implying otherwise is either doing something lighter than that or not sustaining it. That is not a reason to avoid the band — for timed reading practice and summary technique it is good value — but it is a reason to be specific about what you expect back.
