sections.heading: The Sharjah English market, cheapest to dearest
paragraphs: With the free steps done and the pricing model understood, the market itself becomes easy to read. English has the deepest tutoring supply of any subject in this emirate, because almost every candidate sits it, which means the price range is wider than in maths or the sciences and the quality range is wider still.

At the budget end, published online rates start at roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from about AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. In University City the undergraduate supply makes this band particularly easy to access. It buys contact time: reading practice, summary attempts, someone to sit with a student through a past paper. For a candidate who needs pacing and technique rather than writing development, it is sound value and should not be dismissed. What it does not buy is criteria-based marking of a composition, and expecting that at this rate leads to disappointment.

The middle band, AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor with Unitors listing IGCSE support from AED 150, is where most 0500 arrangements sit and where the variation in what is delivered is widest. Two tutors at the same rate can be doing completely different work: one correcting grammar, one marking against the 24-and-16 split. Asking for a marked sample in the trial session is the only way to tell, and it costs nothing.

Above that, specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table running to AED 450 plus for exam-year specialists; premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650, with BartyED listing that figure. In English, the honest case for the upper bands is narrower than in a technical subject: what you are buying is marking judgement, which matters enormously for a student stuck at a grade 5 or 6 and matters much less for one who needs timed reading practice. All figures here are the published market rates of the providers and survey named, not ours.

sections.heading: Why English sits where it does in this market
paragraphs: Prices in a tutoring market are set by supply and by what the work costs the person doing it, and English has an unusual profile on both counts. Understanding it stops a family either overpaying out of anxiety or underpaying and getting nothing marked.

On supply, English is the most available subject in the emirate. Every Cambridge candidate sits an English qualification, every education graduate has studied the language, and the University City undergraduate population adds a large pool of competent, cheap, willing tutors. Deep supply pushes the entry price down, which is genuinely good for families. The problem it creates is discrimination: a tutor who is excellent at reading technique and a tutor who can mark a composition against criteria present identically on a profile and often at the same rate.

On cost of work, English runs the other way. A maths tutor finishes when the session finishes. A 0500 tutor who marks a composition properly spends real time on each piece and does so between sessions. That cost is either priced in, absorbed quietly until it stops being done, or billed separately. This is why the question about marking matters more in English than anywhere else, and why a specialist rate in this subject is buying time you never see rather than expertise you watch being used.

The result is a market where the top and the bottom are both defensible and the middle requires questions. A budget tutor who honestly sells contact time is good value. A specialist who honestly sells marking judgement is good value for the student who needs it. The arrangement to avoid is the mid-priced weekly hour where nobody has specified what happens to the student's writing, because that is where most of the wasted money in Sharjah English tutoring sits.

sections.heading: Spending a limited budget: the reading paper against the writing paper
paragraphs: Suppose a family in Al Nahda or Muwaileh has AED 600 a month to spend on 0500 and eight months before the papers. Where that money goes depends entirely on which paper is losing the marks, and the two answers barely overlap.

If Paper 1 Reading is the weaker side, the money goes a long way. The summary question is a technique: select the relevant points, condense them, use the student's own words, control the length. Two or three sessions plus unsupervised practice generally settles it permanently. The comprehension responses need the question stem read properly and the mark allocation checked, which is one session and a habit. The language-analysis question is harder and needs several marked attempts, but the attempts are short. A reading-side budget of AED 600 a month buys more than enough, and much of it can taper off after the first term.

If Paper 2 is the weaker side, the same budget has to be deployed differently and more carefully. Compositions improve through redrafting, each cycle needs real marking, and three to four full cycles are usually required before the pattern holds under timed conditions. At AED 600 a month that is perhaps two sessions and two marked pieces, which is a slower but genuine route. Spending the same money on four cheap contact hours with nothing marked produces almost no movement, which is the most common way a reasonable English budget is wasted in this market.

There is a third case worth naming because it is frequent: both papers are adequate and the mark is stuck in the middle because the student does not know which of the 24 structure marks and 16 accuracy marks they are losing. That is a diagnostic problem, not a volume problem, and the correct spend is one session — available here as the free trial lesson with no card required — followed by a plan the family executes themselves. Some Sharjah families should spend nothing after that, and a provider unwilling to say so is not worth the fee.

sections.heading: 0500 or 0510: the entry decision that changes the whole budget
paragraphs: No single factor affects a Sharjah English budget as much as whether the child is on the right syllabus, and it is a question families frequently avoid asking because it feels like a judgement about the child.

Cambridge offers English as a First Language 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510 as separate qualifications with different papers, different demands and different grade profiles. The entry decision belongs to the school and is normally made from evidence in the student's written work. In a multilingual emirate where many students speak English fluently but did not acquire it first, the boundary is genuinely difficult, and schools make it with more information than a family or a tutor has.

The budget consequence is substantial in both directions. A student correctly entered for 0500 who needs composition development has a defined problem and a defined cost. A student entered for 0500 whose written English is at second-language level can absorb a weekly specialist hour for a year with the mark barely moving, because the gap is not a technique gap. Equally, a genuinely first-language student placed on 0510 may coast, and the cost there is an opportunity rather than a fee. Asking the English department directly which entry is planned, and on what evidence, is free and should happen before any arrangement starts.

What a tutor can honestly contribute is evidence rather than an opinion on placement. A marked composition against the 0500 criteria shows whether the losses are in content and structure or in the accuracy and range of the language itself, and that distinction is the one the school is weighing. Handing that marked work to the English teacher is more useful than asking either party to decide alone, and it is what we would suggest a family in this position do first.

sections.heading: What the composition redraft cycle costs to run properly
paragraphs: This is the part of 0500 that money genuinely buys, so it is worth being precise about what a cycle involves and therefore what it should cost.

One cycle is four steps. The student writes a composition under timed conditions. Someone reads it closely against the published criteria and marks it on both parts of the split, naming what cost the marks — not correcting the grammar, but identifying that the structure gave away eight of the 24 available marks because the piece had no shape beyond chronology. The student then rewrites the same piece against that feedback. And the rewrite is marked again, so the student sees the movement on an identical task. Three to four cycles is normally where a middling mark starts to hold at a higher level.

The cost is mostly in the second and fourth steps, and this is why the arrangement has to be specified rather than assumed. A provider selling a weekly contact hour at a mid-market rate may or may not be absorbing eighty minutes of marking across a month. For a Sharjah family deciding between options, the honest comparison is cost per marked cycle rather than cost per hour, and a provider that cannot quote the former is pricing something else.

Two limits belong here. The cycle works on practice compositions, not on assessed work. Where a centre enters the coursework portfolio in place of Paper 2, the writing in that folder must be the student's own, and a tutor may teach, discuss and give general feedback but may not edit it to completion or dictate it — that boundary is set by the awarding body and breaching it puts the student at risk, not the tutor. And no cycle, however well run, licenses a promise about a grade. No tutor can guarantee a particular Cambridge result, and the honest evidence is the mark gap between a first draft and a rewrite of the same piece.

sections.heading: In-home English in Sharjah, and what the travel line buys
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real market here and families are right to ask what it costs. Published in-home one-to-one rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits are advertised in this market. Set against a qualified online rate of AED 150 to 300, the gap is largely logistics.

For English specifically, the trade is sharper than in other subjects, and the reason is where the value sits. A physically present tutor helps a student who will not otherwise sit down and write, which is a genuine and common problem at this age. But the component that moves a 0500 grade is the marking, and marking happens between sessions wherever the tutor is. Paying a travel premium does not improve the marking; it improves attendance. Families should decide which of those two they are buying.

The Sharjah timing arithmetic makes this concrete. A household in Al Khan or Al Nahda whose children attend a Dubai campus often sees the bus arrive after 16:30. An in-home session booked for 17:00 starts late because the tutor is in the same traffic, and the hour is billed from 17:00. In the outlying communities — Tilal City, Sharjah Garden City, and the east-coast towns of Kalba and Khor Fakkan — the quotes rise further and the available pool narrows to whoever will make the drive, which for a subject where marking judgement is the product is the wrong selection criterion.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India, and no tutor will be sent to a Sharjah address. What a family gets instead is the specialist rather than the nearest available English graduate, and a marked composition returned annotated on screen that the student keeps and can show the school.

sections.heading: Four free checks before any payment
paragraphs: Four things a Sharjah parent can verify independently, none of which costs anything, and all of which are worth more than a testimonial page.

First, the permit position. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered through MoHRE, whose service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. It is granted free of charge for two years, with a two-working-day completion time, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the ministry has published no fine schedule, so any page naming an amount has invented it. Because the permit is free, no quote should contain a licensing charge.

Second, the claims. Ask whether the provider asserts approval, accreditation or licensing from a regulator or an awarding body. The correct answer is that it does not. Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools — a school-level remit that confers nothing on a tutoring provider. IB Gram holds no approval from SPEA, from the Ministry of Education or from Cambridge, and a provider claiming otherwise is making the most dangerous claim available in this market.

Third, what is included. Get the session length in writing, and get a direct answer on whether written work is marked, how it is marked, and how quickly it comes back. In English this single question separates most good arrangements from most disappointing ones, and it is free to ask.

Fourth, the materials position. Cambridge syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes are the awarding body's copyright material, distributed through schools and published on the official site. A tutor references them and works from the school's copies. A provider offering to supply a bundle as a download, or offering to produce coursework, has told you what it is. On the other side of the ledger, a free trial lesson should have its conditions stated plainly on the same screen as the word free — ours is one hour, online, with no card required and no obligation.

process.title: Write one timed composition at home first
process.description: Two hours, one past-paper question, unsupported. It costs nothing and it answers the question a report cannot: is the problem pacing, shape or sentence craft. Bring that piece to any conversation with a provider, because it converts a vague worry into a specific and priceable problem.

process.title: Ask the English department three factual questions
process.description: First-language 0500 or second-language 0510. Coursework portfolio or Paper 2. And whether the recent composition losses sat in the 24 content and structure marks or the 16 style and accuracy marks. All three are free, all three are answered quickly, and all three change what is worth buying.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson as the diagnostic
process.description: One hour, online, no card required, no obligation. Bring the timed composition and the most recent marked school paper. A specialist will say where the marks are going and what the cheapest route to recovering them is, in writing. Some families need no paid session after this, and we will say so when that is the case.

process.title: Decide the model, then the figure
process.description: Choose between technique sessions for the reading paper, marked redraft cycles for the composition, or a hybrid of both. Then fix the monthly number of sessions and marked pieces so the cost is known. Compare providers on cost per marked cycle rather than cost per hour, because in English those are different things.

process.title: Review on paired drafts at week eight
process.description: Compare a first draft and a rewrite of the same composition, both marked, eight weeks in. If the gap on the 24-and-16 split is real, the arrangement is working. If it is flat across three cycles, change the arrangement rather than buying more hours of the same thing.

whyPoints.title: The free options are listed before the paid ones
whyPoints.description: A timed composition at home, three questions to the English department and twenty minutes with the published criteria will tell a Sharjah family more than a first month of poorly aimed sessions. All three are free, and we would rather a family did them first and bought less than bought more and learned nothing.

whyPoints.title: Marking is specified, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Written work is marked against the published criteria on both parts of the composition split, with the lost marks named rather than the grammar corrected. What arrives, and how quickly, is agreed before the first paid session, because an unspecified marking promise is the commonest weakness in English arrangements at every price.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure is attributed
whyPoints.description: The bands on this page come from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, BartyED and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, each named next to its figure. None of them is an IB Gram price. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: A diagnostic session can be the only session
whyPoints.description: Some students need a plan rather than a programme: one hour to identify where the 24 structure marks and 16 accuracy marks are going, then a term of unsupervised practice. That is available as the free trial lesson, and we will tell a family when it is the right answer rather than selling a weekly hour.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Where a centre enters the coursework portfolio, the writing in that folder is the student's own. A tutor teaches, discusses and gives feedback; nobody here edits a folder to completion or dictates it. No Cambridge syllabus, past paper or mark scheme is supplied as a download either — those belong to the awarding body and the school already holds them.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that fits a Sharjah evening
whyPoints.description: One protected hour in Gulf Standard Time, late enough to survive a bus arriving after 16:30 from a Dubai campus and an evening that already contains Arabic and Islamic education homework. Sessions can move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. A slot that holds for a term is what makes a redraft cycle possible at all.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing we can do for 0500 that actually helps?
faqs.answer: Have the student write one composition at home under timed conditions, two hours, unsupported, from a past paper. It costs nothing and it distinguishes three problems that cost very different amounts to fix: running out of time, writing fluently without shape, or writing carefully with nothing happening in the piece. Then ask the English department whether the recent composition losses sat in the 24 content and structure marks or the 16 style and accuracy marks. Those two free steps decide what is worth buying, and plenty of Sharjah families find they need far less paid support than they assumed.

faqs.question: Are we paying for teaching time or for marking time in an English session?
faqs.answer: Both, in proportions that vary widely and are rarely stated. An hour that includes a properly marked composition involves the session plus thirty to forty minutes of close reading against the published criteria, done between sessions. Some providers price contact time only and mark nothing. Some absorb light marking, which usually means corrections rather than criteria-based assessment. Some charge per marked piece, which is the most transparent arrangement. Ask which model applies before paying, because in 0500 the marking is what moves the composition mark and it is the first thing a cheap plan stops doing.

faqs.question: What does an English tutor charge an hour in the Sharjah market?
faqs.answer: The published range is wide because supply is deep. Budget online rates start at roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from about AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. Qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE support from AED 150. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits run roughly AED 180 to 500 including travel. Those are the providers' and rate survey's own figures, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Is marking a composition worth paying for separately?
faqs.answer: For a student stuck in the middle of the range, it is often the best value purchase in the subject. A composition carries 40 marks split 24 for content and structure and 16 for style and accuracy, and a middling mark is usually leaking from the first of those rather than the second. Criteria-based marking identifies which, and a student who has seen that distinction on their own writing changes what they do. Buying marking by the piece also keeps the cost visible, which an hourly rate with unspecified marking does not. Compare providers on cost per marked cycle rather than cost per hour.

faqs.question: Why is English tutoring often cheaper than maths or physics in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Because supply is much deeper. Every Cambridge candidate in Sharjah sits an English qualification, every education graduate has studied the language, and the University City undergraduate population adds a large, willing, inexpensive pool. That pushes the entry price down, which is genuinely good for families. The cost is that English is the hardest subject in which to tell two tutors apart from a profile: someone excellent at reading technique and someone who can mark a composition against criteria look identical and often charge the same. Asking for a marked sample in the trial session is the only reliable filter.

faqs.question: Should we spend the budget on the reading paper or the writing paper?
faqs.answer: On whichever is losing the marks, and the two cost very different amounts. The reading paper responds to technique: the summary question settles in two or three sessions plus practice, comprehension responses improve once the question stem and mark allocation are read properly, and language analysis needs several short marked attempts. A modest budget goes a long way there and can taper after a term. The writing paper improves through marked redraft cycles, each of which needs real marking time, so the same money buys fewer but heavier interventions. Spending writing-paper money on reading-paper methods is the common error.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor who is not an English specialist a false economy for 0500?
faqs.answer: Not always, and it depends on the task. For timed reading practice, summary attempts, pacing and general comprehension work, a capable non-specialist at the budget band is reasonable value and many Sharjah families use exactly that. Where it fails is the composition. Marking 40 marks split 24 and 16 requires familiarity with the published criteria, and without it the feedback defaults to grammar correction, which addresses the smaller half of the mark scheme. If the composition mark is the problem, the cheap option will absorb months without moving it.

faqs.question: How many compositions does a 0500 candidate need marked, and what does that cost?
faqs.answer: Three to four full redraft cycles is where a middling mark usually starts to hold higher, and a cycle is four steps: a timed write, criteria-based marking, a rewrite of the same piece, and a second marking. Spread across a term that is a manageable commitment, and it is the part of the subject that money genuinely improves. The cost depends on the provider's model, which is why the comparison to make is cost per marked cycle rather than cost per hour. A provider who cannot quote per cycle is pricing contact time and calling it something else.

faqs.question: Does moving from 0500 to 0510 reduce what we need to spend?
faqs.answer: It can change the problem entirely, but it is not a family decision. English as a Second Language 0510 is a separate Cambridge qualification with different papers and demands, and the entry choice belongs to the school, normally made on evidence from the student's written work. The budget consequence is real in both directions: a first-language candidate whose written English is at second-language level can absorb a weekly specialist hour for a year without the mark moving. What a tutor can contribute is a composition marked against the 0500 criteria, which shows the school whether the losses are structural or linguistic.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a single diagnostic session and nothing more?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some students that is the right purchase. One hour with the student's own timed composition and most recent marked school paper is usually enough for a specialist to say where the marks are going and what the cheapest route to recovering them is, in writing. The family then executes the plan without further paid hours. That session is available here as the free trial lesson, one hour, online, with no card required and no obligation. A provider who will not tell you when you need nothing further is not worth the fee.

faqs.question: Does a small group bring the cost of English support down?
faqs.answer: For the reading paper, often yes. Summary technique, comprehension questioning and timed practice work reasonably with two to four students, and the per-student rate falls meaningfully. For the composition, it rarely works, because the component improves through individual marking of individual writing and a group session cannot deliver that. The practical compromise some Sharjah families reach is group work for reading technique and individually marked pieces for the composition, which keeps the total down without hollowing out the part that actually moves the mark.

faqs.question: What does an in-home English tutor in Sharjah add to the hourly figure?
faqs.answer: Published in-home one-to-one rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online hour. The premium is largely movement. For English there is a specific reason to think hard about it: the component that moves the grade is the marking, and marking happens between sessions wherever the tutor is. A travel premium buys attendance, not better marking. In Al Khan or Al Nahda it also buys a late start, because a session booked for 17:00 in Dubai-bound traffic frequently begins at 17:25 and is billed from 17:00.

faqs.question: Are English sessions priced per sixty minutes or per piece of work?
faqs.answer: Both conventions exist in this market, which makes advertised rates hard to compare. A session may be 45, 50, 60 or 90 minutes, and a monthly package quoting a number of sessions says nothing until the length is stated. Separately, marking may be inside the hourly fee, charged per piece, or absent. Before comparing two quotes, get the session length and the marking arrangement in writing and convert both to a cost per sixty minutes and a cost per marked cycle. This is the single most common reason a cheaper-looking English package turns out to be dearer.

faqs.question: Our budget is AED 500 a month. What is the best use of it for 0500?
faqs.answer: Start with the free steps, because they change the answer. If the reading paper is the weak side, AED 500 a month buys enough technique work to settle the summary question and the comprehension responses within a term, after which the spend can taper. If the composition is the weak side, the same money is better spent on fewer sessions with marked redraft cycles than on more contact hours with nothing marked. If both papers are adequate and the mark is simply stuck, spend nothing beyond one diagnostic session and execute the plan at home. That is a genuine recommendation, not a modest one.

faqs.question: Does the coursework portfolio route cost less to support than sitting Paper 2?
faqs.answer: It usually costs less in paid hours, for a reason families should understand before treating it as a saving. Where a centre enters the coursework portfolio in place of Paper 2, the assessed writing is produced over time under the school's supervision and must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach technique, discuss approaches and give general feedback, but may not edit a folder to completion or dictate it — that limit is set by the awarding body, and breaching it puts the student at risk. So the legitimate support is narrower, and therefore cheaper, than preparation for a timed paper.

faqs.question: Does paying for English tutoring help with UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Tutoring is not part of the equivalency process and nothing here should suggest it is required for it. The British-track rule asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade; Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. English is ordinarily one of the five a candidate presents, so the grade matters. Equivalency itself is administered by the Ministry, and the requirements should be verified on moe.gov.ae rather than taken from any tutoring page.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-english-first-la.closingHeading: Do the free steps first, then decide what to buy
sharjah/cambridge-igcse-english-first-la.closingBody: If you are weighing up English support for a Year 10 or Year 11 student in Sharjah, spend nothing for a week. Have your child write one timed composition at home, ask the English department whether the losses sit in the 24 content and structure marks or the 16 style and accuracy marks, and read the published criteria together. Then bring that composition to a free trial lesson, one hour online with no card required, and a specialist will tell you what is worth paying for and what is not. Lessons run online, one to one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

intro.heading: A 0580 grade is a stack of marked papers, so start by reading one properly
paragraphs: Almost every conversation about Cambridge IGCSE mathematics starts in the wrong place. A parent says their child is weak at maths, or is predicted a 6 and needs an 8, and a tutor is hired on that description. The description is not evidence. The evidence is the marked paper, and a marked 0580 paper is unusually informative because Cambridge mark schemes are explicit about why each mark was awarded or withheld. Learning to read one takes a parent about twenty minutes and changes what they buy.

So this page is built around the paper rather than around the syllabus. It covers what the entry code on your child's statement actually commits them to, how to dissect a mock question by question, what the mark-scheme codes mean and what each one is worth, which topics leak marks in this cohort, and how many past papers a candidate should have properly marked before a session. A Cambridge IGCSE Maths 0580 Tutor in Sharjah who cannot do that reading with you is selling hours rather than marks.

The reason this matters more at IGCSE than earlier is that 0580 marks are recoverable in identifiable blocks. A student who loses eleven marks across a paper has usually lost them in three or four recognisable ways: method abandoned halfway, accuracy thrown away by premature rounding, a question left because the command word was misread, and arithmetic errors concentrated in the non-calculator paper. Each of those has a different repair, and only one of them is about understanding mathematics.

Sharjah adds two local variables. The first is which board a school actually uses: 0580 is Cambridge, and a sizeable number of campuses in this emirate enter candidates for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE instead, which has different papers, different mark-scheme conventions and different timetables. Families comparing notes across schools regularly compare incompatible things. The second is the Cambridge zone system, which sets different timetable versions by region and has a consequence most parents have never been told about.

One operational point. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visits in Sharjah are not a service we sell at all; our in-home offering exists only in India. For 0580 this is more suitable than it sounds: a marked paper is a document, and the natural way to work through one is both people looking at the same scan on screen, annotating as they go, with a record of what was agreed at the end of the hour.

Nothing here promises a grade or quotes a price of ours. Every dirham figure further down is a published market rate attributed to whoever published it, and every Cambridge date is given with its source so a Sharjah parent can check it against the official timetable before anybody is paid.

A parent who hires a tutor for 0580 when the school enters 4MA1 has bought the wrong mark scheme, and the mark-scheme conventions are a meaningful part of what is being taught.

programmes.description: The stage feeding IGCSE, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. Those tests are diagnostic rather than certificating, and they are the earliest formal signal of whether a student is heading towards a Core or an Extended entry two years later.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-maths-0580-tutor.subjectsIntro: The 0580 syllabus is organised into nine content areas, examined across both papers at both tiers with the Extended tier going further in each. The notes below say what each area is and where its marks are usually lost.

subjects.name: Number
subjects.description: Integers, fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form, bounds and limits of accuracy. Upper and lower bounds are the quiet killer here: students who can calculate perfectly lose whole questions because they never learned to handle a measurement given to the nearest centimetre.

subjects.name: Algebra and graphs
subjects.description: Manipulation, equations, inequalities, sequences, functions and graph sketching, with the Extended tier reaching harder rearrangement and more demanding graph work. The largest single source of recoverable method marks on the calculator paper.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry
subjects.description: Gradients, midpoints, equations of straight lines and parallel or perpendicular conditions. Short questions with full marks available to anyone fluent in the formulae, and a reliable place to pick up marks quickly in a short intervention.

subjects.name: Geometry
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, polygons, circle properties, congruence and similarity, and constructions. Reason-giving is the issue: an angle found without the stated reason loses the accuracy mark even when the number is right.

subjects.name: Mensuration
subjects.description: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume, including compound shapes and parts of circles. Losses are almost always unit errors or premature rounding carried through a multi-step calculation rather than a failure to know the formula.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry and Pythagoras at both tiers, with the sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle and three-dimensional work on the Extended tier. Bearings questions sit here and are the single most commonly abandoned question type in the paper.

subjects.name: Transformations and vectors
subjects.description: Reflection, rotation, translation and enlargement, with vector work and combined transformations on the Extended tier. Marks go missing on description: students perform the transformation correctly and then fail to state the centre, the scale factor or the mirror line.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree diagrams and, at Extended, conditional probability. A topic where a well-drawn tree diagram earns method marks even when the final arithmetic goes wrong, so it rewards disciplined presentation directly.

subjects.name: Statistics
subjects.description: Collection, representation, averages, cumulative frequency and histograms. Histograms with unequal class widths are the recurring trap, and cumulative frequency questions are usually worth more marks than students expect for the work involved.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.levels: Examined on one of the two papers
subjects.description: Not a syllabus area but the skill one whole paper assumes: long multiplication and division, fraction arithmetic, surd and index manipulation, and estimation. A calculator-raised student can be mathematically able and still lose a grade here.

sections.heading: What the entry code on your child's statement actually commits them to
paragraphs: Before any teaching, establish four facts in writing from the school: the syllabus code, the tier, the series and the papers. The code matters because 0580 is Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics and the mark-scheme conventions taught alongside it are Cambridge's. A school entering candidates for a Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is using a different specification with different papers and a different style of mark scheme, and a tutor hired for the wrong one will teach good mathematics and the wrong exam technique.

The tier matters more than almost anything else on this page. 0580 is entered at Core or at Extended, and the two are different entries sitting different papers with different attainable grade ranges. This is not a difficulty setting applied on the day. It determines which papers arrive in the examination hall, and it is confirmed by the school months before the series. A parent who has not asked which tier their child is entered for does not yet know what grade is available to them.

The paper structure is straightforward once the tier is known: a candidate sits two written papers, each carrying 50% of the grade, and one of the two is sat without a calculator. Durations and total marks differ by tier, and Cambridge has revised this syllabus in recent years, so confirm the current structure against the 0580 syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org rather than against an older past-paper pack or a sibling's memory of it.

The series matters for planning. Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Most Sharjah candidates sit June. A November entry is a genuine option for a retake or for a candidate who needs another six months, and it is worth knowing it exists before a disappointing June result rather than afterwards.

sections.heading: The first session dissects a marked paper, question by question
paragraphs: A first session spent teaching is a first session wasted. What a 0580 candidate needs at the start is an audit, and the material for it already exists in the form of a marked mock. The method is mechanical. Go through the paper question by question. For each question record the marks available, the marks awarded, and then the single most useful piece of information: the type of loss. Not the topic. The type.

Four loss types cover the overwhelming majority of 0580 marks. Method abandoned, where a student started correctly and stopped before the mark scheme would have paid out. Accuracy thrown away, where the method was right and the answer was wrong through rounding, units or transcription. Omission, where the question was left blank or half-attempted because the command word or the context was misread. And arithmetic, where the mathematics was understood and the calculation failed, concentrated almost entirely on the non-calculator paper.

The audit produces a number that parents find clarifying: the recoverable mark count. Add up the marks lost to accuracy, omission and arithmetic, and you have the marks available without the student learning any new mathematics at all. On a typical mid-range 0580 paper that figure is often larger than the marks lost to genuine gaps in understanding, which is why so many candidates move a grade within a term while their teacher reports no change in ability.

There is a secondary output worth asking any tutor for. A per-question timing estimate, reconstructed with the student: which questions took too long, and whether the marks abandoned at the end of the paper were abandoned for lack of knowledge or lack of clock. Those are completely different problems with completely different fixes, and a paper read without that distinction will send a term's work in the wrong direction.

sections.heading: Mark-scheme literacy: M1, A1, B1 and the conventions nobody explains
paragraphs: Cambridge mark schemes are written in a compact notation, and a student who cannot read it is working blind. M1 is a method mark, awarded for a correct approach whether or not the final answer is right. A1 is an accuracy mark, usually dependent on the method mark before it. B1 is an independent mark, awarded for a correct statement or value on its own terms. These three account for most of the marks on a 0580 paper, and the distinction between them is the whole argument for showing working.

Then the conventions. FT means follow-through: a later answer can still earn marks even when an earlier value was wrong, provided the subsequent method is correct — which means a student who abandons a question after noticing a mistake is throwing away marks that were still available. SC is a special case allowance. The abbreviation 'oe' means or equivalent, so a correct answer in a different acceptable form still scores. 'cao' means correct answer only, with no method marks available. 'isw' means ignore subsequent working, so a correct answer followed by an incorrect simplification is not always penalised.

Teaching this to the student rather than to the parent is the point. A 15-year-old who understands that M1 exists will stop writing bare answers. One who understands follow-through will stop crossing out an entire question because the first line was wrong. One who understands 'cao' will know which questions demand a check and which do not. This is twenty minutes of instruction with a measurable effect on the next paper, and most candidates never receive it.

The practical exercise is to re-mark one of the student's own papers together against the published mark scheme, with the student doing the marking. They discover how generous method marks are and how little working they had been showing. That exercise changes behaviour faster than being told to show working, because the student has just watched themselves give marks away in their own handwriting.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: a tier decision made from marks, not from a feeling
paragraphs: The tier decision is the highest-stakes judgement in the whole course, and it is often made on an impression. Core and Extended are different entries with different papers and different attainable grade ranges, and the practical consequence is that a Core entry closes the straightforward route into A Level mathematics. That makes it a decision about the student's next three years, not about which paper feels more comfortable in Year 10.

The evidence that should drive it is a set of marked papers at both tiers, not one mock and a conversation. Sit the student on a past Extended paper and a past Core paper, mark both properly, and look at the shape of the losses rather than the totals. A student scoring modestly on Extended but with most losses in accuracy and arithmetic is an Extended candidate who needs technique work. A student whose Extended losses are concentrated in whole topics they have never met is a different case.

Two patterns justify Core, and they are worth stating honestly because the pressure usually runs the other way. The first is a student who, on marked evidence, cannot access a substantial share of Extended content with the time remaining, for whom an excellent Core result is better than a poor Extended one. The second is a student whose post-16 route genuinely does not require A Level mathematics, where the opportunity cost of two years of struggle is real.

What does not justify a tier decision is a predicted grade with no paper behind it, a comparison with a sibling, or a general sense that the student is 'not a maths person'. Ask the school three questions: which tier is my child currently entered for, when is the entry confirmed, and which marked papers support that decision. If the answer to the third is that there are none, that is the thing to fix before anything else, and it costs nothing but a weekend.

sections.heading: Four leaks that recur across Sharjah 0580 papers
paragraphs: Across marked papers from this emirate the same four losses appear with unusual regularity, and all four are cheap to close relative to what they cost. The first is bearings. Trigonometry questions set as bearings are the most commonly abandoned question type in the paper, not because the trigonometry is hard but because students do not have a reliable routine for converting a bearing into a labelled triangle. Twenty minutes on that routine, then four practice questions, usually ends it.

The second is upper and lower bounds. A measurement given to the nearest centimetre, or a value rounded to two significant figures, carries a range, and questions built on that range are worth full marks to a student who has been taught the convention and are worth nothing to one who has not. It is a single short topic in the Number area and it recurs in mensuration and in algebra, so the losses are spread across the paper and easy to miss in a topic-by-topic review.

The third is transformation description. Students perform a reflection, rotation or enlargement correctly and then lose the marks for describing it, because they state the transformation without the mirror line, the centre and angle, or the scale factor and centre. The mark scheme wants all components. This is pure notation discipline, it has nothing to do with mathematical ability, and it is one of the fastest repairs available in the whole syllabus.

The fourth is premature rounding carried through a multi-step calculation, which is where accuracy marks go to die in mensuration and trigonometry. A student rounds an intermediate value to two decimal places, carries it forward, and arrives at a final answer outside the accepted range. The fix is a rule the student applies without thinking: keep full precision in the calculator, round only at the end, and state the rounding used. Each of these four appears in the table in the costing section further down as a line item, because each one has a measurable mark value.

sections.heading: Counting past papers: how many, marked by whom, and what the numbers should do
paragraphs: Past papers are the most-recommended and least-well-used resource in IGCSE mathematics. Students complete them, check answers against a mark scheme, note a score and move on. That produces a sequence of numbers with no diagnostic value, because nobody recorded why the marks were lost. A paper worth doing is a paper that is marked properly, categorised by loss type, and compared against the previous one on the same categories.

The quantity question has a reasonable answer. A candidate sitting a June series should have a handful of full papers properly marked by the end of the autumn term, a steady rhythm of one every week or two through the spring, and the last several sat strictly to time. What matters more than the count is whether the loss profile is changing: arithmetic losses should fall after non-calculator work, omission losses should fall after timing work, and method losses should fall as topics are repaired.

Who marks them matters too. Self-marking against a mark scheme is useful for arithmetic and useless for method, because a student who did not show working will award themselves a mark the examiner would not. Parent-marking has the same problem. The productive arrangement is that the student marks their own paper first, then a tutor re-marks the disputed questions, and the difference between the two marks is itself the lesson.

Two warnings. First, doing papers from the wrong tier flatters or crushes a student for no reason, so check the tier on every paper used. Second, a paper sat without timing measures knowledge and not performance, and the gap between the two is where most candidates lose a grade. A student who scores well untimed and badly to time has a clock problem, and no amount of additional topic teaching will touch it.

sections.heading: Cambridge sessions, zones, and the entry deadline nobody mentions
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. That much most families know. What almost nobody has been told is that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable.

For a Sharjah family that is a specific, actionable risk rather than an abstraction. A parent who downloads a timetable from a search result, or who takes a date from a cousin in another country, may be reading the wrong zone's version. The fix is free: ask the school's examinations officer for the timetable version that applies to their centre, in writing, and work from that document alone. This single question is probably the highest-value thing on this page.

The second thing families underestimate is how early entries close, and the cleanest way to see it is as the choice between the two series a Sharjah candidate can sit. June is the main sitting: entries for it close in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper, on a date the centre prints on the statement of entry, with forecast grades following weeks before the papers, results on Direct in August and certificates after that. November is the resit route, and its entry closes in the preceding months on the same pattern. So a November retake is not a decision taken after a June result has been digested; it is taken within weeks of it. Families who only learn that in September have already lost the option.

Apply that shape to your own series and the planning consequence is obvious: a tier change, a retake decision or a private-candidate entry has to be made months before the examination, not in the term before it. For comparison, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official document rather than a restated date. Separately, private schools in this emirate are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves fees, curricula and assessment methods at school level but sets none of these board dates.

sections.heading: What 0580 support costs in Sharjah, priced against recoverable marks
paragraphs: Published rates in this market start low. Online tutoring from a university student is advertised from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya, which places the budget tier roughly between AED 45 and 150 an hour. For 0580 that tier is a more reasonable gamble than it is for a Diploma subject, because the content is well documented and a strong mathematics undergraduate can teach much of it. What they usually cannot teach is mark-scheme behaviour, and that is where the recoverable marks are.

Above that, a qualified subject teacher working online runs about AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist sits at AED 200 to 450 or more, where TutorChase quotes AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaches AED 450 and beyond. At the top, premium named tutors are published at AED 650 by BartyED. In-home visits are separately quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors.

Judge any of those against the audit rather than against each other. If a paper dissection shows eleven marks lost to accuracy, omission and arithmetic, the question is how many hours it takes to close those three loss types and what that costs. Four targeted hours at a mid-band rate is a smaller number than most families expect, and it is a very different proposition from an open-ended weekly commitment across two years at the same rate. Monthly, published figures run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Every figure in this section is a published market rate attributed to whoever published it, and none of them is an IB Gram price list. Three of six ranking pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Sharjah family transacts in. Our own number comes from the consultation after a free trial lesson, once there is an audit to price against.

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes, and what we will not send you
paragraphs: A request we receive regularly and decline: please send us the 0580 past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables. We do not supply them, and neither should anyone else. Those documents are Cambridge International's copyright material. The right approach is to reference them, cite the official source and link to it, and to work from material the school has legitimately issued or that is published on cambridgeinternational.org. A provider who emails you a folder of papers has told you something about how they treat other rules too.

What a tutor can legitimately do with past material is substantial. Work through a question with the student. Explain how the published mark scheme awards marks on that question. Set the student a question type and mark their attempt. Show them how to find the official syllabus and the specimen materials themselves. None of that requires redistributing a document, and the last one is more useful than the folder, because a student who can navigate the official site keeps that skill after the tutoring stops.

The same boundary applies to the work itself. 0580 is examined by written paper, so the honesty risks are narrower than in a coursework subject, but they are not zero: a mock sat at home, a timed paper completed with help, or a practice paper done with a calculator on the non-calculator paper all produce a number that misleads the people making the tier decision. If a mock is going to inform an entry, it has to be sat honestly, and that is worth saying to the student rather than assuming.

Finally, two things nobody should promise about this syllabus. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any provider attaching a number to an outcome is making a claim they cannot stand behind. And no tutor has access to grade boundaries before they are published, to unreleased papers, or to marking in progress; anyone implying otherwise is either mistaken or selling something that does not exist. What is honestly available is the audit, the repair and the practice, which on the evidence of most marked papers is already worth a grade.

process.title: Confirm the code, the tier and the series
process.description: Ask the school in writing whether mathematics is entered as Cambridge 0580 or a Pearson equivalent, which tier the student is entered for, which series, and the timetable version that applies to the centre's zone. All four are free and all four change the plan.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: A single marked mock with the examiner's or teacher's annotations intact is worth more than any description of how the term is going. Send the paper rather than the grade, and send it before the first session rather than bringing it to one.

process.title: Free first lesson spent on the audit
process.description: The first session costs nothing, takes no card details and is taught by the tutor who would continue. It works through the paper question by question and ends with a loss-type list and a recoverable mark count, both in writing.

process.title: Repair the loss types, then re-test
process.description: Short blocks aimed at the loss types the audit named, followed by a fresh paper to confirm the leak closed. Topics come from the student's own papers rather than from a generic running order, which is why the audit comes first.

process.title: Timed papers, logged, before the series
process.description: Full papers sat to time in the weeks before the examination, marked against the published mark scheme, with the timing recorded alongside the mark. We will tell you when the loss profile has flattened and further sessions are not buying anything.

whyPoints.title: The audit comes before the teaching
whyPoints.description: A first session spent teaching is a first session wasted. Reading one marked paper question by question produces a loss-type list and a recoverable mark count, and those two outputs decide what the next ten hours should actually do.

whyPoints.title: Mark-scheme literacy taught to the student
whyPoints.description: M1, A1, B1, follow-through, 'oe' and 'cao' are twenty minutes of instruction with a measurable effect on the next paper. Most candidates never receive it, which is why so many write bare answers to multi-mark questions.

whyPoints.title: The board checked before anything is bought
whyPoints.description: Sharjah campuses enter candidates for Cambridge and for Pearson side by side, sometimes on neighbouring streets. A tutor hired for 0580 when the school enters a Pearson specification teaches the wrong exam technique with the right mathematics.

whyPoints.title: The zone timetable question asked out loud
whyPoints.description: Every Cambridge centre sits in one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the examinations officer for the version that applies to your centre.

whyPoints.description: We do not send past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They are Cambridge International's copyright material. We cite the official source, work from what the school has issued, and teach the student to navigate the syllabus site themselves.

faqs.question: What do the mark codes M1, A1 and B1 mean on a 0580 mark scheme?
faqs.answer: M1 is a method mark for a correct approach, awarded whether or not the final answer is right. A1 is an accuracy mark, usually dependent on the method mark before it, for the correct value correctly rounded. B1 is an independent mark for a correct statement or value on its own terms. Between them they account for most marks on the paper, and the distinction is the whole argument for showing working. A student who writes a bare answer to a multi-mark question forfeits the method marks even when the answer is correct.

faqs.question: Which two 0580 papers will my child sit in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: That depends on the tier the school has entered them for. A 0580 candidate sits two written papers, each carrying 50% of the grade, and one of the two is sat without a calculator. Durations and total marks differ between the Core and Extended entries, and Cambridge has revised this syllabus in recent years, so confirm the current structure against the 0580 syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org rather than from an older past-paper pack. Ask the school which tier your child is entered for and on what evidence.

faqs.question: How do I read my child's 0580 mock paper properly?
faqs.answer: Go through it question by question and record three things per question: marks available, marks awarded, and the type of loss. The type matters more than the topic. Four types cover most of it: method abandoned before the mark scheme paid out, accuracy thrown away through rounding or units, omission because the question was misread or left, and arithmetic errors concentrated on the non-calculator paper. Add up the last three and you have the recoverable mark count — marks available without learning any new mathematics.

faqs.question: How many marks is my child losing to arithmetic on 0580 Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Only a marked paper answers that, which is exactly why the audit comes first. What is predictable is where those losses concentrate: the non-calculator paper, in long multiplication and division, fraction arithmetic, index and surd manipulation, and estimation. A calculator-raised student can be genuinely able at mathematics and still lose a grade there. The repair is deliberate non-calculator practice rather than more topic teaching, and the log should show arithmetic losses falling within two or three papers once that practice starts.

faqs.question: Can a 0580 grade move from a 5 to a 7 in twelve weeks?
faqs.answer: Nobody honest will guarantee it, and anyone attaching a number to an outcome is making a claim they cannot stand behind. What can be said is what the evidence shows. If a marked paper reveals a large recoverable mark count — losses to accuracy, omission and arithmetic rather than to whole unlearned topics — then twelve weeks of targeted work on those loss types plus timed practice has a realistic chance. If the losses are concentrated in content never taught, twelve weeks is a different and harder proposition, and we will say so.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered for Core or Extended 0580?
faqs.answer: Decide it from marked papers at both tiers rather than from an impression. Core and Extended are different entries with different papers and different attainable grade ranges, and a Core entry closes the straightforward route into A Level mathematics. Sit a past paper at each tier, mark both properly and look at the shape of the losses. Mostly accuracy and arithmetic on Extended means an Extended candidate needing technique work. Whole topics never met means a different case. Ask the school which marked papers support their recommendation.

faqs.question: How much does Cambridge IGCSE 0580 tutoring cost in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject teacher online is about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Price any of those against the recoverable mark count rather than against each other.

faqs.question: Which 0580 topics do Sharjah students lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: Four recur with unusual regularity in marked papers from this emirate. Bearings, which are the most commonly abandoned question type, usually because the student has no routine for turning a bearing into a labelled triangle. Upper and lower bounds, where rounded data carries a range the student was never taught to handle. Transformation description, where the transformation is performed correctly and the mirror line, centre, angle or scale factor is omitted. And premature rounding carried through multi-step mensuration and trigonometry. All four are cheap repairs relative to their cost.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone timetable and why does it matter in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential to use the correct version of the examination timetable for the zone. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A parent who downloads a timetable from a search result, or takes a date from a relative in another country, may be reading the wrong version. Ask your school's examinations officer for the timetable version that applies to the centre, in writing.

faqs.question: When are the Cambridge IGCSE maths entry deadlines?
faqs.answer: Months before the examination. For the June series that most candidates here sit, entries close in the spring, forecast grades go in weeks before the papers, results reach Direct in August and certificates follow. The November series, the normal resit route, closes its entries in the preceding months on the same pattern. The February and March series belongs to India and is not a session a UAE centre enters, so disregard any timetable that quotes it. Apply that shape to your own series: a tier change, a retake or a private-candidate entry has to be decided well in advance, and the centre's examinations officer holds the real dates.

faqs.question: Does SPEA decide which exam board my child's Sharjah school uses?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods at school level. The specific board entry for a subject is the school's own operational decision within that framework, and the examination dates, mark schemes and grade boundaries are set by Cambridge International or Pearson, not by any UAE regulator. Ask the school directly which specification mathematics is entered under.

faqs.question: Will you send us 0580 past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and nor should anyone else. Past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are Cambridge International's copyright material, and redistributing them is not something a legitimate provider does. What a tutor can do is work through a question with your child, explain how the published mark scheme awards marks on it, mark their attempt at a question type, and teach them to find the official syllabus and specimen materials themselves. A provider who emails you a folder has told you how they treat other rules.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 0580 and 0980?
faqs.answer: They are closely related Cambridge IGCSE mathematics syllabuses that differ in the grading scale reported, with 0580 reporting letter grades and 0980 reporting a numeric scale. The mathematics assessed is substantially the same, which is why a tutor who knows one can teach the other, but the entry code on the school's statement is what determines the papers sat and the grades reported. Check which code your child is entered for before buying any tutoring, and check the tier at the same time, because the tier matters more.

faqs.question: How many 0580 past papers should my child have marked before the exam?
faqs.answer: Count matters less than the trend. A reasonable rhythm for a June candidate is a handful of full papers properly marked by the end of the autumn term, one every week or two through the spring, and the last several sat strictly to time. What matters is whether the loss profile is changing: arithmetic losses falling after non-calculator work, omission losses falling after timed practice, method losses falling as topics are repaired. A sequence of scores with no loss categories recorded has no diagnostic value at all.

faqs.question: Is 0580 enough for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Mathematics is one subject within a wider requirement, and the published British-track rule asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which does not match the source. Verify the current requirement on the ministry's own channel; IB Gram does not perform equivalency.

Each profile shows the boards and levels covered and the slots open in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Why a student who understands physics still loses 0625 marks
paragraphs: There is a particular kind of 0625 report that brings a Sharjah parent to a page like this. The physics teacher says the student is engaged, asks good questions and can explain ideas aloud. The mock paper comes back at a grade D. Nothing in those two statements is contradictory, and the reason is specific to how Cambridge physics is assessed: a large share of the marks are awarded for the form of an answer rather than for the understanding behind it. A student can know why a resultant force produces acceleration and still score one mark out of four on a question about it.

This page works through that gap component by component. Cambridge 0625 is assessed in three papers for any one candidate. There is a multiple-choice paper — Paper 1 at Core, Paper 2 at Extended — of 45 minutes and 40 marks, carrying 30% of the grade. There is a theory paper, Paper 3 at Core or Paper 4 at Extended, of one hour fifteen minutes and 80 marks, carrying 50%. And there is a practical component worth 20%: either Paper 5, the practical test, taken in a laboratory, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, written on paper. Which of those your child sits is a decision made by the school, and the examinations officer at the campus is the only reliable source for it.

The syllabus itself divides into six topic areas: motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics. Those are not equal in difficulty or in the marks they quietly cost. Electricity and magnetism is where most Sharjah candidates lose the largest block, partly because circuit reasoning has to be done in a specific order and partly because the magnetism half of the area is often taught last and revised least. Motion and forces is where the long theory paper usually opens, which means a student who is shaky there starts the paper badly and loses time as well as marks.

What a session fixes depends entirely on which of those two problems is present. A student who cannot calculate is a different student from one who calculates correctly and then writes an explanation that earns nothing. The first needs technique and repetition. The second needs to be shown, on their own marked script, that the mark scheme was looking for a change in one quantity and a consequence in another, and that a paragraph about the general idea collects neither. That second conversation takes one session and frequently moves a grade boundary's worth of marks, which is why we ask for the marked mock before anything else.

Sharjah shapes the practical side of this more than parents expect. A significant number of households in Al Nahda, Al Khan and Al Majaz send children to Dubai campuses, so the school is under KHDA rather than SPEA and may enter a different practical component from a Sharjah centre a few kilometres away. Lessons here are delivered online, one to one, over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, which are a service we provide only in India. For a practical paper taught from a candidate's own written scripts, that distinction changes the logistics and not the teaching.
