sharjah/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tut.programmesIntro: Cambridge physics sits inside a sequence, and where a Sharjah student is in that sequence changes what a session should contain. These are the stages this page connects.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics
programmes.description: Separate-sciences physics, assessed in three papers: a 45-minute multiple-choice paper worth 30%, a one-hour-fifteen theory paper worth 50%, and a practical component worth 20% taken either as the laboratory practical test or as the written alternative to practical. Content is organised into motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics.
programmes.countryNote: Most Sharjah candidates meet it as one of three separate sciences in Years 10 and 11. Whether a campus enters the practical test or the written alternative varies between schools in the same emirate, and it changes what the last eight weeks of preparation should look like.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Science
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course, where forces, energy, circuits and waves are met for the first time without the mathematical treatment 0625 adds. Checkpoint tests are available in March, May and October. The habits that matter later are formed here: drawing a diagram rather than describing one, and recording a unit with every number.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 is the cheapest point at which to fix the arithmetic that later presents as a physics problem — unit prefixes, rearranging a formula, reading a scale. Sharjah families who do that work early spend far less in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge AS and A Level Physics 9702
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation. It assumes the 0625 Extended treatment of motion, energy, waves and electricity and then adds vectors resolved properly, uncertainty analysis and a far heavier algebraic load. The step is in the mathematics and in the expected precision of written explanation rather than in the physics ideas themselves.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah students moving into Year 12 either locally or at a Dubai campus feel the gap most in the practical write-up and in significant-figure discipline. A 0625 candidate who has been marked properly on Paper 6 style questions arrives better prepared than a grade alone suggests.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Physics
programmes.description: The other common Year 12 destination, taken at Standard or Higher Level. Content overlaps substantially with 0625 Extended at the start, but the assessment is different in kind: command terms are defined by the IB, and there is an internal investigation with no Cambridge equivalent that the student designs and writes themselves.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah families switch to a Dubai Diploma campus after Year 11. The physics transfers; the writing conventions do not. One honest conversation about command terms before Year 12 starts saves a term of confusion.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tut.subjectsIntro: 0625 is six topic areas, and each one loses marks in its own way. This is what a tutor is actually looking at when a marked paper arrives, ordered by how much of the grade is usually at stake.

subjects.name: Electricity: circuits, resistance and the potential divider
subjects.description: The largest single mark block for most candidates. Series and parallel reasoning has to be performed in a fixed order — total resistance, then current, then potential difference across each component — and students who work out of order get plausible wrong answers. The potential divider question is a reliable loss at Extended.

subjects.name: Magnetism and electromagnetism
subjects.description: Field patterns, the motor effect, electromagnetic induction and the transformer. Often taught late in Year 11 and revised least. Marks here are won by stating a cause and a consequence in separate clauses; students who describe the apparatus instead of the effect score nothing despite understanding it.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and energy
subjects.description: Speed, velocity, acceleration, graphs of motion, resultant force, momentum at Extended, work, power and efficiency. Typically where the long theory paper opens, so weakness here costs time as well as marks. The free-body diagram is the specific skill: forces drawn from a point, labelled with a name rather than a letter.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Particle models, thermal expansion, specific heat capacity, latent heat, conduction, convection and radiation. The written explanations here are the most formulaic in the syllabus, which is good news: a student who learns the particle-level sentence structure for each process can convert this area from a weakness into reliable marks in two sessions.

subjects.name: Waves: general properties, light and sound
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, dispersion, total internal reflection, lenses, the electromagnetic spectrum and sound. Distinctive because a substantial number of marks are awarded for a drawing: ray lines with arrows, normals dashed and at right angles, angles measured from the normal rather than the surface.

subjects.name: Nuclear physics
subjects.description: Atomic structure, isotopes, the three radiation types and their properties, half-life and safety. A short area with an unusually high ratio of marks to content, and therefore the best return on revision time late in the course. Half-life questions are mechanical once the pattern is seen.

subjects.name: Space physics
subjects.description: The solar system, orbits, stellar life cycles and redshift. Frequently the last area taught and the first abandoned in revision, which is a mistake: the questions are descriptive, the content is finite, and the marks are among the easiest in the paper to secure in a single session.

subjects.name: Practical skills for Paper 5 and Paper 6
subjects.description: Reading instruments, tabulating with units in the heading, plotting, drawing a line of best fit, identifying an anomaly and suggesting an improvement. Assessed either in a laboratory as the practical test or on paper as the alternative to practical, and in both cases the marks follow the recording conventions as much as the experiment.

subjects.name: Equations: recalled against supplied
subjects.description: The syllabus specifies which relationships a candidate must recall and which are provided in the paper. Students who assume everything is given lose calculation marks they could have scored, and students who memorise the supplied list waste revision time. Checking that split against the current syllabus is a ten-minute job with a long payoff.

subjects.name: Units, prefixes and the arithmetic inside physics
subjects.description: Converting between milli, kilo and mega, rearranging a relationship before substituting, and giving an answer to a sensible precision. Not physics content, but responsible for a steady drip of lost marks across every topic area, and usually fixable alongside the physics rather than in separate maths sessions.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tut.regionsIntro: Where a Sharjah family lives changes which school their child attends, which practical component that school enters, and what time a weekday session can realistically start. These are the communities this page is written for.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: On the Dubai boundary, with a high proportion of children at Dubai campuses under KHDA rather than SPEA. Those schools may enter a different 0625 practical component from a Sharjah centre, which is worth confirming before planning the final eight weeks.

regions.name: Al Majaz and Al Qasba
regions.note: Central Sharjah with a dense cluster of British-curriculum campuses. Separate sciences are widely offered here, so physics-specific support is more often about the theory paper's written answers than about whether the subject is taught at all.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Home to several Cambridge centres and a settled Year 10 and 11 population. A common pattern locally is a strong mathematician scoring poorly in physics, which is almost always an explanation-writing problem rather than a numerical one.

regions.name: University City and Al Nouf
regions.note: Close to the higher-education cluster, where families are often already planning towards AS and A Level Physics 9702. That makes the practical-skills component worth more attention in Year 11 than its 20% weighting suggests.

regions.name: Al Khan and Al Taawun
regions.note: Coastal and heavily committed to the Dubai commute. Evening traffic means a session scheduled for 17:00 is a session that begins late; online delivery is what makes a 18:00 physics hour hold for a whole term here.

regions.name: Aljada and Al Zahia
regions.note: Newer communities with a younger school-age population, so the 0625 cohort is still small. Families here benefit most from early work in Year 9 and Year 10 on units and formula rearrangement, before the physics gets mathematical.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan, Kalba and Dibba Al Hisn
regions.note: The east-coast exclaves under SPEA, hours from the city schools and effectively outside any local market for separate-sciences physics support. Teaching over live video is the only arrangement here that survives a full academic year.

sections.heading: Three things to settle before a single 0625 session is booked
paragraphs: Physics tutoring that starts from a general sense that the subject is going badly tends to spend its first month finding out what the problem was. Three pieces of information remove that month, and all three are available to a Sharjah parent within a day.

The first is which papers the child is entered for. Cambridge 0625 is tiered: a Core candidate sits the Core multiple-choice paper and the Core theory paper, an Extended candidate sits the Extended versions, and every candidate adds a practical component. The tier decides the ceiling, because Core entry in a tiered Cambridge subject caps the grade at C. Many parents do not know which tier their child is on, and the school's examinations officer can confirm it in a sentence.

The second is which practical component the centre enters. Paper 5 is a practical test sat with apparatus in a laboratory; Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, written on paper and testing the same skills through described experiments. The preparation for the two is not identical, and a tutor working towards the wrong one for eight weeks is a real and avoidable waste. This also varies between Sharjah campuses and the Dubai campuses that Al Nahda and Al Khan families attend.

The third is the component breakdown on the most recent marked paper, not the overall grade. A student on 28 out of 40 for multiple choice and 31 out of 80 on theory is a completely different case from one with those numbers reversed, and the two need different first sessions. Send a photograph of the marked script with the enquiry and the first hour becomes teaching rather than investigation.
bullets: The tier: Core caps at grade C, Extended reaches A*
The practical component: laboratory practical test or written alternative
The component split on the marked mock, not the headline grade

sections.heading: The three papers a Sharjah candidate sits, and what each one rewards
paragraphs: Every 0625 candidate sits three papers, and the three reward different behaviours. Treating physics as one undifferentiated subject is the most common planning error in this syllabus, because a student can be strong at one of the three behaviours and weak at the other two while the grade reports only the average.

The multiple-choice paper is 45 minutes for 40 marks and carries 30% of the grade. Its constraint is pace: a little over a minute a question, with no credit for working. It rewards recall and quick elimination, and it punishes a student who reasons every item from first principles. The honest preparation for it is timed sets, not more teaching. A student losing marks here is usually losing them in the last ten questions.

The theory paper is one hour fifteen for 80 marks and carries 50%. This is where the grade is made or lost, and it rewards something quite specific: an answer in the form the mark scheme expects. A six-mark question is six separate marking points, not one essay, and the examiner is looking for named quantities changing in stated directions. Students who write a paragraph about the general principle collect one mark out of six while believing they have answered fully.

The practical component carries 20% and rewards recording discipline — units in a table heading, a line of best fit drawn rather than joined dot to dot, an anomaly identified and a sensible improvement suggested. These are learnable conventions, and they are the cheapest marks in the subject to recover because so little physics content is involved. The table below sets the three side by side.

sections.heading: Electricity and magnetism: the order of reasoning that earns the marks
paragraphs: If a Sharjah candidate is losing a block of marks in one place, this is usually the place. Electricity and magnetism is the largest topic area by assessed weight in most series, and it has a structural feature that makes it unforgiving: the sub-answers depend on each other in a fixed sequence, so one early slip propagates through the whole question.

The sequence is total resistance first, then current in the main circuit, then the potential difference across each component, then power if asked. Students who start by writing down the quantity the question asks for and work backwards reach an answer that looks reasonable and is wrong. In a marked script this is visible instantly: the arithmetic is correct and the physics order is not. One session spent re-establishing the order of operations typically moves more marks than three spent on more circuit theory, because the student already knows the theory.

The magnetism half of the area behaves differently. Field patterns, the motor effect, induction and the transformer are taught late in most Year 11 schemes and revised least, which makes them a predictable gap in April. The marks here are awarded for cause and consequence in separate clauses: the flux through the coil changes, so an electromotive force is induced. A student who describes the apparatus — there is a coil and a magnet and it moves — has written a true sentence that earns nothing. This is a vocabulary and structure problem, not a comprehension problem, and it is one of the fastest things to fix in the whole syllabus.

The potential-divider question at Extended deserves separate mention because it is where strong candidates lose marks. It requires seeing that two resistances share a supply voltage in proportion, and that a change in one changes the share rather than the total. Once a student has drawn that proportion explicitly on three past questions, the topic stops being a problem.

sections.heading: Motion and forces: the free-body diagram as a mark-scoring object
paragraphs: The long theory paper usually opens with motion and forces, which means a candidate who is weak there begins the paper badly and loses composure as well as marks. The topic area covers speed, velocity and acceleration, graphs of motion, resultant force, work, power and efficiency, and at Extended the momentum treatment of collisions.

The specific skill that carries the marks is the free-body diagram, and it is taught as a sketch in many classrooms when it is in fact a scoring object. The marks follow conventions: forces drawn as arrows from a single point on the body, each labelled with the name of the force rather than a letter, arrow length indicating relative size, and no forces included that act on something other than the body in question. A student who draws weight and reaction and then adds the force the object exerts on the floor has shown a misunderstanding the examiner must penalise even though the diagram looks thorough.

Motion graphs are the second scoring object. For a distance-time graph the gradient is the speed; for a speed-time graph the gradient is the acceleration and the area under the line is the distance travelled. Those two facts generate a large number of marks across a series, and the recurring loss is a student calculating a gradient from a single coordinate pair read off the axes rather than from the change in each quantity across a chosen interval. Reading the triangle correctly is a technique that takes twenty minutes to install and persists.

The momentum work at Extended is more mechanical than it looks and rewards a fixed presentation: total momentum before, total momentum after, an equation that sets them equal, and a direction stated. Students who treat direction as implicit lose the sign and therefore the mark. None of this is conceptually hard. All of it is specific, and specificity is what a marked script reveals.
bullets: Forces drawn from one point, labelled by name, nothing included that acts elsewhere
Distance-time gradient is speed; speed-time gradient is acceleration; area is distance
Gradients taken across an interval, not from one coordinate pair
Momentum answers state a direction, every time

sections.heading: Waves and the marks that live in a drawing
paragraphs: Waves is the topic area where a candidate's pencil earns or loses the marks. Reflection, refraction, dispersion, total internal reflection and lenses are all assessed partly through diagrams, and the diagram conventions are marked as strictly as any calculation.

Four rules carry most of it. A normal is drawn as a dashed line at right angles to the surface at the point of incidence. Angles are measured from the normal, never from the surface. Ray lines carry arrows showing the direction of travel. And a refracted ray bends towards the normal on entering a denser medium and away on leaving it. A student who knows the physics and omits the arrows, or measures from the glass surface, loses marks that have nothing to do with understanding. This is worth stating plainly to a student once, on their own script, where they can see the marks that were available.

Total internal reflection questions add a condition that has to be stated rather than assumed: the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, and the ray is travelling from the denser medium to the less dense one. Both clauses are marking points. The lens work rewards the same discipline — principal axis drawn, focal points marked, the two standard construction rays used, and the image described with three properties rather than one.

The electromagnetic spectrum and sound are the descriptive end of the area and are often under-revised because they feel like general knowledge. They are not: the order of the spectrum, a use and a danger for each region, and the fact that sound requires a medium while electromagnetic waves do not, are all specific recallable facts that appear in multiple-choice items where speed matters. A single session of flashcard-style work here is a reliable return.

sections.heading: Thermal, nuclear and space physics: the cheap marks most candidates leave behind
paragraphs: Three of the six topic areas are smaller than the others and are routinely under-revised for exactly that reason. Taken together they are a substantial share of a grade, and they are the areas where a few sessions move the most marks per hour spent.

Thermal physics is the most formulaic writing in the syllabus, which makes it the easiest to convert from weakness into reliability. Each process has a sentence shape. Conduction involves particles vibrating more and passing energy to neighbours, with free electrons in a metal. Convection involves a region becoming less dense, rising, and being replaced. Evaporation involves the faster particles leaving the surface, lowering the average energy of those remaining. A student who learns those shapes and the specific heat capacity and latent heat calculations has secured the area in two sessions.

Nuclear physics has an unusually high ratio of marks to content. Atomic structure, isotopes, the properties and penetrating powers of the three radiation types, half-life and safety precautions are a finite list. Half-life questions are mechanical once the halving pattern is seen, and the safety and detection questions reward a specific named precaution rather than a general statement about care. This is the area to revise late in the course because it stays learnt.

Space physics is last on most schemes of work and first to be abandoned, which is a planning error rather than a judgement. The solar system, orbital relationships, the life cycle of stars and redshift are descriptive, bounded and heavily recall-based. For a candidate four weeks from the paper and choosing where to spend the remaining hours, this area and nuclear physics are the two with the clearest return, and electricity is the one that needs the time it will not get.

sections.heading: What one session fixes, what four fix, and what nothing fixes in six weeks
paragraphs: Parents ask how many sessions are needed and the honest answer depends on which problem is present. Some 0625 losses are conventions that can be installed in an hour. Some are topic gaps needing a bounded block. And some are two years of unfinished arithmetic that a six-week run before a series cannot repair, which is worth saying out loud rather than selling around.

The one-session fixes are the ones that make the largest immediate difference and are the reason we ask for a marked script. Measuring angles from the normal. Putting arrows on ray lines. Stating a direction in a momentum answer. Writing the constant of proportionality into a potential-divider argument. Separating cause from consequence in an induction answer. None of these is physics teaching; all of them are marks that were available and not taken. A student shown their own script with the available marks circled rarely needs telling twice.

The four-to-six-session fixes are topic-area repairs. Rebuilding circuit reasoning in the correct order. Installing the thermal physics sentence shapes. Working through the practical-component recording conventions with the student's own tables. Converting the motion graph work from intuition into technique. Each has a definable end point and a re-test, which is how a family knows it finished rather than lapsed.

What six weeks cannot do is give a student fluent algebra they never acquired, or make a Core candidate into an Extended one, or recover a syllabus that has not been taught. In those situations the useful plan is narrower: pick the areas with the highest marks-per-hour return, secure them properly, and accept that the rest will be answered from partial knowledge. That is a better outcome than attempting everything and securing nothing, and any provider who tells you otherwise within six weeks of a paper is selling rather than teaching. No tutor can promise a particular grade in a Cambridge examination.

sections.heading: SPEA, the Sharjah centre, and who decides what your child sits
paragraphs: Physics in this emirate is delivered inside a regulatory structure that is worth understanding, mostly because it tells a parent who to ask about what. Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools in the emirate. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge holds a comparable remit, while Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools to ADEK, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education.

What that means in practice for a 0625 candidate is a division of responsibility. The regulator oversees the school. The school decides whether to offer separate physics or Co-ordinated Sciences, which tier each student is entered at, and whether the centre enters the practical test or the alternative to practical. Cambridge sets the syllabus, the papers and the series, and allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable — Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

None of those decisions belongs to a tutoring provider, and no tutoring provider can claim standing with any of those bodies. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from SPEA, from the Ministry of Education, or from Cambridge, and nothing on this page should be read as implying otherwise. What a parent can do is ask the school three precise questions — the tier, the practical component and the centre's administrative zone — and get three precise answers.

The federal picture adds one more element to a Sharjah week. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, and in Dubai, KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Families attending Dubai campuses from Al Nahda therefore carry a specific homework load into the same evenings a physics session has to fit into, which is a scheduling fact rather than a complaint.

sections.heading: What a 0625 tutor does with school work, and what nobody should do
paragraphs: Physics generates a steady stream of school-set work — problem sheets, practical write-ups, past-paper questions for homework — and families reasonably want to know how a tutor should handle it. The boundary is simple to state and worth stating, because at least one provider ranking for these searches sells across it.

A tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on the student's own work. In a 0625 context that means working through a question type until the student can do it unaided, then watching them do it; reading a written answer and showing which marking points were and were not present; and discussing a practical write-up so the student can improve their own recording. It does not mean producing the answers to a problem sheet the school will collect, and it does not mean dictating a write-up line by line. The distinction matters for the student, because work submitted as their own has to be their own, and it matters for the school's ability to see where the student actually is.

The second boundary concerns materials. Cambridge syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the awarding body's copyright material, distributed to schools and published on the official site. A tutor references them, cites them and works from the copies the school already holds. A provider that offers to supply a bundle of them as a download is telling you something about how it operates, and the same applies to anyone offering unreleased material.

The third is claims. No tutor can guarantee a grade in a Cambridge examination, and a page promising one should be read sceptically rather than trusted. What can honestly be shown is movement in marked written work: an explain question that scored one mark in October scoring four in January, a circuit question answered in the right order, a practical table with units in the headings. That evidence is available weekly, it is specific, and it is what we ask families to judge the arrangement on.

process.title: Send the marked mock, component by component
process.description: Photograph the whole marked script rather than reporting the grade. The split between the multiple-choice mark and the theory mark tells a physics specialist whether the problem is recall, pace or written form, and the annotations show which topic areas lost marks together. This single step removes a month of exploratory teaching.

process.title: Confirm the tier and the practical component
process.description: Ask the school's examinations officer two questions: is the entry Core or Extended, and is the centre entering the practical test or the alternative to practical. The answers decide which papers the sessions prepare for. Guessing either one and finding out in April is the most common avoidable error in this subject.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson on a real question
process.description: One hour, online, no card required and no obligation. Spend it on two questions from the marked script. Watch whether the tutor shows the student the marking points that were available rather than re-explaining the physics. That behaviour is what distinguishes a 0625 specialist from a capable science graduate.

process.title: Agree the component and the topic order
process.description: Decide which paper the work targets first and in which order the six topic areas are addressed. For most candidates that means electricity early because it is large and sequential, and nuclear and space physics late because they stay learnt. The plan is written down so progress can be checked against it.

process.title: Review at week six on written answers
process.description: Six sessions in, compare marked answers rather than impressions. Explain questions scoring more marking points, circuit questions worked in order, practical tables with units in the headings. If those are moving, continue. If they are not, change the arrangement rather than adding hours to it.

whyPoints.title: Marked against the published scheme, not against a feeling
whyPoints.description: Written answers come back annotated with the marking points that were present and the ones that were not. That is the only pre-results evidence available in this subject, and it is specific enough for a parent or a school to check. It is also what shows whether an explain-question problem is being fixed.

whyPoints.title: The component split drives the plan
whyPoints.description: A candidate strong on multiple choice and weak on theory needs different work from one with the reverse pattern, even though both have the same grade. Sessions are built from the breakdown on the marked paper rather than from a generic revision sequence applied to every student.

whyPoints.title: Practical skills taught from the student's own recording
whyPoints.description: The practical component is 20% and most of those marks follow conventions rather than apparatus: units in table headings, a drawn line of best fit, an anomaly identified, a specific improvement suggested. Working from the student's own tables and graphs is how those conventions become habits.

whyPoints.title: Subject-matched rather than distance-matched
whyPoints.description: Separate-sciences physics specialists are not evenly distributed across this emirate, and for families in Kalba, Khor Fakkan or Tilal City the local pool is very small. Online delivery removes geography from the choice and puts it back on who has taught the 0625 papers and marked them.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built around a real Sharjah evening
whyPoints.description: A protected hour in Gulf Standard Time that accounts for a bus returning after 16:30 from a Dubai campus and an evening that already contains Arabic and Islamic education homework. Sessions can move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. A slot that survives the term is worth more than a convenient one.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on what a tutor will do
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nobody here produces answers for a problem sheet the school will collect, and no Cambridge syllabus, past paper, mark scheme or boundary table is supplied as a download — those belong to the awarding body and the school already holds them.

faqs.question: What does a free-body diagram have to show to score marks in 0625?
faqs.answer: Four conventions carry the marks. Every force is drawn as an arrow starting from a single point on the body. Each arrow is labelled with the name of the force — weight, normal contact force, friction, air resistance — rather than a letter. Relative arrow lengths indicate relative sizes, so a body in equilibrium should not show one arrow twice as long as its balancing pair. And nothing is included that acts on something other than the body in question, which is why adding the force the object exerts on the floor loses the mark. Students who learn the diagram as a scoring object rather than a sketch gain marks immediately.

faqs.question: My son can state Newton's third law but cannot use it in a question. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: Almost always the same thing: naming both bodies. The law concerns a pair of forces acting on two different objects, and a student who writes about action and reaction without saying which object each force acts on cannot apply it. The fix is mechanical and quick. For three past questions, write the two bodies down first, then the force each exerts on the other, then the answer. One session usually installs it. If the problem persists afterwards, the underlying issue is normally the free-body diagram rather than the law, and that is where the next session goes.

faqs.question: How are marks awarded for the gradient of a graph in 0625?
faqs.answer: For a change in each quantity taken across a chosen interval, not from a single coordinate pair. On a distance-time graph the gradient is the speed; on a speed-time graph the gradient is the acceleration and the area under the line is the distance travelled. The usual loss is a student reading one point off the axes and dividing, which gives a number that is sometimes right by accident and is not awarded the method mark. The technique is to mark a triangle on the graph, read both changes from it, and show the division. It takes about twenty minutes to install and then persists.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter lose marks for writing more than the question asked?
faqs.answer: She probably is not losing marks for the extra writing itself, but for what the extra writing displaces. A six-mark 0625 question is six separate marking points, and the examiner awards each one where it is clearly present. A long general paragraph about the principle involved can contain one of those points and bury the other five. The remedy is structural rather than about effort: identify how many marks are available, then write that many distinct statements, each naming a quantity and what happens to it. Students find this a relief, because it is less writing rather than more.

faqs.question: Which part of the electromagnetism topic is worth a separate session?
faqs.answer: Electromagnetic induction, for two reasons. It is taught late in most Year 11 schemes and therefore revised least, and its marks are awarded in a structure students rarely produce unprompted: a stated change in the flux through the coil, then the consequence, which is an induced electromotive force. Describing the apparatus — a coil, a magnet, movement — is a true statement that earns nothing. Field patterns and the motor effect are usually safer. The transformer calculation is mechanical once the turns ratio is set out properly. One session on induction answer structure is a reliable return in this topic area.

faqs.question: Is the principle of moments still examined in Cambridge 0625?
faqs.answer: Moments, turning effect and the conditions for equilibrium are part of the forces content and do appear, so they are worth revising rather than dropping. The structure of the answer is what earns the marks: the sum of clockwise moments equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about a stated pivot, with each moment given as a force multiplied by a perpendicular distance. The two recurring losses are forgetting to state the pivot and using a distance that is not perpendicular to the force. Confirm the exact content for your child's series against the current syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org, since syllabus content is revised periodically.

faqs.question: What can one 0625 session realistically change?
faqs.answer: More than parents expect, if the session is spent on conventions rather than on content. Measuring angles from the normal instead of the surface, putting arrows on ray lines, stating a direction in a momentum answer, separating cause from consequence in an induction answer, writing six marking points for a six-mark question — each of these is a block of marks that was available and not taken, and each can be shown to a student on their own script in under an hour. What one session cannot do is teach an untaught topic area or repair weak algebra. That is why the marked paper comes first.

faqs.question: Our physics mock came back at a grade D. Which topic area do we start with?
faqs.answer: Start from the script rather than from the grade, because a D is reached in several different ways. If the marks are lost in a block around circuits, begin with electricity and rebuild the order of reasoning. If they are spread thinly across every topic area, the cause is usually explain-question structure or arithmetic, and the first session should be about answer form rather than any single topic. If the practical-component marks are low while theory is sound, the issue is recording conventions. Each of those is a different first month, which is why a photograph of the marked paper is the most useful thing to send.

faqs.question: Does the school decide the physics tier, or can we ask for a change?
faqs.answer: The school decides, normally on attainment and usually during Year 10, and the decision matters because Core entry in a tiered Cambridge subject caps the grade at C. Whether a change is still possible depends on how close the entry deadline is and on the school's own judgement. Entries for a Cambridge series close months before the papers, with a June entry fixed in the spring and the November resit entry fixed in the months before that session, so the conversation has to happen early. Ask the examinations officer directly what tier your child is entered at and what the deadline for amending it is. Those are both factual questions with factual answers.

faqs.question: Does 0625 reward a correct answer with no working shown?
faqs.answer: Partly, and relying on it is expensive. A correct final answer normally earns the answer mark, but calculation questions typically carry method marks that are awarded for a correct relationship stated and a correct substitution made. A student who writes only the final number and gets it wrong scores nothing, where the same student showing the relationship and the substitution would have kept most of the marks. The habit worth building is relationship, substitution, answer with a unit, on every calculation. It costs a few seconds per question and it is the cheapest insurance in the paper.

faqs.question: My child's school enters the alternative to practical. What does that paper actually ask?
faqs.answer: It tests practical skills in writing rather than with apparatus. Typical tasks are reading a described instrument, completing a results table, plotting points and drawing a line of best fit, identifying an anomalous reading, stating a conclusion supported by the data, and suggesting a specific improvement to a described method. The marks follow conventions closely: units belong in the table heading rather than beside each value, a line of best fit is drawn rather than joined point to point, and an improvement has to be specific enough to act on. All of that is teachable over video from the student's own attempts.

faqs.question: How late can a physics session start for a family in Al Nahda attending a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, and that is usually the right choice. Where children travel from Al Nahda or Al Khan to a Dubai campus, the bus frequently returns after 16:30, and an evening that also contains Arabic and Islamic education homework leaves little room before 18:00. Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time and are commonly held at 18:00, 19:00 or later, and they can shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. The practical point is that one protected slot late enough to actually happen is worth more than an earlier one that is cancelled twice a month.

faqs.question: Does the Sharjah Private Education Authority inspect physics teaching at my child's school?
faqs.answer: SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and, like Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools. That is a school-level remit covering the institution rather than a report on an individual subject department. For Dubai campuses the equivalent body is KHDA, and for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK. None of them regulates private tutoring, and no tutoring provider — IB Gram included — holds any approval or accreditation from them. Published regulator material is useful context about a school; it is not a verdict on its physics teaching.

faqs.question: What should a tutor do with the physics homework the school has already set?
faqs.answer: Use it as the material and leave the authorship with the student. A good session takes a question type from the set work, teaches it until the student can do it unaided, then watches them do one and marks it. What a tutor should not do is produce the answers to a sheet the school will collect, because work submitted as the student's own has to be theirs and because the school needs to see where the student actually is. The same applies to a practical write-up: discuss it, show which recording conventions are missing, and let the student rewrite it.

faqs.question: How much of the 0625 grade can be recovered in the last eight weeks?
faqs.answer: A useful amount if the remaining hours are aimed well, and the aiming matters more than the number of hours. The highest return in a short window usually comes from answer structure on explain questions, the practical-component recording conventions, and the two compact topic areas — nuclear and space physics — that are descriptive and stay learnt. Electricity needs more time than eight weeks comfortably allows, so it is worth securing the sequential circuit reasoning rather than attempting the whole area. What cannot be done in eight weeks is repairing unfinished algebra, and no honest provider will promise a particular grade in that window.

faqs.question: Does 0625 Extended need more mathematics than 0580 provides?
faqs.answer: No, and that is worth knowing because it changes where the money goes. The mathematics 0625 requires — rearranging a relationship, substituting, converting between unit prefixes, reading a gradient, handling standard form and sensible precision — is all inside the Extended Mathematics 0580 syllabus. When a physics problem looks mathematical, the cause is usually fluency rather than content: the student can do the algebra given time and cannot do it under exam pressure. That is normally better addressed inside the physics session, using physics quantities, than by adding a separate maths arrangement and a second fee.

sharjah/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tut.closingHeading: Send the marked script and we will tell you what it shows
sharjah/cambridge-igcse-physics-0625-tut.closingBody: If a 0625 mark has come back lower than your child's understanding of physics suggests it should, the useful next step is not more revision. Photograph the marked script, ask the school two questions — Core or Extended, and practical test or alternative to practical — and take a free trial lesson with no card required. In that hour a physics specialist will show your child the marking points that were available on two of their own answers, which is usually the moment the problem becomes visible. Lessons run online, one to one, over live video in Gulf Standard Time; home visits are a service we offer only in India.
